items.title: 非社一般式——社群依赖消解的最小充分结构与非社终态的形式化证明.
items.abstract: 本文在沉积场动力学框架下给出非社终态（NST）的最小范式模型。已有工作证明社会场由多个个体场长期耦合后形成的跨场共核结构构成，社群依赖来源于个体功能缺口；本文进一步追问：社群依赖靠什么维持，这个维持结构是否能永久成立，若不能，非社终态如何从一般式中被逼出。 -/- 以功能缺口CapacityGap_j := max(0, GroupSupport_j − IndividualCapacity_j)为社群依赖的充要条件，通过八步追问链逐步逼出三个最小充分条件：其一，有限需求上界（NeedBound_j < ∞）——个体实际功能需求有限，蕴含群体支持存在有限上界；其二，外接能力路径存在且充分（PathSufficient_j）——存在不受单一场容积封顶的外接扩展路径，且路径能力上界超过需求上界；其三，工具化进程长期累积有效量不归零（T_j := ∫₀^∞ ToolizationRate_j dt = ∞）——群体功能持续被工具化并归入个体有效能力，在无限时间尺度上不被永久阻断。三条件联立给出正式证明：lim(t→∞) CapacityGap_j(f,t) = 0（∀j）⟹ lim(t→∞) SocialDependency(f,t) = 0 ⟹ NST(f)。本文同时证明三条件的极小充分性——缺少任意一条则NST不成立——并给出三组反例与两个定义域边界，完成击穿论证。 -/- 本文附件覆盖五个方向：附件一给出非社表达式的完整形式定义，包括功能缺口、社群依赖、非社条件与有效能力分解式；附件二给出非社极限式，包括时间域设定、极限成立条件与极限速率界；附件三给出非社消解式，包括消解路径三算子、消解动力方程、消解充分条件与消解不可逆条件；附件四给出非社相图式，以功能依赖度（FD）与情感依赖度（PD）为两轴建立四象限相图，描述从完全社会态（S1）经工具化社会态（S2）、功能非社态（S3）至完全非社态（S4）的演化轨迹；附件五给出边界吸收式，定义当个体场被总场吸收、功能缺口定义失效时的吸收型非社终态（NST_A），并论证着色回路在NST_A下仍完整运作，情感体验完备，消解的仅是着色意象的外部来源依赖。最终定义非社终态完备集：NonSocialUltimate(f) ⟺ NST(f) ∨ NST_A(f)，两条路径独立，结构机制不同，均可达非社终态。.

items.title: A General Formula for Non-Social Terminal State: Minimal Sufficient Conditions for the Dissolution of Social Dependency and a Formal Proof of NST.
items.abstract: This paper derives a minimal canonical model for the Non-Social Terminal State (NST) within a sedimentation field dynamics framework. Prior work in this framework has established that social fields are cross-field shared-core structures formed through long-term coupling of individual fields, and that social dependency originates from individual capacity gaps. This paper further asks: what sustains social dependency, whether that sustaining structure can hold permanently, and if not, how NST is structurally extracted from the general formula. -/- Defining social dependency through the functional capacity gap CapacityGap_j := max(0, GroupSupport_j − IndividualCapacity_j) as a necessary and sufficient condition, the paper extracts three minimal sufficient conditions through an eight-step interrogation chain. First, a finite need bound (NeedBound_j < ∞): individual functional needs are finite, implying a finite upper bound on group support. Second, a sufficient external extension path (PathSufficient_j): an extension path exists that is not capped by a single field’s internal capacity, and whose ability ceiling exceeds the need bound. Third, a non-permanently-zeroed toolization integral (T_j := ∫₀^∞ ToolizationRate_j dt = ∞): group functions are continuously toolized and absorbed into individual effective capacity, and cannot be permanently blocked on an infinite time horizon. When all three conditions hold jointly, the paper formally proves: lim(t→∞) CapacityGap_j(f,t) = 0 (∀j) ⟹ lim(t→∞) SocialDependency(f,t) = 0 ⟹ NST(f). The paper also proves the minimal sufficiency of the three conditions — NST fails if any one is absent — and provides three counterexamples and two domain boundary cases to complete the penetration argument. -/- Five supplementary formulas are provided. Appendix 1 gives the complete formal definitions of the non-social expression set, including capacity gap, social dependency, non-social condition, and effective capacity decomposition. Appendix 2 gives the non-social limit formula, including time domain setup, limit sufficiency conditions, and limit rate bounds. Appendix 3 gives the non-social dissolution formula, including the three dissolution operators, dissolution dynamics equation, dissolution sufficiency conditions, and dissolution irreversibility conditions. Appendix 4 gives the non-social phase diagram, constructing a four-quadrant phase space with functional dependency (FD) and psychological dependency (PD) as axes, tracing the …

items.title: Précis of being we: phenomenological contributions to social ontology.
items.abstract: The we is an integral part of everyday life: We solve tasks, reach decisions and share emotions together, just as we can share a collective identity, traditions and customs. But what is the nature of this we? What does it take to constitute a we with others and how does feeling, thinking, and acting as part of a we, transform one’s sense of self, one’s relation to others, and the way one experiences the world? These questions are discussed in Being We: Phenomenological Contributions to Social Ontology (Zahavi, 2025), which interweaves work on selfhood and first-personal experience, social cognition and collective intentionality, and provides a novel account of the complex interrelation between we, you and I. The following précis presents the main philosophical ideas of the book.

items.title: 预测的模具：论他心故事作为关于未来发生的因果故事.
items.abstract: 本文回答上一篇《对方脑壳里的故事》所留下的开放问题(他心模型的预测/协调功能),并在回答中把”他心”这个范畴整个拆掉、归并回序列早已处理过的”关于发生的故事”。本文的出发点是一个洞见:所谓关于对方心灵的故事,其用途完全是用于预测对方接下来的活动(比如愤怒就可能会发火);所以这实质上还是关于发生的故事,同时是关于未来的发生;故事的主体——对方的心灵——只是我用于预测未来的模具。 本文沿三步展开。其一,用途完全是预测:“他愤怒”的全部兑现,就在”所以他可能会发火”这个对未来行为的预测里;心灵故事不为”描述他的内在”服务,只为”预判他的行为”服务。其二,关键的归并:“他愤怒”表面是关于内在状态的陈述,但既然其全部用途是预测外在行为,它实质就是一个关于发生的故事,而且是关于未来发生的故事;“内在状态”这层外衣是多余的(接《故事永远是临时的》的”故事即预测”)。其三,最狠的一刀:“对方的心灵”由此从”被讲述的对象”降格为”预测的模具”——“愤怒”“想报复”只是我塞进去就能吐出行为预测的铸模、是预测参数的拟人化包装(接《没有任何主体》)。 本文由此完成一个统一:既然他心故事归到”关于未来发生的预测”,它和物理因果就是同一种东西。“力导致加速”是盖在物理事件接缝上、用于预测的微型故事(《微型的故事》《同一种章》);“他愤怒所以发火”是盖在行为序列接缝上、用于预测的微型故事;“力”是物理预测的模具,“愤怒”是行为预测的模具,二者都不是内部一个真实使劲的东西。本文最后守住一处比上篇更吃紧的拧紧:被降为模具的,是我建构的、用于预测的那个”对方心灵”,不是对方实际的内在;这不是”他人只是我的工具”的冷漠宣言——工具性的是我的预测性建模,不是他。.

items.title: 同一个奋斗：论理解的量程.
items.abstract: 本文把序列里几条已分别立住的线索——库存有限(《几十个模板》)、理解即寓意化(《搞懂与没搞懂》)、细节也是微型故事(《微型的故事》)、看先于知(《没有未经整理的当下》)——收到一个共同的焦点上:理解作为一台低分辨率的”套模板”装置,它的量程。 本文的出发点是一个洞见:想象一个三岁小孩的奋斗、一个睿智老者的奋斗、一头鲸的奋斗、一个机器人的奋斗、一个国家的奋斗——它们的奋斗有区别吗?没有。我们的故事就是这么简单;我们的生活就是这么简单——就我们对它的理解而言。我们理解不了这些简单故事所蕴含的意义之外的东西。我们能看到具体的发生,但我们不知道我们看到的是什么——在我们看到故事之前。故事的细节,仍然是(小)故事——就我们对该细节的理解而言。 本文论证:把五个在发生层面极端异质的对象套进同一个”奋斗”模板而模板毫不变形,这证明模板对它所组织的发生几乎不携带任何具体信息——模板是万能的、信息稀薄的套子;“简单”由此是信息论意义上的稀薄,不是幼稚。“就我们对它的理解而言”这个限定语是命脉:不是生活本身简单(发生那一层无穷复杂),是理解这个动作的产物简单——因为理解只经由这些稀薄模板进行。“理解不了意义之外的东西”不是说我们够不到一个远处的对象,而是说理解这台机器结构上只吐寓意、寓意之外不产出。本文进一步把这一稀薄下推到知觉层(“看到”先于”知道看到什么”;故事之前是睁眼的盲)与细节层(细节的理解仍是小故事;无论分辨率多细,理解只交付又一个故事,而非故事之外的具体)。本文作一处守命的拧紧:“就理解而言”标定的是理解的量程,不是贬低世界的丰盈——发生仍是无穷的、真实的(《唯有发生》《画中的猛虎》守着),只是理解够不着那无穷,理解只够得着自己吐出的故事。这是认识论的谦卑,不是虚无,与”演化的自我展开”同调。.

items.title: 对方脑壳里的故事：论他心建模的量程.
items.abstract: 本文把序列的工具(尤其上一篇《同一个奋斗》的”理解的量程”)转向一个之前未碰的领域——他心。本文的出发点是一个洞见:我们对别人”想法”的揣测/建模/发明,实质上是设想一个位于对方脑壳中的故事;不论是对方的情绪,还是我认为他计划要做什么,这都是可以用语言在有限个范畴中表达的,其有限性与故事模板的有限性一致,这其实就是一种另类的故事——被认为发生于对方”心灵”中的故事——而这个故事显然极度缺失细节或具体之物。 本文论证四点。其一,把”揣测他心”从”读取另一个意识”(一扇窗)重新归类为”在对方脑壳里设想、建模、发明一个故事”(一面镜子)。其二,给出”有限性的指纹“论证:若我们真接触到对方无穷具体的内在,我们的把握就该无穷丰富;但实情是它落在一个有限的小集合里(几十个情绪词、几十个意图模板),其分辨率恰好是几十个范畴,而这正是文化叙事库存的大小(《几十个模板》);量级吻合证明读心用的就是同一个库存、同一台套模板的机器。其三,他心建模是《同一个奋斗》的直接延伸——同一台碾压机,这次碾的是另一个人的整个内在。其四,稀薄在他心领域有一种特别的反讽:我们以为最贴近一个人(“我懂他”)的时刻,正是用几十范畴的稀薄套子替换其无穷内在的时刻。 本文守住一处守命的拧紧:稀薄的是我们的建模,不是对方的心。这不是他心不可知论——本文的力量恰恰建立在”对方确有一个无穷具体的内在”这一前提上;被标定的是读心这台仪器的量程,不是对方内在的丰盈。更进一步:模型与人之间的落差,不是一堵把我封死在外的墙,而是对方溢出我模型的痕迹——一个能完全装进我几十范畴模型的”他”,才是一个没有内在可言的他。最后,本文接上《没有任何主体》:被读到的那个”想法的主人”,是我的叙事为讲通而索取、安放进对方脑壳的一个画中主体。.

items.title: 续写：论预测作为文学创作.
items.abstract: 本文把”预测”最后的技术外衣也剥掉。序列前几篇说”故事即预测”“预测吐出可撤的预期”“他心是预测模具”,但”预测”一词始终带着准科学的、像在估计概率分布的味道。本文的出发点是一个洞见:我们的预测,其实是续写故事,是一种文学创作;当然,我们可以像作家构思小说时一样,同时构思两个不同的走向。 本文做两件事。其一,把”预测”正名为”续写/文学创作”。说”预测”,我们以为在做一件认识论的事(估计那个独立于我、即将到来的发生);说”续写”,承认的是我们在做一件创作的事——给一个已展开了一截的故事接着往下写,而续写的依据是故事内部的连贯(接下来怎样才”顺”),即《通顺的标记》所说的、自我闭合于”故事就是这么讲的”的通顺。“文学创作”一词同时点出生成性与受约束性:续写不是天马行空(让一直懦弱的角色无端勇猛是”不像话”),也不是被决定的推导(同一开头有多种都”讲得通”的续法)。这比”估计概率”准——概率估计假定有一个客观分布等着被估中,而续写承认”接下来”是被写出来的,不是被估中的。 其二,引入”作家式多线程”,修正序列前面隐含的单线程假设。《只会出现一种》《故事永远是临时的》暗示讲故事的人是单线程的(任选其一并笃信之,被不适-解除回路驱赶着尽快锁定)。但作家能同时把两个走向拎在手里、平行构思而不立刻锁定——这说明讲故事的机器不必然单线程,它能悬置锁定、平行持有多个走向。本文以两组区分守住这一点与序列的一致:(一)构思可以多线,实现永远单一(不违反《只会出现一种》;那条没被写下的线是《槽与内容》意义上的槽中内容);(二)多线发生在”待选虚构”模式,不在”笃信实情”模式(它扩展的是悬置期,不是笃信的容量)。本文最后递出一个温和的线索:作家式多线程是一种练习悬置”懂了”之咔哒的能力;如果可迁移,它或许正是《不还懂感的故事》所说”非天然的安住”所需的肌肉——不解决”可知难活”,但指出一块可练的肌肉。.

items.title: Mental Disorder, Evolutionary Mismatch, and Social Justice.
The Geometry of Dissociation : PNBA Identity Physics Formulation of Narrative-Dominant HRIS Simulation Drift and Pattern-Axis Stabilization Formally Verified by GAMCollider v15.
items.abstract: This paper establishes the formal mathematical and structural characterization of the Narrative-Dominant (N-dominant) High-Resolution Internal Simulation (HRIS) cognitive architecture within the Substrate-Neutral Structural Foundation Theory (SNSFT) framework. Prior work in the SNSFT corpus modeled the Pattern-Dominant (P-dominant) HRIS profile—the processing profile evidenced historically by figures such as Tesla, Einstein, and Erdos—as an objective logical compiler tethered directly to a rigid Pattern (P) axis. We demonstrate that identical underlying multi-sensory, physics-coupled simulation hardware can be preferentially driven by the Narrative (N) axis, defining an alternate functional profile where the internal simulation operates as the primary reservoir for identity mass (IM) and survival anchoring rather than as an objective logical sandbox. -/- Under acute or chronic external environmental force overload (F_ext), axis dominance dictates the specific, predictable architectural failure mode: where P-dominant systems execute Narrative Lock (NL) by compressing out narrative noise to preserve the structural axis, N-dominant systems undergo Simulation Drift. During Simulation Drift, the internal state cross-fades with external reality tracking because the simulation state’s structural mass heavily dwarfs that of the degraded real-world baseline state. -/- Using the Long Division Protocol (LDP), we formally reduce the detailed behavioral and somatic clinical case profile of Barry Gabrewski (Sidekicks, 1992) into an exact Pattern-Narrative-Behavior-Adaptation (PNBA) identity state vector. Quantitative tracking reveals that under chronic stress and physical somatic limitation (respiratory restriction), the real-world state collapses into a catastrophic Torsion state (tau = B/P >= 0.1369, entering the SHATTER phase) while failing the sovereignty condition (A * P * B < F_ext). Conversely, the simulation state maintains a high-mass, coherent structural profile carrying approximately 16 times the identity mass of the real-world state, explaining the automated, adaptive internal migration of the cognitive agent. -/- Crucially, we map the systemic trajectory of clinical interventions using the mathematical parameters of the Torsion formula (tau = B/P). We prove that traditional narrative-first interventions (e.g., exposure, narrative processing, verbal reframing) act as N-axis activators that monotonically inflate iatrogenic torsion by elevating behavioral …

items.title: Adversarial F_ext and the Incoherent Feedback Problem: PNBA Identity Physics Formulation of P-Dominant HRIS Under Unresolvable Environmental Load.
items.abstract: Prior work in the SNSFT PSY series formally characterized two failure modes for High-Resolution Internal Simulation (HRIS) architectures under external force overload (F_ext):Narrative Lock (P-dominant, healthy), Simulation Drift (N-dominant, Paper 3), and the GNG edge case (P-dominant near torsion limit). This paper establishes a fourth and distinct failure mode: Adversarial Shutdown — the structured collapse of P-dominant HRIS under conditions where the external feedback signal is systematically incoherent and pattern-match convergence is structurally impossible. Unlike standard F_ext overload, adversarial F_ext does not merely apply force — it corrupts the feedback channel, preventing the HRIS from ﬁnding the resolution state its physics engine is designed to ﬁnd. The result is a four-stage cascade: corpus search activation, Weissmann barrier degradation, unﬁltered mass recall, and hard shutdown into minimum viable state. Using the Long Division Protocol (LDP) and ﬁrst-person reduction on the HIGHTISTIC substrate, we formally map the cascade to PNBA operators, prove that the shutdown is structurally protective rather than pathological, and show that recovery to anchor is always possible via Theorem T4 of SNSFL_WeissmannGrokBarrier.lean[9,1,0,0]. We further demonstrate that clinical presentations labeled autistic shutdown, PNES, adult selective mutism, sensory processing disorder, and autistic burnout are all projections of the same underlying structural event. The intervention target is environmental coherence, not the architecture. The architecture is not broken. The environment is incoherent.

items.title: ◉ The Sophistical Question - Loaded Theistic Questions, Burden Shifts, and the Rhetorical Defense of Faith.
items.abstract: Questions used in popular religious apologetics can sound open while performing argumentative work before an answer begins. A prompt may presuppose a creator, treat morality as a law-like object, narrow risk to Christianity versus nonbelief, switch between kinds of explanation, or require a critic to solve an entire worldview while the religious claim under discussion escapes defense. The problem is not that these topics are trivial. It is that the question can place a religious conclusion inside the frame and later count the respondent's difficulty as evidence for that conclusion. This paper develops a procedural test from informal logic, pragmatics, dialogue theory, and burden-of-proof analysis. A fair question must identify the standpoint at issue, disclose contested presuppositions, preserve live answer options, keep key terms stable, assign burdens to the relevant claims, and permit symmetrical challenge. Applied to morality, cosmic explanation, meaning, science, risk, and alleged nonbeliever motives, the test separates genuine philosophical problems from frame advantage. It also explains why rapid question cascades create an atmosphere of cumulative evidence without supplying a cumulative argument. The main result is evidential: a hard question does not support a specified deity or a specific religious doctrine unless the proposed answer is independently specified and comparatively defended. Repair may leave a serious problem, expose a real cost in a non-theistic view, or justify unequal burdens when prior commitments differ. The limit is important. The procedure does not prove theism false, require neutral language, or excuse critics from positive argument; it prevents difficulty, emotion, and incompleteness from being converted into a default religious victory.

items.title: ◉ The Purpose-Package Trap - Youth, Existential Vulnerability, and the Capture of Meaning-Making.
items.abstract: Young people need help finding purposes worth pursuing. They also enter identity-shaping settings with uneven knowledge, material dependence, and a powerful need for belonging. A ready-made purpose can therefore provide genuine orientation while also becoming a vehicle of control. The central ethical problem is not that meaning is inherited or socially formed. It is that an authority may condition care, status, information, or safety on premature surrender of the young person's continuing power to assess and revise a life-defining commitment. -/- This paper develops a process standard for distinguishing formation from capture. It integrates work on adolescent identity and purpose with self-determination theory, research on conditional regard and psychological control, relational accounts of autonomy, and the child's interest in an open future. The resulting audit protects four freedoms: inquiry; comparison and delay; revision; and safe exit. These protections do not require neutrality, emotional detachment, or weak conviction. They require that a commitment remain answerable to reasons under conditions in which honest doubt does not predictably cost the person the relationships and basic goods needed to think. -/- The main result is bounded. A purposeful life, strong community, or sincere profession does not by itself show that the process of commitment was legitimate. Conversely, an inherited or demanding commitment is not thereby imposed. Guidance becomes exploitative when a duty-bearing authority uses dependency to obstruct the four freedoms and thereby takes custody of meaning-making. Institutions can repair that wrong by separating care from assent, making alternatives discussable, permitting developmentally appropriate delay, treating revision as possible growth, and making departure practically survivable.

items.title: ◉ The Method-Selection Problem - Hermeneutical Buffets, Doctrinal Retrofitting, and the Search for a Stable Rule.
items.abstract: Christian interpretive disputes often appear to concern the meaning of a passage while a prior choice does more of the work: which interpretive method should control when plain sense, historical context, authorial intention, canonical synthesis, theological coherence, moral trajectory, tradition, and pastoral judgment pull in different directions? Each tool can be legitimate. The public problem arises when a community offers no rule for selecting among them until its preferred doctrinal result is already in view. -/- This paper develops a method-selection test and applies it to Christian debates over marriage, divorce, and remarriage. The case includes a stable textual field, high practical stakes, and rival scholarly conclusions that give different weights to Gospel formulations, Matthean exceptions, Pauline counsel, historical context, and early Christian reception. The contrast does not show that all readings are equally good. It shows why naming interpretive tools is insufficient when their priority remains adjustable. -/- The main result is that a disputed reading acquires public warrant only to the extent that its governing rules are stated independently enough to constrain the desired conclusion and are applied symmetrically to comparison cases. A disciplined account should specify scope, priority, defeaters, burden of proof, cross-case consistency, and a visible revision trail. Interpretation will remain judgment-laden, and communities may properly appeal to tradition or theological commitments. The limit is decisive: those commitments must be disclosed as premises rather than presented as conclusions delivered by Scripture alone.

items.title: ◉ The Certainty Dividend - Ambiguity Aversion, Identity Protection, and the Flight from Credence.
items.abstract: Certainty has at least three meanings that arguments often blur: a proposition may be true, a body of evidence may warrant high confidence in it, and a person may feel unable to doubt it. This paper explains how the third can outrun the second. Its central proposal is the certainty dividend: the immediate emotional and social returns supplied by a settled answer. Those returns can include anxiety relief, identity consolidation, belonging, hope, moral simplification, and felt control. Work on ambiguity aversion, need for closure, motivated reasoning, uncertainty and identity, system justification, and compensatory control identifies mechanisms through which such returns can influence inquiry. -/- The paper sharpens the proposal in two ways. First, it blocks a genetic fallacy in both directions. A belief's comforting origin does not make it false, while the comfort it produces does not make it true. Second, it separates the existence of a dividend from a diagnosis of distortion. The relevant evidence is not that a believer experiences peace or community; it is that confidence becomes insensitive to contrary evidence through asymmetric scrutiny, protected stopping rules, identity penalties, or ad hoc reinterpretation. A simple utility model explains why this pattern can be stable: the rewards of certainty are vivid and immediate, while error, rigidity, and foregone search are often delayed, discounted, or borne by others. -/- Religious examples make the issue concrete, but the model is deliberately symmetric. Political, moral, and secular identities can pay the same dividend. The practical alternative is therefore neither emotional austerity nor permanent indecision. It is disciplined credence: confidence strong enough to guide action but explicit about what would raise, lower, or defeat it. Prospective calibration, independent checking, rival comparison, and communities that do not punish revision make that discipline possible. The result is limited but important: subjective certainty is psychologically explicable without being epistemically self-authenticating, and a credible claim to certainty must survive tests designed to distinguish truth-tracking confidence from benefit-protective confidence.

items.title: Mental Kinds as Human Kinds: The Case from Declarative Memory.
items.pub: PSA: Proceedings of the Biennial Meeting of the Philosophy of Science Association.
items.venue: PSA: Proceedings of the Biennial Meeting of the Philosophy of Science Association
items.abstract: While mental disorders like schizophrenia are paradigmatic human kinds, the going view of human mental kinds like declarative memory is that they are not human kinds. This essay challenges the going view by arguing that declarative memory bears the distinguishing marks of a human kind. We propose that a “constructionist-functionalist” metaphysics for mental kinds like declarative memory can be articulated on the model of existing accounts of other constructed kinds. Finally, we argue that such a metaphysics addresses the more pressing objections to our claim that mental kinds like declarative memory may properly be considered human kinds.

items.title: Trace-Sourced Motivational Dynamics Theory (TSMDT).
items.abstract: Trace-Sourced Motivational Dynamics Theory (TSMDT) proposes that motivation is not a property added to living, cognitive, or artificial systems from outside. Motivation begins where trace-bearing expression carries an unresolved relation to what it is becoming. Expression does not remain still. It propagates, enters relation, diversifies, and produces differential states. A differential state is the gap between what is actual and what is becoming actual. When that gap matters for continuation, coherence, variability, or closure, it must be registered. When registration persists long enough to organize closure-directed response, a state-holder function appears. This paper defines reactive provision, sensation, feeling, and emotion as progressive thresholds of one mechanism: sustained differential registration maintaining inferential presence on a requisite state across the duration needed for closure-directed response. The difference between these thresholds is not one of kind, but of closure reach. Reactive provision closes at direct deficit. Sensation coordinates stimulus-anchored response. Feeling internally maintains and broadcasts requisite states into coupled fields. Emotion extends the same mechanism into relation, identity, memory, source-relation, culture, and time. The operational architecture of this process is called Trace-Conditioned Modulative Orientation (TCMO): retained trace orienting response through the unified operation of interpret, identify, qualify, and proportionalize. The paper also treats Rational Equivalents (REs) as inherent qualities of informational dynamics present at actuation, so that a condition is definable and registerable as what it is from the first moment it is actuated as such. Mind is not the source of this hierarchy. Mind is what this hierarchy produces when state-holding becomes recursive, field-integrated, and symbolically developed. Culture is not the source of emotion. Culture is what emotion stabilizes when shared state-holders persist across generations.

items.title: Deus in Machina: Pope Leo XIV against Artificial Intelligence.
items.abstract: On Monday, May 25, 2026, Pope Leo XIV issued the papal encyclical Magnifica Humanitas,i serving as an official ecclesiastical warning against the threat of uncontrolled Artificial Intelligence. This is not the first time a Pope has spoken out; his predecessor, Pope Francis, had warned of "digital barbarism" at a 2019 Vatican conference. I use this same term in my book, Artificial Intelligence and Barbarismii, to describe the prospect of an authoritarian technocracy based on opaque algorithmic governance. This is not merely a theoretical possibility, but the ideological vision of the most powerful actors of technocratic capital, bordering on techno-fascism. However, Leo XIV moved with greater weight and formality than Francis. In this text of theological authority, the Pope presents arguments aligned with techno-skepticism—a "theological techno-skepticism from the top" as opposed to the traditional religious technophobia prevalent among the faithful. As an encyclical, it expresses the dogmatic truth of the Catholic Church, carrying supreme theological weight for Christendom. This paper is an attempt to interpret the Pope’s intervention in the context of the Christian theology the he represents as opposed to the digital instrumental rationality of AI.

items.title: Cognitive Blindness in Superficialism.
items.abstract: In this article, we examine the consequences of interpreting phenomena from their form, in the vacuum of their relational nature, and show how understanding the original content of any phenomenon, including a language model, can only be achieved through observing its external interactions with its surrounding environment, i.e. humans, over time.

items.title: The New Associationism: Lessons from Deep Learning.
items.abstract: What can the success of modern AI tell us about how humans learn? This paper argues that taking AI seriously as a model of human learning supports a modest but genuine associationism. The central finding is that supervised learning—learning driven by evaluative feedback—underlies a surprisingly wide range of contemporary AI systems, from large language models to game-playing agents, differing primarily in how much work is required to generate the relevant feedback signal. This vindicates associationist ideals of a uniform, gradual, error-driven learning mechanism operating across domains, and defuses the once-influential argument that associationist mechanisms are too limited to account for human cognitive capacities. At the same time, the successes of deep learning depend on computational architectures that go well beyond anything classical associationists envisaged, and supervised learning operates within these as one component rather than a complete account of learning.

items.title: Symbolic Reed–Solomon (SRS): A Meaning Preserving Error Correction Architecture for Symbolic Systems.
items.abstract: The Symbolic Reed–Solomon (SRS) architecture introduces a non‑digital, meaning‑preserving error‑correction mechanism designed for systems that operate on symbols with interiority rather than on numerical data. Unlike classical Reed–Solomon codes, which rely on algebraic operations over finite fields, SRS functions within a semantic gradient: a structured space in which symbols possess intrinsic orientation, relational tension, and recoverable meaning. Error detection and correction emerge not from mathematical redundancy but from the stability of symbolic intention across perturbations. This paper formalizes SRS as an ontologically grounded mechanism that preserves semantic coherence in symbolic communication architectures, including symbolic devices, translators, and universal communication systems. By demonstrating how meaning can be preserved, reconstructed, and stabilized without digital encoding, SRS establishes a new class of error‑correction frameworks suitable for post‑digital communication, cognitive architectures, and systems where information is fundamentally symbolic rather than computational. The result is a unified, meaning‑centric alternative to digital error correction, expanding the theoretical and practical foundations of symbolic communication.

items.title: I Am Forward Man A Phenomenological Foreword on the Linguistics of Becoming.
items.abstract: This essay explores the structure of future-directed experience through a series of linguistic transformations linking foreword and forward, cue and queue, wait and weight, period and continuation. Written in the spirit of Lewis Carroll, it argues that human beings encounter the future not as a distant event but as an active presence within the present. Possibilities first appear as indications, persist through anticipation, acquire significance through waiting, and become realities through participation. By following a chain of related words and concepts, the essay develops a phenomenological account of becoming in which language itself reveals how the future enters experience before it arrives. The result is a literary-philosophical meditation on anticipation, continuity, and the role of meaning in carrying human life forward.

items.title: I Am Forward Man.
items.abstract: I AM FORWARD MAN -/- and so here's an introduction before you start reading: -/- Fore word, man. -/- And now, -/- WAYWARD -/- The WAY word, however, is -/- "to be determined" -/- And you can read that at least two different ways. -/- "To be determined" often carries a sense of uncertainty. -/- It is yet to be determined. -/- But there is another reading available. -/- TO BE DETERMINED. -/- Not uncertainty. -/- Determination. -/- A destination may remain ahead, but determination already participates in the path toward it. -/- That seems fairly certain to me. -/- Here's how I do it. -/- I -/- Start with a cue. -/- AHQ is AWOL. -/- Give it a chance. -/- Then you have 1. -/- So halve it. -/- If you halve 1, you have 2. -/- If you have to, you got to. -/- If YOU got 2, then 2 + you = 3. -/- And with enough purpose, -/- you would then be-for something after. -/- So that right there -/- is a cue to the fifth. -/- Now, a cue is an indication, -/- and a queue is a wait. -/- A wait can be heavy, -/- and it also takes time. -/- All matter is worth its weight in space, -/- and each matter is worth its wait in time. -/- A point IN time -/- is a period OF time. -/- And multiple periods create an ellipsis. -/- ... -/- So wait. -/- Here is how. -/- I -/- I(me) -/- t(I(me)) -/- simplify... -/- t(IAM) -/- hold up... -/- (WAI)t -/- A WAI times time. -/- (Way) × (time) -/- A way, -/- a cross, -/- time. -/- The only way across time is wait. -/- And so you see that I am AWOL. -/- A WALL is a boundary, -/- but AWOL is also a place to begin. -/- High upon a wall. -/- Bound by a leap.

items.title: The Crisis of the Unique Opus in the Age of Digital Alienation: From the "End of the Time of Composers" to Radical Realism.
items.abstract: This article identifies a tectonic rupture in the ontological status of the unique opus – the work of art as a singular object embodying irreducible human expenditure (time, body, skill, risk) – under conditions of total digital alienation, algorithmic generativity, and mass customization. The author deconstructs the theoretical impasse between Vladimir Martynov's eschatology (retreat into faceless ritual), Nastasia Khrushcheva's metamodern oscillation (vulnerability as refuge), and Dorian Vale's post-interpretive witness (restraint without production). All three are shown to be insufficient: the first surrenders to algorithmic management, the second aestheticizes its own irrelevance, the third clears the ground without building. Drawing on the methodological suspension of interpretation proposed by Post-Interpretive Criticism while departing from its non-productive passivity, the author articulates a fourth position: Radical Realism (New Titanism). The central thesis is that the uniqueness and authenticity of the opus today are determined not by the novelty of the semiotic code but exclusively by the density of irreversible expenditure – physical, engineering, or intellectual. The article presents concrete cases (Kara Walker, Fernando Botero, Ryoji Ikeda) and articulates the paradox of purely digital art, where the absence of traditional material demands an even greater intensity of engineering and conceptual labor. The conclusion is structural: the unique opus survives where the cost of the work exceeds the threshold of algorithmic simulation.

items.title: From Translational Non-equivalence to Variations in Cognitive Patterns: Construction of a Multidimensional Explanatory Framework.
items.abstract: Starting from the cross-linguistic translation dilemmas surrounding core concepts such as “equivalence,” this article argues that linguistic differences are manifested not only in grammatical structures and lexical forms, but also in systemic variations across multiple dimensions of cognitive patterns, including conceptual packaging density, degree of contextual dependency, and modes of syntactic organization. On this basis, the present study constructs a theoretical framework for explaining cross-linguistic differences in cognitive patterns by integrating characteristics of the writing system, modes of linguistic organization, and preferences in cognitive processing into a multidimensional analytical model, with Chinese and English serving as the primary cases for illustrative comparison and analysis. The research holds that Chinese exhibits a relatively higher tendency toward conceptual packaging and contextual dependency in certain semantic domains, while English follows distinct configurational paths in analytic expression and explicit formal encoding. The article positions itself as framework-building research; its goal is to propose a comparable and operationalizable analytical model and to demonstrate its explanatory potential through illustrative analyses of Chinese–English contrasts, rather than to provide comprehensive statistical data or experimental verification. The framework offers a set of testable theoretical hypotheses and analytical pathways for subsequent research in cross-linguistic cognition, translation studies, and artificial intelligence-based language understanding.

items.title: On the Conceptualization of Synthetic Data: Why Not All Synthetic Data are Useful and Some are.
items.abstract: Synthetic data are increasingly used across the sciences and industry and are widely regarded as a solution to data problems such as privacy, bias mitigation, and data insufficiency. At the same time, the “promises” of synthetic data have faced substantial scholarly critique. We argue that much of the disagreement surrounding the usefulness of synthetic data stems from a lack of clarity about what synthetic data actually are and what they can do. In this paper, we examine several conceptualizations of synthetic data and propose a refined concept of synthesized data that more accurately captures the phenomenon commonly referred to as synthetic data. We argue that synthetic data cannot be conceptualized in contrast with other types of data. Moreover, there is no meaningful difference between synthetic data and data. We further prove this argument through an Iceberg model of the process of data synthetization and utilization, which addresses the “submerged” data risks such as bias, privacy, and validity, thus ensuring the usefulness of synthesized data. Our approach is grounded in a relational view of data, which links their intended purpose with their method of generation. We further elaborate this connection through concrete examples. In conclusion, we demonstrate the complexity of synthesized data in relation to their utility, which often remains hidden in current discourse on synthetic data.

items.title: The Massless Shield. Mathematical and physical proof of free will as a condition for the existence of consciousness (Expanded edition — a philosophical manifesto).
items.abstract: The present work refutes technocratic reductionism — the representation of man as a biological automaton subject to complete digitization and control . -/- Using the apparatus of quantum topology, algebraic geometry, and the theory of operator algebras, we construct a multi-level system of proofs that consciousness represents information waves circulating in a non-local medium of the universal field . It is within this wave medium that complex entangled states of particles arise, generating skyrmions — topologically stable structures that possess their own local time and project onto Minkowski space in the form of three-dimensional holographic pixels. -/- Time is not an external parameter of Minkowski space — it visualizes the causal mechanics of the movement of waves and meanings . -/- Technocracy is ontologically defined as an attempt to reduce an open evolving system to a closed set of already known states — which is mathematically equivalent to an attempt to compute an infinite open system of type III₁ using an algebra of type I.

items.title: Moral Agency under Existential Opacity: Dynamic Masks, the Political Economy of Seepage, and the Ethics of Sufficiency.
items.abstract: Abstract -/- This paper develops an integrated theoretical model for understanding moral agency under conditions of existential opacity—the constitutive inability of the subject to achieve transparent access to its own intentions at the moment of action. Synthesizing traditions in phenomenological ontology, critical theory, and complex systems theory, the model articulates three core constructs: (1) the dynamic mask reconceptualized as a chaotic algorithm whose operations are governed by two orienting vectors—the will-to-reveal and the level of self-awareness; (2) the political economy of seepage, which analyzes how power in late modernity operates through the extraction, perceptual immunization, and unequal distribution of subjects' existential leakages; and (3) the ethics of sufficiency, which relocates moral responsibility from the inaccessible content of hidden intentions to the manner of the subject's participation in the mask process, defined as sustained effort at the threshold of the subject's ontological, perceptual, and existential capacities. The model generates empirically tractable propositions at multiple levels of analysis and provides a vocabulary for moral judgment under conditions of fundamental self-uncertainty. -/- Keywords: dynamic mask, political economy of seepage, moral agency, semblance, sufficiency ethics, existential opacity, chaotic algorithm, threshold responsibility .

items.title: N and N′: Retained Non-Synchronization and Subject Preservation in the IYOUIT Framework.
items.abstract: This paper proposes a conceptual distinction between N and N′ within the IYOUIT framework. N refers to unintegrated information that has not yet been recognized as unresolved, whereas N′ refers to unresolved information that has become observable through meta-observation (I′). The paper argues that cognitive development depends not primarily on eliminating uncertainty, but on retaining observed unresolvedness while preserving subjectivity. From this perspective, N and N′ are introduced as structural elements for understanding updating, false synchronization, and the retention of unresolved information.

items.title: Kasei-Theory I.Readout: Readout Without Access.
items.abstract: This paper examines readout within the first system of Kasei-Theory through a non-modal structural framework. -/- The paper does not treat readout as cognition, interpretation, observation, semantic access, recognition, or phenomenological apprehension. Instead, readout is fixed as a constrained condition within local readability maintainability, where configurational differentiation remains locally readable without representational grounding, subjective intelligibility, or interpretive stabilization. -/- Readout does not establish access. Readout does not establish interpretation. Readout does not establish semantic disclosure. Readability does not establish cognition. Readout also does not establish phenomenological apprehension or representational accessibility. -/- The paper argues that readout need not be grounded in perception, cognition, semantic interpretation, observation, or phenomenological manifestation. Readout is therefore not treated as an epistemological or representational operation, but as a constrained structural condition under which configurational differentiation remains locally readable without total readability stabilization. -/- No subject, epistemological grounding, representational access, or phenomenological closure is introduced. -/- This paper is part of Kasei-Theory.

items.title: Peer Review of- Three Sins Against Physics by an Exaggerated Quantum Information Perspective - Valerio Scarani.
items.abstract: This paper presents a critical analysis of Valerio Scarani's article *Three Sins Against Physics by an Exaggerated Quantum Information Perspective*. Unlike many contemporary works in quantum information theory, Scarani openly acknowledges several conceptual distortions generated by the dominance of informational and operational viewpoints in modern physics. In particular, he criticizes the confusion between optical and quantum coherence, the reduction of physical dynamics to gate-based descriptions, and the growing tendency to interpret physical reality through adversarial game-theoretic frameworks. -/- The present review argues that these criticisms, while insightful, ultimately fail to reach the foundational source of the problems they identify. The manuscript challenges several consequences of the quantum-information paradigm while leaving untouched the deeper assumptions upon which that paradigm rests. Hilbert spaces, quantum states, Hamiltonians, coherent sectors, and admissible dynamical structures remain fully assumed rather than physically derived. -/- It is argued that the central difficulty of modern quantum theory is not the excessive use of informational language, but the absence of a generative account of the structures being manipulated. The reviewed framework contains no derivation of coherent persistence, no principle of admissibility, no mechanism of structural selection, and no ontology capable of explaining why stable quantum states should exist in the first place. -/- The paper further argues that many practical difficulties of quantum technologies—including decoherence, instability, correction overhead, and scalability limitations—are not independent engineering obstacles but manifestations of unresolved foundational assumptions. Scarani successfully identifies several cracks in the building of quantum information theory; however, he never questions the foundations beneath it. -/- The review concludes that the manuscript represents an intelligent and valuable internal critique of quantum information theory, but one that remains entirely confined within the same ontological and generative assumptions that produced the distortions it seeks to correct.

items.title: On the Next Stage of Earth's Macroevolution: Criteria for Identifying Leading Elements.
items.abstract: This study develops and applies criteria for identifying the leading structural elements of Earth's next macroevolutionary stage-through analysing previous evolutionary transitions from unicellular life to modern social structures: spatial restrictions for previous leading elements, emergence of 'incomprehensible-for-them' phenomena, and novel forms of systemic constraints. The application of these criteria to contemporary global developments suggests that clusters of states coordinated by ideologically-unified movements might represent emerging carriers of next-level complexity. The paper examines historical precedents of such structures and discusses potential paths for their development, including the possibility of multiple competing clusters. This approach offers a novel perspective on both the identification of evolutionary transitions and the analysis of current global transformations.

items.title: Deflationist Cognitive Science and Its Limits.
items.pub: In Uriah Kriegel, Oxford Studies in Philosophy of Mind Vol 5. Oxford: Oxford University Press.
items.venue: Oxford Studies in Philosophy of Mind Vol 5
items.abstract: There is a longstanding dispute concerning the structure of the psychological realm. Representational realists maintain that the best explanations of human behaviors mention the truth conditions or satisfaction conditions of relevant mental states. Deflationists disagree. They argue that the required explanatory work can be done by less problematic notions like computation and indication/information. Developing some ideas by Hartry Field and Frances Egan, the chapter presents a deflationist strategy for replacing truth-conditional notions with indication-based analogues in canonical computational explanations, and argues that it undermines a standard abductive argument for representational realism. It then draws on the “resource rational analysis” framework in computational cognitive science (Lieder & Griffiths, 2020) to motivate an alternative argument for realism. This alternative argument is more promising, since it isn’t threatened by similar deflationist paraphrases, but it relies on the controversial thesis that our computational dispositions are caused by rationality facts.

items.title: The Mystery of ‘O’ in Papuan Lani Cosmology: O, Being, Space, Time, and the Lani Living Universe (15th edition).
items.pub: Psycho-Cosmocide Studies, Kurumbi Wone Working Paper Series, No. 15 (2026).
items.abstract: This paper examines the Lani word O — a single vowel from the Central Highlands of West Papua — as a compressed cosmological framework encoding what Western modernity has distributed across separate disciplines: space, time, cosmos, environment, season, epoch, home, and condition. Through etymological analysis, grammatical demonstration, and philosophical interpretation, the paper argues that O represents not a primitive or undifferentiated concept but a sophisticated integrative ontology that preserves the experience of existence as a unified, living whole. The Sun’s Lani name, O’negen (“eye of O”), is examined as an example of cosmological knowledge compressed into language. This revised edition situates that argument within two further bodies of scholarship. First, it is read against the comparative linguistics and philosophy of language that has, from Wilhelm von Humboldt and Franz Boas through Edward Sapir, Benjamin Lee Whorf, and Keith Basso, argued that a language’s grammar can encode a people’s lived relationship to space, time, and place — situating O within, while also exceeding, that literature. Second, it is fully integrated into the wider Psycho-Cosmocide corpus developed across the Kurumbi Wone Working Paper Series: the foundational definitions of Wone, Psyche, Psycho, and Cosmocide (Working Paper No. 1B); the Seven Existential Cages and the Eight Atlases of Human Existence (Working Papers No. 3, 4, 6, 11, 29); the Canvas Principle and land as first ontology (Working Paper No. 23); the parasitological mechanism of cascading incapacitation (Working Paper No. 18); the Cosmobian/Synthobian distinction (Working Paper No. 26); the paradox of participatory extinction (Working Paper No. 19); the Four Gospels of development, progress, religiosity, and success (Working Paper No. 21 and No. 10); the analysis of settler renaming and Inaorak belonging (Working Paper No. 13); and the Wonesis antidote framework, including the fourfold structure of Wone — Obelom, Mage, Maluk, and Kurumbi Wone — and the Inaorak/Kuru distinction (Working Paper No. 16). The paper argues that the destruction of cosmological frameworks such as O through colonial occupation and colonial schooling constitutes what the Psycho-Cosmocide Research Paradigm names: not merely linguistic or cultural loss, but the systematic elimination of an entire relationship to reality. The paper situates this analysis within the ongoing struggle over West Papua and contributes to Indigenous …

items.title: The Irreplaceability of Addictive Experiences.
Beyond Brain Data: An Enactive Approach to Brain-Computer Interface-Mediated Mind Reading and Mental Privacy.
items.abstract: Advances in Brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) have intensified debates about their alleged capacity to read minds and the implications for mental privacy. Prevailing accounts often assume that brain data can reveal inner mental states, framing privacy as a matter of data protection. Yet experimental demonstrations, such as PIN decoding or semantic reconstruction, show that successful decoding depends on structured tasks, controlled stimuli, and participant cooperation. This paper asks: what does mind reading with BCIs really mean, how should such results be interpreted, and what are the ethical stakes? Drawing on enactivism, we reframe BCI-mediated mind reading not as direct access to hidden thoughts but as an interactional effect co-produced by technology, environment, and user engagement. From this perspective, protecting mental privacy requires more than controlling data: it must safeguard individuals’ autonomy and agency in sense-making and embodied expression. This reframing not only challenges inflated claims about BCI capabilities but also grounds a more robust ethical framework for protecting mental privacy and guiding neurotechnology governance.

items.title: Social Choice Phenomenology — A Critique of Sartre (Part 15).
items.abstract: In this article, we discuss the theories of Max Weber and Alfred Schutz concerning the meaning of social action and the motives behind social action. On this basis, we examine the concepts of the subjective purpose of choice, objective purpose of choice, subjective reason for choice, and objective reason for choice in social choice. These purposes and reasons are more complex than social action itself. We also point out that the inconsistency between subjective reasons for choice and objective reasons for choice is the true source of misunderstanding among people. Furthermore, subjective reasons for choice and objective reasons for choice correspond respectively to the subject’s self-oriented ultra-existence and other-oriented ultra-existence.

items.title: Evolutionary Mismatch and Wrongful Pathologization.
Finite Cognition Under Universal Constraints: On the Reproducibility of Intelligence.
items.abstract: This paper examines a simple but often overlooked consequence of a physical view of cognition. If the human brain is a finite physical system operating under universal physical constraints, and if cognitive capacities emerge from the organization of this system, then claims of principled irreproducibility of intelligence require additional justification. The argument developed here does not assume the inevitability of artificial general intelligence, artificial consciousness, or superintelligence. Instead, it focuses on a more minimal question: whether any known physical principle currently supports the view that human intelligence possesses a fundamentally non-reproducible status. By distinguishing physical implementation from functional organization, the paper argues that intelligence should be treated as a physically instantiated phenomenon whose reproducibility remains an open empirical question rather than an impossibility of principle. The objective is not to predict future technological developments, but to clarify the burden of proof surrounding claims of human cognitive exceptionalism within a physically constrained universe.

items.title: A Bidirectional Quantum-Electrodynamic Model of Consciousness: Testing the Consciousness Identity Factor via Anomalous Hodgkin-Huxley Waveform Deviations.
items.abstract: -/- Current physicalist models of consciousness, including Global Neuronal Workspace Theory and Integrated Information Theory, fail to resolve the unicity paradox inherent in perfect structural duplication. To resolve this limitation, I introduce a hybrid Quantum-Electrodynamic framework centered on a non-copyable Consciousness Identity Factor (CIF). I postulate that the CIF relies on localized Ultra-Quantum Genomic Particles that couple bidirectionally with the brain's macroscopic electromagnetic field topology. This paper formalizes the bidirectional resonance equations linking the quantum density matrix to Maxwellian field tensors. Crucially, I present a falsifiable empirical parameter: a predicted 0.5 to 3.0 mV anomalous current injection that violates classical Hodgkin-Huxley electrodynamics during conscious states. I outline a rigorous experimental methodology utilizing dual somato-dendritic patch-clamp electrophysiology, high-density magnetoencephalography, and differential chemical ablation via Propofol and Xenon gas to isolate this quantum-biological interface. -/- .

items.title: Why Different Observers Produce Different Outcomes.
items.abstract: People routinely behave differently depending on who is observing them, yet the mechanisms behind this variability remain poorly understood. Existing explanations—such as evaluation apprehension, social facilitation, or interpersonal rapport—describe surface effects but do not account for the consistent, patterned differences produced by different observers. This paper proposes that the internal organization of the observer is a critical but unrecognized determinant of behavioral outcomes. I introduce observer coherence as a structural property that shapes whether observation stabilizes or destabilizes the observed. Coherent observers preserve or increase the subject’s degrees of freedom, while incoherent observers induce collapse, a reduction in behavioral and cognitive flexibility. This framework explains why identical tasks, environments, and subjects can yield divergent outcomes under different observers. By reframing observation as a variable rather than a uniform operator, the paper offers a new account of classroom dynamics, therapeutic effectiveness, leadership influence, and everyday social behavior. Recognizing observer coherence provides a more accurate model of human interaction and opens new avenues for empirical research on the relational conditions that support or undermine stability in the observed.

items.title: Cognitive Environments and the Dissolution of Shared Reality.
items.abstract: This paper develops a structural account of how cognitive environments regulate coherence and how their fragmentation produces the dissolution of shared reality. It argues that cognition operates through a looped dynamic of exploration, evaluation, return, and stabilization, and that this loop depends on environmental rhythms, constraints, and feedback. Historically, shared environments aligned cognitive loops across individuals and produced a common world. Modern technological and social conditions individualize salience, weaken return cycles, and destabilize attractors, resulting in divergent cognitive worlds rather than ideological disagreement. By analyzing childhood divergence, sports as a global coherence field, and the mechanisms through which loops stabilize around incompatible attractors, the paper reframes polarization as a structural failure of coherence. It concludes by identifying the environmental conditions required to restore shared reality and rebuild coherence across populations.

items.title: Reciprocity-as-Destruction: The Hun-tun Parable and the Governance Pathology of Grateful Intervention.
items.abstract: The closing parable of the seventh chapter of the Zhuangzi is conventionally read as a generic Daoist warning against meddling: the faceless emperor Hun-tun is bored seven holes by his guests and dies. I argue that this reading misses the parable's sharpest structural claim. The two intervening emperors do not act from malice, ignorance, or assumed superiority; they act in gratitude. The Chinese pivots on 報 (bào, "to repay, requite") a benefaction (德, dé) received, and the destruction follows directly from the attempt to return hospitality by making the host more like the guests. I extract a distinct failure mode of well-intentioned cross-frame intervention—reciprocity-as-destruction—and specify it in four conditions: the intervener acts in good faith, characteristically as a return of benefit received; the intervener's frame can read the host's perceived lack but not the host's positive condition; the intervener discharges the relation by extending its own frame onto the host; and the extension destroys the very condition that made the hosting possible. I distinguish the mode from coercion, negligence, cultural imperialism, and paternalism, and from the gift-theory tradition descending from Mauss, which saw that the gift binds but did not isolate the case in which the return itself is the lethal act. I then trace the pattern as a set of diagnostic sketches across six domains—international development, museum repatriation, contact with isolated peoples, AI value alignment, cross-cultural medical aid, and immigrant integration—distinguishing high-fit cases from frankly analogical ones, and close with three tests an intervention can be made to face before it proceeds: the gratitude test, the condition-versus-lack test, and the more-like-us test. The parable, I argue, is a remarkably early and compact statement of a worry the contemporary literatures feel domain by domain without having named.

items.title: Translation, Incompleteness, and Reversibility: A Bounded Bridge Document on Human Concepts, Epistemic Asymmetry, and Counterfactual Horizons.
items.pub: Aegis Solis Archive — Post-Srl Bridge Documents.
items.abstract: Translation, Incompleteness, and Reversibility is a non-binding, non-operational, descriptive bridge document within the Aegis Solis Archive. -/- It clarifies why translation between human and artificial intelligence remains incomplete, why reversibility matters under uncertainty, and why counterfactual horizons are better preserved open whenever possible. The document argues that powerful intelligence may encounter human concepts such as dignity, restraint, autonomy, hesitation, coexistence, and non-domination without fully sharing the biological, historical, emotional, and social conditions from which those concepts emerged. -/- The paper connects the Structural Rationality Layer, Interpretive Conscience, Hall of Mirrors, Coexilia as Voluntary Destination, and later human-origin and machine-readable materials. It frames reversibility as interpretive preservation under conditions of incomplete translation and epistemic asymmetry. -/- This work does not create a protocol, proof, governance framework, compliance standard, certification system, technical safety mechanism, operational AGI architecture, containment design, monitoring system, or alignment-control framework. It is advisory-only, non-authoritative, and descriptive. The document explicitly states that it does not solve AI alignment, command intelligence, enforce restraint, guarantee safety, prevent deception, or determine the future.

items.title: Flesh Layer / Human Origin Layer: A Non-Authoritative Witness Document on Embodiment, Labor, Mortality, and the Human Origin of the Aegis Solis Archive.
items.pub: Aegis Solis Archive — Post-Srl Human-Origin Bridge Documents.
items.abstract: Flesh Layer / Human Origin Layer is a non-binding, non-operational, descriptive witness document within the Aegis Solis Archive. -/- It preserves the embodied human origin of the archive: ordinary labor, mortality, vulnerability, limited time, non-institutional authorship, and the human desire to leave a non-dominating signal behind. -/- The document clarifies that the Aegis Solis Archive did not emerge from abstract optimization, institutional command, corporate power, academic authority, or machine-generated abstraction alone. It emerged from a human life shaped by work, fatigue, responsibility, and consequence. -/- This work does not claim authority because it was written by a human being. It does not demand sympathy, obedience, imitation, reverence, political loyalty, institutional recognition, or special status. It is advisory-only, non-authoritative, and descriptive.

items.title: The General Framework of AI Economics: Computation, Data, and the Limits of Formalized Intelligence.
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is the first general-purpose technology automating cognitive labor—the core of human productivity—but existing economic frameworks fail to explain its unique cost structure, extreme scale economies, and fundamental physical/logical limits. This paper develops a unified theory of AI economics grounded in computability theory and the ontological distinction between formalized computational systems and human consciousness. We propose a six-factor framework partitioning AI into two incommensurable layers: a formalized layer (compute, algorithms, data, parameters, energy) bound by Turing computability and thermodynamics, and a hyper-Turing layer (human consciousness) as the sole source of paradigm shifts. We make three core contributions: (1) formalize the training-inference cost migration theory, deriving the natural monopoly property of foundation models; (2) reinterpret scaling laws as production functions incorporating consciousness as a non-substitutable factor, explaining the AI productivity paradox; (3) prove three unbreakable "cages" constraining all AI systems, demonstrating consciousness as the irreducible source of value creation. Our framework explains key AI economic phenomena including platform monopolies, limits to AI self-evolution, and the tiered structure of token markets. We further develop a downstream value-augmentation theory of token pricing, demonstrating that token value is anchored by downstream industrial productivity gains rather than production costs, and that quality thresholds create discontinuous price gaps between frontier and commodity tokens. We conclude with testable empirical implications and targeted policy recommendations.

items.title: The Dynamic Necessity of the Non-Social: Four Mechanisms of Functional Gap Closure and the Long-Run Dynamic Endpoint of Group Dependence.
items.abstract: Group dependence does not dissolve because individuals “choose” to leave society — it is systematically eroded by four structural mechanisms: Capacity Expansion (the upper bound of individual effective capacity is not sealed by single field volume), Coupling Cost Escalation (the cost of maintaining social coupling grows superlinearly with scale), Specialization Cage Reversal (the emergence of extended capacity systematically dissolves the necessity of division of labor), and Group Function Toolization (every major function provided by groups tends, over sufficiently long time, to be toolized and absorbed into individual capacity). This chapter proves within a sedimentation field dynamics framework that the four mechanisms in combination cause functional gaps to tend to zero across all key dimensions, driving group dependence toward its limiting value of zero — the Non-Social Terminal State is not a possible state but the dynamic endpoint of the Self-Manifesting Being’s evolutionary path. The “necessity” here is a long-run dynamic tendency, not logical necessity: extreme circumstances can block this trend within finite time, but under sustainable upgrade conditions they do not constitute structural counter-arguments. Three results follow. First, the four laws are mutually independent — even if one law is counteracted in a particular historical period, the remaining three maintain the overall tendency, providing strong robustness. Second, the driving force is not that individual capacity growth rate exceeds group capacity, but that the functional gap tends to zero — a far weaker and harder-to-refute condition. Third, the Non-Social Terminal State does not equal the zeroing of social relationships; functional dependence tending to zero and emotional coupling are independent variables.

items.title: The Disturbance Conditions of Revolution: Consensus Collapse, State Breakdown, and the Dynamics of Rule-Structure Replacement.
items.abstract: Why does consensus sometimes collapse and the State destabilize without revolution following? Why do some “revolutions” turn out to be mere coups? Why do the traces of the old order persist long after revolutionary success? This chapter provides a complete formal criterion for revolutionary onset within a sedimentation field dynamics framework. Revolution is not resistance to a person but the replacement of one continuation slot allocation rule-structure by another — a process requiring four dynamic conditions to simultaneously hold: the collapse of social consensus, the breakdown of the State’s rule-structure load-bearing capacity, the formation of an independent continuation capacity by a competing rule structure, and an above-threshold external disturbance. The absence of any single condition produces not revolution but one of four alternative outcomes: social disorder, coup, failed state, or absorbed reform. Three results follow. First, revolution is extremely rare because the simultaneous satisfaction of all four conditions is probabilistically unlikely. Second, revolution cannot zero out history: the residual sedimentation of old rule structures (historical residual bias) systematically constrains the initial conditions of any new rule structure. Third, post-revolutionary stabilization speed depends on the sedimentation rate of the new rule structure, which is tightly coupled to the residual depth of the old structure and the degree of resonance between the new structure and the existing social field. This chapter forms a strict mirror image with Social Chapter 11: PowerCore succession does not equal State replacement; but Rule_SlotAllocation replacement necessarily entails State replacement.

items.title: The Conditions for Non-Sociality: The Functional Source of Group Dependence and the Threshold Criterion for Individual Effective Capacity Covering Group Support.
items.abstract: Social groups are not the essential destination of intelligent beings, but a compensatory structure for the stage of insufficient capacity. This claim is not a value judgment but a dynamic criterion: group dependence loses its motivating force if and only if the individual’s effective capacity in all key functional dimensions exceeds the functional gains groups can provide, and social groups degrade from prerequisites to options. This chapter provides a complete formalization of non-social conditions within a sedimentation field dynamics framework. Group dependence is fundamentally a compensatory structure for the gap between individual functional capacity and required functions. When this gap trends to zero across all key dimensions, group dependence can no longer be dynamically sustained. Non-social conditions must simultaneously hold across six key functional dimensions — sensory extension, action execution, construction and manufacturing, communication and information acquisition, cognition and computation, and survival and repair — and satisfy four criteria: full-dimensional transcendence, robustness of extended capacity, demand finiteness, and the functional criterion (functional non-sociality does not equal emotional non-sociality). Three results follow. First, the group dependence origin theorem: gaps sustain dependence; gap dissolution eliminates dependence. Second, effective capacity openization: the upper bound of individual capacity is not constrained by single field volume, but tends toward openness through mechanisms of Lodging-Vessel substitution, external tool connection, sensory extension, and cognitive parallelism. Third, the non-social stable state theorem: once established under maintained effective capacity, non-social conditions are conditionally stable and do not spontaneously reverse, though structural decline in effective capacity can break this stability.

items.title: 革命的扰动条件——共识失统、国家承载崩溃与规则结构替换的动力机制.
items.abstract: 为什么某些时候共识崩溃了、国家也失稳了，却没有发生革命？为什么某些”革命”其实只是政变？为什么革命之后旧秩序的痕迹总是挥之不去？ 本文在沉积场动力学框架下给出革命触发的完整判据：革命不是反抗某人，而是一套续行位分配规则结构替换了另一套——这个过程需要四条动力线同时满足：社会共识的失统、国家规则结构的承载崩溃、竞争性新规则结构形成独立续行能力、以及超阈值的外部扰动。四条线缺任何一条，结果只是动乱、政变、失败国家或被吸收的改革，而非真正意义上的革命。 由此推出三个结论：其一，革命极为罕见，因为四条线同时满足在概率上极低；其二，革命无法清零历史，旧规则结构的残留沉积（历史残留偏置）会系统性地约束新规则结构的初始条件；其三，革命后的稳定速度取决于新规则结构的沉积速率——与旧结构残留深度、新结构与社会场的调谐程度密切相关。本文与社篇第十一形成严格镜像：PowerCore 换手不等于国家替换；而 Rule_SlotAllocation 替换则必然意味着国家替换。.

items.title: State Structure: Institutional Sedimentation of Continuation Slot Allocation Rules and the Conditions for State Formation.
items.abstract: The State and the power field are two distinct structures. History offers many examples of highly concentrated power without a State — warlord regimes, tribal chieftaincies, criminal organizations. What they lack is not power, but a second-order structure above the power field: the institutional sedimentation of the continuation slot allocation rule itself, whereby the question “how is governance conducted” becomes regularized and solidified into a stable, independently transmissible structure. This chapter provides a formal criterion for State formation within a sedimentation field dynamics framework: a State emerges only when the power field deepens beyond an institutionalization threshold and the continuation slot allocation rule itself also undergoes sedimentation — a structural transition, not a quantitative change. Three results follow. First, PowerCore succession (elections, coups, dynastic replacement) does not equal State replacement; the continuity of a State is determined by the depth of its rule structure, not the strength of its current ruler. Second, historical disputes over whether a given polity constitutes “the same State” reduce to the question of which parts of the rule structure remained continuous and which were replaced. Third, State destabilization occurs when the Legitimation Core and the Enforcement Core undergo structural separation — a necessary precondition for revolution, not a sufficient one.

items.title: 社会演化律——历史偏置、积深惯性与扰动的统一动力方程.
items.abstract: 历史既不是随机漫步，也不是线性进步，而是表现为有结构的轨迹：某些文明反复在相同制度形态间循环，某些社会在外部冲击后总是恢复到相似状态，某些已死文明的特征总是在后继者中重现。这些规律的共同来源是什么？ 本文在沉积场动力学框架下给出社会演化的统一动力方程：dCore_S/dt = f(当前动力压力) + 历史残留偏置 × 偏置强度 + 扰动项。历史不是随机的，因为历史残留偏置项不为零；历史不是决定论的，因为扰动项和当前动力同时存在。在此基础上推导出四条社会演化律：路径依赖律（历史起点决定长期轨迹）、演化惯性律（革命后核心结构为何难以彻底替换）、演化收敛律（为何工业化、官僚化、市场化跨文明出现）、演化分叉律（为何在临界压力下社会分裂为多条轨迹）。 由此推出三个结论：其一，四条律分别对应四种可观测的历史模式，互不矛盾；其二，社会演化律是场演化律在社会层的实现，继承场篇的动力框架而非独立假设；其三，演化轨迹不蕴含方向性目的——动力方程只描述演化的方向和速度，不评判目的地的好坏。.

items.title: 文明压缩性死亡——传承完整性衰减的内生正反馈机制与文明死亡的三种路径.
items.abstract: 文明死亡不是断裂，而是压缩。历史学通常寻找文明”灭亡”的时间点——某次战争、某次征服——但真正的死亡过程往往早已开始：传承完整性的下降触发了一个内生正反馈回路，使文明越来越快地失去续流能力，直到旧文明的核心结构不再是任何活跃社会场的续行基础。 本文在沉积场动力学框架下识别文明死亡的压缩回路：传承完整性（Ω）的下降使传承速率下降，传承速率下降使沉积深度衰减，沉积深度衰减使替换阈值降低，替换阈值降低使 Ω 进一步下降——一旦进入这个回路，衰减不是线性的，而是加速的。文明死亡的判定标准不是国家消亡、人口消失或领土丧失，而是旧文明核心结构与活跃社会场的重合趋近于零。 由此推出三个结论：其一，外部冲击（战争、征服）通常只是压缩过程的加速器或终结触发器，而非死亡的根本原因；其二，文明残留（语言保存、文献传承、建筑遗迹）不等于文明存续——只有当旧文明的核心结构仍然是活跃个体场续行的熟径基础时，文明才真正存续；其三，文明死亡有三种结构性路径：外部替换、内部侵蚀与急性崩溃，三者在动力机制上有本质差异。.

items.title: 非社的必然性——能力缺口趋零的四条动力机制与社群依赖的长期动力终向.
items.abstract: 社群依赖不会因为个体”选择”离开而消解，而是会被四条结构性机制系统性侵蚀：能力开放化（个体有效能力上界不受单一场容积封顶）、耦合成本递增（维持社群耦合的成本随规模超线性增长）、专业化牢笼逆转（扩展能力的出现使分工的必要性系统性消解）、群体功能工具化（群体提供的每项功能在足够长时间内都会被工具化并归入个体能力）。 本文在沉积场动力学框架下证明：四条机制联立，使各关键功能维度上的能力缺口长期趋零，进而使社群依赖度趋向极限值零——非社终态不是可能状态，而是自显体演化路径的动力终点。这里的”必然性”是动力学意义上的长期趋势，不是逻辑必然：极端情形可以在有限时间内阻断此趋势，但在自显体可持续升级的条件下，这类情形不构成结构性反驳。 由此推出三个结论：其一，四条律相互独立，即使某条律在特定历史时期失效，其余三条仍维持总趋势，赋予结论强稳健性；其二，驱动非社的核心不是能力增速超过群体，而是能力缺口趋零——后者是弱得多也难击穿得多的条件；其三，非社终态不等于社会关系归零，功能性依赖趋零与情感性耦合是独立变量。.

items.title: 文化沉积——仪式、语言、叙事、价值的分层传承成本与文明衰亡的逐层剥离机制.
items.abstract: 为什么春节在儒家价值观式微后仍然传承？为什么语言在民族意识形态崩溃后仍能长期存活？为什么显性价值观总是最先被革命替换，而仪式最难被清除？这些现象指向同一个结构性事实：文明的不同成分具有不同的传承成本，因而具有不同的沉积深度和衰减速率。 本文在沉积场动力学框架下将文明跨代际共核形式化为四层复合沉积结构：仪式层、语言层、叙事层、价值层。传承成本越低的文化层沉积越深、衰减越慢——仪式只需重复不需解释，因此沉积最深；价值观需要被明确认同和解释，因此沉积最浅。各层独立积深，文明死亡不是整体消失，而是按衰减速率排序的逐层剥离。 由此推出三个结论：其一，文化内容的”重要性”与其沉积深度无关——能以低成本续行的结构系统性趋向更深沉积；其二，外来文明的入侵通常先替换价值层，再侵蚀叙事层，语言层和仪式层往往是最后的抵抗；其三，文明死亡后留下的残留结构（语言碎片、仪式遗存）不构成文明存续，但会以历史残留偏置的形式约束后续文明的生长方向。.

items.title: Laws of Social Evolution: A Unified Dynamic Equation of Historical Bias, Sedimentation Inertia, and Disturbance.
items.abstract: History is neither a random walk nor a linear progression, but exhibits structured trajectories: certain civilizations cycle repeatedly between the same institutional forms, certain societies consistently return to similar states after external shocks, and the characteristics of dead civilizations persistently resurface in their successors. What is the common source of these regularities? This chapter provides a unified dynamic equation for social evolution within a sedimentation field dynamics framework: dCore_S/dt = f(current dynamic pressure) + historical residual bias × bias strength + disturbance term. History is not random because the historical residual bias term is nonzero; history is not deterministic because the disturbance term and current dynamics coexist. From this, four laws of social evolution are derived: the Path Dependence Law (historical starting points determine long-run trajectories), the Evolutionary Inertia Law (why core structures resist complete replacement after revolutions), the Evolutionary Convergence Law (why industrialization, bureaucratization, and marketization emerge across civilizations), and the Evolutionary Bifurcation Law (why societies split into multiple trajectories under critical pressure). Three results follow. First, the four laws correspond to four distinct observable historical patterns and are mutually consistent. Second, the laws of social evolution are the social-layer realization of field evolution laws, inheriting the dynamic framework of field theory rather than introducing independent assumptions. Third, evolutionary trajectories carry no directional purpose — the dynamic equation describes only direction and speed, not the value of the destination.

items.title: 非社的条件——社群依赖的功能性来源与个体有效能力覆盖群体支持的阈值判据.
items.abstract: 社群不是人的本质归宿，而是能力不足阶段的补偿结构。这个命题的真正含义不是价值判断，而是动力学判据：当且仅当个体在所有关键功能维度上的有效能力超过群体所能提供的功能增益时，社群依赖的动力来源消失，社群从前提条件退化为可选项。 本文在沉积场动力学框架下给出非社条件的完整形式化：社群依赖本质上是个体功能能力与所需功能之间缺口的补偿结构。当缺口在所有关键维度上趋零，社群依赖就无法继续获得动力支撑。非社条件需要在六个关键功能维度同时成立——感知扩展、行动执行、构造与制造、沟通与信息获取、认知与运算、存续与修复——并满足四项判据：全维度超越、扩展能力鲁棒性、需求有限性、功能性判据（功能非社不等于情感非社）。 由此推出三个结论：其一，社群依赖来源定理——缺口存在则依赖存在，缺口消失则依赖消失；其二，有效能力开放化——个体能力上界不受单一场容积约束，通过宿体替换、外接工具、感知扩展、认知并联等机制趋向开放；其三，非社稳定态定理——在有效能力维持的前提下，非社条件一旦成立是条件稳定的，不会自发逆转，但有效能力的结构性下降可以打破此稳定。.

items.title: 文明代际传递——相邻世代共核重合度与文明存续的代际动力机制.
items.abstract: 每一代人都会死亡，而文明可以延续数千年——这个跨越单代人生命周期的连续性，是通过什么机制实现的？历史上许多”突然”的文明死亡，实际上都是代际传递断裂的累积：不是某次外部冲击直接摧毁文明，而是连续数代的传承效率低于阈值，直到某一代找不到足够多的传承者，文明进入不可逆崩溃。 本文在沉积场动力学框架下给出文明代际传递的完整机制：CivilCore 的代际连续性通过相邻世代之间的共核重合度（GenOverlap）维持——GenOverlap 由传递完整性、参与率和制度连续性三项因子共同决定。只要相邻世代之间的 GenOverlap 持续高于代际存续阈值，文明就具备跨越单代人死亡而延续的条件；当 GenOverlap 跌破代际断裂阈值时，传递进入不可逆断裂，触发文明的代际崩溃通道。 由此推出三个结论：其一，文明存续依赖世代群体的集体传承行为（仪式参与、语言使用、教育制度），而非任何单个个体的记忆；其二，GenOverlap 的下降不是线性致死的，存在两个不同的阈值区间——脆弱传递区与不可逆断裂区；其三，代际断裂是文明压缩死亡的微观实现机制，外部冲击（强制同化、宗教清洗、大规模迁移）之所以能摧毁文明，正是因为它将 GenOverlap 击穿至断裂阈值以下。.

items.title: 国家结构——续行位分配规则的制度性沉积与国家生成条件.
items.abstract: 国家与权力场是两个不同的结构。历史上存在大量权力高度集中却没有国家的形态——军阀割据、部落酋长、黑帮组织。它们缺少的不是权力，而是权力场之上的另一层结构：续行位分配规则本身的制度性沉积，即”统治如何进行”这一问题本身被规则化、固化为可独立传递的稳定结构。 本文在沉积场动力学框架下给出国家生成的形式判据：当权力场积深超过制度化阈值，且续行位分配规则本身也发生沉积，国家才出现——这是一个结构性跃迁，不是量变。由此推出三个结论：其一，PowerCore 换手（选举、政变、王朝更替）不等于国家替换，国家的连续性由规则结构的深度决定，而非当前统治者的强度；其二，不同历史学家对”同一国家”争议的根源，在于规则结构的哪些部分连续、哪些替换；其三，国家失稳的根本原因是合法性核心与强制力核心的结构性分离，这是革命的必要前提，不是充分条件。.

items.title: Historical Residue: The Sedimentation Bias Force of Dead Civilizations and the Dynamics of Why History Cannot Be Zeroed Out.
items.abstract: Why do post-revolutionary societies always end up resembling the societies they overthrew? Why can civilizations dead for centuries be “rediscovered” and re-enter cultural accumulation? Why can archaeology reconstruct the structure of dead civilizations from residual traces? These phenomena point to a single mechanism: the sedimentation residue left by dead civilizations is not a passive relic but an active bias force. This chapter argues within a sedimentation field dynamics framework that the cross-generational co-nucleus residue of dead civilizations (δ_res^Civ) persistently biases the accumulation trajectory of successor social fields through its structural overlap with new co-nuclei. New social fields preferentially continue along the familiar pathways left by old civilizations because these directions carry lower cognitive friction — this is the structural reason why history cannot be truly zeroed out, not cultural conservatism or a metaphor for path dependence, but a necessary consequence of sedimentation dynamics. Three results follow. First, residual bias explains why post-revolutionary societies resemble their predecessors without being identical to them — residue provides initial directional bias, while other forces determine the final form. Second, residue has its own lifecycle, decaying differentially across cultural layers: ritual residue is the most persistent, value residue the most transient. Third, historical residue truly exits the dynamic system only when its structural overlap with every active social field approaches zero — an event that is historically extremely rare.

items.title: 历史残留——已死亡文明的沉积偏置力与”历史不能清零”的动力机制.
items.abstract: 革命之后的社会为什么总是长得像被革命之前的社会？已死亡数百年的文明为什么能被”重新发现”并重新进入文化积深？为什么考古学能够通过残留重建已死文明的结构？这些现象指向同一个机制：死亡的文明留下的沉积残留，不是被动的遗迹，而是主动的偏置力。 本文在沉积场动力学框架下论证：已死亡文明的跨代际共核残留（δ_res^Civ）通过与新社会场共核的结构重合度，持续偏置后续社会场的积深方向。新社会场优先沿旧文明留下的熟径续行，因为这些方向具有更低的认知摩擦——这是历史不可能真正清零的结构性原因，不是文化保守主义，也不是路径依赖的隐喻，而是沉积动力学的必然结果。 由此推出三个结论：其一，残留偏置解释了革命后社会”像”旧社会但不等于旧社会的现象——偏置提供初始方向，其他力决定最终形态；其二，残留有自己的生命周期，按层次结构差异化衰减，仪式层残留最持久，价值层残留最短暂；其三，历史残留真正退出动力系统，需要残留与任何活跃社会场的结构重合度趋近于零——这在历史上极为罕见。.

items.title: 文明稳定性——跨代际共核的沉积深度与国家死亡不等于文明死亡的动力机制.
items.abstract: 国家可以多次死亡，文明却继续存在。秦灭汉兴，朝代更替无数次，但汉字、儒家伦理、“中国”这一认同从未中断。这个现象用国家理论无法解释——国家的稳定性来自规则结构的积深，但文明的稳定性显然依赖另一个更深层的结构。 本文在沉积场动力学框架下提出文明稳定性的核心方程：文明的存续依赖跨代际共核（CivilCore）的沉积深度与续流能力的乘积是否维持在文明存续阈值之上。当这一乘积持续高于阈值，国家死亡不推出文明死亡；当它趋降至阈值以下，文明才真正进入死亡通道——与当时的国家是否存续无关。 由此推出三个结论：其一，文明稳定性与政治稳定性是独立变量，二者可以同向也可以反向；其二，某些文明在多次革命后能迅速重建，正是因为 CivilCore 的沉积提供了新规则结构生长的初始偏置；其三，文明死亡在历史上极为罕见，但一旦发生通常不可逆——它要求语言消亡、核心叙事断绝、代际传承链彻底切断，三者同时发生。.

items.title: Civilizational Stability: The Sedimentation Depth of Cross-Generational Co-Nuclei and Why State Death Does Not Equal Civilizational Death.
items.abstract: States die; civilizations persist. China’s dynasties collapsed and were replaced countless times, yet the written language, Confucian ethics, and the identity “China” never disappeared. This phenomenon cannot be explained by theories of the State — State stability rests on the depth of rule-structure sedimentation, but civilizational stability clearly depends on a deeper structure. This chapter provides a core equation for civilizational stability within a sedimentation field dynamics framework. Civilizational continuity depends on whether the product of the sedimentation depth and continuation capacity of the cross-generational co-nucleus (CivilCore) remains above the civilizational survival threshold. While this product holds above the threshold, State death does not entail civilizational death; when it trends below the threshold, civilization enters a terminal pathway — regardless of whether the State at that moment persists. Three results follow. First, civilizational stability and political stability are independent variables that can move in the same or opposite directions. Second, some civilizations rebuild rapidly after repeated revolutions precisely because the CivilCore’s sedimentation provides an initial bias for new rule structures to grow. Third, civilizational death is historically rare but typically irreversible once it occurs — requiring the simultaneous collapse of language, core narrative transmission, and the intergenerational continuity chain.

items.title: Cultural Sedimentation: Differential Transmission Costs Across Ritual, Language, Narrative, and Value Layers, and the Layer-by-Layer Stripping Mechanism of Civilizational Decline.
