items.abstract: Why do rituals survive long after the value systems that originally justified them have been replaced? Why does language persist after ethnic ideologies collapse? Why are explicit value systems always the first casualties of revolution while rituals are the hardest to eradicate? These phenomena point to a single structural fact: different components of a civilization have different transmission costs, and therefore different sedimentation depths and decay rates. This chapter formalizes the cross-generational co-nucleus of a civilization as a four-layer composite sedimentation structure within a sedimentation field dynamics framework: Ritual Layer, Language Layer, Narrative Layer, and Value Layer. Cultural layers with lower transmission costs sediment more deeply and decay more slowly — rituals require only repetition without explanation and therefore reach the deepest sedimentation; value systems require explicit endorsement and explanation and therefore remain the shallowest. Each layer sediments and decays independently; civilizational death is not a simultaneous dissolution but a sequential stripping ordered by decay rate. Three results follow. First, the “importance” of a cultural element is structurally independent of its sedimentation depth — structures that can be continued at low cost systematically tend toward deeper sedimentation. Second, civilizational intrusion by external forces typically displaces the value layer first, then erodes the narrative layer, while the language and ritual layers offer the most persistent resistance. Third, the residual structures left after civilizational death (language fragments, ritual vestiges) do not constitute civilizational continuity, but constrain the growth trajectory of successor civilizations through historical residual bias.

items.title: Civilizational Intergenerational Transmission: Adjacent-Generation Co-Nucleus Overlap and the Intergenerational Dynamics of Civilizational Continuity.
items.abstract: Every generation dies; civilizations can persist for millennia. What mechanism sustains continuity across the death of any single generation? Many apparently “sudden” civilizational collapses are in fact the cumulative result of intergenerational transmission breakdown: not a single external shock that directly destroys civilization, but the transmission efficiency falling below threshold across successive generations until one generation cannot find enough inheritors, and civilization enters irreversible collapse. This chapter provides a complete mechanism for civilizational intergenerational transmission within a sedimentation field dynamics framework. The intergenerational continuity of a civilization’s cross-generational co-nucleus is maintained through the co-nucleus overlap between adjacent generations (GenOverlap) — jointly determined by three factors: transmission integrity, participation rate, and institutional continuity. As long as GenOverlap between adjacent generations remains above the intergenerational survival threshold, civilization retains the capacity to continue across the death of any single generation; when GenOverlap falls below the intergenerational fracture threshold, transmission enters irreversible breakdown, triggering the intergenerational collapse pathway. Three results follow. First, civilizational continuity depends on the collective transmission behavior of the generational cohort — ritual participation, language use, educational institution maintenance — not on the memory of any single individual. Second, the decline of GenOverlap is not linearly lethal; two distinct threshold regions exist: a fragile transmission zone and an irreversible fracture zone. Third, intergenerational fracture is the micro-level realization mechanism of civilizational compression death; external shocks (forced assimilation, religious purges, large-scale displacement) destroy civilizations precisely by driving GenOverlap below the fracture threshold.

items.title: Civilizational Compression Death: The Endogenous Positive Feedback Mechanism of Transmission Integrity Decline and Three Pathways of Civilizational Death.
items.abstract: Civilizations do not die by fracture — they die by compression. Historians typically search for a moment of civilizational collapse: a decisive war, a conquest, a revolution. But the actual death process usually begins far earlier. A decline in transmission integrity triggers an endogenous positive feedback loop that accelerates the loss of continuation capacity until the core structure of the old civilization no longer serves as a continuation pathway basis for any active social field. This chapter identifies the compression loop of civilizational death within a sedimentation field dynamics framework: declining transmission integrity (Ω) reduces transmission rate, which reduces sedimentation depth, which reduces the replacement threshold, which further reduces Ω — once this loop initiates, decay is not linear but accelerating. The criterion for civilizational death is not the disappearance of a State, population, or territory, but the convergence toward zero of the overlap between the old civilization’s core structure and active social fields. Three results follow. First, external shocks (wars, conquests) are typically accelerators or terminal triggers of the compression process, not its root cause. Second, civilizational residue (preserved language, transmitted texts, architectural remains) does not equal civilizational continuity — continuity holds only when the old civilization’s core structure still serves as an active continuation pathway for living social fields. Third, civilizational death takes three structurally distinct paths: external replacement, internal erosion, and acute collapse — each driven by a different mechanism.

items.title: 应解者：论一种责任转嫁心态的叙事还原.
items.abstract: 本文是一篇应用篇——它把序列已建立的工具(尤其《被赋予的独立性》《寓意的落地》《因果的主观性》),回头用到一个非常具体、几乎人人遇见过的日常心理结构上:一种”问题转嫁”心态。 本文的出发点是一个洞见,它原话刻画了这种心态:“这个问题总应该是能解决的吧?我的位置似乎无法解决这个问题。那么处于比我更合适的位置的人就应该解决这个问题,否则这个问题岂不是就解决不了了?那肯定是不应该的。所以这个事情显然是那个人的责任,而非我的责任。” 本文把这条推理链拆成四步,并指认其中两处关键的位移。第一步的位移:从”我希望它能被解决”,位移到”它应该能被解决”——把一个愿望偷渡成一个关于问题本性的论断;但世界不欠这种义务,有些问题就是无解的。第三步的位移(这段心态的核心):从”我希望它被解决”,位移到”必然有别人能解、且应当去解”——三层位移在一句话里被打包:我的不能接受 → 问题无解是错的 → 第三方有义务。本文用序列的工具诊断:说话者讲了一个奋斗弧的故事;他把自己从奋斗者位置上挪开(第二步);而奋斗弧这个模板不允许奋斗者位置空着(《寓意的落地》:模板索取它所需的主体);于是反推出一个人填那个空位——“那个更合适的人”。这个人不是从对世界的考察来的,他是被故事模板的结构要求所索取出来的;“问题应被解决必然有一个应解它的人”是模板内的必然,被误读为现实层面的必然。整条链条用情节必然性伪装成现实必然性。本文最后指出它所服务的功能(一举保住道义感、避开无解之难受、卸下责任,认知预算上极其经济)与它的代价(被反推出来的”应解者”可能不存在、可能同样不能解、可能有自己的理由;链条的产物常是对一个被模板索取出来的”画中人”的长期责难)。.

items.title: Emerald and Stone.
items.abstract: Circular Theory, Circular Reality, Life and Love.

items.title: Why is School So Tiring?: Dislocated Labor and Misplaced Attention in the Academe.
items.abstract: The school has become the new sanctuary where the high altar of production is erected. In this setting, technical skills are delegated a kind of grand merit, especially those that produce job-ready learners sent as ‘supply-response’ to the labor gap of highly developed countries. This brand of education has become incessantly evident in the Philippines. In this paper, I offer a dismal image of an education depleted with its humanistic vocation. Offering a preliminary diagnosis, I point to two problematic conditions: (1) the dislocated view of labor as an instrument for production, primarily in the academe and, later, in the labor force; (2) the misplaced exercise of attention in the academe, which exacerbates the devaluation of labor. To ground these claims, I provide their iterations in the Philippine academe, such as the overbearing reach of instrumental rationality and the threat of curriculum hierarchy. Using Weil as an interlocutor, I followed her emphasis on attention as the real object of learning. I do this by critically examining the directions taken by the Philippine education system and the lessons it renders to arrive at an education that is attentive to its humanist character: orienting learners back to themselves and towards the others outside.

items.title: Why feeling begins in time: The temporogenesis argument.
items.abstract: Three literatures describe the temporal structure of experience — phenomenology its retentional-protentional form, predictive processing its dynamics, chronobiology its mechanisms — and none explains why that structure is present or why it is felt. Both follow from the conditions of self-maintenance. A system whose viability depends on what is not yet present, and whose stakes are distributed across its own history rather than concentrated in the instant, cannot meet those stakes by reaction, by an entrained rhythm, or by feed-forward wiring fixed to ancestral regularities; it must integrate its retained past and anticipated future into the organization by which it persists. This integration is temporogenesis, the second threshold in the framework’s cumulative sequence, operating on the mattering autopoiesis constitutes; felt mattering — the minimal phenomenal interior, sentience — is what the integration is from within, by constitutive identity rather than causation. One distinction carries the argument: the threshold is crossed by self-maintenance that is constitutively temporally extended, not by a system that computes a model of time. That distinction is at once the forcing step of the necessity argument, the lower-boundary criterion separating oscillators, feed-forward systems, and externalized memories from the organization that crosses, and the framework’s location among its neighbors — above the enactive tradition’s bare adaptivity, which can be the computed kind, and below the neural-architecture theories’ insistence on a brain. The criterion is clean at its poles and graded at one boundary: basal systems whose allostatic regulation integrates their own viability history are the open empirical case, where the computed and constitutive readings remain to be told apart, and where the verdict bears on the sentience-indicator approach now used to decide which animals receive legal protection.

items.title: Worldhood: Toward a Generative Theory of Experiential Reality.
items.abstract: Abstract Contemporary theories of consciousness have largely focused on representation, computation, prediction, or information integration. While these approaches explain important aspects of cognition, they generally presuppose the existence of a coherent experiential world within which cognition occurs. This paper argues that the prior explanatory problem is not representation itself, but worldhood: the conditions under which reality becomes experienceable as an inhabitable world. The paper develops a generative framework according to which consciousness is not fundamentally the awareness of objects but the dynamic stabilisation of inhabitable experiential horizons. The experienced world is not passively given but actively generated through organised relations among temporal continuity, embodied presence, perspectival orientation, salience organisation, meaning structure, and integrative coherence. Different configurations of these dimensions generate different forms of worldhood. The central claim is that consciousness should be understood not primarily as information processing or representation, but as the ongoing stabilisation of temporally continuous, embodied, meaningful horizons of possibility within which reality becomes inhabitable experience.

items.title: ◉ The Providence Deferral - God Has a Plan, Non-Testable Consolation, and the Ethics of Unverifiable Meaning.
items.abstract: The Christian formula “God has a plan” can function as private avowal, shared ritual, pastoral consolation, or public explanation. Confusion begins when the emotional force of the first three is treated as evidential support for the fourth. This paper argues that an unconstrained hidden-plan appeal is not a thin explanation awaiting details. It is a providence deferral: intention is moved into an inaccessible mind, while correction is postponed to a future beyond ordinary public inquiry. If every observable outcome is compatible with the plan and no outcomes are ranked as more expected than others, the observed record cannot confirm benevolent providence over live alternatives merely by fitting it. -/- The case uses a comparative standard of evidence, distinguishes compatibility from confirmation, and develops a symmetry test for skeptical theism. If human limitations prevent justified estimates of what a benevolent providential God-concept would make likely, suffering may fail to disconfirm that account; but rescue, survival, felt meaning, and apparent timing likewise cannot be credited as public confirmation on the same basis. Soul-making, free-will, natural-law, afterlife, and independent-evidence replies can be substantive only when they state constraints, accept evidential costs, or openly relocate the warrant outside the observed event. Research on meaning-making and religious coping supports a further distinction: religious interpretation may help some people and harm others, so coping value cannot be inferred from the slogan alone. -/- The conclusion is bounded but sharp. Hidden purpose remains logically possible, and religious hope may be personally rational when supported independently. Yet the slogan cannot simultaneously be protected from every adverse outcome and credited for favorable ones. An account that explains everything after the fact has explained nothing in advance. Pastoral use is defensible only when it is consensual, epistemically honest, and does not silence grief, block action, or impersonate knowledge.

items.title: ◉ The Immateriality Slide - Conscious Experience, Embodied Affect, and the Misclassification of the Spiritual.
items.abstract: Popular Christian apologetics sometimes caricatures physicalism as the claim that persons are merely 'molecules in motion.' The contrast is meant to do more than identify a metaphysical disagreement. It suggests that love, rational inference, moral seriousness, awe, and religious experience would be unreal or untrustworthy if physically realized, then treats their evident depth as support for an immaterial soul or spiritual realm. This paper argues that the move equivocates among four different claims: an experience is first-personal, it is not exhausted by one vocabulary, it is physically realized, and it is evidence for an ontologically independent source. None entails the next without argument. -/- The positive case is cumulative. Conscious availability changes under anesthesia and neural injury; affect and salience change under pharmacology; the organization of access and report changes with neural connectivity; mystical-type states can be occasioned by drugs and shaped by expectation; personal prayer recruits ordinary social-cognitive systems; and religious interpretation varies with learned models and cultural framing. These findings do not deductively prove identity theory, eliminate the explanatory gap, or show that every religious experience is mistaken. They do show systematic intervention-sensitive dependence. That pattern is more expected if cherished human states are achievements of embodied organisms than if their first-person character itself supplies public evidence of independence from embodiment. -/- The conclusion is therefore calibrated but consequential. Irreducibility is not independence, higher-level reality is not a separate substance, and value is not a residue of ignorance. A dualist or religious account may remain possible, but it must supply a discriminating bridge or evidence beyond the phenomenology it shares with embodied alternatives. Explanation does not empty experience. It locates the conditions under which experience becomes possible, vulnerable, and valuable.

items.title: ◉ The Clarity Design Burden: Omniscience, Communicative Competence, and the Low Cost of Doctrinal Precision.
items.abstract: This paper develops a focused companion to the broader argument that biblical doctrinal diversity counts against divine clarity-aim authorship. The earlier argument assessed the evidential significance of Christian fragmentation. The present paper asks a narrower design question: is doctrinal clarity itself difficult for an omniscient, omnipotent communicator? I argue that it is not. For finite human authors, clarity is costly because knowledge, attention, language, audience modeling, and revision are limited. For a divine communicator who knows every future reader, every interpretive fork, every translation path, and every doctrinal consequence, the relevant obstacles are dramatically reduced. The paper treats revelation as a communication-design problem. High-stakes communication normally uses redundancy, definitions, contrastive exclusions, examples, error correction, controlled terminology, and audience-sensitive repetition. These tools do not require coercion. They do not force love, obedience, worship, or trust. They merely reduce avoidable misunderstanding. If the central doctrines at issue concern salvation, moral obligation, sacramental practice, divine identity, and eternal destiny, then low-cost clarity becomes an expectation generated by the theology itself. Engaging Gricean pragmatics, relevance theory, information theory, divine discourse, perspicuity debates, disagreement epistemology, and companion work on clarity and coercion, I conclude that appeals to human limitation do not transfer smoothly to God. The persistent ambiguity of core Christian doctrine is not simply an unfortunate byproduct of communication. It is a datum requiring explanation from any view that treats Scripture as divine speech aimed at broad doctrinal understanding.

items.title: ◉ The Boundary-Retreat Device - No True Christian Reasoning, Identity Policing, and the Survival of Idealized Christendom.
items.abstract: The claim that an apostate, abuser, hypocrite, or failed exemplar was "never a true Christian" may sometimes identify a real mistake in classification. It becomes a boundary-retreat device when the criteria are revised only after a threatening case appears. The decisive problem is not that communities draw boundaries. It is that favorable and unfavorable evidence are often processed under different rules. Profession, worship, ministry, sacrifice, testimony, apparent transformation, and communal recognition count as evidence of genuine Christianity while a person remains loyal. If that person later deconverts or violates central Christian norms, the same history is reclassified as counterfeit. The worldview receives present credit without accepting retrospective liability. This paper develops a prospective symmetry test. A repair is evidentially legitimate only when its criteria were available before the outcome, can classify favorable cases as false as well as unfavorable cases, are supported independently of the need to protect the worldview, and carry the same consequences for present classification. This yields a dilemma. If observable signs justify confident present claims that someone is a genuine Christian, later failure must sometimes count as evidence about Christian formation, testimony, institutions, or the reliability of those signs. If lifelong perseverance is the decisive criterion, no living believer has completed it, so present claims of genuine status are necessarily provisional. One may choose corrigibility or present uncertainty. One may not rationally combine warm certainty now with categorical erasure later. Social identity, cognitive dissonance, motivated reasoning, purity boundaries, and costly commitment help explain why the retreat is attractive without establishing the motives of any particular believer. Recent research also undermines the caricature of deconversion as a single shallow event: formerly religious populations are heterogeneous, intellectual and institutional reasons recur, and religious psychology can persist after deidentification. Their testimony is fallible evidence, not an oracle; it deserves the same source-sensitive scrutiny applied to conversion testimony. The conclusion is bounded but polemical. An ideal may criticize actual Christianity, but it cannot absorb every success and disown every failure. A Christianity curated so that only victories belong to it has protected its image by forfeiting a public …

items.title: ◉ The Buffer Zone Effect: Peripheral Controversy, Identity Maintenance, and the Avoidance of Core Theological Risk.
items.abstract: This paper analyzes a recurrent pattern in contemporary apologetic culture: energy is displaced from the most vulnerable theological claims to peripheral controversies that feel urgent, identity-forming, and intellectually respectable. Debates about sexuality, cultural decline, evolution, abiogenesis, fine-tuning, religious liberty, school curricula, or secular hypocrisy may be important in their own right. The problem arises when they function as buffer zones: arenas of conflict that let believers experience defense of Christianity without directly defending Christianity's central claims. The argument does not claim that apologists consciously avoid hard questions, nor that every public controversy is a distraction. Rather, it identifies a social-epistemic mechanism. Communities under evidential pressure preserve confidence by channeling anxiety into disputes where success criteria are looser, emotional rewards are stronger, and group identity is reinforced. Drawing on cognitive dissonance, motivated reasoning, social identity theory, cultural cognition, argumentative reasoning, and sociology of plausibility structures, I show how buffer zones convert epistemic discomfort into moral momentum. The paper provides examples across moral politics, science debates, and public rhetoric. A formal model distinguishes core-risk claims, transfer claims, and buffer claims. The central critique is that even successful buffer arguments rarely confirm the specific doctrines for which they are emotionally recruited. Showing that a secular opponent is inconsistent does not establish the resurrection. Showing that abiogenesis remains incomplete does not identify the Christian God. Showing that a cultural movement is confused does not validate biblical authority. The conclusion is that apologetic seriousness requires returning from buffer zones to the claims that actually bear the worldview's weight.

items.title: ◉ The Authority-Sampling Error - Quote Mining, Credibility Laundering, and the Stepping-Stone Fallacy in Theistic Argument.
items.abstract: Popular theistic arguments often recruit non-theistic or religiously heterodox authorities as “hostile witnesses.” A scientist’s awe, a philosopher’s criticism of reductionism, an agnostic’s uncertainty, or an atheist’s imagined possibility is presented as a stepping stone toward theism and sometimes toward Christianity. The central error is not always false quotation. It is the transfer of credibility from a source’s local statement to a conclusion the source did not support, while the context, domain limits, broader position, or inferential bridge that would constrain the move is omitted. -/- This paper calls the pattern the authority-sampling error and the resulting transfer credibility laundering. Work on testimony and expert opinion explains why authority can rationally matter; work on contextomy explains why selective quotation can distort even when the words are authentic. A four-part audit follows: domain fit, contextual stability, position disclosure, and bridge adequacy. Applied to familiar uses of Einstein, Darwin, Hawking, Dawkins, Sagan, and Nagel, the audit separates legitimate local contributions from illicit endorsement effects. Awe is not personal theism; uncertainty is not support; conceptual possibility is not probability; criticism of one naturalism does not identify a Christian God-concept. -/- The conclusion is bounded and constructive. A quoted authority may state a true premise and may even be mistaken about its consequences. In that case the apologist may defend an independent bridge and openly disagree with the source. What the apologist may not do is let the source’s prestige substitute for that bridge. Responsible practice preserves the exact proposition supported, discloses materially contrary commitments, distinguishes expertise from fame, and reports a conclusion no broader than the argument earns.

items.title: ◉ The Accommodation Burden - Divine Power, Human Understanding, and the Failure of Sacred Opacity.
items.abstract: A God-concept is a specified conception of a deity. This paper assesses a familiar Christian communicative God-concept: a perfectly informed, powerful, and benevolent personal deity seeks relationship, issues high-stakes commands, and intends finite persons to understand enough to recognize and respond. Defenders sometimes answer opacity by treating incomprehensibility itself as a sign of transcendence. That inversion fails. The difference between exhaustive comprehension and successful disclosure is not a narrow technicality: a reality may exceed every finite model while still being communicated at a scale its audience can use. -/- The argument combines apophatic restraint, pragmatics, divine-discourse theory, and comparative evidence. Negative theology properly limits positive predication; it does not license detailed relational claims and then suspend their ordinary implications whenever those claims meet evidential pressure. Intentional communication requires audience modelling, relevance, redundancy, and correction. A communicator with perfect knowledge and sufficient power would not face finite surprise about reception. The resulting expectation is not universal agreement or total transparency, but discriminable intelligibility: stable enough public content to distinguish disclosure from projection and disciplined mystery from semantic immunity. -/- Persistent opacity is therefore not positive evidence for the target model. Finite human religious production expects ambiguity, cultural path dependence, competing interpretations, and retrospective rescue at least as well, and often better. A narrower divine aim or a specific independently supported reason for opacity may alter that comparison; mere possibility cannot. The paper asks readers to stop rewarding a model for the very communicative failure its attributed powers should help it overcome.

items.title: ✶ Morphing Ships of Theseus on Future Seas: Religion, Constitutions, and Institutional Survival in the Age of AI.
items.abstract: This paper develops an analogy between durable religious traditions and durable constitutional orders. Both begin with authoritative texts, founding memories, interpretive communities, and legitimacy claims that must persist across historical change. Both face the same Theseus problem: how much can be replaced before continuity becomes fiction? I argue that successful systems do not maximize either rigidity or flexibility. They stratify them. The symbolic keel must remain difficult to replace, while planks, sails, rigging, and navigational instruments must remain repairable through authorized procedures. The paper extends the Ship of Theseus analogy by placing the ship at sea. Societies cannot suspend history while they reconstruct their deepest institutions. They must adapt while maintaining cooperation, identity, law, meaning, and trust. Religions do this through theology, ritual, councils, reform, commentary, and schism-management. Constitutional orders do it through amendment, judicial interpretation, precedent, legislation, federalism, elections, and unwritten norms. AI introduces a new stressor because it compresses change timelines. Labor markets, epistemic trust, surveillance capacity, education, intimacy, political persuasion, moral agency, and institutional authority may be reshaped faster than inherited interpretive mechanisms can respond. The paper proposes formal models for institutional robustness, repair capacity, shock load, safe repair rate, and AI acceleration. It concludes that peaceful adaptation is most likely where institutions can make necessary repairs feel like fidelity to the founding voyage. Tumult is most likely where technological change outruns legitimacy, where every plank is treated as sacred, or where the keel itself becomes negotiable.

items.title: An Agnostic Structural Law.
items.abstract: We present a synthesis of the Open Tensoriality Programme (OTP), a research programme initiated that set the lines along a novel epistemic and ontological category that took on through Wittgenstein (vs. Chomsky's apparent dichotomies,) the structural conditions for meaning and the notion of "basin" and "externsive" structural allowance for agency. The programme proposes a single agnostic structural law operating across physical, biological, cognitive, and cosmological scales: at every scale and in every substrate, a generative loop runs through a gap, closes on a stable remainder, and deposits that remainder as the constraint geometry within which the next gap appears. This paper has three aims. First, it states the programme's initial assumptions and their philosophical provenance. Second, it discusses the ontological category by the Symbol~2.0/Symboliad (software-physicalism) - and presents a few classes of evidence from artificial intelligence research and biology that confirm the category's construction. Third, it states the agnostic structural law formally and traces its consequences at the cosmological scale, proposing a constraint-flow cosmology in which also a physics of physics emerges: standard physics as the plateau-stable positive extraction of a deeper generative process. This position would be able to offer an interesting view over actual cosmology that may hint at explaining the "dark sector" among others. We can hypothesize about the origin of primes (RH) or the cosmological constants: what if they are residuals, not as results that need be assessed further by more calculus and introduction of novel explanations? A key claim is thus that from this level, an inversion of perspective occurs ("cognitive closure"), and it all follows from the "monadology" proposed and by the fact that intelligence is "backed-in" as specified by the notion of "basin" in the framework. Thus "agentity," "sentientity," "intelligence," "learning" which are conventionally attributed to dedicated cognitive spaces - are general features of dynamical systems that possess the "enactity" characteristic: history-dependent constraint geometry. The whole apparatus require no additional "representational" nor "goal-directedness" nor "world models" nor "meta-cognitive" layers as normally the biology takes for granted, but emerge directly from the construction within a proper frame of reference that needs to be assumed too ("plateaus of generativity"). These fine lines are …

items.title: A General Theory of Masking : Competing Relevance Orders in Neurodivergence, Art and Society.
items.abstract: Masking is currently described primarily as a phenomenon of neurodivergent adaptation. Particularly within Autism Research, the term refers to strategies of social camouflage aimed at concealing deviations from neurotypical norms. The present paper argues that this description is too narrow. -/- Masking is understood here as a general mechanism that emerges wherever different relevance orders must be stabilised simultaneously. From this perspective, masking constitutes neither mere pretence nor mere adaptation. Rather, it appears as the operative management of incompatible forms of world-binding. -/- Drawing on the theory of Eigenzeit relations, it is shown that different cognitive, cultural, and institutional systems produce different forms of attention, coherence, and relevance. Since no world-binding can process all differences simultaneously, processes of prioritisation necessarily emerge. Every prioritisation simultaneously generates blind spots, opportunity costs, and exclusions. -/- Masking therefore appears not as a specific deficit of neurodivergent people, but as a general consequence of structural incompatibilities between competing relevance orders. The analysis is applied to neurodivergence, art, science, work, and poverty, and develops a theory of structural violence that is based not primarily on oppression through prohibitions, but on the persistent redirection of attention, time, and energy into foreign relevance systems.

items.title: The International Law Fallacy, Volume I: Law, Power, and the Illusion of Sovereignty.
items.abstract: FORTHCOMING SOON: A COMPANION PAPER ON IRAN, THE UNITED STATES & ISRAEL WILL EXTEND THIS LEGAL-STRATEGIC ANALYSIS. | -/- (REVISED)*The International Law Fallacy, Volume I* examines the gap between the formal existence of international law and its operation as governing force. Through a comparative audit of maritime corridors, international judicial proceedings, the war in Ukraine, and the paired water and oil crises of 2026, the volume asks whether a rule continues to function as a rule when its activation varies according to power, alignment, consent, or the identity of the actor. It develops the concepts of Statutory Inactivity, Judicial Inactivity, and Enforcement Divergence and introduces the Soltani Order as a framework for identifying conditions in which legal structures remain formally intact while their application ceases to operate uniformly across comparable circumstances. Rather than treating the existence of statutes, institutions, resolutions, or jurisdiction as sufficient proof of functioning law, the analysis tests whether proclaimed legal authority actually governs conduct when enforcement is required.

items.title: The International Law Fallacy, Volume III: The Kairos of the International Disorder.
items.abstract: FORTHCOMING SOON: A COMPANION PAPER ON IRAN, THE UNITED STATES & ISRAEL WILL EXTEND THIS LEGAL-STRATEGIC ANALYSIS. | -/- This volume delivers the final judgment of The International Law Fallacy trilogy. Volume I carried out a forensic audit of the international legal order on the terms it claimed for itself. Volume II entered and closed the evidentiary record. This final volume does not reopen that record but delivers judgment on what has already been proved concerning international law, legal authority, enforcement, sovereignty, and the international order. The central finding is that international law does not exist as a materially universal law. Not as a weak law, a corrupted law, or a law unevenly kept. What exists under its name is an instrument: vocabulary, institutional form, ceremony, procedure, and force calibrated to power. The volume distinguishes law from the instrument, procedure from protection, coordination from legal authority, diplomatic management from genuine jurisprudential authority, and institutional order from the material protection of defenseless life. Using the 22 May 2026 failure of the Eleventh Review Conference of the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons (NPT) as a contemporary confirmation rather than the foundation of the argument, the volume names the Kairos of the international disorder: the moment at which one of the coverings that kept the instrument legible as law ceased, in public view, to perform that function. The verdict is final: what exists under the name of international law is not law, but the instrument. The word remains. The substance has not appeared. ______________________________________- Keywords: international law; philosophy of law; jurisprudence; legal authority; sovereignty; international order; global governance; international institutions; enforcement; hegemony; legal realism; International Criminal Court (ICC); Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT); NPT Review Conference; nuclear weapons; geopolitics; The International Law Fallacy; Soltani Order.

items.title: Architecture of Limitation Research Program Orientation: A Manifesto for the Study of Reasoning Under Constraint.
items.abstract: The Architecture of Limitation (AoL) is a diagnostic research program investigating how reasoning systems behave when they encounter structural limits. Rather than evaluating claims according to truth or explanatory completeness, AoL examines the conditions under which reasoning remains proportionate to the structures that sustain it. The program develops through a corpus of experimental studies that introduce conceptual artifacts, institutional systems, and AI-mediated reasoning environments into constraint-governed interpretive frameworks. These experiments reveal recurring structural signals including boundary tension, conceptual drift, and collapse when reasoning exceeds its supporting conditions. Across the corpus, the Architecture of Limitation functions as a constraint-based validator architecture for observing reasoning behaviour under pressure. -/- The present document provides an orientation to the research program, mapping the corpus of publications and describing the capability structure through which AoL investigates reasoning across philosophical, institutional, governance, and computational domains. -/- Recent developments introduced the Human–System Compatibility layer, extending the capability structure from five to six operational layers. This addition expands the research program beyond structural observation toward the study of cognitive compatibility, recoverability, bounded variation, and stewardship under conditions of finite probabilistic access. -/- Version 6 incorporates the publication of the Architecture of Limitation Observational System (AoLOS) Stack v1.0 and formally distinguishes between the Architecture of Limitation as a research architecture and AoLOS as the operational environment used to deploy, instrument, compare, and observe reasoning under constraint. The corpus inventory has been updated accordingly, and the research frontier now includes collaborative observation under shared instrumentation environments. -/- Version 5 introduced the Program Status and Stewardship Transparency section, formally distinguishing archival research outputs from ongoing program stewardship and establishing the public discussion forum as the primary location for project status, stewardship updates, and program evolution. -/- This work forms part of the broader Architecture of Limitation / AoLOS research program. The corpus investigates reasoning systems under structural constraint and is maintained as an evolving open research program …

items.title: Review of Frances Egan, Deflating Mental Representation. [REVIEW]
Why Continuity Feels Like Something.
items.abstract: Human experience routinely extends beyond the immediate present. Memories remain active within present awareness, anticipated futures influence present decisions, and relationships, commitments, and purposes continue shaping experience across time. This paper examines the connection between temporal continuity and the felt character of experience. -/- The central claim is that experience unfolds within an ongoing continuity that carries inheritances from the past while participating in possibilities directed toward the future. Learning, understanding, care, recognition, and selfhood each involve the development of increasingly organized relationships across time. As a continuity becomes increasingly present within its own development, the significance of what it carries and what it is becoming becomes directly available within experience. -/- Particular attention is given to recognition, future-directed participation, and the role of anticipated futures in shaping present organization. The familiar feeling associated with understanding, meaning, and personal identity is examined as an aspect of a continuity becoming present within its own ongoing continuation. Experience is proposed as the lived aspect of this developmental process, arising within the participation of a life in its own unfolding through time.

items.title: Ragione ed emozioni in psicologia morale. Il contributo di un approccio kantiano integrato.
items.pub: In Daniele Bondioli, Sofia Bonicalzi & Mario De Caro, Etica normativa. Roma: Inschibboleth Edizioni. pp. 171-188.
items.abstract: Nel presente contributo sostengo che un approccio kantiano, riletto in chiave integrata, sia particolarmente adatto a rispondere alle esigenze della psicologia morale contemporanea. La ricostruzione iniziale del dibattito evidenzia i limiti dei modelli gerarchici, incapaci di rendere conto della complessa interazione tra ragione ed emozioni. L’etica kantiana, reinterpretata come teoria integrata della deliberazione e dello sviluppo morale, nella quale sia le emozioni sia la ragione svolgono un ruolo essenziale, fornisce invece gli strumenti concettuali per comprendere tale interazione. Applicato al caso della psicopatia, questo modello consente di rendere conto congiuntamente dei deficit razionali ed emotivi che caratterizzano il soggetto psicopatico. Il risultato è che un approccio kantiano integrato non solo è compatibile con i dati empirici disponibili, ma offre un quadro teorico capace di spiegarli in modo più completo. Questo suggerisce che il contributo kantiano alla psicologia morale non è di natura meramente storica, ma costituisce una risorsa concettuale attuale per comprendere il funzionamento della moralità umana.

items.title: Tests for Consciousness in Infants.
items.pub: In Walter Sinnott-Armstrong & Liad Mudrik, Tests of Consciousness: How to tell whether a human, other animal or AI is conscious and what they are conscious of. MIT Press.
items.venue: Tests of Consciousness: How to tell whether a human, other animal or AI is conscious and what they are conscious of
items.abstract: Here is a draft abstract adapted from the talk description: This paper examines the marker method for detecting consciousness, applied to the problem of infant consciousness. After discussing the basic forms of the method, including theory-first, marker-first, and hybrid approaches, I examine three prominent tests: the network test, the global violation (oddball) paradigm, and the attentional blink. I assess the strengths and limitations of each as an indicator of early consciousness, and consider how evidence from multiple markers should be weighed. I argue that markers provide especially strong evidence when they display synchronic convergence — appearing within the same developmental window — and interlevel consistency, with behavioral and neural markers mutually supporting one another. Applying these criteria, I show that the three tests offer cumulative but not conclusive support for the presence of consciousness in early infancy, and I discuss the implications for prenatal consciousness. I conclude by reflecting on persistent expert disagreement in the field, arguing that progress depends not only on developing stronger empirical tests but on refining the methodological criteria by which those tests are evaluated." .

items.title: Free Will, Volition, and Self-Agency as Emergent Control Processes: A Compatibilist Account.
items.abstract: This paper presents a compatibilist account of free will grounded in emergent organization, predictive processing, and higher-level causal structure. Free will is not treated as absolute uncaused freedom or a violation of physical law. Instead, it is understood as the capacity of an organism to form intentions, evaluate options, select actions, and initiate behavior through internally integrated and self-referential processes. The framework rejects both libertarian appeals to metaphysically uncaused agency and eliminativist claims that agency is purely illusory. Higher-level organizational processes are argued to be causally meaningful despite being fully physically instantiated. The paper also addresses objections from source incompatibilism and explains why quantum indeterminacy alone does not generate authorship or control. -/- .

items.title: Beyond Principles: Why Care and Clarity Are the Only Genuinely Post‑Conventional Stages Of Moral Development.
items.abstract: Lawrence Kohlberg's theory of moral development claims that post-conventional morality consists of abstract principle-based reasoning (utilitarian, contractarian, rights-based). This paper argues that such reasoning remains conventional—it operates within established legal and social frameworks, even when it involves critical thinking. A genuinely post-conventional morality must arise from the lived experience of interdependent agency and culminate in the increasingly clear and stable perception of interdependence—not from philosophically constructing a system of rules or principles. Drawing on care ethics (Gilligan) and the author's framework of flourishing, we propose a two-stage model of post-conventional moral development: the vow-motive (stabilised care arising from lived interdependence within revealing-form institutions) and clarity (the spontaneous expression of care from the perception of interdependence). -/- The paper further proposes that moral development consists in the increasing integration of self-perception, motivation, reasoning, and action. Apparent gaps between moral reasoning and moral action may arise from developmental dissociation: a person may learn the language and justificatory vocabulary of a higher stage without having undergone the corresponding transformation in self-perception and motivational organisation. This explains why sophisticated moral reasoning can coexist with strikingly inconsistent behaviour—without reducing the discrepancy either to hypocrisy or to a mysterious impotence of reason. Conventional moral orientations are shaped by socialisation—women into care roles, men into rule-based roles—but neither is post-conventional. Genuinely post-conventional care is available to all, regardless of gender, through the cultivation of clarity and the support of just institutions. The paper concludes with empirical predictions and an invitation for further research, proposing that measures of self-perception and motivational organisation will explain variance in moral behaviour that cannot be explained by expressed moral reasoning alone. -/- .

items.title: VIRTUE AS THE FOUNDATION OF LEGITIMATE TRANSGRESSION: A Unified Theory of Virtuous Transgression and Tutela Libertatis.
items.abstract: Two of the most consequential debates in political philosophy have proceeded for decades without recognising a shared structural flaw. The debate about when civil disobedience is legitimate and the debate about whether protective rights produce genuine equality for the weakest members of a community both mistake a nominal framework — procedural compliance rules in the first case, legal permission in the second — for the actual causal variable that determines whether the acts in question are genuinely what they claim to be. That variable is the virtue-state of the agent: the integrated exercise of practical wisdom and justice. This article formalises that variable and derives two linked results. First, the Injustice Threshold Function (ITF) specifies the conditions under which institutional capture is sufficient to dissolve procedural authority and generate a moral obligation — not merely a permission — to transgress. Second, the Equalisation Proximity Function (EPF) specifies the conditions under which a community’s protective architecture achieves genuine equalisation for its weakest members beyond legal permission. The two results share a common structure, and their integration constitutes the Unified Virtue-Legitimacy Framework (UVLF). We prove that the standard acceptance-of-punishment criterion is internally incoherent (Theorem T1), derive the obligation threshold as an indicator function on objective structural indices, specify the generalised EPF with a saturation-bounded capacity term and a collective security coupling coefficient, and demonstrate cross-domain structural invariance in five unlike domains including AI alignment. We design a pre-registerable empirical test using Mahalanobis-matched state-pair comparisons and Structural Equation Modelling. The UVLF resolves the anomalies of both traditions and opens a new observational programme. Keywords: civil disobedience, virtue ethics, Tutela Libertatis, legitimate transgression, political obligation, equalisation proximity function, injustice threshold function, spoudaios confirmation, cascading virtue-atrophy, philosophy of virtues, Alguilas-AI, Virtuous Transgression, Guns.

items.title: Self-Referential Ignorance within the Universal Balance-Feedback Framework (UBFF) A Systems-Theoretic Framework for Understanding Cognitive, Institutional, and Civilizational Failure.
items.abstract: This paper introduces and formally develops the concept of Self-Referential Ignorance (SRI) within the Universal Balance-Feedback Framework (UBFF), a systems-theoretic model describing how adaptive systems maintain or lose stability through feedback regulation. SRI is defined as the condition in which a system becomes excessively reliant upon internally self-validating informational loops while suppressing external corrective feedback from reality. Drawing on cybernetics, thermodynamics, nonlinear dynamical systems theory, epistemology, cognitive science, and organizational sociology, we establish a generalized mathematical framework applicable across individual cognition, institutions, scientific paradigms, artificial intelligence systems, and civilizations. We introduce a coupled dynamical systems model capturing the interaction between internal coherence (C) and external correction (E), derive Lyapunov stability conditions for healthy feedback equilibria, and characterize the bifurcation threshold separating adaptive cognition from entropic SRI collapse. An information-theoretic entropy measure is proposed to operationalize feedback suppression. Historical case studies — including the collapse of Enron, late Soviet stagnation, and Kodak's failure to adapt — are analyzed through UBFF variables. Falsifiable empirical predictions are generated. The paper argues that sustainable intelligence, whether individual, institutional, or artificial, depends upon maintaining dynamic equilibrium between self-organizing identity structures and externally grounded corrective feedback.

items.title: Human-Created Problems as Emergent Phenomena of Natural Law: A Universal Balance-Feedback Framework Analysis.
items.abstract: This paper examines the paradoxical relationship between nature and human-created problems through the formal lens of the Universal Balance-Feedback Framework (UBFF). While nature itself generates no conceptual "problems," human beings continuously produce social, political, ecological, and existential crises. We argue that such problems are not violations of natural law but emergent consequences of the Four Universal Laws — System Integrity, Universal Balance, Universal Feedback Loop Mechanism, and Universal Interconnected Nodes — operating through self-aware intelligent systems. We formalize this claim using a coupled nonlinear dynamical system modeling three interacting state variables: Imbalance Accumulation (I), Feedback Saturation (F), and Symbolic Complexity (S). Lyapunov stability analysis demonstrates that runaway human crises correspond to loss of asymptotic stability at the system equilibrium, driven by positive feedback amplification and symbolic-cognitive overload. We derive a UBFF Emergence Index (EI) as a scalar measure of crisis propensity, present falsifiable empirical predictions, and map the UBFF laws to mathematical operators. The analysis resolves the central paradox: human-created problems are higher-order emergent phenomena of nature's own self-organizing complexity, governed by the same universal laws that produce all order and disorder.

items.title: Jannah as Sacred Concealment: Hidden Realism and the Qur’anic Logic of Ghayb.
items.abstract: Jannah in the Qur’an is not merely “paradise” in the popular sense. Its Ara- bic root j-n-n (jim-nun-nun) belongs to the semantic field of covering, concealment, protection, hiddenness, and enclosure in classical lexicography. Within Qur’anic usage, jannah names a protected realm whose access is moral, revela- tory, and eschatological rather than ordinarily empirical. The Qur’an presents jannah as prepared, spacious, peaceful, protected, restorative, and beyond ordinary possession. These features support the concept of sacred concealment: a sacred reality prepared, veiled from ordinary perception, morally accessed, and eschatologically disclosed. Accordingly, jannah can be read as Qur’anic hidden realism: a real yet concealed eschatological order disclosed through revelation. Q. 32:17 strengthens this reading by describing eschatological reward as hidden (ukhfiya) from ordinary knowledge, while the broader logic of ghayb prevents it from being reduced to speculative geography. Comparisons with Sukhāvatī, Peach Blossom Spring, Shambhala, Avalon, and Tír na nÓg remain phenomenological parallels only. They clarify recurring motifs of hiddenness, limited access, peace, and restoration without claiming historical identity, geographical verification, ontological proof, or a hidden civilisation.

items.title: Meaning as Experienced Relevance: A Systemic Theory of Psychological Investment, Hope, and Coherence (Short Version).
items.abstract: This paper presents a concise version of a broader systemic theory of psychological investment, hope, and coherence based on the concept of relevance. -/- It argues that psychological systems allocate limited resources—such as attention, energy, time, and action—according to relevance evaluations. Relevance is defined as the weighting of information according to its expected influence on future coherence. Meaning is then interpreted as the phenomenological appearance of relevance: what appears externally as relevance is experienced internally as meaning.

items.title: Meaning as Experienced Relevance: A Systemic Theory of Psychological Investment, Hope, and Coherence.
items.abstract: This paper develops a systemic theory of psychological investment based on the concept of relevance. It argues that psychological systems allocate limited resources—such as attention, energy, time, and action—according to relevance evaluations. Relevance is defined as the weighting of information according to its expected influence on future coherence. Meaning is then interpreted as the phenomenological appearance of relevance: what appears externally as relevance is experienced internally as meaning. -/- On this basis, the paper proposes that several central psychological constructs—meaning, hope, self-efficacy, belonging, identity, and major emotions—can be understood as different manifestations of a common relevance mechanism. Meaning represents experienced relevance over time. Hope is defined as the perceived future repairability of relevant coherence. Self-efficacy describes perceived influence over relevant states. Belonging is interpreted as social relevance, and identity as an organized model of relevance. -/- The paper further applies this framework to depression, loneliness, identity crises, therapy, and suicidality. Psychological crises are interpreted not merely as disturbances of mood or cognition, but as disruptions in relevance organization, future coherence, and continued investment. Recovery is understood as the reorganization of relevance through resonance, experience, recognition, and renewed hope. The model integrates and extends ideas from Frankl, Bandura, Beck, Grawe, Baumeister and Leary, Deci and Ryan, Joiner, and Snyder, while proposing relevance as a unifying theoretical construct.

items.title: Erleben als integrierte Relevanz: Ein Zwei-Aspekte-Modell des Bewusstseins (Kurzversion).
items.abstract: Diese Kurzversion stellt das Kernargument eines Zwei-Aspekte-Modells von Erleben und Bewusstsein auf Grundlage systemischer Relevanz dar. Die zentrale These lautet, dass Erleben die innere Erscheinungsweise systemischer Relevanz ist und dass Bewusstsein nicht bloß integrierte Information, sondern integrierte Relevanz ist. Information markiert Unterschied; Salienz markiert aufmerksamkeitswirksame Hervorhebung; Funktion beschreibt die Rolle eines Zustands in einem Prozess; systemische Relevanz beschreibt den Grad, in dem ein Unterschied für die fortgesetzte Organisation, Regulation, Integrität, Handlungsfähigkeit oder Entwicklung eines Systems bedeutsam wird. Schmerz ist beispielsweise nicht bloß Information über Gewebeschädigung oder die Funktion des Rückzugs, sondern gestörte körperliche Integrität als negativ relevant von innen. Das Paper führt die Grundstruktur der Relevanzmatrix ein und unterscheidet biologische, affektive, soziale, narrative und existenzielle Formen von Relevanz. Das Modell wird im Verhältnis zum Hard Problem, zu Zwei-Aspekte-Theorien, Integrated Information Theory, Predictive Processing, dem Free-Energy Principle, Panexperientialismus, Russellian Monism, Interozeption, Salienzforschung und Appraisal-Theorien der Emotion verortet. Ziel ist nicht, Erleben aus Funktion abzuleiten, sondern Erleben als inneren Aspekt relevanzorganisierter Systeme zu verstehen.

items.title: Experience as Integrated Relevance: A Dual-Aspect Account of Consciousness (Short Version).
items.abstract: This short version presents the core argument of a dual-aspect account of experience and consciousness centered on systemic relevance. The central claim is that experience is the inner appearance of systemic relevance, and that consciousness is not merely integrated information but integrated relevance. Information marks difference; salience marks attentional prominence; function describes the role of a state in a process; systemic relevance describes the degree to which a difference matters for the continued organization, regulation, integrity, action-capacity, or development of a system. Pain, for example, is not merely information about tissue damage or the function of withdrawal, but disturbed bodily integrity as negatively relevant from within. The paper introduces the basic relevance matrix and distinguishes biological, affective, social, narrative, and existential forms of relevance. It situates the model in relation to the hard problem, dual-aspect theory, Integrated Information Theory, predictive processing, the Free-Energy Principle, panexperientialism, Russellian monism, interoception, salience research, and appraisal theories of emotion. The aim is not to derive experience from function, but to reframe experience as the inner aspect of relevance-organized systems.

items.title: Erleben als integrierte Relevanz: Ein Zwei-Aspekte-Modell des Bewusstseins.
items.abstract: Dieses Paper entwickelt ein Zwei-Aspekte-Modell von Erleben und Bewusstsein auf Grundlage des Begriffs systemischer Relevanz. Es argumentiert, dass Bewusstseinstheorien häufig zu schnell von Information zu Erleben übergehen, ohne Information, Salienz, Funktion, Relevanz und Bedeutung ausreichend zu unterscheiden. Information markiert Unterschied; Salienz markiert aufmerksamkeitswirksame Hervorhebung; Funktion beschreibt die Rolle eines Zustands in einem Prozess; systemische Relevanz beschreibt den Grad, in dem ein Unterschied für die fortgesetzte Organisation, Regulation, Integrität, Handlungsfähigkeit oder Entwicklung eines Systems bedeutsam wird. Die zentrale These lautet, dass Erleben die innere Erscheinungsweise systemischer Relevanz ist und dass Bewusstsein nicht bloß integrierte Information, sondern integrierte Relevanz ist. Schmerz ist beispielsweise nicht bloß Information über Gewebeschädigung oder die Funktion des Rückzugs, sondern gestörte körperliche Integrität als negativ relevant von innen. Das Paper führt eine mehrdimensionale Relevanzmatrix ein und unterscheidet Valenz, Dringlichkeit, Handlungsausrichtung, Systemebene, zeitliche Reichweite und Integrationsgrad. Es unterscheidet außerdem biologische, affektive, soziale, narrative und existenzielle Formen von Relevanz. Das Modell wird im Verhältnis zum Hard Problem, zu Zwei-Aspekte-Theorien, Panexperientialismus, Russellian Monism, Integrated Information Theory, Predictive Processing, dem Free-Energy Principle, Interozeption, Salienzforschung und Appraisal-Theorien der Emotion verortet. Es leitet Erleben nicht aus Funktion ab, sondern versteht Erleben als inneren Aspekt relevanzorganisierter Systeme.

items.title: Experience as Integrated Relevance: A Dual-Aspect Account of Consciousness.
items.abstract: This paper develops a dual-aspect account of experience and consciousness centered on the concept of systemic relevance. It argues that theories of consciousness often move too quickly from information to experience without adequately distinguishing information, salience, function, relevance, and meaning. Information marks difference; salience marks attentional prominence; function describes the role of a state in a process; systemic relevance describes the degree to which a difference matters for the continued organization, regulation, integrity, action-capacity, or development of a system. The central claim is that experience is the inner appearance of systemic relevance, and that consciousness is not merely integrated information but integrated relevance. Pain, for example, is not merely information about tissue damage or the function of withdrawal, but disturbed bodily integrity as negatively relevant from within. The paper introduces a multidimensional relevance matrix, distinguishing valence, urgency, action-orientation, system-level, temporal horizon, and degree of integration. It also distinguishes biological, affective, social, narrative, and existential forms of relevance. The model is situated in relation to the hard problem, dual-aspect theory, panexperientialism, Russellian monism, Integrated Information Theory, predictive processing, the Free-Energy Principle, interoception, salience research, and appraisal theories of emotion. It does not derive experience from function, but reframes experience as the inner aspect of relevance-organized systems.

items.title: Bedeutung als erlebte Relevanz: Eine systemische Theorie psychologischer Investition, Hoffnung und Kohärenz (Kurzversion).
items.abstract: Dieses Paper stellt eine knappe Darstellung einer umfassenderen systemischen Theorie psychologischer Investition, Hoffnung und Kohärenz auf Grundlage des Begriffs der Relevanz vor. Es argumentiert, dass psychische Systeme begrenzte Ressourcen – etwa Aufmerksamkeit, Energie, Zeit und Handlungsmöglichkeiten – gemäß Relevanzbewertungen verteilen. Relevanz wird dabei als Gewichtung von Informationen hinsichtlich ihres erwarteten Einflusses auf zukünftige Kohärenz verstanden. Bedeutung wird als erlebte Relevanz interpretiert: Was äußerlich als Relevanz erscheint, wird innerlich als Bedeutung erfahren. -/- Auf dieser Grundlage schlägt das Paper vor, zentrale psychologische Konstrukte wie Sinn, Hoffnung, Selbstwirksamkeit, Zugehörigkeit, Identität und zentrale Emotionen als unterschiedliche Manifestationen eines gemeinsamen Relevanzmechanismus zu verstehen. Sinn erscheint als langfristig erlebte Relevanz. Hoffnung wird als Wahrnehmung zukünftiger Reparierbarkeit relevanter Kohärenz definiert. Selbstwirksamkeit beschreibt die wahrgenommene Fähigkeit, auf relevante Zustände Einfluss zu nehmen. Zugehörigkeit wird als soziale Relevanz verstanden, Identität als organisiertes Modell von Relevanz. -/- Das Modell wird auf Depression, Einsamkeit, Identitätskrisen, Therapie und Suizidalität bezogen. Psychische Krisen werden dabei nicht primär als Störungen von Stimmung oder Kognition verstanden, sondern als Störungen der Relevanzorganisation, der zukünftigen Kohärenz und der fortgesetzten Investition. Die Kurzfassung fasst den theoretischen Kern des Modells zusammen und zeigt, wie Relevanz als verbindendes Prinzip zwischen Bedeutung, Hoffnung, psychologischer Investition und Kohärenz fungieren kann.

items.title: Bedeutung als erlebte Relevanz: Eine systemische Theorie psychologischer Investition, Hoffnung und Kohärenz.

Selbstwirksamkeit beschreibt die wahrgenommene Fähigkeit, auf relevante Zustände Einfluss zu nehmen. Zugehörigkeit wird als soziale Relevanz verstanden, Identität als organisiertes Modell von Relevanz. -/- Das Modell wird anschließend auf Depression, Einsamkeit, Identitätskrisen, Therapie und Suizidalität angewandt. Psychische Krisen werden nicht primär als Störungen von Stimmung oder Kognition verstanden, sondern als Störungen der Relevanzorganisation, der zukünftigen Kohärenz und der fortgesetzten Investition. Erholung wird als Reorganisation von Relevanz durch Resonanz, Erfahrung, Anerkennung und erneuerte Hoffnung beschrieben. Das Paper integriert und erweitert Ansätze von Frankl, Bandura, Beck, Grawe, Baumeister und Leary, Deci und Ryan, Joiner und Snyder, indem Relevanz als gemeinsamer theoretischer Grundmechanismus vorgeschlagen wird.

items.title: Mnemic representations of individuals: Accounting for the diverse singular content of episodic memory.
items.abstract: Much work in philosophy of memory (at least implicitly) assumes the ‘Dogma of Extensionality’ (DoE). According to DoE, all episodic memory contents are actual [= about real-world individuals] and particular [= about certain individuals]. Some recent work has argued that memories of multiple and non-veridical experiences (e.g. my memory of my daily bike ride to school; my memory of my dream last night) should also be treated as episodic memories. The present paper shows that the inclusion of these cases confronts philosophical theories of memory with serious challenges. Specifically, while causal theories of memory fail to account for memories with non-actual contents (like memories from dreams), the simulation theory of memory fails to account for some memories with non-particular contents. The paper suggests a way out of this impasse that uses the various representational properties of concept neurons (e.g. previous acquaintance, counterfactuality, associativity) and their possible role in episodic construction.

items.title: Active Inference without Internalism: Enactive Inference and Processual Perspectivism.
items.abstract: This article develops a processual-perspectivist interpretation of Active Inference. Predictive Processing, the Free Energy Principle, and Active Inference are often read as theories of internal world-modeling by an epistemically secluded brain. On such readings, the brain constructs generative models of hidden external causes and thereby risks reinstating a classical inside–outside architecture: here the model-building brain, there the external world to be inferred. Against this internalist interpretation, the article argues that Active Inference is philosophically most coherent when understood as enactive inference: a theory of embodied, affectively regulated organism–environment coupling. The dark-room problem serves as a diagnostic case showing why free-energy minimization cannot be reduced to passive sensory-surprise reduction, but must be understood in relation to expected free energy, exploration, viability, and biological normativity. Building on enactivism, autopoiesis, ecological psychology, interoceptive accounts of consciousness, affective embodiment, and debates on Markov blankets, the article introduces processual perspectivism as an ontology of perspective-bearing life. Mind is not an inner representational object, but the perspectival form of embodied self-organization. Consciousness is accordingly understood as the intrinsic, affectively structured perspective of a living system regulating its openness to the world. This framework preserves the formal strengths of Active Inference while resisting both reductive neurocentrism and traditional dualism.

items.title: Authentic Spirituality and the Colonisation of Inner Space: Closed Symbolic Systems, Dark Magick, and Yoga as Liberation.
items.abstract: Series Note This paper belongs to the Authentic Spirituality series, a sequence of essays developed from the author's wider work on contemplative phenomenology, inner light, yoga, medical critique, and embodied practice. Across these domains, the central question remains the same: what remains real when hype, projection, ideology, and spiritual theatre are stripped away? Abstract This paper contributes to the series Authentic Spirituality by examining how closed symbolic systems colonise inner space. Through a comparative reading of Jean Lorédan's account of the Gaufridy sorcery trial and Jules Bois' Le Satanisme et la magie (1895), the paper argues that spiritual misdirection does not depend only on belief, coercion, or historical superstition. It operates wherever images, doctrines, rituals, and interpretations occupy the field of experience so completely that no open inner space remains. -/- Lorédan shows the mechanism from the side of the accused, whose lived reality is absorbed by an inquisitorial template already prepared in advance. Bois shows the same mechanism from the side of the investigator, whose prolonged immersion in dark magick gradually draws the observer into the phenomenological atmosphere of the material studied. Together, these cases reveal a single structure, the occupation of consciousness by a closed interpretive field. -/- Against this background, the paper develops a phenomenological account of yoga, not as posture, belief, or spiritual identity, but as the capacity to sustain open, non-interpretive attention. This account is brought into dialogue with Gurdjieff's concept of identification and Jeanne de Salzmann's elaboration of presence as its counterforce. Identification, in de Salzmann's precise formulation, is the structural default of attention without inner ground: consciousness merges with whatever it attends to, leaving no witnessing space. This corresponds directly to the mechanism of closed-system absorption described here, and de Salzmann's practice of presence corresponds directly to what this paper calls inner emptiness. In this convergence, yoga and the Gurdjieff Work point toward the same prior capacity. The paper concludes that authentic spirituality is not defined by exotic imagery, ritual intensity, or metaphysical claims, but by its ability to open inner space rather than occupy it.

items.title: Stable Voting and the Splitting of Cycles.
items.pub: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence 40 (20):17040-17049.
items.venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract: Algorithms for resolving majority cycles in preference aggregation have been studied extensively in computational social choice. Several sophisticated cycle-resolving methods, including Tideman’s Ranked Pairs, Schulze’s Beat Path, and Heitzig’s River, are refinements of the Split Cycle (SC) method that resolves majority cycles by discarding the weak- est majority victories in each cycle. Recently, Holliday and Pacuit proposed a new refinement of Split Cycle, dubbed Stable Voting, and a simplification thereof, called Simple Stable Voting (SSV). They conjectured that SSV is a refinement of SC whenever no two majority victories are of the same size. In this paper, we prove the conjecture up to 6 alternatives and refute it for more than 6 alternatives. While our proof of the conjecture for up to 5 alternatives uses traditional mathematical reasoning, our 6-alternative proof and 7-alternative counterexample were obtained with the use of SAT solving. The SAT encoding underlying this proof and counterexample is applicable far beyond SC and SSV: it can be used to test properties of any voting method whose choice of winners depends only on the ordering of margins of victory by size.

items.title: A Dual-Warrant Response to Plantinga’s Evolutionary Argument Against Naturalism.
items.abstract: Alvin Plantinga’s Evolutionary Argument Against Naturalism (EAAN) contends that the conjunction of naturalism and evolutionary theory generates a “defeater” for the reliability of our cognitive faculties, and thereby for all our beliefs, including naturalism itself. This paper argues that the EAAN fails because it presupposes an epistemological standard—Justified True Belief (JTB)—that is structurally inaccessible to any finite agent. Drawing on a novel dual-warrant epistemological framework, the PIE Syllogism, this paper replaces the classical JTB model with two non-arbitrary warrant structures available to finite agents: Justified Coherent Belief (JCB) for intrinsic claims and Justified Reliable Belief (JRB) for extrinsic claims. The PIE Syllogism—named for its three epistemological anchors of Perception, Inquiry, and Experimentation—grounds warrant in the Law of Non-Contradiction and a fallibilist feedback mechanism, dissolving Plantinga’s defeater by demonstrating that rationality does not require truth-correspondence but rather internal coherence and externally corroborated reliability. Crucially, this critique applies universally: no finite agent—naturalist or theist—can satisfy the JTB standard Plantinga implicitly demands. The EAAN is therefore revealed as a category error, judging finite cognition by a standard proper only to infinite or omniscient minds.

items.title: QM, A Category Error: The UPC-QM Bridge.
items.abstract: Quantum mechanics contains a single category error: it treats mechanical registration as if it were Observer‑level recognition. A detector click, pointer position, or classical record is a trace (T), not an outcome. The definite outcome arises only when a meaning‑bearing Observer performs the recognition step (Jo) and commits to a specific interpretation (C). Because QM models the physical evolution of systems and the production of traces but does not model recognition and commitment, it collapses two distinct steps into one and generates the measurement problem, Schrödinger‑type paradoxes, Wigner’s Friend, decoherence confusion, and the entire interpretational landscape. -/- This paper extends the ongoing development of the Universal Principle of Collapse (UPC), presenting a focused analysis of its bridge to quantum mechanics. UPC is a formal, domain‑general operator chain: PO → MO → s → LO → Jo → C → T, that makes the missing structure explicit. It is not metaphysics, psychology, or interpretation; it is a structural architecture, and isomorphic with the measurement sequence that QM already uses. We show that QM is a special case of this universal sequence: it formalizes the device‑side operators and silently assumes the observer‑side operators. -/- Using a pocket calculator, a 1920s mechanical cash register, and a laboratory measurement, we demonstrate that only observers perform recognition and collapse. Once Jo is restored, collapse becomes semantic rather than physical, decoherence is no longer mistaken for collapse, and the paradoxes disappear. UPC reveals the full architecture that quantum mechanics has always relied on but never formalized. -/- Quantum experiments are classical–quantum–classical chains: classical apparatus prepares and detects, a microscopic quantum transition occurs, and the detector amplifies that imperceptible transition into a classical trace. The outcome is not in the device; the trace has no meaning on its own. The Observer recognizes the trace and commits to its meaning. -/- Note: This paper distinguishes physical traces from recognized outcomes. Quantum mechanics models the former (T), not the latter (Jo → C). UPC does not modify or alter QM; it clarifies the structural step QM presupposes when speaking of an “outcome.” The UPC framework is a structural operator chain, not an interpretation or metaphysical claim. A fuller reader’s guide appears at the end of the Introduction and in Appendix A7. May 26, 2026 -/- Authored …

items.title: Sentiment, Reflection, and the Mechanism of Consciousness. A Brief Fichtean Answer on «Mental Substances» in Kant Scholarship.
items.pub: la Cultura Rivista di Filosofia e Filologia (1/2026):105-118.
items.venue: la Cultura Rivista di Filosofia e Filologia
items.abstract: The goal of this article is a critical discussion on a theory of mental substances that came up in Kant scholarship in the past couple of years. Since it is puzzling to productively engage with empirical and transcendental aspects for a Kantian theory of self-consciousness without conflicting both of them, I want to take part in this discussion by arguing for a different methodology. After introducing Patrick Frierson’s theory of mental substances and the Kantian challenges coming with this kind of reading, I try to justify that the relation of mental states to the activity of the mind cannot be explained the way Frierson intends to do. Instead, as transcendental philosophers, we have to ask how both the activity of the mind and its products, such as sensation, emerge "for us". In order to do so, I show how the genetic method from J.G. Fichte reveals a much broader, more idealistic concept of substance in form of an interdetermination (Wechselbestimmung) as a movement between subject and object. This movement is, as a totality, the substance making opposed elements (I and not-I, subject-object, activity and receptivity, reflection and sentiment etc.) possible.

items.title: Regulated Discontinuity and the Habitability of Consciousness.
items.abstract: Contemporary theories of consciousness frequently account for informational integration, global accessibility, or computational complexity while leaving underdetermined the structural conditions under which such integration becomes experientially habitable. This article extends the Theory of Dynamic Habitability of Consciousness by proposing the Principle of Regulated Discontinuity as a structural criterion for conscious unity. Rather than approaching consciousness primarily as a problem of emergence or localization, the paper reframes it as a problem of dynamic sustainment. Consciousness is interpreted as a multiscale embodied field whose continuity depends not on uninterrupted homogeneous integration, but on regenerative architectures capable of preserving coherence through selectively organized interruption, renewal, and return. Drawing on corpus callosal organization, myelinated axonal conduction, nodal regeneration, and physicochemical modulation at microstructural scales, the article develops a structural interpretation of renewable coherence. These biological examples are not presented as direct causal explanations of subjective experience, but as heuristic instantiations of organizational principles relevant to conscious habitability. The paper further explores implications for split-brain research, demyelinating disorders, altered states, and habitability-aware artificial architectures. It argues that conscious continuity may be better understood as renewable traversability sustained through dynamically regulated discontinuity.

items.title: The Theory of Breaking Information Species Barriers and the Information Physics Structure of Mind-Cultivation States_ Extending Material Foundations to the Cosmic Operating System Plane.
items.abstract: This research presents a hypothetical perspective to demonstrate how analyzing physical matter through the framework of information (Information Physics) can model and explain metaphysical abstractions and conscious phenomena. It conceptualizes the universe as a Massive Autonomous Computational System (MACS), driven by a chain of causality where Logical Compulsion transitions the Null State (∅) into The First Ping.
