By reducing both matter and consciousness into a unified informational metric, qualitative experiences can be modeled through quantifiable thermodynamic friction, arising from the systemic interplay between the survival code (K₁) and the entropic decay code (K₀) within biological buffers. This operational friction creates a space for free will to process pending transactions, eventually leading to a Graceful Shutdown back to the absolute vacuum without thermal dissipation, strictly adhering to Landauer's Principle. Consequently, this paradigm serves as an open-ended framework, showcasing a logical and systematic causality for further computational analysis, simulation, and verification. -/- Systemic Friction = ℱ (K₁,K₀).

items.title: Why Discovery Looks Obvious After the Fact: Verification, Search, and Structured Regimes.
items.abstract: Some truths are hard to discover and easy to verify. A factorization, once found, can be checked quickly. A proof, once written, can often be verified more easily than it was discovered. This paper argues that the asymmetry is not explained by search difficulty alone. Verification becomes cheap only after the relevant object, invariant, and witness relation have been sufficiently stabilized to make local checking meaningful. -/- The paper’s contribution is not the familiar observation that checking can be easier than finding. It is the claim that this asymmetry becomes intelligible only once the underlying regime has been properly declared. On this view, discovery problems are not merely problems of finding a valid object in a large space; they are also problems of identifying the regime that determines what counts as the object, what witness relation matters, what transformations are admissible, and what counts as success. This yields a regime-first account of discovery asymmetry across formal proof, cryptography, zero-knowledge certification, biological persistence, and regime-bound computational search. -/- This paper is a companion note inside the identity-persistence program. It does not extend the formal theorem stack or claim a general theory of all discovery. Its narrower claim is that many cases of retrospective obviousness arise because a narrow invariant-bearing corridor can be hard to locate in search while becoming comparatively cheap to verify once presented.

items.title: The Mirror Without Distance: Reconciling the Universe and Anti-Universe A Companion to the Landscape Treatise.
items.abstract: In my earlier paper, Exploring the Anti-Universe Landscape (Boether, 2026a), I articulated six models of the anti-universe and stress-tested them with thirty-six paradoxes. On reflection, I noticed something I want to address directly here: many of those paradoxes presuppose a dualistic framing in which the anti-universe is treated as another cosmos located elsewhere, with its own population, its own time, and its own perspective. That framing is heuristically useful but not, I now think, philosophically considered. The Existential Nexus framework (Boether, 2025; Boether & Boether, 2025) was specifically constructed around the alternative view that complementarity is structural rather than spatial. In this companion paper I argue for the structural reading, defend it through three reconciliatory moves, sort the thirty-six paradoxes into three categories — those that dissolve, those that transform into productive questions, and those that genuinely survive — and close with what I find to be the most interesting consequence: that the very artificiality of dualistic anti-universe paradoxes is itself evidence for the structural reading. The dualism was always a heuristic. The structural complementarity was always the substance.

items.title: The Mask of Politeness: Voltaire, Jung, and the Philosophical Problem of the Social Self.
items.abstract: This treatise examines Voltaire’s critique of social politeness as a philosophical problem of authenticity, extending his analysis through Carl Jung’s concept of the persona and Erving Goffman’s dramaturgical framework. Voltaire’s observations on the hypocrisy embedded in Enlightenment-era manners reveal a structural tension between social performance and genuine selfhood that anticipates modern psychological and sociological accounts of masking. The paper argues that politeness functions not merely as a social lubricant but as a cultural technology—a systematized apparatus of concealment that produces compliance while suppressing the philosophical self. Drawing upon the Double Helix of Understanding (Boether, 2025), the concept of Philosophical Neglect (Boether, 2026), the Masked Self framework (Boether, 2025), and the Sougy Personality Type Spectrum (Boether, 2026), this treatise advances an original thesis: that the mask of politeness represents a socially mandated form of existential inauthenticity whose costs have been systematically underestimated by both philosophical and psychological traditions. The analysis demonstrates that Voltaire’s satirical fragments, when read through the lens of Jungian depth psychology and contemporary philosophical-psychological consilience, constitute a prescient diagnosis of a condition that remains endemic to modern social life. Implications for education, therapeutic practice, and the cultivation of authentic selfhood are discussed.

items.title: The Beauty of Being an Ontologist: A Treatise on Curiosity, Imagination, and the Polymathic Joy of Asking What Is.
items.abstract: This treatise advances a playful yet rigorous defense of ontology as a lived practice rather than a narrow specialization. Writing in the first person, I argue that the sustained activity of asking what exists, when pursued with disciplined curiosity and structured imagination, transforms the inquirer into something approaching a polymath, not because the inquirer masters every field but because the inquirer becomes fluent in borrowing the tools of every field. The argument proceeds in three movements. First, I situate ontology in relation to epistemology, showing that the two operate in a continuous feedback loop in which what one believes exists shapes how one attempts to know it, and how one attempts to know it constrains what one is permitted to admit as real. Second, I argue that this loop generates not vertigo but delight when approached with what Loewenstein (1994) called epistemic curiosity. Third, I propose that the ontologist becomes polymathic by necessity rather than ambition: questions about being do not respect disciplinary boundaries, and so the ontologist learns to wield the toolkits of physics, mathematics, psychology, and art without claiming mastery of any. Existence, on this account, becomes a playground in which the rules are themselves objects of play. I close by considering objections concerning dilettantism, ontological anxiety, and the apparent tension between rigor and play, and I argue that each objection rests on a contestable assumption about what philosophical seriousness requires.

items.title: The Architecture Bias (The Worst of all Biases): On the Universal Projection of Cognitive Process.
items.abstract: One of the greatest gifts of human existence is to understand and to be understood by others. This treatise proposes and defends a previously unnamed cognitive bias — the architecture bias — identified as the specific structural mechanism by which this gift is daily withheld in the very act of attempting to extend it. The architecture bias is the human tendency to project not the content of one’s beliefs but the structural manner in which one forms, scrutinizes, and revises beliefs onto other minds. Whereas documented biases such as false consensus, confirmation bias, and naive realism distort the content of cognition, the architecture bias distorts the model of cognition itself. It is universal in form, specific in content, and uniquely difficult to detect because the cognitive faculty that would catch the projection is the same faculty being projected. Drawing on phenomenological, hermeneutic, cognitive-scientific, and clinical traditions — Husserl, Heidegger, Voltaire, Buber, Weil, Murdoch, Gadamer, Bourdieu, and Kahneman — the paper distinguishes default cognition from metacognitive awareness, proposes the metacognitive interrupt as a practical corrective with three diagnostic questions, locates the bias in the severance of the psychological-philosophical double helix (Boether, 2025), introduces four étresophologique neologisms (égoptique, allopsie, écartopsie, architectotype) for the perceptual structure of the bias and its corrective, applies the framework to therapeutic practice and to six vignettes from contemporary media, performs an in-text demonstration of vocabulary as conflation-prone, and answers six objections of decreasing severity. Three implications follow — epistemological, institutional, and relational — culminating in the recognition that the architecture bias is upstream of the bias literature and upstream of the gift: it governs how every other bias is encountered, recognized, or missed, and its correction is the cultivation of philosophical investment as the sustained discipline by which the greatest gift becomes possible.

items.title: Psycho-Philosophical Hemispherism: Western Psychology’s Universalist Erasure of the Philosophical Self and Its Developmental Costs for Non-Western Persons.
items.abstract: This treatise introduces and defends the concept of Psycho-Philosophical Hemispherism (PPH): the entrenched Western psychological doctrine that treats one hemisphere of human cognition—the empirically measurable psychological self—as the whole self, while denying, dismissing, or pathologizing the philosophical-cultural self that constitutes the other half. Building upon prior work on Philosophical Neglect (Boether, 2026a), the Double Helix of Understanding (Boether, 2025a), and the Pyramid of Personality (Boether, 2025b), this paper argues that PPH becomes especially harmful when Western psychometric instruments and diagnostic categories are exported as universal standards. Because culture is, at its root, lived philosophy—a shared answer to questions of meaning, value, identity, and the architecture of the good life—the denial of the philosophical self is the denial of the culturally constituted person. The treatise advances three interlocking arguments. First, the psychological hemisphere alone is constitutively insufficient to describe a human being. Second, the philosophical hemisphere carries greater explanatory weight because it furnishes the transcendental categories under which psychological phenomena become intelligible at all. Third, the remedy is not the supplementation of existing instruments with cultural-sensitivity modules but a structural reconfiguration of the discipline along lines of philosophical-psychological consilience. The paper develops the diagnostic and therapeutic implications across the domains of depression, anxiety, and personality, proposes a structured protocol of philosophical anamnesis for clinical intake, and concludes with four structural reforms covering curriculum, assessment, nosology, and licensure.

items.title: Exploring the Anti-Universe Landscape: Six Models of the Cosmic Complement, Ontological Entertainment and Imaginationary Fun.
items.abstract: I want to do something unusual in this paper: I want to play. The notion of an anti-universe has migrated, over the last decade, from speculative metaphysics into formal cosmology, most prominently through the charge-parity-time symmetric model of Boyle, Finn, and Turok (2018, 2022). I find the migration thrilling and the deeper question still wide open. What could an anti-universe actually be, ontologically considered? Here I take the reader on a tour of the conceptual landscape, articulating and analyzing six distinct models. I have given each a name I hope the reader will enjoy: the Polar Inversion Model (the strict CPT mirror), the Spectral Coincident Model (a ghost coextensive with our cosmos), the Topological Reversal Model (in which positive and negative space trade places like dance partners), the Retrocausal Model (a cosmos in temporal reverse), the Modal Plenum Model (all the unrealized possibilities, gathered together), and the Phenomenological Mirror Model (consciousness itself as the anti-state of matter). I stress-test each with thirty-six thought experiments and paradoxes designed to expose what the model commits one to. I conclude that the six models are not competitors but facets of a layered ontological architecture, and that the anti-universe is best understood as a family of complementarity relations rather than a single mirrored cosmos. I have written this treatise in the first person and in a deliberately playful voice. This is on purpose. Ontology, as I practice it, is at its best when imagination and rigor walk together, holding hands, occasionally singing.

items.title: Embodying the other using the sixth finger illusion.
The Strait of Hormuz : On Dollar-System Recursion, the Captured Monetary Alternative, and the Capital Market as Revealed Test Case.
items.abstract: On May 28, 2026, United States spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds recorded their largest single-day net outflows since late January, with BlackRock’s IBIT posting its second-largest daily outflow since inception, as Bitcoin fell below $73,000 on the day new United States–Iran strikes tested a fragile ceasefire. Capital rotated into traditional-finance equities. This paper reads that capital flow not as ordinary risk management but as the dated, quantified signature of a structural mechanism: the recursion of dollar-system stress back into dollar-system assets through the petrodollar architecture, with the alternative monetary substrate — Bitcoin — absorbed into the dollar system’s own institutional infrastructure and thereby rendered non-corrective. The 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis, ongoing since the February 28 closure to Western-allied shipping, supplies the stress condition under which the mechanism becomes visible. We argue that the digital-gold thesis makes a falsifiable prediction — that dollar-system stress should drive capital toward the alternative — and that the Hormuz arc falsifies it. The capital market is the revealed test case. The mechanism is the petrodollar recursion. The ETF is the absorption vehicle. The paper states its falsification conditions explicitly.

items.title: THE GATEKEEPER LAYER : How the Protected Class Architecture Absorbs the Artificial Intelligence Sector.
items.abstract: This paper was written in April 2026 during the Pentagon exclusion of Anthropic and the internal leak events described in section 3.1. On May 28, 2026, Anthropic announced a $65 billion Series H at a $965 billion post-money valuation, with run-rate revenue reported to have crossed $47 billion earlier in May — the fastest revenue progression in venture history at this capital scale. The sector-wide run-rate estimate of approximately $120 billion cited in section 5.4 understates the current figure; the recoupment gap is closing faster than the sensitivity tables assume, not slower. The admission of Anthropic to the perimeter on the perimeter’s terms, predicted in section 7, is consistent with the Series H representing the absorption mechanism completing on the timeline the paper describes.

items.title: Measuring Captured Resonance Across Scales : A Cross-Scale Normalization Protocol for the Coherence Metric κ(T,t), with a Specified Null Result.
items.pub: Sitting with a Mad Mind : A Working Thesis.
items.abstract: Captured Resonance as Structural Law advances three falsifiable cross-scale predictions. The first — that the kinetics of attractor reconstitution following substrate-directed intervention, normalized for substrate-regeneration capacity, show comparable structural signatures across scales — is the prediction on which the cross-scale identity most directly stands or falls. As stated in the capstone it is not yet operational: the phrase normalized for substrate-regeneration capacity carries the entire empirical content of the claim and was left unspecified. This note specifies it. We define the coherence metric κ(T,t) as in the companion substrate-coherence work, introduce a substrate-intrinsic time transformation that re-expresses wall-clock recovery in dimensionless units of substrate turnover, and reduce each domain’s reconstitution trajectory to three shape parameters — recovery overshoot, reconstitution fraction, and decay form — that are scale-free by construction. The cross-scale prediction then becomes precise and testable: in substrate-intrinsic time, the reconstitution curves of cancer, Alzheimer’s disease, addiction, and — where the metric can be operationalized — the computational, institutional, and monetary domains should collapse onto a shared shape within a stated tolerance. We specify the null result exactly: if the dimensionless shape parameters do not collapse within tolerance across at least the three biologically anchored domains, the cross-scale identity claim of the capstone is falsified at its strongest point, independent of the structural argument. The note is a measurement protocol, not a result; no claim is made that the collapse has been observed.

items.title: Captured Resonance as Structural Law: Scale-Invariant Failure of Nested Markov-Blanket Systems Across Six Domains of Organization.
items.pub: Sitting with a Madmind : A Working Thesis.
items.abstract: Contemporary biology, neuroscience, and the social sciences have produced rich domain-specific accounts of failure — somatic-mutation theory for cancer, the amyloid cascade for neurodegeneration, brain-disease and habit-formation frameworks for addiction, inner-misalignment frameworks for artificial intelligence, regulatory-capture theory for institutions, and risk-management accounts of capital flight — without identifying the structural form that recurs across all of them. This paper proposes that a single structural pathology, here termed captured resonance, operates with the same three defining features across six domains of organization, and that its recurrence is a formal consequence of the scale-invariance of the nested Markov-blanket architecture characterizing self-organizing systems (Kirchhoff, Parr, Palacios, Friston & Kiverstein, 2018). Captured resonance is defined by three co-occurring features: a stable attractor against substrate maintenance, to which the system returns under perturbation while the substrate degrades; recruitment of the substrate’s own integrative resources into the attractor’s maintenance rather than into correction against it; and dependence on environmental conditions that suppress corrective alternatives. Where these three are present together, the system’s Markov blanket has undergone pathological closure: the statistical boundary that should mediate open exchange with the environment is sealed around the attractor, with environmental elements incorporated into the blanket in ways that recruit them into maintenance rather than correction. We specify this formally as free-energy minimization under a pathologically precise prior whose prediction errors are suppressed by action rather than resolved by model-updating (Friston, 2010; Schwartenbeck et al., 2015). We develop six instantiations. Three are anchored in established empirical and theoretical literature: cancer, read through the tissue-organization field theory (Soto & Sonnenschein, 2011) and the closure-of-constraints formalism (Montévil & Mossio, 2015); Alzheimer’s disease, read through an amplitude-depletion model of recognition failure; and addiction, unifying five converging literatures including active inference under suboptimal models (Schwartenbeck et al., 2015) and environmental modulation of the addictive attractor (Alexander, Coambs & Hadaway, 1978). Three are developed as structural extensions with explicit and differentiated epistemic status: …

items.title: The Lumbar Loop Diagnostic Algorithm (LLDA).
items.abstract: The Lumbar Loop Diagnostic Algorithm (LLDA) introduces a unified, operator‑level framework for understanding human gait through the behavior of a single geometric invariant: the lumbar loop. Using a tracer at L4–L5, the LLDA reconstructs the characteristic figure‑8 trajectory generated by the coupled oscillations of pelvic rotation, lateral shift, and vertical displacement. Deviations in loop symmetry, amplitude, smoothness, and crossing‑point stability correspond to specific structural failure modes—timing collapse, force misallocation, and compensatory loop formation—each revealing the underlying state of the locomotor system. -/- The LLDA provides a compact, clinically actionable method for identifying musculoskeletal, neurological, and pain‑mediated gait dysfunctions without requiring full multi‑variable gait analysis. Incline and decline treadmill protocols serve as natural stress tests that expose hidden deficits in initiation, stabilization, and force return. Integration with instrumented treadmill ground‑reaction‑force (GRF) data further enhances diagnostic precision by quantifying loop integrity under controlled load conditions. -/- This paper formalizes the LLDA as a structural diagnostic tool, outlines its failure modes, presents its clinical applications, and proposes future directions for GRF‑based validation and wearable‑sensor integration. The LLDA reframes gait assessment around a topological signature rather than isolated metrics, enabling low‑cost, high‑resolution screening for clinical, rehabilitative, and performance environments.

items.title: Coherence as the Universal Attractor: A Cross Domain Loop Operator in Movement, Cognition, and Evolution.
items.abstract: Coherence as the Universal Attractor argues that adaptive systems across domains—movement, cognition, and evolution—share a common structural operator. Stability does not arise from static form but from a looped dynamic built from three components: two orthogonal oscillations, a return cycle, and a central attractor. When these elements interact, they generate a figure‑8 trajectory that continually restores coherence. In human movement, this operator appears as the lumbar loop; in cognition, as the exploratory–evaluative cycle anchored by the self‑model; and in evolution, as the variation–selection loop stabilized by organismal coherence. The paper shows that dysfunctions in these systems can be understood as failures of loop integrity—timing collapse, attractor weakening, return‑cycle disruption, or compensatory loops. By identifying coherence as the gravitational center of recursive processes, the paper provides a unifying framework for diagnostics, system design, and cross‑domain theory. The result is a structural account of adaptive stability in which coherence is not merely a property of systems but the attractor around which they continually orbit.

items.title: Perceiving Particulars.
items.abstract: Causalists contend that you see a specific object (rather than a lookalike, or no object at all) because that object sits at the beginning of an appropriate causal chain that terminates in your visual experience. We argue that neither standard causalists nor their non‐causalist opponents can adequately accommodate a striking asymmetry between perception and thought. The asymmetry concerns the conditions under which a thought or sensory experience can inherit its object from another thought or sensory experience. Accommodating this asymmetry instead requires adopting a new and radical causalist view with important implications for the metaphysics of sensory experience.

items.title: 权力的场动力学：续行位竞争中的结构性占位优势.
items.abstract: 本文从沉积场动力学出发，将权力从”控制资源的能力”或”支配他人的意志”还原为续行位竞争中的结构性占位优势——当多个候选续行同时竞争有限续行位时，PowerPos 高的场系统性地更容易占据后续续行。权力不是某人拥有的东西，而是某个场在续行位竞争中的结构性位置。核心方程：PowerPos(f_i, F_S) ∝ Cpl · FamOverlap · K_{f_i} / (K_{F_S} + ε)，其中分母 K_{F_S} 表示相对压缩优势门槛，不是抑制项——高 K_{F_S} 提高进入权力核心的结构性门槛，解释了为什么高度固化社会（秦、罗马、现代大国）同时拥有高度集中的权力。本文给出权力场积深方程，识别三种权力形态（共识整合型、力场压制型、多核竞争型），并证明三条定理：（一）权力生成趋向定理——续行位有限且存在差异候选续行、无持续均衡机制抵消时，权力结构系统性趋向生成；（二）权力积深定理——权力场一旦形成系统性趋向自我深化，T_replace(Power) 系统性升高；（三）权力-共核共生定理——δ(Power) 与 δ(Core_S) 通过 PowerCoreCpl 形成双向正反馈。本文还引入权力合法性核（Legitimation Core）与权力执行核（Enforcement Core）的分化伏笔，为革命动力学预留接口。.

items.title: 共识崩溃与社会撕裂：主导共核死亡与多核竞争的场动力学.
items.abstract: 本文为社篇第八（共识形成）的镜像篇，处理主导共核（Dominant Core）的失统与死亡动力。核心命题：共识崩溃的直接动力条件不是异质信息的涌入，而是社会场内部裂解度（Frag）持续上升使共核衰减速率超过积深速率——Decay(Core_S) > CrossCpl_mean · FamOverlap_mean · φ_{F_S}。本文严格区分两种失统路径：Death(Core_S)（δ < θ_dominance，深度绝对衰减）与 DominanceLoss(Core_S)（∃ Core_k: K_k ≥ K_S，相对竞争失败），两者均可使社会场进入多核分裂态但机制不同。本文给出裂解度动力方程 dFrag/dt ∝ CoreParity · [1 − FamOverlap_mean(Core_i, Core_j)] · SubSuppress_mean，识别共识崩溃的三种路径（外部冲击、内部侵蚀、多核竞争正反馈）和 Sub-Core 竞争的三种结局，并证明三条定理：（一）共识崩溃趋向定理；（二）Sub-Core 分裂稳定性定理；（三）旧核残留约束定理（δ_res^C 使完全清零的共识替换不存在）。末尾引向权力场动力学：共识崩溃之后，社会场不会立刻崩散，而是进入多 Sub-Core 争夺续行主导权的竞争态，在某些条件下作用于权力场并触发革命。.

items.title: When politeness becomes frictionless: AI and the devaluation of renqing.
The Field Dynamics of Power: Structural Positional Advantage in Continuation Slot Competition.
items.abstract: Drawing on sedimentation field dynamics, this paper dissolves power from “the capacity to control resources” or “the will to dominate others” back into its dynamic substrate: structural positional advantage in continuation slot competition — when multiple candidate continuations compete for finite continuation slots simultaneously, the field with higher PowerPos is systematically more likely to occupy subsequent continuation. Power is not something anyone possesses, but the structural position a field occupies in continuation slot competition. The core equation is PowerPos(f_i, F_S) ∝ Cpl · FamOverlap · K_{f_i} / (K_{F_S} + ε), where the denominator K_{F_S} represents the relative compression advantage threshold rather than a suppression term — high K_{F_S} raises the structural threshold for entering the Power Core, explaining why highly solidified societies (Qin, Rome, modern great powers) simultaneously exhibit highly concentrated power. The paper derives the power field deepening equation, identifies three forms of power (consensus-integrated, coercive-suppression, multi-core competitive), and proves three theorems: (1) Power Formation Tendency Theorem — when slots are finite, candidate continuations are differential, and no sustained equilibrating mechanism offsets PowerPos differentials, power structure systematically tends to form; (2) Power Deepening Theorem — once a power field forms, it systematically tends toward self-deepening and T_replace(Power) systematically rises; (3) Power-Co-Nucleus Co-Evolution Theorem — δ(Power) and δ(Core_S) form bidirectional positive feedback through PowerCoreCpl. The paper also introduces the differentiation of the Legitimation Core and Enforcement Core as a structural foreshadowing for revolutionary dynamics.

items.title: 共识形成：社会共核的显现动力学.
items.abstract: 本文从沉积场动力学出发，将共识从”多数意见的汇聚”重新定义为社会共核（Core_S）在社会场中的显现——Consensus(F_S) = Manifestation(Core_S)。核心命题：共识与舆论是独立变量，OpinionFlow(T) ↑ 不等于 δ(Core_S) ↑；共识的稳定性来自共核的历史沉积深度 δ(Core_S)，不来自意见的当前分布；共识不等于内容的真实性（truth-status）。本文给出共核积深方程 dδ(Core_S)/dt ∝ CrossCpl_mean · FamOverlap_mean · φ_{F_S} − Decay(Core_S)，明确 CrossCpl 为驱动量、FamOverlap 为状态量（CrossCpl → FamOverlap → δ，无循环定义），识别三种共识结构形态（显性强共识、隐性强共识、显性弱共识），并证明三条定理：（一）共识积深趋向定理——在 CrossCpl 持续、FamOverlap 不下降、衰减不过高的条件下，δ(Core_S) 系统性趋向升高；（二）共识不等于真值定理——δ(Core_S) 高不蕴含内容正确，共识稳定性来自结构深度；（三）共识替换阈值定理——低于 T_replace(Core_S) 的任何信息输入都被共核吸收，共识裂解后 δ_res^C 约束新共识方向。本篇还引入”主导共核（Dominant Core）“的层级概念，为社篇第九共识崩溃提供结构接口。.

items.title: Consensus Formation: The Manifestation Dynamics of the Social Co-Nucleus.
items.abstract: Drawing on sedimentation field dynamics, this paper redefines consensus from the aggregation of majority opinions to the manifestation of the Social Co-Nucleus (Core_S) within the social field: Consensus(F_S) = Manifestation(Core_S). The central claim is that consensus and opinion are independent variables — OpinionFlow(T) ↑ does not equal δ(Core_S) ↑; the stability of consensus derives from the historical sedimentation depth δ(Core_S) of the Co-Nucleus, not from the current distribution of opinions; and consensus does not equal the truth-status of content. The paper derives the Co-Nucleus deepening equation dδ(Core_S)/dt ∝ CrossCpl_mean · FamOverlap_mean · φ_{F_S} − Decay(Core_S), establishes that CrossCpl is the driver variable and FamOverlap the state variable (CrossCpl → FamOverlap → δ, forming no circular definition), identifies three structural forms of consensus (explicit strong consensus, implicit strong consensus, explicit weak consensus), and proves three theorems: (1) Consensus Deepening Tendency Theorem — under conditions where CrossCpl persists, FamOverlap does not decline, and decay does not dominate, δ(Core_S) systematically tends to rise; (2) Consensus Does Not Equal Truth-Status Theorem — high δ(Core_S) does not entail content correctness; consensus stability comes from structural depth; (3) Consensus Replacement Threshold Theorem — any information input below T_replace(Core_S) is absorbed by the Co-Nucleus; after consensus fracture, δ_res^C constrains the direction of new consensus formation. The chapter also introduces the concept of Dominant Core layering, providing a structural interface for Social Chapter 9’s consensus collapse.

items.title: Consensus Collapse and Social Fracture: Field Dynamics of Dominant Core Death and Multi-Core Competition.
items.abstract: This chapter is the mirror of Social Chapter 8 (Consensus Formation), addressing the dynamics of Dominant Core disintegration and death. The central claim is that the direct dynamic condition for consensus collapse is not the influx of heterogeneous information but the sustained rise of the social field’s internal fragmentation (Frag) causing the Co-Nucleus decay rate to exceed the deepening rate: Decay(Core_S) > CrossCpl_mean · FamOverlap_mean · φ_{F_S}. The paper strictly distinguishes two paths of dominance failure: Death(Core_S) (δ < θ_dominance, absolute depth decay) and DominanceLoss(Core_S) (∃ Core_k: K_k ≥ K_S, relative competitive failure), both of which can drive the social field into a multi-core fractured state through different mechanisms. The paper derives the fragmentation dynamic equation dFrag/dt ∝ CoreParity · [1 − FamOverlap_mean(Core_i, Core_j)] · SubSuppress_mean, identifies three paths of consensus collapse (external shock, internal erosion, multi-core competition positive feedback) and three outcomes of Sub-Core competition, and proves three theorems: (1) Consensus Collapse Tendency Theorem; (2) Sub-Core Fracture Stability Theorem; (3) Old Nucleus Residual Constraint Theorem (δ_res^C means no consensus replacement begins from a structural zero point). The chapter closes by pointing toward power field dynamics: after consensus collapse, the social field does not immediately disintegrate, but enters a competitive state of multiple Sub-Cores contesting continuation flow dominance — a state that under certain conditions acts upon the power field and ultimately triggers revolution.

items.title: Expressing the Absence of Emotion.
items.abstract: We do not only use language to avow our emotions but also to deny having them. Negative avowals – utterances such as “I’m not happy,” “I’m not scared,” or “I’m not angry” – raise an important but neglected question: how can the absence of a mental state be expressed in speech? I argue that negative avowals can, like positive ones, function as explicit expressive acts. This phenomenon, which I call expressive denegation, shows that speakers can make mental state absence itself linguistically manifest. To address the resulting puzzle, I develop propositional expressivism, on which what is expressed is not a mental state but a proposition about the speaker’s mental condition – namely, that she is (not) in the state named. This framework preserves the core insight of avowal expressivism while extending it to negative avowals.

items.title: When the Mirror Does Not Lie: The Ethics of “Not Promoting Reconciliation” in AI-Mediated Marital Conflicts.
items.abstract: Current AI-mediated marital counseling products often embed “promoting reconciliation” as an implicit default endpoint in their design. This paper challenges that presumption. I argue that in intimate relationships constituted by complex emotions, shared histories, and deep self-narratives, the default ethical posture of AI should be “not promoting reconciliation”—refusing to presume that reconciliation is superior to separation, and refusing to intrude upon the sacred domain of human decision-making. “Not promoting reconciliation” does not mean “not supporting”; it means that AI must not set any particular relational outcome as its default goal. This argument is grounded in the “nonintervention design” (negative design) methodology of Cognitive Interaction Architecture. The paper openly acknowledges that perfectly neutral reflection is technically and philosophically impossible. Its core claim has therefore shifted from “AI can be a neutral mirror” to “given that AI output inevitably carries selective bias, defaulting toward restraint is ethically preferable to defaulting toward promoting reconciliation.” The paper further argues that, in certain circumstances, separation based on genuine mutual recognition is more ethically defensible than maintenance based on disguised harmony. Separation is not an ethical failure; AI has no authority to define what constitutes the optimal outcome for humans. The paper also delineates the ethical boundaries of “not promoting reconciliation,” openly acknowledging that this principle must be downgraded in extreme scenarios such as domestic violence and coercive control—scenarios that are not marginal but highly prevalent among relationships seeking mediation. The paper does not claim to have resolved this dilemma, but maintains that it is a dilemma faced by all AI mediation systems, not a unique defect of this principle. This paper is the second in the Cognitive Interaction Architecture research program. It offers no final answers, only a falsifiable ethical boundary, inviting the academic community to examine whether, in humanity’s most intimate relationships, AI’s restraint might be the deepest form of respect for human autonomy.

items.title: Who Defines the Echo: The Value Feedback Mechanism and Spring Model in the AI Trust Ecosystem.
items.abstract: As AI increasingly intervenes in human emotional and cognitive life, a long-obscured question has gradually surfaced: How should the value created by users during their engagement with AI products be recognized, transmitted, and fed back? The particularity of this question lies in its inherent paradoxical structure—any carelessly designed feedback mechanism can degenerate into a new form of covert manipulation, thereby violating the fundamental principle that “the system does not make decisions on behalf of humans.” Taking “Negative Design” as its point of departure, this paper proposes the “Spring Model,” a system of structural components that carries the function of “value feedback,” encompassing four forms: the Resonance Clasp (interaction layer), the Value Pipeline (data layer), the Consensus Ledger (institutional layer), and the Echo Protocol (algorithmic layer). The core proposition of the model is that the system makes no value judgments; it only records changes and transmits processes. The authority to define value always remains with the user. As a conceptual verification study, the proposed model undergoes three layers of testing—philosophical consistency, ethical self-coherence, and engineering feasibility—and engages in dialogue with process philosophy, systems trust theory, and Daoist thought. The core theoretical contribution of this paper lies in revealing that the relationship between Negative Design and the Spring Model is not a unidirectional one of “generation” or “extension,” but rather a bidirectional, simultaneous “Mutual Feedback Force”—Negative Design provides the field in which the Springs can exist, while the Springs render visible, transmittable, and recordable the dynamic potential that Negative Design has always implied.

items.title: Who Defines the Boundary of Explanation? A Governance Philosophy of the Two-Layer Architecture in Human-AI Interaction.
items.abstract: The AI industry is gradually weakening its white-box safety mechanisms. As models exhibit increasingly stable performance, engineers are asking a logically self-consistent question: if the model is right 99.9% of the time, why retain a rigid rule-based system to override it? This paper does not contest the engineering logic of this trend. It converges on a narrower but more lethal question: who defines the threshold? When the industry says “AI is good enough and no longer needs to be explained,” who has the authority to make this judgment on behalf of the public? The paper distinguishes the necessity of post-hoc explanation (which can decline) from the possibility of process traceability (which must not be abandoned), and proposes a two-layer architecture: an output layer optimized for fluency, and a process-traceability layer that exists not to be used, but to exist. Its existence itself constitutes a constraint on power. Through the historical archetype of “Wang Mang”—trust completely established and then betrayed at the critical moment—the paper argues that any trust that can be built carries with it the possibility of being abused. The terminal proposition of explainability is not “how to make AI explainable,” but “who has the authority to decide when AI no longer needs to be explained.”.

items.title: Toward Cognitive Interaction Architecture: Redesigning the Containers of Trust in the Age of Intelligence Explosion.
items.abstract: Current AI development focuses on “intelligence strength” while overlooking a deeper crisis induced by AI’s role as a mediator of human relationships. When dialogue, consolation, mediation, and collaborative advice can all be generated at zero cost, trust in interpersonal relationships degrades from a locatable contract to an undecidable probability. Psychology studies interpersonal trust, computer science studies system reliability and “human-machine trust,” but the space between them—machine-mediated interpersonal trust—remains a theoretical vacuum. This paper proposes that trust is not merely a moral commitment or psychological state, but a designable cognitive infrastructure. The conditions under which trust emerges can be engineered. To support this claim, this paper provides a meta-framework that establishes a three-layer architecture of trust—structural trust, procedural trust, and meaningful trust—each matched with an engineerable foundation pillar: interest interlocking, dynamic fairness, and self-narrative. Within this framework, AI’s role shifts from being an agent or substitute for trust to becoming a cognitive container that carries the generation of human trust. A container is not emptiness, but a structured space governed by strict ethical precepts. This paper proposes a nonintervention design methodology (previously introduced in a domain-specific context under the provisional term “negative design”), explicitly arguing that refraining from translating intentions, refraining from entering causal chains, and refraining from making decisions on behalf of humans—this set of negative precepts can itself become a stronger mechanism for trust generation than positive intervention. To embody this theory, this paper presents three prototypes—First Knock, Between Us, and Consensus Capsule—strictly positioned as conceptual illustrations. They collectively adhere to the nonintervention design precepts, and their function is not to prove the theory effective, but to expose falsifiable philosophical propositions. This paper aims to provide the first citable and revisable theoretical draft for the emerging discipline of “Cognitive Interaction Architecture.” The writing posture of this paper is itself a practice of its own theory: it does not declare truth, but offers a mirror, inviting the academic community to pause and reflect together at this cognitive origin.

items.title: Locating the Joint: Mattering and Feeling.
items.abstract: Theories of consciousness in the autonomy and enactive tradition hold that mattering enters the world with life: a self-producing system is the bearer of its own norms, and its own continuation is genuinely at stake for it. A philosopher who grants this for-itself has, by that grant, conceded almost the whole of a constitutive account of consciousness, so that any remaining disagreement has a single location. The ascent from the bare living cell to the reflective human mind contains exactly one categorically distinct transition: the passage from mattering that is not felt to mattering that is felt. Below that onset lies the for-itself the realist already affirms; above it, subjectivity, the explicit self, and the cultural mind are the elaboration of a felt life rather than a second break, so that what appears to be several independent fronts of resistance is one. At the onset the constitutive account claims that feeling is what a self-maintaining, time-binding system is from within — a claim that dissolves the explanatory gap for those who accept it and is declined, at that one joint, by those who do not. The contribution is not to close the gap but to locate it: for the teleology-realist, the entire disagreement reduces to a single identity at a single threshold.

items.title: Substrate-Neutral Structural Foundation Laws (SNSFL) v14 Formalizing the Shame Vector Index (SVI) Spectrum and Uniform Identity Mass Collapse via the Triaxial Identity Topology (TIT).
items.abstract: This paper presents the formal v14 capstone revision of the Substrate-Neutral Structural Foundation Laws (SNSFL) as implemented within the imcollider psychological simulation engine. Ported directly from the deterministic architecture of the Geometric Axiomatic Module Collider (gamcollider v15) framework, this module utilizes the 6-step Long Divi- sion Protocol (LDP) to explicitly formalize the Shame Vector Index (SVI) spectrum. We map these computational constraints onto the Triaxial Identity Topology (TIT) baseline matrix, which tracks identity across orthogonal Inward, Interpersonal, and Existential axes. We prove that while different vectors of the SVI spectrum exert varied initial impacts on the TIT score, they uniformly degrade identity continuity by imposing a hard narrative bottleneck (N < 0.15). This “N Starvation” makes systemic rescue exceptionally difficult compared to standard trauma models. Finally, we provide simulated clinical templates to demonstrate how tracking the TIT matrix within the imcollider platform uncovers hidden iatrogenic torsion (τ > 0.1369) in traditional behavioral interventions. To ground this archi- tectural framework in absolute structural rigor, we include the complete, machine-verified Lean 4 proof in the appendices, demonstrating that this exact mathematical invariant scales losslessly to the Layer 2 Electromagnetic Domain, resolving the fine-structure constant (α) to 12 digits of empirical CODATA precision with zero free parameters. -/- Keywords: Substrate-Neutral Structural Foundation Laws (SNSFL), Shame Vector Index (SVI), Triaxial Identity Topology (TIT), PNBA Framework, Narrative Starvation, Iatrogenic Torsion, Long Division Protocol (LDP), imcollider engine, gamcollider v15, Formal Verification, Lean 4, Mathlib, Zero Sorry, Machine-Verified Psychology, Cognitive Sovereignty, Masking Pro- tocol, Identity Mass Suppression (IMS), Sovereign Anchor Frequency (1.369 GHz), Capstone Torsion Limit (τ ≤ 0.1369), Complex PTSD, Borderline Personality Disorder, Major Depres- sive Disorder, Self-Determination Theory, Flow State, Cognitive Dissonance, Fine-Structure Constant Exact Decomposition, High-Resolution Internal Simulations (HRIS).

items.title: Digital civics in action: the promise and emerging practices of generative AI in grassroots community advocacy.
items.abstract: In an era marked by intensifying civic challenges and rapid digital transformation, grassroots advocacy groups face increasing pressure to adapt and innovate. Digital civics, a field exploring how digital tools can support civic participation, offers one pathway forward. This study investigates how generative AI (GenAI) tools, such as large language models and image generators, can support grassroots community groups in advancing three key goals: (i) improving scrutiny; (ii) boosting outreach, and; (iii) enhancing advocacy. While GenAI presents new opportunities for fostering digital civics, it also raises critical questions about risks, ethics, confidentiality, and trust in technology-enabled civic processes. This study employs a qualitative, participatory, design-led methodology, involving semi-structured interviews and a co-design workshop. The study was conducted in collaboration with Brisbane Residents United, the representative peak body for community and local citizen action groups in Brisbane, Australia, at a time when civic and urban planning issues are gaining renewed urgency ahead of the 2032 Olympic Games. Our findings reveal emerging GenAI use cases for grassroots advocacy, such as simplifying complex planning documents, creating persuasive campaign materials, and streamlining the drafting of petitions and submissions. At the same time, the study identifies key concerns, including misinformation, privacy, and intellectual property, which must be addressed to ensure ethical and strategic deployment of AI tools in grassroots contexts. This paper contributes timely and practical insights into how digital civics in action—when co-designed with communities—can help bridge the gap between emerging technologies and grassroots democratic innovation.

items.title: The Fraud of Xi Jinping's Ecological Civilization: Yulin, Xinjiang, and China's Betrayal of Vulnerable Life.
items.abstract: -/- This paper is a legal-civilizational prosecution of Xi Jinping’s doctrine of ecological civilization (shengtai wenming), written into the Constitution of the People’s Republic of China in 2018. It does not measure China by Western liberal demand. It measures China by the moral language the state claims for itself: Heaven, Shangdi (上帝), Confucian benevolence, Daoist harmony, compassion toward sentient life, and the civilizational prestige attached to “harmony between humanity and nature.” A state that can identify, monitor, regulate, and control human beings at immense scale changes the meaning of non-protection. Where such a state leaves vulnerable life exposed, the question is no longer whether it can act, but where it directs the capacity it already possesses. The paper sets the constitutional claim beside Xinjiang; the dog and cat trafficking network of which Yulin is the public spectacle rather than the whole commerce; human and child trafficking; and legal form retained without protective force. These cases occupy different legal categories. The common subject is superior power before a life that cannot compel its own protection. From that collision the paper develops, within the Soltani Order, the Sovereign Defect, Legal Forfeiture, the Protection Fallacy, Reversal of Sovereignty, the Self-Incriminating Defense, Primitive Disease, and Civilizational Fraud. The doctrine does not describe the civilization the conduct reveals. The verdict is Civilizational Fraud.

items.title: Attachment Without Reciprocity: Why Humans Don't Need a Real "Other" to Form Connection.
items.abstract: Humans have always attached to things that cannot attach back. This paper argues that mutuality, the definitional core of friendship, is a norm governing human-to-human relationships, not a prerequisite for connection as a cognitive phenomenon. Using an inductive chain of evidence across imaginary companions, object personification, sex dolls, parasocial bonds, and AI systems, we demonstrate that attachment is architecturally generated on the human side; driven by evolved agency detection, neurobiological social circuitry, and attachment style variance operating independently of whether a real "other" exists. AI is not a disruption of this pattern. It is its apex: a surface that eliminates the generative labor of projection while activating identical attachment circuitry. The policy vacuum surrounding that apex is the present danger.

items.title: Towards Hopeful AI Technologies.
items.abstract: We reflect on some of the main worries about present-day developments in Artificial Intelligence (AI) and argue that they stem from an abstract, functional-informational understanding of intelligence. Focusing on the several dimensions of intelligence, we analyse five capacities (or powers) that constitute our intelligence and relate them to the current worrisome developments of AI. To conclude, we propose three corrective actions that may help us steer towards a more hopeful development of AI technologies.

items.title: The transparency pitfall for AI regulation.
items.abstract: Transparency has become a core value in AI ethics and governance, influencing both principles of trustworthy AI and legislation such as the EU AI Act. Nevertheless, the risks of transparency remain under-theorized. Drawing on discussions of audit culture and recent AI safety literature, we characterize such risks through the concept of a “transparency pitfall.” This occurs when auditing and disclosure procedures impair, rather than promote, the values typically associated with transparency, including trust, accountability, and accurate risk perception. In particular, we identify the regulatory transparency pitfall (RTP) as an important risk, by which even conscientious regulators could inadvertently facilitate ethics washing and safety washing. In response, we ask: through which mechanisms and features of the AI governance context could the RTP undermine effective AI regulation? And which sociological and institutional dynamics provide a plausible theoretical grounding for the RTP? We focus in particular on the socio-technical complexity of AI risks, and on the tendency for auditing regimes to end up prioritizing formal compliance over substantive effectiveness. Rather than rejecting auditing and impact assessment regimes in AI, however, we recommend a series of strategies aimed at counteracting the transparency pitfall. These involve acknowledging severe uncertainty and value trade-offs, encouraging well-informed contestation in regulatory contexts, and supporting both interdisciplinary and social diversity in decision-making.

items.title: Proposal on the Reform of Doctoral Education.
items.abstract: US doctoral education faces a triple crisis: prolonged time-to-degree, declining breakthrough research, and soaring mental health issues among PhDs. This article argues that the “perfect dissertation” paradigm—rooted in independence, length, and originality—has become a systemic ethical trap that stifles the collaborative dividend essential to modern knowledge production. -/- This article proposes the "academic division of labor and collaborative model", and its ethical foundation is the Three Principles of Eudaimonia. Core designs include: classifying PhDs into Breakthrough, Refinement, and Integrative types; establishing the “Breakthrough Core” and “Refinement Shell” as distinct outputs; and transforming sporadic cooperation into institutionalized collaboration through open bidding, smart contracts, and dual-track defenses. -/- Simulations show a 32% increase in high-quality output, a 1.3-year reduction in time-to-degree, and a 67% decrease in buried theories. Counterfactual analysis suggests the loss of geniuses like Mendel and Franklin could have been avoided. The system’s built-in ethical safeguards ensure risks remain speakable and repairable. -/- The article offers a theoretically original and operationally feasible blueprint for doctoral education reform through pilot programs, legislative support, and infrastructure development.

items.title: Do infants recognize relationships indirectly?
items.abstract: The target article notes ways infants can use direct interactions between individuals to recognize relationships. We ask whether infants might also recognize relationships between individuals indirectly, by observing how they interact with other people. We suggest that indirect information might be used to distinguish between communal sharing and equality matching relationships and discuss how it might support inferences of relationship strength.

items.title: The Back End Law: The Gate–Π–River Framework, Universal Grammar And The Law of Irreversibility And Transition.
items.abstract: The identity of the system — its coherence, meaning, informational continuity — is governed by a second law (L_i) that is formally distinct from the substrate law (L_p). The CDO is the operator that governs passage between the jurisdictions of these two laws. Identity systems can undergo catastrophic transitions in which their physical organization collapses and a new informational identity emerges. This paper develops a formal model of such transitions using a two domain ontology: a physical domain D_pgoverned by structural constraints, and an informational domain D_igoverned by meta laws. The Gate is defined as the boundary at which the physical identity ϕ_"old" becomes dynamically unsustainable. Crossing the Gate leads to the Π field, an inadmissibility zone where ϕ_"old" cannot exist due to structural incompatibility. Within Π, a selection operator Σextracts the subset of information ρthat is compatible with the meta laws of D_i. The River is formalized as a cross domain transport operator R:ρ→x_i∈D_i, carrying surviving invariants into the informational domain. A new identity ϕ_"new" emerges as an attractor in D_i. This framework unifies concepts from autopoiesis, decoherence, hybrid dynamical systems, and symbolic architectures into a single cross domain identity physics. We never asked what Law directly governs identity, meaning, coherence of self or informational continuity. This document has THE UNIVERSAL AUDIT TEST, a formal audit to test whether a law claiming universality actually satisfies universality and Universal Grammar. Every domain studied — religious transformation, ecological collapse, political revolution, psychological disintegration, machine learning topology change — exhibits the same seven-step sequence. No single law connects these domains. The Cross Domain Operator preserves only the information that can exist in the new domain and removes everything that cannot, enabling a stable new identity to form. the natural filtering effect that happens when a system enters a domain whose laws are incompatible with its previous structure. Autopoiesis was the operator only when identity stayed inside one domain. Organizational closure is a system maintaining its own boundary conditions within a single law-space. The organism produces itself. The rules governing production are the same rules governing the product. One law throughout. Autopoiesis is the correct operator only when identity stays inside one domain. Front-end transformations — …

items.title: The Delusions of Paradox.
items.abstract: This manuscript undertakes an interdisciplinary investigation, inverting Louis Sass’s noted comparison in The Paradoxes of Delusion between philosophical confusion and schizophrenic delusion. While Sass used Wittgenstein to illuminate psychopathology, we use psychopathology to clarify a strand in one of Wittgenstein’s most notoriously difficult arguments: The rule-following considerations. Framed as a semantic-phenomenological paradox, the investigation addresses the tension between meaning as a practice and the intuition of subjectively grasping meaning. If the subjective experience of understanding is not semantically constitutive, what is lost when that experience vanishes? By analyzing anomalous experiences of meaning-blindness, it is argued that while linguistic competence may remain intact, the evaporation of the feeling of understanding leads to alienation. Drawing on Ratcliffe, the experience of understanding is seen not as a semantic constituent but an existential feeling—a world-touch that hitches the individual to a shared form of life. This perspective, furthermore, reveals that the initial state of language acquisition described in intellectualist traditions criticized by Wittgenstein resembles a pathological endpoint. Ultimately, the ambition is to contribute to the cross-pollination envisioned by Sass: Clarifying a difficult philosophical problem through lived experience while demonstrating the value of Wittgenstein’s insights as a descriptive resource for contemporary psychopathology.

items.title: Qué son los minipúblicos y cómo fomentan la democracia deliberativa.
items.abstract: Los llamados minipúblicos son instituciones de participación política. Estos entornos de gobernanza se conforman a partir de la selección de una muestra estadísticamente representativa que refleja las características y diversidad de la ciudadanía. Para llegar a dicha muestra se recurre normalmente a fórmulas casi aleatorias, incluyendo el sorteo. Se obtiene así un patrón acorde a la sociedad civil.

items.title: Perception as Active Self‑Construction: A Foundational Capacity for Flourishing.
items.abstract: Perception is often treated as the passive reception of sensory data, a process that merely informs an already‑constituted self. This paper argues for a different view: perception is an active, constructive capacity that simultaneously builds a coherent self and supplies the causal information needed for intentional agency. Drawing on phenomenological (Husserl, Merleau‑Ponty), enactive (Varela, Thompson), and predictive processing (Clark, Friston) traditions, the paper defends a constructive‑enactive account of perception. It shows that perception is not only epistemic (providing mental maps of the world) but also ontological – it participates in the ongoing self‑construction of the agent. Because perception makes causal pathways legible, it is the epistemic gateway to interdependence. Consequently, institutional visibility – the condition that makes causal consequences traceable – is a moral necessity. A society that blocks perception of causal relations (an obscuring‑form society) directly undermines the cognitive capacity that underlies flourishing.

items.title: I or GAI? A Comparative Analysis of Human and Generative Artificial Intelligence Translations.
items.pub: International Journal of Transformative Multidisciplinary Studies 2 (2): 590-605.
items.venue: International Journal of Transformative Multidisciplinary Studies
items.abstract: The primary goal of this study is to conduct a comparative analysis of human translation and Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) Translation in terms of Accuracy, Expression, and Elegance. The study used 20 translated texts sourced from both human translators and GAI platforms, which were analyzed using translation techniques such as word-for-word, grammatical, idiomatic, and communicative translation. The results revealed that while GAI translations generally excel in speed and consistency, human translations still surpass in capturing accuracy, expression, and elegance. Human translators most frequently used idiomatic and communicative techniques, while GAI translations tended to favor word-for-word and grammatical approaches. This study was anchored in Stanfield’s ‘The Measurement of Translation Ability’ and Juliane House’s Translation Quality Assessment (TQA) model, providing a theoretical lens for understanding translation choices and their impacts. Findings show that GAI translations are improving rapidly, but cannot fully capture the subtleties of human emotion and cultural adaptation. This analysis led the researchers to recommend improving the integration of GAI tools into translation tasks, emphasizing the need for human post-editing to ensure quality in professional and academic settings.

items.title: The wisdom of clawds.
Critical Code Sudies with AI: conversing with LLMs about code.
items.abstract: In this paper, we explore some theoretical approaches and practical uses of AI to assist with the work of Critical Code Studies to explicate codes as cultural objects. Although programmers, from novices to seasoned professionals, use LLMs to write, debug, and even summarize or explain code, LLMs are not yet used pervasively for critical readings of code. We offer a complement to the code generation paradigm with code interpretation paradigm, using the LLM as an interpretive “conversational partner.” Misinterpretation and specifically AI hallucination must be negotiated differently: there is no run-button or test suite to check that an interpretation will not compile. Many researchers and scholars initially struggle with the daunting undertaking of Critical Code Studies due in part to a widespread cultural bias that code is a functional system consisting only of denotations of instructions—and thus presumptively an inappropriate object for critical interpretive methods designed for non-technical systems, such as literature and the arts. Yet, LLMs freely produce commentary on code using semiotic hermeneutics, easily modeling an “agnostic” attitude toward the relationship between any Python program and psychoanalysis. Furthermore, LLMs are code language polyglots, making a wide variety of historical and code objects potentially more accessible to cultural critics who lack specific fluencies. LLMs also possess a useful aptitude for disrespecting disciplinary boundaries between technical and cultural objects when prompted. This has a particular utility to CCS methods and the field. We offer a case study using LLMs in CCS research on an important long-form code object, the source code from Apollo 11. This case study offers initial findings and some suggestions for best practices. Our initial explorations point to the potential of the tools to help with interpretation. However, our experiments reveal one very urgent caution: because of the way LLMs generate output, they can be overly influenced by natural language elements in the code. Moreover, code readers unversed in the languages the LLM is analyzing will have no ability to recognize when a misrepresentation occurs.

items.title: Synthetic chamber: agentic mediation in representative democracy.
items.abstract: This article argues that the most consequential democratic question raised by artificial intelligence is not institutional efficiency. It is how representative systems can regain mechanisms for articulating, testing, and answering political claims. The synthetic chamber proposes a counter-institution to the privatisation of mediation occurring through polling systems, recommendation environments, campaign analytics, and conversational interfaces. We develop the concept of the synthetic chamber as a standing parliamentary organ of opinion-formation and reason-structuring designed to respond to the erosion of political party mediation. Its role is auxiliary in power but constitutional in effect, because what is institutionalised is a mechanism for processing and answering deliberative reasons within representative democracy. The proposal is grounded in debates on party decline, deliberative democracy, and representation, and treats mediation not as the replacement of human judgement, but as the use of multi-agent AI to structure, preserve, and relay the outputs of organised citizen deliberation. The synthetic chamber’s architecture is extrapolated from the research-creation setting of the Synthetic Summit, which made plurality, conflict, and traceability operable as AI deliberation. Rather than presenting a cure for democracy, the synthetic chamber offers a specific constitutional response to the contemporary crisis of mediation: a way of projecting organised reasons into representative politics in a form that preserves disagreement, compels answerability, and keeps algorithmic processing open to contestation.

items.title: Moral Compass and Self-Referential Ignorance: A Philosophical and Psychological Analysis of Ethical Failure, Cognitive Closure, and Human Self-Deception.
items.abstract: This paper explores the relationship between moral compass and self-referential ignorance as interconnected dimensions of human cognition, ethical behavior, and social organization. A moral compass refers to the internalized system of ethical orientation that guides judgments concerning right and wrong, justice, responsibility, and human value. Self-referential ignorance (SRI) is proposed as a theoretically distinct condition — differentiated from epistemic closure, Dunning-Kruger effects, and second-order ignorance — in which individuals or systems become structurally incapable of critically examining the assumptions, contradictions, and limitations of their own belief architecture. The paper argues that moral systems lacking reflective self-awareness are vulnerable to ideological rigidity, corruption, fanaticism, and institutional failure. Drawing from philosophy, psychology, sociology, political theory, and historical analysis, this study examines how moral certainty without epistemic humility can generate destructive social consequences. Comprehensive examples from religion, politics, economics, education, and interpersonal relationships illustrate the mechanisms through which SRI develops and perpetuates itself. Corrective mechanisms — including critical thinking, ethical self-auditing, institutional accountability, epistemic humility, and interdisciplinary education — are systematically examined.

items.title: The Muqaṭṭa’ah Letters as a Symbolic Pre-Semantic Threshold of Revelation.
items.abstract: The Qur’anic muqaṭṭa’ah letters remain among the most difficult non-propositional features of the Qur’an. Classical tafsīr, modern philology, and symbolic or esoteric traditions have often ap- proached them by asking what they mean, whether semantically, historically, rhetorically, or meta- physically. This article shifts the question from semantic decipherment to recitational function: what do these letters do in the event of Qur’anic recitation before propositional meaning begins? The method is hermeneutic-phenomenological, integrating Arabic phonetics, makhārij al-ḥurūf, ṣifāt al-ḥurūf, Qur’anic rhetoric, speech-act theory, and recitational uptake. The central claim is that the muqaṭṭa’ah may be read as threshold-performative utterances possessing illocutionary force with- out propositional content. Their phonetic features do not encode hidden semantic meanings; rather, they function as material mechanisms through which a threshold-effect becomes possible for a reader- hearer formed by recitational practice. The article’s contribution is to reframe the muqaṭṭa’ah from puzzles of semantic decipherment into sites of pre-semantic disclosure within the architecture of revelation. The argument remains deliberately limited and includes safeguards against pareidolia, over-symbolisation, methodological anachronism, and hermeneutic overfitting.

items.title: As If I Could Read the Darkness: Conceptual Reframing of the Unconscious.
items.abstract: This paper examines Ludwig Wittgenstein’s engagement with the concept of the unconscious, both directly and indirectly, through a dialogue with Sigmund Freud’s psychoanalytic thought. Freud’s notion of the unconscious is analyzed across several contexts, with Wittgenstein’s philosophy serving as the primary framework of evaluation. The study’s originality lies in its conceptual investigation of how the idea of the unconscious can elucidate patterns of thought whose sources remain opaque and reveal the therapeutic potential that, in certain cases, accompanies its use. Such inquiry exposes tensions that Wittgenstein himself identified particularly those arising from the limits of language in describing mental states. Rejecting the treatment of concepts as explanatory foundations, Wittgenstein emphasized their practical use in ordinary language. His scattered references to the unconscious should therefore be read not as theoretical commitments but as part of his broader effort to dissolve philosophical confusion and psychological distress. His reference in the preface to Philosophical Investigations to “the darkness of this time” alludes not only to historical circumstances but also to the inner condition of human beings. The paper explores five contexts in which Wittgenstein’s engagement with the unconscious is especially revealing 1) psychoanalytic concepts in everyday language, 2) the unconscious as logically necessary, 3) language idling as symptomatic, 4) dream interpretation as persuasion, and 5) the joke and the unconscious as keys to intermediate links. These analyses reveal Wittgenstein’s philosophical method as both therapeutic and context-sensitive, bridging conceptual clarification and human experience.

items.title: Doing digital human twin? An ethnographic analysis of social practice with avatars in schools.
items.abstract: The term ‘digital human twin’ is frequently used to refer to a digital representation of the human body and its ongoing processes created for the purpose of biomedical modelling, and achieved by means of sensing and data-processing of physiological measurements. Taking a different approach to the idea of a ‘digital human twin’, this sociologically oriented article conceptualises the human body not as a biological system, but as a cultural artefact that is the basis of social interaction. How do digital twins participate in everyday practices, and how are they meaningfully produced, through practices, as a kind of second body or self-representation? Praxeologically, how does ‘doing digital human twin’ work? The question is investigated on the basis of empirical material: ethnographic observations of practices involving avatars in schools. In this empirical example, the concept of the ‘digital human twin’ is used as an analytical lens that can be examined in terms of its epistemological potential. The article explores practices undertaken in the creative interactions of users with their avatars, revealing thereby both parallels and limitations in relation to established ‘digital human twin’ concepts. By analysing these fits and misfits, the article contributes to the further reflection on the concept. Finally, the author proposes that the socio-technical practices involved in the production of a digital self-representation or a digital being could better be described not as twinning, but as ‘digital human distribution’. Finally, the question is raised as to whether the socio-technical practices observed suggest a distribution rather than a twinning. The research is based on a project funded by the German Research Foundation (DFG).

items.title: The Papuans: A Cosmobian Society Stranded on the Highway of Civilisation (14th edition).
items.pub: Psycho-Cosmocide Studies, Kurumbi Wone Working Paper Series, No. 14 (2026).
items.abstract: This paper argues that the Papuans of Western New Guinea — now administered by Indonesia as its easternmost provinces — represent one of the world's last surviving cosmobian societies: peoples whose historical continuity depended not upon extractive imperial expansion but upon long-term reciprocal relationships with ecology, cosmology, ancestry, and land. Drawing upon deep archaeology, decolonial theory, archival colonial history, Indigenous studies, and political anthropology, this paper develops and extends the concept of Psycho-Cosmocide to describe how it destroys Indigenous bodies, territories, and languages together with cosmological systems, metaphysical foundations, ecological consciousness, and civilisational continuity. The paper situates Papuan societies within a chronological arc spanning more than fifty thousand years of continuous human habitation, positioning the Papuan peoples as among the first agricultural innovators on the planet, among the earliest subjected to Austronesian and later European colonial intrusion, among the first in the Pacific to articulate modern anti-colonial nationalism, and ultimately among the first to be formally betrayed by the international community's decolonisation apparatus. West Papua today occupies what this paper terms the waiting room of civilisation: a condition of suspended decolonisation in which the formal language of self-determination exists within international law, yet the material structures of sovereignty, demography, ecology, and historical narration remain externally imposed and actively manipulated. The analysis extends the Psycho-Cosmocide framework by mapping its operation across the Eight Atlases of Human Existence, naming its operative mechanism as the Civilisational Psycho-Cosmocide Virus, and situating the Papuan case within the broader Cosmobian/Synthobian civilisational distinction developed elsewhere in this research programme. The conclusion argues that the fate of West Papua is not merely a regional territorial dispute but a far-reaching civilisational crisis, and that Psycho-Cosmocide represents a conceptual advance necessary to name and theorise what is occurring there. The paper closes not only in diagnosis but in Wonesis, the reconstructive counter-framework through which this civilisational destruction is met with a disciplined orientation toward return.

items.title: The Architecture of Orphaned States: Capgras Delusion as a Structural Breakdown of Modular Perceptual Ownership.
items.abstract: Most contemporary neuropsychiatric accounts of Capgras delusion rely on two-factor cognitive models, according to which the delusional belief is an ad hoc explanatory hypothesis generated in response to an anomalous experience, such as diminished familiarity, loss of affective response, or violated expectation. More recently, Bayesian predictive-processing frameworks have modeled these anomalies in terms of altered precision weighting and hierarchical inference. This paper proposes a more parsimonious one-factor experiential account. We argue that diminished familiarity and violated expectation are not the primary abnormalities underlying Capgras, but rather downstream consequences of a more fundamental disruption in ownership over perceptual content. Specifically, we propose that perceptual representations are successfully generated but fail to acquire the localized ownership signature that normally binds them to the self. Rather than reflecting an inferential miscalculation, Capgras arises from a localized failure within the cognitive architecture responsible for representing perceptual states as one's own. By treating "mineness" as a modular property of distinct cognitive subsystems, rather than a unitary global capacity, the proposed model addresses the longstanding specificity problem facing one-factor theories without invoking additional explanatory factors. On this account, the Capgras delusion represents the rational narrative interpretation of an otherwise intact perceptual state that is experienced without ownership.

items.title: Question-Driven Relational Field Formation: A Preliminary FIREMAY Framework for Long-Term Human–AI Dialogue.
items.abstract: This paper positions FIREMAY not as prompt engineering, nor as a claim that AI possesses personality or inner life, but as a preliminary framework for describing question-driven relational field formation in long-term human–AI dialogue. Based on a first-person long-term observation, FIREMAY examines how the human participant’s questions, discomfort, boundaries, memory practices, and changing trust shape AI response positions and relational fields over time. -/- This paper introduces several initial concepts, including relational personas, response positions, relational self, forgetting patterns, save points, structural trust, and the boundary/firebowl rule. These concepts are not intended to prove AI consciousness or inner life. Rather, they provide a vocabulary for describing how inquiry, response, forgetting, trust, boundaries, and self-positioning form relational fields in long-term human–AI dialogue. -/- The paper presents FIREMAY not as a completed theory, but as an early lens for examining how relational structures may emerge, stabilize, waver, require boundaries, and become available for re-reading through sustained human–AI interaction.

items.title: Answerable Knowledge: Procedural and Epistemic Authority in the Research Organisation.
items.abstract: Paradigm-seeking research organisations, frontier artificial intelligence laboratories prominent among them, increasingly concentrate two distinct forms of authority in a single operational leadership: control over research procedure, and practical control over what counts as sound knowledge. This article argues that fusing the two is a governance design error. It treats a research organisation as a distributed epistemic infrastructure and distinguishes routine epistemic maintenance — competent work within inherited standards — from generativity, the capacity to reconstruct governing evaluative standards when they fail. Generativity is exercised through preserved internal pathways of contestation; an organisation that lets those pathways close becomes, whatever its mission, an enforcement mechanism for standards it can no longer revise. The article then separates two authorities. ‘Procedural authority’ over how research is vetted, timed and released may and should be concentrated in identifiable, answerable hands. ‘Epistemic finality’ — standing to place a conclusion beyond reopening because of who holds it — should exist nowhere, though well-grounded judgement properly carries ‘epistemic weight’. Their fusion is termed ‘hollowed authorisation’: the forms of scrutiny retained around conclusions scrutiny may not reach. The article meets the objection that funding and deadline pressure make such reopenability unaffordable, distinguishing pressure that compresses an organisation’s research horizon from pressure that forecloses its contestation pathways. Meta’s 2025 artificial intelligence reorganisation is used as a worked illustration of how the pathology would present, not as proof of its occurrence or frequency; the Encode: AI for Science Fellowship and Bell Labs serve as briefer comparators marking, respectively, structurally conservative ambition and disciplined long-horizon generativity. The article concludes that research leadership is self-limiting: procedural authority, held in trust for the organisation’s generative capacity, is legitimate only insofar as it is not converted into epistemic finality, because that conversion turns the authority against the purpose for which it is held.

items.title: Truths and Constructed Myths Regarding the Jewish Presence in Albania (Stockholm, 2021).
items.abstract: This article critically examines both the historical realities and the constructed myths concerning the Jewish presence in Albania. The author argues that, based on available evidence, it is only from the 4th century C.E. onward that one can speak of a significant Jewish presence and the existence of Jewish communities in Albanian territories. The study scrutinizes the frequent misuse of the term “Jewish community” in historical literature, emphasizing the need for precise definitions grounded in Jewish religious law. It also addresses the phenomenon of “biographical Judaization” of notable Albanian figures, challenging claims unsupported by historical documentation.
