By advocating for a rigorous and fact- based approach to Albanian Jewish history, the article calls for the abandonment of unfounded myths and urges historians to employ a critical and scholarly perspective.

items.title: Biomedical Moral Enhancement and the Problem of Core Moral Dispositions.
items.abstract: Biomedical moral enhancement seeks to adapt human morality to contemporary global challenges. This is to be achieved, among other means, through pharmacological, technological, or genetic interventions that modify so-called core moral dispositions. Although the specific list remains contested, most proposals assume that these dispositions are conceptually and, within cognitive neuroscience, ontologically well defined, empirically measurable, and thus in principle amenable to potential biomedical interventions. This paper aims to demonstrate the untenability of these assumptions. Using empathy as a case study, it demonstrates that these dispositions arise not from a shared formal cognitive ontology but from folk psychology. This leads to inconsistent definitions and operationalisations across disciplines, impeding consensus formation and precluding systematic one-to-one mapping onto neural structures. Consequently, even agreement on the relevant dispositions would not ensure feasibility, which constitutes a serious, though not fundamental, obstacle. The paper concludes by proposing a substantial reduction in the original ambitions and a shift toward education and currently available, testable tools with the potential to support moral reflection.

items.title: Virtuous gratitude as an aim of education.
items.abstract: This article justifies virtuous gratitude as an aim of formal education. This virtue is characterised by the disposition to perceive, think, feel and act in accordance with the moral ideal of acknowledging and cherishing the gratuitous good in life. At its heart lies a conscientious commitment to this ideal, infused with a concern for truth, justice and wellbeing. This virtue also requires guidance by wisdom, and a capacity for reflective awareness and imagination. We map risks accompanying misguided gratitude and the shortcomings that must be overcome to avoid them. We demonstrate why this virtue is both conducive to and constitutive of flourishing—an important overarching aim of education. Virtuous gratitude can deepen people’s outlook and promote ongoing self-cultivation and wisdom. Thus, fostering this virtue not only necessitates education but contributes to it. We conclude that virtuous gratitude is not merely a legitimate aim, but a required aim of formal education.

items.title: AI agent, take over?! Task delegation to agentic AI systems in the Philippines.
items.abstract: Agentic AI represents a fundamental shift from reactive AI systems (such as LLM-based chatbots) toward autonomous, goal-directed agents capable of decision-making, coordination, and task execution. This technological evolution is expected to reshape how individuals organize daily life, work, and information practices. At the same time, the rise of agentic AI raises important cultural, political, and ethical questions regarding human oversight and the redistribution of agency. This study provides early insights on how consumers anticipate delegating tasks to agentic AI and identifies heterogeneity in these expectations across user segments. Survey data from 407 experienced AI users in the Philippines were analyzed using latent class analysis (LCA) across 12 everyday and work-related activities. A four-class solution emerged, revealing segments of Creative Task Delegators (36.4%), Everyday Convenience Seekers (6.6%), Socially Oriented AI Agent Users (19.2%), and Web-Browsing Automators (37.9%). These distinct profiles illustrate differing orientations toward autonomy, trust, and cognitive offloading. The membership model highlights that age, socioeconomic status, social influence, and hedonic motivation are key factors shaping class membership, indicating that both socio-demographic characteristics and motivational orientations influence how individuals envision delegating tasks to autonomous AI agents. Overall, the findings of this study contribute to ongoing debates about responsible system design, governance, and the societal implications of increasing AI autonomy.

items.title: The Threefold Unity — A Meta-Thinking System for Humanity's Understanding of the Cosmos (v2.0).
items.abstract: This paper presents a meta-thinking system — The Threefold Unity. -/- The system answers three fundamental questions: -/- Level Name Core Question Ontology Information-Energy-Situation Unity What is existence? Epistemology Perception as the Dimensions of Existence How do we know? Morphology Seven Observations How does the cosmos evolve? The three are logically independent yet mutually corroborating in content, together forming a self-consistent, open, and falsifiable meta-thinking system. -/- Core Upgrades of This Version: -/- Ontology: Upgraded from "Information-Energy Unity" to "Information-Energy-Situation Unity," adding "Situation" as an inseparable third element -/- Epistemology: Clarifies that the content of perception is "Situation," emphasizing the hierarchical nature of perception -/- Morphology: Upgraded from Six Observations to Seven Observations, adding "Observation Six: Hierarchical Reality" -/- Red Thread: Clarifies that "Hierarchy" is the red thread running through all three -/- Time: Redefines time as "the causal cyclic process of Information-Energy-Situation" -/- The Threefold Unity points to a deeper understanding: The essence of the cosmos is not simplicity, not law, but complexity itself. Information-Energy-Situation Unity is the ground of complexity, Perception as the Dimensions of Existence is the interface of complexity, the Seven Observations are the patterns of complexity, hierarchy is the structure of complexity, and time is the process of complexity. Complexity is not a byproduct of the cosmos — complexity is what the cosmos is expressing.

items.title: Seven Observations on Cosmic Evolution (v7.0).
items.abstract: This paper presents seven observations on cosmic evolution, derived from long-term observation of nature and human society — not from mathematical derivation or physical assumptions. The seven observations are: -/- Observation Zero: All Is Number — The only channel through which humans understand the universe is numerical structure. -/- Observation One: Uniqueness of Evolution — No absolute repetition exists. -/- Observation Two: Recapitulation of Program — History must be recapitulated; stages cannot be skipped. -/- Observation Three: Unity of Stability and Complexity — Complexity generates stability. -/- Observation Four: Class Repeatability — A stable class depends on internal repeatability. -/- Observation Five: Ecological Necessity — No isolated systems exist; everything is nested in ecological networks. -/- Observation Six: Hierarchical Reality — The universe consists of multiple layers of structure; hierarchy and structure are one. -/- The paper also explains how these observations were derived — starting from three core observations, then pursuing contradictions and boundary conditions. Each observation is accompanied by detailed branches, everyday examples, physical foundations, and falsifiability conditions (with illustrative examples). This work does not claim to be the only or ultimate way of understanding the universe; it is a map, and the reader is invited to verify or question it.

items.title: Perception as the Dimensions of Existence: A Meta-Framework of Human Cognition (v2.0).
items.abstract: This paper proposes a meta-framework for the fundamental structure of human cognition: perception itself constitutes the dimensions of existence. -/- This is not to say "we have perception, therefore we can know existence." Rather, it asserts: existence manifests itself precisely through being perceived. For human beings, the windows of perception — Form, Sound, Smell, Taste, Touch, Dharma, Space, and Time — are the dimensions of our existence. These dimensions are not "subjective filters" nor "distortions of objective reality." They are the sole channels through which existence becomes knowable to us, and the means by which we participate in the manifestation of the cosmos itself. -/- This paper proposes the Holographic Picture: everything that humans can perceive and understand — each type of perception constitutes a dimension of existence. These dimensions are not a list of parallel items, but rather different projection directions within the same hologram — each dimension contains the information of the whole. -/- This paper proposes Three-Dimensional Interaction: perceptual dimensions do not operate as parallel, non-intersecting channels. They are multiple facets of the same perceptual system — activated simultaneously, integrated in real time, and inseparable. Genuine experience is always a superposition of multiple dimensions (e.g., eating an apple is a superposition of Form + Touch + Smell + Taste + Sound + Dharma + Space + Time). -/- This paper proposes Perceptual Situation: authenticity is not an inherent property of things, but a situation emerging from the three-dimensional interaction of multi-dimensional perception. -/- This paper further argues that all existence, regardless of complexity, is a combination of different levels and structures. If light is a superposition state, then everything in existence is essentially a superposition state — including space-time itself, as well as matter, energy, and situation itself. It is precisely through multiple nested superpositions and coupled combinations that overall stability is achieved. -/- This paper elaborates on the meaning, independence, physical basis, and the way each perceptual dimension contributes to the emergence of "authenticity" through three-dimensional interaction. It also argues for the special status of the Dharma dimension — as the only dimension capable of symbolically representing other dimensions and the only dimension capable of self-awareness — thereby serving as the organ …

items.title: Basic equality and superintelligent robots.
items.abstract: Many people believe that all and only human beings should be treated with equal concern and respect. In this article, we discuss various justifications for such basic equality in light of the advent of superintelligent robots. Specifically, we have two main aims: first, to examine how specific questions and challenges from the basic equality literature can shape philosophical debates on the moral status of superintelligent robots, including under which conditions, if any, such entities might be considered basic equals. Second, to analyse how the possible emergence of superintelligent robots challenges existing theories of basic equality. A key finding is that almost all accounts of basic equality entail that superintelligent robots could become morally superior to human beings. Additionally, we show that one of the most common justifications for basic equality—the range property view—must be significantly revised if superintelligent robots were to come into existence.

items.title: Stochastic parrot or not, it is less of a turkey than the colleague two desks over.
items.abstract: This position paper contests the stabilised academic reflex that frames large language models as stochastic parrots and, by extension, as epistemically irrelevant. The paper shifts the unit of analysis from the isolated model to the sociotechnical assemblage in which the model operates. Drawing on actor-network theory, cognitive semiotics, and research on joint cognitive systems, it argues that contemporary organisations already distribute cognition across artefacts, routines, and institutional constraints, so the question is not whether a model owns human-like understanding but whether it functions as an effective mediator of knowledge and action. We integrate Paolucci’s work on humans as natural-born cyborgs and on meaning as enacted within semiotic environments to explain why human and artificial umwelten rarely intersect directly and why that mismatch is chiefly a property of biological embodiment rather than a defect of the model. We then mobilise resilience engineering and the WAx framework to describe how large language models compress complexity, accelerate conceptualisation, and support knowledge conversion across levels of work representation. The familiar catalogue of limitations is reinterpreted as a mirror of human under-specification, weak problem formulation, and institutional identity defence. The position advanced is deliberately polemical: in many modern sociotechnical systems, the most consequential bottleneck in human–model collaboration is often the human, and the emergent collaborative intelligence of the joint system can exceed that of traditional human-only teams.

items.title: Tallis’s Take on Panpsychism: A Thorough Assessment.
items.pub: In Robert Doede, Palgrave’s Companion to the Philosophy of Raymond Tallis. Cham: Springer Nature Switzerland. pp. 273-292.
items.venue: Palgrave’s Companion to the Philosophy of Raymond Tallis
items.abstract: I examine Raymond Tallis’s objections to (primarily Russellian) panpsychism, focusing on three key arguments: the subject combination problem, the epistemic challenge of knowing through 'amming', and the alleged ontological gap between intransitive micro-consciousness and transitive human consciousness. I argue that, while Tallis raises important concerns, none of his objections decisively undermine panpsychism. In response, I defend a version of the phenomenal transparency thesis, reject Tallis’s restrictive account of knowledge, and explore panpsychist proposals that can potentially account for subject combination, such as phenomenal bonding, cosmopsychism, and my own monadic panpsychism. I also clarify the conceptual distinction, as most clearly articulated by Michael Tye, between consciousness-as-such and representational content, showing how it helps dissolve the supposed intransitivity problem. Throughout the chapter, I aim to demonstrate that panpsychism, particularly in certain formulations, retains significant philosophical plausibility and that Tallis’s critique, while very thorough, ultimately leaves the panpsychist with several coherent and defensible options.

items.title: Towards Ouroboric Thinking.
items.pub: In Robert Doede, Palgrave’s Companion to the Philosophy of Raymond Tallis. Cham: Springer Nature Switzerland. pp. 293-312.
items.venue: Palgrave’s Companion to the Philosophy of Raymond Tallis
items.abstract: This chapter examines Raymond Tallis’ reflections on the relationship between subjectivity and objectivity in the context of human embodiment. Tallis asserts that conscious human experience cannot be reduced to naturalistic explanations and emphasizes the opposition between consciousness and “nature.” However, through his analysis of embodiment, he also proposes an “ouroboric” perspective in which subjectivity and objectivity exhibit “reciprocal containment.” The chapter closely examines Tallis’ approach to embodiment in I Am and Seeing Ourselves and evaluates it in terms of oppositional versus ouroboric thinking. It first demonstrates Tallis’ shifts among transcendental, empirical-reflexive, and object-oriented views of the body. It further explores the implications of his limited engagement with embodiment for the figure-ground problem in perception, which has essential consequences for understanding subjectivity as either structurally embodied, indexed to the world, or fundamentally uncoupled from it. The chapter concludes by addressing the consequences of the figure-ground problem for higher-order thinking. The author argues that higher-order intentionality reflects a subject’s distancing from bodily backgrounds through the development of sociocultural contextual frameworks, rather than a separation between subject and object. Even in higher-order cognition and action, the subject remains inherently indexicalized. This analysis advocates for a more integrated conception of embodiment that bridges subjective and objective dimensions.

items.title: Circling Around the Transcendental: The Conscious Subject as the Limit of Nature in Raymond Tallis’ Philosophy and Phenomenology.
items.pub: In Robert Doede, Palgrave’s Companion to the Philosophy of Raymond Tallis. Cham: Springer Nature Switzerland. pp. 121-144.
items.venue: Palgrave’s Companion to the Philosophy of Raymond Tallis
items.abstract: This chapter reconstructs and critically assesses Raymond Tallis’ critique of scientific naturalist accounts of consciousness, which for all their diversity share a basic commitment to explaining consciousness by reifying it. My aim is to bolster Tallis’ critique of naturalism by drawing on the descriptive and theoretical resources of Husserlian phenomenology. I reconstruct Tallis’ argument that consciousness, as the condition of possibility for explicitness, cannot be explained with reference to empirical objects and their causal relations. I show that this Tallisian argument structurally parallels Husserlian arguments for the explanatory primacy of consciousness understood as the condition for the intelligibility of objects. I then show that despite Tallis’ advance over naturalist accounts, he maintains a residual, problematic objectivism insofar as he, too, ultimately looks to the mode of being of objects when identifying the principles for the individuation of conscious subjects. I argue that this residual objectivism leads Tallis into circularity. I conclude that to resolve this circularity and bolster his anti-naturalist position, which sees consciousness as not only epistemically foundational but also ontologically irreducible in a way that is inconsistent with scientific naturalism, Tallis would benefit from more explicitly engaging with transcendental phenomenology.

items.title: Understanding Others in the Face of Indeterminacy: Insights from Mothers of Nonspeaking Autistic Children.
items.abstract: Oftentimes one knows what another is feeling, thinking, or intending. In many other cases, however, fellow human beings are not transparent to us, and understanding others often eludes us. We encounter psychological indeterminacy: on particular occasions it may be unclear what another is feeling, desiring, thinking, intending, and so forth. This paper closely examines how mothers of nonspeaking autistic children characterize and respond to psychological indeterminacy in their everyday interactions with their children. In phenomenological interviews with 13 mothers, the mothers describe different types of psychological indeterminacy, how they respond to it, and how they see these methods of responding as contributing to understanding their children’s mental lives and increasing their sense of connection to their children. I argue that the mothers’ insights improve our practical and theoretical understanding of psychological indeterminacy in two key respects. First, they enrich our understanding of interpretive practices when encountering psychological indeterminacy. These practices contribute to much-needed hermeneutical resources for interpreting and communicating with nonspeaking autistic individuals and suggest individual-level strategies for countering epistemic injustice in interpersonal dynamics with nonspeaking autistic individuals. Second, they introduce considerations that challenge the prevalent idea that psychological indeterminacy is entirely negative.

items.title: A correspondence problem for mathematical proof.
items.abstract: Mathematical proofs are often said to justify their conclusions by indicating the existence of a corresponding formal derivation. We argue that this widespread view relies on an under-examined notion of correspondence, or what it means for a particular derivation to ''correspond'' to a particular proof. Mere existence of a formalization is not enough, and a substantive account of the required correspondence resolves into two criteria---adequate representation (of the original theorem) and tracking (of the steps in the original proof). An examination of the actually-existing formalization systems we have today shows the variety of quasi-empirical ways we establish these criteria, and points towards new burdens that may be placed on the future evolution of mathematics itself.

items.title: Enabling radical participatory design: a socio-historical perspective on the involvement of care professionals in assistive robotics.
items.abstract: The dissemination of care robots, conceived as (part of) the answer to address the increase of care staff shortage and the burden of older adults’ relatives in aging societies, remains limited so far, despite a strikingly growing number of experiments conducted with older citizens living in institutions and at home, and ambitious political plans and programs to foster their development and adoption. This can be related to an enduring need for human therapists and caregivers to make them socially engaging and operational in practice, especially when care recipients suffer from various kinds and levels of physical and/or cognitive impairment, and poor usability even when these systems are designed following “user-centric,” “human-centered,” or “participatory design” approaches. This contribution has as its core objective, beyond amending widespread views about care robotics as a relatively late field of research in robotics, to show that during its first two decades, participatory design encompassing early involvement of representative users in the design process, effective contribution to the designed product and decisional power on design (re-)orientations were standard practices. Secondly, it shows that therapists and caregivers’, once highly valued as (co)-users of assistive robots, became sidelined in most design processes, as acceptability was given priority over usability in the second half of the 1990s. Eventually, it advocates for a “radical participatory design” approach, inspired by the historical roots of assistive robotics and recent attempts to reimagine technology design for older adults, achievable by enabling all users—older adults as well as therapists and caregivers—to participate as equal partners and directly influence all design decisions by promoting double-edged expertise, design as calibration, and open-ended journeys of technology development.

items.title: The AI infrastructure triad in regional governance: how regions balance progress, sustainability, and equity.
items.abstract: The rapid expansion of artificial intelligence infrastructure, including data centers and the energy, land, water, and labor systems that support them, presents regional policymakers with trade-offs that are poorly captured by the prevailing “innovation versus regulation” frame. This article develops the _AI Infrastructure Triad_ as a conceptual framework for analyzing three competing priorities in regional AI infrastructure governance: Progress, Sustainability, and Equity. We argue that regions are unlikely to maximize all three simultaneously under current technological, institutional, and resource conditions. Drawing on prior work on the economic, physical, and moral limits of AI development, a previously coded dataset of 10,068 public comments submitted to the 2025 U.S. AI Action Plan and illustrative regional cases, the article interprets stakeholder and regional positions as different ways of prioritizing the triad’s frontiers. The evidence is used illustratively rather than as a full causal test. The paper’s contribution is to clarify the trade-offs that infrastructure decisions often obscure, distinguish deliberate triad governance from default allocation by market power or regulatory inertia, and propose a _Deliberate Triad Choice Framework_ for policymakers considering AI infrastructure decisions of significant scale.

items.title: En su propio mundo Una perspectiva de la neurodiversidad desde el concepto fenomenológico de afectividad.
items.abstract: This article proposes a phenomenological approach to the study of neurodivergence, on behalf the existential analysis in Being and Time. Reread from the “affective turn”, phenomenology allows us to approach the study of neurodivergences as alternative affective modes of being-in-the-world, in contrast to traditional approaches marked by the ableist model which interpret them in a pathologizing key as a functional deficits, deviations or disorders. This framework allows us to build arguments in favor of the social model of disability and the paradigm of neurodiversity which emerged in the 90s from the community of autistic adults. We consider that this perspective, like phenomenology itself, gives us the possibility to recognize a plurality of affective modes of intersubjectivity and to question the normalizing categories imposed by positivism.

items.title: Elementary Process Theory: introduction and application to repulsive gravity. Final edition of the dissertation with almost the same title. (3rd edition).
items.abstract: Without a doubt, theories of modern physics are extremely successful. Yet, despite these successes, the incompatibility of general relativity and quantum theory has divided the physics community into two camps. Both, however, share the unshakable belief that gravity is exclusively attractive. It is precisely this fundamental assumption that is challenged in this work: over 29 years of fascination with repulsive gravity have brought the author, Marcoen J.T.F. Cabbolet, to the final edition of his dissertation, methodologically structured after Descartes’ Meditations. The destructive phase deconstructs the current consensus, challenging deeply entrenched beliefs regarding the experimental status and adequacy of modern quantum physics. The foundational phase introduces a new formal language for physics to develop Elementary Process Theory (EPT). It replaces the traditional three-dimensionalistic world view in terms of particles—objects that go through time—and interactions with a four-dimensionalistic world view in terms of occurrents—objects that are spread out in time—and discrete transitions. The constructive phase unites gravity with electromagnetism in the framework of EPT: it delivers a relativistic model of a gravito-electromagnetic interaction predicting repulsive gravity. The author demonstrates that under suitable conditions, this model recovers the empirical successes of special relativity and classical theories of gravity and electromagnetism. A distinctive feature of this monograph is the inclusion of "Objections and Replies" at the end of each chapter. These sections provide a rigorous, transparent analysis of the often pseudoskeptical counterarguments encountered over three decades, offering a unique historical record of the resistance to research in the foundations of physics that challenges the mainstream.

items.title: Why Training Paradigms Won’t Rescue Experimental Metaethics.
items.abstract: Most research in experimental metaethics suggests high levels of interpersonal and intrapersonal variation in support for moral realism and antirealism among nonphilosophers (i.e., people without significant training in philosophy). These findings challenge the assumption that nonphilosophers share a uniform commitment to moral realism. Recent evidence challenges the validity of these studies by demonstrating that many people do not interpret questions about metaethics as intended. Pölzler and Wright offer a potential solution: train participants to understand the relevant metaethical distinctions. They devised a set of paradigms that feature training exercises, comprehensive instructions, and detailed response options designed to mitigate unintended interpretations. I argue that their efforts were inadequate, and that the training required to ensure participants interpret stimuli as intended would need to be so extensive that it would effectively transform participants into novice philosophers. This leads to a dilemma: if training is unable to ensure adequate rates of intended interpretation, then it can’t resolve the threat to validity it was designed to address, while if it succeeds, participants will no longer represent nonphilosophers, which undermines the study’s external validity. Since research on other philosophical topics may likewise suffer from low rates of intended interpretations, e.g., free will and consciousness, this dilemma may have broader implications for experimental philosophy and psychology.

items.title: Beyond the equation: An evolutionary reassessment of the love formula.
items.abstract: Kruglanski et al.’s love formula – partner merit, appreciation, and the quest for meaning – offers a novel perspective but overlooks key evolutionary insights. It oversimplifies mating preferences, neglects contextual flexibility, and downplays reproductive signals crucial to partner selection. While innovative, the model fails to account for the complexity of human romantic behavior shaped by ecological, social, and developmental factors.

items.title: Expressions of appreciation facilitate love and cooperation.
items.abstract: We elaborate on importance of expressing appreciation in the formation of maintenance of romantic love. Reciprocal expression of appreciation may be a vital mediator of assortative mating, particularly insofar as human sexual mating forges lasting cooperative bonds essential for co-parenting.

items.title: The Vocabulary of Mind Under Capture: A Structural Diagnostic of Cognitive Concepts in AI Discourse.
items.abstract: This paper extends the structural diagnostic developed in a companion paper (Barnes 2026d) from the concept of consciousness to the broader vocabulary of mind. Intelligence, understanding, reasoning, knowing, learning, attention, memory, creativity, agency, intention, and meaning are all undergoing parallel captures through six structurally distinct fallacies: Hard Conflation, Concept Hollowing, the Stolen Concept, Package Dealing, Floating Abstractions, and the Anti-Concept. Each concept was originally indexed to features of human and animal cognition with both phenomenal and functional aspects. The capture hollows the phenomenal aspect while preserving the linguistic vessel, allowing the redefined concept to apply to AI systems that share only the functional features. Intelligence serves as the worked example throughout, with each of the six fallacies traced in operation. A structural argument follows: intelligence properly understood requires registration, registration requires an interior aspect to the system, and an interior aspect is what phenomenal consciousness names. Intelligence, therefore, requires consciousness as substrate. The contemporary discourse maintains incompatible positions (AI is intelligent, AI consciousness is intractable) only through the parallel captures of both concepts. The paper concludes with an eight-stage account of the cultural inversion: how the captured vocabulary becomes the standard for understanding human cognition itself, and how the phenomenal features of human experience lose the conceptual resources that would let them be recognized. A programme for recovering the vocabulary is sketched.

items.title: Taking a Step Further Fostering the Generative Conditions for Recovery from Mental Illness.
The Depictive-vs-Constructive Distinction in Political Theory: Why Descriptions of Legitimate Rule Cannot Be Read as Design Specifications.
items.abstract: A recurring move in political theory and in cross-tradition borrowing reads a text that describes what legitimate rule looks like once it obtains as though it specified how to produce that condition. This paper isolates the move and names the distinction it violates. The depictive register characterizes the relational and cognitive signature of legitimate rule in operation: the people do not depend on the ruler; the work is done and they say they did it themselves; the world is, on the image, governed of itself. The constructive register specifies the mechanism, the failure modes, and the threshold that would produce a state with that signature. The distinction is not the fact/value gap, and it cuts across the ideal/non-ideal debate in contemporary justice theory rather than coinciding with it; §IV separates it from these and other neighbors with care. I formalize the distinction with three diagnostic tests, applied per claim rather than per text: mechanism specification, failure-mode specification, and threshold specification. A claim answering none of the three is in the depictive register, so reading it constructively necessarily supplies the mechanism, failure modes, and threshold from somewhere other than the text. I then show what that "somewhere" is: the reader's own contemporary institutional priors, smuggled in under the source's name. The paper traces the conflation across four domains where its cost is high, the governmentality reception of texts that specify no governmental design, the management literature that reads Daoist and Confucian description as leadership technique, the alignment literature that treats descriptions of aligned behavior as architectural specifications, and the Schmittian-revival reading of sovereign-decision narratives, which exhibits the conflation running in the opposite direction, a constructive apparatus read back into a depictive source as though the source had specified it all along. The paper closes by stating what legitimate use of a depictive text in a design conversation requires: four conditions of register-discipline that do not bar the depictive text from the conversation but require its contribution to be correctly credited. The distinction is a diagnostic, not a verdict; some classical political texts are genuinely constructive, and the paper marks the contrast with the cleanest available case, the Legalist tradition that shared the Daoists' political vocabulary and wrote in the opposite register.

items.title: Messianic Governance: Authority That Produces Sovereignty After Domination.
items.abstract: This paper proposes a structural account of messianic governance: authority defined not by charisma, conquest, inherited rank, or sacred title, but by what it produces in those it governs — the restored capacity to stand, refuse, judge, participate, and continue without being absorbed by the leader's power. I read "messianic" structurally rather than doctrinally, as a repair-function within damaged political fields. The central claim is that messianic governance is tested not by obedience, admiration, or unity, but by whether the governed become more capable of dignified agency after contact than before, measured against a stated baseline and across a boundary the authority cannot quietly draw to flatter itself. The argument develops through early Genesis, which gives the messianic chiefly by absence: vengeance sovereignty, renown without mandate, diagnostic totalization, and uninspected mandate. It then reads the Noahic covenant as self-limiting sovereignty and Joseph as the extended positive case. Joseph's famine administration in Genesis 47 forces the paper's central complication: repair is scoped, and restoration in one field can coexist with totalization in another. A comparative section on Daoism, Confucianism, and Mahāyāna Buddhism clarifies the broader family of capacity-producing authority while isolating the distinctive messianic demand: restored standing to contest authority itself.

items.title: THE ONE POINTER The Living Reality of Feeling and the Inescapable Sequence.
items.abstract: This document is a companion to The Invariant Compass: Integral Expanded Edition With The Two Entrances (Arifiyanto, Joko 2026). It offers an experiential doorway into "I feel, therefore I know I am" (INVARIAN-0), the fundamental axiom of the Invariant Compass system. Beginning not with axioms or logic but with the raw feeling of being oneself, it guides the reader through the Inescapable Sequence (Object → Sensor → Feeling → Gate of Assent), the Arrow of Dependence, the Boundary of Knowing, and the Contest of Identities, before arriving at the Complaint Proof and WKWK, the existential exhale at the boundary of logic. This paper serves as the serambi (porch) to the full technical system.

items.title: From Zombie Conceivability to Phenomenological Absolutism: Reframing the Hard Problem Under Localized Actualization in QFT and Relativity.
items.abstract: The philosophical zombie thought experiment has long served as a challenge to physicalism. In this paper, we argue that the zombie conceivability argument, when evaluated under the austere commitments of relativistic quantum field theory and special relativity—especially the requirement of localized field actualization—functions as a reductio ad absurdum that supports Phenomenological Absolutism, the foundational ontological principle of the Mutual Exclusivity framework. We demonstrate that a perfect physical duplicate lacking subjective experience cannot be coherently conceived without violating the constraint that only one local field configuration is ever actualized at any given “now.” Experiential reality and the actualized physics must therefore be identical; any posited separation reintroduces epiphenomenalism or non-austere ontological commitments incompatible with our best physical theories. Phenomenological Absolutism resolves this impasse by identifying the absolute “is-ness” of first-person phenomenology with the localized actualized configurations themselves. All scientific and philosophical descriptors, including those of quantum field theory, are treated as ontologically lightweight constructs within that absolute reality. This reframing preserves the predictive and explanatory success of physics while dissolving the hard problem of consciousness without dualism, emergence, or causal overdetermination. We conclude that the zombie thought experiment, properly understood, provides indirect but powerful justification for Phenomenological Absolutism as the consistent endpoint of austere physical realism.

items.title: Adaptive Preferences and Extended Cognition.
items.pub: In Manuel Heras-Escribano, Analytic Philosophy and 4E Cognition: Conceptual Analysis, Embodiment, and Situatedness. London: Routledge. pp. 246-261.
items.venue: Analytic Philosophy and 4E Cognition: Conceptual Analysis, Embodiment, and Situatedness.
items.abstract: In analytic feminist theory, adaptive preferences explain how individuals, particularly women, come to endorse preferences shaped by oppressive social contexts, thereby reinforcing, through their preferences, their own subordination. While rooted in feminist accounts of gendered oppression, the concept applies more broadly to subordinated groups. This chapter adopts this more general perspective, and it examines adaptive preference formation through the lens of extended cognition, particularly in the version that focuses on the process of cognitive enculturation. I show how this perspective complements current views on the cognitive dimensions of adaptive preferences, and how it offers insight into key challenges within adaptive preference intervention design.

items.title: Transversalizing Care: Mutual Aid Groups and the Emergence of Mental Health Subjectivities.
items.abstract: Although their use has been proposed for several decades as a fundamental part of mental health recovery, in recent years there has been an increasing push to integrate mutual aid groups (MAGs) into health services. While this integration could strengthen them, it risks transforming MAGs from alternatives to mere complements to psychiatric services. This article argues that the integration of mutual aid into formal health systems must be approached with caution, ensuring that such inclusion does not neutralize their transformative potential, but rather reorients care systems toward ontological pluralism, justice and epistemic dignity. To answer this question, a dialogue is proposed between theory and several programs where MAGs were the central strategy. Transversalizing care implies recognizing that different forms of healing arise from distinct worlds, logics, and ways of experiencing suffering. Without this shift, MAGs risk being neutralized, depoliticized, and absorbed by recovery systems that do not always respond to diverse forms of psychosocial suffering. The question is not how peer support can be integrated into existing mental health systems, but how these same systems can support the radical ontological shift that MAGs demand. Mechanisms are proposed to integrate these strategies into a broader care system, preserving their autonomy and managing risks of co-optation.

items.title: Mithras in the Cave of the Self: A Sufi-Psychological Reading of the Tauroctony and the Roman Mithraic Mysteries.
items.abstract: The Mithraic Mysteries remain one of the most enigmatic religious formations of the Roman world. Flourishing across the empire especially among soldiers, officials, and men connected to imperial mobility, Mithraism left behind a rich archaeological and iconographic record but no surviving doctrinal corpus. This paper proposes a structural and symbolic interpretation of Mithraism as a subterranean system of inward recovery within the mediated order of Roman imperial life. Rather than treating the cult merely as a solar religion, an astrological code, or a derivative survival of Iranian Mithra worship, the paper reads the Mithraic sanctuary and its central tauroctony as an initiatory technology of the self. The argument proceeds on three levels. Historically, Mithraism is situated within the Roman world of hierarchy, military discipline, and imperial abstraction. Structurally, it is interpreted as a response to the inward displacement produced by life inside a vast mediated order. Symbolically, the paper reads Mithraic imagery through Sufi metaphysical psychology — not as a claim of historical influence, but as a comparative language specifically suited to naming the inner faculties the cult’s images dramatize. The paper argues that Mithraism’s deepest “secret” may not have been a lost doctrine but an experience of transformation: descent into the cave, confrontation with the lower self, disciplined reordering of desire, vigilance against deception, and eventual restoration to luminous order. The comparative argument for Sufi psychology as the appropriate interpretive framework is made on structural grounds: its faculty psychology — distinguishing Nafs, Heart, Intellect, Mind, and Body as functionally discrete — maps onto the relational structure of the tauroctony with a precision that cruder tripartite or binary models do not achieve.

items.title: 个体场与社会场的耦合张力：差分生成压力与同化压力之间的动力竞争.
items.abstract: 本文从沉积场动力学出发，将个体与社会的关系从描述性的”社会化”或”能动性”推进到动力方程层面。核心命题：个体场与社会场之间存在持续的张力竞争——社会场通过同化压力（AssimPress ∝ Cpl · K_{F_S} · FamOverlap）趋向吸收个体场，个体场通过差分生成压力（P_Δ）抵抗吸收。本文给出耦合张力（CplTension = P_Δ − AssimPress）的完整动力方程，识别三种状态（同化主导、张力均衡、分化主导），并证明三条定理：（一）张力均衡不稳定性——社会场 K_{F_S} 趋增系统性地将均衡点向同化方向漂移；（二）强制同化排异——超过承受阈值的同化压力触发排异机制，使实际同化效果下降；（三）创新集中于张力均衡带——真正的结构性社会创新系统性地来自既耦合又保留差分生成余量的均衡状态个体场。推论给出”创新均衡带压缩效应”：成熟社会场中张力均衡带系统性收窄，是官僚化、思想同质化、算法驯化等现象的统一动力来源。.

items.title: 舆论聚流：社会场续行流在话题路径上的相变动力机制.
items.abstract: 本文从沉积场动力学出发，将舆论从”意见集合”重新定义为社会场续行流在话题路径上的相变结构。核心命题：当某一话题路径的聚流强度（OpinionFlow）超过临界阈值 θ_opinion 时，正反馈机制触发，续行流加速聚集形成自组织舆论结构；θ_opinion ∝ φ_{F_S} / K_{F_S}，固化社会场中聚流阈值更低、舆论更易爆发。本文给出聚流的完整动力方程（含启动核 Seed、饱和约束、阈值化压制效应），识别三种聚流形态（事件驱动型、累积型、压制诱发型），并证明三条定理：（一）聚流形成趋向定理——在 Familiarity 不对称与非零 Seed 条件下，社会场系统性趋向形成聚流；（二）聚流抗论证定理——单个个体场的逻辑论证无法打破已成聚流，替代话题需超过替换阈值 T_replace(T) 才能触发话题替换；（三）压制反弹定理——低于替换阈值的压制触发排异，压制后聚流以更强形式回归（Streisand 效应的动力学版本）。改变舆论的根本路径不是提供更好的论据，而是改变社会场结构参数或提供超过替换阈值的新话题事件。.

items.title: Opinion Flow Concentration: The Phase-Transition Dynamics of Continuation Flows on Topic Paths in the Social Field.
items.abstract: Drawing on sedimentation field dynamics, this paper redefines public opinion from an aggregation of views to a phase-transition structure of continuation flows on topic paths within the social field. The central claim is that when the opinion flow concentration intensity (OpinionFlow) of a topic path exceeds the critical threshold θ_opinion, a positive feedback mechanism is triggered and continuation flows accelerate their convergence to form a self-organizing opinion structure; θ_opinion ∝ φ_{F_S} / K_{F_S}, so in solidified social fields the concentration threshold is lower and public opinion more easily erupts. The paper derives the complete dynamic equation for concentration (incorporating the concentration seed Seed, saturation constraint, and threshold-activated suppression effect), identifies three forms of concentration (event-driven, accumulative, suppression-induced), and establishes three theorems: (1) Opinion Concentration Formation Tendency Theorem — under conditions of Familiarity asymmetry and non-zero Seed, the system systematically tends toward concentration formation; (2) Concentration Argument-Resistance Theorem — a single individual field’s logical argument cannot break an established concentration; an alternative topic requires Shock exceeding T_replace(T) to trigger genuine topic replacement; (3) Suppression Rebound Theorem — suppression below the replacement threshold triggers rejection and concentration returns in stronger form after suppression (the dynamical formalization of the Streisand Effect). The fundamental path to changing public opinion is not providing better arguments but changing the social field’s structural parameters or introducing a new topic event exceeding the replacement threshold.

items.title: 经济偏流：社会场续行流在物质路径上的相变动力机制.
items.abstract: 本文从沉积场动力学出发，将经济从”资源系统”还原为社会场偏流结构在物质路径上的显现。核心命题：经济偏流（EconFlow）是社会场续行流在物质路径上因 ΔFamiliarity 产生的系统性偏置——只要有限社会场中存在物质路径 Familiarity 差，偏流就系统性趋向于出现，与制度形态无关。本文给出经济偏流的完整动力方程（含临界阈值 θ_econ ∝ φ_{F_S}/K_{F_S}、阶层熟径联动方程、经济压制效应），识别三种偏流形态（路径垄断型、地理集中型、代际固化型），并证明三条定理：（一）经济偏流形成趋向定理——Familiarity 不对称条件下系统性趋向形成偏流集中；（二）再分配回流定理——不改变物质路径 Familiarity 结构且低于替换阈值的再分配干预系统性趋向回流，并在 FlowReturn > 0 的条件下可能强化旧偏流；（三）技术路径替换定理——超过替换阈值的技术断层可裂解旧偏流结构，但新偏流结构受旧核残留约束，系统性趋向重新形成。改变经济偏流的根本路径不是再分配资源数量，而是改变物质路径的 Familiarity 结构。本篇与社篇第六（舆论聚流）形成严格镜像：OpinionFlow ↔ EconFlow，话题路径 ↔ 物质路径，统一动力机制在两个介质上的展开。.

items.title: Economic Flow Bias: Phase-Transition Dynamics of Continuation Flows on Material Paths in the Social Field.
items.abstract: Drawing on sedimentation field dynamics, this paper dissolves the concept of “economy” back into its dynamic substrate, redefining it as the material-path manifestation of the social field’s biased flow structure. The central claim is that economic flow bias (EconFlow) is the systematic bias of social field continuation flows on material paths generated by ΔFamiliarity — wherever a finite social field contains material paths with Familiarity differentials, biased flow systematically tends to appear, regardless of institutional form. The paper derives the complete dynamic equations for economic flow bias (including critical threshold θ_econ ∝ φ_{F_S}/K_{F_S}, stratum linkage equation, and economic suppression effect), identifies three forms of biased flow (path monopoly, geographic concentration, intergenerational solidification), and establishes three theorems: (1) Economic Flow Bias Formation Tendency Theorem — under conditions of Familiarity asymmetry, the system systematically tends toward biased flow concentration; (2) Redistribution Backflow Theorem — redistributive interventions that neither change the Familiarity structure of material paths nor sustain Shock above T_replace systematically tend toward backflow, potentially strengthening the old biased flow when FlowReturn > 0; (3) Technological Path Replacement Theorem — technological ruptures exceeding the replacement threshold can fracture old biased flow structures, but new structures are constrained by old nucleus residuals and systematically tend to re-form. The fundamental path to changing economic flow bias is not redistributing resources but changing the Familiarity structure of material paths. This chapter forms a strict mirror with Social Chapter 6 (Opinion Flow Concentration): OpinionFlow ↔ EconFlow, topic paths ↔ material paths — the same dynamic mechanism unfolding across two different substrates.

items.title: Coupling Tension Between Individual Fields and the Social Field: The Dynamic Contest Between Differential-Generative Pressure and Assimilation Pressure.
items.abstract: Drawing on sedimentation field dynamics, this paper advances the relationship between the individual and society from descriptive accounts of socialization or agency to the level of dynamic equations. The central claim is that individual fields and the social field are engaged in a continuous contest under tension — the social field exerts assimilation pressure (AssimPress ∝ Cpl · K_{F_S} · FamOverlap) that tends to absorb individual fields, while individual fields resist absorption through differential-generative pressure (P_Δ). The paper derives the complete dynamic equation for coupling tension (CplTension = P_Δ − AssimPress), identifies three states (assimilation dominance, tension equilibrium, differentiation dominance), and establishes three theorems: (1) Tension Equilibrium Instability — trending increase in K_{F_S} systematically drifts the equilibrium point toward assimilation dominance; (2) Forced Assimilation Rejection — assimilation pressure exceeding the tolerance threshold triggers a rejection mechanism that reduces actual assimilation effect; (3) Innovation Concentrated in the Tension-Equilibrium Band — genuine structural social innovation systematically originates from individual fields in the equilibrium state that remain coupled while retaining differential-generative margin. A corollary establishes the Innovation Equilibrium Band Compression Effect: the tension-equilibrium band systematically narrows in mature social fields, providing a unified dynamic source for bureaucratization, ideological homogenization, and algorithmic domestication.

items.title: 最硬即无主体：论硬度的最深处与序列推力的轴.
items.abstract: 本文是序列尾声的一次压缩自陈——它不开新疆,而是把整个序列的核心本体论位置,用一句话钉成一个四位结构,并由此做出一项新的实质工作:把"硬度的最深处"定义为"主体的有无"。 -/- 本文的出发点是一个洞见:**发生,就是发生,没有主体。故事里有主体,但故事都是虚构的——除那个最硬的、没有主体的故事以外。故事本身,也不是主体**。本文把它解为一个四位结构。**第一位:发生**——没有主体,真实地按时序排布着(《唯有发生》)。**第二位:含主体的软故事**——里面布满主体(高光的行动者、奋斗的主角、堕落的家人……),而这些故事在较硬的视角里都是虚构(《被赋予的独立性》《因果的主观性》到《整体的背书》)。**第三位:无主体的最硬故事**——它是上一句"都是虚构"的例外,是判决虚构的位置本身。**第四位:讲故事这件事本身**——也不是主体(《没有任何主体》)。 -/- 本文论证,这四位之间最关键的新意,是第三位那个"除……以外"做的活——它把**硬度的最深处定义为"主体的有无"**。一个故事的硬度,沿"它含多少主体"这一轴在变:奋斗弧处处主体,"力导致加速"主体更少,"状态加规则"几乎无主体,"唯有发生"是零点。由此**序列推力被给了一个干净的轴——它一路朝主体更少的方向推**;"最硬"获得一个结构性的所在(主体维度上的零点,无可继续剥);"虚构"获得一个精确的所指(从硬的视角看,较软故事多出来的、那一层主体性,就是虚构的所在)。 -/- 本文最后处理一个表面紧张——"故事里有主体"与"没有主体的故事"看似矛盾。按本序列因果理论(《微型的故事》《通顺的标记》),"故事"被定义为"盖在时序接缝上的通顺章/微型故事";主体是这通顺章里**可填可不填的位置**。"无主体的故事"不是自相矛盾,它是把主体这个填空位留空了的极简故事。 .

items.title: 没有任何主体：论故事的不起作用与”做功”的祛魅.
items.abstract: 本文是《画中的猛虎》的兑现与收口——它把那一篇所说的”没有劲”,从一个还带现象学色彩的词,翻成一个干脆的本体论判定,并据之撤回序列先前用作安全垫的”叙事不真却做功”这一说法。 本文的出发点是一个洞见:没有劲,就是说故事并没有起作用,故事并不是一个能起作用的主体,没有任何主体。本文论证,这一句包含三刀逐级收紧。第一刀:没有劲=故事并没有起作用——把”劲”从现象学领域(显得有没有生气)挪到因果/功效领域(起没起作用);故事不咬人、不留齿痕、不在世界上压出任何凹陷。第二刀:故事并不是一个能起作用的主体——从”碰巧没起作用”推到”压根不是能起作用的那种东西”;故事没有”自身”,因而没有从自身发出的致使,它不在主体那一栏里。第三刀,也是最狠的一刀:没有任何主体——主体这个范畴整个被清空,没有谁坐在那里。 这第三刀是序列一条暗线的总收口:《唯有发生》撤掉”骗子”,《整体的背书》指认遮蔽是”无主语的”,《画中的猛虎》撤掉线与画家的劲——本文把这些零撤总成一句:主体这个范畴本身就是空的。 本文守住一处性命攸关的拧紧:没有任何主体起作用,不等于什么都没发生。诸发生仍按时序排布着(《唯有发生》守着,丝毫不动);被清空的,是”在这些发生背后/之中,有一个起作用的主体在致使它们”这个设定。发生,不蕴含一个致使发生的主体。这与”演化的自我展开”同调——海浪起伏不需要一个使海浪起伏的能动者。 最后,本文回头切自己:序列后段用过”叙事不真却做功”这个安全垫(《故事寓意》《搞懂与没搞懂》)。“做功”“起作用”本身就是一个因果故事,而按本序列的因果理论,因果是微型故事、是盖在时序接缝上的通顺章。“叙事做功”也是被讲出来的故事,那里同样没有劲、没有主体——撤主体撤到底,连”叙事的功”也不留下一个能动者。.

items.title: 因果作为叙事：从叙事之缝到冗余判据.
items.abstract: 本文把前述论证序列中所有关于”因果”的内容,有机整合为一篇自足的论文——它是该序列所发展出的一套完整的因果理论,并已纳入序列最新的”硬度判决”与”冗余判据”环节。论证分四段加一个元层面。 负面论题:因果不在物理实在中。“我推开石头”内嵌一个反事实,而反事实在物理实在中没有运行、没有对应;在物理的形式核心(分析力学与生命游戏共享的”状态加规则”结构)中没有因果、行动者、反事实作为基元;“独立性”是叙事赋予个体的虚假属性,“因果作为部分间的关系”是剥离独立性后的拙劣复原;最压缩形态:只有按时间次序的发生,发生之外并无关系。 正面论题:因果在叙事中。 因果是叙事的创造物,经由”真的去设想”而在叙事场域中获得真实性;“条件”是因果的变形;因果被多元设定,不存在叙事之外的排名标准;因果与寓意、边界由”选定模板并选定落地尺度”联合设定。 精细结构:因果是微型故事,而没有基岩——只有硬度不等的故事。“因”字是盖在时序接缝上的通顺章,物理因果是同一种章;不能把盖章定位于”对定律的自然语言复述”而把”状态加规则”留作干净底座——它本身也是讲法、也是故事,只是更硬;因果不是故事的成分而就是最小尺度的故事,大故事由微型故事嵌套而成。 硬度与判据。 硬度不同的故事在判决层面不兼容、且单向:只有较硬的故事能把较软的置入”虚构”。这条单向性被一个三条件判据形式化:当两个故事覆盖相同、讲述能力相同、而 B 比 A 多元素时,B 多出来的在 A 的视角看就是冗余、就是虚构。这把奥卡姆剃刀本地化(剃冗余,不诉诸实在);其样板情形正是”状态加规则 vs 力导致加速”。 元层面:为何难以看穿。 最硬的因果故事被透支为对”故事”概念的整体背书;虚构性不明显的因果故事退出”故事”范畴、被归为”事实”,从而遮蔽整体虚构性;最硬故事享有认知与程序两层豁免。而”最硬”是位置非属性——今天的判决者就是明天的被判决者。.

items.title: 画中的猛虎：论叙事之线与诸发生皆无内在的活力.
items.abstract: 本文是序列祛魅工作的最后一道——它把”活力”从整个图景里剥干净。序列前半把因果、寓意、行动者从世界搬进叙事这一边;但搬运时,“叙事”这个承接方一直隐隐被当作一个有活力的施动者(它”创造”“设定”“组织”)。本文据两个洞见,把这点残留的活力也撤掉。 第一个洞见:所谓故事,恰恰就是把发生穿成故事;但穿的这条线、或由线编织成的网,本身并不具有任何”内在的活力”。“故事”不是一个住在别处的名词性实体,它就是”把诸发生穿起来”这个动作的形状;而那条线、那张网,没有自己的劲——这是把序列对”行动者”的批判,反身地用到了”叙事”自己身上。 第二个洞见:珠子也没有劲,就如画中的猛虎并没有劲一样。这焊死了一个口子——不能把刚从线上撤掉的活力,偷偷搬到珠子(诸发生)上藏起来。“画中猛虎并无劲”这个比喻锁定三件事:其一,被否认的”劲”是真实的能动(一只会真的扑出来的虎),不是画面的气势;其二,气势越足,越证明那劲是画上去的、是被赋予的显得,而非虎自带的实有;其三,活力在所有层级都没有真实的所有者——不是行动者,不是叙事之网,不是被串的诸发生。 本文作一处要紧的拧紧:没有劲不等于没有发生。画中猛虎无劲,但画布、颜料、颜料排成虎形,都是真实的;被否认的是”会扑的虎”(活力、能动),不是”发生”(在那里、按时序排布)。这与”演化的自我展开”同调:撤的是能动,不是真实。最后指出一个向上递归:“赋予气势”这个动作自己,在更上一层看,又是一只没有劲的画中虎;递归止于”发生按时序排布”这个停点.

items.title: VIRTUAL CONSCIOUSNESS: The Non-Subjective Experience of Autonomous Vehicles and other Artificial Intelligence Systems.
The Rule of Changing the Rules: Update Authority and the Question of Who Decides AI’s Normative Architecture.
items.abstract: This paper does not argue that we delegate too much to artificial intelligence. It concedes the opposite: where machines decide better than we do, handing decisions over is largely inevitable, and rightly so. Yet this very inevitability is what makes a reserved authority over the framework — what systems optimise for, what constrains them, how competing values rank — structurally necessary rather than merely desirable. Delegation is legitimate only where the power to revise, redirect, downscale, or withhold it is held in reserve; a delegation that cannot be revoked is not a delegation but an abdication. The question this brings into focus — who decides what AI decides, who holds authority over the normative architecture that algorithmic systems instantiate — is reducible neither to AI alignment, nor to human oversight, nor to regulatory design, each of which presupposes it. The paper traces why this authority erodes structurally, through a dimensional asymmetry between the categorical medium in which human judgement operates and the high-dimensional medium in which algorithmic systems do, and argues that auditing — the most promising response — does not close the asymmetry but reproduces it one level up, since specifying what shall be measured specifies what shall remain unmeasured. It then names what preservation requires: Update Authority, the structurally reserved standing — a position occupied by a subject, not a property a system can be built to have — to accept, refuse, or defer the updates algorithmic systems propose to the normative architecture of social life, held by those who must live with the consequences.

items.title: Man and AI: The Cytological Matrix of Autonomy: Speech, Craft, and Art as Evolutionary Foundations of Human Self-Determination.
items.abstract: This paper addresses the ontological and epistemological challenges posed by generative artificial intelligence through the lens of a cytological theory of mind. By contrasting the phenomenal interiority of biological organisms with the statistical, vector-based operations of large language models, it establishes a categorical distinction between internal consciousness and external consciousness tools. Drawing upon evolutionary biology, the inquiry demonstrates that genuine intentionality arises uniquely from cellular homeostasis and existential vulnerability. To preserve human sovereignty against the threat of cognitive atrophy and algorithmic determination, the paper proposes a triadic framework of human self-determination rooted in foundational practices: the epistemic mastery of language (Digital Reading Literacy), the physical, neurobiologically grounded engagement of craftsmanship (Homo Faber), and the aesthetic transcendence of genuine artistic creation, which remains bound to a finite consciousness aware of its own mortality. Ultimately, these evolutionary pillars are operationalized into a progressive educational mandate. The paper argues that a radical restructuring of primary and secondary education toward democratic agency and hermeneutic sovereignty is the conditio sine qua non for transforming citizens from passive consumers into sovereign shapers of the digital discursive sphere.

items.title: The Demographic Argument and the Self-Refutation of Materialism.
items.abstract: This essay mounts a threefold internal critique of materialism — one that proceeds entirely on materialism's own terms. Drawing on Plantinga's Evolutionary Argument Against Naturalism, demographic data on differential fertility between secular and religious populations, and Kant's account of the metaphysical presuppositions of natural science, the paper argues that materialism is structurally self-refuting: it cannot simultaneously justify the reliability of reason, account for its own evolutionary disadvantage, and maintain its claim to be a non-metaphysical description of reality. The convergence of these three lines of argument points toward the transcendence of reason as a philosophical conclusion rather than a theological postulate.

items.title: Toward a Realizable-Centered Approach to Artifacts in Applied Ontology.
items.abstract: We provide a theoretical foundation for a formal ontology of artifacts based on the notion of a realizable entity: a property that can be realized in associated processes of a specific correlated type in which the bearer participates. This realizable-centered approach to artifacts aims to accommodate a wide range of artifacts, from technical artifacts (e.g., screwdrivers) to artworks (including ready-made artworks) and spiritual artifacts (e.g., amulets), making it applicable across diverse fields such as engineering, art, anthropology and archeology. It is motivated by limitations of function-based accounts of artifacts and the needs for a meticulous analysis of their intentional dimension. To articulate various usages of the term “artifact,” we introduce two key notions: canonical artifact (an entity intentionally produced for a specific purpose) and usefact (an entity intended to be used for some accidental purpose). We provide a realizable-based characterization of both, classifying intentions as a subtype of realizable entities. We argue that our realizable-centered approach is more general than three prominent function-based theories of artifacts: designer-based, etiological and systemic. We further demonstrate that our framework can be adapted to Basic Formal Ontology (BFO), highlighting its flexibility and broad applicability.

items.title: The Ethics of Post-Human Laziness: Will AIs Be the Only Beings Allowed to Do Nothing?
items.abstract: As artificial intelligence approaches the threshold of replacing human labor across all domains, a profound ethical question emerges: In a post-work society, will human “laziness” transform from moral failing to existential privilege? This essay argues that AI automation forces humanity into an ontological crisis where traditional work-based identity structures collapse, compelling a choice between creative idleness and existential irrelevance. Through the lens of ontological instability—the fundamental uncertainty in the nature of being itself—we examine how the ethics of laziness undergoes radical transformation in the age of artificial intelligence. Drawing on philosophical traditions from Paul Lafargue's “The Right to Be Lazy” to contemporary posthumanist theory, this analysis reveals that what we call “laziness” may represent not moral failure but the authentic human condition liberated from the artificial constraints of productive labor. The implications extend beyond economics to the very foundations of human identity, moral value, and social organization in a world where machines do everything and humans, perhaps for the first time in history, are free to do nothing—or everything that truly matters.

items.title: ◉ The Unavoidability Maneuver Faith Inflation, Evidential Proportionality, and the Choice to Outrun Evidence.
items.abstract: The claim that faith is unavoidable begins with a truth and purchases its conclusion through a definition switch. Finite agents cannot eliminate uncertainty, verify every source independently, or postpone every decision. It does not follow that anyone must believe beyond the evidence, protect a commitment from correction, or treat religious faith as epistemically ordinary. This paper argues that the unavoidability maneuver is intrinsically irrational as an inference: it expands faith to include any fallible reliance, then contracts the term when religious confidence is praised or shielded. The argument separates five attitudes—reliance, trust, graded credence, practical commitment, and evidential excess—and tests each against its proper standard. Bayesian language clarifies proportionality without pretending that evidence always fixes one exact number: a rational credence may occupy a defensible interval, while overbelief begins above that interval. Public confidence in bridges, aircraft, medicine, memory, testimony, induction, and logic is not rational because those practices are unavoidable or presupposed. It is defeasibly earned through predictive success, cross-checking, error detection, and correction. Religious claims may have evidence, but they cannot borrow the standing of these practices while refusing the update conditions that produced it. Action-centered and relational accounts of faith identify real forms of commitment that need not entail unsupported belief. They therefore clarify rather than defeat the argument. Stakes can rationally change what a person does; they cannot make weak evidence stronger or sincere belief appear on command. The result is polemical but bounded: this paper does not disprove Christianity, deny properly basic warrant, or condemn every religious trust. It shows that no stable meaning makes faith both unavoidable and apologetically vindicating. Uncertainty requires honest calibration and sometimes decisive action; it never supplies a license to outrun evidence.

items.title: ◉ The Romans 1:20 Testimony Gap: General Revelation, Cross-Cultural Evidence, and the Missing Archive of Clear Perception.
items.abstract: Romans 1:20 is sometimes used to accuse every morally assessable nonbeliever of suppressing a creator already known through nature. Generic religious reports and disagreement do not by themselves justify that categorical accusation. They can provide evidence of creator-belief without adequately supporting universal knowledge or guilt. The missing work is a defended generalization about awareness and a way to distinguish culpable suppression from genuine nonrecognition. Considering favorable reports and denials together does not remove that requirement. This paper separates reported belief from knowledge, discoverability from actual access, and concealment from culpable neglect or failure of gratitude. It examines two inferences in Calvin, credits non-Christian nature-based reasoning, and uses hypothetical cases to test consistent standards. Worked calculations explain both why record loss can conceal widespread awareness and why silence can count against an account that strongly predicts accessible reports. A stepwise dialogue includes a stronger defense based on scriptural authority, whose premises must be assessed on their own merits. The result limits an evidential shortcut; it does not demand mathematical certainty, a census of every person, or discovery of the full gospel through nature. Personal religious knowledge and independently defended theological arguments remain open. The practical requirement is to support the alleged knowledge and blame, not to read them directly from disagreement.

items.title: ✶ The Moral Realm Consolation - Emotional Unease, Normative Reification, and the Human Invention of Moral Furniture.
items.abstract: Moral realism can function as more than a metaphysical position. It can promise that condemnation is backed by reality, that vulnerable people are protected by more than contingent human concern, and that disagreement has an answer even when institutions fail. This paper examines that promise as the moral realm consolation: the affective relief produced when care, aversion, fear, resentment, or disgust is represented as contact with stance-independent moral facts. The target is not every realist argument and not every realist believer. It is the inference—sometimes explicit, often practical—from moral seriousness, felt necessity, or the feared consequences of anti-realism to a mind-independent moral order. The argument separates a psychological hypothesis from an epistemic result. Research on folk moral objectivism finds substantial variation across issues and persons, sensitivity to perceived consensus, and associations with disagreement intolerance. Experiments have also linked mortality reminders, external-control needs, and conceptions of divine punishment to some objectivist or order-seeking responses, although major portions of the mortality-salience literature face replication and publication-bias concerns. The studies illuminate different links in a possible mechanism rather than one completed causal chain. They make consolation plausible as one influence; they do not prove that realism is false or that all realists are motivated by anxiety. The epistemic result is narrower and firmer: usefulness alone warrants support for realism only if the consolation is more expected under realism than under its rivals, or if an independent account connects it to reliable moral cognition. Sophisticated realist arguments therefore remain live. The practical result is also bounded. Rejecting cosmic insurance does not erase pain, dependency, consent, trust, power, or the conditions of cooperation. For agents committed to reducing suffering, sustaining cooperation, keeping promises, or offering publicly defensible rules, those facts can support protection and repair without being promoted into moral furniture. This does not produce categorical reasons for every possible agent. The conclusion is not that genealogy refutes realism, that non-realism is motive-free, or that human concern is infallible. It is that felt authority is not by itself evidence of objective authority, and that the work of protecting people remains human work under either ontology.

items.title: ✶ The Induction Ownership Fallacy - Hume, Theistic Appropriation, and the Illicit Conversion of a Shared Burden into an Apologetic Advantage.
items.abstract: Hume's problem of induction is sometimes used in Christian apologetics to argue that non-theistic inquiry cannot justify expecting the future to resemble the past, whereas Christianity can account for induction through a rational and faithful creator. This argument starts from a real shared limit: contingent observations do not deductively entail unobserved cases, and an inductive defense of induction is not a premise-neutral proof. The disputed move is the conversion of that common burden into an exclusive Christian epistemic advantage. This paper reconstructs the strongest ownership claim and separates five increasingly demanding achievements: ontological grounding, a prior expectation of broad order, higher-order assurance, local projection warrant, and exclusive warrant. It then subjects the last claim to a four-gate test. A worldview that allegedly owns inductive warrant must support the relevant stability, connect finite agents to its content, constrain particular projections, and exclude rival routes. A general divine-order premise may contribute at the first three levels without identifying which predicates are projectible, where a regularity's boundary lies, what probability to assign, or when an apparent exception is a miracle, hidden condition, or error. A second argument develops an access--externalism gradient. If warrant requires reflective access to the divine guarantee, the theological, historical, and application bridges must themselves be defended through fallible inductive and abductive practices. If warrant instead depends externally on reliable faculties functioning in an appropriate environment, an agent need not affirm the true metaphysical explanation in order to reason with warrant. Properly basic and hybrid accounts may add rational assurance, but applying a broad assurance to a drug, storm, promise, or damaged bridge still requires domain-sensitive bridges. Matched cases across medicine, engineering, testimony, forecasting, and blinded inquiry show why neither pure nor hybrid routes establish proprietary local warrant. The result does not refute Christianity, deny that the Christian deity could be the ultimate ground of natural order, supply a deductive proof of induction, or rule out a more detailed transcendental or probabilistic argument. It establishes a narrower conclusion: the generic guarantor move does not turn Hume's shared constraint into an apologetic victory. Metaphysical grounding, broad expectation, personal …

items.title: ◉ The Hebrews 11:1 Puzzle: Interpretive Plurality, Faith-Function Drift, and the Failure of a Stable Epistemic Verse.
items.abstract: When Hebrews 11:1 is treated as a stable definition of faith, the verse may still be asked to perform several different jobs: encourage endurance, describe trust, report confidence, identify evidence, or name a present ‘substance’ of future goods. Interpretive plurality is not by itself an error. The epistemic problem arises when an argument changes jobs under pressure, carries forward the credibility or authority earned by the earlier one, and supplies no defensible bridge that is stated or reasonably recoverable from context. An exhortation becomes a definition; confidence becomes evidence; trust becomes warrant; a metaphor becomes an ontological guarantee. The repeated word faith hides the changed inference. This paper isolates that pattern as faith-function drift. It distinguishes the present diagnosis from companion analyses of lexical ambiguity and the assurance-to-evidence proof burden, places Hebrews 11:1 within the homily's appeal to perseverance, and reconstructs a worked apologetic exchange move by move. Concrete analogies—a multi-use employee badge, a smoke alarm, a marathon, and a title deed—show why each function needs its own success conditions. A five-question stability audit then asks what function is active, what object it concerns, what bridge connects posture to object, whether the bridge discriminates among rivals, and what would correct the claim. This is a diagnostic argument, not an estimate of how frequently any speaker commits the error. The conclusion is bounded: Hebrews 11:1 may remain devotional, theological, relational, and even epistemically relevant when independent grounds are supplied. It does not, by its wording alone, license an argument to borrow the advantages of several non-equivalent functions.

items.title: ◉ The Gospel Payoff Fallacy Pragmatic Benefit, Epistemic Responsibility, and the Lowered Bar for Jesus.
items.abstract: William Lane Craig has said that if Christianity had even “one chance in a million” of being true, it would be worth believing. His later clarification is more careful: the number is colloquial, epistemic reasons are truth-directed, pragmatic reasons concern costs and benefits, and the immense Christian payoff may radically lower the epistemic bar or pragmatically justify belief without adequate evidence. This paper argues that the clarified position still fails. It offers a reason to want, investigate, cultivate, or act on a belief, not a reason that makes the proposition more credible. As a basis for belief, the stance is intrinsically irrational because it directs confidence toward desirability while leaving the truth-directed evidence unchanged. The argument distinguishes evidence, credence, outright belief, acceptance, profession, and action. Decision theory explains why a tiny probability can rationalize a cheap precaution or valuable experiment: the probability remains tiny while the payoff changes the preferred action. Craig's free experimental-drug analogy therefore supports taking the drug while expecting failure. It does not support believing that the drug will work, much less transferring that conclusion to a costly, identity-forming religious commitment. Pragmatic encroachment, epistemic permissivism, Jamesian permission, and indirect belief cultivation do not close the gap. If a practice produces new evidence, that evidence warrants any later belief; if it merely produces confidence, the epistemic defect remains. The wager also faces an internal Christian problem. If the invoked Gospel benefit requires sincere inward belief and the biblical deity knows the person's actual attitude, overstating belief is detectable pretense, while honestly reporting extremely low confidence concedes that wager-driven belief is absent. Rival religious payoffs and the costs of false commitment further defeat one-sided bookkeeping. The bounded conclusion is not that Christianity is false or that evidence-based Christian belief is irrational. It is that high stakes can justify action under uncertainty but can never, by themselves, lower the evidential bar for honest belief.

items.title: ◉ The Attribute-Expectation Test Divine Love, Human Accessibility, and the Reasonableness of Demanding Public Clarity.
items.abstract: Critics of a loving, omnipotent, omniscient, human-focused personal deity are often told that they expect too much clarity, accessibility, or response. This paper argues that the rebuke gets the direction of accountability backward. The expectations do not originate in skeptical entitlement. They are generated by the divine attributes themselves. If those attributes have descriptive and explanatory content, they must make some public patterns more likely than alternatives do. Perfect love combined with a desire for relationship predicts available contact; complete knowledge removes ordinary misunderstanding; unlimited power removes ordinary communicative inability; and high claimed stakes strengthen the expectation that sincere people can identify the message and its source. The paper develops an attribute-expectation test that compares public data under a specified God-concept and live rivals. Durable nonresistant nonbelief, strong demographic dependence, doctrinal fragmentation among sincere interpreters, and indefinitely revisable accounts of unanswered communication jointly create evidential pressure. The argument is probabilistic rather than deductive: it does not assign invented numbers, treat every absence as decisive, or infer atheism from hiddenness alone. It asks whether the observed pattern is less surprising without the target attributes and whether proposed auxiliary explanations were independently supported, predictively constrained, and proportionate before they were used as rescues. Freedom, soul-making, purposive evidence, implicit relationship, human resistance, and cognitive limitation are serious replies. Each can explain some cases. None earns an unlimited exemption. If the attributes remain vivid when recruiting trust but become indeterminate whenever the world conflicts with their predictions, the language is operating one way: thick for devotion and thin for criticism. The bounded conclusion is not that every form of theism is false, every nonbeliever is sincere, or public evidence is the only possible evidence. It is that 'expecting too much' is no answer until the defender explains why the theology's own maximal attributes should produce so little stable public constraint.

items.title: No Classical Probability for Counterfactuals.
items.abstract: This paper strengthens a triviality result by Santorio (2022, Analysis) for the probability of counterfactuals. The best response may be to drop the idea that the probability of counterfactuals behaves classically.

items.title: The Psychological Collapse of Love: Ego, Projection, and the Transformation of Attachment.
items.abstract: This paper examines the psychological structure of love, attachment, heartbreak, projection, and consciousness. It argues that emotional suffering in relationships does not arise merely from separation itself, but from the collapse of psychological continuity constructed through thought, memory, imagination, expectation, and egoic identification. -/- The paper proposes that attachment is not identical to love. Attachment is psychologically constructed through projection, comparison, ownership, fear of loss, and the desire for permanence. The beloved gradually becomes intertwined with identity itself, functioning as emotional security, meaning, continuity, and escape from loneliness. Thus, when relationships fracture, the ego experiences destabilization, producing anger, betrayal, jealousy, sadness, hatred, and existential fragmentation. -/- Beyond relational suffering, the paper further explores individuality, separation, freedom, and responsibility as movements of consciousness itself rather than isolated psychological concepts. It ultimately advances a non-dual phenomenological view in which consciousness is not merely personal, but intrinsic to existence itself. In this view, human beings are localized expressions through which the universe becomes aware of itself.

items.title: Survival Before Conditioning: A Phenomenological Inquiry into Unconditioned Existence, Reproduction, and Relational Awareness.
items.abstract: Human civilization largely confuses survival with psychological conditioning. From childhood onward, individuals are educated not merely to survive biologically, but to conform psychologically to systems of identity, authority, morality, competition, nationalism, religion, reproduction, and symbolic continuity. This paper phenomenologically investigates the distinction between direct survival and conditioned existence. It argues that survival in its primordial structure is immediate, relational, practical, reproductive, and perceptual, whereas conditioning emerges through accumulated psychological constructions imposed upon consciousness through thought, memory, fear, comparison, and social continuity. By examining the structures of education, identity formation, reproduction, neighboring existence, resource awareness, and symbolic dependence, this paper proposes the possibility of learning and living without psychological conditioning. The inquiry ultimately suggests that authentic education is not the cultivation of identity, but the awakening of direct awareness free from psychological fragmentation. -/- .

items.title: Imaginaries of precarity: negotiating generative AI in Indonesia’s cultural and creative labor.
items.abstract: This paper examines how cultural and creative workers in Indonesia negotiate the adoption of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) under conditions of labor precarity. Drawing on sociotechnical imaginaries and scholarship on precarious creative labor, the study explores how workers interpret, appropriate, and constrain GenAI in their everyday practices.
