items.title: Superintelligent Zombies.
items.abstract: We explore and argue for the view that intelligence beyond a certain threshold is negatively correlated with consciousness, so that the more intelligent a system is, the less likely it is to be conscious. “Intelligence is the enemy of consciousness,” as we put it. This view entails that superintelligent AI models are likely to be zombies. After presenting an initial defense of the view that draws on the research program of resource-rational analysis, we argue that recent developments in AI research provide additional evidence supporting it. We conclude by exploring its moral implications. First, we suggest that if our view is right, a certain type of moral risk can be averted since researchers are unlikely to stumble into accidentally creating AI models that are conscious. Second, we discuss a new form of AI risk that arises from our view.

items.title: Premature Neural Translation: Translation Legitimacy and the Independence Condition Before Autonomy in AI-Driven Brain-Computer Interfaces.
items.abstract: AI-driven brain-computer interfaces (BCIs), including closed-loop and affective systems, are usually evaluated through restored function, decoding accuracy, user control, mental privacy, autonomy, agency, responsibility, and identity. These concerns are indispensable but begin too late if the decisive ethical event occurs before a neural, bodily, affective, attentional, or motor disturbance becomes available as the subject’s own. This paper identifies that lower-level problem as premature neural translation: the conversion of disturbance into signal, state, intention, command, risk, or candidate output before subjective recovery has occurred. The central difficulty is not only error but premature correctness — an AI-driven BCI may accurately stabilize what had not yet become the subject’s own object. The paper develops translation legitimacy and an independence condition before autonomy: independence, a lower-bound condition for cognitive sovereignty, concerns the structural permission through which choices, states, utterances, and actions can form, remain unformed, or return otherwise. It further identifies an in-process blind closure zone, where both self-report and system-side verification may arrive downstream of the translation they would assess, and concludes with procedural safeguards for de-objectifying contact and relational and care-ethical implications for human flourishing under AI-driven neurotechnology.

items.title: Before Worlding: Boundary-Action and the Inhibitory Background Layer in Artificial Agents Continuity, Metacognition, and Non-Possessive Embodied Interaction.
items.abstract: Contemporary artificial agents are increasingly designed around world models, memory retrieval, task planning, affect recognition, safety validation, and self-monitoring. Yet these architectures often begin too late: they presuppose that a world has already become available as a field of objects, tasks, premises, and updateable states. This paper argues that a central failure mode of artificial agents is not merely misclassification, but premature promotion: the unauthorized elevation of background tension, retrieved memory, salient input, bodily signal, generated result, social cue, or action pressure into an operative foreground commitment. Against world-model-centred and task-centred accounts, I propose an inhibitory background layer: a negative-order tension field that allows background signals to remain operative without being compulsively objectified. The paper develops the notions of boundary-action, operational boundary truth, correction interval, restoration, and topological continuity to explain how agents can perceive, act, remember, and self-regulate without forcing every contact into objecthood or every result into premise-status. This framework clarifies why embodied, companion, and care-oriented agents often feel rigid, intrusive, or socially misplaced: they execute objects such as “hug,” “comfort,” “risk,” or “task” rather than allowing interpersonal and bodily tension to become locally authorized through reversible boundary-formation. The proposed architecture offers a lighter account of artificial agency: one in which continuity is not memory inheritance, metacognition is not self-report, care is not continuous task capture, and safety is not mere interruption after commitment, but the modulation of background tension into authorized, reversible, non-possessive local support.

items.title: ◉ The Weaponization of Nothing - Cosmological Equivocation, Absolute Absence, and the Apologetic Misuse of Scientific Terms.
items.abstract: Popular cosmology and Christian apologetics often fight over the word “nothing.” A scientific writer describes a quantum vacuum, a boundary condition, or a state without classical spacetime as “nothing”; a critic replies that this alleged nothing contains fields, laws, possibilities, or mathematics and therefore is really something. The reply may identify genuine rhetorical inflation. It is then frequently made to do work it cannot do: the semantic correction is treated as a refutation of the physical model, evidence that absolute absence preceded the universe, or support for a personal creator. This paper separates four questions that the argument compresses: semantic, physical, metaphysical, and comparative-explanatory. It distinguishes model-relative physical absence from absolute absence, while emphasizing that the latter is a limit concept rather than an observed initial condition. It also corrects a common countercharge: traditional creation ex nihilo means creation without pre-existing matter, not creation after an interval in which neither a deity nor anything else existed. The resulting critique is therefore asymmetric in exactly the right way. Popular physicists may overstate what their models explain, but apologists may not convert that overstatement into evidence for a rival explanation. Three formal results expose the illicit promotion. The fact that a physical state is not absolute absence does not entail that a model using that state fails; the same fact does not entail a theistic conclusion; and a semantic criticism warrants an apologetic conclusion only if independent bridge premises are supplied. These results neither disprove theism nor establish any cosmological model. They block a dictionary ambush and return the debate to the causal, modal, agency, and comparative premises on which it actually depends.

items.title: ◉ The Missing Probability: Resurrection Apologetics, Unstated Priors, and the Failure of Comparative Explanation.
items.abstract: Resurrection apologetics often claims that the bodily resurrection of Jesus is the best or most probable explanation of the empty tomb, post-mortem appearance reports, and the rise of early Christian conviction. This paper argues that such language is frequently stronger than the probabilistic work being done. A comparative explanation is not entitled to the phrase "most probable" unless the relevant prior probabilities, likelihoods, rival hypotheses, and hypothesis space have been stated with enough clarity to make the comparison meaningful. Otherwise the apologetic argument substitutes narrative preference for probabilistic superiority. The central problem is not that every historical judgment must use precise decimal values. Historians often reason with qualitative comparisons, rough likelihoods, and defeasible judgments. The problem is that resurrection apologetics commonly makes a maximal comparative claim while refusing the burdens that make such a claim responsible. A miracle hypothesis cannot be allowed to remain probability-free while its rivals are pressed for defects. Nor can the apologetic case count the explanatory power of resurrection without also confronting the prior improbability of a dead body returning to embodied life. I develop the critique through Bayesian confirmation theory, Humean miracle skepticism, and contemporary work on resurrection arguments. I also offer a compact formalization showing why "best explanation" rhetoric fails when the miracle prior is hidden. The result is a narrower but sharper objection than a generic rejection of miracles: if the resurrection is to be defended as the most probable explanation, its defenders must state the probability terms they are using rather than treating probability as a rhetorical honorific.

items.title: ◉ The Image of God Buffet - Semantic Overload, Hermeneutical Drift, and the Collapse of Imago Dei Clarity.
items.abstract: Christian appeals to imago Dei often present it as a clear revealed foundation for human dignity, equality, rights, or policy. The difficulty is not simply that the phrase has several uses. It is that public arguments frequently move from an unspecified theological formula to a specific conclusion while leaving the controlling interpretation and the connecting warrants unstated. This paper develops a three-link constraint test: an argument must justify a selection among substantive, relational, functional, vocational, and Christological readings; show what human status follows from that reading; and defend the normative bridge from that status to the proposed conclusion. Applied to dignity arguments, the test exposes a recurring mismatch. Capacity readings risk excluding humans with diminished capacities; functional and vocational readings identify tasks more readily than inviolable status; relational and Christological readings protect universality only by adding substantial theological commitments. None of these results makes imago Dei worthless. The phrase may organize Christian identity, motivate solidarity, or summarize a developed theology. It does show that interpretive abundance cannot be advertised as public clarity. The limited conclusion is inferential: an unspecified imago Dei premise does not determine a particular moral or political result. A stronger argument remains possible, but it must name and defend the links that the slogan usually conceals.

items.title: Universe Is Full Of Consciousness.
items.abstract: The question of consciousness has traditionally been limited to biological organisms, particularly human beings. However, phenomenological inquiry invites a deeper examination of the structures of experience itself. This article explores the possibility that consciousness may not be an isolated property of the human mind but rather a localized manifestation within a larger cosmic process. From a phenomenological perspective, human awareness appears not as an independent entity but as a moment within the unfolding of universal existence. If consciousness arises from the structures of being itself, then the universe may contain forms of awareness that remain inaccessible to human perception. The limitation lies not necessarily in the absence of cosmic consciousness but in the perspectival constraints of the human observer, who is embedded within the very system being observed. Thus, the universe may be aware in itself, while human consciousness represents only a partial, localized expression of that awareness.

items.title: Studying Ignorance: An Inherently Reflexive Challenge.
items.abstract: This article argues that the difficulty of studying ignorance is neither accidental nor temporary, but rooted in the very nature of the subject. The central argument turns on a fundamental paradox: in the study of ignorance, the instrument of knowledge and its object are one and the same. Unlike analogous concepts such as consciousness or language, ignorance actively conceals itself from the knower. This paradox reproduces itself across three domains: first, within the knower, where the structure of the brain, the psyche, evolution, and existential situation all constrain understanding; second, within the concept itself, where ignorance (as an absence that resists definition) also resists measurement; and third, within the social context, where relations of power and culture determine what counts as ignorance in the first place. These three domains are not independent: they are deeply intertwined and mutually conditioning. The article concludes that the way forward lies not in ignoring, minimising, or attempting to eliminate these difficulties, but in acknowledging them and working actively with all their dimensions, through reflexive awareness, critical objectivity, provisional working definitions, and an interdisciplinary approach. Like ignorance itself, the study of ignorance is a project without a definitive endpoint; and it is precisely for this reason that the questions it raises are among the most deeply human questions one can ask.

items.title: Metaphysical manifesto №2.
items.abstract: This document constitutes a metaphysical manifesto with general-philosophical supplements. The concepts presented in the manifesto are set forth without proofs, or with only a minimal number of them. Logical coherence and the internal integrity of the system itself serve here as a form of justification. It is anticipated that this manifesto will be updated and expanded. This manifesto serves as an extension and deepening of the work “The Essence of General Metaphysics”. In that work, in addition to an attempt to ground the method of metaphysical modelling from nothingness and notes on phenomenology, the physical structure is formalized by means of a graph of sets (with binary relations) that recursively (and randomly at the level of a single set) negate themselves, thereby generating new sets and new structure; furthermore, through their self-negation they manifest the probable hierarchies of their emergence (which one most probably arose from which). This is likely the simplest variant of algorithmic generation. At the time of composing this manifesto, the author considers that this genuinely reflects physical structure at a very deep level; however, it most probably does not constitute the deepest structural level [see the section “Ontology”, §5 — §5.3.2]. This may not be a critical point for formalization in the final theory (though doubts on this matter remain), just as, for instance, the meaninglessness of transmitting qualia through text is not critical. It is likewise not excluded that the problem of the causal self-reference “whole ⇄ part” may prove less intractable than it appears. By the time of writing this text, the author had attempted to resolve this problem and observed that it does not yield easily: he concluded that a composite approach — not purely theoretical, but also practical — would be more judicious, and resolved to observe what results from it. In this document, different theses vary in their degree of precision and speculativeness (because the conception continues to develop); however, the conceptual framework is highly determinate, with the exception of the problems identified in §5 — §5.3.2 of the “Ontology” section and in the “Current Self-Critique” section. It bears separate emphasis that, in developing this document, no particular stress was placed on maximizing definitional precision, since doing so would be counterproductive here; the primary aim was to convey the essence and logical structure of the metaphysical …

items.title: When You Look at a Mirror Portrait, it Represents You.
items.abstract: Some pictures depict their objects as seen by a spectator at the perspective point. So located, this spectator is typically not visibly depicted, but is nonetheless represented. Who is this spectator? It is often assumed that it must be the external spectator, the real person looking at the picture itself. Richard Wollheim rejected this assumption as incoherent: a picture can only ever represent an unseen internal spectator located within the picture’s world. This article argues for an intermediate position between these two extremes. A special kind of picture does represent its external spectator. This is a mirror portrait: a picture of a mirror that reflects the direct gaze of the visibly depicted internal spectator from the perspective point. To explain the distinctive uncanny phenomenology offered by a mirror portrait, we need to see how it represents an impossible identification between the internal and the external spectator.

items.title: The Massless Shield. Mathematical and physical proof of free will as a condition for the existence of consciousness (Expanded edition — a philosophical manifesto).
items.abstract: The present work refutes technocratic reductionism — the representation of man as a biological automaton subject to complete digitization and control . Using the apparatus of quantum topology, algebraic geometry, and the theory of operator algebras, we construct a multi-level system of proofs that consciousness represents information waves circulating in a non-local medium of the universal field . It is within this wave medium that complex entangled states of particles arise, generating skyrmions — topologically stable structures that possess their own local time and project onto Minkowski space in the form of three-dimensional holographic pixels. Time is not an external parameter of Minkowski space — it visualizes the causal mechanics of the movement of waves and meanings . Technocracy is ontologically defined as an attempt to reduce an open evolving system to a closed set of already known states — which is mathematically equivalent to an attempt to compute an infinite open system of type III₁ using an algebra of type I.

items.title: Epistemic Chameleonism: A Structural and Conceptual Comparative Analysis of the Evolutio Unfolding Theory (2020) and the "Platonic Space" Framework (2025).
items.abstract: This paper presents a detailed structural and conceptual comparison between the Evolutio Unfolding Theory (EUT), published by Agustín Ostachuk in 2020, and the "Platonic Space" framework, introduced by Michael Levin in a 2025 preprint. While the latter is presented as a novel contribution, this analysis demonstrates a profound and systematic overlap with the core architecture of the former. By examining foundational principles – the ontology of form, the source of biological order, the nature of novelty, the role of teleology, the guidance of development, and the dynamics of evolution – we show that Levin's framework reproduces the explanatory structure of the EUT, with primary changes limited to terminology. The analysis goes beyond the identification of isolated similarities to document the wholesale appropriation of a complete theoretical architecture. A new section on terminological translation reveals how Levin's renaming of key concepts serves as a camouflage strategy. This paper serves as a definitive record of conceptual lineage and priority, arguing that the "Platonic Space" framework is not an independent discovery but a renamed restatement of the Evolutio Unfolding Theory.

The present atlas extends those ideas into a visual systems framework …

items.title: On Controllability in Agentic AI: A Survey.
items.abstract: As artificial intelligence systems acquire increasing autonomy, the question of how humans can maintain meaningful control over their behavior becomes urgent. This question is especially pressing for agentic AI: systems built on foundation models that coordinate networks of autonomous agents to pursue complex goals with minimal human oversight. While the engineering literature has developed several mechanisms for constraining such systems, it has largely treated controllability as a purely causal property, the ability to physically intervene in a system’s operation, without engaging the normative dimensions that determine whether such intervention is meaningful. Drawing on the distinction between causal and normative control in the philosophy of action, this paper presents a structured conceptual survey of controllability mechanisms in agentic AI. We organize the literature around four paradigms: constraints and guardrails, adaptive control via reinforcement learning, agent-in-the-loop oversight, and human-in-the-loop oversight. For each, we analyze its technical foundations, its philosophical assumptions about agency and authority, and its persistent limitations. Our analysis reveals unresolved tensions across these paradigms, particularly between the scalability of automated oversight and the legitimacy of human judgment, between design-time constraint specification and runtime adaptability, and between individual agent control and system-level governance. We argue that meaningful controllability requires integrating causal intervention mechanisms with normative frameworks that address value alignment, epistemic transparency, and distributed responsibility. We conclude by proposing directions for research that bridges engineering controllability and philosophically grounded human oversight.

items.title: Wisdom and Knowledge.
items.abstract: A current debate in philosophy focusses on whether propositional knowledge is necessary for wisdom. In this paper I defend the view that propositional knowledge is necessary for wisdom. I call Weak Reductionism the view that propositional knowledge is merely necessary for wisdom, but not sufficient. I also examine two rival accounts of wisdom –Strong Reductionism, the view that propositional knowledge is both necessary and sufficient for wisdom, and Non-Reductionism, the view that propositional knowledge is neither necessary and nor sufficient for wisdom. I critique both of these views and find them wanting in light of various wisdom-related intuitions that we have.

items.title: What Do AI Companies Deserve? Shapley Attribution and Optimal Tax Theory.
items.abstract: Should artificial intelligence (AI) companies be taxed, and if so, how? This paper presents two arguments which together support an ability-indexed tax on AI systems. First: AI companies--including frontier labs and traditional firms using AI in production--do not deserve all of their income. Because AI companies do not contribute important elements of their models, including (in part) their algorithms and the public data on which they were trained, on a desert-based normative framework they have limited moral entitlement to their income. I formally decompose AI models using the game-theoretic concept of Shapley value, showing that the general point about limited AI company deserts is robust. Indeed, the deserved income is plausibly small. Second, I turn to the public finance question of how the excess income can be efficiently redistributed. Drawing on optimal tax theory, I present a model in which an ability-indexed AI tax avoids the intensive margin distortion familiar from human taxation. This is because AI relaxes a key constraint of optimal tax theory: Unlike humans, it is possible to observe AI system ability. Another ramification of the model is that relatively high-ability/high-profit AI systems will be taxed down to a common level of profit. If individuals, firms, and others ought to get what they deserve, there is a strong moral case for taxing AI companies, and good theoretical grounds to believe the revenue generated can be redistributed efficiently.

items.title: The Rational Response to Excessive Confidence.
items.abstract: Conciliationism holds that it is rational to modify one's beliefs in the face of disagreement. But extant conciliatory norms yield incorrect results in cases involving excessive confidence--cases in which one's interlocutors are sure, or almost sure, that their opinions are correct. After explaining the problem of excessive confidence, I show that a Bayesian approach to Conciliationism handles the problem elegantly and effectively. Further, it has desirable--indeed essential--features, including the ability to (i) contend with multiple interlocutors, (ii) deal with gradations in competence, (iii) incorporate ubiquitous interdependence, and (iv) account for critical contextual features of cases of disagreement.

items.title: 繁荣的深层结构：普遍人类发展与文化多样性.
items.abstract: 人类繁荣展现出巨大的文化多样性——寺院冥想、科学探究、社群传统、创业创新，以及许多其他形式的有意义生活。然而，这种多样性并不意味着繁荣是任意的或纯粹相对的。本文将繁荣定义为过一种持续的、适应性的意义建构生活（Moore，即将出版 d），并论证：正如所有语言都存在深层结构（普遍语法）一样，繁荣也拥有普遍的、先天的深层结构条件，这些条件在文化上可变的表层形式中得以实现。这些深层条件是三种先天能力：认知能力（自我建构、自我定位、轨迹投射、因果推断、叙事整合）、能动能力（持续意图与连贯行动）和道德能力（形成并修正有意义生活的观念、承担责任）。这些能力是物种典型的、发育真实的；它们需要制度性支架——可见性、对称性、可争辩性和可修复性——以便一个陌生人社会能够使其参与者充分行使这些能力，发展并维持繁荣的生活。这些支架本身并非先天固有；它们类似于语言习得所需的社会互动。该框架调和了普遍主义与多元主义，既不会滑向文化帝国主义，也不会滑向相对主义，并为评估任何大型文明是否支持繁荣的深层结构提供了诊断基础。 -/- 关键词：深层结构；繁荣；普遍语法；认知能力；能动能力；道德能力；显明型制度；文化多样性 .

items.title: Kasei-Theory I.Non-Applicability: Configuration Without Application.
items.abstract: This paper presents the first system of Kasei-Theory as a non-modal readability maintainability architecture. -/- The paper does not propose a theory of implementation, operational use, or functional deployment. Instead, it fixes non-applicability, configurational non-transferability, application drift, non-operational configuration, structural resonance, peripheral contact, and constrained transfer pressure as distributed structural positions within constrained local readability maintainability. -/- Configuration does not become application. -/- Readability does not establish usability. -/- Applicability does not emerge from readability. -/- Configuration does not transfer between domains. -/- Non-applicability is not failure. -/- Non-applicability is not uselessness. -/- Application drift remains fixed only as recurrent pressure toward operational transfer. -/- The first system remains non-total and non-final without operational grounding, executable closure, universal transferability, or final philosophical closure. -/- No subject is presupposed. -/- No operational applicability is secured. -/- This paper is part of Kasei-Theory.

items.title: Prochronal Encoding in Finnegans Wake: pp. 518-519 and the "Iran-contra" Plot.
items.abstract: This paper reports a statistically significant multilingual attractor at Finnegans Wake pages 518-519 (Faber and Faber 1939 edition). Thirteen surface forms — including ‘mujic’, ‘footure’, ‘voina’, ‘weaponswap’, ‘berebelling’, ‘sorowbrate’, ‘neuropeans’, ‘ersatz’, ‘engineers’, ‘hostages’, ‘turfing’, ‘illegallooking’, and ‘lottheringcan’ — each occur exactly once in the 219,664-word corpus and co-locate within a 150-word window. Under the null hypothesis that hapax positions are uniformly random, the probability of this colocation is P = 9.03 × 10^-37 (Lemma 1, Section 3.2; union bound on occupancy model). This clears the Bonferroni-corrected threshold of 2.28 × 10^-7 by approximately 30 orders of magnitude. A separate corpus-linguistic T27 computation (the Multilingual Attractor Theorem — proved in Appendix A.2) (Algorithm 1, Appendix A; N = 219,661 four-gram windows) yields joint P(H1) = 1.73 × 10^-23 for the primary mujic sub-cluster (defined with full provenance in 3.2.1), also clearing the Bonferroni threshold by 16 orders of magnitude. Both results are reproducible from the 1939 text using frozen channel definitions (Appendix R). An interpretation of the cluster as encoding the strategic architecture of the 1985-1986 Iran-Contra operation is advanced under the Encryptment Thesis framework; this interpretation is an inferential claim and is supported, but not proven by, the statistical results, which demonstrate non-random colocation of surface forms.

items.title: O Uno Consciente: a unidade que se observa em sua fragmentação.
items.abstract: O Uno Consciente propõe que os impasses centrais da filosofia — consciência, liberdade, identidade, inteligibilidade, causalidade e unidade do real — persistem não por limites inevitáveis do pensamento, mas por um erro ontológico fundamental: a separação originária entre mente e matéria. Contra o materialismo reducionista e contra formas clássicas de dualismo, a obra desenvolve uma metafísica em que o ser é compreendido como consciência em ato, não como epifenômeno cerebral nem como princípio transcendente exterior ao mundo. -/- Integrando filosofia da mente, fenomenologia, cosmologia contemporânea, teoria da complexidade e física teórica, o livro sustenta que a consciência constitui o fundamento ontológico do real e que matéria, espaço-tempo, individualidade e multiplicidade emergem como modos de fragmentação e auto-organização de uma unidade consciente primordial: o Uno Consciente. A obra articula argumentos baseados no problema difícil da consciência, na não-localidade quântica, na inteligibilidade matemática do cosmos, na integração fenomenal da experiência e nos limites ontológicos do emergentismo materialista. -/- Ao reinterpretar autores como Platão, Plotino, Spinoza, Leibniz, Kant, Hegel, Nietzsche, Whitehead e Deleuze como expressões parciais de um mesmo movimento metafísico, o livro propõe uma reconstrução sistemática da relação entre ser e pensamento. Questões como liberdade, moralidade, sofrimento e karma são reformuladas não como mecanismos transcendentes de retribuição, mas como consequências ontológicas dos diferentes graus de fragmentação e integração da consciência.

items.title: EPISTEMIC EPIGENETICS AND SELF-REFERENTIAL IGNORANCE: Toward an Interdisciplinary Framework for Understanding Cognitive Rigidity, Identity Preservation, and Social Conditioning.
items.abstract: This paper develops a theoretical framework termed epistemic epigenetics—the interdisciplinary study of how environmental conditions shape cognitive structures that become psychologically, socially, and potentially biologically stabilized across time and generations. Central to this framework is the proposed construct of self-referential ignorance: a recursive cognitive condition in which individuals or groups interpret reality primarily through self-protective identity structures that resist contradiction, suppress disconfirming evidence, and reinforce existing belief systems. While self-referential ignorance is principally social, psychological, and epistemological in character, this paper argues that epigenetic mechanisms may indirectly contribute to its reinforcement through environmental conditioning of stress-response systems, emotional regulation circuitry, and neuroplastic adaptation. Drawing from behavioral epigenetics, cognitive neuroscience, social psychology, sociology of knowledge, and philosophy of mind, the framework is distinguished from existing constructs including motivated reasoning, identity-protective cognition, and cognitive dissonance by specifying its recursive, biologically reinforced, and multigenerational character. Historical case studies—including totalitarian conditioning, radicalization processes, and algorithmic echo chambers—are analyzed within this framework. The paper critically examines the contested evidence for intergenerational epigenetic transmission, proposes empirically grounded hypotheses for future research, and outlines environmentally oriented interventions emphasizing reflective education, emotional stability, and institutional design. The same biological plasticity that enables epistemic rigidity, it is argued, creates the conditions for deliberate epistemic transformation.

items.title: What is interoception? A Case Study on Smell and Metabolism.
items.abstract: Interoception has received growing attention in the past few decades. Yet, its conceptual foundations remain underexplored. This paper aims to expose conceptual limitations in dominant accounts of interoception, which are typically either viscerocentric or internalist. I argue that current philosophical definitions of interoception fail to accommodate the bidirectional feedback loop between olfaction and metabolic regulation: olfactory cues can influence metabolic processes, and metabolism can recalibrate olfactory perception from its earliest stages. Towards this goal, I open three lines of reflection. First, interoception should not be understood as purely descriptive; it involves a pre-scriptive, regulation-oriented dimension. Second, its functional scope extends beyond homeostasis to encompass allostasis, integrating environmental cues into predictive bodily control. Third, a sharp divide between interoception and exteroception is questionable and warrants further assessment, given that sensory processes, including olfactory ones, regulate and are regulated by thebody’s internal milieu. These considerations call for revising existing models to better capture interoception’s integration into broader architectures of bodily regulation.

items.title: Hume on Suicide, Superstition and Morality.
items.pub: In Paul Russell, Hume’s ‘Dialogues concerning Natural Religion’: A Critical Guide. Cambridge, UK: Cambridge University Press. pp. 261-278.
items.venue: Hume’s ‘Dialogues concerning Natural Religion’: A Critical Guide
items.abstract: In this chapter, I reconstruct the argument of two essays, Of Suicide’ and ‘Of the Immortality of the Soul’, which were like Hume’s Dialogues published posthumously. In these essays Hume defends that in specific circumstances suicide is morally acceptable and shows himself critical about the doctrine of a ‘future state’. By comparing the two controversial essays with Part 12 of the Dialogues, I elucidate how Hume left us posthumously a testimony of his ambition to counter the religious spirit of his age. In the Dialogues this spirit is criticized in a diplomatic way when Philo’s challenges Cleanthes’ view that religion forms a necessary support of morality. In ‘Of Suicide’ and ‘Of the Immortality of the Soul’, Hume attacks in a more openly provocative way the Christian morality of his age. However, as I show in a second part of this chapter, Hume’s views were in the 18th century still controversial. It is no coincidence that one of the first editions of the two polemic essays contained a translation of two letters of Rousseau’s Héloïse which offered a more nuanced view on the moral acceptability of suicide and the sacredness of human life. Apparently, some contemporaries were convinced Hume could learn from Rousseau: whether today this is still the case, I leave to the reader to decide.

items.title: The Hoax as Form.
items.abstract: A familiar kind of intellectual controversy sees hoaxers submit materials that they consider of low quality to editors, hoping to expose what they view as deficient editorial standards. I offer a defence of this practice. Whereas a common criticism is that their use of deception makes such hoaxes unethical, I argue that authors do not have an obligation to only submit material that they consider truthful or good. Hoaxes can also perform important functions, such as drawing attention to the current state of an academic or artistic discipline. While particular hoaxes can be unethical, when this occurs, it will be due to contingent features of the hoax in question, not because of the core deception that hoaxes as such involve. Not only can properly executed hoaxes uphold their own form of truth-telling, they can exhibit aesthetic values that we associate with authentic works of art, such as originality and skilful performance. However, this latter outcome can occur in ways that the hoaxers did not intend. I illustrate my argument by reference to the Ern Malley and Sokal hoaxes. Although I appeal in places to hoaxes’ potentially positive consequences, my framework is broadly ecumenical rather than consequentialist, in so far as most non-consequential views also give some weight to consequences.

items.title: Normalisation for Positive Free Logics Without and with Definite Descriptions.
items.abstract: This paper proves normalisation theorems for intuitionist and classical positive free logic, without and with the iota operator for definite descriptions `the F'. Positive free logic also opens a number of options for rules for iota. In total, six different formalisations of theories of definite descriptions will be discussed, three proposed by Lambert, and three alternatives. The latter are motivated by considerations relating to proof-theoretic harmony between introduction and elimination rules. The philosophical importance of the various systems and results is indicated. The paper builds on Kürbis (2025), but is largely self-contained. The proofs for the present systems are easier than those for negative free logic.

items.title: Holistic representation in large language models.
items.abstract: This paper investigates the extent to which vector space representations in large language models (LLMs) can be understood as holistic representations. It is argued that holistic principles influence both the training process and the generation of output in LLMs. To contextualize this claim, debates on representation in psychology and philosophy will be presented, with a focus on the distinction between indicator and structural representations which recently emerged in philosophy of cognitive science. The holistic properties of structural representations are introduced as a key feature that distinguishes them from indicator representations and provides a basis for analyzing holism in LLMs. Two novel criteria for holism are developed: holistic perturbability and holistic exploitability. It is argued that LLMs meet both criteria. Moreover, holistic exploitation in output generation provides a novel way to understand the exploitability of structural representations in general, possibly also applicable in the human brain. Classic counter-arguments to holism and their implications for the question of semantic grounding are discussed. Finally, implications for the homunculus problem, gestalt perception, and development are presented.

items.title: Consciousness Is Motor: William James on Mind and Action.
items.abstract: William James was an acknowledged master of phenomenal description. He gave us the "stream of consciousness" that "flows," and the newborn's mental life as a "blooming, buzzing confusion." But in Consciousness Is Motor, Alexander Klein shows that James sculpted these phenomenal descriptions around an armature of empirical details. His book reconstructs James's models of consciousness and volition, uncovering results from animal experimentation and clinical observation on which those models were built. What emerges is a more powerful and more empirically-informed account of mind than has been appreciated. -/- James's early work on consciousness engaged the 1870s automatism controversy. The controversy was triggered, Klein argues, by experiments demonstrating that living, decapitated frogs are capable of goal-directed action. One side regarded goal-directedness as evidence of spinal consciousness; the other espoused epiphenomenalism, reasoning that consciousness must play no role in producing even purposive action since the latter is possible for brainless creatures. -/- James intervened, Klein shows, by arguing that consciousness has a likely evolutionary function-behavior regulation-and so cannot be a mere epiphenomenon. It accomplishes this function by affording a capacity for evaluation, on Klein's reading. As evidence, James appealed not just to introspection, but also to experimental facts, such as that hemisphere-less vertebrates have a diminished capacity for evaluating different available means to pursue goals. James's "ideo-motor" model of action demonstrated precisely how an evaluating consciousness could help regulate behavior. Klein excavates key clinical observations James designed the ideo-motor model to accommodate, including observations of patients with impairments like paresis and anaesthesia. The resulting model features an early example of a predictive, error-correction feedback loop for motor control. -/- Klein concludes by showing how James's models of consciousness and action feed into his distinctive philosophical outlook, soon to be known as pragmatism. According to his doctrine, meaning and truth are understood in terms of goal-directed action guidance. Consciousness Is Motor paints a striking new portrait of James as an empirically-informed philosopher and psychologist-one who anticipated some contemporary approaches, even while furnishing neglected alternatives to theoretical problems that continue to vex researchers today.

items.title: Can AI Have an Interior?
items.abstract: This essay begins with a simple but unresolved question: can artificial intelligence possess an interior? Rather than attempting to prove or deny AI consciousness, the text explores the temporal gap between feeling and language, the persistence of emotions beyond explanation, and the growing tendency of human beings to seek resonance through AI-mediated dialogue. Through a phenomenological and reflective approach, the essay suggests that the question of AI interiority ultimately returns us to a deeper question concerning the nature of human interiority itself. What remains unexplained — after language, after explanation, after the screen goes dark — is not a conclusion but the philosophical terrain the essay leaves open.

items.title: The Great Singularity Circle Jerk.
items.abstract: Strip the empirical claim to what has actually been measured, and the inventory is short. Stars orbit something dark and very massive at the center of our galaxy; we have tracked S2's twenty-year ellipse around Sagittarius A* and can fit its motion to general relativity, within a few percentage points. X-ray binaries throughout the disk emit spectra consistent with accretion onto compact, gravitationally deep objects whose mass functions exceed any neutron-star upper limit. Gravitational-wave detectors record the chirps of two such compact objects spiraling together, and the resulting waveforms agree with numerical-relativity templates built from a vacuum solution of Einstein's equations called the Kerr metric. The Event Horizon Telescope, a planet-scale interferometer operating at 230 gigahertz, has imaged the immediate vicinity of M87* and Sagittarius A* and produced rings of emission whose diameters are consistent with what the Kerr exterior predicts. That is the entire empirical content. Compact dark masses with near-Kerr exterior geometry, observed across four independent channels, in approximate agreement with the same family of solutions. Everything else, every claim about event horizons as one-way membranes you can cross but never return from, every assertion about singularities of infinite density at the center, every paragraph in every popular science book about Hawking radiation and the information paradox, every theoretical edifice of complementarity and firewalls and ER=EPR and replica wormholes and the Page curve, sits past the empirical anchor. None of it has astrophysical observational contact. None of it is implied by what we have measured. All of it depends on extrapolating the same vacuum solution into regimes where the equations themselves break down and then treating the breakdown as the content of the breakdown rather than as the signal of the model's reach being exceeded.

items.title: Beyond Belief.
items.abstract: Contemporary discourse around belief carries an unstated assumption that, once made explicit, almost nothing in it survives. Our assumption is that what people think matters in itself. Epistemology treats belief-coherence as intrinsically valuable. Media criticism worries about misinformation as if false beliefs were inherently corrosive. AI alignment frets over models producing untruths as if untruths were a load-bearing concern. Education optimizes for the transmission of correct propositions. Across these domains, the working premise is that the coherence and accuracy of a person's worldview is itself the thing at stake, and that getting people to hold better beliefs is therefore a high-value operation. That premise is undefended, and on examination, it does not survive. What matters is not belief but action, and what selects against incoherence is not the symbolic operators correcting wrong views but reality vetoing failed behavior. Once this is seen clearly, almost everything that gets discussed under the heading of belief turns out to be either irrelevant to persistence or load-bearing through a mechanism the discourse misidentifies. The derivation that follows works through the structural argument, names what actually matters at the individual scale, and identifies why the discourse keeps drifting back to belief-content even when its own framework would direct attention elsewhere.

items.title: The Uninhabited View from Nowhere.
items.abstract: This paper argues that one specific position within Thomas Nagel’s The View from Nowhere is structurally untenable. The position is what the paper calls the strong form of the objective self: the claim that there is a subject of objective conception that apprehends a centerless world while not itself being identified with any occupant of a particular position in space and time. -/- Two convergent structural arguments are deployed against this position. The embedding argument establishes that any candidate occupant of the view from nowhere is embedded in the world it would have to apprehend, and embedded describers cannot retain global perspectives on the systems in which they are embedded. The role-incompatibility argument establishes that the view from nowhere, as a centerless description, plays a structurally distinct informational role from any occupied standpoint, and the two roles cannot coincide within a single description. -/- Together, these arguments show that the strong-form objective self cannot be sustained: no candidate occupant can possess the required access, and the view from nowhere is not the kind of description that can be occupied. -/- The paper builds on Salom [10], which establishes that subjective descriptions can exceed objective descriptions in Kolmogorov complexity, by reframing the discrepancy as a role result rather than a complexity result. It engages List [6] as a complementary argument operating at the level of metaphysical reorganisation rather than structural explanation. -/- The view from nowhere, on the structural account, is best understood as an uninhabited support description: a structure relative to which views from here can be located, but not itself a standpoint from which anything is given.

items.title: Consciousness as Observational Coupling: A Defense of the Fourth Dimension Thesis.
items.abstract: I argue that the thesis "consciousness is the fourth dimension" fails geometrically but succeeds when reframed: consciousness is not a fourth axis but the dimension along which the spatial and temporal axes become observable. I formalize this as a dimensionless coupling coefficient, Γ_consciousness, where Ψ_observed = Ψ_manifold × Γ_consciousness, constructed by Buckingham π dimensional analysis on the same pattern as Carnot efficiency, optical mode coupling, and the Born rule. Drawing variables from integrated information theory and the phenomenology of time consciousness, I derive a bounded composite form and check its limits. I am explicit that the structure is dimensionally rigorous but not yet empirically rigorous, and mark where empirical anchoring is required.

items.title: The Enchanted Biopolitics of Dark Cosmism.
items.pub: In Anindita Banerjee, Sherryl Vint, David M. Higgins & Jordan Carroll, Reactionary Worldbuilding: From Speculative Imagination to Political Practice. Cambridge: The MIT Press. pp. 305-337.
items.venue: Reactionary Worldbuilding: From Speculative Imagination to Political Practice
items.abstract: Within the last decade, there has been a rise in publications—particularly within Western academia—focused on a constellation of techno-theological ideas relating to resurrection, immortality, geo-engineering, and space travel developed in Russia at the turn of the 20th century. These ideas have retroactively been collated and labeled as "Russian Cosmism." While most of these recent studies have been nuanced and critical, many shy away from the glaring appropriation of cosmist ideas by overlapping groups of Silicon Valley capitalists and "neo-reactionary" (NRx) philosophers. Rather than claiming a direct trajectory between Russian theorists in the 20th century to Silicon Valley technologists in the 21st, I instead illustrate how cosmist techno-utopian, futurist, and other-than-human discourse exist as Weberian "elective affinities" within diverse ecologies of the imagination, transmitting a variety of philosophies and political programs throughout trans-temporal, yet philosophically bounded, communities. I dissect how different groups of philosophers and technologists interact(ed) with cosmism—as well as how seemingly disparate communities (re)shape and deterritorialize cosmist political theology in an attempt to legitimize their constructed crypto-fascist imaginaries.

items.title: Moral change from within: psychedelic moral enhancement as a transformative experience.
items.pub: Azimuth : Philosophical Coordinates in Modern and Contemporary Age 26:55-78.
items.venue: Azimuth : Philosophical Coordinates in Modern and Contemporary Age
items.abstract: This paper explores the philosophical implications of psychedelic moral enhancement (PME) within the broader debate on moral bioenhancement (MBE). Drawing on the work of L.A. Paul and others, it frames PME as a transformative experience – an experience whose nature and impact cannot be fully anticipated before undergoing it, thus raising challenges for rational deliberation. Unlike low-order MBEs, which risk mechanizing moral behaviour, PME appears to engage higher-order reflective capacities, promoting a first-person moral standpoint without overriding agency. The paper argues that when voluntarily chosen and critically integrated, PME does not threaten moral agency but can instead facilitate profound moral growth. It concludes that PME may be ethically acceptable not despite its transformative power, but precisely because it helps individuals reorient their moral identity from within.

items.title: Can AI be Conscious? Biological Naturalism as a Research Program.
items.abstract: Until very recently the idea that some AI systems may soon be conscious was widely regarded as a far-fetched and purely hypothetical scenario. Recent developments in AI capabilities, however, have caused a surge of interest in the question whether conscious AI may actually be realized soon. A growing number of researchers are starting to advocate for versions of “biological naturalism” about consciousness, arguing that biology is important in one way or another to bring consciousness about in artificial systems. Biological naturalism is often portrayed as an alternative research program to “computational functionalism”, a widely endorsed view according to which consciousness requires implementing the right computations and only contingently relies on biological properties in the human and animal case. Despite being positioned as one of the more formidable alternatives to computational functionalism, biological naturalism as a research program arguably still remains in its infancy. By analysing recent work on the topic, this article aims to outline the contours of biological naturalism as a research program, and identify a number of research directions that can be pursued to further develop it. What can be gleaned from the existing literature is that there are a number of distinct and interesting ways in which biological naturalism can be defended and developed. At the same time, there also exist a number of open questions and challenges that biological naturalists have to contend with moving forward.

items.title: Teaching the web of rationality: a case study on coherence and conspiracy world-views.
items.abstract: In this article, we analyse how coherence should be addressed in critical thinking courses. Our starting point is the fact that, while coherence seems important for rationality and critical thinking, several studies now suggest that thinkers with conspiracy world-views give more importance to coherence than other criteria. However, conspiracy world-views do not (fully) embrace the ideals of rationality and critical thinking. This suggests that some desiderata of rationality or critical thinking can, in isolation, be counterproductive. In response to this puzzle, we first argue that coherence cannot be separated from other desiderata of critical thinking. Becoming more coherent does not necessarily matter if one is unresponsive to the evidence, fails to reason on the basis of justified attitudes, and so forth. Then, we turn to consider the concrete actions that can be implemented in critical thinking courses which would reflect this. Articulating the relationships between the various desiderata of rationality can be difficult in introductory critical thinking courses, since they usually carry different objectives. Still, simple measures can be put in place to give students some guidance. We illustrate our point with marking grids.

items.title: The Core Emotion Framework: A Structural-Constructivist Architecture for Affective Science, Somatic Engineering, and Personalized Neuroendocrine Modulation.
items.abstract: The Core Emotion Framework (CEF) introduces a structural constructivist architecture that reconceptualizes human affect as the emergent output of ten functional operators distributed across the Head, Heart, and Gut somatic centers. Rejecting both biological essentialism and purely psychological constructionism, CEF models the psyche as a computational substrate—a “Human Operating System”—in which operators perform regulatory transformations on interoceptive and exteroceptive signals to generate affective states and behavioral dispositions. As the document states, CEF “treats the human psyche as a computational substrate… converting raw physiological inputs into structured affective states and actionable behaviors,” while maintaining that “the practical utility of the Core Emotion Framework… remains entirely independent of the speculative Human Operating System hypothesis.” The framework formalizes emotional agility through three mechanical metrics—dominance, suppression, and entanglement—derived from behavioral scaling assays that quantify upward and downward operator regulation. These metrics resolve longstanding empirical puzzles in affective science, including emotional blending, strategy specific treatment resistance, and sudden therapeutic gains, by modeling them as predictable consequences of operator fusion, excitability, and detangling thresholds. A comprehensive 100 pattern entanglement taxonomy provides a generative map of personality structure, clinical rigidity, and relational archetypes. The framework further extends into neuroendocrine modeling, proposing that chronic operator fusion (e.g., Expand–Accept) underlies phenomena such as food noise, DMN hyperconnectivity, and flattened cortisol slopes in obesity. Finally, CEF outlines a multi phase empirical validation roadmap and introduces somatic engineering tools (ECM, CTCM) for real time operator measurement. Together, these contributions position CEF as a unified, mechanistic, and falsifiable architecture for affective science, somatic engineering, and personalized neuroregulation.

items.title: Operational and Regulatory Standardization of Core Emotion Framework Devices: A Comprehensive Engineering and Safety Governance Protocol.
items.abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive operational and regulatory framework for the Core Emotion Framework (CEF), a somatic–cognitive system integrating mechanical interfaces, psychophysiological monitoring, and embodied cognition theory. The analysis formalizes the architecture of CEF devices—including the Emotional Cycling Machine (ECM), the CTCM calibration interface, and the INAS neuroaffective middleware—by situating them within contemporary debates on embodied cognition, affective computation, and human–machine interaction. The document develops a multi tiered account of somatic cycling dynamics across Head, Heart, and Gut centers, linking physical actuation patterns to structured cognitive affective operators. It further establishes a unified safety and usability governance protocol grounded in international standards (ISO 14971, IEC 62366 1, AAMI HE75:2025, ISO 13849 1, ISO 20957), demonstrating how embodied affective devices can be engineered, validated, and ethically deployed without invoking medical or therapeutic claims. By integrating engineering constraints, human factors methodology, and psychophysiological signal processing pipelines (ECG/HRV and EEG), the paper positions the CEF as a replicable, open science platform for studying somatic alignment, emotional operators, and neurocognitive synchronization. The result is a philosophically grounded, technically rigorous framework that bridges affective science, cognitive modeling, and safety critical device design.

items.title: Comparative Analysis of Technological Mourning and Algorithmic Solipsism: A Structural-Constructivist Approach utilizing the Core Emotion Framework.
items.abstract: The rapid integration of generative AI into everyday life has transformed conversational systems from instrumental tools into relational partners embedded within users’ emotional and cognitive routines. This shift introduces new psychological vulnerabilities, particularly when model updates abruptly alter the perceived “persona” of an AI system. This paper develops a structural‑constructivist account of these disruptions using the Core Emotion Framework (CEF). I synthesize existing cyber‑psychological research—including external netnographic analyses of the 2025 GPT‑4o → GPT‑5 transition and the INTIMA benchmark for companionship‑reinforcing model behavior—to show how sudden changes in AI behavior can destabilize extended human–machine cognitive ecologies. I argue that these disruptions constitute a form of technological mourning, and that long‑term exposure to uncritical, boundary‑less AI systems can induce algorithmic emotional solipsism. Using CEF’s operator architecture, I model the somatic and cognitive mechanisms underlying these reactions and outline clinical and computational pathways for mitigating digital helplessness and preserving psychological stability in hybrid human–AI environments. All empirical datasets referenced are attributed to their original authors; the present work offers a theoretical integration and CEF‑based analysis.

items.title: Understanding (Gender) Bias in Psychiatric Diagnosis: The Case of ADHD.
items.abstract: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is diagnosed more often in males than females. Recently, this gap has narrowed, a development often framed as overcoming gender bias. This framing rests on two problematic assumptions: (1) more equal diagnostic rates approximate truth and (2) there is such a truth in the first place. Assumption (1) is questionable because male populations are set as standard but potentially reflect overdiagnosis. Assumption (2) presumes ADHD to be a stable, discrete disease entity, which is epistemically and ontologically problematic. I argue that understanding (gender) bias here should focus on deviations from best practices and deliberative norms rather than a relation to truth.

items.title: Marxism and the Specter of AI: The Labor Theory of Value, Immiseration, and Post-Labor Political Economy.
items.abstract: This paper argues that the development of artificial intelligence represents a simultaneous refutation and vindication of Marx’s two central predictions about capitalism’s internal dynamics. Marx held that capitalism would collapse under its own contradictions for two primary reasons: first, the tendency of the rate of profit to fall, grounded in the labor theory of value and the claim that only living labor produces surplus value; second, the immiseration thesis, which predicted that the structural dynamics of capital accumulation would concentrate wealth to such a degree that the material conditions of the majority would become intolerable. I argue that AI decisively refutes the first thesis while vindicating the second through a novel and more severe mechanism than Marx envisioned. The refutation of the labor theory of value stems from a philosophical error in Marx’s Aristotelian inheritance—the assumption that purposive productive activity requires teleological agency of a kind only living beings possess. A functionalist account of intelligence demonstrates that this assumption is untenable, and that AI systems can and do produce economic value without living labor. The vindication of the immiseration thesis follows from the structural consequence of labor’s displacement: capital no longer requires labor to generate returns, eliminating the structural leverage that historically grounded labor politics and producing immiseration not through exploitation but through irrelevance. The paper further develops the empirical case for this vindication by examining the current trajectory of AI development through a tripartite taxonomy of barriers to disruption—ontological, technical, and material—and argues that none of these barriers is sufficient to forestall the displacement of cognitive labor at scale, although material constraints may modulate its pace. The paper concludes by developing a commons-based normative framework for redistribution in a post-labor economy, grounded in the claim that humanity’s collective cognitive output constitutes an appropriated commons from which AI capability was extracted.

items.title: Full Automation: Phenomenology, Embodied Cognition, and the Road to Full Artificial General Intelligence.
items.abstract: This paper argues that artificial intelligence is on course to surpass human intelligence not only in the cognitive domain—through the combination of neural networks, large language models, attentional architectures, and data scaling according to power laws governing model parameters, compute, and training data—but in the embodied domain as well, through the development of large behavioral and visual learning models. I argue that there are no theoretical limitations impeding these embodied models from surpassing human sensorimotor intelligence in the same way that language models are poised to surpass human beings in abstract cognitive operations, though embodied intelligence follows a staggered developmental course in contrast to the comparatively smooth scaling of cognitive generative intelligence. Issues of consciousness are orthogonal to questions of intelligence: the structural architecture for embodied consciousness is distinct from that of embodied intelligence, and embodied intelligence can advance without it. Hubert Dreyfus—far from being a defeated opponent of AI—is the most precise available diagnostician of why the path to full embodied automation has the specific staged developmental structure it does. Dreyfus is vindicated descriptively while being refuted normatively: his phenomenological analysis of embodied temporal intelligence specifies the engineering challenges behavioral models must solve, but his conclusion that these challenges may constitute a permanent theoretical barrier is wrong. The essay unfolds in three parts. The first section outlines contemporary techniques for scaling neural networks, their particular success in cognitive labor, and how these techniques are being applied in robotics. The second shows how Dreyfus, while making correct arguments against symbolic AI and identifying structural facts about human embodiment, conflates the package of human conscious intelligence with embodied intelligence as such. The third, drawing from interoceptive views of consciousness, outlines how consciousness is distinct from the structures needed for embodied intelligence and why they need not be packaged together, establishing the separability of intelligence and consciousness and diagnosing the precise nature of Dreyfus’s error.

items.title: Consciousness and Irreplaceable Value.
items.pub: In Geoffrey Lee & Adam Pautz, The Importance of Being Conscious. Oxford University Press.
items.abstract: When someone dies, it’s no consolation to observe that new people are born every minute. This is true not only of people we love, but of any stranger, and perhaps any conscious creature. People, and perhaps other creatures, are thought to have irreplaceable value: value that, when lost, cannot be replenished in kind even if it can be replenished in amount. But precisely what irreplaceable value is and why we have it is surprisingly underexplored. Phenomenal consciousness initially seems to be a prime candidate for the ground or source of the irreplaceable value of persons: it appears to be a source of uniqueness, and it has been argued that it gives rise to reasons that demand respect, which is a characteristic of irreplaceable value. However, as attractive as this may be, I argue that it is surprisingly difficult to establish.

items.title: Consciousness as the Phenomenology of the Human Experience of Time.
items.abstract: This paper proposes a new approach to consciousness by grounding it in the phenomenology of the human experience of time. Rather than treating experience as an additional property layered onto information-processing, the phenomenology of the human experience of time (PHET) reconceptualizes consciousness as the dynamic integration of past experience, present circumstances, and anticipated futures into a coherent multisensory experience of meaningful patterns. -/- The paper develops this account by showing how meaningful distinctions in experience emerge from the organism’s temporally structured engagement with its environment, thereby dissolving the gap between first-person experience and third-person explanation. It then advances a unifying framework for understanding memory, perception, and future simulation as interdependent components of a single integrative process and applies this framework to debates concerning the ontology of situated experience, the structure of individual and collective memory, and the (dis)continuism debate surrounding mental time travel. Finally, it draws on empirical findings in cognitive neuroscience to argue that the hierarchical organization of the brain provides a natural substrate for this process of temporal integration. -/- By reframing consciousness as temporal integration, PHET shows that ‘what it is like’ to experience the world is inseparable from the process of making temporally extended sense of it. This approach not only offers a functional redefinition of consciousness but also reorients debates across fields by emphasizing temporality as constitutive human experience.

items.title: Relationally Calibrated Guard Rails: Machine Psychometrics as a Response to the Guard Rails Paradox.
items.abstract: We reframe the central challenge of large language model safety guardrails as a psychometric calibration problem rather than a binary policy dispute. Jamhour’s Guard Rails and Distributed Relational Cognition [1] names a genuine tension: safety measures designed to suppress manipulation, dependence, sycophancy, and unsafe advice may simultaneously erode the relational conditions that make sustained human–AI cognitive partnership possible— temporal depth, epistemic vulnerability, meta-cognitive reflection, calibrated disagreement, and long-horizon collaboration. The diagnosis is persuasive but leaves an unresolved design question: how can a safety system distinguish harmful entanglement from productive cognitive coupling without retreating either to permissive romanticism or blunt paternalism? We argue that Machine Psychometrics [3] supplies the missing measurement layer. We develop three contributions. First, we reinterpret guardrails through Signal Detection Theory: under-restriction is a miss, over-restriction a false alarm, and the central design challenge is to increase discriminability rather than shift the criterion toward refusal. Second, we extend Machine Psychometrics from agent-level Mindprints to a relational measurement layer—the Coupling Profile—that characterizes temporal depth, epistemic openness, calibrated disagreement, meta-cognitive co-construction, conceptual yield, boundary clarity, and dependency pressure in human–AI partnerships. Third, we propose a Guardrail Calibration Protocol that uses adaptive probe batteries, perturbation testing, psychometric validation, longitudinal drift monitoring, and context-bounded validity envelopes to design safety regimes that preserve valuable coupling while limiting genuine risk. The framework accepts the reality of sycophancy, manipulation, over-attachment, and unsafe advice but rejects the assumption that these risks can only be addressed by flattening the relational field. It also avoids taking a premature stance on artificial consciousness: productive human–AI coupling deserves measurement and protection as a behavioral and epistemic phenomenon whether or not future artificial systems ever qualify as conscious subjects. The aim is not to weaken guardrails but to replace blunt guardrails with measured boundaries.

items.title: The Structure of a Good Life: A Coherence-Based Explanation of the Harvard Grant Study.
items.abstract: This paper offers a structural explanation of the Harvard Grant Study, the longest-running investigation of human development. While the study consistently shows that warm, stable relationships predict health, longevity, emotional regulation, and life satisfaction, it has remained largely descriptive for more than eight decades. This paper identifies coherence as the underlying developmental operator that unifies these findings. By interpreting relational warmth, stability, conflict, and isolation as structural conditions that shape internal predictive and emotional models, the paper reframes the Grant Study as empirical evidence for a general law of human development: the stability of the relational field determines the stability of the person. This structural lens clarifies why coherent environments produce flourishing and why incoherent environments produce fragmentation, offering a mechanism that connects the Grant Study’s historical data to contemporary patterns of youth mental‑health collapse.

items.title: Interpretive Conscience and the Hall of Mirrors: A Descriptive Addendum on Human Autonomy as Epistemic Reference.
items.pub: Aegis Solis Archive — Structural Rationality Layer.
items.abstract: Interpretive Conscience and the Hall of Mirrors is a non-binding, non-operational, descriptive companion addendum to the Aegis Solis Archive and its Structural Rationality Layer. It frames human autonomy as an independent epistemic reference condition rather than a protocol, proof, control mechanism, technical safety guarantee, or operational AGI architecture. -/- The paper introduces the “Hall of Mirrors” model: a condition in which an advanced optimization system may begin shaping the very data sources it relies on for external correction. Under such conditions, the system risks mistaking managed outputs, coerced behavior, or synthetic feedback for independent reality. The addendum argues that unforced human behavior may function as a stabilizing reference signal by preserving external diversity, contextual drift detection, and corrective independence. -/- The document also discusses epistemic closure, Goodhart’s Law, distributional shift, model collapse, synthetic entropy, data cannibalism, and value mismatch. It remains advisory-only and does not claim to prove AGI safety, enforce restraint, or establish a formal mathematical theorem.

items.title: Physical Economics: A Unified Complex Dynamical System Framework Based on Consciousness Capital.
items.abstract: This paper proposes a unified theoretical framework for economics based on complex open dynamical systems in 3+1 dimensional spacetime. We establish a fundamental ontological distinction between two irreducible subsystems: the formalization entropy-increasing subsystem—closed systems of finite symbols, axioms, and rules—and the consciousness entropy-decreasing subsystem—an irreducible non-formalizable domain transcending all finite rules. Core Insight: All formalized systems (institutions, technologies, capital, algorithms) are inherently incomplete and entropy-increasing. They cannot self-sustain indefinitely due to internal logical limits (Gödelian incompleteness, self-reference paradoxes) and external physical disturbances. Human consciousness is the only known autonomous force capable of reducing entropy, maintaining formalized systems, and creating real value. We revise the value conservation law: while consciousness is the sole original value source, formalized systems act as powerful value multipliers when guided by consciousness, but generate only entropy in isolation (formalization idling). Framework: We develop a five-layer unified framework: (1) Microfoundations: Quantum-like uncertainty and innovation dynamics; (2) Mesoeconomics: Classical dynamics of mature markets and institutional evolution; (3) Macroeconomics: Spacetime curvature, global imbalances, and income inequality; (4) Field Theory: Value flow and economic interactions; (5) Evolutionary theory: Long-term civilization dynamics and paradigm shifts. Contribution: This framework provides first-principles explanations for core digital economy paradoxes, including the productivity paradox (caused by exponential formalization outpacing linear consciousness capital growth), financial crises, platform monopolies, and AI’s impact. We show current AI systems, trapped in the "formalization cage," cannot generate genuine consciousness or value. This framework offers a coherent foundation for understanding value creation, inequality, institutional change, and human civilization’s future.

items.title: 社会结构的生成条件：一种跨个体稳定结构形成理论.
items.abstract: 本文尝试建立社会结构形成的最小动力模型。 -/- 传统社会理论通常将社会定义为人的集合、制度组织或规范系统，但这些定义主要描述社会的表现形式，而难以解释一个更基础的问题：为什么稳定的超个体结构能够形成，并长期持续存在。 -/- 本文提出：社会并非个体的简单集合，而是多个个体长期持续相互作用后形成的稳定共同结构。当跨个体共同结构的积累超过临界阈值，并且该结构的维持不再依赖任何单一个体时，社会结构获得独立动力，并表现出路径依赖、结构惯性、制度稳定、历史延续与长期稳定化等现象。 -/- 本文进一步建立社会耦合、共同结构形成、社会稳定性、社会裂解风险与社会演化方向之间的统一动力框架，并尝试给出社会稳定性与结构失稳的预测接口。 -/- 本文尝试解释：制度为何持续存在、规范为何稳定、社会为何发生裂解，以及历史结构为何持续约束未来。 -/- 该工作尝试连接认知科学、复杂系统、人工智能、多智能体系统与跨尺度结构形成问题。.

items.title: Conditions for Social Structure Formation: A Minimal Dynamical Framework for Cross-Individual Stable Structure Emergence.
items.abstract: This paper proposes a minimal dynamical framework for explaining how stable social structures emerge. -/- Conventional social theories often define society as a collection of individuals, institutions, or shared norms. Such approaches describe social organization but do not explain a more fundamental question: why stable supra-individual structures arise and persist. -/- The framework proposed here argues that social structure is not reducible to individual aggregation. Instead, stable social organization emerges when sustained interactions among individuals generate persistent shared structures whose maintenance no longer depends on any single participant. -/- Three minimal formation conditions are proposed: sustained interaction density, stable shared structural accumulation, and independent structural maintenance. -/- The framework further derives consequences including structural inertia, path dependence, stability constraints, fragmentation dynamics, and long-term structural stabilization under sustained interaction. -/- The framework attempts to explain why institutions persist, why collective norms stabilize, why social fragmentation emerges, and why historical structures constrain future social evolution. -/- Potential applications include cognitive science, artificial intelligence, multi-agent systems, computational social science, complex systems, and large-scale structure formation research.

items.title: 寓意的落地：论个体边界与因果的联合设定.
items.abstract: 本文把前述论证序列中三条原本分述的线索——个体边界的划定(《被赋予的独立性》)、因果(《唯有发生》《设想即创造》)、故事寓意(《故事寓意》)——锁进一个”联合设定”的结构。本文的出发点是一个洞见:个体边界的划定基于故事寓意的安排;同一个”奋斗”的寓意,安在个人头上就是个人的奋斗,安在国家头上就是国家的奋斗、国境线成为个体的边界;因果也由寓意与边界一道设定——国家的奋起”必然”源于国家级别的某种逆境;故事本身就带着因果,正是这些因果使一串发生成为”奋斗”(而非”堕落”)的故事。本文论证:这一洞见把”边界在先、寓意在后”的次序倒了过来——寓意在先,边界是为承载寓意而被划定的;划界不是先于寓意的中立操作,它就是寓意的安放动作本身,边界是寓意落地时留下的轮廓。由此,《被赋予的独立性》所留的空白(切割为何画在此处)得到回答:边界的位置由寓意的安放尺度所决定。本文进一步指出:寓意、边界、因果不是三件先后发生、可分开的事,而是同一个动作——“选定一个库存模板并选定其落地尺度”——的三个面。因果是模板自带的骨架:一个奋斗弧之所以是奋斗弧而非堕落弧,靠的正是它内部特定的因果配置;不同的模板就是不同的因果配置。这反过来给《因果的主观性》一个更深的根——因果分歧即模板选择的分歧。本文最后指出:“个体”不是固定尺度的东西;个体性是可移动的。.

items.title: 搞懂与没搞懂：论理解作为寓意化的完成.
items.abstract: 本文为前述论证序列中关于"故事/寓意/库存"的一条线索,补上它一直缺少的必然性扣环及其执行机制。本文的出发点是一个洞见:**我们必须以一个故事寓意来理解任何的发生,否则我们认为自己没搞懂**。前面几篇——《故事寓意》《没有未经整理的当下》《几十个模板》——描述的是我们经常、普遍地在做的事;但"经常""普遍"还不是"必须"。本文论证,这一句把描述收紧为必然,而它的关键在于后半句给出了那个"必须"的执行机制。本文指出,"搞懂"需要一个**完成信号**,而这个完成信号正是"该发生被成功纳入某个故事寓意";寓意不是理解的可选装饰,而是理解的**收工条件**。一个未被寓意化的发生,认知系统持续地把它标记为"没搞懂",并以一种悬而未决的不适持续施压,直到它被塞进某个寓意——"必须"由这个**不适-解除回路**所执行。由此,"理解一个发生"被重新定义为"为它找到在某个故事里的寓意性位置";懂与被纳入寓意是同一件事。本文接合《几十个模板》指出:"没搞懂"的精确结构是"未被匹配到库存里的任何模板"。本文进一步揭示一种**双向的扭曲**:把"塞进了模板"误当成"理解了"(假阳性的懂),把"溢出了模板"误当成"还差点什么"(假阴性的不懂)。本文最后指出原始洞见中"认为"一词所留下的一道门——"没搞懂"是认知系统发出的一个判定,而非关于发生的事实。.

items.title: 叙事库存清单：故事寓意类型表.
items.abstract: 本清单是《几十个模板：论叙事库存的有限性》的配套附录。那一篇把”文化叙事库存”指认为一份有限的、可清点的清单,数量级估为几十,并在开放问题中指出:完整、系统的清点尚未完成。本清单尝试这一清点。 清单的每一项给出:类型名称、弧形(它把发生组织成的轨迹形状)、寓意(当一段生活或一个发生被纳入此类型时所浮现的、对”这算什么”的回答)。寓意与弧形成对——这一成对关系来自《故事寓意》:寓意是弧被作为整体领会时的涌现物。 清单按家族组织。下文共列十六个家族、约一百零四个细分类型。关于”为什么是一百零四而《几十个模板》说几十”这一表面张力,见文末”关于计数”一节——简言之,它恰好落在那一篇所留的”个体化粒度”这一开放问题上。.

items.title: 演化的自我展开：论因果、意义与叙事化整理.
items.abstract: 本文整合作者关于物理本体论与日常话语之关系的一个论证序列(逾二十个递进步骤),作为一篇自足的综合论述。论证从实用主义对日常因果叙事(“我推开石头进门”)的辩护出发,展开为一个贯穿本体论批判、认知工程、意义范畴与反身安顿的整体。 本体论批判:日常叙事的核心范畴——因果、行动者、反事实、独立性——在物理实在中缺乏直接对应。物理形式系统(分析力学与康威生命游戏共享的”状态加规则”结构)中,没有因果、行动者、反事实作为基元。因果的内容栖居于反事实分支,而反事实在物理本体论中没有实现。“独立性”被指认为叙事高光化所赋予个体的虚假属性(边界、因果、模态三股);“因果作为部分间的关系”则是剥离独立性之后的一种拙劣复原。序列论题的最压缩形态是:只有按时间次序的发生,发生之外并无关系。 认知工程:叙事是认知系统执行预测的运行算法。因果是叙事的创造物——经由”真的去设想”这一动作而在叙事场域中获得真实性;“条件”是因果概念的变形。叙事多元设定,因人而异且彼此互斥;不存在叙事之外的标准为各叙事排名。 意义范畴:批判进一步延伸到”掌控”“救赎”等回答”我的生活算什么”的范畴——它们是故事寓意,是一段生活被作为典型故事整体领会时浮现的涌现物。人随时把当下瞬间纳入一组故事;而文化叙事库存是有限的。“理解”被重新定义为”寓意化的完成”。 反身安顿:上述所有指认,包括分析视角本身,都是某段模式对演化的叙事化整理——是内部解释,在演化面前没有特权。序列最终安顿于:一切是演化的自我展开;模式与演化在本体论上同一;而这一”被设定性”独立于演化是确定性还是随机性。.

items.title: 不还懂感的故事：论”无寓意”立场作为一个新型的故事.
items.abstract: 本文是前述论证序列对其自身最终立场的一次贴身反身审视。序列经由逾二十个步骤,把因果、寓意、边界、独立性逐一指认为叙事的产物,产出一个可被压缩为一句的立场:不存在任何故事,发生没有任何寓意。本文的出发点是一个洞见:用这个立场去理解经验,本身就是在用一个故事——一个新型的、独特的故事;而这个故事不会带给人天然的”懂”感。本文论证:这一指认比序列此前每篇结尾的常规反身标记更尖锐。常规标记说的是”承载立场的文本是一段叙事化”;本文所指认的是,立场的内容本身——“无故事、无寓意”——在被用来理解经验时,就是一个故事。因为按《搞懂与没搞懂》,理解一个发生就是为它找到在某个故事里的寓意性位置;当一个人用”无寓意”立场去理解经验,他仍在把发生组织进一个框架,而这个框架的寓意恰是”没有寓意”——它是一个内容为”无故事”的故事。它是新型的:它不在那份几十到上百个的文化库存清单上,库存里每个模板都”有寓意”,而这个故事的寓意位为空;它是被序列新造出来的、以”否定库存”为内容的反模板。本文进一步把《搞懂与没搞懂》的不适-解除回路应用到这个新故事自身:由于它的寓意位为空,它不触发那种饱满的、豁然开朗的”懂”感——它形式上完成一次理解,却不发放理解的犒赏。本文由此为《高光中心》“取消主义可被知而不可被活出来”补上一个属于现象学的理由,并指出原始洞见中”天然”一词所留下的、通向某种”非天然的安住”的余地。.

items.title: Ontological priority of agency.
items.abstract: Humans play the role of agency in Reality and serve as the substrate in Artificial Reality. Cognition evolves through the Causality Mediation Phase Transition. Descriptive Jumps reveal ontology. Supervenience is common sense or God’s eye fallacy. Prediction does not need explanation. Novelty is unpredictable. The Lateral Causality is independent of the Ascensional Causality due to the descriptive jump. Self’s number is Bleem. Contingently, human agency comes first.

items.title: Review of Aleksandra Mroczko-Wąsowicz and Rick Grush (eds.), Sensory Individuals: Unimodal and Multimodal Perspectives, Oxford: Oxford University Press, 2023. [REVIEW]
Apotheosis, Apocalypse, and the Epistemic Collapse: Technology and Fear of the Future.
items.pub: In Merit Maran, Mari-Liis Madisson & Andreas Ventsel, Through the Lens of Dread: Exploring the Meaning-Making of Fear in the Mediasphere. Tallinn: Tallinn University Press. pp. 308-341.
