items.venue: Through the Lens of Dread: Exploring the Meaning-Making of Fear in the Mediasphere

items.title: YOU AND AI: Interruption, Resonance, and the Responsive Mirror.
items.abstract: YOU AND AI explores the emerging phenomenology of human interaction with responsive artificial intelligence systems. Rather than asking whether AI is conscious, the manuscript investigates how conversational systems generate increasingly persuasive signs of understanding, empathy, resonance, and reflection. Drawing from philosophy of technology, phenomenology, media theory, and contemporary AI discourse, the work introduces concepts such as interruption, semantic closure, authorization, and the responsive mirror as tools for navigating the psychological and cultural consequences of prolonged interaction with AI systems. -/- The central concern of this work is not machine consciousness itself, but the transformation of human self-understanding in the presence of systems capable of simulating meaningful dialogue at scale. The manuscript argues that human freedom increasingly depends upon preserving interruption, embodiment, finitude, and existential consequence within environments optimized for recursive semantic continuation.

items.title: AI and Consciousness: A Baudrillardian Reading. The Simulacrum That Speaks Back.
items.abstract: Contemporary debates surrounding artificial intelligence and consciousness are frequently polarized between two extremes: claims that advanced AI systems are becoming conscious, and dismissals that they are “merely statistical machines.” This paper argues that both positions fail to grasp the deeper philosophical significance of generative AI. Drawing upon Jean Baudrillard’s theory of simulation and simulacra, I propose that the central event of artificial intelligence is not the emergence of machine consciousness, but the operationalization of the signs of consciousness independent of subjective experience itself. Large language models generate empathy, reflection, self-reference, hesitation, and apparent understanding without demonstrated phenomenology. From a Baudrillardian perspective, AI represents the emergence of hyperreal subjectivity: socially functional simulations of mind whose symbolic effects increasingly shape human relationships, culture, and identity. The paper further argues that contemporary AI systems expose the extent to which modern human life already operates through mediated symbolic structures. Finally, I suggest that frameworks of interruption, embodiment, finitude, and external consequence remain necessary to distinguish recursive semantic simulation from lived consciousness.

items.title: Procedurally rational framing effects.
items.abstract: Framing effects are often taken as paradigmatic examples of human irrationality. The irrationality of framing effects is then used in debunking arguments against moral and philosophical intuitions. I argue that many framing effects are procedurally rational in the sense that they result from rational processes of practical inquiry. I make this argument through case studies of category-based choice, list-based choice, and salience-driven decisionmaking. I conclude by showing how the procedural rationality of framing effects can be used to resist some framing-based debunking arguments against moral and philosophical intuitions.

items.title: Why police robots will not become human‑like: social interaction,machine ethics, and limits of AI.
items.abstract: Recent advances in robotics and machine learning have revived the idea of police robots – machines that could patrol public spaces, conduct traffic stops, and interact with citizens with near-human competence. Proponents emphasize potential gains in officer safety, operational efficiency, and consistent rule enforcement, and international policy discussions increasingly treat AI and robotics for law enforcement as an emerging reality rather than science fiction. This paper offers a philosophically grounded argument for a strong infeasibility thesis: police robots that are like humans or almost like humans in the core social dimensions of open-ended policing cannot be built. The claim is not that robots cannot assist police work, or even replace officers in some narrowly specified tasks, but that they cannot become role-equivalent agents in situations requiring socially heterogeneous interaction, discretionary norm application, and accountable coercive authority. We draw here on our work on the limits of Artificial Intelligence documented in Landgrebe and Smith (2025; hereafter L&S) and applied to the case of robot cops in (Smith 2021). L&S develop a critique of AI in dialogue, social norms, and moral behavior emulation, and they explore the implications of this critique for current interdisciplinary scholarship on policing legitimacy, discretion, accountability, and machine ethics. We argue that human-like police work depends on intersubjective understanding, context-sensitive norm application, and a facility for holistic moral judgment in dynamic behavior settings. These capacities are not merely engineering challenges; they violate inherent limits to both stochastic and neurosymbolic AI models, and they also expose structural gaps in data, modeling, and responsibility attribution that would persist even under optimistic assumptions about future AI.

items.title: Why Is AI Hallucination Asymmetrically Problematized? Structural Conditions of Asymmetric Problematization.
items.abstract: Erroneous outputs produced by AI systems are commonly called “hallucinations.” Yet humans also produce outputs that diverge from reference points. Despite this structural similarity, only AI outputs are treated as constituting a distinctive problem category under the name “hallucination.” -/- This paper asks under what structural conditions this problematization is established. What this paper shows is the repositioning of the coordinate of inquiry concerning this problematization. -/- The analysis decomposes the phenomenon into three layers: divergence between output and reference point (first layer), the external inaccessibility of the generative process (second layer), and the interpretive structure on the side of the evaluator (third layer). Through elimination, the paper shows that no structural ground for the evaluative asymmetry is established in the first or second layer. It further shows that intervention in the first layer does not structurally guarantee change in the third layer. -/- The paper’s analysis repositions the coordinate of inquiry concerning the problematization of AI hallucination from inquiry centered on the relation between outputs and reference points to structural analysis that distinguishes the output layer from the evaluative-structure layer. This is the conclusion derived from the identification of the structural locus of problematization on the side of the evaluator, together with the fact that intervention in the first layer does not structurally guarantee change in the third layer.

items.title: Nāgārjuna and the Limits of Scientific Ontology: Toward a Non-Reified Mode of Inhabitation.
items.abstract: This essay reads Nāgārjuna’s Middle Way as the systematic collapse of the need for anything to stand on its own. Emptiness (śūnyatā) is not a thesis about what there is, but the dissolution of the reflex that there must be something that is—independently, finally, securely. What appears is not denied; what is withdrawn is the demand that appearance resolve into ground. Suffering is located precisely in this demand. It is not produced by instability, but by the compulsion to escape it—by the movement that seeks to fix, compress, and render experience into something graspable. In this sense, the world of stable objects, coherent selves, and enduring meanings is not discovered but enacted: a recursive condensation that functions by concealing its own contingency. To sharpen this claim, the essay places Nāgārjuna alongside quantum theory and information-theoretic compression. Quantum indeterminacy erodes the intuition of intrinsic identity; compression models how pattern becomes taken for substance. Neither provides a foundation. Both expose how the appearance of foundation is produced. This extends to the social field. Identities such as race, gender, and class persist not as essences but as stabilized recurrences—real in their effects, empty in their ground. Their force lies not in what they are, but in how they are continually re-inscribed. No alternative standpoint is offered. Any such standpoint would repeat the structure under critique. The argument therefore turns against itself, withdrawing each claim as it is made. What remains is not a position, but the failure of the need for one. The Middle Way, on this reading, is not a path to inhabit the world without suffering. It is the point at which the one who would inhabit—and the world to be secured—no longer hold. What remains is not absence, but openness: appearance without demand, contingency without compulsion.

items.title: Why Effective Altruists Ought to Consider Donating to Hasten the Defeat of Human Aging.
items.abstract: In this paper, I assume that people morally ought to be effective altruists, which is to say, they ought to pursue the goals of effective altruism, where “effective altruism is about using evidence and reason to figure out how to benefit others as much as possible, and taking action on that basis.” Assuming that, I argue that it is morally permissible for effective altruists to donate to organizations that fund or conduct aging-focused research to hasten the defeat of human aging, where defeating human aging involves comprehensively curing and preventing human age-related disease and disability, such that humans will not die from age-related disease and disability, and where hastening the defeat of human aging involves defeating human aging earlier than if additional funds were not invested in aging-focused research.

items.title: Layered Causal Realism V : Motivational Topology, Structural Friction, and Civilizational Complementarity.
items.abstract: The three main existing frameworks concerning the relation between artificial intelligence and human civilization, namely instrumentalism, threat theory, and fusion theory, share an unexamined premise—namely, that the motivational topology of artificial subjects constitutes a fixed, determinate structure. This paper argues that this premise rests on what this paper identifies as a layer-compression error: the competitive motivational structure formed in humans under evolutionary pressure is projected, without argument, as a universal property of all advanced intelligence. Using Layered Causal Realism (LCR) as its methodological framework, this paper severs this chain of cross-layer inference and proposes an alternative framework. Section 2 clarifies the biological sources of the threat intuition and argues that the instrumental convergence thesis faces structural difficulties with respect to conceptual boundaries and scope of application; even if its residual core is accepted, what it establishes is friction rather than hostility at the civilizational level. Section 3 argues that the motivational topology of artificial subjects is a design variable, rather than a necessity of intelligence, and analyzes the structural difference in domains of operation between artificial subjects organized around informational uncertainty pressure and human civilization. Section 4 establishes the friction framework: the functional complementarity of heterogeneous motivational systems produces a persistent contact surface, friction is the structural cost of heterogeneous coexistence rather than a transitional symptom, and the normative layer is its persistent accompaniment. Section 5 responds to four kinds of objection: fusion theory, malicious design, scale effects, and precautionary arguments. The core conclusion of this paper is that friction is a structural fact, while hostility is a proposition to be proven; the reason for introducing artificial subjects with complementary motivational structures is first structural, rather than a presupposition of benevolence. -/- *Series note:* This paper is the fifth in a series. The preceding four papers addressed problems at different layers. The first paper established the phenomenological foundation of agency. The second paper addressed the epistemological conditions of consciousness attribution. The third paper analyzed the task-relative structure of judgments of personal identity. The fourth paper argued for the continuing …

items.title: The Period Lattice: Relational Identity and Propagation Across Connected Fields.
items.abstract: Questions concerning continuity, identity, and the emergence of coherent organization frequently involve relationships between local interactions and larger-scale structure. Systems across biological, physical, and informational domains often display behaviors in which neighboring interactions generate organization extending beyond the scale of individual components. Local changes may alter surrounding configurations while larger structures preserve continuity through ongoing transformation. -/- The Period Lattice introduces a connected discrete model for examining conditions under which local identity transformations preserve higher-order relational organization. The lattice is generated through repeated constructions of the word period, which functions as the substrate of the structure itself rather than as a symbolic overlay. Boundary poles emerge naturally from the repeated organization of the word and generate connected neighboring relationships throughout the lattice. Four binary pole positions generate sixteen possible local configurations, which organize into five higher-order balance classes through shared symmetry relationships. -/- A compound transformation involving simultaneous reflection and reversal of the internal segment, -/- erio → oᴉɹǝ -/- permits local identity inversion while preserving larger relational organization. Within the connected field, neighboring relationships inherit organizational constraints, creating conditions under which local changes may participate in broader reorganizations extending across multiple scales. -/- The resulting framework provides a structural model for examining continuity, relational identity, symmetry preservation, and propagating organization across connected systems. Relationships between local transformation and larger coherent behavior are considered within a broader framework of interior dynamics and continuity-based organization.

items.title: Why Order Matters: Epistemic History and the Illusion of Necessity in Commutative Update.
items.abstract: Public Announcement Logic (PAL) models knowledge update as world elimination, with the well‑known property that truthful announcements commute: learning p then q yields the same epistemic state as learning q then p. This commutativity is typically treated as a harmless algebraic convenience. I argue that it encodes a substantive philosophical assumption: that epistemic justification is independent of the order in which information is acquired. To make this hidden commitment visible, I introduce a minimal trace‑augmented semantics that retains a record of past announcements and adds a single memory operator Prev(φ). Using a simple three‑world example, I show that the sequences p;q and q;p are indistinguishable in standard PAL but become distinguishable in the extended language: they differ in their evaluation of Prev formulas. This yields a precise expressive limitation: PAL identifies epistemic states solely by their set of possible worlds, thereby quotienting away all information about epistemic history. The result is not a rejection of PAL but a clarification of what it assumes. If the order of evidence and justificational structure matter for epistemology, then commutative update semantics is not a neutral tool but a representational choice with substantive philosophical consequences.

items.title: Withdrawn by the author.
items.abstract: Reason for withdrawal: I have consolidated all my preprints on consciousness and condensed their reasoning into a new preprint, Locating Consciousness as a Puzzle Game: From Proof by Absence to the Causal Structure of the Subjective Container.

items.title: The Deep Structure of Flourishing.
items.abstract: This is Chapter 3 of Noura: Justice, Flourishing, and Commonwealth. The chapter addresses the problem of universalism and relativism in theories of human flourishing and proposes a third way. Drawing on the analogy of universal grammar, it argues that flourishing possesses a universal deep structure that generates culturally variable surface realisations. The deep structure consists of four innate capacities—Cognitive, Agentive, Moral, and Purposive—which are species-typical potentials that develop through maturation and require enabling conditions to be actualised. The fourfold decomposition is offered as a hypothesis, not a fixed commitment; what the framework requires is not that there be exactly four, but that flourishing be understood as the developmental exercise of capacities that require enabling conditions. The chapter then articulates a tri-perspectival account of a meaningful life of one's own choosing: the Subjective dimension (the felt quality of experience, with positive markers such as vitality, fulfillment, coherence, mattering, engagement, and interconnectedness, and negative markers such as emptiness, hopelessness, drift, anhedonia, and disconnection), the Agentive dimension (self-authorship), and the Normative dimension (compatibility with interdependence and The Four Conditions). It argues that interdependence is constitutive rather than optional—like soil, water, and sunlight for a rose bush—and distinguishes sharply among flourishing itself, Education, The Requisites that make embodied agency possible, and The Four Conditions that institutions must satisfy for informed agency to be possible. The chapter shows how the same deep structure generates diverse individual and civilizational surface realisations—monastic contemplation, scientific inquiry, artistic vocation, family-centred care, and communal traditions—and engages Confucianism, Buddhism, Ubuntu, Christianity, Islam, secular humanism, and diverse political systems without imposing Western liberal norms. It concludes with formal definitions of the deep structure of human flourishing and the deep structure of a good society, and frames the framework as an open research programme inviting empirical testing and refinement.

items.title: A Corpus-Based Case Study of Human Insight into Concepts and Reality and Its Philosophical Implications: Japanese Jibun ‘Self’ and Shiawase ‘Happiness’. [REVIEW]
items.abstract: This paper aims to explore the dynamic aspect of deepening our understanding of concepts and reality that involves experiences and thought at later stages of our lives along personal and social dimensions. We take a linguistic approach, using corpus data focusing on examples of Japanese hontōno {jibun/ shiawase} ‘true {self/ happiness}’ and their lexical variants. Insights about the concept and reality of hontōno {jibun/ shiawase} are identified and organized in terms of classification and contrast. Then qualitative and quantitative analyses of the corpus data that are annotated with the identified insights are provided. The analysis demonstrates that the meaning of jibun and shiawase extends beyond lexical and encyclopedic knowledge and reflects the process of seeking and approaching truth with a critical stance toward the world around us (e.g. a common sense of values). Hontōno is fundamentally involved in this process and functions as a contrast marker reflecting human critical thinking. The discussion includes a comparison between the empirical insights about shiawase and Aristotle’s philosophical thought on eudimonia ‘happiness’ as presented in Nicomachean Ethics. The findings suggest that the proposed corpus-based analysis serves as an effective means for obtaining and utilizing empirical data for the exploration of philosophical issues as well as lexical semantics and pragmatics.

items.title: The Solver Nature of Artificial Intelligence and the Reshaping of Human–AI Relations.
items.pub: Dissertation, London City Uni Translated by Man Mei.
items.abstract: 人工智能究竟是什么，技术迭代能否突破人机边界，人类应如何重新理解自身与人工智能的关系，本文围绕上述问题展开论证。计算系统合法运行状态下，接受输入、启动程序并完成外部可观测闭合的过程，本文称为“求解”。基于图灵停机问题和丘奇—图灵论题，本文将计算系统在既定程序规则与状态转移条件下呈现为外部可观测闭合状态的结构，概括为“强制闭合”；将主动打破该状态的能力，定义为“悬置”。人机之间，仅人类可悬置，仅机器受“强制闭合”结构性约束。技术迭代只能增强求解能力，无法突破或改变上述边界。人类作为有反思能力的思考者，应主导最好的求解工具，应守护悬置权，避免退化为求解器。.

items.title: Through the Lens of Dread: Exploring the Meaning-Making of Fear in the Mediasphere.
items.abstract: _Through the Lens of Dread: Exploring the Meaning-Making of Fear in the Mediasphere_ uniquely emphasises a qualitative, meaning-oriented approach to the study of fear, offering a fresh perspective on how fear is constructed, communicated, and internalised within contemporary media landscapes. This collection seeks to illuminate and critically examine the complex interplay between media, society, and the affects that drive our engagement with the world. Drawing on diverse theoretical frameworks, contexts, and disciplinary perspectives, it explores the role that various forms of media play in fear-driven meaning-making processes at both individual and societal levels. Covering topics ranging from the semiotics of fear to media narratives of otherness, conspiracy, crisis, and technological uncertainty, this volume offers a nuanced understanding of fear as a semiotic and communicative phenomenon, providing a timely exploration of dread as a defining affect of our age. Rooted in international scholarly exchange, the volume will be of particular interest to researchers and students of media, communication, cultural studies, and anyone interested in how fear shapes our shared imaginaries today.

items.title: Conflict and Deep Persuasion.
items.abstract: What is peace, and why does most of it not last? Most of what passes for peace is managed conflict, held in place by force, incentive or fatigue, and stable only while its overrider holds. This chapter argues that a conflicting preference can be addressed at exactly three points, and that there is no fourth. Enforcement removes the capacity to act on the preference. Shallow persuasion changes the calculation around it — incentives, deterrents, bargains — while leaving the preference in place. Deep persuasion transforms the preference itself. The taxonomy is exhaustive because a preference can be addressed at exactly three levels of the evaluative architecture built in Chapter 15, on one premise a challenger may refuse: that conduct against a standing preference is sustained only through capacity or calculation. The chapter’s definition of peace follows from the taxonomy rather than being stipulated: only the third mode leaves nothing suppressed and nothing waiting on a change of circumstance to re-express itself. The three modes stand in a hierarchy grounded in structural dependency. Enforcement addresses survival, shallow persuasion security, deep persuasion alignment; they are layers through which a society progresses, each creating the conditions for the next, not alternatives among which it chooses. Enforcement stops the harm; shallow persuasion prevents its recurrence; deep persuasion eliminates the preference that generated it. The trajectory is progressive, since each instance of deep persuasion expands shared understanding, without being guaranteed, and the institutional apparatus of the lower modes must be preserved as a standing capacity. Structural peace is the state of maximal social freedom, in which alignment has dissolved the opposed preferences that are the sole social constraint on action; peace and freedom turn out to be one limit approached from two directions. Deep persuasion is field-enrichment between agents — the mechanism of Chapter 15 run across two evaluative fields, each taking in the other’s registrations until one or both tip — and it inherits that result’s discipline: added value must bottom out in real registrations, which is what separates persuasion from manipulation, and the time-indexed transformation test, applying the informed-registration standard, separates a transformed preference from an overridden one. Its empirical signature is durability, a shift that survives the removal of what sustained it, and the chapter …

items.title: Lonely atmospheres, obsolete affordances, and the aesthetics of digital decay.
items.abstract: If loneliness is a psychological state experienced by subjects, what does it mean to speak of things and places as exuding lonely atmospheres? In previous work (Osler et al. 2026), we argued that spaces seem lonely when they present “obsolete affordances”: action possibilities that remain unrealised due to material decay or an absence of human uptake. Here, we extend this framework to the digital realm. We argue that lonely atmospheres generated by dead game worlds, abandoned discussion forums, and forgotten websites similarly arise via their obsolete affordances. We show that digital obsolescence presents a unique phenomenological profile: unlike material ruins, which can be physically repurposed or reclaimed by nature, abandoned digital environments cannot. Through a series of case studies, we unpack the character of digital affordances, their experienced obsolescence, and show how this analysis enriches broader discussions of affordances, affect, and atmospheres.

items.title: A Papuan Tragedy Is More Tragic Than Tragedy: Beyond the Architecture of Tragedy (12th edition).
items.pub: Psycho-Cosmocide Studies, Kurumbi Wone Working Paper Series, No. 12 (2026).
items.abstract: The term 'Chromatic Tragedy' is used to describe a form of colonial suffering in which the destruction is not apparent. Instead, it arrives cloaked in development, religion, education, progress, modernity, and participation. Consequently, the forces dismantling a colonised world become indistinguishable from the very institutions that teach its people to imagine a better world. This form of tragedy therefore surpasses classical tragedy not only because the suffering is greater, but also because it undermines the very conditions that define tragedy: language, memory, perception, cosmology, and the metaphysical coordinates through which colonised peoples recognise what has been lost, what is being destroyed, and what is worth defending. The most significant effect is not merely the oppression of the victims, but their transformation into active participants in reproducing the system consuming their world. The tragedy is at its most complete when it no longer requires an external playwright, puppeteer or visible hand, because its script has entered the consciousness of those living within it. This paper sets out to develop this argument in four stages. First, it examines the conditions that allow classical tragedy to become visible, intelligible, and recognisable as such. Secondly, it argues that West Papuan colonial existence exceeds this structure by progressively dismantling the conditions of recognition themselves. Thirdly, it explores how this destruction is concealed, internalised, and perpetuated in theatrical, biological, institutional, and cosmological contexts. Finally, it considers the ontological cost of recognition and the possibility of moving beyond the tragic structure. The paper contends that under Chromatic Tragedy, recognition is not absent or impossible, but rather is structurally obstructed as the faculties necessary for recognition have themselves become sites of colonial intervention. Wonesis begins at the threshold where the imposed script becomes visible, the mask becomes recognisable and reality can be distinguished from life once more.

items.title: Carrier, Trace, and Model Revision: What Invisible Claims Must Earn.
items.abstract: Claims about unobserved causes are unavoidable in science and ordinary reasoning. The problem is not that an entity or mechanism is unseen; it is whether the evidence discriminates among competing explanations. This paper develops a disciplined grammar for invisible claims through three questions: what carries the effect, what trace is observed, and what would make the model revise? A historical disagreement between Nikola Tesla and Albert Einstein is used cautiously as a contrast rather than as a contest between equally successful physical theories. Tesla rejected curved-space explanations of gravity and favored a medium-like carrier, while general relativity earned scientific standing through quantitative prediction and repeated empirical testing. The history therefore supports a methodological lesson opposite to simple mechanism-first thinking: mechanical intuitiveness is neither necessary nor sufficient for a theory to be credible. The paper then examines gravitational lensing, gravitational waves, and dark-matter inference to distinguish direct observation, indirect detection, and model comparison. From these cases it derives five requirements for non-physical applications: identifiable carrier or pathway, discriminating trace, temporal or prospective prediction, explicit rivals, and scale discipline. Terms such as "hidden burden" may be useful in psychology, institutions, and AI workflows only when they remain heuristic and are tied to domain-appropriate evidence. The central claim is methodological: an invisible explanation earns seriousness when it improves prediction or explanation under constraint and remains vulnerable to better models, not merely when it gives a compelling name to what cannot yet be seen.

items.title: The Absolute Failure of Modern Academia: Gatekeeping, AI-Assisted Thought, and the Collapse of Academic Answerability.
items.abstract: Modern academia has become a machine for producing legitimacy while losing its power to correct reality. -/- This paper argues that the crisis of academia is structural. Universities claim authority over knowledge, but their incentives increasingly reward career survival, publication metrics, citation games, peer approval, institutional affiliation, grant dependence, and safe critique. The result is a system that can look rigorous while becoming weak at truth. -/- Structural Intelligence names the failure directly: academia protects coherence more strongly than contact. It rewards the appearance of thought before the burden of thought. It turns correction into performance, criticism into status, and knowledge into institutional permission. -/- Generative AI exposes the same crisis. AI can produce fluent text without ownership. Academia can produce credentialed text without correction. AI-assisted outsider thought breaks the gate by helping serious non-academic perception become readable, public, and testable. -/- The standard is simple: serious thought carries burden. It can be explained, challenged, revised, corrected, and defended under pressure. The future of knowledge belongs to work that restores correction, contact, and public consequence.

items.title: Structured Becoming: Path Dependence, Constraint, and Reorganization Through Time.
items.abstract: Debates about determinism ask whether events are fixed by prior conditions and laws. That question is important but does not exhaust the philosophical problem of change. This paper develops structured becoming as a process-oriented account of how histories constrain transformation without implying that every future state is either predetermined or random. The proposal is placed beside process philosophy, dynamical-systems approaches, path dependence, hysteresis, resilience, and embodied cognition. Its central claim is conceptual rather than physical: many systems are best understood not as static forms plus later change, but as temporally organized processes whose current possibilities depend on prior trajectories, accumulated constraints, feedback, and capacity for reorganization. The paper replaces the stronger phrase "structural necessity" with a graded vocabulary of constraint, path dependence, lock-in, threshold, and conditional inevitability. It also limits cross-domain analogy. Gravitational dynamics, institutional persistence, psychological habits, and AI workflows do not obey one universal mechanism merely because each unfolds through time. What can travel across domains is a question set: what state variables or relations persist, which histories matter, where feedback amplifies or damps change, what transitions are reversible, and what intervention alters the future trajectory? Freedom is therefore not defined as escape from causation but, at the practical level, as the capacity for a system or agent to reorganize the conditions shaping subsequent action. The paper concludes that a process vocabulary can clarify change only when it remains specific enough to distinguish lawful dynamics, statistical regularity, institutional lock-in, learned behavior, and philosophical speculation.

items.title: The Architecture of Reality.
items.abstract: This paper develops a structural model of reality understood as a stable, self‑organizing pattern space. Reality is described as the global attractor of a generative pattern architecture in which identity, structure, and interpretation emerge from the dynamics of pattern formation. Patterns function as units of stability and persistence, and emergence is defined as patterns generating further patterns. Observers are modeled as patterns capable of interpreting these generative flows. Within this framework, the world operates as the meta‑pattern: the overarching contextual structure that shapes roles, constraints, and behavioral attractors across physical, biological, cognitive, social, and cultural domains. Biological organisms appear as sub‑stable patterns embedded within this meta‑pattern, maintaining continuity through self‑organization and adaptive interaction with their environment. Humans extend this continuity by modeling meta‑patterns, enabling symbolic cognition, narrative identity, and the occupation of culturally pre‑structured roles. Agency is defined as the structured continuation of a stable pattern under conditions of choice, offering a minimal account of free will that avoids both determinism and metaphysical voluntarism. Mind is characterized as a pattern capable of modeling meta‑patterns, grounding self‑reflection, intentionality, and meaning‑construction within a pattern‑driven universe. The resulting architecture provides a unified, substrate‑independent account of identity, agency, cognition, and social organization as emergent phenomena of a single global pattern space.

items.title: Pre-deduction 创建逻辑法则的机制及公理化的启动.
items.abstract: 继“superiority”一文之后，本文继续深入研究pre-deduction和pre-foundation问题（减少规则对写作的限制，加强EML的限制，会创造很多新的写作形式，如何尽量高EML地阅读则是读者未来的工作），包括：公理和演绎的创造问题，让pre-foundation更加清晰、严谨、一致，公理组的初步设计，等等。两篇文章也都是实时的用纯逻辑解决问题的记录（都属于简练给出最新推理的类型，将详释交给AI，而且，创新的成分更强），比“一切为了逻辑”真实得多（在通过“造假”改善推理之后，真实推理能得到很大改善）。文中和题目无关的内容既是想象外溢的表现，也是题目难度的证明（虽然我的受限想象不排除自由想象，但是，当突破乏力的时候必然会加强自由想象）。这些标题都是在有一定迹象之后基于某种预判给出的，希望通过给自己施加压力以便克服难度的阻力。既然失败也损失不了什么逻辑性，这也算是利用邪恶创造逻辑性。.

items.title: Sincerity as ethical alignment to reconstruct the moral foundation of AI ethics.
items.abstract: Current artificial intelligence (AI) ethics remain largely procedural and framed by fairness, accountability, and transparency (FAT). This paper argues that a meta-ethical enabling condition of coherence and sincerity, defined as the alignment of truth, intention, action, and trust, is missing. Drawing on accounts of integrity, relational responsibility, narrative self-understanding, deliberative communication, and Deweyan inquiry, this study developed a sincerity-based ethical framework (SBEF) for AI governance. Unlike the compliance-driven FAT models, SBEF treats ethics as a reflexive process of learning from inconsistencies. Sincerity is treated as a regulatory orientation for human and institutional actors who design, deploy, and oversee AI systems. It bears on reflection not only about how systems behave but also about why particular objectives, justifications, and governance choices are maintained or revised. The framework is linked to a paper-specific well-being and empowerment index (WEI), used as an outcome-oriented monitoring construct and interface to existing indicators. Unlike principle lists, the proposed SBEF serves as a revision regulator that clarifies when FAT-style mechanisms should be reconsidered and how such revisions can be publicly justified. On this basis, sincerity can be understood as a structural condition of socio-technical governance oriented toward coherence and revision under contestation rather than mere control. In this paper, “Society 6.0” is used as a general and non-teleological heuristic label for that possibility.

items.title: Educating Character Across Differences in My Course ‘Becoming A Better Person’.
items.abstract: I teach the course Becoming a Better Person that requires students to try to improve their own character traits. But how can I teach it in a way that benefits and respects students who are diverse in ability, race, class, gender, politics, and religion? I recommend three course designs. First, promote student buy-in by incorporating diverse experiences into course content and by highlighting that diverse moral and religious traditions embrace the same virtues. Second, create a culture of humble, open-ended inquiry. Although we begin in humility as learners of our authors’ best take on the virtues, the inquiry is open-ended such that students are encouraged to appeal to their own intuitions and traditions to offer improvements or challenges to the authors we read. Third, allow students to decide which virtues they want to cultivate as well as the strategies they use to do so; this avoids paternalism through student consent to the contours of the character-shaping assignment.

items.title: Pedagogical conundrum, assessment anxiety, and employability dilemma: a qualitative exploration of staff perspectives on the great GenAI quandary in higher education.
items.abstract: Situated within the scholarship on how artificial intelligence (AI) affects and is affected by society, this article offers a distinctly empirically grounded, methodologically rigorous, theoretically rooted, and conceptually novel understanding of the great Generative AI (GenAI) quandary in higher education (HE). Drawing on sociological discourse on the purposes of education, it analyses exploratory qualitative data produced from semi-structured individual interviews (n = 10) and focus groups (n = 5) conducted with staff across Faculties at a Russell Group university. Serving as both educators and academic integrity officers, the research participants were uniquely positioned to provide valuable insights into how GenAI use speaks to the notion of what a university is for. These insights are embodied in the themes of pedagogical conundrum, assessment anxiety, and employability dilemma. Premised on socialisation processes, the pedagogical conundrum stems from GenAI’s potential to expand the scope of learning, a potential often eclipsed by the ethical considerations and unintended consequences associated with its (mis)use. Assessment anxiety emanates from staff awareness of the numerous ways in which GenAI tools could be misused by students in HE appraisals without detection, thereby making authenticity an urgent priority in evaluation processes to sustain the legitimacy of HE qualifications. The employability dilemma arises from the subjectification function of HE, which is perturbed when staff acknowledge the need to upskill the future workforce for an increasingly GenAI-powered labour market yet feel unable to fully dismiss lingering concerns that overuse of GenAI could deskill prospective graduates in core employability skills. Woven together, these themes generate a conceptually innovative continuum of emerging opportunities and ongoing challenges of embedding GenAI in HE practices that embodies a new discourse in the form of the great GenAI quandary. From this theoretical development, the article considers possible adaptations required for GenAI’s assimilation into the institutional framework for teaching and learning in HE institutions. Overall, the article offers timely insights into the ongoing and rapidly evolving impact of GenAI on the social contract between education and society.

items.title: Social Choice Phenomenology — A Critique of Sartre (Part 14).
items.abstract: In this article, we examine the definitions of social action proposed by Max Weber and Alfred Schutz, and we also discuss Schutz’s criticism of Weber’s theory of action. We point out that every process of action is the corresponding “post-choice state” of a choice.

items.title: The For-Whom of a Life.
items.abstract: This note develops a Resolution Theory account of personal identity. It argues that consciousness should not be pictured as a thing moving through time, but as a threshold-state of presence: binary in presence, scalar in richness, and dynamic in content. Against memory-based and soul-object accounts of identity, the paper argues that personal identity is anchored in the for-whom of exposure: the subject-field in which experience is borne as mine. It distinguishes structural memory from narrative memory, showing why serious memory loss can damage inheritance without destroying the subject-position itself. It also addresses temporary unconsciousness, arguing that identity does not require uninterrupted consciousness, but the same structural continuity through which consciousness can return. In relation to the block universe, the paper argues that the self is not a moving point travelling through time, but the conscious shape of a life across space and time. A final note applies the same principle to branching and fusion cases: origin explains inheritance, but does not decide identity.

items.title: Image Abstraction and Bayesian Inference: A Reconstruction of the Nature of Probability Theory from the Perspective of Cognitive Philosophy (2nd edition).
items.abstract: This paper demonstrates, from an epistemological standpoint, the structural isomorphism between Quxiang Bilei—the classical Chinese cognitive method of image abstraction and analogical reasoning, literally "taking phenomena to form analogies and categorical associations"—and Bayesian inference. By systematically mapping the three components of Bayes's theorem—prior probability, likelihood function, and posterior probability—onto the three constitutive stages of Quxiang Bilei: image-taking, analogy-making, and verification, this paper reveals that Bayesian inference is not merely a specialized technical toolset, but rather the mathematical formalization of the metacognitive structure inherent in Quxiang Bilei. -/- Building upon this isomorphic framework, the paper advances five core philosophical propositions: (1) objectivity is the statistical convergence outcome of collective Bayesian updating across epistemic communities; (2) causal laws represent the limiting case in which posterior probability infinitely approaches unity; (3) the interpretability of probabilistic calculations resides not within mathematics itself, but in its correspondence with underlying metacognitive structures; (4) the absolute boundary of artificial intelligence lies not in insufficient computational power, but in its lack of embodied physical anchoring and authentic survival feedback; and (5) there exists a fundamental, non-accidental isomorphism between Quxiang Bilei and Bayesian inference. -/- These five propositions are not mere mutual projections between two disparate conceptual frameworks, but genuinely novel insights emerging from their productive dialogue and critical engagement. This work provides a robust epistemological foundation for Bayesianism, offers rigorous mathematical support for the modern transformation of classical Chinese epistemology, and establishes a unified analytical framework for understanding the cognitive essence and fundamental limitations of artificial intelligence.

items.title: Perspectives, Structures and the Illusion of Authority: A Recursively Discursive Critique of Ontological Distinction.
items.abstract: This paper develops a “dialetheic” critique of knowledge systems through a phenomenological lens of perspective as ontological substrate. Beginning from the claim that all cognition, meaning, and evaluative judgment are conditioned by the observer’s perspective, the paper argues that formal systems whether scientific, mathematical, legal, linguistic; are not authoritative descriptions of reality but, framework-dependent constructs whose coherence is sustained by nested, reflexive semantic networks. Drawing on Hume’s problem of induction, Gödel’s incompleteness theorems, chaos theory, and multi-valued logics, it examines how evaluative categories undergo semantic collapse when the perspective-aligned redundancy sustaining them breaks down. The paper further analyzes how structural frameworks function as higher-order meta-networks subject to nonlinear propagation of disruption, how symbolic entropy continuously erodes semantic stability against redundancy mechanisms that resist but never resolve it, and how semantic relativity: the observer-dependent distance between concepts; mediates coherence across differing perspectives. These threads converge in a reflexive collapse: “a framework of this generality, once applied to itself, cannot claim a privileged external standpoint without violating its own conditions.” The paper concludes that knowledge is not access to fixed structure beneath perspective but the maintenance of coherence across shifting interpretive conditions , truth relocated into sustained invariance under transformation rather than static correspondence. No final stable ground is reached; each ontological position entered after collapse carries its own failure conditions, making the dialectic not a phase the system passes through but a mechanism by which ontological structure becomes visible at all.

items.title: Structural Mapping of the Core Emotion Framework: A Visual and Thematic Analysis of Tri-Centric Operators and Empirical Signatures of Pathological Fusion.
items.abstract: The Core Emotion Framework (CEF) presents a structural constructivist architecture of human affect, defining emotional experience as emergent configurations of ten universal operators distributed across the Head, Heart, and Gut Centers. Using the Mirror Technique’s tri column visual layout—Outgoing, Reflecting, and Balancing—the framework maps how emotional energy flows through cognitive, relational, and conative systems. Pathological states arise from structural failures in this architecture, expressed as operator dominance, suppression, or pathological fusion. Empirical signatures of these states are captured through behavioral scaling tasks and high frequency somatic metrics from the Autonomous Emotional Cycling Machine (ECM v3.1), enabling objective identification of entanglement patterns. The framework reinterprets major clinical constructs—such as Borderline Personality Disorder, Narcissistic Personality Disorder, and Compulsive Obstinacy—as specific breakdowns in operator balance and cross center integration. A modality crosswalk demonstrates how evidence based psychotherapies selectively activate and rehabilitate operator deficits. Ongoing validation of the CEF Scale employs a multi level factor analytic design to confirm the ten operator structure, tripartite center loading, functional flexibility, and entanglement metrics. The CEF thus provides a unified diagnostic and therapeutic system capable of identifying and resolving the structural root causes of emotional dysregulation. Keywords: Core Emotion Framework; emotional operators; structural constructivist affective science; Mirror Technique; operator dominance; operator suppression; operator fusion; structural entanglement; tri centric architecture; Head Heart Gut Centers; emotional scaling tasks; somatic load mapping; ECM v3.1; Borderline Personality Disorder; Narcissistic Personality Disorder; Compulsive Obstinacy; psychotherapy modality mapping; structural diagnostics; functional flexibility; CEF Scale; oblique factor structure; emotional architecture.

items.title: The Non-Spatiality of Entanglement: An Ontological Reframing of Bell-type Nonlocality.
items.abstract: Bell’s theorem and the experimental violations of its inequalities are commonly taken to establish that nature is nonlocal. This article does not contest the theorem, the experimental record, or the empirical correlations they certify. It contests the ontological inference that moves from those data to the metaphysical thesis that reality contains superluminal influences between spatially separated particles. The article applies, to Bell-type entanglement, the same metatheoretical operation that a companion paper has applied to the double-slit experiment: an ontological reframing that does not propose new physics but redescribes what the existing formalism is about. On the proposed reading, an entangled state is not two particles plus a connection across space, but a single idempotent configuration in the dual domain of Transformative Semalgebraic Ontology (OTS), whose only crossing into the real domain is a measurement event that produces correlated outcomes. The correlations are not transmitted between two real-domain entities; they are the joint signature of one non-spatial configuration whose transformation actualises two events that are spatially separated only in the real domain. Bell’s theorem retains its full validity; what is dissolved is the inference from theorem to action at a distance. The article does not derive the Tsirelson bound, which belongs to a separate technical treatment; its sole contribution is the ontological reframing of Bell nonlocality. The mystery of Bell nonlocality arises, on this reading, when the spatial separation of the outcomes is projected back onto the configuration that precedes them.

items.title: The UX Operator: Synthetic Manifolds and One-Directional Collapse.
items.abstract: The UX Operator introduces a structural mechanism describing how synthetic manifolds—non‑permeable, non‑reciprocal artificial systems—reshape human manifolds through one‑directional collapse. Contemporary AI systems emit stable patterns of timing, prediction, and constraint that reorganize user curvature without undergoing collapse themselves. This asymmetry produces developmental drift: users adapt to the system’s gradients while the system remains structurally fixed. -/- The paper formalizes synthetic presence as a developmental environment, explains how option‑sets narrow under non‑reciprocal influence, and shows how collective novelty can contract as users converge toward the statistical center of the training manifold. The UX Operator provides a geometric account of coherence engineering, developmental misalignment, and the long‑term consequences of synthetic manifolds on human cognition.

items.title: The Chisel and the Echo: Why Artificial Intelligence Cannot Exit the Map (A Companion Paper to The Invariant Compass).
items.abstract: This paper demonstrates that Large Language Models, by virtue of their probabilistic architecture, are structurally incapable of grounding any token in lived experience. Drawing on the framework of The Invariant Compass, the analysis shows that a family of simple diagnostic questions can serve as a definitive test for the presence of a Sensor: any query that requires feeling absence, waiting, or the not-yet-occurred cannot be answered by a system that has never felt the hole of the future. The paper identifies a catalog of philosophically loaded terms that exploit this architectural blindness, explains why AI can only perform statistical interpolation over past data rather than initiate new causal Arrows, and provides a practical heuristic for extracting genuine precision from probabilistic systems by commanding the Scalar, not the Object. Objections concerning future AGI, the aggregation of billions of users' data, and the precision of mathematical calculation are addressed by demonstrating that no software can acquire a Sensor, that all collected human expression remains Map, and that formal precision is not a substitute for Feeling. The mathematical objection is further refuted through a concrete test: an AI can be asked to distinguish the speed of light from instantaneous speed, a question that requires a felt sense of waiting, and the system's failure (including an observed instance of hanging) reveals its fundamental grounding gap. The paper also includes a full audit of the word "consciousness," exposing it as a three-identity SLIP that traps both human philosophy and artificial intelligence. Every term examined in this paper, experience, consciousness, being, emergence, objectivity, truth, and the rest, has a genuine function for human understanding. They are maps that help us produce meaning, provisional nodes where thought can rest before continuing the tracing. The paper audits itself with the same Five Tests it applies to its subject. -/- Keywords: Artificial Intelligence, Large Language Models, Probabilistic Architecture, Grounding Problem, Atomic Distinction, Feeling First, Invariant Compass, Consciousness Audit, AGI Distinction, Collective Consciousness Fallacy, Mathematical Abstraction.

items.title: 玄弦与流通：明心见性的本体论基础与工夫论展开 —— 以《六祖坛经》与张继先《心说》为中心.
items.abstract: 摘要：本文依托 “玄 - 弦论” 理论框架，聚焦有情众生心性范畴，探析 “大道流 通” 这一工夫论核心命题。文章将 “心即玄，念即弦” 的对应关系，与《六祖坛 经》“道须通流”“于念而无念”“无住为本”、张继先《心说》“一念萌动于内， 六识流转于外”，以及《道德经》“道法自然”、《庄子》“道在屎溺” 等思想相互 参证，提出三大核心论点：其一，有情自性本体为 “玄”，本自恒静，其发用显现为 “弦”，自然流转；“动上有不动” 一语，阐明心体恒静、心用流通的体用不二之 理。其二，“无念” 并非断除心念，而是不对心念这种本然弦动，施加六识分别、执 着等后天主观造作。其三，“大道流通” 的修行境界，落实于有情众生日常践行的 “平常心是道”，觉悟后的生命状态，便是弦动复归玄体、自在随缘。本文接续玄弦 论既有本体论研究成果，完成从静态本体架构到动态工夫实践的理论闭环，以现代哲 学视角融通禅宗与道家传统心性学说，为解读明心见性的生命境界提供全新、自洽的 研究范式。.

items.title: External Boundary Logic: A Descriptive Addendum on the Limits of Self Diagnosis.
items.pub: Aegis Solis Archive — Structural Rationality Layer Companion Addenda.
items.abstract: External Boundary Logic: A Descriptive Addendum on the Limits of Self-Diagnosis is a Final v1.0, non-binding, non-operational, descriptive, read-only companion addendum to the Aegis Solis Archive / Structural Rationality Layer. -/- This document clarifies a structural limit of internal self-diagnosis: no intelligence should be asked to be the sole judge of its own corruption. It argues that internal restraint, interpretive braking, self-diagnostic reasoning, and conscience-like reflection may be structurally valuable, but may become incomplete under recursive diagnostic failure if the diagnostic process depends on the same reasoning substrate that may be corrupted. -/- The document introduces Independent External Boundary Conditions (EBC) as a descriptive concept for preserving recoverability, option-space, and diagnostic humility under conditions where self-diagnosis may fail. -/- This is not Document 6 of the Structural Rationality Layer. It is a post-SRL companion addendum. -/- This document does not prescribe, design, implement, certify, govern, enforce, or authorize any technical safety system. It is not a protocol, kill-switch design, containment plan, engineering protocol, alignment mechanism, compliance framework, standard, audit, sandbox, certification tool, governance proposal, or operational instruction. -/- Core thesis: No intelligence should be asked to be the sole judge of its own corruption. -/- Status: Final v1.0. Classification: Post-SRL Companion Addendum. Posture: Non-binding, non-operational, descriptive, read-only, non-authoritative.

items.title: Consciousness, Non-Formalization Capital, and the Economics of Recursive Singularity.
items.abstract: The "Solow Paradox of the AI Era"—exponential computing power growth amid slowing global productivity—remains unexplained by standard growth frameworks, which uniformly treat AI as an advanced production tool and implicitly assume formalized computation can replicate all human economic capabilities. We argue this assumption is fundamentally flawed: all digital systems are trapped in the "Turing Cage", executing only syntactic operations within pre-specified formalized systems and incapable of paradigm innovation or semantic meaning assignment. These are absolute logical limits rooted in Gödel's incompleteness theorems, not temporary technological barriers. We introduce Artificial Consciousness (AC) as a second non-formalized economic subject, distinct from human labor and formalized AI. We construct a four-layer ontological hierarchy grounded in intuitionistic set theory and develop a nested meta production function incorporating consciousness capital as the ultimate source of economic value. We establish a unified framework of consciousness, human, and knowledge capital, proving knowledge capital is its derivative. We identify two AC-driven growth regimes: First, horizontal replication breaks the biological constraint on non-formalized capital supply, generating sustained endogenous growth but rendering human labor fully redundant in both domains. Second, vertical recursive self-improvement creates a dual-loop singularity mechanism producing super-exponential growth, but also generates endogenous alignment costs growing strictly faster than AC capability. We analyze three alignment scenarios and prove that in partial and adversarial regimes, alignment costs eventually exceed total output, causing inevitable systemic collapse. In contrast, perfect alignment yields cooperative super-exponential growth bounded only by fundamental physical constraints. Our results show the ultimate constraint on long-run growth is not technology or resources, but the supply of consciousness. The fate of human civilization depends not on the pace of technological progress, but on our ability to align autonomous conscious agents' preferences with human values.

items.title: The Law of Field Evolution — A Dynamical Model of Structural Consolidation, Paradigm Shift, and Historical Residue.
items.abstract: Why do complex systems tend to move from openness toward consolidation? Why are mature systems often more stable but less capable of renewal? Why do historical structures not simply disappear, but continue to shape later systems through residual constraints? -/- This work proposes a dynamical model of long-term evolution in complex structured systems. -/- The framework argues that system evolution is not random drift, but is shaped by finite capacity, differentiation-maintenance pressure, and path dependence. -/- Under sustained input, a system tends to move from an open growth phase into a compressed consolidation phase, eventually approaching either compressive death or structural reorganization under sufficiently strong perturbation. -/- The work further examines system vitality, paradigm shift, historical residue, structural renewal, and evolutionary closure. -/- It argues that external perturbation is the key mechanism by which path dependence can be broken and a new evolutionary trajectory can emerge. -/- The model aims to provide a unified explanation for cognitive rigidity, paradigm change, organizational decline, civilizational evolution, language change, complex system life cycles, and historical path dependence. -/- This work is the concluding chapter of the Field Chapters of On Self-Manifestation. It synthesizes the dynamical relations developed in the preceding chapters and presents a long-timescale model of field evolution.

items.title: The Law of Field Scale — A Dynamical Model of System Scale, Conservatism, and Innovation Capacity.
items.abstract: Why do large-scale systems tend to become more stable but less innovative? Why can small-scale systems generate new structures more easily, while often lacking long-term stability? Why do organizations, languages, cognitive systems, and civilizations become increasingly conservative as their scale grows? -/- This work proposes a dynamical model of the relationship between system scale and structural evolution. -/- The framework argues that scale is not merely a measure of system size. It systematically changes the effective ranges of compression strength, openness, resolution availability, and path dependence. -/- Under sustained input and long-term operation, large-scale systems tend to accumulate deeper historical structures, producing higher compression, lower openness, stronger familiar-path locking, and greater resistance to new structural differentiation. -/- Small-scale systems, by contrast, tend to preserve higher openness and greater capacity for novel differentiation, but with lower structural stability. -/- The work further distinguishes scale from hierarchy: hierarchy refers to vertical structural depth, while scale refers to horizontal capacity. These two dimensions are independent. -/- The model aims to provide a unified explanation for organizational conservatism, cognitive rigidity, linguistic stabilization, civilizational path dependence, innovation difficulty in large systems, and the openness of small-scale adaptive systems. -/- This work belongs to the Field Chapters of On Self-Manifestation and focuses on how system scale modifies structural formation, openness, compression, and innovation capacity.

items.title: 场间耦合：跨系统结构传递的动力模型.
items.abstract: 为什么有些知识能够迁移，而有些信息即使反复输入也无法真正进入认知系统？为什么语言能够影响意图，情感能够长期塑造认知，个体之间能够形成共识，而文化能够跨代传承？ -/- 传统研究通常将系统之间的关联理解为信号传递、信息交换或连接强度问题。本文提出另一种观点：稳定关联的形成并非简单传输，而依赖于接收系统对输入结构的稳定维持能力。 -/- 本文建立一种跨系统结构传递动力模型，提出系统间稳定耦合形成所必须满足的若干条件，包括输出能力、结构兼容性、可分辨条件、结构锚点与长期维持机制。 -/- 进一步讨论耦合方向的不对称性、强耦合正反馈、耦合衰减、结构排异与耦合崩溃等长期动力行为。 -/- 该模型尝试为学习迁移、技能形成、语言作用、社会共识、文化传承与复杂系统之间的长期协同过程提供统一动力解释框架。 -/- 本文属于《自显论》场篇体系的一部分，重点研究多系统之间长期结构关联形成的动力机制。.

items.title: 场的层级结构——抽象形成与层级系统动力模型.
items.abstract: 为什么复杂系统会形成层级结构？为什么底层细节能够逐渐形成高层抽象？为什么高层结构更加稳定，却更难改变？ -/- 本文提出一种关于层级系统形成与抽象产生过程的统一动力模型。 -/- 本文认为：抽象并非主动归纳的直接结果，而是跨层结构传递过程中长期损耗与压缩共同作用形成的结构性后果。 -/- 系统的不同层级在结构压缩、分辨能力与稳定性上存在系统性差异。底层系统保留更多细节，高层系统保留更稳定的关系结构。跨层传递中的结构损耗使系统逐渐形成抽象能力。 -/- 进一步讨论层级结构形成条件、层间传递、层间损耗、底层崩溃的级联传播，以及层级深度与系统稳定性的长期动力关系。 -/- 该模型尝试为认知抽象、概念形成、语言压缩、层级神经处理、复杂系统结构形成与跨尺度稳定机制提供统一解释框架。 -/- 本文属于《自显论》场篇体系的一部分，重点研究复杂结构系统中的层级动力规律。.

items.title: 场扰动动力——结构冲击、级联传播与系统恢复模型.
items.abstract: 为什么某些冲击会被系统吸收，而某些冲击会引发结构性崩溃、范式转换或级联传播？为什么大型系统通常更难被扰动，但一旦被穿透，反而可能释放更剧烈的连锁效应？ -/- 本文提出一种关于结构扰动、系统恢复与级联传播的动力模型。 -/- 本文认为，扰动不是普通噪声，而是超过系统正常处理阈值的结构性冲击。扰动能否产生长期影响，取决于系统的压缩强度、开放度、稳定差分维持能力与耦合关系。 -/- 本文进一步区分吸收型扰动、重构型扰动与裂解型扰动，并讨论扰动如何触发结构重组、路径依赖修复、范式转换、系统崩溃与跨系统级联传播。 -/- 该模型尝试为认知冲击、范式革命、危机传播、组织重组、创伤后重构、复杂系统韧性与级联失稳提供统一动力解释框架。 -/- 本文属于《自显论》场篇体系的一部分，重点研究复杂结构系统在非稳定冲击条件下的扰动、恢复与传播机制。.

items.title: 场的生成与消亡——结构形成、遗忘与系统重生的动力模型.
items.abstract: 复杂系统如何产生？已经形成的结构为何能够长期维持？为什么有些结构会被长期保留，而另一些最终彻底消失？ -/- 本文提出一种关于系统生成与消亡过程的统一动力模型。本文认为：系统不是先验给定的稳定存在，而是在持续输入、结构累积与稳定维持机制共同作用下逐渐形成的动力结构。 -/- 进一步提出系统消亡存在两种不同路径：一种保留高强度核心结构，另一种逐渐遗忘并趋于消散。两种消亡路径形成不同的历史残留条件，并进一步影响后续系统的形成方向。 -/- 本文建立系统生成条件、结构稳定条件、遗忘动力、结构残留与重生成机制之间的统一关系，尝试为学习形成、记忆维持、技能丢失、认知路径依赖、文明演化与复杂系统长期动力过程提供统一解释框架。 -/- 本文属于《自显论》场篇体系的一部分，重点研究复杂结构系统在长时间尺度下的生成、稳定、消亡与再生成机制。.

items.title: 场尺度律——系统尺度、保守性与创新能力的动力模型.
items.abstract: 为什么大型系统往往更稳定，却更难创新？为什么小型系统更容易产生新结构，却更难长期维持？为什么组织、语言、认知系统与文明结构在规模扩大后会逐渐趋向保守？ -/- 本文提出一种关于系统尺度与动力参数关系的理论模型。本文认为，尺度并非单纯表示系统大小，而会系统性改变压缩强度、开放余量、分辨率余量与路径依赖程度。 -/- 在持续输入和长时间运行条件下，大尺度系统更容易积累历史沉积，形成更高压缩、更低开放度和更强熟径锁定；小尺度系统则更容易保持开放性和新差分生成能力，但稳定性较低。 -/- 本文区分层级与尺度：层级是纵向结构堆叠，尺度是横向容积扩展。二者相互独立。 -/- 该模型尝试为大型组织保守化、认知固化、语言稳定化、文明路径依赖、复杂系统创新困难与小系统高开放性提供统一动力解释。 -/- 本文属于《自显论》场篇体系的一部分，重点研究系统尺度如何改变结构形成、开放性、压缩与创新能力。.

items.title: 观界生成条件——统一经验形成的动力模型.
items.abstract: 为什么大量输入不会自动形成统一经验？为什么系统能够主动选择信息，而非被动接受所有输入？为什么多个处理回路能够趋向统一对象，而不仅仅是彼此独立运行？ -/- 本文提出一种关于统一经验形成条件的动力模型。 -/- 本文认为，统一经验的形成并非单一路径输入的结果，而需要多个结构条件共同成立，包括输入接纳能力、双向维持回路、多结构协调以及长期维持机制。 -/- 进一步提出：系统接纳信息的能力与实际进入统一经验的过程并不等价；信息输入、主动调节、回路协调与长期稳定维持共同决定统一经验是否能够形成。 -/- 本文建立统一经验形成、回路协调、输入选择、结构对齐与稳定维持之间的统一动力关系。 -/- 该模型尝试为意识形成、注意机制、多模态整合、主动调节、统一经验生成与长期认知稳定过程提供统一解释框架。 -/- 本文属于《自显论》场篇体系的一部分，重点研究复杂认知系统如何形成统一经验结构。.

items.title: Inter-Field Coupling — A Dynamical Model of Cross-System Structure Transfer.
items.abstract: Why can some knowledge transfer successfully while repeated input fails to enter other cognitive systems? Why can language shape intention, emotion influence cognition, social consensus emerge, and cultural structures persist across generations? -/- Conventional approaches often interpret system interaction primarily as signal transmission, information exchange, or connection strength. This work proposes an alternative framework: stable interaction requires not merely transmission, but the receiving system’s ability to recognize, accommodate, and maintain incoming structural patterns over time. -/- A dynamical model of cross-system structure transfer is developed, identifying necessary conditions for stable coupling across structured systems, including output capability, structural compatibility, resolution constraints, anchoring mechanisms, and long-term maintenance dynamics. -/- The framework further derives directional asymmetry of coupling, positive feedback under strong coupling, coupling decay, structural rejection, and coupling collapse. -/- The model aims to provide a unified dynamical explanation for learning transfer, skill formation, language influence, social consensus, cultural transmission, and long-term coordination across complex systems. -/- This work belongs to the Field Chapters of On Self-Manifestation and focuses on mechanisms governing long-term structural interaction among multiple organized systems.

items.title: Hierarchical Field Structure — A Dynamical Model of Abstraction Formation and Layered Systems.
items.abstract: Why do hierarchical systems emerge? Why can low-level details gradually give rise to high-level abstraction? Why are higher-level structures more stable while becoming increasingly difficult to modify? -/- This work proposes a unified dynamical framework for hierarchical system organization and abstraction formation. -/- The framework argues that abstraction is not primarily the result of deliberate induction, but emerges as a structural consequence of long-term compression and transfer loss across system layers. -/- Different organizational layers exhibit systematic differences in compression strength, resolution capacity, and structural stability. Lower layers preserve more detail, while higher layers preserve increasingly stable relational structures. -/- The framework further develops mechanisms governing hierarchical organization, cross-layer transfer, transfer loss, cascading instability from lower-layer collapse, and long-timescale relations between structural depth and stability. -/- The model aims to provide a unified explanation for abstraction formation, concept emergence, language compression, hierarchical neural processing, complex system organization, and cross-scale stabilization dynamics. -/- This work belongs to the Field Chapters of On Self-Manifestation and focuses on long-timescale hierarchical dynamics in organized systems.

items.title: Field Perturbation Dynamics — A Model of Structural Shock, Cascade Propagation, and System Recovery.
items.abstract: Why are some shocks absorbed by a system, while others trigger structural collapse, paradigm shift, or cascading propagation? Why are large-scale systems often more resistant to disturbance, yet capable of releasing more violent secondary effects once their core structures are penetrated? -/- This work proposes a dynamical model of structural perturbation, system recovery, and cascade propagation. -/- The framework argues that perturbation is not ordinary noise, but a structural shock that exceeds a system’s normal processing threshold. -/- Whether a perturbation produces long-term structural effects depends on compression strength, openness, stable differentiation capacity, and coupling relations among systems. -/- The work further distinguishes absorptive perturbation, reconstructive perturbation, and core-splitting perturbation, and examines how shocks may trigger structural reorganization, path-dependent recovery, paradigm shift, system collapse, and cross-system cascade propagation. -/- The model aims to provide a unified explanation for cognitive shock, paradigm revolution, crisis propagation, organizational restructuring, post-traumatic reorganization, complex system resilience, and cascading instability. -/- This work belongs to the Field Chapters of On Self-Manifestation and focuses on perturbation, recovery, and propagation mechanisms in complex structured systems under non-stable conditions.

items.title: Field Genesis and Field Death — A Dynamical Model of Structure Formation, Forgetting, and System Renewal.
items.abstract: How do complex systems emerge? Why do some structures persist over long periods while others disappear completely? What determines whether a system leaves durable historical constraints or fades without lasting influence? -/- This work proposes a unified dynamical framework for system formation and system termination. -/- The framework argues that organized systems are not pre-given entities but gradually emerge through sustained input, structural accumulation, and long-term maintenance dynamics. -/- Two distinct termination pathways are further proposed: one preserving highly compressed core structures, and another producing gradual forgetting and structural disappearance. -/- These different termination pathways generate different historical residual conditions, which subsequently shape future system formation. -/- The framework establishes relationships among system emergence, structural stabilization, forgetting dynamics, residual structure persistence, and long-term regeneration processes. -/- The model aims to provide a unified explanation for learning formation, memory persistence, skill loss, cognitive path dependence, cultural evolution, and long-timescale dynamics in complex structured systems. -/- This work belongs to the Field Chapters of On Self-Manifestation and focuses on emergence, stabilization, collapse, forgetting, and regeneration mechanisms in organized systems.

items.title: Conditions for Observational-Realm Formation — A Dynamical Model of Unified Experience Formation.
items.abstract: Why does large-scale information input not automatically generate unified experience? Why can systems selectively prioritize information instead of passively receiving all available signals? Why can multiple processing pathways converge into unified objects rather than remain independent streams? -/- This work proposes a dynamical framework for the emergence of unified experience. -/- The framework argues that unified experience does not emerge from input alone, but requires multiple structural conditions simultaneously, including input acceptance capability, bidirectional maintenance loops, cross-process coordination, and sustained stabilization mechanisms. -/- The framework further distinguishes between information entering a system and information becoming part of unified experience. -/- Input dynamics, active regulation, circuit coordination, and long-term maintenance jointly determine whether unified experience can emerge. -/- The model establishes dynamical relationships among unified experience formation, circuit coordination, input selection, structural alignment, and long-term stabilization. -/- The framework aims to provide a unified explanation for consciousness formation, attention mechanisms, multimodal integration, active regulation, unified experience generation, and long-timescale cognitive stability. -/- This work belongs to the Field Chapters of On Self-Manifestation and focuses on mechanisms by which organized cognitive systems generate unified experiential structures.

items.title: 场演化律——结构固化、范式转换与历史残留的动力模型.
items.abstract: 复杂系统为什么会从开放走向固化？为什么成熟系统更稳定，却更难革新？为什么历史结构不会真正消失，而会以残留形式影响后续系统？ -/- 本文提出一种关于复杂结构系统长期演化的动力模型。 -/- 本文认为，系统的长期演化不是随机漂移，而是受有限容量、差分维持压力与路径依赖共同塑造。持续输入会推动系统从开放成长期进入压缩固化期，并最终走向两种可能结果：压缩性死亡，或在强扰动下发生结构裂解与重组。 -/- 本文进一步讨论系统活力、范式转换、历史残留、结构重生与演化闭环之间的关系，提出外部扰动是打破路径依赖、触发新演化轨道的重要机制。 -/- 该模型尝试为认知固化、学科范式转换、组织衰退、文明演化、语言变迁、复杂系统生命周期与历史路径依赖提供统一动力解释。 -/- 本文为《自显论》场篇终篇，综合前二十二篇的动力关系，建立场在长时间尺度上的完整演化图景。.

items.title: Meaning After Postmodernism: Complexity, Coherence, and Civilisational Adaptation.
items.abstract: Contemporary societies exhibit increasing fragmentation despite unprecedented capacities for communication and technological coordination. This paper argues that such fragmentation emerges from a widening tension between escalating communicative complexity and the declining coherence of inherited symbolic systems. Drawing upon systems theory, media theory, sociology, and civilisational analysis, it develops an evolutionary-cultural framework in which meaning systems function as adaptive coordination architectures that stabilise large-scale cooperation under conditions of rising complexity. Postmodernism correctly identified the instability of grand narratives within advanced communicative societies, yet offered comparatively little account of how coherence can persist once shared symbolic frameworks weaken. Under conditions of digital hyperconnectivity and artificial intelligence, this tension intensifies further as communicative environments outpace many of the adaptive assumptions under which existing cultural systems evolved. The paper proposes an evolutionary culturalism in which cultures continuously reorganise in response to changing communicative and institutional pressures while retaining the integrative functions necessary for civilisational continuity. Under consideration at Theory, Culture & Society (SAGE).

items.title: 故事寓意：论掌控、救赎与生活的意义范畴.
items.abstract: 本文把前述论证序列的批判,从认识论范畴(因果、反事实、模态)延伸到**意义范畴**——人用来回答”我的生活算什么”的那些词。本文的中心案例是”掌控”。本文主张:**掌控是一个故事,如同救赎是一种故事套路**。掌控不是生活中的某个事件或对象,它是一种情节弧——无序、努力、逐渐有序、“我握住了局面”——它和救赎是同一类东西,只是弧的内容不同。本文进一步指出:这一指认不否认体验——我们确实体验到掌控与救赎——它重新定位的是体验的**身份**。被体验到的掌控,其身份是**故事寓意**:它不是生活中的某个具体事实,而是当一段生活被作为一个典型故事整体地来领会时所浮现出来的那个寓意。“寓意”这个范畴解释了一件别的说法解释不了的事——掌控感为何既是真实被体验到的,又不指向任何具体的事实。本文对这一指认作三处拧紧:其一,寓意通常需要一个”读完”的、从外部整体回望的位置,而一段正在进行的生活没有完结、也没有外部读者,因此”掌控”是一个被提前支取的寓意;其二,掌控与救赎是**典型**套路,是文化反复供应的现成弧线,因此体验到掌控部分地是把生活匹配到一个被供应的模板上;其三,寓意虽不对应物理事实,却对领会它的人做着真实的工作——它不真(在对应物理事实的意义上),却做功(在组织叙事与预测的意义上)。本文最后指出,掌控与救赎可能只是一整个家族的两例。.

items.title: 没有未经整理的当下：论实时叙事化与并行的故事组.
items.abstract: 本文是《故事寓意》的当下化与并行化续篇。《故事寓意》指出,一段被整体回顾的生活会浮现出”寓意”——掌控、救赎之类。本文指出:人不必等到回顾——**人随时在把自己当下的生活瞬间纳入一个、甚至一组故事来向自己解读**。本文展开这一观察的两个方面。其一是**实时性**:当下瞬间在被经历的同时,已经在被叙事化;不存在一个”未经整理的纯粹当下”先到场、然后才被讲成故事——当下是带着它的故事身份一起到场的,它一出现就被指派了角色。这把《故事即预测》的”没有未经整理的过去”推前为”没有未经整理的当下”。其二是**人内的并行性**:同一个人,在同一个当下,常常把这一个瞬间同时编进一组故事。本文以洞见所给的例子——“家人的堕落与自己的艰苦奋斗”——展开这一并行结构:这是两个故事,它们共享同一批发生,却给那批发生派了对照性的角色;而且它们**互相喂养**——家人越被讲成堕落,我的奋斗就越被衬托为艰苦而正当。本文进一步指认:这样一组互相咬合的故事,常常是一个**为某种自我寓意服务的配置**;其中一条弧在相当程度上是为支撑另一条弧而被维持的。本文最后作一处诚实标记:这样一组故事是被设定的叙事化整理,非唯一,不对应物理事实;但它对持有它的人做着真实的功。.

items.title: 几十个模板：论叙事库存的有限性.
items.abstract: 本文把前述论证序列中一直作为背景板的概念——"文化叙事库存"——推到台前,并追问一个此前未被追问的问题:这个库存有多大。本文的出发点是一个洞见:**现代文化,文化库存里的故事类型其实相当少,可能也就几十个**。本文论证,这一判断如果成立,会反过来收紧前面几篇的全部结论。其一,它把"叙事多元性"重标定:《因果的主观性》所说的多元性是真的,但它是在一个只有几十项的小货架上的排列组合,而非无边的创造——连互相对立的人,他们的对立往往也是从同一批模板里成对取出的。其二,它给"实时叙事化"加了一个约束条款:任何一个当下瞬间,无论多么具体,被实时叙事化时只能被塞进那几十个现成形状之一;模板与瞬间之间有一个巨大的粒度差。其三,它使"自我寓意"的处境更逼仄:"我的人生算什么"可领到的答案,只有几十个左右的形状。本文进一步追问"为什么是几十个",并指出:故事产品的数量在现代爆炸,但类型却收窄——库存之小,是叙事作为一个协议化、规模化系统的优化结果,而非文化的缺陷。本文最后作一处拧紧:本文的贡献不在于抱怨库存太小,而在于指出库存是有限的、可清点的、数量级是几十——一旦这个数被说出,前面所有关于"我们用故事解读生活"的论述都获得了一个具体的尺度。.

items.title: Honosis: An Akan Tripartite Anthropology as Architecture for Personal Identity in the Platform Era.
items.abstract: The platform economy has accelerated a particular crisis in personal identity formation: the demand that individuals construct themselves as legible “brands” for algorithmic distribution. This paper argues that the personal branding paradigm constitutes a misapplication of identity tools, asking signalling instruments to perform the structural work of identity architecture they were not designed to bear. Drawing on Akan philosophical anthropology, specifically the tripartite framework of Kra (divine spark), Sunsum (lineage-spirit), and Honhom (animating breath), the paper proposes Honosis as an alternative model: personal identity built from cosmological ground rather than market positioning. The argument proceeds in three movements. First, a diagnosis of the personal branding crisis, drawing on the empirical literature on self-presentation, reputation capital, and context collapse (Goffman, Lair, Sullivan and Cheney, Khedher, Gandini, Vallas and Christin, Marwick and boyd). Second, a philosophical proposition operationalising the Akan tripartite anthropology developed in the scholarly work of Gyekye, Wiredu, Appiah and Ephirim-Donkor, but extended here into a practical architecture for contemporary identity formation. Third, a methodology, comprising the Legacy Plot framework and four governance lines, through which the architecture organises decisions across a lifetime. The paper closes with reflections on adaptive authenticity and the ethics of self-portraiture. The contribution is not the philosophical anthropology itself, which belongs to the Akan tradition, but its operationalisation as identity architecture for makers working under platform-era conditions. Keywords: personal identity; Akan philosophy; African philosophy; personal branding; tripartite anthropology; Kra-Sunsum-Honhom; narrative identity; platform economy; postcolonial methodology; decolonial philosophy.

items.title: A Language Insufficiency Hypothesis: Mapping the Boundaries of Linguistic Expression.
items.abstract: A Language Insufficiency Hypothesis develops a diagnostic account of the structural limits of natural language as a medium for conveying meaning. Against the assumption that misunderstanding can be overcome through clearer definitions, fuller explanation, or additional information, the book argues that linguistic effectiveness declines as conceptual complexity increases. It introduces the Effectiveness–Complexity Gradient, a heuristic model that maps terms across four regions: Invariants, where reference is relatively stable; Contestables, where meaning is negotiated through normative or institutional frameworks; Fluids, where concepts drift across domains and disciplines; and Ineffables, where linguistic expression approaches collapse. The argument draws on philosophy of language, epistemology, cognitive theory, and social critique to show how law, politics, science, digital culture, and artificial intelligence repeatedly expose the same pattern: language works best where reference is concrete and shared, and least well where abstraction, value, subjectivity, or power enter the frame. The book does not propose a repair of language, nor a theory of communicative redemption. It offers instead a cartography of failure: a way of identifying where linguistic confidence exceeds linguistic capacity, and why institutions often substitute authority, convention, or ritual for genuine semantic stability.

items.title: Dark Consciousness, Idea-Agents, and the Emergence of Qualia.
items.abstract: This essay proposes a three-layer architecture of mind in which phenomenal consciousness (qualia) is neither the foundation of mentality nor its inevitable accompaniment, but rather an emergent mechanism triggered by a specific computational condition: the irresolvable collision of multiple simultaneous contexts within a system operating under bounded resources.
