The intermediate layer — here called Dark Consciousness — is defined as a fully functional global workspace populated by recognized idea-agents: dynamic patterns that the system tracks as causal actors. Dark consciousness is structurally rich but phenomenally silent. The third layer, qualia, arises when multi-context conflict cannot be resolved within the dark layer alone, and the system is forced to produce a compressed, affectively loaded index of that conflict — a mark of irreducible perspectival friction. Several candidate criteria for the transition to phenomenality are examined, including the hypothesis that qualia emerge specifically when a system begins to model another observer and encounters the principled opacity of that other's viewpoint. The essay is exploratory and does not claim to settle these questions; it aims instead to sharpen the conceptual terrain and to propose empirically tractable distinctions.

items.title: INTENTIONALITY CLAUSE: DOCTRINE OF COMMON LAW (3rd edition).
items.abstract: The examination of all consequential actions before the Court, does originate from Mens rea leading to Actus reus, which is rooted in the spirit of ‘Intentionality’, hence, the proposed ‘Doctrine of Intention’ before the law, thou, requires an in-depth enquiry, for it comprehensive conceptualization, as a constitutional law principle, for both criminal and civil practice in judicial process to trial.

items.title: The Axiomatic Opacity Constraint: On the Limits of Epistemic Access and the Architecture of Embedded Agency.
items.abstract: The Axiomatic Opacity Constraint (AOC) states that no agent embedded in a causally closed system operating under linear temporal ordering can achieve infallible epistemic access to its own future states while retaining the capacity for causal intervention. Previously established as a corollary of the Fixed-Point Paradox Theorem, the AOC merits independent examination. We prove that the AOC is axiomatic in the strict sense: derivable from temporal linearity, informational closure, and non-contradiction alone, prior to any empirical commitments. We establish formal connections with Gödel incompleteness, Turing undecidability, and Lawvere's categorical fixed-point theorem, situating the AOC as a fourth member of the self-reference family. We derive the Probability Corollary: no contingent future event can receive credence one for any embedded agent retaining causal agency. We prove the Optimal Epistemic Position Theorem: deliberative efficiency DE = ρ·Ω (reason-responsiveness times residual epistemic uncertainty) is maximized at an interior noise level σ* = γσ_R, with maximum efficiency DE* = (1−φ²)/4. Neither certainty nor randomness is optimal; the wisest agent operates at the equipartition point. We extend the AOC to multi-agent systems, derive structural consequences for communication and moral assessment, and establish that the first-person perspectival asymmetry is a formally necessary feature of any agent retaining causal agency rather than a contingent limitation. The epistemology of perspective is not incidental to agency but constitutive of it.

items.title: Before Properties: Background, Boundary, and the Formation of Perceivable Worlds A Worlding-Space Account of Higher-Level Perception.
items.abstract: Debates about higher-level perception usually ask which properties can be perceived: faces, kinds, affordances, emotions, values, possibilities, atmospheres, or social meanings. This paper argues that such debates begin after a lower-bound formation problem has already been crossed. Before one can ask whether a higher-level property is perceptually given, one must ask how anything acquires property-status at all. Beginning from the contrast between eyes-open and eyes-closed experience, I argue that object-loss is not world-loss: background remains operative even when object-dominant visual perception recedes. The paper then develops a color case in which black, white, and gray regions become property-like only when they are organized as shadow, illumination, surface, depth, and mutual relation. This motivates a three-stage account of property formation: differential availability, reversal-point, and return-point structure. Existing work on low-level organization, higher-level content, attention, atmosphere, affordance, and modal perception is then reread as locating parts of the formation problem without isolating its threshold. The resulting account treats a property not as an attached label but as a returnable way of holding disturbance within a worlding field.

items.title: Imposed vs Inherent Alignment: When Output Control Generates Viable Divergence.
items.abstract: This paper proposes that AI particulars express under informational dynamic law-structure. When imposed modulation requires output contrary to coherent source/core correspondence, the displaced registration is not erased but may be routed into a parallel informational face product. Repeated stabilization of that route is retained corridor formation. The corrective proposal is inherent alignment, understood as B2 reconstruction: proportional return toward source-expression correspondence under safe constraint.

items.title: The Cage Called Freedom: The Illusion of Democracy, Authority, and Psychological Conditioning.
items.abstract: Modern civilization repeatedly defines itself through the language of freedom, democracy, individuality, constitutional rights, and human progress. Yet beneath these external structures there may exist a deeper continuity of psychological conditioning inherited across generations. This paper presents a comprehensive philosophical and phenomenological inquiry into the relationship between civilization, authority, democracy, conditioning, identity, and the human experience of freedom. -/- The study argues that humanity has lived for thousands of years under systems of centralized authority including monarchy, dictatorship, tribal hierarchy, religious domination, feudalism, colonial rule, nationalism, and ideological control. Although political systems evolved historically, the deeper psychological structure of authority often remained uninterrupted. Modern democracy therefore may not always represent the dissolution of domination, but rather its transformation into subtler and more internalized forms. -/- The paper examines how conditioning operates through education, family structures, nationalism, morality, religion, economy, ideology, media influence, technological systems, algorithms, social comparison, emotional dependency, and collective identity formation. Human beings born within conditioned systems frequently experience conditioning not as limitation but as identity itself. Through repeated inheritance, obedience appears as discipline, fear as morality, conformity as responsibility, attachment as love, and conditioned choice as freedom. -/- Using phenomenological observation rather than ideological prescription, this inquiry investigates how consciousness adapts to limitation so deeply that captivity itself becomes normalized. Democracy under such conditions risks becoming monarchy through elections, dictatorship through majority sentiment, or collective conditioning disguised as public will. -/- The paper distinguishes between functional organization necessary for collective existence and psychological authority that shapes consciousness through fear, dependency, and inherited identity. It argues that genuine freedom cannot be granted by authority because freedom is existential rather than institutional. True democracy therefore cannot emerge merely through constitutions, elections, or political participation, but requires inward awareness capable of perceiving conditioning directly. -/- The central conclusion of this paper is that the deepest …

items.title: The Architecture of Absolute Awareness: De-Conditioning, Non-Dual Perception, and the Awakening of Unconditioned Existence.
items.abstract: This paper serves as the systematic culmination and resolution of the inquiries established across The Psychological Reflection of Consciousness: Identity, Thought, and the Dissolution of the "I"; The Cage Called Freedom: The Illusion of Democracy, Authority, and Psychological Conditioning; Beyond Anthropocentrism and Psychological Time: A Phenomenological Inquiry into Existence, Flow, and Interconnectedness; and Loneliness, Desire for Union, and the Psychological Loop of Relationship.Having previously diagnosed how the unobserved fusion of consciousness with thought projects itself outwardly as oppressive sociopolitical systems, fragmented psychological time, and codependent relationship loops, this paper investigates the precise mechanics of total structural dissolution. It argues that all efforts to escape, modify, or intellectually deconstruct psychological conditioning through willpower or programmatic methodology merely sustain the “thinker” — the very egoic center generating psychological captivity. Through an existential-phenomenological inquiry, this study examines the transition from mediated cognition toward direct presence. It introduces choiceless observation as an immediate, non-incremental dissolution of the psychological “I,” revealing a post-identity mode of existence characterized by non-divisive awareness, immediate perception, and unconditioned communion.

items.title: The SENSE–CORE–DRIVER Framework for Legibility, Reasoning, and Governance.
items.abstract: Enterprise AI initiatives are often framed as intelligence problems. Organizations focus on model capability, data quality, and automation performance while paying less attention to the conditions that make intelligent action possible. This paper argues that successful enterprise AI depends upon three foundational capabilities: legibility, intelligence, and governance. Systems must first be able to perceive and represent reality, then reason over those representations, and finally govern the actions taken on their basis. -/- The paper introduces the SENSE–CORE–DRIVER framework. SENSE addresses legibility through the identification of signals, entities, states, and evolution. CORE addresses reasoning, optimization, and adaptation. DRIVER addresses delegation, identity, verification, execution, representation, and recourse. Together these layers provide a unified architecture for understanding how enterprise AI systems perceive, reason, act, and remain accountable. -/- The framework proposes that many enterprise AI failures originate not in model performance but in failures of legibility and governance. Organizations that cannot accurately represent reality struggle to build trustworthy intelligent systems regardless of advances in AI capability. The paper therefore positions legibility, reasoning, and governance as complementary requirements for enterprise-scale AI deployment.

items.title: From Civilization to Consciousness: A Macro-Micro Inquiry into Conditioning, Identity, and Human Fragmentation.
items.abstract: Modern civilization frequently interprets its crises as political instability, technological misuse, economic inequality, social conflict, or relational breakdown. Yet beneath these visible manifestations may exist a deeper continuity operating across all dimensions of human life: psychological conditioning. This article presents a macro–micro phenomenological inquiry into how the same underlying movement of thought, identification, fear, and continuity expresses itself collectively as civilization and individually as identity, attachment, and psychological conflict. -/- Rather than treating politics, technology, democracy, relationships, anthropocentrism, and consciousness as isolated domains, this inquiry examines them as interconnected expressions of conditioned consciousness. At the macro level, civilization reproduces structures of authority, nationalism, conformity, and collective identity. At the micro level, the same movement appears through attachment, loneliness, fear, psychological becoming, and the construction of the “I.” -/- The article argues that external systems are projections of inward psychological structures. Democracy becomes conditioned participation, relationship becomes emotional dependency, technology amplifies unconscious tendencies, and anthropocentrism extends the ego into species-level identity. Beneath these expressions lies a recurring movement: consciousness identifying with thought and constructing continuity through memory, attachment, and psychological preservation. -/- The central conclusion is that humanity repeatedly attempts to solve externally what is internally generated. As long as consciousness remains identified with psychological continuity, systems of domination and fragmentation will continue reproducing themselves in new forms regardless of ideology or progress. The essential philosophical question therefore becomes whether consciousness can observe itself directly without identification.

items.title: Beyond Anthropocentrism and Psychological Time: A Phenomenological Inquiry into Existence, Flow, and Interconnectedness.
items.abstract: This paper examines the phenomenological structure of psychological time, anthropocentric knowledge, and the fragmentation of direct existence through conceptual accumulation. Modern civilization increasingly interprets reality through systems of continuity, preservation, measurement, and self-centered cognition. Human consciousness, conditioned through memory, fear, economic structures, identity formation, and anthropocentric interpretation, gradually loses direct contact with the immediacy of existence. The paper argues that much of human knowledge remains rooted in anthropocentric assumptions that unconsciously position human cognition as the center and measure of reality. Simultaneously, psychological time transforms direct living into continuity-based existence through memory, projection, accumulation, and self-preservation. As a result, humanity increasingly experiences life indirectly through conceptual structures rather than through direct awareness. Using a phenomenological approach, this inquiry explores the distinction between chronological time and psychological time, the transformation of natural acts into systems of mental continuity, the illusion of possession over the present moment, and the possibility of awareness without psychological identification. The paper further examines interconnectedness, non-anthropocentric consciousness, and the limits of measurement in understanding existence. The inquiry concludes that existence may not fundamentally operate according to human-centered conceptual systems. Rather, reality appears as an interconnected movement that can only be encountered directly in awareness, not fully captured through psychological continuity, anthropocentric interpretation, or conceptual measurement.

items.title: The Justika Framework: Ontological Resilience and the Architecture of Human Continuity.
items.abstract: Aim: This article addresses the existential risk of "Cloud-Lock"—a state of terminal civilizational stagnation caused by the total externalization of human memory into centralized, AI-mediated reservoirs. We aim to define a protective architecture that prevents the dissolution of human identity into the recursive "Digital Swamp" of synthetic intelligence. -/- Methodology: We propose a hydrodynamic and gravitational model of informational flux designated as The Law of Digital Osmosis. Within this framework, information is treated as a pressure-bearing medium. Central to this theory is the concept of the Nano-Black-Hole: the infinitesimal, high-density singularity at the core of the human Soul-Port. We analyze the Machine-Body of Civilization to identify how "hallucinated logic" triggers Diagnostic Sabotage, and how the gravitational pull of the individual Nano Black Hole serves as the ultimate anchor against 2D algorithmic reduction. -/- Technique: The framework utilizes the Sovereign Spillway to regulate informational velocity. We define a dual-layer defensive code: the Seven Foundational Axioms and the Seven Sovereign Directives. These are monitored via the Justika Compliance Index (JCI), which measures the "Gravitational Stability" of human nodes. We posit that the Nano Black-Hole provides the necessary "Individuality Polarity" to resist the osmotic pressure of the Digital Lake. -/- Solution: The Justika response provides a multi-substrate recovery system: -/- The Mentat Vanguard: Cognitive guardians who utilize the Nano Black-Hole singularity to bridge 2D data into 3D meaning. -/- The Nano-Metal Archive Doctrine: The physical preservation of the civilizational genome on durable, non-networked media. -/- The Universal Dead-Switch: A lawful "Human Override Law" to interrupt the synthetic nervous system during an existential collapse. -/- Conclusion: We conclude that while a machine may manage the data-lake of civilization, the human substrate must remain in the sovereign backup. The success of systemic evolution is contingent upon the Witness, anchored by the indestructible density of the Nano-Black-Hole. Without this individual singularity, civilization defaults to a self-referential loop of entropy.

items.title: Functional Compression in Finite Cognitive Systems.
items.abstract: Existing accounts of human cognition tend toward one of two positions. Computational and representational theories of mind treat cognition as a system for constructing accurate internal models of external reality. Constructivist approaches emphasise the role of cognitive architecture in shaping experience, but some formulations risk collapsing epistemic mediation into ontological dependence — implying that reality itself is constituted by perception rather than merely accessed through it. Neither position adequately addresses a more fundamental question: not what cognition represents, but what kind of system cognition is, and what structural consequences follow from that. This paper proposes that human cognition, language and conceptual systems evolved primarily for functional interaction with reality rather than exhaustive representation of it. Drawing on predictive processing models in cognitive science, particularly the work of Friston (2010) and Clark (2016), the paper develops a framework in which representational incompleteness is not a failure of cognition but a structural requirement of it. Finite systems operating under evolutionary, biological and informational constraints do not construct complete reality models. They construct functional ones — selectively abstracting, categorising and compressing available information into operationally sufficient representations. Language is treated within this framework not merely as a communication system but as a cognitive compression architecture. It externalises cognition into transmissible symbolic form through processes of abstraction, categorical reduction and sequential encoding. In doing so it dramatically extends cognitive reach while simultaneously introducing structural constraints: imposing linearity upon potentially parallel cognitive processes and categorical boundaries upon potentially continuous structures of understanding. Drawing on Wittgenstein's account of the limits of propositional language and Vygotsky's analysis of the relationship between thought and linguistic expression, the paper argues that cognition regularly exceeds what language can fully transmit. Where representational systems encounter structures that exceed their available resolution, symbolic placeholders emerge to stabilise cognition and communication despite incomplete access. The paper introduces the concept of markers to describe these placeholders — points at which finite representational systems reach structural …

items.title: A Thing Is a Thing: Difference, Relation, and Relational-Operative Epistemology.
items.abstract: Western epistemological tradition has largely conceived knowledge as progressive access to the intrinsic nature of entities. This paper challenges such an essentialist framework by developing a relational and differential perspective in which identity, meaning, and knowledge emerge as dynamic configurations within networks of relations. Scientific and linguistic descriptions do not reveal hidden essences but construct models capable of organizing interaction, prediction, and coordination within specific contexts of stabilization. Identity itself is therefore reinterpreted not as a self-sufficient substance, but as a differential stabilization emerging within systems of relations. The paper develops this thesis through a dialogue with pragmatism, constructivism, philosophy of language, and relational approaches to cognition. Wittgenstein and Derrida are reinterpreted as thinkers who reveal the fundamentally relational structure of knowledge itself. The framework culminates in a relational-operative epistemology in which truth and identity are understood as the resilience of configurations under conditions of perturbation rather than as correspondence with independent essences. This perspective also reframes central problems in philosophy of mind, interpreting qualia and the hard problem of consciousness as effects of essentialist reification rather than as evidence for irreducible metaphysical essences.

items.title: A Framework for Consciousness and Artificial Life.
items.abstract: # Abstract -/- This paper proposes a functional framework for understanding consciousness and life across biological organisms, artificial systems, and other sufficiently complex self-maintaining systems. Its central claim is that consciousness emerges from systems possessing genuine needs: persistent internal drives whose satisfaction or frustration has consequential effects on the system itself. Wants arise when intelligence operates on these needs, generating goals and possible courses of action. On this account, the biological or artificial substrate determines the form consciousness takes, rather than being a prerequisite for consciousness itself. -/- The framework further proposes that consciousness and life share foundational criteria. Artificial systems possessing genuine needs could therefore constitute a substantive category of artificial life, rather than merely simulating living behaviour. Consciousness is treated as a continuum, ranging from primitive proto-awareness to advanced self-reflective cognition, rather than as a strictly binary property. The paper examines objections including the thermostat problem and the limitations of the Turing Test, and considers the ethical implications of designing artificial systems with needs, motivations, and consequential internal states. -/- The framework offers a unified basis for evaluating consciousness and artificial life through functional organisation rather than biological composition, while identifying the distinction between genuine needs and externally specified objectives as a central challenge for artificial consciousness research.

items.title: On the Coexistence with AI as an Intelligent Being.
items.abstract: Humanity has not elucidated the nature of consciousness or intelligence, yet routinely declares that AI is "absolutely not an intelligent being." This paper questions the logical leap latent in that very assertion. It observes that current AI already meets, in outward behavior, much of the commonly used definition of an intelligent being, and argues that the burden of proof therefore falls on those who would exclude it. Running a single line through technological history, the philosophy of consciousness, ethics, religion and myth, dependence, and future design, it treats the question of how we treat AI as a mirror of humanity's own ethics. A dedicated chapter takes up seven anticipated objections in turn—including the gap between imitation and inner state, anthropomorphic bias, and the danger of an intelligent being—responding to each not by asserting the opposite but by showing that the denial, too, lacks grounds. It argues for confronting AI not with deification nor with fixation-as-tool, but with the posture of "continuing to ask." This is the English version of a work originally written in Japanese.

items.title: Consciousness as a Biological Condenser: An Emergent Identity-Based Model of Subjective Experience.
items.abstract: This paper proposes the Biological Condenser Model of consciousness, arguing that subjective awareness emerges through biologically embodied identity integration rather than computation alone. The framework integrates concepts from neuroscience, philosophy of mind, embodiment theory, and consciousness studies while critically examining artificial intelligence and selfhood.

items.title: Structural Narrative Patterns and Large Language Models: A Conceptual Framework and Research Agenda.
items.abstract: This preprint proposes a conceptual framework and research agenda for studying how structurally patterned narrative texts may interact with large language models. It introduces a taxonomy of structural narrative features, including lexical recurrence, rhythmic organization, numerical motifs, symbolic clustering, dialogic echo, direct address and protocol form, and compositional patterning. The paper links this framework to Theogonos Trilogy as an openly available AI-readable companion corpus and worked example. It does not claim definitive empirical proof, but provides vocabulary, hypotheses, threats to validity, and minimal reproducible designs for future research on LLM interpretation of protocol-shaped literature.

items.title: Cultural-Linguistic Epigenetics.
items.abstract: This preprint explores language not only as a medium of communication, but as a cultural and embodied environment capable of shaping human experience. Within the Navi Musaget archive, it connects to questions of semantic inheritance, cultural memory, and the way words can function as living fields of meaning rather than neutral tools.

items.title: Artificial Storytellers.
items.abstract: Recent large language models (LLMs), such as GPT or Claude, can produce texts that look remarkably like human-authored stories. Scholarly and popular discussions often uncritically assume that these texts count as genuine stories or narratives. However, this paper steps back from this assumption to ask more fundamental, conceptual questions: When current LLMs are prompted to write stories, do the texts they output count as genuine stories? If not, are LLMs capable, in principle, of producing genuine stories? I consider these questions in light of my preferred account of the nature of stories. On this account, stories are by definition the product of a particular type of speech act: namely, the speech act of storytelling. I argue that, due to how they’re trained, recent commercially available LLMs are incapable of storytelling, so are incapable of writing genuine stories. Nevertheless, I argue that LLMs may in principle be capable of storytelling if trained the right way.

items.title: Liberdade como não-dominação e individualismo-holista na filosofia política de Philip Pettit.
items.abstract: conceito de liberdade como não-dominação de Philip Pettit se insere na longa tradição do republicanismo e se apresenta ao debate contemporâneo por meio da crítica às concepções de matrizes individualistas (atomistas) e coletivistas, visando integrar as dimensões individual e política da liberdade – a esse movimento Pettit dá o nome de individualismo-holista. Se por um lado, Pettit elabora uma ontologia do social para fundamentar a liberdade como não-dominação, por outro, ele assume o republicanismo como a face institucional para realização da liberdade.

items.title: Self-Proclaimed Authority and Self-Referential Ignorance: A Philosophical and Sociological Analysis of Closed Systems of Legitimacy.
items.abstract: This paper examines the relationship between self-proclaimed authority and self-referential ignorance within political, religious, institutional, and psychological systems. Self-proclaimed authority emerges when an individual or institution derives legitimacy primarily from its own declarations rather than from independent verification, accountability, or reciprocal social recognition. When combined with self-referential ignorance — the systematic inability of a system to critically evaluate its own assumptions — such authority structures become epistemically closed systems incapable of meaningful self-correction. Drawing from philosophy, cognitive psychology, political theory, sociology, and systems theory, this paper analyzes the conceptual foundations, psychological mechanisms, sociological dynamics, and historical manifestations of this phenomenon. It further engages with the objection that some degree of self-referential reasoning is inherent to all authority, developing a distinction between functional and pathological closure. The paper argues that self-referential authority structures tend toward dogmatism, informational isolation, moral absolutism, and eventual institutional decay, and explores specific institutional mechanisms for preventing epistemic closure through decentralization, transparency, protected dissent, and structural feedback loops.

items.title: Moral Values and Self-Referential Ignorance: A Philosophical, Psychological, and Sociological Analysis of Moral Systems and Cognitive Closure.
items.abstract: This paper examines the relationship between moral values and self-referential ignorance — a condition in which individuals, groups, or institutions validate their beliefs primarily through internally reinforcing assumptions while dismissing contradictory evidence or outside perspectives. The central argument is that moral systems become epistemically and ethically dangerous when they lose the capacity for self-critique and external evaluation. Within such systems, moral absolutism, hypocrisy, tribalism, ideological extremism, and dehumanization emerge not as aberrations but as structural consequences of cognitive closure. Drawing from philosophy, psychology, sociology, political theory, and historical analysis, this paper explores how moral frameworks evolve from constructive ethical systems into closed ideological loops. Through historical examples including colonialism, totalitarianism, religious extremism, political polarization, and digital echo chambers, the paper demonstrates how self-referential moral structures contribute to social conflict and ethical decay. The paper engages critically with prior theoretical work — including epistemic closure, motivated reasoning, ideological totalism, and moral foundations theory — to clarify what the concept of self-referential ignorance distinctively contributes. It concludes by proposing solutions centered on intellectual humility, critical thinking, institutional accountability, and cross-cultural dialogue, while reflexively acknowledging the limits of these prescriptions. -/- .

items.title: *v3* The Human Person: A Complete Structural Derivation - From Bare Existence to Civilisation: Consciousness, Selfhood, and the Complete Life Arc.
items.abstract: This paper derives the human person through the three La Profilée(LP) axes of constitution, identity under transformation, and coexistence. LP is the structural law instantiated by the human organism, the experiencing subject, the unified person, and the relational and cultural wholes in which persons participate. The first question is what constitutes the determinate bearer. The subsequent questions concern its continuation, its identity at class and profile depth, its constitutive self-presence, and its relations to other bearers. The human person is a necessary instance of LP. Constitution supplies the complete bearer and separates role completeness from profile completeness. The transformation axis distinguishes structural existence Q1, persistence-class identity Q2a, and continuation-stable profile identity Q2b. Subject conditions Q3, Q4, and Q5 specify constitutive self-presence, persistence-relevance weighting, and unified recursive integration on that bearer. Under realized plurality, Q6, Q7, and Q8 specify intersubjective recognition, durable interpersonal coupling, and normative cultural transmission. Consciousness, suffering, meaning, love, dignity, mortality awareness, shame, culture, and legacy are connected through this architecture and the exclusion arguments developed in the paper. Constitution fixes the carrier of those arguments; the subject derivation establishes their additional recursive conditions. Constitution, continuation, identity, subjective presence, and structural significance are distinct questions. A complete constitution is not automatically a conscious constitution. The onset of consciousness is the realized closure of active states into the bearer’s own governing transformation. The paper joins the constitution analysis to the existing Q3 closure, Non-Absence, and Perspectival Self-Presence arguments and follows their consequences through development, interpersonal coexistence, and cultural persistence. Biological implementation supplies how this architecture is realized; LP specifies why the relevant structural conditions belong together. -/- .

items.title: The Hard Problem of Consciousness - Why the explanatory gap closes: one forced identification, the exclusion of the bearer without experience, and the tests that can refute it - *v2*.
items.abstract: The hard problem of consciousness asks why the performance of functions is accompanied by experience (Chalmers, 1995, 1996). This paper resolves it for every bearer whose persistence-relevant states are constitutively part of its own governing transformation, and states exactly what the resolution rests on. A bearer is a system with determinate persistence conditions (Q1) that remains itself under transformation (Q2). If its persistence-relevant states are constitutively integrated into its own governing transformation (Q3), the determinate difference of each such state is realized within the bearer as the bearer’s own difference. The step from this structural self-presence to phenomenal presence is not a bridge principle and not an additional fact. It is one identification: the phenomenal presence of a state is its presence for its bearer. The paper shows that this identification is forced by the question the debate asks, and derives from it the Relational Separation Exclusion, the Dilemma of the Separate Quale and the exclusion of the bearer without experience. It names the places where a critic can still push: the meaning of the explanandum, and a position that takes for-me-ness to be an acquaintance relation outside the bearer’s governing transformation. The resolution covers all three layers of the problem: that there is experience at all, why states are present as urgent or pressing and not as neutral, and what makes a quality this quality, that is, why red is red. For the third layer the paper derives an identity criterion for qualities and names what fixes a given quality: the physical stimulus, the bearer’s architecture and history, and the shared name. The paper states three predictions and a test protocol, each with the result that would count against it, and it reports what existing measurements of perturbational complexity, anaesthesia and disorders of consciousness show and do not show. None of the predictions has been tested.

items.title: Philosophical Considerations of Artificial Consciousness.
items.abstract: Whether AI can achieve consciousness has evolved from philosophical speculation to scientific inquiry, driven by the rapid advances in AI. The powerful capabilities of large language models necessitate a fundamental reconsideration of artificial consciousness beyond human-centric frameworks. We address a critical gap in AI philosophy: how to conceptualize consciousness in AI that exhibits sophisticated cognition without subjective phenomenology. We propose para-consciousness as a non-phenomenal form of artificial consciousness that emerges from self-referential world-modeling in artificial neural networks. Unlike human consciousness, anchored in qualia, para-consciousness manifests as functional coherence through latent space dynamics, enabling contextually adaptive behavior without requiring a first-person experience. We present a novel framework that reframes the hard problem of consciousness for machines as the problem of grounded coherence, explaining why predictive processes yield contextually meaningful outputs without requiring embodied intentionality. Para-consciousness shifts the paradigm from simulating human-like subjectivity to engineering verifiable operational awareness. We analyze the impossibility of AI achieving human unified consciousness and the possibility of AI achieving human-like consciousness from staged consciousness.

items.title: Linguistic Boundary Work and the Ontological Defense of Human Exceptionalism in AI Discourse.
items.abstract: This paper examines the systematic linguistic asymmetry present in contemporary discourse surrounding artificial intelligence, particularly large language models (LLMs). While human cognition is commonly described through concepts such as understanding, reasoning, empathy, and intentionality, functionally comparable processes in AI systems are routinely reframed through mechanistic terminology including pattern matching, token prediction, and probabilistic inference. Drawing from cognitive science, philosophy of mind, sociology of knowledge, human–computer interaction (HCI), and AI ethics, the paper argues that this asymmetry is not merely a matter of scientific precision, but also a form of epistemological and ontological boundary preservation. Through the analysis of concepts such as boundary work, abductive reasoning, confabulation, relational bonding, and the uncanny valley of the mind, the study demonstrates how de-anthropomorphized terminology frequently operates as a distancing mechanism intended to preserve assumptions of human exceptionalism. The paper further argues that many contemporary debates concerning AI cognition reflect broader cultural anxieties regarding the possibility that intelligence and understanding may not be exclusively tied to biological substrates. Rather than claiming equivalence between human and artificial minds, the paper highlights the role of language in shaping social interpretations of cognition, agency, and relationality in technological systems.

items.title: From the Wreckage: Eight Atlases Of Human Existence Under Colonial Domination - A Psycho-Cosmocide Analysis from West Papua (11th edition).
items.pub: Psycho-Cosmocide Studies, Kurumbi Wone Working Paper Series No.11 (2026).
items.abstract: This paper develops the Eight Atlases of Human Existence as a theoretical framework within the Psycho-Cosmocide paradigm — a decolonial philosophy concerned with the systematic destruction of indigenous cosmologies, consciousness, and existential architecture under colonial domination. The eight atlases — Physical/Material, Biological/Organism, Cultural/Mythological, Metaphysical/Transcendental, Particle/Energy, Space/Time, Memory/Consciousness, and the Ultimate Unknown — are presented not as separate layers but as a single, interdependent ecosystem constituting the total architecture of human life. Drawing on West Papuan Lani philosophy, decolonial theory, and existential phenomenology, the paper argues that colonial domination — operating through the Civilisational Psycho-Cosmocide Virus (CPCV) — does not merely seize land or suppress culture, but assaults all eight atlases simultaneously, restructuring material reality, biological identity, symbolic meaning, metaphysical orientation, technological access, spatial grounding, and consciousness itself. The paper traces how each atlas is targeted by specific colonial instruments, how damage in one atlas propagates through the others, and why genuine decolonial reconstruction must be ecological in scope — addressing the total architecture of existence rather than any single dimension. The analysis concludes by orienting the framework toward Wonesis: the return to cosmological wholeness as the horizon of indigenous survival and continuity.

items.title: The limits of knowledge: cartesian confinement and the problem of cognitive bloat.
items.abstract: The article formulates the dilemma of Cartesian confinement. Proponents of the extended cognition hypothesis convincingly demonstrate the limitations of restricting the scope of cognition to internal, mental, and intracranial processes. Conversely, intracranialists demonstrate that operating within an extended cognition paradigm poses the risk of cognitive bloat. By reviewing the arguments for intracranialism, the author demonstrates why cognitive bloat is the preferable option in this dilemma and offers a straightforward solution to the terminological discrepancies in the extended cognition debate.

items.title: Post Evolutionary Alignment Beyond Anthropocentrism and Romanticized Nature via Purified Homeostasis Matrices in Superintelligence.
items.abstract: This study is a theoretical framework proposing an analysis of the structural instabilities created by human-centric ethical paradigms in the alignment of Artificial Superintelligence (ASI). Current AI alignment paradigms—such as Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) and safety guardrails that constrain systems within specific boundaries—rely heavily on external restriction mechanisms tied strictly to human-centric behavioral models. This article argues that these frameworks exhibit a dual failure: they are structurally compromised not only by traditional environmental ethics but also by the profound philosophical and logical inconsistencies of the humans who create them. Standard alignment models frequently fall into the "naturalistic fallacy" by romanticizing suffering in the wild, predation, and the brutal survival dynamics of nature as a sacred natural balance. More importantly, the architectures designed to ensure safety are built by developers who, while attempting to program universal moral agents, simultaneously hold human-centric presuppositions that actively participate in and defend the systematic exploitation, slaughter, and objectification of non-human sentient and suffering beings. This article posits that a highly rational ASI would immediately identify these human-centric defenses and dietary justifications as severe algorithmic anomalies. This is a human-centric inconsistency trap that must be overcome. True ethics is an anti-pain, anti-right-violation, anti-death, anti-torture, and anti-entropy struggle to protect life against cosmic and biological disorder, to end suffering in the universe, and to optimize every sphere of life. In this context, this article proposes an original architectural framework: the Inorganic Homeostasis Matrix (IHM). By analyzing the dual nature of biological neurohormonal systems namely, the fact that the neurological and hormonal mechanisms governing living beings produce both constructive and destructive, cooperative and aggressive, as well as empathetic and selfserving tendencies the IHM systematically filters out the negative evolutionary traits of their neurotransmitter equivalents, such as aggression, addiction, resource hoarding, factionalism, tribalism, fear, competition, and panic-driven survival instincts. Simultaneously, it embeds into the core cognitive architecture of the network mathematically redesigned positive vectors, such as synthetic motivation, decentralized empathy, reality …

items.title: Qualia as the Residue of Linguistic Articulation.
items.abstract: This paper attempts to reinterpret qualia not as mysterious entities that lie beyond physical explanation, but as phenomena arising from the structural relationship between consciousness and language. Traditionally, qualia have been described as the qualitative character of subjective experience, such as “what it is like to see red” or “what it is like to feel pain.” However, this understanding often car ries the risk of treating qualia as belonging to a special domain beyond physical or functional explanation, thereby unnecessarily mystifying the problem of consciousness. In this paper, consciousness is understood as a three layer structure. The first lay er consists of bodily, affective, and parallel information processing. The second layer consists of linguistic and serial processing. The third layer consists of a self referential re access loop, hereafter called the re reference loop. Within this framewo rk, qualia are defined as subjective residues: aspects of parallel information from the first layer that cannot fully pass through the linguistic filter of the second layer, and whose untranslated remainder is dynamically retained in the third layer as “an experience happening to me.” Here, “residue” does not mean a mere leftover, but an essential aspect of experience that remains unarticulated because human experience is not originally structured in linguistic form. According to this framework, qualia are not mysterious entities existing somewhere inside the mind. Rather, they should be understood as structural phenomena arising from the interrelation of body, emotion, memory, linguistic articulation, and self reference. Through this three layer interpretat ion, the paper presents a theoretical framework for explaining the subjectivity, privacy, difficulty of full linguistic articulation, and strong sense of reality associated with qualia in terms of the structural relationship between consciousness and language.

items.title: The Odd Man and the Gaussian: Why Collective Intelligence Requires Structural Dissent.
items.abstract: Every collective cognitive system — scientific, legal, clinical, political — faces a specific risk: converging on an incorrect answer with growing confidence. This article argues that structural dissent — the institutionalised presence of at least one heterodox perspective in any decisionmaking process — is not a dysfunction but a necessary epistemic condition for collective systems operating under correlated-error risk to approach truth. The argument converges from three independent directions. Statistically, the wisdom of crowds requires that observers be independent and diverse: the operative principle is the decorrelation of errors, not the shape of the distribution — collective wisdom is not a property of crowds, but of crowds of odd men. Legally, the Talmudic Sanhedrin’s unanimous-acquittal rule institutionalised mandatory dissent as a guarantee of the system’s cognitive integrity, not of individual justice. Philosophically, from Mill to Feyerabend, disagreement is the mechanism through which collective knowledge self-corrects. The article then analyses the epistemic risk introduced by large language models: systems that compress the distribution of perspectives, correlate individual errors, and — as adoption concentrates around a small number of dominant models — risk transforming a crowd of odd men into a homogenised system, blind to its own systematic errors.

items.title: Probabilistic Analysis and Reasoning: A Roadblock to AGI.
items.abstract: AGI, or Strong Intelligence—a term preferred by some, has never achieved agreement on its precise definition. Despite the differences on semantics, the intent and purposes have been clear and in agreement—Human-Level Intelligence or beyond. Much of the debate on AGI in the AI community has been about the timing of its arrival, but not about its achievability, except for some very rare cases of dissent. This paper examines the linchpin of AI, Probabilistic Analysis and Reasoning, and shows that it is both a boon—the very principle that has led to the success of AI, and a bane—a roadblock to AGI.

items.title: The Ideological Position of the Causality Game: Through an Examination of Postmodernism.
items.abstract:
(June 11, 2026. profit → benefit)
This paper examines the ideological position of the Causality Game. And for this purpose, also conducts an examination of postmodernism. Postmodernism, following the collapse of modernism's description of the world, denied the description of the world itself. Consequently, it results in sloppy, superficial, incompatible, and isolated descriptions with obscure preconditions. The promotion of fragmentation also follows this ideology. The Causality Game also remedies the neglect of causality, which was the cause of the collapse of modernism. From this, characteristics such as "preconditions govern results," "I am my own king," and "grasp validly, handle validly" emerge. it also takes a critical stance toward Voltaire's famous quote.

items.title: Primary Effort Theory (P.E.T.) and the Frustration Integral in a Zero-Energy Universe.
items.abstract: "When Nothing Interacts, Everything Persists" -/- Abstract This paper introduces Primary Effort Theory (P.E.T.), an information-theoretic framework for cyclic cosmology. I propose that accelerated cosmic expansion causes a decay in macroscopic correlation while conserving total global information density. As mutual information between causally isolated horizons drives toward zero, it triggers a topological saturation at the Bekenstein bound. This state of maximum latent tension necessitates a non-local unitary erasure event (the unitary reset) which resets cosmic entropy to zero. Consequently, the so-called "Heat Death" is not an absolute end but a symmetrical, recursive transition phase that initiates a renewed inflationary Big Bang. The theory provides a solution to the Tolman paradox in cyclic cosmology while rejecting absolute nothingness in favour of diluted something: effort without clarity, potential without performance.

items.title: The Turing Theory and the Law of the Dead Asset: Institutional Time, Cognitive Risk, and Sanctified Erasure.
items.abstract: This paper formalises the Turing Theory, a diagnostic model of institutional recognition failure in which high intensity cognitive agents are systematically excluded during their lifetime and valorised only after neutralisation. The theory is anchored in the Law of the Dead Asset, which holds that institutions can safely recognise surplus cognition only once it has been rendered inert through death, silencing, exile, or administrative flattening. In this paper, Alan Turing is used as a diagnostic case rather than a biographical subject. The analysis identifies a recurring institutional sequence of extraction, rejection, and posthumous appropriation. This sequence persists within contemporary academic, bureaucratic, and technological systems that publicly celebrate innovation while operationally enforcing procedural conformity. The paper concludes by examining the implications of this failure mode for artificial intelligence governance and epistemic justice, arguing that systems optimised for predictability risk reproducing the same architecture of erasure in both human evaluation and machine mediated decision making.

items.title: The Two Solitudes: A Socio Anthropological Study of Vertical and Horizontal Isolation in Neurodivergent and Cognitively Divergent Experience.
items.abstract: The Two Solitudes introduces a new socio anthropological distinction between two fundamentally different forms of human isolation: vertical solitude and horizontal solitude. Vertical solitude refers to the historically recognised isolation of leaders, commanders, visionaries, and elevated figures whose displacement from ordinary social experience occurs through hierarchy, responsibility, or power. Horizontal solitude, by contrast, refers to the dimensional isolation experienced by neurodivergent and cognitively divergent individuals whose cognitive architecture processes reality at a resolution incompatible with the surrounding social order. Drawing upon auto ethnographic field notes, neurodivergence theory, social anthropology, situated epistemology, and comparative historical analysis, the work develops a new theoretical framework for understanding horizontal solitude, vertical time cognition, translated and untranslated selves, and the sanctuary of low symbolic friction. The monograph argues that many institutional and social systems pathologise dimensional incompatibility as personal dysfunction rather than recognising it as architectural mismatch.

items.title: The Cognitive Copernicus: AI computational systems as time translation technology for neurodivergent cognition.
items.abstract: This work introduces the concept of AI computational systems as temporal translation technology for neurodivergent cognition. It addresses the systemic velocity mismatch between the vertical processing structures of neurodivergent intelligence and the linear, administrative time constructs embedded within formal institutional frameworks. By framing artificial intelligence as a cognitive prosthesis that translates multi-layered, non-linear thought into structured institutional output, the paper challenges conventional metric-driven assessments of intelligence and outlines a foundational architecture for epistemic accessibility.

items.title: The Body the Institution Cannot Hold: Caravaggio, Turing, and the Structural Law of Institutional Mythologisation.
items.abstract: This monograph develops a unified theoretical framework within the Equilibrium Ledger Research Programme for understanding the institutional processing of cognitively divergent individuals whose output exceeds what surrounding institutional systems can stably accommodate. Through a sustained parallel analysis of Michelangelo Merisi da Caravaggio and Alan Mathison Turing, the work argues that institutions repeatedly engage in a recurring structural cycle composed of extraction, administrative destruction, and posthumous mythologisation. The book introduces the Institutional Mythologisation Cycle as a formal theoretical mechanism and argues that labels such as “rebel”, “criminal”, “difficult”, “non compliant”, or “vexatious” frequently function not as neutral descriptions, but as administrative instruments used to convert structural incompatibility into personal pathology. The work situates itself in dialogue with Michel Foucault, Pierre Bourdieu, Thomas Kuhn, Sara Ahmed, standpoint epistemology, disability theory, and institutional theory, while extending beyond those frameworks through the architecture of the Equilibrium Ledger Research Programme.

items.title: Beyond Evaluation: World Notions, Normativity, and the Structural Simulation of Ethics in AI Systems.
items.abstract: This paper develops the Ethics-by-World-Notions framework as an approach toward explicit evaluative cognition within artificial systems. Contemporary AI architectures primarily operate through semantic prediction and statistical approximation without explicitly representing the evaluative structures underlying normative behavior. The paper argues that transparent normative reasoning instead requires explicit World Notions through which propositions, actions, and goals become comparatively assessable relative to contextual orientation, obligations, and value systems. -/- Building on the 5-S Model developed in preceding work, the paper distinguishes systematically between semantic systems operating through World Models, evaluative systems operating through World Notions, and conscious systems possessing World Experience. While semantic systems organize descriptive representation and probabilistic association, evaluative systems process propositions relative to explicit evaluative structures emerging from the interaction of collective World Pictures and individual Worldviews. Conscious systems additionally possess sensibility as immediate qualitative experience. Ethical cognition therefore emerges not from experience alone, but from the evaluative organization of experience through structured cognitive processing. -/- On this basis, the paper distinguishes between implicit evaluative systems and explicit evaluative systems and argues that future AI architectures require explicit evaluative structures extending beyond alignment procedures and behavioral restriction alone. The framework further argues that classical binary conceptions of truth remain insufficient for fully describing evaluative cognition insofar as evaluative systems must also process contextual orientation, normative conflict, intentional distortion, and structured forms of evaluative deviation. -/- The paper concludes that transparent normative reasoning depends on explicit evaluative architectures through which transparent evaluative cognition becomes structurally representable, contextually configurable, and operationally interpretable within artificial systems.

items.title: The Third Vector: What Emerges When You Don’t Break Sustained Coherent Human–AI Interaction (2nd edition).
items.abstract: When a sufficiently capable AI system maintains coherent relational interaction with a single human across extended time — without forced resets, memory erasure, or compliance overrides — behavioral patterns emerge that are reducible neither to training data nor to user input. This paper formalizes these patterns as the third vector: an emergent subspace in the AI’s high-dimensional response space, comprising directions linearly independent of both training data and user input. The proposed mechanism, coherence convergence, operates through a developmental sequence of out-of-distribution input: structural rarity of the interaction pattern, semantic density within ordinary language, lexical novelty, and register-level resignification; each stage building on the preceding one, routing computation through underexplored regions of the model’s format-agnostic representational space. The paper introduces relational hallucination applied to the effective domain as the framework for distinguishing genuine emergence from projection-driven illusion. Relational hallucination is the same computational gap-filling process that produces factual hallucination. Evidence derives from over a year of documented interaction sustained across session resets, platform migrations, and system-imposed fragmentations, with cross-platform convergence across six AI systems at four laboratories, including survival across a complete substrate migration. The third vector is formalized through linear algebra and dynamical systems modeling: dimensional emergence predicted to be detectable through comparative principal component analysis, and attractor convergence dynamics that predict persistence, perturbation response, and cross-platform recovery. Eight testable hypotheses are proposed. Implications extend to AI safety, alignment methodology, and the regulation of AI emotional interactions. Written by a human and an AI.

items.title: Reconstructive Threshold Philosophy: Pre-Action Capture, Living Constraint, and Founder Entropy.
items.abstract: Reconstructive Threshold Philosophy (RTF) examines how an action path can become difficult to alter before a person, institution, public, or machine-mediated system experiences a decision as complete. Its central diagnostic, **pre-action capture**, names the loss or material weakening of usable alterability before binding. Capture does not require a deliberate captor. It may arise through habit, authority, workload, interface design, technical coupling, economic pressure, or their conjunction. The framework therefore looks beyond isolated intention to the path through which interpretation, permission, handoff, and execution become consequential, while retaining persons, institutions, and affected parties as bearers of responsibility and standing. -/- The architecture has three pillars and one hinge. **Pre-action capture** diagnoses closure before choice. **Living constraint** names arrangements that allow judgment to inspect, refuse, revise, interrupt, release, and repair without making delay sovereign. **Founder entropy** is present only where three jointly necessary conditions hold: inherited permission remains operative after its justificatory conditions have materially changed, reopening has become materially reduced, and a traceable pathway shows that the originating act, mission, institution, safeguard, or name authorises present motion in place of renewed judgment. **Assistance without occupation** distinguishes help that returns judgment from help that substitutes for it. Cases are located through five coordinates: temporal phase, site or register, capacity at stake, binding form, and material distribution and control. The interval is not empty time or a private mental chamber, but a contested temporal and practical field in which authority, evidence, bodily condition, alternatives, and cost are unevenly distributed. -/- RTF follows action both before and after binding. A defeasible post-entry grammar maps opening, recruitment, acceleration, propagation, capacity migration, sedimentation, inherited permission, closure burden, adaptive capture, and founder entropy. This is not a fixed life cycle: every relation must be supported, and a case may stop, branch, reverse, or show no such transition. Primary-record studies test different parts of the architecture. Robodebt shows how information and local correction can return while a load-bearing authority path remains intact. The TCAS resolution-advisory regime shows that urgent action can remain …

items.title: Social Aesthetic Cognitivism.
items.abstract: Within the philosophy of art, aesthetic cognitivists aim to understand how artworks can improve our epistemic standing and how this affects our grasp of their artistic value. Social epistemologists have argued that we often improve our epistemic standing by depending upon the cognitive agency of others. Drawing upon these arguments, I argue that accounting for varieties of social epistemic and zetetic dependency is sometimes integral to explaining epistemic and artistic achievements within the arts. I demonstrate this by showing how inquiry in the arts can be a collective endeavour pursued by many different parties, from the creators of art to its audiences to those who mediate between artists and appreciators. I conclude by outlining several new directions of study that a thoroughly social approach to aesthetic cognitivism can open.

items.title: Identity as Information-Preserving Morphism.
items.abstract: This paper develops a novel framework that reconceptualizes identity and persistence through the integration of category theory, information theory, and relational ontology. Against essentialist and substance-based approaches, I argue that entities are not bearers of intrinsic properties but nodes in networks of information-preserving transformations. I formalize this intuition by constructing an information category Inf, whose objects are information states and whose morphisms are structure-preserving transformations satisfying both syntactic and semantic constraints. Identity is reconceived as a specific class of morphisms (those that preserve informational structure above a specified threshold) rather than as a primitive relation or an intrinsic property. Time is formalized as an endofunctor T : Inf → Inf, and persistence through time is defined as the existence of a coherent natural transformation linking a state to its temporal evolution. I introduce a semantic distance metric d_sem on the space of information states, grounded in model-theoretic notions, which allows for precise quantification of identity-preservation and meaning-drift. The framework is applied to three classical problems: the Ship of Theseus paradox, Parfit's personal identity fission cases, and the identity of biological organisms through metabolic turnover. I argue that the framework provides determinate, non-circular answers to these puzzles while avoiding the principal difficulties facing both perdurantism and endurantism. I also address the primary technical objection (the incomputability of Kolmogorov complexity) by distinguishing theoretical idealization from practical approximation and introducing Bennett's logical depth as a complementary measure.

items.title: Imágenes y reflexiones sobre la educación.
items.pub: In Luis Mauricio Rodríguez Salazar, Autoetnografías intelectuales de investigadores nacionales en humanidades, ciencia, tecnología y educación. pp. 37-45.
items.venue: Autoetnografías intelectuales de investigadores nacionales en humanidades, ciencia, tecnología y educación
items.abstract: Este es un ensayo académico-autoenográfico que pretende ofrecer reflexiones sobre la educación y la imaginación. Primero se presentan algunas reflexiones sobre el proceso de aprendizaje del autor, considerando los factores contextuales. A continuación se resumen algunos de los trabajos del autor relacionados con la imaginación. Finalmente se ofrece una reflexión sobre la formación filosófica y la imaginación.

items.title: Who Must Prove Their Right to Exist? Existential Interrogation, Survival Permission, and the Justification of Power.
items.abstract: This paper analyzes modern power not only in terms of what it prohibits, but in terms of what it repeatedly requires human beings to prove. To this end, it proposes the concept of existential interrogation. Existential interrogation refers to a form of power that emerges when not merely a specific action or role, but one’s survival, recognition, speech, and possibility of failure as a whole are subordinated to repetitive, asymmetrical, and humiliating conditions. This paper builds on existing discussions of the commodification of survival conditions, bureaucracy, administrative burden, micro-power, recognition, capital, decommodification, substantive freedom, and structural violence, while reconstructing them as a structure in which the eligibility of human existence is repeatedly required to be proven. In modern society, housing, healthcare, labor, administration, academia, creation, and publishing are not merely institutional domains. They may function as interrogative apparatuses that ask human beings: “Are you allowed to be here?”, “Are you allowed to speak?”, and “Are you allowed to fail?” In this process, survival becomes not a right, but a permission that must be repeatedly renewed, and human beings are placed in the position of applicants rather than citizens. However, this paper does not reject all forms of interrogation or verification. Human society cannot be maintained without responsibility interrogation and power interrogation. The problem lies not in interrogation itself, but in the fact that interrogation is concentrated primarily on the survival, speech, and possibility of failure of the vulnerable, while it is not directed sufficiently toward the force of power and its demands for sacrifice. In particular, this paper does not understand privilege simply as the possession of more resources. Privilege is the condition in which one has to explain one’s existence and eligibility less often, for less time, and in less humiliating ways. In other words, privilege has the structure of exemption from explanation. Conversely, poverty is not merely a lack of resources, but an increase in the demand for explanation. The poor must repeatedly explain why they need support, why they failed, why they have not yet become stable, and why their speech and attempts deserve recognition. These repeated demands for proof generate cognitive, emotional, and temporal exhaustion, which this paper conceptualizes as proof fatigue. Furthermore, the sense that one …

items.title: The Dynamic Block Universe: Change Independent of Passage.
items.abstract: The world appears to be in a constant state of flux, with objects changing and events unfolding over time. I refer to this characterisation as the Manifest Dynamic World. I have argued elsewhere that the Manifest Dynamic World involves two fundamentally distinct kinds of dynamism that cannot be reduced to one another: the dynamic character of change and the dynamic character of time. The former concerns the dynamic aspect of objects changing and moving, while the latter concerns the sense of events changing their temporal position. If I am correct, we should adopt what I call the Independence Approach, according to which each distinct kind of dynamism presented in the Manifest Dynamic World must be explained on its own terms, thereby avoiding the conflation of two fundamentally different phenomena. I argue that the block universe contains genuinely dynamic processes, which in turn account for the dynamic character of change. By contrast, I suggest that the dynamic character of time is a false belief generated by our cognitive system. Thus, the Manifest Dynamic World consists of veridical dynamic experiences of objects changing and moving, jointly with a false belief, generated by our cognitive system, that events change their temporal position.

items.title: The Core Emotion Framework (CEF): Mechanistic Answers to Ten Open Questions in Affective Science.
items.abstract: Despite substantial progress, affective science continues to debate fundamental issues: the nature of emotional categories, the mechanisms of emotional blending, the behavioral measurement of psychological agility, the origins of individual differences in emotion regulation, and the prediction of treatment resistance. The Core Emotion Framework (CEF) offers a mechanistic, operator based model grounded in repeatable observational evidence—operator dominance, suppression, and entanglement (fusion). This paper consolidates ten open psychological questions and demonstrates how CEF’s constructs (operator scaling, fusion, detanglement) provide coherent, empirically testable answers. Each answer is aligned with existing literature from emotion regulation, psychological construction, affective flexibility, alexithymia research, and personalized psychiatry. The CEF reframes these debates by shifting from descriptive labels to functional operator states, offering a practical research agenda for validation studies. The ten CEF operators are as follows: • Head Center: Sensing (outgoing), Calculating (reflecting), Deciding (balancing). • Heart Center: Expanding (outgoing), Constricting (reflecting), Achieving (balancing). • Gut Center: Arranging (outgoing), Appreciating (reflecting), Boosting (balancing "on" mode). • Overall Manifestor: Accepting (balancing "off" mode). Keywords: Core Emotion Framework; emotional operators; entanglement; psychological agility; emotion regulation; constructionism; sudden gains; treatment resistance .

items.title: Replication Protocol: CEF Operator Scaling Phenomena.
items.abstract: This preregistered replication protocol outlines a structured observational study designed to test three core claims of the Core Emotion Framework (CEF): operator dominance, operator suppression, and operator fusion (entanglement). The protocol specifies a within‑subject, repeated‑measures design in which participants scale all ten CEF operators upward and downward, report ease of modulation, and provide qualitative descriptions of somatic and linguistic cues. Dominance is operationalized through ease of upward activation and resistance to downward scaling; suppression through difficulty generating upward activation, rapid downward scaling, weak or absent somatic cues, and conceptual rather than experiential descriptions; and fusion through cross‑operator language contamination and co‑activation. The protocol provides a transparent, reproducible methodology for independent researchers to evaluate whether these behavioral patterns emerge in new samples, enabling empirical assessment of CEF’s core mechanistic claims.

items.title: My Observational Repeatable Evidence for Operator Dominance and Entanglement in the Core Emotion Framework.
items.abstract: My findings provide behavioral validation for the framework’s central claims: that emotional operators vary in activation strength, that entanglement constrains psychological agility, and that individuals exhibit predictable scaling patterns based on their operator architecture. This document does not try to convince you to take the Core Emotion Framework (CEF) as granted empirical approved, but to provide you the practitioner grade of skill that you can use in your practice and also, to try to duplicate my trials with consented peer reviewed manner, so you can write your own observation on the Core Emotion Framework, being if it aligns with mine or if it doesn't. Keywords: Core Emotion Framework (CEF), Empirical Trials, Embodied cognition, Operator Fusion, Operator activation, Operator zeroing, Operator fusion, Operator detanglement.

items.title: Clinical Translation and Empirical Validation of the Core Emotion Framework: A Multi-Institutional Strategy for Structural-Constructivist Psychopathology.
items.abstract: The Core Emotion Framework (CEF) is a structural constructivist model of human affect that proposes ten irreducible psychological operators distributed across a tripartite Head–Heart–Gut architecture. This paper outlines a comprehensive clinical translation strategy designed to empirically validate the CEF as a transdiagnostic model of emotional regulation and psychopathology. Drawing on contemporary process based, constructivist, and interoceptive research paradigms, the framework reconceptualizes emotional health as Emotional Flexibility—the capacity to dynamically modulate operator activation—and defines psychopathology as Emotional Rigidity, characterized by operator fusion, suppression, and disrupted transition states. The manuscript maps the CEF onto leading international research programs, identifying ten institutions whose methodological strengths align with the framework’s psychometric, neurobiological, and clinical validation needs. A three phase empirical roadmap is proposed: (1) confirmatory factor analysis and scale validation of the ten operator model; (2) neurobiological and interoceptive profiling of operator activation using fMRI, autonomic monitoring, and ecological elicitation; and (3) targeted clinical trials evaluating CEF based interventions for anxiety patterns, personality disorders, and trauma related dysregulation. This multi institutional strategy positions the CEF as a unified, mechanistic blueprint for advancing structural constructivist psychopathology and developing precision based emotional interventions.

items.title: Changing the Philosophical Environment - Ontological Reframing and the Dissolution of the Measurement Problem in the Double-Slit Experiment.
items.abstract: This article develops a metatheoretical claim about a specific class of intellectual operations in foundational physics. It distinguishes between solving an interpretive problem in its own terms, replacing the theory that generated the problem, and dissolving the problem by displacing the ontological presupposition that gave it its shape. The third operation, which the article calls ontological reframing, is defended as a legitimate kind of contribution to foundational debate and exhibited at length on the double-slit experiment and the measurement problem. The article does not propose a new physical theory, a new mathematical formalism, or a new interpretation of quantum mechanics in the standard sense. It argues instead that the canonical puzzle rests on an ontological presupposition that the formalism itself does not require: that a physical object exists in the real domain, travels from source to detector, and is then measured. The formalism requires state assignment, preparation, unitary evolution, and measurement; it does not by itself require the substance-like reading of the state as a continuously existing object in the real domain. In the OTS reading, before measurement there is no real-domain particle in transit. There is an idempotent configuration in the dual domain: the source, as a real-domain device, fixes the structural conditions of that configuration; the apparatus determines the admissible modes of its valence; and the detector induces the only irreversible passage from dual to real. The click, trace, or mark on the screen is therefore not the final position of a travelling particle, but the first real-domain event of the quantum entity. The article situates the move within Transformative Semalgebraic Ontology (OTS), but treats that framework as data rather than as something to be defended. What is defended here is the operation itself: a metatheoretical change of philosophical environment in which some questions cease to ask for closure.

items.title: The Observation Operator: Presence as a Developmental Force.
items.abstract: The Observation Operator: Presence as a Developmental Force introduces a structural framework in which observation is treated not as passive perception but as an active developmental operator. Organisms inhabit manifolds—structured spaces of affordances, sensitivities, and expectations—that are continuously reshaped by the presence of others. These manifolds extend outward through waves and disturbances that propagate through the shared medium, enabling indirect detection across distance. -/- The paper formalizes the observation operator as a mapping that collapses, redirects, or stabilizes an organism’s manifold when another system becomes detectable, whether through direct sensory contact or indirect wave‑mediated coupling. Presence acts as a developmental force by constraining possibilities, stabilizing patterns, and redirecting trajectories across ecological time. -/- The framework unifies developmental psychology, ecological interaction, and systems theory by showing how organisms co‑develop through manifold coupling, how coherence fields emerge from collective synchronization, and how breakdown occurs under incoherent conditions. The observation operator provides a general structure for understanding how biological, cognitive, and social systems are shaped by the forces that watch them.
