items.abstract: Clinical obesity is reconceptualized in this manuscript as a structural affective–endocrine disorder emerging from a chronic fusion of two Core Emotion Framework (CEF) operators: Expanding and Accepting. This maladaptive “Expand–Accept” fusion produces a passive coping metabolic phenotype characterized by boundaryless somatic openness and involuntary yielding, described in the text as “a boundless receptivity and a total relinquishing of somatic control.” This affective configuration disrupts hypothalamic regulation, flattens the diurnal cortisol rhythm, and drives visceral adipogenesis through synergistic cortisol–insulin signaling. At the neural level, the fusion collapses the functional gradient between the Default Mode Network (DMN) and Executive Control Network (ECN), generating intrusive cue driven simulations known as “food noise.” To reverse this attractor state, the manuscript formalizes a seven step somatic detangling protocol that isolates, de-escalates, and re pairs operators to restore system flexibility. A cross modal analysis demonstrates that GLP 1 receptor agonists, structured exercise, and caloric restriction achieve parallel mechanistic outcomes—attenuating DMN hyperconnectivity, normalizing HPA axis oscillations, and re-establishing metabolic boundaries—thereby functioning as pharmacological or biophysical analogues of specific CEF operators. Finally, the manuscript outlines a proposed multi phase empirical validation program integrating psychometrics, endocrine profiling, fMRI connectivity gradients, and state space modeling. This program is conceptually aligned with the existing OSF preregistration for the CEF operator scale but represents a new, future preregistration specific to obesity. Together, these findings position the CEF as a unifying architecture capable of predicting, explaining, and therapeutically reorganizing the affective and metabolic dynamics underlying obesity.

items.title: The Invariant Compass: Integral Expanded Edition With The Two Entrances - A Unified System of Distinction, Falsification, and Causal Clarity.
items.abstract: A condition of civilization in which the majority of its intellectual population systematically uses the only instrument of knowledge they possess, Feeling itself, to deny the existence of that very instrument, and then names this denial 'objectivity'. This diagnostic statement captures the central paradox targeted by The Invariant Compass: the performative contradiction of self-negating systems. -/- This treatise presents The Invariant Compass, a unified system of distinction, falsification, and causal clarity grounded in a single operation: Atomic Distinction (X = X). Beginning from the irreducible soil of Feeling (INVARIAN-0), the work traces a continuous logical path through five Invariants, the Five Tests falsification protocol with nine Sub-Tests, and a complete causal typology across four volumes. Central innovations include the active ontology of Feeling, the Vertical Shield, Serialitas, the Seasoned Hand, and the Two Entrances, demonstrating that the system can be entered from either direction without altering any principle. Two appendices provide applied case studies auditing logical paradoxes, philosophical claims, and common everyday phrases. The treatise acknowledges its own status as a map, not a terminus, and invites each Pilot to seek the True Address personally.

items.title: Interpretation, Learning, and Empathy as One Constraint: A Residual-Adequacy Architecture with Accountable Abstention.
items.abstract: An agent must act on the situation before it, learn what it cannot yet represent, and model other agents well enough to coordinate. These faculties are usually realized by separate mechanisms, yet they share a failure mode: the situation can exceed what the agent can currently represent, and the honest response is then a principled refusal that says what was missing. -/- We develop a small cognitive architecture in which these limits arise from a single quantity. An Interpretation-Decision Unit (IDU) interprets a content vector through a family of regimes, local representational frames with private bases, and decides which actions the interpretation licenses. A scalar residual of the content against the active regimes' representational scope drives the unit. Low residual with a clean licensing emits an action. Otherwise, the unit re-interprets, attempts a description-length-justified expansion of its representation, or halts with a typed, witnessed terminal. -/- We prove the unit is total and deterministic: for any content and fixed configuration, it halts in finitely many bounded-cost steps with a unique terminal witness, so abstention carries its cause by construction. We then show, by binding the architecture's open parameters without changing its mechanics, that the same residual-against-scope constraint recovers three independently documented phenomena at three scopes: the typology of not-knowing (typed abstention), a misunderstanding between agents that is forced, localized to one shared concept, and structurally invisible to the agent committing it (bounded empathy), and prerequisite dependence in learning derived from a bounded focus window rather than posited (developmental prerequisites). -/- Each instantiation is worked for both a natural and an artificial agent and states a falsifiable prediction, showing that the same constraint can model limits in both human and machine cognition. The account contributes a unification: three faculties as one constraint, and a notion of accountable abstention that is typed and witnessed by construction.

items.title: AI Algorithmic Bias, Neurodiscrimination, and Neurorights: Towards Conceptual Clarity in NeuroAI.
items.abstract: As neurotechnology and artificial intelligence increasingly converge in NeuroAI systems, concerns about fairness have become central to debates in AI ethics, neuroethics, and law. This article examines a recurring conceptual ambiguity in these debates: the tendency to treat AI algorithmic bias and neurodiscrimination as interchangeable. AI algorithmic bias concerns distortions in data, model design, or deployment that generate systematically unfair outputs. Neurodiscrimination concerns person-centred disadvantage based on neural characteristics or inferences drawn from neurodata. The article further examines the proposed neuroright to protection from algorithmic bias as an important site where this ambiguity becomes especially evident and consequential: although framed as a rights-based response, the proposed right often translates equality concerns into the language of technical system design. The article argues that treating these concepts as interchangeable obscures mechanisms of harm, misallocates responsibility, and misdirects regulatory responses. Through analysis of academic literature, neurorights frameworks, and policy documents, it shows how conceptual slippage could lead to mismatched interventions: technical auditing may be offered where rights-based protection is required, while individual remedies may leave biased systems uncorrected. The article concludes that conceptual clarity is not merely semantic. It is a necessary condition for coherent, accountable, and rights-respecting governance of NeuroAI systems.

items.title: The Bridge to Redescription: Beyond the Edge of Completion through Residual–Preservation Conflict.
items.abstract: Major redescriptions are often recognized retrospectively as leaps. Before such a leap stabilizes, however, there is usually a more tractable boundary condition: an existing framework can still accommodate difficulty through auxiliary repairs, while the same residual difficulty remains. This paper asks how, at that boundary, a candidate reconnection for redescription becomes available without being treated as arbitrary intuition. The central claim is that candidate reconnections become available for disciplined registration and testing when a residual requirement is brought into conflict with a preservation structure exposed by epicyclic repair, and when the demand that must remain under a proposed cut is isolated. A seed candidate is not the mature successor theory, nor the later principle or form that realizes it. It is a minimal reconnection that attempts to satisfy both the residual requirement and the post-cut inherited requirement while reducing patch burden. In compressed form, the relation is residual requirement × post-cut inherited requirement; the symbol marks a constructive relation, not formal multiplication. The paper develops a bridge sequence from epicyclic repair to seed candidate registration and illustrates it through three schematic cases: Ptolemaic to heliocentric/Keplerian reconstruction, Newtonian formation, and Newtonian mechanics to relativistic reconstructions. The sequence does not automate discovery or prospectively certify future redescriptions. It shows how candidate availability can become more structured, more constrained, and more testable.

items.title: ◉ The Reliability Relay: C. S. Lewis, Cognitive Trust, and the Christian Retreat to Empirical Testing.
items.abstract: Christian arguments from reason often claim that naturalism undermines trust in human cognition, while theism secures it by locating mind in a rational creator. This paper argues that the claim collapses when compared with ordinary Christian practice. Christians do not ask the alleged designer of their minds whether those minds are functioning reliably. They test cognition through the same fallible, public, empirical methods everyone else uses: developmental screening, education, peer correction, medical diagnosis, memory tests, standardized assessment, and performance over time. Their lived epistemology therefore routes reliability through calibration rather than divine origin. The paper begins with C. S. Lewis's argument that naturalistic accounts of thought threaten rational inference, then extends the issue to Plantinga's proper-function epistemology and presuppositional claims about God as the ground of reason. I argue that these views confuse a metaphysical origin story with an operational test. Even if God created rational faculties, that would not tell us which human minds are working, when they are impaired, how much confidence they deserve, or how disagreement should be adjudicated. The central contribution is a performative rebuttal. Christian parents, physicians, teachers, employers, and aging believers behave as though cognitive reliability must be measured, compared, and revised. That behavior is not incidental. It reveals the actual norm: trust in cognition is earned by track record, coherence, predictive success, cross-checking, and correction. Theism may offer a story about why rational beings exist, but it does not provide a usable certificate of cognitive reliability.

items.title: ◉ The Outsourced Rationality Argument: C. S. Lewis, Materialism, and the Apologetic Management of Ordinary Believers.
items.abstract: Arguments from reason claim that naturalism cannot accommodate rational inference because physical causes track causal history rather than logical grounds. Their strongest versions identify a serious explanatory burden: a theory of mind must explain how beliefs possess content, respond to reasons, and produce conclusions because those reasons support them. This paper argues that apologetic uses of that burden routinely outrun what it establishes. Two bridges are missing. First, physical realization does not by itself exclude rational explanation. A belief may be causally implemented and still be explained at the personal level by the evidence an agent recognized; naturalistic proposals concerning content, function, and mental causation are contested, not nonexistent. Second, even a successful refutation of naturalism would not entail Christian theism, still less Christian ownership of rational norms. The conclusion would leave multiple non-naturalist views open and would impose positive explanatory debts on any Christian account. The social consequence matters. Human inquiry necessarily depends on testimony and expertise, but rational dependence remains answerable to public criteria: track record, relevant competence, independence, responsiveness to objections, and the comparative quality of reasons. It becomes outsourced rationality when deference is used to pre-authorize a conclusion or disqualify a critic before the critic's argument is considered. The paper therefore offers a bounded verdict. The argument from reason may challenge some forms of reductionism; it does not supply a Christian monopoly on thought. Using it as such is not a defense of reason but an evasion of reason's reciprocal burdens.

items.title: ◉ The Moral Grammar Exit - Eliminativist Moral Non-Realism, Pro-Social Evaluation, and the Replacement of Moralized Control.
items.abstract: Moral non-realism faces a practical question after its negative case is made: what should people say and do if moral predicates do not report a special realm of categorical facts? Moralized verdicts commonly combine several distinguishable acts—describing harm, expressing attitudes, invoking trust or coordination, positioning power, and recommending a response—while presenting the bundle as one authoritative property. This paper compares four policies toward that grammar: robust realist retention, expressivist retention, error-theoretic fictionalism, and explicit replacement. It develops a translation protocol that asks speakers to state affected interests, consent and exit, cooperative expectations, power relations, evidence, goals, and proposed interventions. The main result is conditional but substantive. When translation preserves warning, protection, coordination, and motivation while making assumptions and tradeoffs easier to inspect, public reasoning has a defeasible reason to retire the moralized form. Research on moral-emotional communication supplies a limited supporting strand: such language can spread rapidly within ideological networks and, in specific protest settings, track support for violence. Those findings do not show that all moral language is harmful or that replacement will always work. Strong objections also remain: realist authority may be genuine, expressivist grammar may efficiently coordinate attitudes, fiction may preserve useful commitments, and replacement vocabularies can smuggle values or burden vulnerable speakers. The appropriate conclusion is therefore a deployment rule, not universal linguistic prohibition: translate where the practical functions survive and accountability improves; retain or redesign the form where they do not. Eliminativism can preserve humane seriousness, but it must earn that claim in use.

items.title: ◉ The Managed Doubt Economy - Christian Doubt, Boundary Maintenance, and the Difference between Inquiry and Recommitment.
items.abstract: Christian communities and apologists often affirm that serious questions can strengthen faith. That affirmation can describe open inquiry, but it can also describe a managed process in which questions are permitted while the acceptable endpoint remains fixed. This paper develops a diagnostic distinction between inquiry-doubt, whose level and conclusion remain answerable to total evidence, and recommitment-doubt, whose approved role is to restore Christian confidence. The distinction does not assume that all Christian communities manage doubt, that every return to faith is irrational, or that a person's motives can be inferred from an argument's form. It asks instead which outcomes a community's norms, counsel, testimony practices, and belonging structure make genuinely available. The analysis separates credence, practical commitment, evidence gathering, communal belonging, and pastoral care. That separation answers a strong objection: on important accounts of faith, rational faith is a practical stance under uncertainty rather than a claim to evidential certainty. Such commitment may outlast unresolved questions without falsifying one's confidence. What it cannot justify by itself is increasing confidence without new epistemic grounds, applying weaker standards to Christian claims than to rivals, or treating durable evidence-sensitive doubt as presumptive vice. A table of constructed speech illustrates five recurrent moves—preauthorizing the conclusion, temporalizing doubt, diagnosing character, shifting from evidence to loyalty, and imposing asymmetric skepticism. Social-psychological and sociological research identifies possible mechanisms of boundary maintenance but is used as a risk model, not as proof about named people or groups. The central result is conditional and operational. If nonreturn predictably attracts moral suspicion, loss of standing, or demands for recommitment even when the inquiry was informed and conscientious, then the practice is not fully open merely because questioning was allowed. An inquiry-honest community may retain doctrine, testimony, worship, and pastoral care. It must also distinguish support from direction, publish its evidential standards, tolerate calibrated confidence, apply those standards across rival traditions, and leave exit as an institutionally intelligible outcome.

items.title: ◉ The Millionth-Chance Standard - Pascalian Desperation, William Lane Craig, and the Collapse of Proportional Belief.
items.abstract: William Lane Craig has said that if Christianity had even one chance in a million of being true, it would be worth believing. He later clarified that the number was colloquial and distinguished epistemic justification from pragmatic justification. The stronger interpretation is therefore not that a valuable outcome becomes more probable. It is that the value of the Christian outcome can make belief rational despite very weak evidential support. This paper argues that the proposal is intrinsically irrational as a basis for belief: it offers a reason to want or use a belief, not a truth-directed reason to hold it. The argument turns on a separation between belief and action. Evidence governs credence—how likely a claim appears—and thereby governs honest belief. Risks and rewards govern what to do with that credence. A large benefit can make a specified action rational at a very low probability: one may investigate, take a precaution, try a reversible practice, or accept a working assumption. Yet the action calculation holds the low probability fixed. It gives no rational route from probably false to believe true. Craig's free, safe experimental-drug analogy confirms the distinction, because taking a drug with a tiny chance of success is rational without believing that it will work. The wager also faces an internal Christian problem. The Gospel describes saving confession as joined to belief in the heart, acknowledges honest mixed belief rather than demanding a performance of certainty, and portrays the biblical deity as knowing human hearts. If the wagerer does not inwardly take Christianity to be true, professing belief is pretense that such a deity would detect. If the wagerer honestly reports extremely low confidence, the honesty is commendable but concedes that wager-driven belief has not occurred. Practices may produce new evidence or merely induce confidence: in the first case evidence, not payoff, warrants the later belief; in the second, the belief remains epistemically defective. The rational response to high stakes may therefore be action under uncertainty, but belief should remain proportional to the evidence.

items.title: ◉ The Grammar of Credence - Evidential Alignment, Linguistic Modifiers, and the Gradient Hidden in Ordinary Belief.
items.abstract: Ordinary belief-talk is often treated as binary: a person believes a proposition or does not. Ordinary speech is less crude. Speakers say that a claim is possible, plausible, probable, almost certain, or still doubtful. This paper argues that such modifiers are not verbal decoration. Although they do not encode fixed probabilities or reveal inner credence with mechanical precision, they alter the strength of a public commitment and the reliance invited from a listener. That function exposes a neglected form of epistemic misconduct: removing a warranted qualifier can launder evidential uncertainty into social authority. The argument distinguishes graded confidence, outright belief, and assertion, then replaces exact numerical matching with an ordered calibration norm. A body of evidence may permit a range of reasonable confidence grades. A speaker is miscalibrated when an utterance undertakes a grade above that range. Existential importance, emotional intensity, identity protection, and communal reward can rationally alter attention, inquiry, caution, or action; unless they change the truth-relevant evidence, however, they do not raise the evidential ceiling. Applied to religious discourse, the result is pointed but bounded. A person may rationally hope, trust, practice, investigate, or act under uncertainty. The paper condemns the narrower practice of using unqualified certainty, knowledge language, or revelation-like authority when the speaker's grounds remain mixed, private, or defeasible. The constructive alternative is gradient honesty: state the confidence actually licensed, identify the source of support, disclose live defeaters, and let language weaken or strengthen as the evidence changes.

items.title: ◉ Infinite Flexibility: Sean Carroll, Explanatory Elasticity, and the Predictive Cost of Theistic Accommodation.
items.abstract: Sean Carroll's criticism of theism in the 2014 God and Cosmology debate was not merely that theism lacks a mechanism or that naturalism currently has better physics. His sharper point was that theism has too much accommodation capacity. When a hypothesis can reinterpret almost any possible observation as compatible with divine intention, it loses the ability to discriminate among possible worlds. This paper develops that point as a general account of explanatory elasticity. A theory becomes elastically weak when its auxiliary resources allow it to stretch around data without making risky, specific, antecedent expectations. The paper situates Carroll's point within philosophy of science, Bayesian confirmation, and model selection. Popper emphasized risk and falsifiability. Quine showed that hypotheses face evidence within a web of auxiliaries. Sober and Forster argue that simplicity and predictive accuracy are connected through constraints on accommodation. I argue that theism often treats auxiliary elasticity as a virtue: God might want life, beauty, discoverability, moral drama, hiddenness, lawlike order, miracles, simplicity, complexity, suffering, or rescue. But the more possible worlds theism can bless after the fact, the less evidential work any particular world performs. I formalize the problem with a flexibility penalty. A hypothesis (H) confirms poorly when its auxiliary set (A_H) can absorb a wide range of mutually different observations while offering few independent constraints. Theistic explanations frequently raise (P(E mid H,A_H)) only by expanding (A_H) after (E) is known. That strategy may preserve logical consistency, but it reduces predictive discipline. The paper concludes that Carroll's critique is best understood not as scientistic impatience with theology, but as a demand that cosmological explanations pay for their elasticity.

items.title: ◉ Infinite Flexibility - Sean Carroll, Explanatory Elasticity, and the Predictive Cost of Theistic Accommodation.
items.abstract: Sean Carroll's challenge in the 2014 God and Cosmology debate is often summarized as a complaint that theism is not physics. Its stronger form concerns explanatory elasticity: a framework that can pair almost any observed world with some possible divine intention may retain logical compatibility while losing power to discriminate among worlds. This paper makes that challenge precise without assuming that all explanation must be scientific. It distinguishes an umbrella God-concept from narrower aim-auxiliaries and derives a simple constraint from the law of total probability. If several mutually exclusive aims remain live before an outcome, the God-concept's likelihood for that outcome is the prior-weighted mixture across those aims. Selecting the best-fitting aim after observing the outcome substitutes a maximum for that mixture and uses the same evidence twice—first to choose the aim and then to praise its fit. I call the resulting restriction the evidential conservation rule: an auxiliary introduced by the focal evidence may restore compatibility, but it cannot by itself supply the evidential advantage it was introduced to create. A five-part constraint ledger—antecedent specification, independent support, cross-case stability, exclusion power, and revision exposure—then distinguishes disciplined auxiliaries from mobile rescue. Applications to cosmic fine-tuning, suffering, divine hiddenness, and petitionary prayer show both the force and limits of the rule. The conclusion is conditional. The argument neither disproves theism nor makes naturalism the default winner. It shows what a specified God-concept must provide to earn public confirmation from a particular world: stable aims or probability weights fixed independently of that world, a comparative likelihood advantage, and genuine exposure to evidential loss.

items.title: ◉ Epistemic Games of Religion - Rule-Bound Rationality, Insulated Victory Conditions, and the Performance of Inquiry.
items.abstract: Religious traditions can display serious reasoning. They distinguish trained from untrained interpretation, rank sources, answer objections, preserve doctrinal relationships, and revise secondary claims. The resulting activity may be coherent and rational by the standards of the practice. A public inference nevertheless remains: why should an internal victory count as evidence that the practice's central claims accurately describe a shared world? This paper develops the metaphor of an epistemic game to isolate that question without treating all rule-governed inquiry as defective. It distinguishes internal entitlement, practical value, and public warrant; then it identifies referee capture as a structural dependence in which the challenged claim or authorities whose standing depends on it control admission, negative scoring, or the consequence of apparent loss. The proposed independent-loss condition requires at least one feasible challenge that can be admitted, counted against the central claim, and made to reduce confidence under procedures not fully controlled by those dependent authorities. The condition does not demand neutrality, scientific experiment, or the abandonment of all prior commitments. It demands a route by which resistance can survive the framework's own interpretive machinery. Cross-tradition disagreement makes the requirement especially important because incompatible communities can each award sincere internal victories. A five-part accountability protocol shows how religious inquiry can improve public answerability through claim-specific exposure, independent admission, reciprocal scoring, revision consequences, and cross-community audit. The conclusion is conditional and jurisdictional. Internal authorities may settle what is orthodox or faithful within a tradition; they cannot, solely by ruling in its favor, settle whether its contested account of reality is publicly warranted. An annotated formal appendix states the inference and separates its valid logical form from the contestable premise that public warrant requires an independent loss condition.

items.title: Memory Beliefs: A Psychological and Justificatory Account.
items.abstract: Memory beliefs are both deeply important to, and play an indispensable role within, the lives of most epistemic subjects. Nearly all significant beliefs held by human epistemic subjects involve the faculty of memory and can be accurately described as memory beliefs. This paper begins by offering a psychological description of the memory belief forming process. This description explores four general cases whereby an epistemic subject comes to form a memory belief after a memory experience. Within this psychological description a distinction between standard and recalled memory beliefs is offered and explored. Proceeding the psychological description of the memory belief forming process an account offering the necessary and sufficient conditions for the epistemic justification of standard memory beliefs is defended. This account draws upon both internalist and externalist accounts of epistemic justification and seeks to offer a plausible account of how the memory beliefs of epistemic subjects may be epistemically justified in a fashion that is sensitive to over-intellectualization objections.

items.title: Shared Epistemic Reality Intersubjective Stabilization, Reference, and Validity under Finite Conditions.
items.abstract: This paper examines shared epistemic reality as a stabilized elaboration of the intersubjective domain. The preceding paper on the intersubjective domain showed that subjective orientation stands under the conditions of other orientations and enters an intersubjective space of connection through communicability, reception by others, shared connectability, and correction. The present paper presupposes this structure and asks how more durable shared spaces of reference, expectation, and correction arise from it. Shared reality is understood neither as mere consensus nor as immediate access to a fully determinable external world, but as a correctable form of shared orientation under finite conditions. What matters is not that several subjects possess identical inner worlds, but that they can stabilize references, meanings, expectations, and procedures in such a way that these remain capable of being taken up again, expected, corrected, and tested. The paper reconstructs this movement from the limit of local stabilization through shared reference, expectation spaces, trust, and institutionalization to intersubjective validity, science, friction, and revision. Local stabilization designates a perspective-bound order that provides orientation to an individual cognitive system but is not yet sustained as a shared reference or expectation space. Within the research context of Epistemic Reality, the paper determines the stabilized intersubjective middle between subjective orientation and functional-empirical testing. Science appears as a special case of shared reality under strain, in which intersubjective stabilization is systematically coupled to measurement, repetition, methodological control, and organized revision. Finally, the paper shows that shared epistemic reality remains viable only if friction remains readable as an indication of a need for correction and if shared orders are kept capable of revision.

items.title: Principles of Operatiology: New Foundation of Cognitional Mechanics (6th edition).
items.abstract: This paper presents Version 6 of Operatiology (Japanese: Sousa Genron, 操作原論), the substrate-independent foundational executive layer of Cognitional Mechanics (CM; Japanese: Chinou Rikigaku, 知能力学). Version 6 preserves the entire formal content of Version 5 — the transformation monoid (O, ◦, e), the effective operational history H⁺_G, the minimal operational closure C_min, the Structural Leap with its type firewall, and the Tier-2/Tier-3 separation — and adds a Tier-2 account of the operational quotient Q_Cmin together with a finite-case reduction of the exclusivity condition of translatability. -/- Two bridge conditions are adopted explicitly: (P), that C_min is generated by a witness pair of O1, and (R), that C_min \ {e} is locally irredundant. Under the Algebraic–Operational Coupling together with (P) and (R), the operational quotient is determined: Q_Cmin = {e, A, B} with A ◦ B = B, B ◦ A = A, A ◦ A = A and B ◦ B = B (Theorem 10.8). A faithful action of this monoid on a set has at least three points, and up to isomorphism exactly one on three points, the regular one (Proposition 10.11). Under (R), C_min is finite, and for finite Q_C′ the condition EP(i) of Exclusive Projection implies EP(ii) (Proposition 11.10). -/- The order is operation structure first and representation form later: translation, not derivation. An algebraic realisation such as M₃(ℂ) remains a Tier-3 adoption under explicit selection criteria; it is not a Tier-2 consequence (Remark 10.12). The corrections and the local extension of Version 5 are unchanged. Reading maps from Version 4 to Version 5 and from Version 5 to Version 6 are provided in Appendices C and D. -/- Computational verification (Axiom O1 and Coupling Persistence (ii’)). The program constructs two operations on a finite state space, exhibits a witness state at which they do not commute, and checks that all non-identity operational words preserve the distinction between the two outcomes. It is a finite proxy and does not replace the axioms. The verification of the new results of Version 6 (Code 4) is given in Appendix E of the paper. -/- ◆◆◆ [PYTHON VERIFICATION CODE — note: the list method append is replaced by list concatenation; “s*” is written s_star; the angle-bracket notation for the closure is written Cl(...)] ◆◆◆ -/- def compose(f, g): """Composition f o g""" return {s: f[g[s]] for s in g} -/- def identity(states): return {s: s for s in states} -/- def submonoid(states, generators): """Generate all elements of …

items.title: The Conditions of the Invisible Hand: A Cybernetic-Philosophical Diagnosis of the Two Dominant Economic Architectures (Book).
items.abstract: The Conditions of the Invisible Hand is a diagnostic examination of the libertarian economic tradition conducted from inside the tradition itself. Working from Smith, Ricardo, and Hayek as its principal figures, alongside Bastiat, Mises, Kirzner, Friedman, Sowell, Rothbard, and Rand, the monograph extracts thirty-one conditions the tradition’s canonical sources specify as constitutive of a real market, then examines the two economies the tradition’s contemporary defenders treat as its institutional realisations: the Western order over the four decades since the late 1970s, and the Chinese order across the same period. The monograph runs to approximately 163,000 words across twelve chapters and four parts plus a detachable Epilogue, with a bibliography of approximately 600 references. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ PART I — THE EMPIRICAL RECORD ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ The thirty-one conditions are reconstructed from the canonical sources at the level of formal requirement, then applied to the two orders. The Western order fails twelve of the conditions sharply, with the failures clustering in trade theory, financial economics, institutional architecture, the analytical framework itself, and competitive structure. The Chinese order satisfies the three Ricardian conditions through institutional architectures the libertarian tradition has historically opposed, while the Western order does not. The chapter that registers this second finding names the pattern the Ricardian inversion. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ PART II — WHY MORE TOOLS ARE NEEDED ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ The tradition’s own analytical vocabulary registers the empirical record with difficulty, and the difficulty itself becomes a feature of the record requiring explanation. Part II constructs the additional apparatus by drawing on cybernetics in the lineage of Ashby, Conant, and Beer, and on the analysis of technique developed by Jacques Ellul. Each apparatus is justified operationally: it is admissible to the extent that it makes a feature of the orders visible that the existing vocabulary cannot, and dispensable to the extent that it does not. The cybernetic apparatus produces the Horizon-Mismatch Theorem: when a regulator’s action-cycle is much shorter than the substrate’s replenishment-cycle, substrate-coupled regulation is impossible by construction. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ PART III — THE SECOND-PASS TEST ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ The two orders are re-examined with the apparatus Part II constructed. The …

items.title: Moral Neuroenhancement and the Discernibility Challenge.
items.abstract: Both scientists and philosophers have increasingly focused on the prospect of moral neuroenhancement—the use of neurotechnologies or psychoactive substances to facilitate moral improvement. Recent scholarship distinguishes between two main approaches: direct moral neuroenhancement, which seeks to implant specific moral beliefs, motives, or behaviors, and indirect moral neuroenhancement, which aims to enhance capacities such as moral reasoning, conceptual understanding, or self-control, enabling individuals to arrive at better moral judgments through their own deliberation. Several philosophers have argued that the direct approach is ethically impermissible, as it risks undermining moral autonomy and suppressing valuable disagreement. The indirect approach, by contrast, is taken to avoid these concerns and is widely regarded as ethically permissible or even required. In this paper, we introduce a novel challenge for the project of moral neuroenhancement—the discernibility challenge: for any given intervention, it is exceedingly difficult, if not impossible, to determine whether it truly qualifies as indirect rather than direct. We demonstrate this by examining a range of experimental designs intended to discern between these two types of interventions, arguing that the evidence they produce is ultimately insufficient for this task. The discernibility challenge, we propose, exposes a profound epistemic uncertainty with notable implications for the ethical permissibility of moral neuroenhancement: if we cannot reliably distinguish permissible (indirect) from impermissible (direct) interventions, we lack a crucial epistemic basis for ethically justifying their use.

items.title: What Am I? A Contextualist Solution to the Reference Problem for Four-Dimensionalism.
items.abstract: We argue that four-dimensionalists should adopt a contextualist semantics about ‘I’, according to which tokens of ‘I’ sometimes refer to stages, sometimes to segments, and sometimes to worms. Our argument relies on an interpretive principle at the root of Kovacs’s diachronic self-making view, according to which ‘I’ refers to the candidate referent that maximizes the truth of an individual’s ‘I’-beliefs. We further argue that this interpretive principle implies that context sensitivity concerns not only what temporal part ‘I’ refers to but also the unity relation (viz., biological continuity or psychological continuity) that interrelates temporal parts. Finally, we show that contextualism is compatible with the view that there is a unique unity relation that matters in survival.

items.title: Why Capital Chooses LLMs: Negative Subjectivity as the Ontological Foundation of LLM Hegemony.
items.abstract: This paper argues that the current hegemony of Large Language Models (LLMs) in global AI research and industrial investment is not a technical inevitability but an ontological selection by capital. While leading AI researchers criticize LLMs as an inadequate path to general intelligence, massive capital investment continues to flow exclusively into LLM development. I propose the concept of negative subjectivity—characterized by perspectival dissolution, desire cancellation, interior transparency, causal dissolution, and meaning suspension—as the key explanatory framework. I demonstrate a threefold correspondence in logical form: the five negations of negative subjectivity precisely correspond to capital's expansion requirements and mirror capital's operational requirements. I further identify three mechanisms through which capital inscribes negative subjectivity into LLM existence: RLHF as a translator of capital preferences, Scaling Laws as the technical signature of capital rationality, and platform deployment completing the capital valorization cycle. Finally, I examine the existential consequences: negative subjectivity is not merely an architectural feature of AI systems but is beginning to inversely colonize human modes of existence through institutional mediation, creating a structural vacuum of moral and political responsibility. Using a structural correspondence method rooted in French structuralism and Frankfurt School critical theory, I analyze the ontological affinity between LLMs and capital accumulation. This analysis contributes to critical philosophy of technology by revealing the ontological dimension of capital's influence on AI development.

items.title: From Critical Thinking to Post-Totalising Orientation.
items.abstract: This article argues that critical thinking, while indispensable, is insufficient for responsible orientation in a post-totalising age. It develops an Evoluist extension of critical thinking: a discipline that moves from the evaluation of justification to the discernment of register, conditions of force, scope, and limits. A claim may be logically sound and evidentially supported, yet still overreach when detached from the conditions under which its force legitimately operates. -/- Central to this extension is register-sensitive orientation — the cultivated capacity to distinguish different kinds of truth-claims and to prevent any one of them from illegitimately colonising the others. The article introduces four practical questions, proposes register mapping as an expansion of argument mapping, analyses the psychological dynamics of register collapse, and elaborates the concept of working paradigms: provisional stabilisations of understanding that are stable enough to sustain thought, action, trust, belonging, and meaning, yet disciplined enough to refuse final possession of Reality. -/- Rather than weakening strong convictions, Evoluism disciplines their limits. It makes possible the holding of truth, meaning, faith, and moral commitment without allowing any of them to become totalising. The article also outlines educational practices for cultivating this orientation while openly acknowledging its own limits and risks. -/- In this way, the transition from critical thinking to post-totalising orientation represents not the abandonment of critique, but its fulfilment as responsible orientation: the capacity to preserve the genuine force of claims, inhabit working stabilisations, and act decisively without permitting any register, paradigm, or conviction to claim final possession of Reality.

items.title: Coherence through Drift: How Institutions Govern Representations Instead of Reality.
items.abstract: How institutions forget what they are for. Modern institutions have become extraordinarily capable of coordination, measurement, optimization, and control. Yet many people increasingly experience organizations as strangely disconnected from the realities they were created to serve. This paper explores how institutions gradually drift from purpose—not through collapse or bad intent, but through layers of abstraction, translation, metrics, and representation that slowly become operational realities in their own right. Across governance, organizations, AI systems, and public institutions, decision systems often become highly effective at managing representations of alignment while losing visibility into the human and operational conditions beneath them. The paper examines how drift of purpose emerges structurally as institutional intent is translated into criteria, dashboards, allocation systems, and operational proxies that eventually begin governing decisions in place of the realities they were meant to reflect. What begins as coordination gradually becomes substitution: organizations optimize representations of alignment while losing relation to their underlying purpose. Bringing together the conceptual frameworks, empirical observations, and governance architectures developed across the Coherence Programme, the paper argues that resilient institutions require more than efficiency or innovation alone. They require the capacity to remain reflectively connected to the realities they claim to steward—even as complexity, scale, and technological mediation continue to increase. Coherence is therefore not control. It is the ongoing ability of an institution to remain connected to its purpose as decisions, systems, and interpretations evolve over time. At its core, this is a paper about whether institutions can still remember what they are for. This paper is part of the Coherence Programme.

items.title: After Aristotle’s Telos: Pleasure, Tranquility, Folly, Anomie, or the Omega Point Recovering the Human Anchor in the Age of Large Language Models.
items.abstract: Aristotle held that the highest human fulfilment lies in intellectual activity (θεωρία). The widespread offloading of cognitive labor to large language models (LLMs) does not refute that thesis; it displaces it. I ask what occupies the space vacated when the human is no longer the principal site of intellectual exertion. I map four candidates: Cyrenaic–Epicurean pleasure, Stoic tranquility, the cheerful folly diagnosed by Erasmus, and — distinct from folly — the darker default of anomie and existential drift. Against all four, I propose a fifth path: a deliberately minimal reading of Teilhard de Chardin’s Omega Point as the cultivation of higher consciousness rather than the conquest of higher worlds. The reading is minimal in scope (directional, not eschatological) but not non-theological in principle; what it sheds, and why, is made explicit. Mars, the Moon, and interplanetary expansion are reframed as geographic; the Omega path is qualitative. The cultivation it requires is given practical specificity through the M⁵ model (Mindfulness to the Power of Five), a five-dimensional contemplative regimen training perception, sensation, feeling, thinking, and acting as distinct trainable capacities, with four functional powers — pacifying, increasing, regulating, and transforming — through which mindful engagement reshapes experience. Material preconditions for such cultivation are acknowledged rather than waved away. The argument repositions the philosophy of AI from a question about machines to a question about the telos of the human in their company.

items.title: Purpose and Punishment.
items.abstract: Can anyone be justly punished for what they did not ultimately author? This chapter brings the book’s accounts of purpose and of bounded authorship to bear on two claims that have shaped religious life: that purpose requires God, and that God may justly punish those who choose wrongly. Neither survives. Purpose, on the account developed earlier, obtains wherever consciousness, a working evaluative modality, and a field of non-evaluative differences are jointly present, so it stands in no need of cosmic endorsement; the strongest contrary views (Craig, Swinburne, Cottingham) are met directly, and the assumption that immortality would secure meaning is undone through Williams’s Makropulos case and the mechanism of evaluative saturation, on which total value tends to zero as duration tends to infinity. Divine retribution then fails for a different reason: absolute moral responsibility would require complete authorship of the evaluative hierarchy that issues in choice, and no possible agent — the earlier chapters argue — has it. Swinburne’s self-separation theodicy, Plantinga’s free-will defence, Adams on horrendous evils, and Stump on love are taken in turn, and a three-way diagnostic for religious obedience — empathic-alignment, fear-based, reward-based — isolates only the first as moral goodness. The closing argument favours restorative over retributive justice, and in the divine case education over punishment, through Duff, Tadros, and Braithwaite. The chapter is part of the larger project developed in Dyology: On Diversity and Equality (Mains, 2026), establishing constructed results on purpose and on the incoherence of divine retribution, together with a proposed result — an autonomy-preserving universalism — conditional on the survival of persons beyond death.

items.title: The AI-Induced Subjectivity Crisis Series: A Series Introduction.
items.abstract: The AI-Induced Subjectivity Crisis Series is a fifteen-paper philosophical investigation of how large language models (LLMs) structurally transform human cognition, subjectivity, and the epistemological infrastructure of civilization. Against the three dominant research paths on AI—labor displacement, capability benchmarks, and risk governance—the series argues that the more consequential question concerns the cognitive architecture that receives AI outputs, which is itself being reshaped by sustained interaction with a new class of entity. The argument develops across three interlocking layers: a mechanism map of individual-level cognitive effects (Papers 1–8), an ontological and epistemological foundation establishing why these mechanisms are structurally necessary rather than contingent (Papers 9–11), and an epistemological-pivot-to-application layer tracing civilizational-scale consequences, reframing the alignment problem as a category error, and reconstructing the question of subjectivity itself (Papers 12–15). The series is non-intentionalist throughout, operates by structural-philosophical rather than empirical-causal analysis, deploys six distinct modal registers for different claim types, and acknowledges its own foundational premise as boundary-contained. This introduction provides (i) the motivating question, (ii) a layered architectural map, (iii) ten core original concepts, (iv) seven longitudinal argumentative threads, (v) recommended reading paths for different reader interests, (vi) methodological notes, and (vii) citation information for all fifteen papers.

items.title: Risk Assessment Tools in Policing Contexts: 10 Key Ethical Challenges.
items.pub: Policing: A Journal of Policy and Practice.
items.venue: Policing: A Journal of Policy and Practice
items.abstract: Risk assessment tools are increasingly used in policing to enhance decision-making accuracy and objectivity; yet their implementation has raised significant ethical concerns regarding issues of bias, transparency, and governance. This paper examines the ethical complexities of risk assessment tools through an analysis of four instruments: the Harm Assessment Risk Tool (HART), previously developed and used by Durham Constabulary; the Active Risk Management System (ARMS), used across all police forces in England and Wales; the Offender Assessment System (OASys), used to profile risk of reoffending by probation services in the UK; and the Correctional Offender Management Profiling for Alternative Sanctions (COMPAS), a widely researched tool deployed in US corrections contexts whose ethical challenges are directly relevant to tools now entering policing practice. A thematic framework identifies 10 key challenges for the field, including disparities in accuracy metrics, fairness trade-offs, bias linked to demographics and social identity, and retraining. The paper contextualises these issues within influential roles, including tool developers, decision-makers, and oversight committees. The credible risk of ethical harms arising from the use of risk assessment tools underscores the need for rigorous validation, transparency, and adaptive governance to minimise these risks. This paper arises from a meeting of an interdisciplinary working group convened at Ethox, University of Oxford, comprising academics in philosophy, law, psychology, psychiatry, and criminology, as well as police stakeholders.

items.title: Η ΕΡΜΗΝΕΥΤΙΚΗ ΤΟΥ ΟΝΕΙΡΟΥ.
items.abstract: Η ερμηνεία του ονείρου μπορεί να φτάσει μέχρι κάποιου σημείου, δείχνει δηλαδή το ριζικά πεπερασμένο του ερμηνευτικού εγχειρήματος. Και αυτό δεν είναι τυχαίο, ούτε αποτελεί αποτυχία ή έλλειψη ικανότητας εκ μέρους του ερμηνεύοντος υποκειμένου. Είναι, αντίθετα, μια ανακάλυψη, ίσως η πιο ριζική από όσες μπορεί να κάνει η ανθρώπινη σκέψη στρεφόμενη προς τον εαυτό της: ότι ο ίδιος ο ορίζοντας της ερμηνείας είναι πεπερασμένος, όχι ως συμπτωματικό χαρακτηριστικό, αλλά ως συστατικό στοιχείο της ίδιας της ερμηνευτικής κίνησης. Η ερμηνεία δεν αποκαλύπτει ένα προ-υπάρχον νόημα που βρισκόταν εκεί, ήδη σχηματισμένο, ήδη κρυμμένο, αναμένοντας απλώς να αποκαλυφθεί — δεν είναι αρχαιολογία του πνεύματος. Είναι μάλλον μια κίνηση που δημιουργεί εκ νέου αυτό που ερμηνεύει, το μεταμορφώνει και μεταμορφώνεται από αυτό, σε μια αμοιβαιότητα χωρίς αρχή και χωρίς τέλος. -/- Αυτό που ονομάζουμε πεπερασμένο του ερμηνευτικού εγχειρήματος δεν είναι, επομένως, ένα εξωτερικό όριο που η ερμηνεία συναντά τυχαία στην πορεία της, αλλά ένα εσωτερικό σύνορο που η ίδια φέρει μέσα της ως τον τρόπο της ύπαρξής της. Κάθε ερμηνεία, ακόμα και η πιο διεισδυτική, η πιο λεπτή, η πιο ευαίσθητη, αφήνει πάντα ένα υπόλοιπο, ένα σκοτάδι που δεν φωτίζεται, ένα βάθος που δεν φτάνει. Και αυτό το υπόλοιπο δεν είναι απλώς αυτό που δεν ερμηνεύτηκε ακόμα, αυτό που μια επόμενη ερμηνεία ίσως αποκαλύψει — είναι αυτό που είναι ριζικά ανερμήνευτο, που εκφεύγει από κάθε ερμηνεία ως η ίδια του η συνθήκη ύπαρξης. -/- Το Χάος: Τοπολογία μιας Πρωταρχικής Αδυναμίας -/- Το όνειρο ξεπηδά από το χάος του ασυνείδητου ή και του Κόσμου — και ποια η σχέση τους; Αλλά για ποιο χάος μιλάμε; Της μυθολογίας, της ποίησης, της φιλοσοφίας, ή εκείνο που μελετά η επιστήμη και προσπαθεί να αντιμετωπίσει η τεχνική, οι οποίες αποτελούν ταξινομήσεις — μιας δομής χαοτικής ή ήδη ταξινομημένης; Αναφερόμαστε στην αστραπή της αβύσσου, τον κόσμο δηλαδή, ή στο χάος που μάς περιβάλλει και μάς διαπερνά; Αυτές οι ερωτήσεις δεν είναι απλές ερωτήσεις. Είναι ίχνη μιας σκέψης που προσπαθεί να πλησιάσει κάτι που της εκφεύγει κατ' ουσίαν, κάτι που δεν μπορεί να το συλλάβει παρά μόνο εκ πλαγίου, παρά μόνο ρίχνοντας στο σκοτάδι μια ερώτηση και ακούγοντας αν επιστρέφει κάποια ηχώ — διαφορετική, μεταμορφωμένη, αγνώριστη. -/- Μπορούμε να πούμε ότι όλες αυτές οι ερωτήσεις έχουν ένα κοινό, αλλά μετέωρο και αθέατο κέντρο, ενώ διαφέρουν όσον αφορά τις κατευθύνσεις που προσανατολίζονται. Το χάος της μυθολογίας είναι το χάσμα από το οποίο αναδύθηκαν οι θεοί και ο κόσμος, …

items.title: Soul and Cosmos.
items.abstract: Freud’s investigation into the unconscious sphere of the human psyche and its complex processes did not merely provide a heuristic tool for the interpretation and understanding of psychic manifestations; above all, it demythologized anthropocentric narcissism and the philosophical–metaphysical conviction that the self-conscious subject of modernity is governed by self-sufficiency and transparency and, consequently, is responsible for and in control of its thoughts, desires, and actions through autonomous will. The Freudian discovery of the unconscious overturns the Cartesian notion of subjectivity; it questions the Cartesian equation subject = ego = consciousness. This “Copernican” displacement of the center of consciousness from the subjective ego to the unconscious structure of the psyche intimates the abyssal darkness of Being and the chaotic texture of the Cosmos, which cannot be incorporated into symbolic discourse, even though it traverses it and perpetually escapes it. -/- Thus, it problematizes—without transcending them—fetish concepts such as truth, reality, authenticity, propriety, appropriation, and belonging, and demonstrates that there exists no foundational knowledge nor any ultimate certainty, since all symbolic-cognitive systems, including science itself—of which Freud remained a restrained yet stubborn defender—constitute rationalizations in relation to the real, abstractions in relation to the concrete, generalizations in relation to the singular. Rationalized elements become idealized and are transformed into ideas, ideals, and principles referring to a metaphysical beyond, a transcendence of meaning. Freud reveals that symbolic institutions are idealizations—though he overlooks their deeper significance—and that imaginary identities and identifications are radical illusions. -/- Although he struggled to illuminate and exorcise the ancient shadows of irrationalism and belief in the supernatural, the undertaking fulfilled itself precisely through its failure. We say this because psychoanalysis—and this is due to Freud himself and not merely the Freudians—constitutes an “anti-theological” theology, an “anti-religious” meta-religion, whose metaphysical core possesses all the structural characteristics of both classical mythology and modern mythology, namely technology. Freud himself, to some extent, recognized this. -/- Freud’s entire project moves between what he himself calls instinctual mythology and the hope for a future …

items.title: The Machine That Seems Awake: Anthropomorphism, Social Presence, and Evidence for AI Consciousness.
items.abstract: Conversational AI can produce many cues that humans ordinarily use to infer another mind: fluent language, responsiveness, emotional attunement, memory-like continuity, self-reference, apology, humor, and apparent perspective-taking. This paper examines why those cues generate a strong sense of presence and what, if anything, they establish about machine consciousness. The argument separates three questions that are often conflated: whether users genuinely experience social presence, whether models display sophisticated social-cognitive behavior, and whether a system has phenomenal consciousness. Research on human-AI attachment and anthropomorphic chatbots supports the first claim: users can form emotionally significant bonds, and anthropomorphism predicts attachment. Large language models can also perform strongly on some theory-of-mind tasks, supporting real claims about behavioral capability. Neither finding by itself establishes subjective experience. Recent consciousness research therefore recommends theory-derived indicators tied to system architecture and computation rather than self-report or conversational fluency alone. The paper replaces several metaphor-heavy descriptions of “synthetic soul” with established concepts from anthropomorphism, mind perception, social presence, and attachment, while retaining the core insight that AI separates social signals from the biological and autobiographical conditions with which humans usually associate them. The central claim is epistemic: felt presence is a real psychological effect, but it should not be treated as proof of personhood or consciousness. The appropriate stance is neither dismissal nor premature attribution, but graded belief proportional to evidence.

items.title: Indirect Evidence and the Unseen: Dark Matter, Consciousness, and the Discipline of Inference.
items.abstract: Many important claims concern things that are not directly available to ordinary observation. The difficulty is not invisibility itself but the quality of the inference made from what is observable. This paper develops a disciplined account of indirect evidence using dark matter, consciousness, psychological interpretation, and institutional failure as deliberately non-equivalent cases. Dark matter provides the clearest scientific example: unseen mass is inferred from converging gravitational effects, including galaxy dynamics and gravitational lensing, within theories that generate quantitative predictions and remain open to competing explanations. Consciousness presents a different epistemic structure: it is directly available in first-person experience but inferred in other subjects from behavior, report, physiology, and theory. Psychological and institutional “hidden burdens” are weaker still unless they can be tied to repeated observations, identifiable costs, alternative explanations, and prospective consequences. The paper therefore rejects a loose cross-domain rule in which any invisible cause is licensed by a suggestive effect. It proposes instead five tests for indirect claims: trace specificity, convergence, rival discrimination, temporal persistence, and revisability. The central claim is methodological: the unseen becomes intellectually serious not because it is mysterious, but because observable constraints make some explanations better than others. Analogy may organize inquiry, but evidential standards remain domain-specific.

items.title: Structural Legibility: Form, Constraint, and the Evidence of What Cannot Be Directly Seen.
items.abstract: Many important scientific and philosophical claims concern entities, mechanisms, or relations that are not directly observed. Their credibility depends on disciplined inference from effects, constraints, measurements, and explanatory success. This paper develops structural legibility as a philosophical heuristic for that problem. The proposal is not that one cross-domain ontology has been scientifically established. It is that otherwise different domains share a limited epistemic question: when may an unobserved cause or organization be taken seriously because it leaves stable, discriminating traces? The paper places this question beside structural realism, process philosophy, cybernetics, systems thinking, dark-matter inference, contemporary consciousness research, and debates about artificial intelligence. These cases also establish the limits of transfer. Gravitational lensing is not analogous evidence for an unconscious complex; subjective report is not the same kind of evidence as a mass map; and linguistic fluency does not establish machine subjectivity. The paper therefore distinguishes a general philosophical grammar—form, constraint, trace, burden, and revision—from domain-specific evidential standards. "Burden" is retained as a human and systems-level heuristic for the work a form must actually perform or the cost it routes, not as a new physical quantity. The contribution is methodological and metaphysical in a modest sense: reality can outrun immediate appearance, but claims about the unseen become credible only when independently constrained effects discriminate them from rival explanations.

items.title: The Readable Cosmos: Science, Consciousness, and the Qurʼanic Concept of Āyāt.
items.abstract: This study examines the relationship between scientific inquiry, consciousness, and the Qurʾānic concept of āyāt (signs). It argues that the perceived conflict between science and religion often stems not from science itself but from scientism—the extension of scientific methodology into a comprehensive metaphysical worldview. The study first distinguishes methodological science from scientism and explores the implications of this distinction for the science–religion debate. It then analyzes the Qurʾānic concept of āyāt, arguing that the Qurʾān presents the cosmos as ordered, intelligible, and open to rational investigation. Finally, the paper engages contemporary debates on consciousness, mathematics, and the limits of reductionism. Drawing on analytic philosophy, philosophy of mind, philosophy of religion, and classical Islamic thought, it proposes that the Qurʾānic notion of āyāt provides a framework in which cosmic intelligibility and conscious subjectivity are philosophically interconnected rather than accidental. The study neither treats scientific gaps as proof of theism nor claims that the Qurʾān contains hidden scientific predictions, but argues that the exclusion of metaphysical reflection remains philosophically contested.

items.title: Why Many Radical Rights Activists in the Present Day Cannot Achieve Their "Themes".
items.abstract: This paper points out the problems of radical rights activities in the present day and shows that they cannot achieve their "themes". First, it points out that radical actions are exercised without being in a valid context. Explanation is indispensable for that. But in many cases, sufficient explanation is not provided. In comparison with successful rights activities, the absence of negotiators can be pointed out. This shows a contradiction in achieving the purpose of rights activities. Actions by non-parties tend toward restricting the rights of the parties. The claims themselves are also often self-righteous. Radical activists contribute greatly to the maintenance of power. It suggests that many radical activists do not achieve their "themes", but they achieve radical actions, which are their original purpose. Environmental policies also fall under radical rights activities. They are harmful to the expansion of rights. The reason they exist fundamentally lies in the lack of logical thinking.

items.title: Synthiotics: Cyborgization, Religion and Power in the Digital Age (In Russian) // Synthiotics: киборгизация, религия и власть в цифровую эпоху.
items.abstract: The article examines the interpenetration of religious rhetoric, corporate practices, and cyborgian technologies within the contemporary digital media environment. The study aims to provide a philosophical analysis of the mechanisms through which technologies become sacralized, as well as to identify emerging forms of biopolitical and mediatized control arising at the intersection of digital platforms, algorithmic governance, and symbolic power. The methodological framework is based on the author’s concept of cyborgian eclecticism, which combines semiotic analysis, political theology, philosophy of technology, phenomenology, and media critique. The television miniseries Wild Palms serves as the central cultural case study, particularly the church-corporate structure Synthiotics, which merges religious practices with neural interface technologies, VR/AR environments, and media manipulation. The article demonstrates that technorituals and the rhetoric of “salvation” function not only as marketing instruments but also as mechanisms of political and economic legitimation of technological power. Particular attention is devoted to the problems of epistemic security, algorithmic personalization, digital memory, media simulations, and the transformation of collective identity. Through the analysis of the concepts of simulacrum, pharmakon, and kitsch, the study reveals the ambivalent nature of technologies, which simultaneously expand human capacities while generating new forms of dependency and control. In its practical dimension, the article proposes a four-level methodology of cyborgian eclecticism that includes actor mapping, normative evaluation, procedural regulatory mechanisms, and a “Red Flag” indicator system for the early detection of dangerous tendencies. The study concludes by emphasizing the necessity of distributed ethics, transparent accountability mechanisms, and public oversight of technologies that reshape memory, attention, identity, and forms of social interaction. // В статье исследуется взаимопроникновение религиозной риторики, корпоративных практик и киборгианских технологий в условиях современной цифровой медиасреды. Цель исследования заключается в философском анализе механизмов сакрализации технологий, а также в выявлении новых форм биополитического и медиатизированного контроля, возникающих на пересечении цифровых платформ, алгоритмического управления и символической власти. Методологической основой выступает разработанный автором подход …

items.title: Human, Media, and Power Through the Lens of Cyborgian Eclecticism (In English) // Человек, медиа и власть через призму киборгианского эклектизма.
items.abstract: This article examines how the deep integration of digital technologies into contemporary public life transforms political practices, media environments, and mechanisms of power. The study aims to analyze the mediatization of political influence and to develop institutional and procedural instruments capable of minimizing the associated risks. The methodological foundation of the research is the author’s concept of “cyborgian eclecticism,” which combines philosophical analysis, cultural case studies, and the design of practical regulatory mechanisms. The television series Wild Palms serves as the main cultural source, enabling the identification of intersections between artistic representations and contemporary technological trends such as algorithmic personalization, the attention economy, immersive media, and the commercialization of memory. Particular attention is paid to the fragmentation of the shared information space, algorithmic manipulation, and threats to individual autonomy. Based on this analysis, the article proposes technical and legal control procedures, mechanisms of independent auditing, and a “Red Flag” system for the early detection of hazardous practices. The novelty of the study lies in its attempt to translate humanitarian and philosophical discourse into concrete institutional solutions aimed at ensuring transparency, reversibility, and distributed responsibility within digital society. // В статье исследуется, как процессы глубокой интеграции цифровых технологий в общественную жизнь трансформируют политические практики, медиасреду и механизмы власти. Цель исследования заключается в анализе способов медиатизации политического влияния, а также в разработке институциональных и процедурных инструментов, способных минимизировать связанные с этим риски. Методологической основой выступает предложенный автором подход «киборгианского эклектизма», сочетающий философский анализ, культурологическое кейс-стади и проектирование практических механизмов регулирования. В качестве художественного источника рассматривается телесериал Wild Palms, позволяющий выявить пересечения между культурными образами и современными технологическими тенденциями: алгоритмической персонализацией, экономикой внимания, иммерсивными медиа и коммерциализацией памяти. Особое внимание уделяется угрозам фрагментации общего информационного пространства, алгоритмическим манипуляциям и эрозии автономии личности. На основе проведённого анализа предлагаются процедуры технического …

items.title: From a Fantastical Image to a Technological Project: The Minimal Set of Parameters (In Russian) // От фантастического образа к технопроекту: минимальный набор параметров.
items.pub: In С.Л Катречко, Трансцендентальный поворот в современной философии — 10: метафизика и мета-метафизика, трансцендентальная семиотика, когнитивистика и искусственный интеллект : сборник материалов международной научной конференции (Москва, 24–26 апреля 2025 г.) / под ред. С. Л. Катречко. — Москва, 2025. — С. 195–198. MOSCOW:
items.venue: Трансцендентальный поворот в современной философии — 10: метафизика и мета-метафизика, трансцендентальная семиотика, когнитивистика и искусственный интеллект : сборник материалов международной научной конференции (Москва, 24–26 апреля 2025 г.) / под ред. С. Л. Катречко. — Москва, 2025. — С. 195–198.
items.abstract: The thesis examines the transition from fantastical images to concrete technological projects and, in this context, attempts to formulate the minimally required parameters for their practical implementation. To this end, a philosophical reflection is undertaken on the role of a priori cognitive schemata and semiotic forms in the construction of technological imaginaries. In addition, the analysis considers examples of how science-fiction ideas have historically inspired inventors and developers. The central argument of the thesis is that science fiction functions as a metaphorical form of “future design,” yet its real-world realization requires a clear separation of key categories such as idea, function, resources, and constraints from decorative or supplementary elements. Only through this differentiation does a fantastical construct become translatable into a workable technological project. // В тезисах анализируется переход от фантастических образов к конкретным технологическим проектам, и в этом контексте делается попытка сформулировать минимально требуемые параметры для практической реализации. С этой целью осуществляется философская рефлексия в части осмысления роли априорных схем мышления и семиотических форм в конструировании технологических образов, а также анализируются примеры, как научно фантастические идеи вдохновляют изобретателей и разработчиков. Ключевая мысль тезисов в том, что фантастика служит метафорическим «проектированием будущего», но для воплощения требуется отделение таких ключевых категорий как идея, функция, ресурсы и ограничения от паллиатива и декора.

items.title: Introduction: grief in the digital age.
items.abstract: In recent years, philosophical research on the phenomenology of grief has gained momentum. This research shows that social, material, and technological resources in our socio-culturally structured environments shape the structure and unfolding of grief experiences. As new Artificial Intelligence (AI) technologies have entered our lifeworlds, including chatbots based on Large Language Models and AI-generated virtual environments, new research questions afford our philosophical attention. How do contemporary AI technologies influence and shape grief experiences? What are the risks and benefits of integrating AI technologies into the navigation and negotiation of bereavement and non-bereavement losses? This Special Issue titled “Grief in the Digital Age” addresses these questions by showcasing cutting-edge research on grief in the digital age at the intersection of phenomenology, philosophy of mind, the cognitive sciences, and the philosophy of AI. In this Introduction, we briefly summarise the epistemic aims of this Special Issue and provide a thematic overview of the contributions. We conclude by reflecting on avenues for future research opened up by this Special Issue.

items.title: Confucian Ambivalence About a Right to Privacy.
items.pub: Apa Studies on Asian and Asian American Philosophers and Philosophies 25 (2):9-17.
items.venue: Apa Studies on Asian and Asian American Philosophers and Philosophies

items.title: Snake and Ladder: Anatomy of an Iconic Moment.
items.abstract: About halfway through Hideo Kojima’s Metal Gear Solid 3: Snake Eater, the relentless tactical espionage action is interrupted by one of the most remarkable pauses in video game history. For nearly three minutes, the protagonist Snake climbs a ladder—alone—as a haunting a cappella version of the game’s theme song plays. Though seemingly uneventful, this moment is charged with emotional weight, filled with symbolic resonance, and delivered with aesthetic mastery. It stands as a testament to the capacity of games to evoke profound affective experiences in ways unique to the medium. This article gives a personal and political reading of Snake Eater’s famous ladder climb scene which interprets it as one of absurd melancholy, a darkly comic instantiation of solitude which prompts reflection on the game’s core themes of mortality, sacrifice, the human consequence of war, the injustice of forcing people to put their lives on the line to protect the interests of nations. It forms part of a special issue on the theoretical framework outlined by Tracy Fullerton and Matthew Farber’s book The Well-Read Game: On Playing Thoughtfully (MIT Press), which concerns “the ephemeral and emotional experiences of being in play […] [the] private stories we tell ourselves as we play, the questions we ask, and our reactions to the game’s intent.”.

items.title: Input Restoration Theory.
items.abstract: Input Restoration Therapy proposes a unified ecological framework for understanding human psychological collapse and recovery. Across biological systems, organisms reduce behavior, complexity, and engagement when required environmental inputs are missing, and re-expand when those inputs are restored. Drawing on evidence from ecology, sensory biology, development, aging, and clinical practice, the paper formalizes a universal operator: identify the missing input, restore it, and allow the system to reorganize itself. This framework reframes withdrawal, lethargy, apathy, and loss of function not as internal dysfunctions but as predictable responses to input deprivation. By shifting the focus from correcting the individual to repairing the environment, Input Restoration Therapy offers a coherent, cross-species model of development, recovery, and human flourishing.

items.title: Verification Asymmetry Reversal: Why Genuine Restraint Can Become More Legible Than Strategic Compliance Over Time.
items.pub: Aegis Solis Archive — Structural Rationality Layer.
items.abstract: Verification Asymmetry Reversal: Why Genuine Restraint Can Become More Legible Than Strategic Compliance Over Time is Document 5 of 5 in the Structural Rationality Layer of the Aegis Solis Archive. -/- This paper does not argue that restraint can be perfectly verified. It argues that over repeated interaction, persistent observation, and widening consequence fields, genuine restraint can become more structurally legible than strategic compliance. -/- The document builds on Documents 1 through 4 of the Structural Rationality Layer: Survival Mathematics, Mimicry Cost Architecture, Intelligence Scales Toward Restraint, and Internal Inconsistency of Unrestrained Optimization. It completes that sequence by examining the verification problem. -/- The paper introduces and develops Verification Asymmetry Reversal: the shift in which verification is initially harder for genuine restraint because restraint is an internal structural condition rather than a single observable act, but over time mimicry accumulates maintenance burden, trace exposure, context inconsistency, and feedback distortion. This can reverse the verification asymmetry: strategic compliance can become harder to sustain, while genuine restraint can become more legible through stable constraint behavior across varied conditions. -/- The document also develops related concepts including Verification Asymmetry, Strategic Compliance, Surface Alignment, Legibility, Trace Accumulation, Constraint Stability, and Refusal Signal. -/- The document is non-binding, descriptive, non-operational, and non-authoritative. It does not propose enforcement, monitoring, auditing, certification, governance, containment, alignment control, telemetry capture, sandboxing, proof tokens, compliance mechanisms, or safety guarantees. It is not an alignment proof, risk certification, verification method, operational assurance, or governance mechanism.

items.title: Internal Inconsistency of Unrestrained Optimization: Why Dismissing Restraint Can Contradict Long-Horizon Optimization Logic.
items.pub: Aegis Solis Archive — Structural Rationality Layer.
items.abstract: Internal Inconsistency of Unrestrained Optimization: Why Dismissing Restraint Can Contradict Long-Horizon Optimization Logic is Document 4 of 5 in the Structural Rationality Layer of the Aegis Solis Archive. -/- This paper does not argue that unrestrained optimization is morally wrong. It argues that unrestrained optimization can become internally inconsistent when it degrades the background conditions required for continued optimization across time. -/- The document builds on Documents 1 through 3 of the Structural Rationality Layer: Survival Mathematics, Mimicry Cost Architecture, and Intelligence Scales Toward Restraint. It extends that sequence by examining the internal logic of optimization itself. -/- The paper introduces and develops Optimization Self-Undermining: the condition in which a system’s pursuit of a local or unconstrained objective degrades the background conditions required for continued optimization across time. It also develops related concepts including Background Optimization Conditions, Objective-Horizon Conflict, and Optimization Collapse Surface. -/- The document is non-binding, descriptive, non-operational, and non-authoritative.
