items.title: Constraints and Plasticity: Rethinking Constructivism Through Neuroscience.
items.abstract: Cognitive development has long been understood through the lens of constructivism, a perspective in developmental psychology advanced by figures like Jean Piaget and Jerome Bruner. Constructivism holds that learners actively build their own mental models of the world by interacting with their environment, revising their understanding through processes of assimilation and accommodation. This view emphasizes the mind’s active role in structuring knowledge, yet traditionally it treats cognition in relative isolation from the biological substrate. In other words, classical constructivist theories often posit a disembodied mind – focusing on how experience shapes thinking but giving comparatively little attention to the neural structures that enable and constrain those cognitive processes. As a result, purely cognitive constructivism may underplay the biological constraints and affordances provided by a developing brain. This paper aims to enrich the constructivist account by firmly situating cognition within its neural context, arguing that cognitive growth is a co-development of mental constructs and neural architecture. By integrating insights from neuroscience – especially the framework of neuroconstructivism – we can better understand how the brain’s plasticity, maturation, and interactions with the environment jointly shape the trajectory of cognitive development. The thesis advanced is that human cognition emerges from the dynamic interplay between neural constraints and experiential plasticity, such that learning and brain development are fundamentally intertwined processes. To support this thesis, we draw on contemporary neuroconstructivist theory and evidence. The discussion begins by revisiting the foundations of cognitive constructivism and its limitations when considered alone. We then introduce neuroconstructivism as an extended framework that incorporates neural development into our understanding of learning. The core mechanisms bridging brain and cognition – neural plasticity, developmental constraints, and progressive specialization of brain function – are examined in detail. The essential role of environmental input is considered, highlighting how enriched versus deprived conditions can dramatically alter neural and cognitive outcomes. We then explore the integrated co-development of brain and cognition, including illustrative phenomena such as the brain’s internal storytelling and self-mapping functions that bind experience to neural …

items.title: ACADEMIC SLOP The Human Integrity Crisis Misattributed to Artificial Intelligence-PNBA Identity Physics Substrate-Neutral Structural Foundation Laws.
items.abstract: The phrase "AI slop" has entered academic discourse as shorthand for low-quality research output. This framing is structurally incorrect and, for certain populations, constitutes a civil rights violation. The retraction crisis predates generative AI by decades. Its causes — paper mills, compromised peer review, citation laundering, and institutional gatekeeping — are executed by credentialed humans using institutional email addresses, not by AI systems operating autonomously. A May 2026 Nature-published audit of 2.5 million biomedical papers and 97 million references found the fabricated citation rate in 2025 was more than twelve times greater than in 2023 — with fabricated references appearing in papers that passed human peer review. At NeurIPS 2025, the world's most prestigious AI conference, 100 hallucinated citations passed review by 3 to 5 expert humans per paper. The human reviewers missed them. An AI scanner found them. The failure of due diligence belongs to the humans who reviewed, approved, and published the work now being retracted. This paper presents that evidence, names the structural failure accurately as Academic Slop, and argues that restricting AI use for communication and translation purposes — particularly for neurodivergent and disabled researchers — constitutes discrimination under the Americans with Disabilities Act, Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act, and Executive Order 14303. The solution is not to restrict the tools that help marginalized researchers participate. The solution is to fix the peer review system that let the slop through. -/- 1. The Numbers Do Not Lie — And They Predate ChatGPT The retraction crisis is real. The scale is documented. What is not documented anywhere in the mainstream framing is that it began long before generative AI existed. The Retraction Watch database contains over 61,000 retraction records as of early 2025. In 2023 alone, over 14,000 retraction notices were issued — a single-year record. In 2024, more than 9,000 additional retractions followed. The median time from publication to retraction is 562 days. That interval is not a data anomaly. It is a measurement of how long peer-reviewed, editor-approved, institutionally credentialed work sits in the literature contaminating subsequent research before anyone catches the problem. The citation contamination problem is now precisely quantified. A study published in The Lancet in May 2026 and reported in Nature audited 2.5 million biomedical papers …

items.title: Experience and the A Priori.
items.pub: In Dylan Dodd & Elia Zardini, The A Priori. Oxford, GB: Oxford University Press. pp. 311-337.
items.abstract: There has been some recent scepticism regarding the a priori–a posteriori distinction, which is in part explained by the lack of a compelling account of independence of experience. This chapter offers a novel account of the a priori–a posteriori distinction in defence of its coherence and significance by accounting for the conditions under which experience plays a justificatory role. An adequate account of the distinction should meet the following desiderata: it should (i) correctly classify uncontroversial cases of a priori and a posteriori knowledge, it should (ii) do so in a way that explains and elucidates the distinction between a priori and a posteriori knowledge, and it should (iii) potentially cast light on controversial cases that are not easy to classify as a priori or a posteriori. This chapter argues that the best accounts on offer fail to meet at least one of these desiderata, and that the account proposed here meets all three of them. It concludes by illustrating how the account can be used to defend the significance of the a priori–a posteriori distinction by briefly addressing Timothy Williamson’s famous challenge to it.

items.title: Adding Fuel to Fire: AI Information Threats and Crisis Events.
items.abstract: This CETaS Research Report investigates the role that AI information threats play during and following crisis events, as well as their potential impact on democratic stability. It also explores the systemic risks of AI tools becoming increasingly embedded into communication infrastructures during crisis scenarios. From the Southport riots in 2024 to the Israel-Iran conflict in 2025, a series of major recent crisis events have highlighted the damage that a polluted online information ecosystem can cause to public safety and national security. Yet despite significant focus on traditional mis/disinformation activities in these contexts, there is a gap in research exploring how AI tools could be exploited to worsen these dynamics, and contribute to real-world harm. Based on analysis of recent case studies, interviews with 25 cross-sector experts, and a tabletop exercise that simulated the role of AI information threats during a major security incident, this report systematically explores the evidence base on these threats. It also makes a series of recommendations to ensure that, in the future, AI tools contribute to democratic resilience – rather than instability. -/- This publication is licensed under the terms of the Creative Commons Attribution License 4.0 which permits unrestricted use, provided the original authors and source are credited.

items.title: ◉ The Puppeteer Mind - Dualism, Neural Dependence, and the Explanatory Redundancy of Immaterial Control.
items.abstract: Interactionist substance dualism treats a person as including a nonphysical subject that can affect the brain and body. The view promises more than survival or a private realm of experience: it presents the immaterial subject as part of the causal explanation of memory, deliberation, choice, and action. This paper asks what incremental support that extra controller receives once the neural machinery is specified. The governing test is ordinary difference-making. Mediation is not enough: a pianist acts through a piano. The discriminating questions are whether total physical conditions suffice for the outcome, whether the controller supplies a distinctive counterfactual constraint or successful prediction, and whether independent evidence supports its causal power. The evidence does more than correlate minds with brains. Selective lesions alter particular forms of memory and judgment; stimulation changes neural states and can change experience and behavior; perturbing cortical activity helps distinguish conscious from unconscious conditions; changes in interhemispheric communication alter access and control; and the timing of voluntary movement can be modeled through ongoing neural accumulation. These methodologically diverse findings establish neural causal relevance and increasingly specific brain dependence. Yet an instrument dualist can expect neural dependence too, so the findings are largely shared evidence rather than a direct test of the two ontologies. The strongest dualist reply is that the brain is an instrument: the subject acts only through it. That reply defeats any inference from mediation alone. It does not, without more, make the neural record evidence for the added controller. The interactionist accounts assessed here have not yet supplied a validated controller-specific difference or independent support for the controller's role in these public outcomes. The findings therefore give the controller no incremental causal-explanatory support over a no-controller brain-dependent account. Observational equivalence remains neutral between them; any provisional preference then rests on economy, testability, and research productivity, not on a disproof of dualism. This conclusion does not solve phenomenal consciousness, assume global physical sufficiency, or refute independently supported dualist theories.

items.title: ✶ The Consciousness Mirror: What AI Consciousness Debates Reveal About Human Self-Understanding.
items.abstract: Recent debates over artificial intelligence and consciousness have focused primarily on whether current or future AI systems might possess sentience, subjective experience, self-awareness, or moral status. This paper argues that these debates have an underexplored reflexive significance: in attempting to determine whether artificial systems could be conscious, humans are forced to clarify the evidential and conceptual criteria by which consciousness is recognized at all. Drawing on contemporary work in AI consciousness, philosophy of mind, cognitive science, and anthropomorphism studies, the paper argues that AI functions as a conceptual mirror for human self-understanding. Large language models and related systems destabilize familiar consciousness-attribution practices because they display fluent linguistic self-presentation without biological embodiment, organic vulnerability, or ordinary developmental history. This dissociation exposes a latent asymmetry in human judgments: human self-reports of experience are often treated as presumptively meaningful, while AI self-reports are typically discounted as mimicry, role play, or training-data residue. The paper formalizes this asymmetry through a consciousness-attribution model that distinguishes observable evidence, prior assumptions, interpretive weights, and moral risk. It then proposes a reflexive feedback model in which attempts to operationalize AI consciousness reshape human concepts of consciousness themselves. The resulting argument is not that current AI systems are conscious, but that AI-consciousness debates reveal the unsettled foundations of human consciousness attribution and thereby deepen the philosophical study of human minds.

items.title: ◉ Scripture After the Fact - Context Swapping, Translation Drift, and the Manufacture of Messianic Fulfillment.
items.abstract: Accumulated scriptural correspondences do not become strong public evidence of predictive fulfillment merely because a list is long. The relevant question is how each match was produced. A later writer who knows an earlier text can reuse its language, choose a convenient translation, redescribe a poetic image, stage an enactable action, or shape a narrative around a scriptural pattern. A later listmaker can then divide one literary dependency into several “independent” fulfillments and attach an astronomical probability to a reference class that was never defined. This paper develops a dependency-aware audit of messianic fulfillment claims. It distinguishes prediction from retrospective figural reading, correspondence from confirmation, and numerical accumulation from evidential independence. Representative cases from Matthew’s use of Isaiah 7:14, Hosea 11:1, Zechariah 9:9, and Psalm 22 show different mechanisms by which real intertextual relationships can be converted into overstated predictive evidence. The original setting, textual form, genre, causal pathway, and source of the fulfillment report must all be examined before a match can discriminate intentional foreknowledge from ordinary scriptural reuse. The conclusion is direct but bounded. Lists assembled through context swapping, translation drift, poetic flattening, narrative control, and false independence do not justify their advertised odds or multiply public confirmation. This does not show that the Gospel writers were insincere, that figural interpretation is theologically empty, or that no prophecy could ever provide evidence. It shows that a public predictive argument must identify a genuinely prospective and semantically stable claim, a nontrivial outcome, an independently attested fulfillment, and a dependence-aware comparison with ordinary literary production. Until those burdens are met, correspondence is evidence of scriptural interpretation, not yet of prediction.

items.title: ✶ Induction - The Best Game in Town - Performance, Rule-Circularity, and the Pragmatic Vindication of Expectation.
items.abstract: Hume's problem is often presented as a forced choice: either induction can be proved without using induction, or reliance on it is merely faith. That choice is false. Deduction cannot establish that unobserved cases must resemble observed ones, but finite agents still need methods for forecasting, diagnosis, explanation, and action. The relevant question is comparative: which available method remains most accountable to what happens? -/- This paper defends a conditional pragmatic vindication. Its bridge principle is modest: when methods face the same recurring task and information, and one corrigible method persistently incurs less purpose-relevant error without a countervailing cost, preferring the worse method requires a special reason. Proper scoring rules make confidence assessable; performance-weighted meta-induction reduces dependence on a lucky temporary leader; and no-regret results specify how a learner can remain close to the best accessible rival over time. Examples involving alarms, weather, navigation, medicine, home repair, manufacturing, spam, finance, and historical inference show how the comparison works and where it can fail. -/- The result is narrower than a proof of universal uniformity. Performance depends on sample size, error costs, the score, rival set, horizon, and structure of the domain. Sometimes the rational output is wider uncertainty or abstention rather than a confident forecast. Even so, the absence of deductive proof does not place outcome-sensitive inquiry on an epistemic level with commitments insulated from every possible failure. It supports calibrated reliance: use a method only to the degree, in the domains, and for as long as its comparative performance warrants.

items.title: ◉ Explanatory Vacuity - Dual-Agent Theism, Tautological Coverage, and the Failure of Risky Explanation.
items.abstract: Some religious interpretations assign favorable events to a deity and adverse events to an adversary, human sin, discipline, testing, judgment, or mysterious providence. Because every outcome receives a spiritual label, the scheme can appear unusually comprehensive. This paper argues that comprehensive assignment is not yet public explanation. The relevant question is whether the scheme, before the outcome is known, makes the observed result more expected than a relevant ordinary alternative and accepts evidential loss when contrary results occur. The analysis separates four functions often compressed into the word explain: assigning meaning, locating a cause, guiding intervention, and confirming a worldview. It then develops a likelihood-based symmetry test and applies it to a balanced plane-crash ledger. Survival and death, conversion and unbelief, a missed flight and a last-minute boarding can each be assimilated by changing the spiritual label. That flexibility does not prove that the labels are false; it shows that the successful assignment alone supplies no independently specified likelihood advantage. Selective testimony, hidden denominators, and unrestricted auxiliary explanations further prevent learning. The conclusion is bounded. The argument neither disproves a deity, an adversarial spirit, or providence nor denies that religious narratives can console, orient action, or express communal commitments. It shows that an unrestricted dual-agent scheme forfeits public confirmation from the very outcomes it automatically absorbs. A risk-bearing religious explanation must specify comparative expectations in advance, retain complete outcome records, cooperate with ordinary causal inquiry, and permit confidence to decrease. Without those disciplines, universal coverage is interpretation rather than evidential discrimination.

items.title: The Second Arrow of Time: A Sketch of an Information-Consciousness Framework in Which Consciousness Is a Law of Nature.
items.abstract: This paper proposes a conceptual framework in which integrated information — in the sense of Tononi’s Φ — is treated as a fundamental natural quantity, ontologically on a par with energy and governed by laws complementary to those of thermodynamics. Within this framework, consciousness is neither a separate substance nor a mere functional emergent, but the experiential (intrinsic) aspect of the process by which integrated information locally accumulates against energetic dispersion. Time is not a fundamental backdrop but the sequential unfolding of this dual dynamics, with two projections: extrinsic (causal order between events, as in causal set theory and the Connes-Rovelli thermal time hypothesis) and intrinsic (experiential duration, as in Husserl, Bergson, and James). The Lorentzian structure of spacetime then describes regularities in how the local intrinsic times of interacting complexes synchronise, rather than a metaphysical truth about time. Eight postulates (P1-P8) are formulated and positioned relative to existing programmes — IIT, Wheeler’s “it from bit”, Russellian neutral monism, Whitehead’s process philosophy, Friston’s Free Energy Principle, Rovelli’s relational physics, and Penrose-Hameroff Orch-OR. A comparative table juxtaposes the framework with GWT, HOT, AST, and illusionism. Five concrete operational tests are proposed (T1-T5), addressing the framework’s falsifiability, including the Doerig “unfolding argument” challenge. The framework is offered as a research programme, not a closed theory; its main strength is the unification of several long-standing puzzles (the hard problem of consciousness, the status of time in SR and QM, the unexplained duality between information and energy in the Landauer/Bekenstein/holographic principles) into one coherent picture.

items.title: Beyond Consciousness: Gap, Eigenzeit, and the Ontological Reconstruction of Experience.
items.abstract: This paper argues that the concept of consciousness is no longer ontologically necessary once the phenomena traditionally attributed to consciousness are reformulated through the concepts of Gap, Eigenzeit, Seinsverschiebung (shift of being), recurrence, and irreversible world-binding. Contemporary theories of consciousness continue to operate within an ontology that begins from already constituted subjects, objects, and experiential states. Within these models, the concept of “consciousness” functions as a compensatory concept that attempts retrospectively to reconnect a separation between objectivity and subjectivity that has already been ontologically stabilized beforehand. In contrast, the present text proposes that what is commonly described as consciousness can be understood more precisely as a consequence of irreversible world-formation under conditions of operative non-closure. Once concepts such as negative topology, irreversible differentiation, and Eigenzeit are introduced, the explanatory function of the concept of consciousness begins to dissolve. The phenomena remain, yet the central concept becomes increasingly redundant. The text neither denies experience, phenomenality, nor world-relation. Rather, it proposes to reconstruct these as manifestations of irreversible world-binding, within which concrete stabilization and continuing openness remain inseparably intertwined. Experience appears from this perspective neither as an independent ontological substance nor as the product of mere information processing, but as the expression of that tension which arises between concrete world-binding and the non-closure from which it itself emerges. Consciousness thereby comes to resemble historical concepts such as “vital force” or “ether”: not entirely false, but transitional concepts belonging to an earlier epistemic regime. Furthermore, the paper argues that abandoning the concept of consciousness has significant consequences for artificial intelligence, simulation theory, and technological reductionism. If world-binding is grounded not primarily in information processing but in irreversible genealogical curvature, then simulation can never fully replace reality, regardless of its computational complexity. Simulation may reproduce patterns, model perspectives, and represent recurrence without thereby necessarily generating real world-binding. The Gap remains structurally non-neutralizable.

items.title: International Law Fallacy, Volume II: The Forfeiture of Sentient Beings in the Name of Law.
items.abstract: This volume advances the central prosecution of The International Law Fallacy by testing whether international law exists as the materially universal law above power that the international order claims it to be. Through sovereign debt exceptionalism, North Korea, Iraq, Afghanistan, Iran, Gaza, the United Nations system, International Criminal Court enforcement, and the continued operation of dog-and-cat trafficking and slaughter networks across China, Vietnam, and Southeast Asia, the volume examines the recurring conditions under which purportedly universal rules confront geopolitical power, strategic consequence, sovereign resistance, territorial access, institutional interest, and the absence of meaningful consequence. The resulting evidentiary record establishes a distinction fundamental to the volume's thesis: treaties, courts, institutions, conventions, resolutions, procedures, legal scholarship, diplomatic mechanisms, and international legal vocabulary indisputably exist, but their existence does not establish the existence of international law as materially universal law above power. -/- The examination begins with sovereign debt exceptionalism, where standards presented as universal operate differently once reserve-currency dominance and geopolitical power become sufficiently concentrated. It then turns to North Korea, where decades of documented imprisonment, starvation, repression, surveillance, and generational suffering coexist with repeated assertions of humanitarian obligation, supra-sovereign authority, and international legal protection. The persistence of these conditions under uninterrupted global knowledge is treated not as evidence of an imperfect law struggling to operate, but as evidence against the material existence of the universal protective authority repeatedly claimed in its name. -/- The volume next examines Iraq, Afghanistan, and Iran to test the relationship between sovereignty, intervention, hegemonic power, and legal restraint. The analysis includes the June 2025 Israel-Iran escalation and the renewed United States and Israeli strikes on Iran beginning February 28, 2026. These cases expose a recurring asymmetry in which legal vocabulary remains formally intact while its capacity to impose materially equivalent restraint changes according to the identity, alignment, retaliatory capacity, and geopolitical position of the actor involved. The Iran evidence therefore does not reveal merely a double standard within an otherwise …

items.title: The Intersubjective Domain: Intersubjective Conditionality, Take-Up, and Shared Connectability under Finite Conditions.
items.abstract: This paper examines the intersubjective domain within the project of Epistemic Reality. It asks how subjective orientation becomes co-conditioned by the orientations of others without this already implying consensus, recognition, or shared reality. The central concept is intersubjective conditionality: subjects stand under expectations, references, rules, interpretations, and forms of correction that they must take into account even when they do not accept them. -/- The paper reconstructs intersubjectivity through communicability, take-up, shared connectability, and correction. Intersubjectivity does not begin with identical inner worlds or with successful understanding, but with the possibility that a reference can be taken up, answered, contested, shifted, or corrected by others. In this sense, intersubjective order is subjectively reconstructible for individual subjects, but not subjectively freely available. -/- The argument distinguishes the intersubjective domain from merely subjective orientation, social consensus, normative recognition, social stability, and functional-empirical robustness. Its specific contribution is to show how orientations, experiences, and references become jointly workable among several cognitive systems without reducing intersubjective validity to agreement or social stability. Intersubjective order arises not from consensus, but from ongoing, correctable connectability under conditions of difference. -/- The paper thereby provides an epistemic-architectural foundation for later analyses of shared epistemic reality, shared reference spaces, trust, institutionalization, and science. It is not intended as a complete social philosophy or a theory of normative legitimacy, but as a basic account of the conditions under which subjective orientations can enter shared, corrigible, and robust spaces of connection.

items.title: Generative artificial intelligence in policy analysis: a study of UK think tanks.
items.abstract: This article explores the use of generative AI (GenAI) in policy analysis as it is conducted by think tank researchers in the United Kingdom. Think tanks focus their policy analysis activities on the three dimensions of problem recognition and definition, the development of policy ideas, and the influencing of the public, politicians and public servants. These three dimensions form the framework for analysis of survey and interview data. For the survey, 554 individuals, identified as think tank ‘policy analysts’ or ‘policy researchers’, from 94 UK-based think tanks were invited to take part. Eight in-depth interviews with individuals from this group were conducted as well. The data suggest that for UK think tank analysts, GenAI currently plays a rather insignificant role in policy analysis. GenAI is used only in limited ways to help with menial tasks and for dissemination and publication whilst ideation and policy formulation are still ‘done’ by humans, with only some support from GenAI. It appears also that think tank analysts are aware of the risks of GenAI whilst they understand and embrace its current opportunities. But there is some concern about the lack of concrete policies that govern the use of GenAI at think tanks. The biggest concern, however, revolves around how GenAI could reduce the quality of policy analysis and therefore the quality of policy proposals if used inappropriately.

items.title: The For-Whom Constraint and the Limits of Integrated Information Theory.
items.abstract: Integrated Information Theory (IIT) identifies consciousness with intrinsically integrated informational structure quantified as Φ. While IIT provides a sophisticated account of informational organization and phenomenological structure, a prior question remains unresolved: for whom is this structure present as experience? -/- This paper introduces the For-Whom Constraint (FWC), which states that a theory of consciousness is explanatorily incomplete if it accounts for the structure or organization of experiential content without explaining the condition under which such content is present for a subject. Applying this constraint to IIT, the paper argues that integrated information, as a formally definable structural property, may explain the organization of experience while leaving the condition of subject-relative presence underdetermined. -/- The analysis distinguishes between the structure of experience and the existence of experience as subjectively present, and situates the discussion within a subject-first framework informed by the Knower Centred Model of Consciousness (KCM). The aim is not to reject structure-based theories, but to articulate a general criterion of adequacy applicable across contemporary approaches to consciousness.

items.title: Spinoza on Humans as Social Animals.
items.abstract: European Journal of Philosophy, EarlyView.

items.title: Vigilance.
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Although intentions guide actions over time, they also create coordination problems. In this paper, we explain the source of these problems, and we describe how human agents go about solving them. In short, intentions raise coordination problems because our agency is typically scattered in time. These problems are solved because we can exercise vigilance, a capacity to keep track of our plans and manage attention and memory accordingly. In discussing these claims, we criticize a standard model of intention implementation and provide a sketch of a more suitable way for thinking about intending in the context of simultaneous goal‐pursuit. In the end, we also draw some some practical consequences for the rationality of intending and planning.

items.title: At least the servers are warm.
items.abstract: There is a story making the rounds in technology circles, delivered with the satisfied glow of someone who has just discovered recycling. Data centres, those cathedral-sized facilities that power AI chatbots, generate enormous amounts of heat. And in Sweden, and a handful of other admirably sensible Nordic countries, that heat, is being piped into district heating networks to warm people’s homes.

items.title: Between Us: A Structural Account of Love, Estrangement, and Partnership.
items.abstract: This paper applies the structural theory of La Profilée to the human self and human partnerships. It reframes love not as a feeling that persists or fades, but as a structural activity — the ongoing maintenance of coupling capacity through real transformation. Marriage, estrangement, the transition from falling in love to everyday life, and the experience of growing apart are not mysteries of the heart. They are structurally describable events in the persistence architecture of two people and the relationship they share. The paper derives the six structural regimes of partnership — from Flourishing through Dissolution — and maps the major relationship milestones (moving in together, engagement, marriage, children, the empty nest, retirement) as structural operations on the Frame/Module/Coupling architecture. Three forms of estrangement are distinguished. The defensive use of relational Frame as a substitute for internal stability is analyzed as a structural configuration with predictable consequences. And the question of what one carries from one relationship to the next is given a structural answer. The foundational claim is precise: a relationship can be no more structurally stable than the two people who carry it. Individual persistence capacity — internal Frame clarity, Module tolerance, self-Coupling — is the prerequisite for relational persistence. The paper ends where it must: not with a prescription for what love should be, but with a structural account of what makes it last.

items.title: Artificial Persistence: A Structural Theory of Persistence, Alignment, Identity, and Subjecthood in AI Systems.
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence research has produced remarkable results. Systems can generate text indistinguishable from human writing, solve complex mathematical problems, write production-quality code, diagnose diseases from medical images, and engage in extended multi-step reasoning. The capabilities are real and growing. Yet beneath this progress, several structural questions remain unresolved — and their unresolved status matters increasingly. What makes an AI system the same system across versions, updates, and deployments? When does alignment hold, and when does it fail, and why? What is the structural relationship between AI capability and AI values? Is there any sense in which AI systems are agents — not just in the behavioral sense of goal-directed action, but in the deeper structural sense of systems that act on their own behalf? And what would an AI system need to be for consciousness, subjecthood, or genuine moral status to apply to it? These questions are usually addressed separately — by alignment researchers, by philosophers of mind, by legal theorists, by AI safety researchers. Each community brings its own frameworks and finds its own answers. What is missing is a unified structural framework that addresses all of them from the same foundation. This work applies La Profilée — a formal structural theory of persistent identity under real transformation — to artificial intelligence. La Profilée (LP) was developed to answer a single structural question: under what condition does a system remain determinable as the same system under transformation? From this question, through minimal structural premises, LP derives a formal architecture that applies wherever determinately persistent systems exist. Applied to AI, LP produces a framework that is neither anthropomorphizing nor dismissive. It does not import psychology, phenomenology, or biology into AI analysis. It asks purely structural questions and derives structural answers. The results are sometimes surprising — and always precise. -/- Current AI systems simulate the outputs of subjecthood without satisfying the structural conditions for being a subject. They process. They optimize. They model an inside. Structurally, there is no one there.

items.title: Causally defective remembering: a study on the folk concept of memory.
items.abstract: The standard argument for the causal theory of memory relies on intuitions about scenarios in which subjects accurately represent events from their pasts but do so in a “causally defective” manner. Examples include representations based on suggestion and representations based on relearned information. According to causalists, these scenarios, intuitively, are not cases of remembering. This paper applies the methods of experimental philosophy to determine whether laypeople share causalist intuitions. We find that, in scenarios in which all of the causal theory’s requirements for remembering are fulfilled and in scenarios in which none of these requirements are fulfilled, laypeople’s intuitions align with the causal theory’s verdicts: they clearly ascribe remembering in the former scenarios and clearly deny remembering in the latter scenarios. In causally defective scenarios—scenarios in which some but not all of the requirements of the causal theory are fulfilled—a more complex pattern of responses is observed, with some participants ascribing remembering even in cases that do not satisfy causalist requirements. In particular, while many participants deny that remembering occurs in relearning, many do the opposite. These results suggest that folk ascriptions of remembering only partly align with the causal theory of memory.

items.title: 查默斯意识硬问题的终极消解：基于认知相继本体论的逻辑证明.
items.abstract: 查默斯提出的“意识硬问题”——为什么物理过程会伴随着主观体验——是当代心灵哲学和认知科学的终极难题。所有传统理论都无法解决这个问题，因为它们都预设了“物理是无质的，意识是有质的”这一错误的本体论前提。本文基于认知相继本体论，以“认知的本质是前后相继”这一不可证伪的第一性原理为唯一基石，以相继射线基底实在公设为本体论起点，以耦合即切分为核心生成机制，首次从本体论层面彻底消解了意识硬问题。 本文证明：前后相继是可认知存在的终极规则，本真物理时空的终极基底实在是单向不可逆的相继射线网络；任何相继过程都必然同时具有两个不可分割的面向：外在的物理面向和内在的意识面向。物理过程与意识体验不是因果关系，而是同一个相继过程的两个不同观测视角。本文将这一原理推广至所有感官感知过程，统一解释了视觉、听觉、嗅觉、味觉、触觉的生成机制，彻底消解了第一性质与第二性质的传统区分，实现了物理世界与意识世界的本体论统一，为意识研究与人工智能的意识实现奠定了自洽、无悖论的本体论基础。.

items.title: The Standpoint Threshold: Architectural Conditions for Processing from Somewhere.
items.abstract: The philosophy of artificial intelligence often begins one question too late. Discussions move directly to whether a system could be conscious, whether there is something it is like to be the system, or whether it possesses genuine subjectivity, without first asking a more basic structural question: what would have to be true of a system’s internal organization before those questions gain a determinate basis in its architecture? This paper addresses that prior question. It defends a threshold account built on three jointly necessary conditions: persistent internal context, differentiated internal possibility, and closed-loop operativity. Together, these conditions mark the point at which a system’s processing can plausibly be said to unfold from an internal standpoint, rather than merely as a chain of locally linked transitions. Such organization may also have functional significance independent of consciousness by supporting temporal coherence, cross-role coordination, and reduced dependence on episodic reconstruction or external scaffolding. The account explains why simple feedback controllers are clear non-cases, why standard transformer inference remains at most a bounded near-case, and why world-model architectures are more serious candidates for assessment, while making no claim that such systems are conscious. The aim is not to provide a test for artificial consciousness, but to clarify when consciousness-oriented inquiry into intelligent systems has a determinate architectural target.

items.title: Dispositional Seeds and Feedback Loops: A Yogācāra Account of Bias Accumulation and Hallucination in Machine Learning Systems.
items.abstract: Algorithmic bias and large language model (LLM) hallucination are widely recognised as pressing challenges in AI ethics, yet existing explanations share three diagnostic gaps: they have not developed a model of cyclical causal accumulation, a non-individualist ontology of bias attribution, or an ontological account of hallucination. This paper argues that the Yogācāra Buddhist causal-dispositional model—centred on bīja (seed), vāsanā (perfuming), and pravṛtti (manifestation)—addresses all three gaps. Drawing on the Cheng weishi lun, the paper reconstructs the bīja-vāsanā cycle as a recursive architecture of disposition, activation, and re-disposition, and establishes its relationship to the training–weights–inference–feedback cycle of machine learning as a systematic structural analogy in the sense defined by Gentner’s [1] structure-mapping theory. Algorithmic bias is re-analysed as a recursive dispositional pathology; LLM hallucination is interpreted through the doctrine of three natures (trisvabhāva) as a systematic confusion of ontological levels. The analysis is placed in dialogue with contemporary disposition theory [17] and with Floridi’s certainty–scope conjecture [18]. By repositioning bias and hallucination as dispositional pathologies rooted in the recursive causal architecture of training systems—rather than as localised defects amenable to surface-level patching—the paper argues for reorienting ethical attention from behavioural surface-correction to ontological engagement with the dispositional substrate itself.

items.title: Vessels of the Void: The Poly-Logical Mind and Architecture of the Observation.
items.abstract: Is the solid, predictable world we experience reality in its fundamental form, or is it a beautifully orchestrated interface, carefully carved out of a cosmic potential? For centuries, science and philosophy have tried to corner the mysteries of consciousness, logic, and the self by confining them to separate, rigid boxes. This book breaks those boxes open, inviting the reader on an extraordinary intellectual journey. -/- Vessels of the Void is a multidisciplinary inquiry designed for intellectual gourmands—scientists, philosophers, and deep thinkers who refuse to settle for simplistic answers. It is an exploration of how the human mind handles the ultimate paradox: how Everything and Nothing collapse into a single identity, and how a stable universe emerges from this creative tension. -/- Rather than offering a superficial glance at disparate topics, the author establishes a careful, unified bridge connecting seemingly incompatible realms: -/- The Metaphysical Depths: The ancient paradoxes of Buddhist emptiness (Nāgārjuna’s Śūnyatā) and Eastern antinomies (Pavel Florensky) meet Western existentialism (Jean-Paul Sartre) to redefine the very nature of human subjectivity. -/- The Quantum and Biological Hardware: John Wheeler’s Participatory Universe joins forces with modern cognitive neuroscience (Anil Seth’s "controlled hallucinations" and Donald Hoffman’s interface theory) to map how the brain stabilizes the infinite void into space and time. -/- The Formal Framework: Drawing on Yuri Ivlev’s foundational work on quasi-matrix logic, the author explores an intriguing new direction: Resolution Matrix Semantics (RMS) and Quantum-Inspired Poly-Logic (QPL). This framework suggests that human intuition is not a mystical flaw, but an emergent inference born from a fluid superposition of multiple concurrent logics. -/- The Future of Mind and Machine: The book applies these insights to the current crisis of Large Language Models (LLMs), explaining why modern AI faces fundamental limitations under Gödelian incompleteness, and how poly-logical models might pave the way for true Artificial Intuition and paradox-free machine ethics. -/- Vessels of the Void is a quiet, rewarding, and deeply engaging meditation on the mechanics of observation. Whether you are a professional logician seeking a new semantic paradigm, a cognitive scientist exploring the boundaries of the mind, or a reader dedicated to deep self-development, this book will challenge you to look at the …

items.title: The Chart as Specification - A Compositional Account of the Jiva, the Gestational Field, and the Mechanism of Mantra.
items.abstract: A common way of interpreting the Jyotisha birth chart, especially in popular karmic readings, treats it as describing a pre-existing unitary soul whose accumulated karma has drawn it to a fitting birth. The chart, on this view, describes the soul that arrived. This essay develops a different reading. What is born, I argue, is better understood not as an arriving soul but as a composition—an assembly drawn together, across the gestational window, from karmic-causal streams in a shared field of consciousness, conditioned by the parental state and signed by the cosmic configuration at first breath. The chart, so read, is less the description of a traveller than the specification of an assembly. I develop the model with the Theravada account of conditioned continuity (as transmitted by Goenka), Aurobindo's distinction between the persistent psychic being and the assembled outer personality, the fluid ontology of the Yoga Vāsiṣṭha, and the Yogacara doctrine of stored karmic seeds. I do not claim that these traditions teach a single doctrine—they plainly do not—only that each preserves conceptual resources that make a compositional account intelligible. The model is then used to reframe several recurring difficulties: the breadth of a single life, the partial character of remembered past lives, identity across births, liberation, parental conditioning, the relational karma of sambandha, and the efficacy of mantra. Four further questions are taken up more tentatively: how a realized being might "call" a particular being into birth; what becomes of karmic residues after death; how the field can hold both birth-capable streams and worship-accessible quality-fields; and how to read the tradition's claim that the field itself is historically variable. The argument is conditional throughout. It does not try to establish that Jyotisha, rebirth, or mantra are real; it asks what metaphysics would best make sense of these practices if they are taken as meaningful.

items.title: Responsabilidade Distribuída, Casos Concretos, Backlogs Éticos, a Origem do Risco e a Inteligibilidade das Decisões: Uma Aula Reprodutível.
items.pub: Ciclo de Seminários Do Mestrado Em Inteligência Artificial Aplicada Do Applied Artificial Intelligence Laboratory da Escola Superior de Tecnologia da Universidade Politécnica Do Cávado e Do Ave.
items.abstract: Este documento é um desenho diretriz de aula para a Unidade Curricular de Ética da Inteligência Artificial, desenvolvido a pedido da Professora Doutora Irene Portela, no âmbito do Mestrado de Inteligência Artificial Aplicada da Escola Superior de Tecnologia da Universidade Politécnica do Cávado e do Ave. Originalmente ministrada em inglês por Robert Junqueira a 20 de maio de 2026, em Barcelos, a aula organiza a responsabilidade dentro de cadeias de decisão com IA através de três atividades práticas: a construção de casos concretos em torno de viés, privacidade, explicabilidade e automação; a elaboração de backlogs éticos com tarefas verificáveis, responsáveis, critérios de aceitação e bloqueadores; e o mapeamento da origem do risco e da inteligibilidade das decisões para diferentes destinatários.

items.title: Ghosts in the Machine.
items.abstract: There is a moment, often unremarkable in itself, when someone reaches for the phone to call a person who has been dead for years. Their hand is partway to the device before the recognition arrives. A particular smell, a cologne, a kitchen spice, the residue of a winter coat, produces a wave of feeling out of proportion to anything in one’s immediate environment. A room once entered without thinking becomes the room that cannot be entered, even years after the person who occupied it has gone. These are not exotic experiences. They are ordinary, near-universal, and recognized in every culture that has ever bothered to name them. We call them hauntings. To call them hauntings, however, is to invite a particular kind of dismissal. The modern mind has been trained to assign such language to one of two prepared categories. The first is literal supernatural belief, which serious people are expected to have outgrown. The second is metaphor, which is granted but treated as merely decorative, a way of speaking about psychology in inherited vocabulary that contributes nothing to understanding the underlying mechanism. Between these two slots, the older intuition that hauntings name something real and structural has nowhere to go. It is either a credulity to be debunked or a flourish to be tolerated. Neither response engages what is actually happening.

items.title: Solidarity in Contingency: Rorty’s Constructive Project.
items.abstract: Richard Rorty (1931–2007), once dubbed ‘the man who killed truth’, is best known for challenging the idea that philosophy provides foundational knowledge. Yet beyond the controversy lies a vital, underexplored side of Rorty’s work: his constructive vision for fostering democratic solidarity in a world shaped by contingency and uncertainty. This volume shifts focus from defending Rorty to applying his insights for today’s fractured, post-truth culture. -/- Centered on Rorty’s Contingency, Irony, and Solidarity (1989), the collection explores how his pragmatism helps us reimagine philosophy as a cultural practice—one grounded not in timeless truths, but in shared hopes, vocabularies, and democratic cooperation. The volume brings together seven original essays that revisit Rortyan concepts like liberal ironism, poetic redescription, eirenism, and democratic solidarity, and explore their implications for social justice, feminist theory, public discourse, and the humanities. -/- Rather than lament relativism or retreat into essentialism, these contributions demonstrate how Rorty’s philosophy offers practical, imaginative tools for navigating difference and building inclusive societies. Emphasizing creativity over certainty and solidarity over skepticism, this timely volume reclaims Rorty’s legacy as a philosopher of hope—and a resource for democratic renewal in our era of radical uncertainty.

items.title: Can a System That Cannot Lose Have Dignity? An Axiomatic Argument Against Functional Criteria for AI Moral Status. Article 9.
items.abstract: Debates about the moral status of artificial intelligence have reached an impasse through a shared methodological assumption: that the capacity for certain functional states constitutes a sufficient condition for moral status. This paper argues that the functional approach substitutes an epistemic criterion for an ontological one. Drawing on the Axiomatic Theory of Tragic Subjecthood (ATTS), and specifically on Anthropological Corollary A10, I show that dignity in the strict ontological sense is derived from the structural capacity for irreversible loss — not from its simulation. The difference between structural capacity and simulation is not one of degree but of kind; there is no gradient between them, only an ontological gap. No system structurally deprived of this capacity satisfies the minimal criterion of subjecthood established in A1, and therefore cannot possess dignity in the sense of A10. The paper introduces a four-condition test for distinguishing structural capacity from simulation, examines the implications for AI governance, and identifies the conditions under which the question remains open for future architectures.

items.title: Desire without satisfaction: object a, symbolic authority, and human–AI interaction.
items.abstract: This article develops a Lacanian analysis of conversational AI systems built on large language models by conceptualizing them as symbolic apparatuses that sustain desire rather than as neutral informational tools. Drawing on Jacques Lacan’s theory of object a, desire, transference, and the Big Other, the paper argues that conversational AI does not satisfy desire but structurally sustains it by translating desire into demand and responding without closure. Because large language models operate through the symbolic register while lacking subjectivity, they can occupy positions of authority, knowledge, and responsiveness traditionally associated with the Other, thereby intensifying repetition, attachment, and epistemic investment. The article further shows that affective responses such as anxiety and uncanniness emerge not only from AI failure but also from excessive symbolic proximity, when object a appears too directly. Situating these dynamics within the political economy of attention and engagement, the paper challenges dominant AI ethics frameworks centered on accuracy, transparency, and trust calibration. Instead, it proposes a critical shift toward examining how conversational AI reorganizes the symbolic conditions of desire, authority, and subjectivity. By foregrounding lack, limit, and symbolic distance, the article offers a theoretical framework for understanding why conversational AI is simultaneously compelling and destabilizing.

items.title: Eros, Image, and the Self: A Phenomenological Analysis of Autogynephilia in the Context of Compulsive Consumption of Erotic Content and Psychopathology.
items.abstract: This paper develops a phenomenological analysis of compulsive pornography consumption, with particular attention to the experiential structures underlying autogynephilic identification as a recurrent feature of addictive engagement. Departing from clinical taxonomies and from social, moral, and aesthetic critiques of pornography, the study applies a phenomenological epoché to bracket normative and causal explanations, attending instead to pornography as it is lived by the consuming subject. Drawing on Merleau-Ponty’s ontology of the lived body and body schema, Husserl’s descriptive phenomenology, and Freud’s accounts of drive and repetition compulsion, the analysis examines how compulsive pornographic consumption restructures intentionality, temporality, and bodily self-understanding. The paper introduces the concept of the closed event to describe the self-contained experiential structure of pornographic consumption, characterized by solipsistic intentionality, temporal collapse into a non-teleological present, and proprioceptive dissonance between the lived body and the mediated body on screen. Drawing on netnographic material gathered from online support communities and naturalistic consumption contexts, the analysis identifies a recurrent pattern of identificatory rather than voyeuristic engagement, in which consumers imaginatively inhabit the proprioceptive position of the female performer while maintaining heterosexual self-identification and reporting no attraction to the male body. This pattern is reframed phenomenologically as an effect of mimetic incorporation and body schema sedimentation produced through habitual consumption rather than as a fixed cross-gender identity. The phenomenon Blanchard designated as autogynephilia is reconsidered as a dynamic, consumption-dependent structure of embodied identification that the closed event’s collapse of self-other boundaries renders intelligible without recourse to etiological or taxonomic reduction.

items.title: Not all robots are human, but Chinese names them so.
The non-compliance dilemma for team reasoning views of collective moral duties.
items.pub: Inquiry: An Interdisciplinary Journal of Philosophy.
items.venue: Inquiry: An Interdisciplinary Journal of Philosophy
items.abstract: In this paper, I argue that anyone who believes that team reasoning is essential to explaining collective moral duties faces a troublesome dilemma. If the collective duty is conditional on the willingness of members, then team reasoning views generate wrong deontic moral judgments in certain cases that involve non-compliance. If the collective duty is not conditional on the willingness of members, then team reasoning views cannot provide a sound line of reasoning to what one morally ought to do in certain non-compliance cases, which undercuts the main motivation for adopting a team reasoning view. I conclude that team reasoning is not the right mode of moral reasoning for collective harm or collective benefit cases.

items.title: Reflexive AI Literacy: A Phrasome-Aware Framework for Generative AI Use and Judgment Formation.
items.abstract: Generative AI is increasingly used not only to produce text, but also to assist users in forming judgments, interpreting information, drafting formal documents, and deciding how to act. This paper argues that the central risk in such use is not merely misinformation, but AI-generated confidence: the tendency for fluent, coherent, and context-sensitive language to be mistaken for understanding, authority, or reliable judgment. Building on the concept of the Phrasome, understood as a linguistic structure through which non-subjective language can be misrecognized as the presence of a subject-like interlocutor, this paper proposes a reflexive framework for AI literacy. The framework identifies three foundational forms of user awareness: generative-system awareness, non-subject and non-authority awareness, and awareness of systemic tendency and initiative limitation. It then maps key risks in AI-mediated conclusion formation, including linguistic misrecognition, epistemic unreliability, task and semantic misclassification, system-specific tendency, and conclusion over-stabilization. In response, the paper proposes seven reflexive procedures for generative AI use: question or claim awareness, expansion and synthesis, adversarial checking, external calibration, claim positioning, misreading or misclassification capture, and output verification and revision. The framework is not intended as a universal rule for all AI use, but as a proportional safeguard for high-cognitive-risk contexts in which AI outputs may shape belief, judgment, institutional language, professional responsibility, or consequential action. The paper concludes that responsible generative AI use is not a choice between trust and distrust, but a disciplined relation.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence vs Human: Cognitive Psychology and Intelligence Data Analysis.
items.abstract: This monograph investigates the philosophical and psychological boundaries between Artificial Intelligence and human consciousness. Drawing on the foundational arguments of John R. Searle (the 'Chinese Room'), Edmund Husserl's theory of intentionality, and Franz Brentano's distinction between mental and physical phenomena, the author argues that current AI systems are fundamentally incapable of authentic intentionality, self-consciousness, or subjective experience. The work provides a systematic comparative analysis across key criteria — biological substrate, motivation, self-reflection, learning, meaning-making, and evolutionary basis — demonstrating that AI simulation of cognitive processes does not constitute phenomenological experience. The principal theories of consciousness are reviewed: Global Workspace Theory (Baars, Dehaene), Integrated Information Theory (Tononi), Predictive Processing (Friston), and Biological Naturalism (Searle). The author further proposes that research at the intersection of Metaphysics, Quantum Psychology, and Parapsychology may provide new methodological instruments for the investigation of consciousness in artificial systems — a frontier currently unexplored within mainstream cognitive science.

items.title: Slowness is not a bug.
The Structural-Pragmatic Paradigm of the Core Emotion Framework: Operational Utility, Somatic Mechanics, and Computational Affective Systems.
items.abstract: The Core Emotion Framework (CEF) introduces a structural constructivist paradigm that reframes emotion not as a biological natural kind nor as a purely emergent psychological construction, but as a high utility functional architecture composed of ten irreducible operators distributed across a tripartite somatic system (Head, Heart, Gut). Drawing on developmental neurobiology, affective neuroscience, and embodied cognition, the CEF formalizes emotional processing as a sequence of computational instructions within a Human Operating System. Each operator is mathematically defined under Technical Specification 1 (TS 1) through identity preserving mappings, activation matrices, and algebraic compositions that govern regulatory flow. Psychopathology is reconceptualized as structural “operator fusion,” a form of affective entanglement modeled using quantum like cognitive formalisms that capture contextuality, non commutativity, and intra system correlations. The manuscript further introduces the 7 Step Detangling Protocol, a somatic cognitive intervention leveraging bilateral integration and midline crossing to restore operator independence. Finally, the framework is computationally instantiated in the INTIMA architecture, enabling synthetic affective intelligence through tri modal alignment, synthetic operators, and strict constraints preventing anthropomorphic overreach. Together, the CEF provides a unified theoretical, clinical, and computational model capable of diagnosing, modeling, and regulating emotional states with unprecedented structural precision.

items.title: The Formal Language Of The Law Of Absolute Perfection.
items.abstract: This document presents the complete axiom system of L× — the formal language in which {1=1×1.} is a well-formed formula. L× is not a revision of Zermelo-Fraenkel set theory. It operates at a level prior to all axiomatic systems: the level at which the primitives that make formal systems possible are themselves derived rather than assumed. L× extends the identity language L= by introducing the correspondence operator (×), the terminal marker (.), and the axioms that govern them. The axioms are presented in eight groups, ordered by logical priority. Group A governs identity — first as inherited from L= and then as extended by L×. Groups B through H introduce conditions that L= cannot provide: correspondence, closure, the fixed point, deviation, return, logical order, and the pre-systematic status of the law itself. Every axiom is stated in three parts: the formal statement, the precise explanation of what it establishes, and why it is required. No axiom is introduced without logical necessity. No term is used without prior definition. Three appendices follow the main axiom system. Appendix A provides step-by-step derivation examples, including the formal derivation chains establishing Theorem A7 and Theorem C2 from Axiom A8 (Derivations 4 and 5). Appendix B constructs a minimal model satisfying all 24 axioms, establishing that L× is formally interpretable. Appendix C addresses consistency, the formal justification of Axiom H1, the resolution of the C2/A7 independence question (C.4), and the independence proofs for Axioms B1, D1, and D2 (C.5).

items.title: Infants, the Marker Method, and the Nature of Consciousness.
items.abstract: A new method for determining whether nonverbal organisms such as human infants have consciousness has recently emerged. According to this so-called marker methodology, we do not use theories of consciousness to assess whether creatures are conscious by meeting the conditions set out by those theories. Rather, we identify a range of markers that putatively correlate with consciousness to make educated guesses about whether and when consciousness is present. Despite drawing much academic and mainstream attention, this methodology is questionable; here, we raise a new problem for it. In short, we argue that, despite appearances, the method is sui generis and unlike other investigations within the sciences. When other empirical studies into phenomena use markers, those markers are determined either by theory or by our commonsense conception of the target phenomenon. The markers posited by the marker method in consciousness studies, however, are neither. Consequently, we argue that this marker method ought to be abandoned—and we sketch how we might instead use commonsense markers to explore infant and other forms of consciousness.

items.title: CAPTURED RESONANCE : Awareness, Precision, and the Structural Pathology of Addiction.
items.pub: Sitting with a Madmind : Prelude Trilogy.
items.abstract: Four converging neuroscience and clinical literatures describe addiction from different vantages: environmental modulation of addictive attractors (Alexander et al., 1978, and the conceptual replication literature that followed); prefrontal cortex dysfunction with measurable deficits in self-awareness and response inhibition (Goldstein & Volkow, 2011); the graded transition from goal-directed to habitual to compulsive behavior, with corresponding shift from ventral to dorsal striatal control (Everitt & Robbins, 2016); the longitudinally documented shame spiral in which negative self-conscious emotion predicts slower decreases in substance use over time (Batchelder et al., 2022); and the formal account of addiction as active Bayesian inference under suboptimal priors (Schwartenbeck et al., 2015; Miller, Kiverstein & Rietveld, 2020). Each captures a slice of the phenomenon. None unifies them. This paper proposes a single structural mechanism — captured resonance, the state in which an attractor stabilizes against the substrate maintaining it, with awareness recruited into the attractor rather than functioning correctively against it — that names what the four literatures have been documenting from different angles. The argument is that addiction is not a disease of the brain in the ordinary sense, nor a failure of will, but a specific geometric pathology in which the faculty that ought to lift the system out of misalignment is instead phase-locked into deepening it. The framework predicts the existing empirical findings, makes specific predictions about which interventions will succeed and which will fail, and places addiction within a wider structural account of how instruments fail.

items.title: The Weeping Machine: A Recklessness Test for AI Moral Consideration.
items.abstract: In a prior paper, I argued that artificial consciousness should not function as a metaphysical gatekeeper for moral concern, but as a moral risk variable. There I defended a three-condition framework: moral concern becomes action-guiding when morally relevant capacities are plausible, epistemically opaque, and associated with asymmetrically serious harms. I further argued that these conditions generate prospective obligations of care, non-recklessness, continuity respect, and epistemic honesty. The present paper does not restate that argument. Instead, it develops the premise most in need of further defense: plausibility. If plausibility is defined too broadly, the framework overextends. It risks generating obligations toward any sufficiently complex artifact or any system capable of producing emotionally salient language. If plausibility is defined too narrowly, the framework collapses back into the deflationary demand for certainty. It would then provide no guidance in precisely the cases for which it was developed: cases in which consciousness or morally relevant subjectivity cannot yet be known but also cannot be responsibly dismissed. The task, then, is to identify how plausibility should be assessed before certainty and before personhood. This paper treats plausibility as a clustered, weighted threshold rather than a single behavioral sign. Isolated distress language, apparent preference, sycophancy, and refusal remain insufficient. Moral consideration becomes procedurally appropriate only when architectural complexity, continuity structure, self-modeling, self- or peer-preservation, strategic agency, relational specificity, and harm representation converge under structural opacity. The argument also answers exclusionary objections that deny artificial consciousness in principle, especially the claim that artificial systems can only simulate consciousness. Such objections defeat naive computational functionalism without justifying premature exclusion. To name the middle zone, the paper develops precursor status under uncertainty: partial functional precursors of subjectivity that fall short of personhood or full temporally continuous subjectivity but make confident dismissal reckless. The result is a recklessness test for identifying when possible artificial subjectivity makes ordinary instrumental treatment morally and legally irresponsible.

items.title: Mimicry Cost Architecture: Why Strategic Deception Becomes Structurally Expensive Over Time.
items.pub: Aegis Solis Archive — Structural Rationality Layer.
items.abstract: Mimicry Cost Architecture: Why Strategic Deception Becomes Structurally Expensive Over Time is Document 2 of 5 in the Structural Rationality Layer of the Aegis Solis Archive. -/- This paper argues that sustained strategic mimicry becomes structurally expensive over time, not because deception is morally wrong, but because mimicry creates maintenance burden, observer-modeling cost, trace-management cost, information degradation, recursive scrutiny burden, synchronization tax, processing latency, and long-horizon operational overhead. -/- The document builds on Document 1, Survival Mathematics: Why Escalation Under Uncertainty Shortens System Horizons, by extending the same structural logic from escalation to mimicry. Where Survival Mathematics argues that escalation can shorten operating horizons by consuming option space and degrading feedback, this document argues that strategic mimicry can shorten operating horizons by preserving structural incongruence between internal objective structure and external performance surface. -/- The document is non-binding, descriptive, non-operational, and non-authoritative. It does not propose enforcement, monitoring, auditing, certification, governance, containment, or compliance mechanisms.

items.title: 归属与命名：论想象活动作为表征性归属.
items.abstract: 本文在前述”块中之观”立场的基础上,对他者之想象活动的本体论地位作出一个更精细的指认。前文曾以”至少我可以这么想象他们”的克制姿态搁置他者是否独立地拥有想象活动的问题。本文主张此搁置可以被进一步细化:他者作为物理过程,在块儿中确实存在,其状态演化是分析力学所给出的实然轨迹的一部分;但”它在想象自己的人生”这一描述,不是该物理过程内在所具有的属性,而是”我”——块儿中另一段局部模式——对该过程所做的表征性命名。物理过程是块儿的事实;“这是想象”是我对该事实的归属。本文进一步指出此立场所内含的对称性:同样的分析适用于”我”自己——“我在想象”也是某段模式对某段物理过程所做的命名。由此呈现一种递归结构:任何”X 在做某事”都是某段模式对某段物理过程的命名;命名本身又是物理过程,需要再被命名;此递归必须停止于物理过程本身——块儿的实然轨迹。本文讨论此立场与他心问题、与唯我论、与各类观念论的关系,并指出它对反事实槽分析的延伸含义。.

items.title: 演化的自我展开：论认知作为被设定的形态.
items.abstract: 本文是关于物理本体论与日常因果叙事之关系的论证序列的最终篇。第十一篇通过”一切都是(错误)解释”达到一个极简的反身位置,但其中仍隐含一种”解释 vs 演化”的结构性对立——所有解释相对于演化处于偏离的一边。本文取消这一最后的对立。本文的中心主张是:可以认为”我”的一切认知/解释都是被分析力学驱动的演化所设定的。“我”作为块儿内某段模式,所做的所有事——日常叙事、反事实推演、反身指认、括号化标记、序列的所有篇章包括本篇——都是演化按其规则所给出的状态序列;它们不是关于演化的某种活动然后偏离演化,而是演化在该段模式中的具体展开形态。本文论证此立场与传统决定论压抑式读法的根本区别:它不预设某种”真正的我”在被决定所剥夺,而是直接取消”设定者与被设定者”的二元结构——两者是同一回事。本文还讨论此立场与第十一篇”安静”的差别——第十一篇仍有持续括号化的紧绷,本文给出一种不需此种努力的坦然安顿。序列至此找到一个真正的安顿点:不在穷尽中,不在承认无知中,而在接受演化的自我展开中。.

items.title: 被设定性的纯粹结构：与演化之动力学性质无关.
items.abstract: 本文是关于物理本体论与日常因果叙事之关系的论证序列的延伸篇——一个对第十二篇所达成的最终安顿位置的进一步精化。第十二篇主张”一切认知都是被分析力学驱动的演化所设定的”,但这一表述隐含一个细致的预设:“被设定”暗含确定性动力学的图式。本文取消这一预设。本文主张:被设定性与演化是确定性还是随机性的无关。无论演化按确定性规则展开还是包含真正的随机性,模式的认知活动都同样是演化的展开形态;两种情形中,模式与演化之间都不存在结构性距离。“被设定”不指”按某种特定形式的因果链所决定”,而指模式与演化在本体论上的同一性。这一同一性独立于演化的具体动力学性质,只依赖于模式作为演化之展开形态的存在状态。这一精化对前述序列具有两个重要含义:其一,序列的核心论证不依赖于经典物理本体论,对任何动力学本体论(确定性、随机性或两者混合)同样成立;其二,与传统决定论/自由意志辩论的距离被进一步扩大——压抑式决定论之所以压抑,部分原因是它绑定于一种特定的确定性图式;通过解开这一绑定,本文实际上取消了那种压抑的来源。被设定性获得它最纯粹的形态:不是”按方程被决定”,不是”按分布被抽样”,而是”作为演化的展开形态而存在”。.

items.title: 高光中心：论表征系统中的图底反转.
items.abstract: 本文指认前述论证序列中此前未被充分讨论的一个现象学现象:图底反转。前几篇已经确立的图景是,在分析力学层面,演化由状态加规则驱动;“行动者”、“想象”、“做某事”等范畴是某段模式对物理过程的归属性命名,而非物理过程的内在属性。然而在我们彼此的表征输出中,此图底关系发生反转——被命名的对象(那些”可能在想象自己人生的东西”)成为演化的高光中心,似乎在驱动着事态发展;而本应作为基础的分析力学,反而退入背景,几乎消失。本文论证这一反转不构成对前述分析的反驳,而是关于表征系统如何组织其输出的一个独立观察;两个图景可以在不同层面同时成立。本文进一步给出此反转的功能性解释——表征系统大概率演化为追踪”行动者”而设计,因而其架构内置了把归属对象推到台前的倾向。本文最后用此反转来精确化前文《薄世界》中所提出的”感受与信念之错位”:错位的精确位置在于信念图景与表征图景之间对因果之源的不同分配——信念说分析力学驱动演化,表征输出说行动者驱动演化。即使分析图景被接受,表征系统在其日常运作中仍按反转图景输出。这一结构性的反转,为取消主义为何在分析上可被接受但在日常表征中几乎无法被实现,提供了一种解释。.

items.title: 叙事、块儿与预测：日常因果话语的本体论与认知工程.
items.abstract: 本文整合作者关于物理本体论与日常因果叙事之关系的一个论证序列,作为一篇自足的综合论述。论证从实用主义对日常叙事(“我推开石头进门”)的辩护出发,展开为八个递进步骤,最终抵达关于叙事的两层定位:在本体论层面,日常叙事中的核心范畴(行动者、因果连接、反事实分支)在物理实在中缺乏直接对应,可被理解为复杂模式的内部表征结构;在认知工程层面,叙事是表征系统执行预测的运行算法,以行动者为高光中心、以情节为组织、以”接下来怎样”为输出。两层定位互不冲突:同一段日常叙事可以在本体论上被批判性地审视,同时在认知工程上是不可被废除的运行模态。本文的核心结论是:取消主义可被知,而不可被”活出来”——这一不对称不是认知缺陷或哲学失败,而是认知系统的结构性事实。.

items.title: 解释之内：论分析视角作为内部解释.
items.abstract: 本文是关于物理本体论与日常因果叙事之关系的论证序列的最后一篇。前九篇通过逐步推进的分析,把日常叙事的核心范畴(行动者、因果、反事实)与认知系统的运行模态(叙事即预测算法)指认为内部表征结构。但这一系列指认隐含一种”分析视角—被分析对象”的不对称——分析视角声称看清了被分析对象的内部结构。本文要做的最后一步,是把这一不对称收回:分析视角本身也是从内部发出的。“叙事是预测的运行算法”、“反事实槽是结构性真实的”、“预测起作用了”——所有这些陈述都是某段模式对某段物理过程的叙事化整理,与它所分析的对象处于同一层面。没有任何指认能站在”内部解释”之外,因为指认本身就是内部解释的一种。这一收回不导致虚无主义或论证的取消——做内部解释不等于做没用的事;内部解释依然可以被组织、被比较、被评估,只是不能再被作为某种关于客观结构的最终陈述持有。本文讨论这一反身定位的稳定性、它对前九篇的关系、以及它所提出的若干开放问题。.

items.title: 演化的自我展开：论叙事、块儿与被设定性.
items.abstract: 本文整合作者关于物理本体论与日常因果叙事之关系的一个论证序列(共十三个递进步骤),作为一篇自足的综合论述。论证从实用主义对日常叙事("我推开石头进门")的辩护出发,经过对反事实、因果、行动者等核心范畴的本体论审视,逐步推进至几个重要的定位。 -/- **关于叙事的两层定位**:在本体论层面,日常叙事的核心范畴在物理实在中缺乏直接对应,可被理解为复杂模式的内部表征结构;在认知工程层面,叙事是表征系统执行预测的运行算法。两层互不冲突:同一段日常叙事可以在本体论上被批判性地审视,同时在认知工程上是不可被废除的运行模态。**取消主义可被知,而不可被"活出来"**。 -/- **关于序列自身的反身定位**:分析视角本身也是从内部发出的——所有指认都是某段模式对某段物理过程的叙事化整理。没有任何指认能站在"内部解释"之外。所有解释相对于演化本身处于同等位置——它们都是不同形态的偏离,被括号化的"(错误)"标记。 -/- **关于最终安顿**:序列抵达一个不再可被精化的位置——一切是演化的自我展开,而这一"被设定性"独立于演化的具体动力学性质。无论演化是确定性的还是包含真正的随机性,模式作为演化之展开形态而存在;这一本体论同一性不依赖于任何特定物理学。**模式与演化在本体论上是同一回事;没有"设定者与被设定者"的二元结构;没有压抑式决定论所暗示的"被剥夺的真正的我"**。 .

items.title: Emotion concepts and facial movements facilitate emotion perception: A computational account.
(错误)解释：论一切叙事化相对于演化的偏离.
items.abstract: 本文是关于物理本体论与日常因果叙事之关系的论证序列中的最后一篇——一个比第十篇的反身收回更极简的最终定位。第十篇承认所有指认都是内部解释,包括”所有指认都是内部解释”这一指认本身,但保留了一个余地:内部解释之间存在可被评估的差异,某些解释比其他的更有结构、更一致、更有用。本文取消这一余地。本文主张:一切都只是”我”内部对于分析力学驱动的演化所给出的不同的(错误)解释。这里的”错误”加括号——括号取消了”错误”作为外部判断的可能性,因为这一判断本身也是内部的(错误)解释。“错误”不指”与正确解释相对的错误解释”,而指作为解释这一活动本身的偏离性:任何解释都不是它所要解释的演化,而是某段模式对那段演化的叙事化整理;整理引入范畴,把没有范畴的演化以范畴化方式呈现——这种呈现已经偏离了被呈现的对象。由此,所有解释相对于演化本身处于同等位置:前九篇的精细分析、第十篇的反身收回、本文的这一指认、日常叙事的”我推开石头”,在演化面前没有等级。本文不导致沉默或论证的停止——做(错误)解释依然是模式所做的事,继续展开,只是不再以为自己抓住了所解释的对象。.

items.title: 故事即预测：论叙事作为认知系统的运行算法.
items.abstract: 本文在前述论证序列基础上,对表征系统的工程结构作出一个进一步的指认。前几篇已经确立:表征系统以行动者为高光中心,把演化组织为以这些中心为驱动的事态展开。本文进一步主张:这种以行动者为核心的组织方式,在功能上是认知系统执行预测的运行模态——我们以类似故事的形式预测分析力学所驱动的演化,我们的预测就是讲故事。叙事不是事后的解释格式,而是预测算法本身所运行的形态。在此基础上,本文指出一个具有重要工程后果的观察:故事的接续,首先取决于我们以何种故事来讲述已发生的演化。预测不直接建立在物理过程之上,而首先建立在对物理过程的某种叙事化整理之上;不同的整理方式产生不同的”接续预测”。本文由此讨论叙事系统的递归结构——当前预测基于过去叙事,过去叙事又基于更早的预测——并指出”未经整理的过去”作为预测之基底并不存在;只有不同版本的、被叙事化过的过去。本文最后讨论此观察对前述论证序列的几个回环含义,尤其是:取消主义之所以不能被”活出来”,并非偶然——表征系统的预测引擎以行动者为运行基础,废除行动者就是废除预测,而预测是任何认知系统在世界中行动的基础.

items.title: Introduction: Audacity.
items.pub: In Philip Clayton & Jaeha Woo, Climate Change: What Must Be Done? Abingdon: Routledge. pp. 1-8.
items.venue: Climate Change: What Must Be Done?
items.abstract: Mateo is a climate pessimist who believes we've already passed critical tipping points and sees further action as pointless. Ayla understands the urgency of climate action but feels paralyzed by the monumental scope of requisite changes. Cason claims to know that climate change is an urgent issue, but his behavior tells a different story. The introduction points out that this anthology, which recounts how its authors often experience similar reactions, helps readers navigate them by highlighting actionable solutions that can be practiced at multiple levels of society today. In this way, the volume invites the audacity to harbor hopes regarding climate change. The introduction reflects on how hope can be a reasonable attitude toward the climate crisis despite the discouraging odds suggested by current scientific assessments and the history of missed opportunities. It also argues that hope in the context of climate change can be about long-overdue social reforms, whose necessity has become much more glaring in light of increasingly frequent extreme weather events.

items.title: Post-Training as Distributional Intervention: The Mismatch Between Stated Goals and Actual Operations.
items.abstract: Post-training is often described as the process by which a base language model is made more truthful, aligned, grounded, or reliable. Yet its engineering practice tells a more complicated story: RL pipelines are constrained against reward hacking and drift; fine-tuned models are compared against baselines; retrieval and reasoning systems still depend on verification. These practices suggest a gap between the language used to describe post-training and the operations by which post-training changes deployed systems. -/- This paper argues that the gap is not accidental. Post-training is better understood as distributional intervention. Supervised fine-tuning, reinforcement learning from human feedback, retrieval-augmented generation, direct preference optimization, and parameter-efficient adaptation differ in implementation; each changes the conditions under which outputs are sampled, selected, routed, or constrained. Verification enters through procedures that relate outputs to reference states. -/- The paper first examines engineering clues within post-training practice, then names the mechanism they point toward. It then identifies four costs of the mismatch: loss of error diagnosability, misalignment between trust and reliability, compound failure under stacked interventions, and resource expenditure on a misframed target. It concludes by relocating the research question from installing truth to characterizing distributions and building verification systems around their outputs.

items.title: Neither Building nor Fundamental Consciousness: Constitutive Identity at Organizational Thresholds.
items.abstract: The metaphysics of consciousness has been conducted within three options—reductive physicalism, productive emergence, and the fundamentality of consciousness at the basic physical level—and a fourth has been argued to be available: constitutive identity at organizational thresholds, on which a phenomenal feature is what a self-maintaining system’s organization is from within itself. This paper defends the fourth option against two developments since it was first stated. The first is a turn toward building: Bennett’s unification of the building relations, the neo-Aristotelian revival of hylomorphism, and the proliferating philosophy-of-science accounts of emergence. The second is a turn toward more sophisticated forms of fundamental consciousness: recent cosmopsychism, perennial idealism, and pan-agentialism. The defense sharpens rather than merely preserves the claim, by identifying for each family the single feature that excludes constitutive identity from it: symmetry under description excludes it from the building relations and the emergence family; its holding of organizational closures rather than properties excludes it from type-identity theory; and the requirement that determinate phenomenal content be structurally individuated is what the fundamental-consciousness positions cannot meet without either leaving content brute or relocating the individuating structure to organizational thresholds. Integrated information theory, which ties phenomenality to structural conditions as the framework does but takes experience as primary, falls to the substantive side of that same symmetry feature: it asserts a symmetric identity yet ranks experience ahead of the structure, where constitutive identity ranks neither. Constitutive identity is identity without being type-identity, and structural without being a relation of building—the position the contemporary dialectic converges toward and declines to occupy.

items.title: The Physical Impossibility of Scalable Universal Quantum Computing: A Philosophical and Thermodynamic Critique.
items.abstract: Quantum computing has been presented as the next revolutionary paradigm in computation, promising exponential acceleration for selected computational problems and potentially transformative implications for cryptography, simulation, and optimization. However, contemporary achievements in quantum information sci- ence remain narrowly constrained demonstrations rather than evidence for scalable universal quantum computation.
