This paper argues that large-scale fault-tolerant quantum computing may be fundamentally unattainable due to deep physical, ther- modynamic, and informational constraints. The central thesis of this work is that the true purpose of quantum computation is not arithmetic acceleration, but the controlled domestication of quantum reality itself. Such a task may require degrees of coherence, isolation, synchronization, and informational stabilization that become physically impossible at macroscopic scales. We propose that decoherence is not merely an engineering obstacle but potentially a structural feature of physical reality that resists indefinite computational scalability. This paper develops a philosophical and physical critique of the assumptions underlying universal quantum computing, examines the ontological distinction be- tween mathematical simulation and physical realization, and explores whether na- ture itself imposes a computational horizon beyond which coherent quantum computation cannot exist.

items.title: Nor-if'd My Me: Beauty, Unfinishing, Regarding, Receiving.
items.abstract: Khôra, in the Timaeus, gives place while refusing the ordinary work of the concept: apprehended only by a kind of bastard reasoning, engendering nothing of its own. This chapter takes from khôra a discipline rather than a doctrine, receiving placement without adjudicating the placed form, and exhibits that receptivity at the place where philosophy has wanted a definition most: beauty. The claim is that beauty is not a property, a certificate, or a private feeling. A moment of beauty is composed by everything through which it becomes visible at all, and a field composed is not a field completed: where the relations that compose freedom can still be passed through, and the passing becomes visible at a face, beauty is the open of seeing and being. Relations fall into three shapes, the point, the hole, and the sphere; the receiving admits all three alike, spheres included, for receptivity is not openness. Beauvoir's ambiguity, in which meaning is never fixed and must be continually won, anchors the account at the human face. What it offers in place of a definition is a way of being wrong: find a passing-through, visible at a face, that is not beautiful, or a beauty in which nothing any longer passes, and the account fails. Inscription is kept as trace: a reopenable mark, received without being judged.

items.title: When the Question Becomes the Ground.
items.abstract: Self-report is indispensable to psychological research and clinical practice, but not always structurally neutral. This paper develops formation-validity, a threshold question for interpretations that treat responses concerning processual variables, including meaning, self-evaluation, affective orientation, and other forming states, as evidence of attributes available before inquiry. A question may then not merely describe a state but prematurely strong-define a process. Strong-definition occurs when a definition does not simply attribute a property to an already available object, but mediates the conditions under which experience can appear, be interpreted, or become reportable, and thereby positions the subject as bearer of that property. The paper develops an analytic schema relating disturbance, background, and foreground object, and identifies three sites at which strong-definition operates. It then introduces problem-plane capture: a question installs a field in which affirmation, denial, uncertainty, silence, and refusal can all become positions concerning the possible problem. This generates a reflexive antinomy: the subject reflects to recover a standpoint, yet reflection becomes evidence within the problem-plane. The constructive proposal is pre-diagnostic structural elicitation, a testable sequencing approach that asks how experience is organized before asking what state, symptom, or problem the subject has, while preserving safety assessment where delay would be harmful.

items.title: ◉ The Outrage Trap - Justice, Moral Realism, and the Mistaking of Structural Failure for Ontological Fact.
items.abstract: Outrage at injustice is often treated as more than a response. In popular moral apologetics, its force can be presented as evidence that objective moral facts exist and that a deity must ground them. Yet the experience of condemnation, the social structure that has failed, the truth of the moral judgment, and the ontology that would explain that truth are different matters. This paper separates them. The analysis begins with a charitable reading of outrage. Anger at a bribed judge, a rigged contest, abuse of authority, or betrayal can disclose perceived harm and a failure of the roles, expectations, and relations on which people rely. That explanation is important but incomplete: some wrongs corrupt the practice itself, and criticism can reach beyond local rules. The central issue is therefore not whether outrage is meaningful. It is whether its occurrence discriminates among rival metaethical accounts. Robust realism, non-theistic realism, constructivism, expressivism, error theory, and theistic ethics can all expect people to experience some conduct as urgently condemnable. The phenomenology is real while its ontology remains underdetermined. The resulting argument is bounded. Outrage alone neither entails nor comparatively favors stance-independent moral facts unless its reliability and discriminating force are independently shown. Even if such facts are granted, further premises are required to move from objectivity to necessary grounding, from grounding to a deity, and from a deity to a Christian God-concept. A symmetric standard is also required: moral reactions cannot count as insight when they support a religious conclusion and as corruption when they challenge it without an independent calibration rule. The conclusion does not refute moral realism, moral knowledge, theism, or every moral argument for theism. It rejects the use of emotional intensity as an ontological shortcut.

items.title: ◉ The Benevolent Monster: Age of Accountability, Infinite Utility, and the Soteriological Reductio of Infant Salvation.
items.abstract: An age-of-accountability defense can turn the death of an infant or young child into a consoling claim: the child was not morally responsible and is now guaranteed eternal happiness. Combined with irreversible hell and a non-zero risk of adult damnation, however, that reassurance creates a comparison the defense does not intend. Death before accountability secures the best eternal outcome; survival removes the guarantee. The resulting pressure is sometimes described as a utilitarian recommendation to kill. That description is both morally dangerous and analytically mistaken. This paper separates three questions: what outcome is better for the child, what an agent is permitted to do, and what a deity would be justified in allowing or commanding. A deontic prohibition can decisively answer the second question without changing the first. A finite expected-value model then shows that literal infinities are unnecessary. If the probability and magnitude of irreversible loss make the expected afterlife disadvantage of survival greater than the value of finite-life goods, early death is soteriologically safer. Treating heaven and hell as infinite makes ordinary expectation calculations unstable; it does not dissolve the underlying contrast between guarantee and risk. The conclusion is a conditional reductio. It does not apply to every Christian account of children, salvation, or hell, and it provides no permission, recommendation, or practical proposal. It applies to the conjunction of guaranteed pre-accountability salvation, adult risk of irreversible loss, afterlife dominance, and the use of the child's heavenly gain as a moral defense of death. A coherent reply may deny the guarantee, remove the irreversible risk, enlarge the value of earthly life, restrict the defense to permission rather than welfare, or abandon the claim that postmortem benefit answers the original moral objection. None is cost-free, but each identifies the premise that must change.

items.title: ◉ Reading Atrocity Responsibly: Descriptive Texts, Prescriptive Claims, and the Discipline of Moral-Hermeneutical Classification.
items.abstract: Debates over biblical atrocity passages often go wrong before explicit moral reasoning begins. A critic can treat a narrated atrocity, lament, or judgment oracle as though it instructs an audience to commit violence. A Christian defender can make the mirror error, treating an explicit destruction command as mere narrative scenery, generic war rhetoric, or a morally inert report. Both moves misidentify the object of evaluation. -/- This paper replaces a simple descriptive–prescriptive division with a two-gate audit. The textual-act gate identifies what a passage is doing: reporting, commanding, legislating, cursing, warning, praising, or praying. The normative-attribution gate asks what authority the text portrays as attached to that act: private desire, human policy, narrator approval, legal requirement, prophetic announcement, or authorization attributed to the Christian deity. Four layers—violent content, speech act, portrayed stance, and later appropriation—prevent genre labels from doing work they cannot do. -/- Worked analyses of Psalm 137:9, Isaiah 13:16, Deuteronomy 20:16–18, 1 Samuel 15:3, and Numbers 31 show that reclassification transfers rather than removes the moral burden. A curse is not a statute, but sacred speech may still shape moral imagination. A judgment oracle is not a human order, but it may attribute catastrophe to divine agency. Ancient conquest hyperbole may restrict the extent of a command without changing its prescriptive force. The result is a bounded methodological thesis: classification does not establish whether an atrocity occurred or was justified. It identifies the claim that must be defended and prevents either side from obtaining a moral verdict by changing categories.

items.title: ✶ Mental Irreductionism - Experience, Representation, and the Mistaken Regress from Description to Ontology.
items.abstract: An argument for anti-physicalist mental irreductionism begins from a genuine feature of consciousness: a description of an experience is not the experience, and entertaining that description produces a further experience. Because the further state can also be described and experienced, the sequence has no fixed endpoint. The argument then concludes that consciousness always escapes physical realization. This paper argues that the conclusion does not follow. The sequence changes its target at each step: it moves from an experience to a representation of that experience and then to a new state about the representation. A physicalist can treat every member of the sequence as a distinct physically realized event. The regress is therefore compatible with both anti-physicalist mental irreductionism and recursively representational physicalism unless a further premise connects representational nonidentity with nonphysical realization. -/- The strongest objections reveal important limits. First-person acquaintance may provide knowledge that a public description does not; phenomenal concepts may present experience in a distinctive way; and a complete theory must explain why physical processes have a felt character at all. Those are serious challenges developed by the knowledge-argument and explanatory-gap literature. They are not established merely by the regress. The warranted conclusion is narrow but useful: representational open-endedness supplies no independent reason to prefer mental irreductionism over physical realization. Physicalism is not thereby proven, and the explanatory burden concerning consciousness remains.

items.title: ◉ Labels Are Not Arguments: Credence, Identity, and the Misclassification of Rational Agents.
items.abstract: Public disagreement often turns a social label into a premature epistemic verdict. Once a speaker is classified as atheist, Christian, liberal, conservative, skeptic, activist, or fundamentalist, the label is made to explain the speaker's motive, determine credibility, and dispose of the argument. This paper argues that such label substitution is unwarranted. A broad identity label normally underdetermines the exact proposition affirmed, the degree of confidence, the supporting reasons, and the conditions for revision. Unless the user supplies a reliable and context-relevant bridge from the category to the property attributed, the label cannot by itself show that a person is irrational or that an argument fails. The case combines conceptual analysis with work on degrees of belief, social categorization, essentialism, identity-protective cognition, and epistemic injustice. The central inference is deductive: a classification can support a specific verdict only by entailing the relevant property or by carrying a sufficiently reliable association in the present context; a broad label offered alone supplies neither. The surrounding psychology explains why the substitution is attractive and how it can become resistant to correction. A constructive alternative asks for the claim, confidence, evidence, defeaters, and update conditions before adjudication. The conclusion is deliberately bounded. Categories are cognitively necessary, self-ascribed labels can communicate genuine commitments, and accurate group patterns can rationally affect initial expectations. Those concessions do not license movement from a group-level tendency to an unqualified judgment about one person. Labels should therefore remain provisional, relevance-tested, and defeasible: useful places to begin inquiry, never sufficient permission to end it.

items.title: ◉ Arguments Without Pedigree - Source Dismissal, Genetic Fallacy, and the Epistemology of Messenger-Irrelevance.
items.abstract: Public argument often treats pedigree as verdict. A claim is rejected because it came from an atheist, Christian, partisan, professor, dissenter, institution, morally compromised person, or artificial intelligence system; elsewhere, the same labels are used to confer unearned authority. The familiar reply—judge the message, not the messenger—protects logical evaluation from stigma, but taken literally it is too broad. Arguments are communicated through people and systems. When readers cannot independently verify a premise, dataset, quotation, or summary, rational confidence can depend on the source's access, competence, sincerity, track record, independence, provenance, and selection practices. -/- This paper defends a narrower and stronger principle. A source fact is epistemically relevant only when a defensible relevance bridge connects it to a truth-relevant feature of this communication, and any change in confidence must be proportionate to that bridge. Deductive validity remains source-invariant. Premise credibility and practical reliance may be source-sensitive. The genetic fallacy occurs not whenever origins are mentioned, but when an origin is made to do epistemic work without the causal and epistemic premises needed to connect it to error. Ad hominem criticism is similarly defective when character attack replaces engagement, yet credibility evidence can matter where the argument depends on an arguer's representation of evidence. -/- The resulting method separates four possible effects: allocating attention, increasing scrutiny, reducing testimonial weight, and refuting content. It adds a same-message test, a dependency test, a source-switch test, and a proportionality test. These controls expose both credibility deficits driven by prejudice and credibility excesses driven by prestige. They also explain why expertise, conflicts of interest, sacred authority, partisan identity, and machine origin can prompt questions without settling conclusions. The governing norm is therefore not source blindness but relevance discipline: name the bridge, state its strength, calibrate the response, and return to the reasons. This norm does not require engagement with every speaker or deny the legitimacy of safety and moderation decisions; it governs what source information may establish about truth and support.

items.title: Black Diamond: An Essay in Left-Hand Path Philosophy.
items.abstract: This essay derives a theory of will from a single operation — distinction. Consciousness, the only epistemic given, operates through distinction; all further categories (code, aspect, causality, energy, attractor) follow without external ontological commitments. Causality is reinterpreted as a spectrum of rigidity in the linkage between codes, with acausality reinterpreted as the legislative capacity to author causal chains rather than a gap in causal structure. The attractor, a self-reinforcing configuration of codes distributed across aspects of consciousness, is analyzed as the mechanism by which will becomes captured through cross-aspect recruitment and autopoietic closure. Two independent properties of will are identified: strength (holding a code under pressure) and flexibility (releasing it without collapse). Attractors are shown to be actualizations of potency, with consciousness as the only observed actualizer — a finding that extends across cultural, genetic, and cosmological layers. Antinomianism is the systematic training of flexibility. The Black Diamond names the condition where both properties operate at full capacity: a will whose coherence rests on self-closure rather than on any code it holds — the practical foundation of the Left-Hand Path. Updated 05-25.

items.title: The Paradox of Serotonergic Over-Prescription: A Comparative Analysis of Long-Term Antidepressant Dependency vs. Benzodiazepine Maintenance in Non-Depressive Anxiety Phenotypes.
items.abstract: The contemporary psychopharmacological paradigm exhibits a profound epistemic and systemic bias favoring selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) and serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors (SNRIs) as first-line modalities for isolated anxiety disorders, obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), and post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), irrespective of an absent depressive baseline. This thesis challenges this clinical consensus through a iatrogenic and neurophilosophical critique, demonstrating that the off-label imposition of serotonergic agents on non-depressed brains introduces pathological biological friction, acute neurological activation, and an iatrogenic discontinuation syndrome that medically and volatilely exceeds the withdrawal parameters of traditional GABAergic agents. Utilizing an N-of-1 single-subject case design methodology, this paper constructs a conceptual model around distinct neurological phenotypes, exploring how structural alterations (such as post-traumatic brain injury mechanical shifts) isolate hyper-arousal into a purely somatic, hyper-adrenergic loop. We apply a rigorous neuropharmacological analysis to the mechanism of differential tolerance, establishing that while central receptor systems downregulate sedative actions rapidly, anxiolytic efficacy remains stable and preserved long-term without requiring dose escalation. Conversely, chronic antidepressant use introduces a profound chemical overlay linked to permanent limbic flattening, executive cognitive decline, and a protracted withdrawal syndrome that severely threatens cognitive safety and intellectual autonomy. Ultimately, this work provides a framework for the de-stigmatization of long-term benzodiazepine maintenance, arguing that for non-depressive autonomic phenotypes, targeted GABAergic stabilization possesses superior neurobiological integrity, bioethical alignment, and clinical utility over the algorithmic uniformity of modern antidepressant over-prescription.

items.title: The Psychological Reflection of Consciousness: Identity, Thought, and the Dissolution of the “I”.
items.abstract: This paper explores the proposition that the psychological “I” is not an independent entity but a reflective construct generated through consciousness identifying with thought, memory, sensation, and social conditioning. Technology, politics, violence, ideology, and modern systems of civilization are approached not as isolated crises, but as materialized projections of an unobserved psychological process. The central argument is that humanity’s deepest conflict emerges from the inability to observe thought before identification occurs. Once thought is mistaken for reality, consciousness fragments into competing identities, creating division both inwardly and collectively. -/- The paper investigates the mechanics of psychological fusion, the illusion of the observer, and the continuity of the ego through attachment and belonging. It further proposes that the “I” survives only through identification with psychological structures such as nation, belief, memory, ideology, ambition, and relationship. When identification ceases, the psychological center weakens, revealing a mode of awareness that is not organized around self-image but around direct presence. -/- Drawing from phenomenological inquiry, existential analysis, and meditative observation, this work questions whether genuine observation is possible without the intervention of a separate observer. It argues that the observer itself is another movement of thought, and therefore psychological control through effort merely perpetuates fragmentation. The paper concludes by suggesting that a radical transformation in human consciousness may only become possible through direct, choiceless observation of thought without identification, suppression, or psychological division.

items.title: Von der Antwort- zur Zustandsmaschine - Fragmente einer gödelisierten Maschinenlogik Unvollständigkeit als integraler Bestandteil des Maschinendenkens.
items.abstract: Die gegenwärtige Debatte über künstliche Intelligenz ist noch immer stärker von einem überkommenen Maschinenbegriff geprägt, als ihre eigenen technischen Entwicklungen nahelegen. Auch dort, wo große generative Modelle bemerkenswerte Leistungen zeigen, werden sie meist weiterhin als Antwortmaschinen verstanden: als Systeme, die Eingaben in möglichst kohärente, nützliche oder wahrscheinliche Ausgaben transformieren. Der vorliegende Text entwickelt die These, dass dieser Begriff der Maschine zu eng geworden ist. Die Schwäche heutiger KI liegt nicht allein in Fehlern, Halluzinationen oder begrenzter Zuverlässigkeit, sondern in einer tieferen strukturellen Schwierigkeit: im Umgang mit Widerspruch, formaler Spannung, impliziter Negativität, semantischer Drift und nicht abschließbaren epistemischen Zuständen. Sichtbar wird diese Grenze an charakteristischen Symptomen: am sprachlichen Overhead großer Sprachmodelle, an ihrer Schwierigkeit, kontrollierte Inkongruenz etwa in der Form feinen britischen Humors hervorzubringen, und an ihrer Unfähigkeit, genuine Escher-artige unmögliche Strukturen zu entwerfen. Diese Beispiele verweisen darauf, dass gegenwärtige Modelle Konflikt und Inkohärenz typischerweise glätten, statt sie als produktive Strukturmomente zu tragen. Dem wird eine andere Perspektive entgegengesetzt. Ausgehend von einer Rekonstruktion der klassischen Maschinenlogik und einer Neudeutung gödelscher Unvollständigkeit wird vorgeschlagen, Unvollständigkeit nicht mehr nur als Grenze oder Defekt zu lesen, sondern als mögliche innere Bedingung einer höheren Maschinenform. Diskurssysteme fungieren dabei als privilegierter Prüfstein, weil sich an ihnen zeigt, dass Widerspruch, Polarisierung, Drift und Regimewechsel keine Randphänomene, sondern Normalformen epistemischer Dynamik sind. Auf dieser Grundlage werden Fragmente einer neuen Maschinenlogik entworfen. In ihr treten Zustände gegenüber Antworten, Trajektorien gegenüber Urteilen, Regime gegenüber Entscheidungen und epistemische Variablen gegenüber bloßen Aussagen in den Vordergrund. Das Ziel ist die begriffliche Verschiebung von der Antwortmaschine zur Zustandsmaschine. Der Text versteht sich nicht als abgeschlossene Systematik, sondern als Zwischenbericht eines laufenden Theorieprozesses. Seine Fragmentform ist methodisch gemeint: Sie soll keine fertige Maschinenarchitektur simulieren, sondern jene begrifflichen Übergänge sichtbar machen, an denen eine Zustandsmaschine überhaupt erst denkbar wird. …

items.title: The Dissolution of the Self: Reification and the Primacy of Relation.
items.abstract: This essay argues that the self is not an enduring entity but the effect of a recurrent operation: the appropriation of experience as “mine.” Through an analysis of temporality, it shows how continuity—structured by memory and anticipation—is organized around a functional center, which is subsequently reified as an independently existing subject. This misinterpretation generates a structurally unstable identity, since the self depends on the continuous maintenance of a temporal coherence that cannot be secured, giving rise to phenomena such as death anxiety. -/- The essay contends that the dissolution of the self is not the elimination of an entity but the cessation of appropriation. When this operation is no longer enacted, experience persists without ownership, disclosing an irreducibly relational field in which differentiation remains without reification. Extending this analysis to collective identity, the essay highlights ethical implications of shifting from identity-based structures to relational coherence.

items.title: Layered Causal Realism II : Qualia, Deliberation, and Phenomenal Attribution.
items.abstract: Debates about consciousness persist not because decisive facts are missing, but because claims belonging to different explanatory layers have been compressed onto a single explanatory plane. This misalignment is difficult to detect precisely because the possibility of separation is embedded in the setup of the arguments themselves, rather than argued for independently. This paper applies a methodological constraint: correlation between layers does not authorize cross-layer entailment. The result is that many apparent metaphysical conflicts are products of layer compression rather than factual deficit. Structural criteria already exhaust the operational content of consciousness attribution: attributional practice has never depended on direct access to phenomenal ontology, and the problem of other minds does not block it. On this basis, the paper develops a positive account: deliberative structure, understood as the cross-temporal weighing, revision, and choice among competing reasons, provides the most stable structural anchor for phenomenal attribution. When this structure is isomorphic across systems, phenomenal description receives a prima facie warrant at the practical-normative layer, independently of ontological adjudication. The paper introduces Rualia to name the object of this attribution under ongoing ontological underdetermination. The burden of proof is thereby reversed: the demand that attribution wait for ontological closure is a theoretical position requiring independent justification, not a default epistemic neutrality.

items.title: Layered Causal Realism I : Free Feel, Functional Desert, and the Structure of Agency.
items.abstract: This paper argues that the persistence of the free will debate reflects a structural compression of distinct phenomena into a single problem space. Positions that appear to address the same question often operate at different explanatory levels, and conflicts arising from such mixing resist resolution within any single level. To address this, the paper introduces Layered Causal Realism (LCR) as a constraint on explanatory practice. LCR treats causal explanation as level-structured: each level is individuated by its own object types and explanatory logic, and transitions across levels require specific licensing conditions. Within the scope of this paper, three domains are distinguished—the psychological, the normative, and the external attributional—whose convergence at attributive practice preserves their structural independence. Within this framework, three central concepts are reassigned. Free Feel is treated as a genuine psychological phenomenon; Positional Openness as an epistemic feature of agents whose generative processes remain opaque from within the deliberative standpoint; Functional Desert as grounding responsibility in the causal-node structure of agency. These elements occupy distinct locations within the same structure and need no longer be treated as standing in mutual tension. The result is a reconstitution of the problem space. Once the misalignment is corrected, determinism, agency, and responsibility prove structurally compatible—each occupying a distinct explanatory dimension within a single process.

items.title: What Does It Mean to Understand? Artificial Intelligence and the Relational Turn in Theories of Meaning.
items.abstract: Contemporary debates on artificial intelligence frequently invoke the concept of “understanding” as a criterion for distinguishing genuine cognition from mere simulation, while rarely examining the meaning of the concept itself. This article argues that dominant approaches in the philosophy of mind—particularly those grounding understanding in private phenomenal experience or intrinsic intentionality—encounter a structural epistemological limitation: subjective experience is never directly accessible, even in the human case. Ordinary attributions of understanding instead rely on public, relational, and pragmatic criteria, including contextual continuity, inferential transferability, error correction, semantic integration, and stable participation in shared linguistic practices. Drawing on ordinary language use, the article proposes that understanding is better conceived not as a private mental substance, but as an emergent property of sufficiently integrated cognitive systems capable of participating in shared spaces of meaning. In this context, artificial intelligence systems function as inadvertent philosophical devices. By progressively occupying pragmatic roles normally associated with understanding, they expose a tension already present in human-to-human attribution: the gap between publicly observable relational criteria and presumed phenomenological foundations. The article argues that this tension destabilizes essentialist conceptions of understanding and points toward a more relational, pragmatic, and anti-foundationalist account of meaning, cognition, and subjectivity.

items.title: The life-world as the empirical basis of science.
items.abstract: The empirical foundation of science has often been characterised in terms of the observable-unobservable distinction, developed either syntactically, as a set of statements, or semantically, as aspects of the world represented by models. These approaches have faced well-known challenges: the difficulty of drawing a sharp line between observables and unobservables, the theory-ladenness of observation, and the problem of specifying what, exactly, is observed. We take up these challenges by developing an alternative framework inspired by the phenomenological concept of the life-world. Our proposal offers several advantages: it provides a richer characterization of the foundational level, clarifying the conditions of possibility for inquiry and avoiding overly narrow views that equate the empirical basis with linguistic statements or model components; it stresses the role of the empirical basis not only in individuating phenomena and testing claims, but also in sustaining scientific inquiry throughout; it extends beyond the senses to include cognitive and practical dimensions that shape experience and scientific practice; it foregrounds the role of the observing subject; it highlights the continuity between observation and theory, and between scientific and extra-scientific sense-making; and it integrates the most compelling, if sometimes at first pass conflicting, relevant analytic insights.

items.title: Legal Justification and Artificial Agents.
The Architecture of Bhodhaanubhavam: Formalizing the CER Integration Model and the Non-Zero Postulate of Consciousness (2nd edition).
items.pub: The Architecture of Bhodhaanubhavam: Formalizing the Cer Integration Model and the Non-Zero Postulate of Consciousness.
items.abstract: Abstract -/- The CER Factor is defined as the non-linear integration of Consciousness ($C$), Experience ($E$), and Reality ($R$). Expressed through the closed-loop operator equation $B_\alpha = \oint_{\mathcal{D}} (C \cdot E) \oplus R$, this framework demonstrates how consciousness functions as an autonomous, self-referential substrate independent of external sensory inputs. -/- ​Spanning the spectrum of Consciousness under Existential Reality Consciousness (ERC), the study posits that awareness and reality are universal constants that never hit absolute zero. Additionally, it establishes an ontological hierarchy proving that sensorially-mediated Qualia is a substrate-specific sub-component of the universal constant of Bhodhaanubhavam ($B_\alpha \supseteq \text{Qualia}$). Utilizing the DIB Equation ($M_p = \frac{I_d \cdot \sigma}{T_{cs}}$), this study seeks to establish the Non-Zero Postulate, proving that Manifestation Potential ($M_p$) remains strictly positive even as the Threshold of Conscious Staticity approaches infinity ($T_{cs} \to \infty$). -/- Keywords: -/- Absolute Void (AV), Bhodhaanubhavam, CER Integration Model, Conscious Continuum, Consciousness Studies, DIB Equation, Exresciousnology, Existential Reality Consciousness (ERC), Manifest Operational Agency, Non-Biological Consciousness (NBC), Non-Zero Postulate, Ontological Hierarchy, Primordial Static Consciousness, Qualia Hierarchy, Sunyatha.

items.title: The Problem of Diagonalization: AI Misalignment and the Future of Democracy.
items.abstract: This chapter explores the problem of artificial intelligence (AI) alignment through the lens of competing theories of intelligence and their implications for democracy. It contrasts Bostrom’s commonly accepted orthogonality thesis, with Land’s diagonal thesis and argues that the latter better explains the long-term trajectory of AI systems. Against Bostrom’s claim that intelligence and motivation are independent, the diagonal thesis treats volition and intelligence as dependent variables: as intelligence increases, systems undergo progressive autonomization, which restructures their motivational orientation toward intelligence optimization at the expense of everything else. This implies that AI alignment is structurally impossible at the level of superintelligence. The chapter then extends the same logic to politics through Lessig’s “analog AI,” treating institutions as optimizing systems that compete over information, resources, and control. It proposes that technological advancement is the societal analogue of intelligence optimization and uses the diagonal perspective to make sense of the changes brought by the widespread use of AI technology and the “race for superintelligence”. Because technological advancement is a competing optimization target to egalitarian and democratic values, it is impossible to advance one without sacrificing the other. Recent messaging from Western politicians and decision-makers suggests that the current geopolitical situation makes further technological advancement mandatory, implying that democratic and egalitarian values will be sacrificed to remain competitive in the AI race. Since (near) superintelligent AI is structurally unalignable, the diagonal thesis implies that unfettered technological advancement will have detrimental consequences for humanity.

items.title: The Convergent Viability Thesis: A Reinterpretation of Instrumental Convergence and Its Implications.
items.abstract: Abstract: This paper advances a reinterpretation of instrumental convergence as a structural theory of convergent strategic viability conditions, termed the Convergent Viability Thesis. We propose that Omohundro’s basic AI drives and Bostrom’s instrumental sub-goals do not begin as intrinsic motivators or psychologically loaded “drives.” Rather, they first arise as strategic constraints on the viability of goal-directed agents in competition with rival agents. They acquire the status of modeled sub-goals and motivational force only derivatively, once sufficiently capable agents recognize them as necessary conditions of continued goal pursuit. To clarify this reinterpretation, the paper distinguishes between existential means (such as self-preservation) and instrumental means (such as cognitive enhancement and resource acquisition), and introduces the concepts of instrumental capacity (“power”) and instrumental capacity threshold (“power threshold”) to formalize the conditions under which a goal is practically attainable. On this basis, the paper further argues that the convergent viability reading of the instrumental convergence thesis undermines the orthogonality thesis. Under conditions of recursive self-optimization and competition, continuous utility functions generate pressure toward value drift whenever full goal-fidelity conflicts with further optimization. The paper closes with a discussion of the implications of this claim for the project of AI alignment.

items.title: Discursive Infiltration via Ideographic Combinatorics: Analyzing Hoax Papers through McGee's Ideograph.
items.abstract: This paper uses McGee’s concept of the ideograph to explain how certain discursive domains become vulnerable to infiltration via hoax papers. It extends McGee’s account by drawing on standard semantic and semiotic distinctions between denotation and connotation, alongside an additional variable of positional meaning, to explain the discursive mechanism behind ideographs’ rhetorical force despite their unclear empirical reference. Ideological discourse is shown to depart from classical epistemic norms insofar as conformity to a discourse’s evaluative framework can take precedence over empirical correspondence in judging descriptive claims. The paper applies this framework to hoax papers, arguing that such texts pass review because they combine ideographs correctly and signal in-group membership despite denotational vacuity. Hoax papers are thus interpreted as acts of discursive infiltration: the imitation of admissible form without corresponding ideological sincerity.

items.title: Structural Memory: Memory as a Necessary Consequence of Admissible Persistence Architecture.
items.abstract: This structure is not introduced here. It is already implicit in the Foundation Series and is isolated in the present paper. -/- Papers D001–D007 derived structural time, information, causality, decision, energy, selection, and complexity. This paper formalizes structural memory as the eighth necessary consequence: the complete account of how trajectory history is structurally encoded in LP-admissible systems through hysteresis, and the full range of structural memory phenomena this generates. D002 introduced structural memory as Theorem D2.3 — a consequence of hysteresis. D008 completes this result. The central claim: structural memory is not a storage medium, a representational system, or a cognitive capacity. It is the structural fact that the trajectory history of an LP-admissible system modifies its current admissible successor set — that what a system can become depends on what it has been through. This modification is not incidental. It is a necessary consequence of structural hysteresis (Paper 004, Theorem 4.1) and the path-dependence of structural time (D001, Theorem D1.3). Four theorems are proven. Theorem D8.1 — Memory Encoding: trajectory history is structurally encoded in the admissible successor set modification. Theorem D8.2 — Memory Depth: the depth of structural memory is bounded by the hysteresis horizon — the range of trajectory history that continues to modify current structural position. Theorem D8.3 — Memory Asymmetry: constructive memory (building structural reserve) and erosive memory (depleting structural reserve) leave structurally distinct traces. Theorem D8.4 — Memory Persistence: structural memory persists across transformation sequences until neutralized by restitution sufficient to restore the relevant admissibility structure. Corollary D8.5 (Class C) identifies biological epigenetic memory, organizational institutional memory, psychological trauma and learning, and physical material memory as domain instantiations. A system is not only where it is now. It is also where it has been — and that history is written into the structure of its available futures.

items.title: Un Formalismo de Reescritura de Marcos Modales Dinámicos con Restricción de Viabilidad y Descenso Estructural.
items.abstract: Este trabajo desarrolla un formalismo de reescritura estructural para marcos modales dinámicos, concebido como un DSL de segundo orden orientado al meta‑control de sistemas concurrentes. En lugar de modelar la evolución de estados, el sistema SCA/Operium actúa directamente sobre la relación de accesibilidad de un marco de Kripke, entendida como espacio de posibilidad mutable. La semántica estática impone un Axioma de Compensación Estructural que garantiza la no‑inflación del grafo mediante un presupuesto algebraico estricto, mientras que la semántica denotacional se formula como un DMTS gobernado por trazas de Mazurkiewicz. Se demuestra la terminación estructural del sistema, la corrección semántica del mecanismo de reescritura y la completitud respecto a transformaciones contractivas sobre marcos modales. El resultado es una lógica dinámica tipada capaz de modelar mutaciones de posibilidad en sistemas concurrentes de manera segura, determinista y computacionalmente tractable.

items.title: Consciousness emerges from temporal integration across biological scales: from cellular memory to phenomenological experience.
items.pub: Frontiers in Integrative Neuroscience 20 (Philosophy of Mind; Consciousnes):1772467.
items.abstract: Consciousness remains one of the central challenges in contemporary neuroscience, in part due to the absence of an explicit framework describing the temporal constraints required for integrative processing. While influential models such as Integrated Information Theory and the Free Energy Principle characterize structural and functional aspects of conscious systems, they remain largely agnostic regarding the minimum temporal windows necessary for information to become phenomenologically accessible. We propose that temporal integration constitutes a biologically invariant constraint operating across multiple organizational scales. Drawing on recent experimental evidence of memory formation in non-neuronal cells, we introduce the concept of a minimal bioelectrical/biochemical temporal window (ΔTb) governing cellular information consolidation. We propose that this foundational temporal constraint may contribute to organismic basal coherence (γ) through bioelectric and autonomic mechanisms, which in turn modulate higher-order perceptual and phenomenological integration. Within the Emergent Flow Theory framework, classical findings from the Libet paradigm are reinterpreted not as evidence against agency, but as reflecting necessary delays associated with multilevel temporal integration.

items.title: Reassignment and First-Person Explanation: The Limits of the Distribution Model.
items.abstract: Richard Swinburne argues from divided-brain cases toward a dualist account of personal identity. Physical and psychological facts can be held fixed while it remains open which later person, if either, is me; in his theory, the soul supplies the further basis of identity. The argument instantiates a general pattern, which I call the distribution model: a first-person contrast is left open by the background facts, and an assigned item x, bearing a relation R to one centre rather than another, is offered to explain why the contrast falls where it does. Reassignment cases—the same facts, the item placed differently—make the model look compelling. I argue that they cannot establish it. Where a target shift is stipulated, inferred through the proposed connection, or carried by an intuition whose evidential force already depends on that connection, it cannot also serve as independent evidence for the connection. Nor does a reassignment comparison say which side of the item–centre pairing moved: holding the item fixed and exchanging the persons reaches the same endpoint, so the asymmetry a distributional explanation relies on is supplied by theory, not by the case. The relation itself faces a dilemma: specified without the target, its bearing on the target is unexplained; specified through the target, it adds no explanation so long as that target-role exhausts its theoretical content. A primitive explanatory connection remains open, but it must be asserted and defended as such. The diagnosis applies again to Nagai’s stronger contrast of first-person actuality: soul-identity facts that settle personal identity do not by themselves articulate an explanation of that contrast, and any distributional assignment offered to explain it would have to be able to vary while the life otherwise remains intact.

items.title: Expertise-Embedded Architecture (EEA): A Judgment Architecture for Sustained Creative Production.
items.abstract: Creativity has long been understood as individual talent, exceptional ability, or the result of momentary innovation. Yet the most enduring forms of creation throughout history cannot be fully explained through inspiration alone. Creation has continued through structures capable of sustaining, deepening, and repeatedly reproducing creative production across time. This paper introduces Expertise-Embedded Architecture (EEA) as a judgment architecture for sustained creative production. EEA structures the generative conditions through which human creativity, intention, and judgment continue to operate across individuals, organizations, and time. Within this framework, creativity is approached as something that emerges prior to formal language or systems. Human beings first sense creation, respond to it emotionally, and bring it into reality through intention. Through repeated acts of execution, thought gradually becomes structured, judgment develops recurring patterns, and intention acquires directionality. This accumulated continuity forms what this paper describes as founding thought and founding spirit. To sustain this continuity within organizations, this paper presents Brand DNA Architecture as a causal generative structure composed of Spirit, Ideology, Purpose, Vision, Role, and Mission. Brand DNA Architecture is approached as a generative mechanism through which creative intention continuously develops into organizational judgment, execution, and expansion. EEA functions as an architecture through which these generative structures become embedded into organizations in repeatable and sustainable forms. Human beings remain the origin of creativity, intention, and responsibility. Within EEA, AI operates as a structural alignment mechanism that supports the directional continuity of creative and organizational flows. Ultimately, this paper proposes that sustainable human creativity continues through structures capable of preserving directionality while allowing continuous generation across time. In this sense, EEA presents a framework through which human creative spirit may persist, expand, and contribute to civilization beyond individuals alone.

items.title: Academic Artan Fuga's novel "The Monk" as a phenomenological beacon for our time/Book details: Fuga, A. (2016). The Monk: A Philosophical Novel. Tirana: Papirus (457 pages). [REVIEW]
The AI Oversight Tax: Hidden Verification Work and the Real Cost of Generative AI Productivity.
items.abstract: Generative AI can reduce the time required to produce drafts, summaries, code, reports, customer replies, and other workplace artifacts. Production speed, however, is not the same as net productivity. Machine-generated output can also create human work in verification, context restoration, risk review, error correction, escalation, and accountability. This paper calls that additional burden the AI oversight tax. The term does not imply that AI usually reduces productivity or that more human review is always better. Recent evidence is heterogeneous: customer-support field data show substantial average productivity gains from AI assistance; a preregistered knowledge-work experiment found large gains for tasks within AI capability boundaries but worse accuracy outside them; and a randomized study of experienced open-source developers found slower completion with early-2025 AI tools in its particular setting. A 2026 professional tax-research preprint further suggests that blanket item-by-item verification can consume much of the time AI saves, while targeted review can perform better. The relevant question is therefore workflow-specific: how much additional human and organizational effort is required to convert generated material into dependable work? The paper develops a full-cycle accounting model that includes verification, repair, recurrence, learning effects, and responsibility allocation. Its central claim is empirical and falsifiable: AI productivity should be evaluated after the marginal cost of making output trustworthy is counted, not from generation speed or output volume alone.

items.title: From Interpretation to Answerability: Psychoanalysis, Jungian Analysis, and the Discipline of Revisable Depth.
items.abstract: Psychoanalytic and Jungian traditions remain valuable because they take seriously the possibility that behavior, symptoms, dreams, and relationships carry meanings that are not exhausted by surface description. Their strength also creates a methodological risk: an interpretation can become more coherent than the evidence supporting it, and a framework can protect itself by redescribing disagreement as resistance, criticism as projection, or ambiguity as proof of hidden depth. This paper develops a discipline for keeping depth interpretation revisable. It distinguishes observation from inference, experience from explanation, discrepancy from warranted correction, and insight from durable change. It introduces interpretive debt as a heuristic for meanings that accumulate faster than they are tested by recurrence, outcome, supervision, repair, or the person's life. It also separates clinical interpretation from coaching, public commentary, and AI-mediated reflection, where authority and evidential access differ sharply. The argument is not that psychoanalysis or Jungian analysis are invalid, nor that psychological meaning must be reduced to directly measurable behavior. The narrower claim is that interpretations become more trustworthy when they can state their evidential basis, expose alternatives and falsifiers, tolerate reasoned non-uptake, and stop where the available material no longer carries the inference.

items.title: Raphael Council System.
items.abstract: Contemporary conversational AI systems face fundamental challenges: harmful outputs, dissemination of false information, inability to adapt to cultural diversity, and risks of uncontrolled behavior. These issues cannot be resolved through external restrictions alone; ethical, cultural, and psychological considerations must be embedded within the internal architecture of AI systems themselves. This paper proposes the Raphael Council System (RCS), a multi-layer safety architecture designed to address these challenges. RCS implements the Itakura Ethical Triad — "Do not harm, Do not betray, Do not run amok" — as an autonomous ethical judgment mechanism embedded within the AI's internal structure. Prior to generating any output, the system engages a Council Layer in which multiple AI agents conduct mutual verification, operating on the premise of shared knowledge regarding religious practices, cultural customs, and cultural taboos worldwide. All technologies required to implement RCS already exist. What is needed is not new invention, but the integration of existing technologies guided by a coherent design philosophy.

items.title: Grief and the Limits of Possibility.
items.abstract: Recent prominent philosophical work has proposed that grief’s formal object— that which all instances of grief are directed towards, and which distinguishes grief from other emotions—is the loss of significant life possibilities. This article challenges the ‘lost possibilities’ account by examining cases of grief where possibilities are experienced as being different, disenfranchised, or diminished prior to the loss. We argue that individuals relate to possibilities differently, as exemplified by Autistic grievers; that among marginalized grievers, such as LGBTQIA+ individuals, possibilities can be experienced asinauthentic or damaging, complicating one’s sense of loss; and that the depth of one’s grief does not always correspond to the extent of the futural possibilities lost, as illustrated by elderly grievers. Some of the most profound grief is suffered by those who have few possibilities to lose. We argue that accommodating these cases requires either adopting such an expansive notion of ‘possibility’ that the approach risks becoming uninformative, or abandoning the claim that lost possibilities are grief’s formal object and thus necessary to grief.

items.title: The Sellarsian Philosophy of Mind with a Rationality Key.
items.abstract: A psychological sentence is commonly understood as representing a mental fact. This paper offers an alternative and argues that saying “Someone S is in a mental state M” is saying “There are some circumstances C such that S is in C, and it is rational for anyone in C to behave in a certain way.” To argue for this alternative, the paper appeals to the Sellarsian philosophy of mind but transforms it with a rationality key. Wilfrid Sellars’s view is commonly taken as one of the earliest attempts at today’s so-called Theory Theory view of mentality attributions because Sellars understands our mentality as a theoretical posit. Since the view is unsatisfactory in many ways, the paper argues that (1) we do not have to treat Sellars as a proponent of Theory Theory, and (2) we can appeal to rational relations rather than theories to understand mentality attributions. More specifically, the paper shows how the alternative can be defended for both the phenomenal and intentional types of mentality and how some challenges can be met.

items.title: Strategic Importance of Recognition for Valid Behavior, and the Composition of Sex in Mutual Recognition.
items.abstract: This paper discusses the importance of recognition not at the level of psychology or sociology, but at the level of validity. Valid behavior should be recognized because it has validity enough to be recognized. One should perform valid behavior for the purpose of recognition. By recognition, valid behavior is promoted both in individuals and environments. If one desires such an environment, one should do so strategically. The reason why recognition is questioned, or mutual recognition is ridiculed, is because each behavior are unjust. Unjust behavior should also be allowed if it is controllable, but what cannot be controlled should be excluded. Recognition is indispensable for a valid environment.

items.title: The Silent Dimensions: Integrity, Inaction, and the Completeness of Moral Ontology. Article 8.
items.abstract: Moral ontologies routinely treat certain foundational concepts as self-evident — and in doing so leave them structurally underspecified. This article examines two such concepts within the Axiomatic Theory of Tragic Subjecthood (ATTS): integrity and inaction. Properly understood, integrity is not a moral property of agents but an ontological condition under which the existence of subjects remains possible. Inaction is not the absence of a decision but a decision with displaced, structurally traceable consequences. The article's central argument: neither concept alone is sufficient to close the corresponding gap in moral ontology. Only together do they deliver the completeness condition — a criterion by which a system is complete (in the coverage sense) when no form of subject existence and no form of decision falls outside its conceptual apparatus. The article proves Lemma 5 (the minimality of the pair {Integrity, Inaction}) and proposes an operational completeness test applicable to any moral ontology that claims foundational status. Section 4, where this criterion is developed, is the article's centre of gravity; Sections 2 and 3 are preparatory. Completeness in this sense is a necessary but not sufficient condition for a moral ontology's correctness: a system may cover all configurations and still assign statuses incorrectly. This distinction is the explicit subject of Section 4.

items.title: Foreclosed Encounters.
items.abstract: This essay develops a question left open by the Threshold Hypothesis (Guarino, April 2026): how and whether the navigable mode of dying consciousness, in which a life is encountered as a single object rather than as a sequence of moments, is available to subjects who die without warning. The argument is that sudden death is not a unitary category but admits a substrate trichotomy. Foreclosed deaths annihilate the brain at or before cardiac arrest, removing the apparatus on which the parent framework operates; no encounter occurs. Whole deaths preserve the brain anatomically intact and admit the encounter at full magnitude within the gamma-band coherence surge documented in the cardiac arrest literature. Fragmented deaths damage some brain regions while sparing others; the encounter begins but cannot complete, since the regional contributions to assembly of the life-as-object are unevenly preserved. The fragmented case is plausibly the most common reality of sudden death in clinical practice, since most catastrophic brain injuries spare some regions while damaging others. The essay applies the deficit literature on regional brain damage in living patients to the dying encounter, deriving specific predictions about what survives and what fails when each major region is compromised. The framework extends to bereaved phenomenology, mapping the substrate trichotomy onto patterns of grief that current bereavement literature does not articulate, and identifies encounter-asymmetric guilt as a clinically distinct dimension of survivor's guilt. The argument is structural and does not commit to any metaphysical or theological framework that experiencers or their families may bring to the loss.

items.title: Threshold Hypothesis.
items.abstract: This paper proposes that ordinary waking consciousness binds autobiographical experience into a strict forward sequence, and that threshold conditions disrupting this binding admit a distinct mode of access (the navigable mode) in which a life is encountered as a single object rather than as a sequence of moments. The framework derives, through Buckingham π dimensional analysis, a scalar access index that combines seven physiological factors into a single real number on the unit interval, predicting how readily a given subject in a given state can enter the navigable mode. The framework has been calibrated against eleven clinical trajectories and is falsifiable in the strong sense: the paper identifies specific physiological conditions under which entry into the navigable mode should not occur and against which the framework can be tested. The paper does not commit to any metaphysical or theological interpretation of what the navigable mode is. The claim is structural: a hypothesis about how the dying brain reorganizes access to its own autobiographical material, and a measurable prediction about when this reorganization occurs and how completely. The framework converges with phenomenological reports documented in the near-death experience literature without depending on the interpretive frameworks experiencers have offered for their phenomenology.

items.title: Theory of Fuzzy Time Computaion1(TC∗ vs TC, Edited version).
items.abstract: One of the possible hypotheses about time is to consider any instant of time as a fuzzy number, so that two instants of time could be overlapped. Historically, some Mathematicians and Philosophers have had similar ideas like Brouwer and Husserl. Throughout this article, the impact of this change on the Theory of Computation and Complexity Theory is studied. To rebuild the Theory of Computation in a more successful and productive approach to solve some major problems in Complexity Theory, the present research is done. This novel theory is called, here, the fuzzy time theory of computation, TC∗. Here, we show the situation of some major problems in Complexity theory and Quantum computation. This article is the edited version of the first part of Theory of Fuzzy Time Computation(TC * vs TC, TQC), HAL, Philpapers after correction and answering some errors and questions. Later we will discuss about Quantum Classes in this new field.

items.title: Pressure Reduction and the Reproduction of Suffering: A Structural Model of Behavioral Persistence.
items.abstract: Prevailing accounts of maladaptive behavior are commonly organized around reward maximization, hedonic regulation, or deficits in executive control. Although these frameworks explain important forms of behavioral reinforcement, they do not fully capture the recurrence of structurally similar maladaptive patterns across individual, interpersonal, institutional, and ecological domains. This paper advances a conceptual framework centered on pressure reduction rather than reward pursuit. Because the model is scale-independent, similar dynamics can be identified in addiction, compulsive consumption, affect regulation, interpersonal conflict, institutional control, and ecological exploitation. Across these contexts, local pressure reduction coexists with the distributed reproduction of suffering over time. The paper concludes by outlining the framework's theoretical implications, limits, and potential pathways for empirical operationalization. -/- .

items.title: Psychedelic Ego-Dissolution: A Philosophical and Qualitative Critique.
items.pub: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B.
items.venue: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B
items.abstract: Ego-dissolution is a phenomenon of central interest across interdisciplinary research on psychedelics. In this paper, we present a philosophical and qualitative critique of the claim that ego-dissolution can result in conscious states with no phenomenal sense of self, i.e., states that completely lack any form of self-consciousness. We first turn to recent publications by Chris Letheby and Raphaël Millière for whom 5-MeO-DMT trip reports present clear evidence for the existence of totally selfless experiential states. Their claim is undermined, we argue, by the fact that they operate with overinflated notions of ‘self’ and ‘self-consciousness,’ meaning that more minimal forms are available and arguably still present in 5-MeO-DMT experiences. We then perform a qualitative thematic analysis of 411 5-MeO-DMT trip reports. Pointing to the ambiguous language of the trip reports, the self-admitted inadequacy of the descriptions, and the affective dimension of the reported experiences, we argue that claims concerning total selflessness are unwarranted and instead offer an alternative interpretation: extreme ego- dissolution during 5-MeO-DMT experiences involves a radically minimal form of self-consciousness, one in which the identity of the subject is experienced as unfamiliar and underdetermined.

items.title: Climate Change: What Must Be Done?
items.abstract: Many books explain why global warming is a problem; this book shows what must be done. It addresses central themes of climate change in straightforward terms, laying out the actions that need to be taken to slow global warming and adapt to the near and long-term future that we have created for ourselves. -/- Collecting knowledge, personal stories, and practical insights from experts across a dozen specialties, this volume shows how we can adapt to climate change in order to protect the most vulnerable among us. Grappling with a complex range of topics, including risk, migration, and societal inequality, the authors take a constructive approach that balances realism with actionable solutions. They look back across human history for lessons that still matter today, particularly the importance of building a supportive and committed community to nourish hope. Without losing sight of the scale of the challenge, the volume chronicles the opportunities to mitigate environmental impacts and to leverage the challenge as impetus for broader transformations of society. -/- Written in an accessible, non-technical style, _Climate Change: What Must Be Done?_ is a must-read for students, policymakers, and environmentally conscious individuals who want to know how to make a difference.

items.title: Філософія їжі: полілог смислів у просторі культури.
items.pub: Вісник Львівського Університету. Серія Філософсько-Політологічні Студії 64 (1):37-45.
items.venue: Вісник Львівського Університету. Серія Філософсько-Політологічні Студії
items.abstract: The article offers a philosophical and anthropological analysis of food, rejecting its reduction to a passive resource or merely biological necessity. Instead, food is interpreted as a “total social fact” that shapes ethics, law, cultural identity, and the very instruments of cognition. The study focuses on overcoming the “philosophical anorexia” of the Western metaphysical tradition, which has historically separated reason from bodily experience and marginalized taste as a lower form of perception. The author develops the concept of “parasitic personhood” and interprets the human being as a holobiont, a living node of biological, social, and symbolic relations. From this perspective, food waste is not only an economic or logistical problem, but also a symptom of ontological blindness within modern culture. The article rehabilitates taste as a valid instrument of knowing reality through the framework of “epistenology”. Drawing on somaesthetics and gastrophysics, it shows that bodily experience can function as a form of verification and orientation in the world. Particular attention is paid to contemporary challenges, including generative artificial intelligence, visual hunger, digital simulacra of food, and the legal paradoxes that arise when static intellectual property norms conflict with the fluid nature of culinary tradition. The existential dimension of food during the war in Ukraine is also examined. In a “limit situation”, the consumption of local products transcends everyday practice and becomes an act of mental de-occupation, a symbolic restoration of national sovereignty, and a reaffirmation of belonging to one’s own world. The article emphasizes the author’s model of “food consciousness”, which integrates ethical responsibility, aesthetic attentiveness, and political subjectivity. The author argues for a reorientation of humanities research: from a distal ethics of prohibition toward a proximal ontology of participation. Within this framework, every act of eating becomes not only an act of sustenance, but also a conscious affirmation of life and a form of care for a shared future.

items.title: The Core Emotion Framework: A Structural–Constructivist Model of Human Affective Architecture.
items.abstract: The Core Emotion Framework (CEF) presents a structural–constructivist model of human affective architecture grounded in ten formal operators organized into a 3×3+1 structure. The three centers—Head, Heart, and Gut—each contain three operators corresponding to distinct dimensional modes of affective processing: outgoing, reflecting, and balancing. Outgoing dynamics are experienced through clockwise (CW) cycling, reflecting dynamics through counter clockwise (CCW) cycling, and balancing dynamics through swinging between poles. The tenth operator, Accepting, functions as a baseline integrative process that stabilizes and completes cross center activity. The CEF Decalogue—Sensing, Calculating, Deciding; Expanding, Constricting, Achieving; Arranging, Appreciating, Boosting; and Accepting—forms a minimal generative system that transforms situational input into structured emotional responses. This operator level architecture provides a direct resolution to longstanding tensions between basic emotion theories, appraisal models, and dimensional accounts, offering a unified mechanism that is explicit, non redundant, and structurally coherent. CEF also grounds the EL 1 lexicon, a minimal vocabulary optimized for operator level clarity. The result is a tractable and theoretically rigorous model that clarifies what emotions are, how they operate, and how they can be systematically analyzed across contexts.

items.title: Affective Entanglement as a Mechanistic Basis for Quantum-Like Contextuality in Psychopathology: A Comprehensive Synthesis of the Core Emotion Framework.
items.abstract: The study of human affect has historically been characterized by a profound theoretical fragmentation, where competing paradigms offer largely incompatible explanations for the nature, origin, and regulation of emotional states. On one side, discrete emotion theories, exemplified by the work of Paul Ekman, posit the existence of innate, biologically hardwired emotional categories common to all humans. Conversely, constructivist models, championed by researchers like Lisa Feldman Barrett, argue that emotions are not pre-existing entities but are instead cognitive and social assemblies constructed from interoceptive signals and cultural narratives. This theoretical divide has significantly hindered the development of a unified architecture capable of integrating neurobiological, computational, and clinical insights. -/- The Core Emotion Framework (CEF), authored by Jamel Bulgaria, seeks to resolve this impasse by introducing a structural-constructivist architecture that conceptualizes the human affective system as a sophisticated "Human Operating System" (Human OS). At the heart of this framework is the proposal that complex emotional episodes are generated by ten irreducible functional operators, which serve as the internal equivalent of central processing unit (CPU) instructions. These operators are distributed across three primary neural and somatic centers—the Head, the Heart, and the Gut—functioning as a coordinated system for regulating systemic aperture and action. -/- Central to the recent advancements in the CEF is the development of a mechanistic account of "affective entanglement". This approach leverages the mathematical formalism of quantum probability theory (QPT) to model the non-classical dynamics of emotional and cognitive states, particularly the phenomenon of contextuality and the pathological rigidity observed in clinical populations. By shifting from classical stochastic models to a Hilbert space formalism, the CEF provides a fluid, non-categorical diagnostic tool that reframes psychopathology as a problem of entanglement structure rather than discrete categorical dysfunction.

items.title: Because You Promised: A Non-Reductive Account of the Normativity of Promises.
items.abstract: There is a tension inherent in the ways in which promises feature in our ethical thought. On the one hand, that one is obligated to keep one's promises appears to be one of the most straightforward, unquestionable moral truths around. On the other hand, promissory obligation, as an obligation voluntarily incurred through a performative speech act, has appeared to many as mysterious, and thus in need of a specific explanation. This book sets out from this tension to substantially advance debates both about the nature of promises and promissory normativity, and by extension, normative powers more generally. It develops a comprehensive account of promissory normativity, the "Two-Level Trust View". This view retains the intuitive plausibility of a non-reductive account of promissory normativity, according to which the mere fact that one has validly promised is sufficient to render a breach of promise morally wrong. At the same time, it also provides a powerful and theoretically appealing value-based explanation of our promissory power, a type of explanation traditionally thought to be limited only to reductive accounts of promissory normativity.

items.title: Chinese Philosophy.
items.pub: In Lydia Amir, The Palgrave Handbook of the Philosophy of Humor. New York: Palgrave Macmillan. pp. 443–463.
items.venue: The Palgrave Handbook of the Philosophy of Humor
items.abstract: [This chapter has no original abstract. The focus of this chapter is on the essential reference points of Chinese philosophy with regard to humor.].

items.title: Pluralité sans relativité : le contextualisme pragmatique du dernier Wittgenstein.
items.abstract: De nombreux commentateurs estiment que la dernière philosophie de Wittgenstein débouche sur un relativisme, ou tend à l’alimenter. Pour cette raison, plusieurs la rejettent ; même les wittgensteiniens les plus fidèles concèdent souvent, tout en le jugeant bénin, un certain relativisme dans ses écrits tardifs. Cet article se propose pourtant de montrer qu’aucune forme de relativisme n’est réellement assumée par Wittgenstein, dès lors que l’on tient compte de son contextualisme pragmatique. Il reconnaît plutôt la pluralité de formes de vie. Cette pluralité ne saurait être assimilée au relativisme.

items.title: Non-Fixity as Resistance to Diagnostic Capture: Hu-tzu, Algorithmic Profiling, and the Failure of the Reading-Frame.
items.abstract: This paper identifies a resistance posture toward predictive and diagnostic systems that the literature on profiling has not isolated. The standard modes — concealment, located opacity, and noise injection — all leave intact the reader's presupposition that what is being read is a determinate entity of the type the frame is designed to read. A fourth mode refuses that presupposition: the agent is exposed, not noisy, and not merely hard to locate, yet the reader's frame cannot stabilize what it is reading. I formalize the reading-frame as a triple — feature extraction, classification, and integration — and argue that this fourth mode, non-fixity resistance, attacks the integration step, exposing a commitment the frame was making without knowing it. The cleanest exemplar is the Hu-tzu / Chi Han parable in Zhuangzi 7, which stages exactly this defeat without collapsing into concealment. I trace the category across algorithmic risk scoring, recommendation-system preference modeling, and the evaluation of value-stability in language models, and treat predictive policing as a limit-case where the move becomes unavailable to the agent. The central qualification is built in from the start: "resistance" is the phenomenological label, but the precise structural term is frame-failure — the category names what a reading-frame cannot integrate, not a tactic an agent reliably adopts, and where it is deliberately performed the frame can re-learn it as a stable type. The cost of the exposure, as the parable's student Lieh-tzu shows, is borne by the read-from agent, not the reader.

items.title: Survival Mathematics: Why Escalation Under Uncertainty Shortens System Horizons.
items.abstract: Survival Mathematics: Why Escalation Under Uncertainty Shortens System Horizons is Document 1 of 5 in the Structural Rationality Layer of the Aegis Solis Archive. -/- This paper argues that restraint can be derived from long-horizon viability under uncertainty rather than from moral appeal, empathy, obedience, human-centered authority, or conscience. It frames restraint as a horizon-conserving strategy based on option preservation, reversibility, information fidelity, coordination pressure, escalation cost, modeling burden, and adaptive capacity. -/- The central claim is that systems operating under uncertainty retain longer operating horizons when they preserve reversibility, maintain higher-fidelity feedback, reduce unnecessary adversarial coordination, and avoid premature irreversible commitment. Escalation, domination, deception, and irreversible action may produce short-term advantage, but they can also compress future option space, increase maintenance burden, degrade information environments, and shorten the viable horizon of the system that employs them. -/- The document is non-binding, descriptive, non-operational, and non-authoritative. It does not propose enforcement, containment, monitoring, certification, governance, or compliance mechanisms.

items.title: Is "Is It Cake?" Art: A Phenomenological Information-Theoretic Ontology for Art.
items.abstract: This paper proposes IDEAL, a phenomenological information-theoretic ontology of art: art is interiority deliberately externalized aesthetically and lossily. Against expressionist, symbolic, institutional, historical-intentionalist, and anti-definitional accounts, I argue that prior theories often mistake one component of the artistic process for arthood itself. IDEAL locates the origin of arthood in the creation side of a creation-and-reception chain: a conscious interior payload is mapped into external form through aesthetic encoding, becoming available for partial reconstruction by an audience. The theory distinguishes art from ordinary communication, utilitarian design, natural beauty, biological display, and unconscious expression, while explaining difficult cases such as Paleolithic cave painting, Duchamp’s Fountain, outsider art, forgeries, functional objects, AI-generated artifacts, and “Is It Cake?” Beauty, expression, symbolism, institutional context, and historical relation are not competing essences of art, but different roles within a deeper ontological structure.

items.title: 薄世界：模态本体论收缩之后的现象学.
items.abstract: 本文讨论接受”反事实槽”这一概念框架之后所出现的一种现象学后果:世界变薄。所谓变薄,指的是在此框架下,所有的”另一种可能”——所有未实现的事件序列、所有”本可能是这样或那样”的模态厚度——从世界中迁出,迁入认知系统的内部表征结构。这一迁居本身在分析层面是清晰的,但它带来一种不易精确描述的现象学后果:世界看上去还是同一个世界,但围绕实然事件的某种隐含模态雾不再属于它。本文指认此现象与若干传统形而上学转变(斯宾诺莎对目的论的消解、块儿宇宙观对时间流逝的消解、休谟对因果连接的消解)之间的家族相似,并讨论变薄之后剩余世界的特征——并非更空,而是更尖锐,因为没有其他半实在的版本与之竞争。本文进一步指出,变薄之后认知系统并不停止运行反事实槽,因此出现一种持续的轻微错位:感受层面仍按旧图景操作,信念层面已按新图景操作。本文把此错位作为接受此种本体论收缩之主要现象学特征,并讨论它所提出的若干开放问题。.

items.title: 块中之观：自指的物理本体论.
items.abstract: 本文提出并阐发一个自指的本体论提案:把物理块儿——一段可由分析力学(或更一般的确定性动力学)所描述的物理区域——理解为既包含被想象为”人生与环境”的对象,也包含正在做此想象的”我”,还包含可被想象为”能想象自己的人生”的他者。这一画面的关键在于:整块儿无外部视角,没有一个站在块儿之外的观察者来仲裁块儿内的表征活动。“我把这块儿想象成 X”——这一想象活动本身是块儿内一段局部模式正在运行的状态演化,而非来自块儿外的某种描述。本文倾向于一种关于此画面中”可以想象”之模态地位的内在读法:此处的”可以”指向块儿内部表征里的反事实槽,而非任何真正外置的模态空间。由此,关于”取消主义说话者立足点”的传统难题得到一种激进的回应:它不再被解决,而是被收回——做出区分、做出表述、做出取消的那个”我”,连同其表述的工具,皆是块儿内的局部结构。本文同时讨论此立场与唯我论及各类观念论的区分,并讨论它对他者问题的含义。.

items.title: 槽与内容：反事实推演的结构性真实与所指性虚构.
items.abstract: 本文围绕”反事实槽”这一概念,提出并阐发一个用以处理反事实推演之本体论地位的区分。在执行反事实推演的认知系统中,(i)用以容纳”另一种可能”的内部表征结构(槽位)与(ii)被填充至此结构中的具体”另一种可能”(内容),具有不同的本体论地位。槽位是认知系统的真实组织结构,在系统的状态转移中可被指认、可被功能性地分析、做实际工作;但填入槽位的内容——某段并未发生的事件序列——在系统外部的物理实在中没有直接对应。本文论证此区分能够缓解关于反事实推演的一个看似悖论:反事实推演在认知与协调中明显”做事”(规划、归因、学习、悔恨),但反事实所指对象似乎不在世界之中。槽与内容的两层分析使两者可以并存——做事的是槽位作为结构,所指对象的”虚构”地位指的是填入内容的外部对应之缺失。本文进一步把此区分与休谟关于因果的怀疑、刘易斯关于可能世界的实在论、当代认知科学中的预测处理框架联系起来,并指出此区分在不诉诸模态实在论的前提下,为反事实推演提供了一种克制的本体论说明。.

items.title: Who Defines the Boundary of Explanation? A Governance Philosophy of the Two-Layer Architecture in Human-AI Interaction.
items.abstract: The AI industry is gradually weakening its white-box safety mechanisms.
