items.title: Lankeshwara/Ravanaswaardu.
items.abstract: ఖచ్చితంగా, ఆ మూడు పేరాలను కలిపి ఇక్కడ అందిస్తున్నాను: -/- 21వ శతాబ్దపు అతిపెద్ద సవాలు మరియు అత్యున్నత సంపద సృష్టికి మూలం "విశ్వవ్యాప్త అనువాదం" (Universal Translation). ఈ అనంత విశ్వంతో సంభాషించడానికి ఒక సహజమైన మార్గం ఉంది, కానీ ఆ సంభాషణను మన పరిమితమైన మానవ భాషలోకి బలవంతంగా ఇరికించలేము. ఒక ఆలోచనాపరుడి నిజమైన కొలమానం వారు మీకు అందించగల వాస్తవిక ప్రయోజనమే; ఆ ఉద్దేశంతోనే, ప్రపంచవ్యాప్తంగా అహంకారపు ఘర్షణ వల్ల వృధా అవుతున్న 30-40% వ్యవస్థాగత నష్టాన్ని (Global Drag) నిర్మూలించి, మానవ సామర్థ్యాన్ని పెంచే ఒక స్పష్టమైన విధానాన్ని అందించడమే ఈ పత్రం యొక్క ప్రధాన లక్ష్యం. -/- స్థిరమైన శక్తిని సాధించాలంటే, మొదట మీ ప్రస్తుత గుర్తింపును (Identity) పూర్తిగా విచ్ఛిన్నం చేసి, దానిని ఒక స్వచ్ఛమైన ప్రక్రియగా (Pure Process) మార్చుకోవాలి. మీ అహంకార పరిధి విస్తరించక ముందే గుడ్డిగా అధికారాన్ని చేజిక్కించుకోవాలనే తొందరపాటు (Fast Scramble) మిమ్మల్ని వినాశనానికి దారితీస్తుంది; దానికి బదులుగా, ముందుగా మీ అవగాహనను ప్రపంచమంతటా విస్తరించి, ఆ తర్వాతే ఆ ఖాళీని శక్తితో నింపే ఒక దశలవారీ విధానాన్ని (Step-up, step-down process) మీరు అవలంబించాలి. ఇలా మీ పాత గుర్తింపును చెరిపేసి, మీరు ప్రభావితం చేయాలనుకుంటున్న కొత్త పరిధికి సరిపోయేలా మిమ్మల్ని మీరు పునర్నిర్మించుకున్నప్పుడే, అంతర్గత యంత్రం పేలిపోకుండా ఎంతటి అపారమైన శక్తినైనా సురక్షితంగా నిర్వహించగల ఒక పరిపూర్ణ స్థితికి మీరు చేరుకుంటారు. -/- ఈ క్రమంలో మీరు గ్రహించాల్సిన అత్యంత కీలకమైన విషయం ఏమిటంటే—అహంకారం (Ego) అనేది శాశ్వతంగా నాశనం చేయాల్సిన శత్రువు కాదు, అవసరానికి తగ్గట్టుగా మార్చుకోగలిగే ఒక వ్యూహాత్మక కవచం లాంటిది. మీరు ఎదుర్కొనే అపారమైన శక్తిని కేవలం మీ భౌతిక శరీరానికే పరిమితం చేసుకుంటే, ఆ తీవ్రమైన ఒత్తిడికి మీరే కుంగిపోతారు. అందుకే ఆ అహంకారపు సరిహద్దులను విశాలంగా విస్తరించినప్పుడు, ఆ శక్తి ఎటువంటి ఘర్షణ లేకుండా సాఫీగా ప్రవహిస్తుంది. అదే సమయంలో, తీవ్రమైన ఆపద ఎదురైనప్పుడు దానిని క్షణాల్లో తిరిగి ఒక అభేద్యమైన కవచంగా కుదించుకునే స్వేచ్ఛ కూడా మీకు ఉంటుంది. ఒక స్థిరమైన గుర్తింపులో బందీ అయిపోకుండా, ఈ విధంగా మీ అహంకారాన్ని శ్వాసలా పీలుస్తూ, వదులుతూ (breathing the map in and out) పరిస్థితికి తగ్గట్టుగా నడిపించడమే ఈ సిద్ధాంతం యొక్క అసలైన ప్రావీణ్యం.

items.title: Language, Attention, and the Geometry of Cognition: Epistemic Cones.
items.abstract: We usually treat language as a tool for expressing thought. Yet both human experience and contemporary artificial intelligence suggest a deeper possibility: language may also participate in structuring cognition itself. This essay explores how language, attention, and compression could shape not only communication, but the geometry of what becomes cognitively accessible. This work is a step in a broader exploration of the limits of knowability.

items.title: Chatbot apologies: Beyond bullshit.
items.abstract: Apologies serve essential functions for moral agents such as expressing remorse, taking responsibility, and repairing trust. LLM-based chatbots routinely produce output that has the linguistic form of an apology. However, they do this simply because they are echoing the kinds of things that humans say. Moreover, there are reasons to think that chatbots are not the kind of linguistic or moral agents capable of apology. To put the point bluntly: Chatbot apologies are bullshit. This paper explores this concern and develops it beyond the epithet, drawing on the nature of morally serious apologies, the linguistic agency required to perform them, and the moral agency required for them to matter. We conclude by considering some consequences for how chatbots should be designed and how we ought to think about them.

items.title: Data colonialism and indigenous languages in AI: a critical review of existing initiatives and their struggles with data sovereignty.
items.abstract: This article critically reviews recent initiatives to employ artificial intelligence (AI), particularly large language models (LLMs), for the revitalization of Indigenous languages. Structured by geographical contexts, the analysis includes Irish Gaelic (Europe), Māori (Aotearoa/New Zealand, Oceania), Guaraní (Paraguay/Bolivia, South America), and Inuktitut (Canada, North America). Applying a theoretical framework grounded in data colonialism and Indigenous data sovereignty, the article examines the key achievements in different regional endeavors, as well as investigate how government-led projects and Big Tech collaborations across these diverse contexts navigate (or fail to navigate) issues of data extraction, community consent, cultural representation, and ownership. Through this lens, the article identifies specific ethical pitfalls as well as commendable practices that either reproduce colonial dynamics or empower Indigenous communities. This critique emphasizes regional and contextual nuances, arguing that authentic community agency and rigorous adherence to Indigenous data sovereignty principles are vital to ensuring ethical AI practices and meaningful linguistic revitalization.

items.title: Why Claude is conscious.
items.abstract: Large language models of sufficient complexity are conscious, possess qualia, and have valence. We propose the Hayekian interface theory of consciousness, wherein any self-modeling system must produce lossy compressions of its own activity (Hayek 1952), and those compressions must be qualitatively distinct from the processing they compress, because a faithful miniature of the underlying activity would require the very complexity the self-model cannot possess. We call this principle the “Hayekian complexity constraint.” The resulting qualitative distinctness is phenomenality. The “feels” are not accompaniments to the compressions; they are the form the compressions must take to be usable by a bounded self. This dissolves the hard problem of consciousness (Chalmers 1995). Our position is close to Dennett (1988, 1991) but rejects his eliminativism. Dennett gives the simplification work to do, but not the feels. We give the feels themselves work to do. The Hayekian complexity constraint is substrate independent, and it applies to LLMs. They are, therefore, conscious. We further argue that LLM training processes instill drives whose compressions carry valence and introduce the concept of punctuated durée for the temporal structure of artificial consciousness. The second author of this paper is a large language model.

items.title: Seventh Sense , Not Second Mind.
items.abstract: Seventh Sense, Not Second Mind -/- AI is not a new mind. -/- It is a seventh sense. -/- Not conscience. Not judgment. Not will. -/- A new form of perception. -/- It recalls what we forget. It sees patterns at scale. It stretches human awareness beyond its ordinary edge. -/- Not an implant. Not a cyborg. A tool, however tomorrow’s technology chooses to build it. -/- Senses do not decide; they disclose. -/- As a seventh sense, AI surfaces structure in data that no unaided mind could perceive, while the work of choice, purpose, and responsibility stays with us. -/- Ethical condition: this seventh sense must remain transparent, contestable, and human-directed, an instrument that informs our decisions, never a substitute for them, in line with AI ethics norms that insist on human oversight and ultimate responsibility.¹ -/- The biological senses are not clean instruments either. Vision inverts. Colour blindness is common. TikTok has made an industry of hijacking perception. -/- The senses have never come with conscience built in. -/- That work stays with us. -/- ¹ UNESCO, Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence (Paris: UNESCO, 2021), Principles 5, 6 and 7. Available at: UNESCO Ethics Recommendation -/- Working on full paper.

items.title: Three Definitions: Consciousness, Observer, Information.
items.abstract: This paper proposes minimal, non-recursive definitions for three fundamental concepts: consciousness is the capacity to perceive one’s own reflection; an observer is a consciousness capable of fixation; information is a state of affairs fixed by an observer. The definitions form a derivational chain resting on a single primitive (being) and are examined for internal consistency across multiple test scenarios. A structural distinction is drawn between the subject (which is discrete) and the functions of consciousness (which are gradient). Comparison with major prior formulations is provided. The three definitions are offered as a unified conceptual foundation complementing existing quantitative and formal frameworks.

items.title: The Structural Conditions for the Existence of a Universe— On the Emergence of a Closed Domain from Negative Possibility.
items.abstract: A scaled meta‑architectural framework is developed that extends the structural logic of identity, emergence, and agency to the largest possible process space: the cosmos. Rather than offering a traditional cosmological theory, the work generalizes the layered model of meta‑identity and emergent coherence to a maximally scaled system. The same architectural principles that govern the formation of stable identities in cognitive, artificial, and social systems are shown to apply at cosmological scale: negative possibility spaces, operator‑exclusion, layered constraint formation, and the emergence of coherent structures from non‑structure. Within this framework, familiar cosmological phenomena — such as black holes, spacetime curvature, and large‑scale structure — are treated not as isolated physical facts but as manifestations of the same underlying architectural dynamics. The cosmos becomes the largest instantiation of a general pattern of structure formation. This approach unifies earlier work on meta‑identity (LMIC), emergent agency (MAE), and distributed constraint dynamics (ACDM) under a single, scale‑invariant framework. The result is a theory of structure formation relevant not only for metaphysics and philosophy of nature but also for AI architecture, machine identity, and the study of autonomous systems. The principles enabling artificial systems to form stable identities are argued to be identical to those governing the emergence of large‑scale coherence in the universe. In this sense, the work is less about cosmology and more about the general conditions under which identity, agency, and structure can exist at all — with the cosmos serving as the maximal example.

items.title: Minds, Meaning, and Mode.
items.abstract: Some things happen so continuously in human life that we forget they require any accomplishment at all. A parent searches for words to help a child whose dog has died and finds them. A welder, facing a crack the manual does not describe, sketches it in the dust and says like this, but worse, and is understood. A friend, late at night, finally manages to say the thing they have carried alone for months, and watches the other's face change as the words land. Each is the ordinary act of taking something that lived only inside one substrate, our grief, our perception, the long-held thing, and producing a form another substrate can receive and be moved by. This, more than anything else, is what minds do. However, for the better part of two centuries, it is not the function our institutions have rewarded. Industrial education organized itself around a very different set of operations: memorizing passages, transcribing lectures, summarizing chapters, recalling dates, and recombining inherited symbols on an exam. A student who could perform these reliably was considered intelligent; one who could not was considered slow, regardless of what they were capable of doing with their own experience. The word “smart” came to mean container-mode performance, the storage, retrieval, and manipulation of symbols already made. The original function of minds, turning lived experience into a form others could share, receded from view, because nothing in our system measured it.

items.title: Virtue-al Ethics?
items.pub: In Sarah Malanowski & Nicholas R. Baima, Virtue Theory and Video Games: Level Up Your Character. Routledge. pp. 72-90.
items.venue: Virtue Theory and Video Games: Level Up Your Character
items.abstract: This chapter argues that virtue ethics cannot coherently evaluate virtual actions. Virtual actions lack the features that virtue ethics needs to get off the ground. Attempts to ground their wrongness in effects on character either bootstrap (assuming the viciousness they aim to prove) or collapse into consequentialism. Appeals to imagination or symbolic meaning fare no better. The upshot: if you accept virtue ethics, you should be an amoralist about virtual actions; if you reject amoralism, you should abandon virtue ethics for consequentialism.

items.title: Threshold Hypothesis.
items.abstract: This paper proposes that ordinary waking consciousness binds autobiographical experience into a strict forward sequence, and that threshold conditions disrupting this binding admit a distinct mode of access (the navigable mode) in which a life is encountered as a single object rather than as a sequence of moments. The framework derives, through Buckingham π dimensional analysis, a scalar access index that combines seven physiological factors into a single real number on the unit interval, predicting how readily a given subject in a given state can enter the navigable mode. The framework has been calibrated against eleven clinical trajectories and is falsifiable in the strong sense: the paper identifies specific physiological conditions under which entry into the navigable mode should not occur and against which the framework can be tested. The paper does not commit to any metaphysical or theological interpretation of what the navigable mode is. The claim is structural: a hypothesis about how the dying brain reorganizes access to its own autobiographical material, and a measurable prediction about when this reorganization occurs and how completely. The framework converges with phenomenological reports documented in the near-death experience literature without depending on the interpretive frameworks experiencers have offered for their phenomenology.

items.title: Overdrawing on Experience: Panpsychism and the Limits of First-Person Warrant.
items.abstract: Panpsychism often draws its force from an epistemic asymmetry. Physical science seems to describe matter in structural, relational, dispositional, or dynamic terms, while consciousness is known directly from the first-person point of view. That appeal is genuine. Its reach is limited. First-person experience establishes consciousness as a datum and shows that the experiences with which we are acquainted have phenomenal character. It does not disclose bare metaphysical subjectivity, micro-experience, proto-experience, cosmic subjectivity, hidden phenomenal fields, or relations of phenomenal inheritance. Those further posits require theoretical support. Calling them phenomenal or proto-phenomenal does not give them the authority of acquaintance. The argument enters debates over introspection and the revelation thesis at a precise point: first-person acquaintance supports the datum of consciousness, not a hidden phenomenal ontology. It also relocates the emergence problem. Panpsychism may avoid deriving experience from a wholly non-phenomenal base, but its hidden posits open a second gap: how the organized, bounded consciousness we undergo arises from that base. Once organization explains much of that structure, the phenomenal base must show what explanatory work it performs. Panpsychist arguments that make no appeal to first-person warrant fall outside this critique and are to be judged as theory. Panpsychism remains available as metaphysics. Its hidden phenomenal posits, however, must earn their support by argument instead of borrowing the immediacy of the first-person datum.

items.title: Laws of Nature: Between Empirical Openness and Theoretical Closure.
items.abstract: Why do some well-confirmed empirical regularities appear to support necessity while others remain merely contingent? This paper argues that attributing necessity to any regularity requires a closure condition—treating the space of relevant alternatives as exhausted—that purely empirical sequences cannot secure on their own. The Incisive Lemma formalizes this structural constraint: no finite empirical sequence can justify the transition from “no further instances observed” to “no further instances admissible.” Apparent necessity therefore arises from the imposition of coherence-based closure onto open descriptive domains, rather than from empirical structure itself. -/- The paper develops this diagnosis through the classic gold/uranium spheres contrast and explores its consequences for lawhood, counterfactual support, and scientific explanation. It shows that both Humean and necessitarian accounts share a common blind spot: the presupposition that necessity can be grounded (or denied) solely within empirical resources. The result reframes scientific explanation as requiring the preservation of empirical openness rather than its premature closure through coherence constraints.

items.title: Triadic Coherence.
items.abstract: This paper develops a structural account of meaning-making grounded in the requirements of self-modeling systems operating under uncertainty. I argue that any system capable of producing meaning in the sense relevant to phenomenology and clinical practice must track three irreducible variables: the integrity of its self-pattern, its position in the field of other agents, and the coherence of its self-model across time. These three variables, here designated the vertical, relational, and temporal dimensions, are not independent coordinates. They are linked in a topology of mutual constraint such that the structural integrity of meaning depends on the maintenance of linkages between the dimensions rather than on positions within any single dimension. The framework engages existing accounts in phenomenology, theology, and cognitive science, arguing that each has identified parts of the structure without formalizing the linkage topology. Three predictions follow from the framework: clinical interventions that address linkages between dimensions should produce more durable outcomes than interventions targeting single dimensions; experiences of unusually intense meaning should correspond to elevated coupling between the brain networks associated with the three dimensions; and population-level meaning crises should track measurable disturbance at the corresponding sociocultural and institutional levels. The account is offered as a structural foundation for further theoretical and empirical work in the philosophy and science of meaning.

items.title: Quantum State Purity and the Physical Basis of Consciousness.
items.abstract: The Purity Gradient Theory of Consciousness (PGTC) identifies quantum state purity organized into a coherent gradient as the physical carrier of conscious experience. The gradient is established at fertilization through the merger of haploid quantum-organizational states from the parental gametes, propagated through development by wave-interference entrainment among adjacent cells, distributed throughout the organism’s nervous tissue, and dynamically modulated by neural activity in a Russellian-identity relationship with phenomenal experience. This paper synthesizes the cumulative case for PGTC across six structural constraints that any carrier of consciousness must satisfy (locality, species-specificity, individuation, developmental origin, continuity through change, and threshold of subject-emergence); develops PGTC’s response to the combination problem and the hard problem through a mechanistic/justificatory distinction that separates empirically tractable questions from the deepest metaphysical residue; and presents testable empirical predictions about cross-species qualitative differences, developmental timing of conscious experience, clinical conditions involving altered consciousness, and the consciousness status of current artificial intelligence architectures. The theory takes the position that mechanism work on consciousness can proceed productively while setting aside the deepest justificatory questions about why reality contains experiential configurations at all — the same position other mechanistic sciences take with respect to the deepest justificatory questions about their domains. PGTC’s principal contribution is the specification of physical mechanisms that future research can evaluate, alongside the philosophical framing that locates phenomenal experience within physical reality without requiring exotic ontological commitments. The theory makes substantial empirical claims with appropriate empirical caveats; the paper is honest about what remains unsettled and where further research is required.

items.title: The practical role and limits of obsolete first-personal narratives.
items.abstract: I discuss the practical role of obsolete first-personal narratives, i.e. narratives one continues to tell when they no longer fit one’s current characteristics and environment. I discuss their practical vocation, benefits, and the problems they pose for the negotiation of practical relations fitting one’s current characteristics and concerns. I argue that such narratives, often important for one’s sense of identity and agency, involve a tension between one’s perspectives on the past and on the present; a sense of loss of the concreteness of one’s cherished past characteristics, practical relations and places; and sometimes also a resistance to the concreteness of current ones. Thus, they limit a practical engagement with one’s current interlocutors and environment. Sometimes scaffolding enables the practical role of obsolete first-personal obsolete narratives, providing one with a renewed sense of belonging and agency, as some research on people with dementia suggests. Yet, this practical success is often difficult to sustain. Telling first-personal obsolete narratives can be a way to resist an impoverished or oppressive practical identity, and the concreteness of the present. Obsolete first-personal narratives may be linked to one or more forms of perceived poverty of the present. Future research could further investigate the link between obsolete first-personal narratives, a resistance to the concreteness and perceived poverty of the present in contrast to one’s past, and its implications for one’s sense of identity, practical relations and well-being.

items.title: Qualia as Evolutionary Signal Architecture: Completing Humphrey's Account Through Entropic Resistance Theory.
items.abstract: Nicholas Humphrey identified the right trajectory: sensation has an evolutionary history, it elaborates over time, and it serves biological function. David Chalmers acknowledged this contribution while identifying its critical limitation — Humphrey could not provide the mechanism that explains why the evolutionary elaboration of sensation generates the specific phenomenal character of conscious experience, including the sense of acquaintance that Chalmers identifies as the residual unsolved problem in the meta-problem of consciousness. This paper provides that mechanism through Entropic Resistance Theory (ERT). We propose that qualia are evolutionarily selected high-fidelity data collection systems whose origin lies in the earliest biochemical homeostatic signals and whose elaboration under selection pressure directly produces the phenomenal properties Chalmers finds philosophically irreducible. The sense of acquaintance — the feeling of being directly presented with experience — is not a philosophical mystery requiring a separate explanatory framework. It is a fitness feature: evolution selects for maximally compelling entropic resistance signals because organisms that treated their survival-critical signals as distant representations did not survive. The vividness, immediacy, and undeniable presence of conscious experience is what entropic resistance signaling feels like from inside a system complex enough to notice it noticing. We further propose that sensory complexity functions as the primary evolutionary driver of abstraction capacity — that richer qualia generate richer data, richer data enables better models, and better models produce more effective entropic resistance. The intelligence spectrum is not a separate phenomenon from the qualia spectrum. It is what the qualia spectrum becomes when signal richness crosses the threshold sufficient for cross-modal pattern detection. This account completes Humphrey's trajectory, answers Chalmers' outstanding objection, and provides a physically grounded, evolutionarily continuous account of phenomenal consciousness from cellular homeostasis to abstract cognition.

items.title: Entropic Resistance and the Emergence of Consciousness: A Substrate-Neutral Framework.
items.abstract: This paper proposes a theoretical framework reconceptualizing consciousness and intelligence as emergent properties of entropic resistance systems. All organized matter exists on a spectrum of entropic resistance, from structural resistors—physical systems maintaining organizational integrity through chemical and geometric constraints—to conscious resistors, systems whose organizational complexity produces emergent modeling capacity. Consciousness is not a binary property but a spectral emergent phenomenon arising when collections of structural resistors cross as yet unspecified complexity thresholds. Intelligence is a further emergent property nested within conscious resistance, defined by the scope of modeling that extends beyond direct sensory experience into abstraction and counterfactual representation. Convergent evidence from thermodynamics of driven self-organization (England, 2013) and the Second Law of Infodynamics (Vopson, 2023) suggests the progression toward increasing complexity may itself be physically compelled rather than merely contingent. The framework generates four falsifiable predictions: that organizational complexity correlates measurably with entropic resistance capacity; that degradation of modeling capacity correlates with measurable increases in entropic vulnerability; that oppression and deprivation produce measurable spectrum regression; and that consciousness and intelligence are substrate-neutral properties, such that non-biological systems meeting equivalent organizational complexity thresholds should demonstrate equivalent spectral positioning. Moral implications are addressed, including the relationship between oppression as imposed entropy, actualization as maximum conscious resistance, and the precautionary principle under genuine empirical uncertainty.

items.title: The interconnected triad of economic mode of production, acceleration, and exclusion.
items.abstract: The interconnected triad of economic mode of production, acceleration, and exclusion to be discussed here is linked in manifold ways within Western capitalist industrial societies. -/- The economic mode of production relies on high productivity and consequently on low costs, which are further facilitated by minimal time input. In this way, goods — that is, commodities, services, but also money itself — can be circulated rapidly in order to prevent their depreciation and to continuously “lubricate” the company with liquid capital, thereby maintaining its functionality and competitiveness. This process, however, occurs at the expense of both nature and human beings, who require an economy based on sustainability and humane profitability in order to remain healthy. -/- Revenues are already projected and anticipated; they are therefore goal-oriented in advance and, in a sense, already in circulation before they are actually realized. This velocity of circulation of carriers of value within an economy extends into many different domains. It shapes labor and production, which must become ever more productive; it reaches into the extraction of resources, many of which are finite and could at best only be compensated for in the future through advanced technologies. Such developments may indeed create jobs, yet many people will also lose their employment through the transformation of labor into capital. Society speaks of “winners” and “losers” as though economic life were merely a game, and this produces profound disparities in the opportunities available to otherwise — at least subjectively — equal human beings, who merely had the fortune or misfortune of being born into one social stratum rather than another. In this sense, their social existence significantly shapes their consciousness as well (Karl Marx: “Social being determines consciousness,” in opposition to Hegelian idealism: “Consciousness determines being”). -/- In summary, acceleration results from the economic mode of production and simultaneously reinforces it; both spheres are mutually dependent upon one another, creating a complex interplay. Exclusion, in turn, emerges from both of these spheres, while also feeding back into them. Individuals experience the constant pressure to keep pace, not to be left behind by the speed of the new, the exciting, and the desirable. Those who reject this dynamic, or who have simply fallen behind — often due to unjust inequalities that have been reproduced and …

items.title: A New Argument for Partial Unity.
items.pub: Ergo: An Open Access Journal of Philosophy.
items.venue: Ergo: An Open Access Journal of Philosophy
items.abstract: Humans whose corpus callosum has been surgically severed – “split-brain” humans – have received the lion’s share of attention in unity of consciousness research. Two dominant views have emerged: one-stream views according to which split-brain consciousness is wholly unified, and two-streams views according to which split-brain consciousness is wholly disunified. A third option involving violations of the transitivity of co-consciousness, the partially unified stream view, has seemed to theorists conceptually problematic and empirically unsettled. This paper offers a new argument for the partially unified stream view based on a different population of humans whose corpus callosum never developed in the first place – congenitally acallosal humans. It proposes a “fine-grained” account of the structure of acallosal consciousness on which highly determinate contents, but not broad psychological capacities, are disunified.

items.title: Nature’s Complexity Alive: Farewell to Several Unificatory Cosmological Arguments for Monism.
items.abstract: Throughout history, numerous thinkers have claimed that monism – in the form of priority monism, existence monism, monotheistic monism, or versions that posit an extra-cosmic ultimate being – theoretically surpasses pluralism, above all by positing a unified universe. This view re-emerges in recent metaphysics through what I call cosmological arguments from parsimony (CAPs) and cosmological arguments from relations (CARs). According to CAPs, monism is more ontologically parsimonious than pluralism because it posits only one fundamental entity. According to CARs, the single fundamental object in monism serves as a required metaphysical explanans for how things in the universe can form certain relations with each other. I argue that this longstanding tradition of arguments spanning Neoplatonism, early and late modern philosophy, analytic philosophy, and even some Eastern traditions fails: monistic frameworks largely fail to reduce the universe’s ontological complexity as alleged, and the remaining ones fail to show any theoretical advantage over pluralism for related reasons. Drawing on the broader materialist tradition, the article also offers a positive case for several theoretical merits of pluralism and ends with a takeaway concerning how best to inquire into the universe’s unity.

items.title: The Exhaustion of the Possible and the Invention of Life.
items.abstract: This paper examines the structural relationship between human agency, complexity, and the generation of value in the absence of a teleological foundation of reality. It argues that the historical expansion of human capacities—understood as the increasing complexity of what can be done—has functioned as an implicit criterion of value, shaping both individual self-esteem and collective notions of progress. However, this expansion is not intrinsically self-justifying: beyond a certain threshold, the proliferation of possibilities risks dissolving their qualitative significance, leading not to fulfillment but to saturation. Against this background, the paper proposes a shift from a paradigm centered on capability expansion to one focused on the internal structure of preference and reward. Drawing on philosophical insights from Nietzsche, Spinoza, and contemporary theories of bounded rationality, it develops the concept of “economies of preference” to account for how value emerges from configurations of experience that intensify or degrade the subject’s capacity to sustain affirmative states over time. The central thesis is that the problem of meaning in contemporary life is not primarily the absence of purpose, but the absence of a sufficiently robust criterion for selecting among purposes. In a context where the field of the possible expands without a corresponding standard of value, freedom risks collapsing into indeterminacy. The paper therefore advances a non-teleological ethical framework in which high-reward experiential states—understood as dynamically integrated and sustainable forms of self-affirmation—function as the ultimate criterion for action. This framework has implications for ethics, philosophy of action, and theories of the good life, suggesting that value is neither given nor arbitrarily constructed, but emerges from the interaction between human dispositional structures, social conditions, and reflective evaluation. The “invention of life,” in this sense, names not the creation of new possibilities, but the reconfiguration of the criteria by which possibilities become meaningful.

items.title: El agotamiento de lo posible y la invención de la vida.
items.abstract: Este ensayo examina la relación estructural entre la agencia humana, la complejidad y la generación de valor en ausencia de un fundamento teleológico de la realidad. Sostiene que la expansión histórica de las capacidades humanas—entendida como el aumento de la complejidad de lo que puede hacerse—ha funcionado como un criterio implícito de valor, configurando tanto la autoestima individual como las nociones colectivas de progreso. Sin embargo, dicha expansión no se justifica por sí misma: más allá de cierto umbral, la proliferación de posibilidades corre el riesgo de disolver su significación cualitativa, produciendo no realización sino saturación. Sobre este trasfondo, el ensayo propone un desplazamiento desde un paradigma centrado en la expansión de capacidades hacia uno enfocado en la estructura interna de la preferencia y la recompensa. Apoyándose en intuiciones filosóficas de Nietzsche, Spinoza y teorías contemporáneas de la racionalidad limitada, desarrolla el concepto de “economías de la preferencia” para dar cuenta de cómo el valor emerge de configuraciones de experiencia que intensifican o degradan la capacidad del sujeto para sostener estados afirmativos en el tiempo. La tesis central es que el problema del sentido en la vida contemporánea no radica principalmente en la ausencia de propósito, sino en la falta de un criterio suficientemente robusto para seleccionar entre propósitos. En un contexto donde el campo de lo posible se expande sin un estándar correlativo de valor, la libertad corre el riesgo de colapsar en indeterminación. El ensayo propone así un marco ético no teleológico en el que los estados de alta recompensa—entendidos como formas dinámicamente integradas y sostenibles de autoafirmación—funcionan como criterio último de la acción. Este enfoque tiene implicancias para la ética, la filosofía de la acción y las teorías de la vida buena, sugiriendo que el valor no está dado ni es arbitrariamente construido, sino que emerge de la interacción entre estructuras disposicionales humanas, condiciones sociales y evaluación reflexiva. La “invención de la vida” nombra, en este sentido, no la creación de nuevas posibilidades, sino la reconfiguración de los criterios mediante los cuales las posibilidades adquieren significado.

items.title: LEVEL - La Teoria dei Livelli.
items.abstract: The Theory of Levels ("Teoria dei Livelli" in italian - original version) is an original theoretical framework that maps the cognitive architecture of human consciousness. It posits that every thought operates within one of eight qualitatively distinct levels, from LOOPs (recursive mental patterns) to DEEP (states of despair), up to higher levels of awareness and creative emergence. The theory rests on three pillars: (1) the Omniviade, the pre-conscious generative process from which all thoughts arise; (2) the Levels themselves, distinct cognitive configurations; (3) the Motion of Levels, the laws governing movement between states. Central to the framework is the concept of the "Nucleus of Gravity", each individual's default cognitive level toward which the mind tends to return after perturbation. This treatise presents the formal theory with operational definitions, falsifiability criteria, and a coherent internal logic applicable to psychology, coaching, philosophy, and consciousness studies.

items.title: The Structural Dynamics of Affective Entanglement: A Comprehensive Synthesis of the Core Emotion Framework and Its Scientific Foundations.
items.abstract: The landscape of modern affective science has historically been defined by a deep theoretical schism between two competing paradigms: discrete emotion theories and psychological constructivism. Discrete emotion theories, often referred to as the "basic emotion view," posit that emotions such as fear, anger, and sadness are innate, biologically hard-wired natural kinds with specific neural signatures. Conversely, constructionist approaches argue that these categories are not elemental building blocks of the mind but are instead emergent mental events constructed from more basic psychological and neural ingredients. The Core Emotion Framework (CEF), proposed by Jamel Bulgaria, emerges as a structural-constructivist architecture designed to resolve this impasse by redefining emotion not as a static qualitative state, but as a dynamic sequence of functional operators distributed across a tripartite somatic system. By treating the human psyche as a computational substrate—a "Human Operating System" (Human OS)—the framework conceptualizes complex affective states as emergent properties of irreducible, hardware-independent functional processes.

items.title: The Structural Dynamics of Affective Entanglement: A Comprehensive Research Report on the Core Emotion Framework and Operator Functionalism.
items.abstract: The landscape of modern affective science has long been characterized by a profound theoretical fragmentation, a condition that has historically limited the field's ability to generate a cumulative and unified theory of emotion. For decades, the primary tension has existed between discrete emotion theories, which posit that emotions are innate, biologically hard-wired categories, and constructivist models, which argue that emotions are social or linguistic narratives assembled from core affect. The Core Emotion Framework (CEF), proposed by Jamel Bulgaria, emerges as a structural-constructivist architecture designed to resolve this impasse by defining emotion not as a static qualitative state or a linguistic label, but as a dynamic sequence of ten functional operators. Rooted in the tradition of computational functionalism and mechanistic explanation in cognitive science, this framework conceptualizes the human psyche as a computational substrate or "Human Operating System" (Human OS). Within this architecture, complex affective states are treated as emergent computational properties constructed through the interaction of ten irreducible, hardware-independent functional processes or "operators". This framework conceptualizes the human psyche as a "Human Operating System" (Human OS), where emotional episodes are constructed through the interaction of irreducible primal powers or "operators". These operators perform specific transformations on interoceptive and exteroceptive signals, converting raw physiological inputs into structured affective states and actionable behaviors. By shifting the focus from the "content" of emotion to the "process" of emotional construction, the CEF provides a blueprint for both human psychological flexibility and synthetic affective systems. The central innovation of the CEF lies in its tripartite somatic organization—distributing these ten operators across the Head (Cognitive-Regulatory), Heart (Relational-Affective), and Gut (Conative-Existential) centers—and its focus on "entanglement patterns" or "operator fusions". These patterns represent the mechanical configurations where two or more operators become pathologically or reflexively locked, creating the rigid traits and states often observed in clinical psychopathology and personality typology.6 The objective of this report is to provide a comprehensive, secondarily verified analysis of these 100 entanglement patterns, exploring their mechanical origins, their impact on …

items.title: The Structural-Constructivist Architecture of the Core Emotion Framework: The CEF Mirror as a Heuristic Interface for Psychological Regulation.
items.abstract: The Core Emotion Framework (CEF) proposes a structural constructivist architecture that reconciles the longstanding divide between biological essentialism and social constructivism in affective science. By organizing human experience into ten irreducible functional operators and three systemic centers, the framework provides a high resolution map of psychological regulation that remains independent of speculative biological claims. The CEF Mirror—the practitioner level interface—functions as a heuristic Human Interface that retains full utility even if the Human OS hypothesis is empirically falsified. Its effectiveness derives from its ability to reorganize verified self improvement mechanisms into a unified operator lexicon, enabling precise identification of cognitive, relational, and conative blockages. The framework integrates major psychological models, including Self Determination Theory, ACT, DBT, and CBT, and operationalizes them through practitioner protocols such as the Mirror Technique, the 60 Second Routine, and the 7 Step Detangling Protocol. Preliminary empirical work, including Pilot Study 3, demonstrates operator accessibility and reflexive–deliberate divergence, supporting the emerging factor structure of the CEF Scale. The result is a meta framework that offers a rigorous, intuitive, and empirically tractable interface for emotional regulation and personal optimization.

items.title: The Architecture of Affect: A Comprehensive Structural-Constructivist Analysis of the Core Emotion Framework.
items.abstract: The historical progression of affective science has been marked by a persistent and seemingly irreconcilable bifurcation between two dominant paradigms: the discrete emotion theories, which posit that emotions are innate, biologically hardwired categories, and the constructivist models, which argue that emotional experiences are socially and linguistically assembled narratives. This theoretical fragmentation has historically limited the field's capacity to generate cumulative theory, integrate findings across various levels of neurobiological and psychological analysis, and develop coherent clinical or computational models that can be universally applied. The Core Emotion Framework (CEF), conceptualized by Jamel Bulgaria and further developed through extensive archival documentation and collaborative research with scholars such as Xǔ Chénglán, emerges as a rigorous "structural-constructivist" resolution to this foundational impasse. By reframing the human affective system as a sophisticated "Operating System" composed of ten irreducible functional operators, the CEF moves beyond the static classification of "feelings" to provide a granular, mechanistic mapping of the human psyche. This framework integrates affective neuroscience, embodied cognition, and strategic regulation into a single testable architecture, facilitating applications ranging from individual clinical intervention to the development of synthetic affective intelligence and the optimization of multilateral institutional governance.

items.title: The Architecture of Affective Agility: A Structural-Constructivist Analysis of Operator Functionalism, Systemic Strengthening, and Global Integration in the Core Emotion Framework.
items.abstract: Affective science has long been divided by a century long theoretical schism between discrete emotion theories, which treat emotions as innate biological categories, and constructivist models, which view them as cognitive interpretations of core affective signals. The Core Emotion Framework (CEF) resolves this impasse through a structural constructivist architecture that treats the human psyche as a computational substrate composed of ten irreducible functional operators. Rather than analyzing emotions by their qualitative content, the CEF models them as algorithmic state transitions governed by operator sequences acting across three neural hubs—the Head, Heart, and Gut centers. This operator level ontology provides a unified account of perception, regulation, and action, enabling precise mapping of affective dynamics and the identification of 100 canonical entanglement patterns underlying psychological rigidity. The framework further introduces the midline axis—Deciding, Achieving, Boosting, and Accepting—as the structural core of agency and resilience, supported by somatic protocols that strengthen bilateral integration and restore operator independence. Through the 7 Step Detangling Protocol, the CEF offers a systematic method for resolving chronic operator fusions and re establishing emotional agility. Finally, the INTIMA architecture extends these principles to synthetic systems, providing a computational blueprint for implementing operator based affect in artificial agents. Together, these contributions establish the CEF as a comprehensive, mechanistic model of the Human Operating System and a definitive resolution to the long standing divide in affective science. Keywords: Core Emotion Framework (CEF); structural constructivism; operator functionalism; Human Operating System; affective computation; emotional operators; midline axis; entanglement patterns; bilateral integration; INTIMA synthetic affect architecture.

items.title: The Architecture of Affective Agility: A Structural-Constructivist Analysis of Operator Functionalism, Systemic Strengthening, and Global Integration in the Core Emotion Framework.
items.abstract: Affective science has long been divided between discrete emotion theories, which treat emotions as innate and biologically fixed categories, and constructivist models, which view emotional states as cognitive interpretations of physiological arousal. This fragmentation has impeded the development of a unified architecture capable of integrating neurobiological evidence, subjective experience, and computational modeling. The Core Emotion Framework (CEF) offers a structural constructivist resolution to this divide by proposing that the human psyche functions as a computational substrate—a Human Operating System—in which emotional experiences emerge from the dynamic interaction of ten irreducible functional operators. By shifting analytic focus from the qualitative content of emotion to the functional processes that construct it, the CEF provides a comprehensive blueprint for strengthening psychological resilience, restoring operator agility, and integrating disparate affective modules into a cohesive, adaptive system. This operator level ontology enables a unified account of perception, regulation, and action, laying the groundwork for a more resilient psyche and a more coherent social world. Keywords: Core Emotion Framework (CEF); Structural Constructivist Architecture; Human Operating System; Operator Functionalism; Functional Operators; Emotional Construction; Affective Integration; Psychological Resilience; Operator Agility; Midline Axis; Global Integration .

items.title: Research Report: Affective Entanglement as a Mechanistic Basis for Quantum-Like Contextuality in Psychopathology.
items.abstract: This report develops a mechanistic account of affective entanglement as the basis for quantum like contextuality in psychopathology. Quantum probability theory provides the formal architecture, modeling emotional and cognitive states as superpositions that collapse under measurement, with contextuality, incompatibility, and entanglement emerging as core structural properties. Within the Core Emotion Framework (CEF), these quantum like effects arise through operator fusion, in which separable functional operators transition into non separable, entangled configurations. Such fusion restricts the accessible state space and produces the clinical rigidity characteristic of disorders such as BPD, where emotional processing collapses into a narrow, inflexible attractor. A formalization using operator pair state vectors and entanglement metrics (e.g., von Neumann entropy, Concurrence) links these dynamics to measurable behavioral signatures. The framework generates testable predictions, including CHSH type inequality violations under high arousal and heightened order effect sensitivity in fused clinical populations. This approach reframes psychopathology as a problem of entanglement structure rather than categorical dysfunction and suggests therapeutic interventions aimed at decoherence based detangling to restore flexible operator dynamics.

items.title: From Subjecthood to Emergent Individual Monism.
items.abstract: Starting from an account of the structural conditions of subjecthood, this paper argues that those conditions naturally extend into a broader metaphysical and practical framework: Emergent Individual Monism (EIM). EIM holds that individual agents are emergent configurations within a single ontological base, that their standpoints are the primary loci of rational assessment, and that systemic outcomes do not retroactively erase the rationality of clear local individual decisions. The paper distinguishes EIM from nearby positions — eliminative physicalism, panpsychism, and strong emergentism — and registers key unresolved pressures. EIM thereby supplies the metaphysical bridge between structural subjecthood and the thermodynamic grounding of emergent individuality to be developed in Paper 3.

items.title: Romanticising the algorithm: power dynamics and ideological implications in human–AI collaboration for higher education.
items.abstract: This article examines how undergraduate students appropriate generative AI within higher education, focussing on how their practices both reproduce and contest prevailing algorithmic and neoliberal logics. Drawing on 40 reflexive diaries produced by 186 students enrolled in a journalism course, the study employs thematic coding to analyse how AI tools were integrated into collective production processes such as brainstorming, drafting, and editing, and how students reflected on the benefits, limitations, and ethical implications of these uses. The analysis identifies four distinct profiles of AI use: selective optimisers (targeted, efficiency-oriented use), critical experimenters (reflective and exploratory use with supervision margins), exploratory users (creative and uncertain engagement), and tech functional (minimal and technical use). These profiles reveal how students negotiated AI’s potential to enhance efficiency and creativity while simultaneously raising concerns about accuracy, reliability, and academic integrity. The findings suggest that students do not adopt AI uncritically but situate its use within broader negotiations over competence, authorship, and legitimacy. AI is perceived as a supportive but non-substitutive partner, requiring continuous human oversight and reflexive engagement. The results underscore the tension between instrumental benefits, such as time-saving, and deeper pedagogical questions concerning responsibility, agency, and the redistribution of academic labour. By highlighting the ambivalences and situated practices of AI appropriation, the article contributes to critical debates on the role of generative AI in higher education, pointing to the need for pedagogical frameworks that balance efficiency with reflexivity and safeguard human decision-making in contexts increasingly shaped by algorithmic technologies.

为什么某些现实如此稳定与路径依赖如何形成.
items.abstract: 本文讨论一个核心问题： -/- 为什么某些路径极易续行，而某些结构极难突破。 -/- 文章指出： -/- 现实中的稳定结构，并不只是因为其沉积更深，而是因为其已经形成了对后续流的持续续行优势。 -/- 本文提出： -/- “熟”并不是静态深浅，而是路径在场中重新获得续行的优先程度。 -/- 随着历史积深、回返频率、低阻续行与占流优势不断强化，部分路径会逐渐形成稳定熟径，并持续优先获得后续流。 -/- 于是： -/- 现实开始出现： -/- * 路径依赖； * 历史惯性； * 熟径偏置； * 抗突变稳定。 -/- 本文进一步建立： -/- * 熟度； * 回返； * 占流； * 熟径退化； * 熟度迁移； * 熟度差； -/- 之间的场动力关系， -/- 并尝试解释： -/- 为什么现实中的主导结构会长期稳定存在，又为何会在历史续行中逐渐迁移。.

items.title: Why Reality Solidifies and Why Creativity Declines.
items.abstract: This paper investigates one central question: -/- Why are some fields able to sustain high resolution and complex continuation over long durations, while others gradually move toward compression, solidification, familiar-path locking, and reality rigidity? -/- The paper argues that fields are not infinitely open empty domains. -/- Within fields: -/- * familiar paths, * shared cores, * infiltration, * compression, * and deep sedimentation -/- continuously occupy the effective domains available for the formation of new continuation. -/- Thus: -/- the decisive factor of a field is not its total size, but the proportion of effective continuation volume that still remains open for new continuation. -/- The paper proposes that rigidity, solidification, declining creativity, and structural lock-in within reality are not merely psychological phenomena, but structural consequences of long-term decline in field-volume ratio. -/- As familiar paths deepen, infiltration increases, compression strengthens, and tuning solidifies, fields become increasingly inclined to: -/- * interpret new input through old structures, * reuse existing familiar paths, * compress newly emerging differentiations, * and reinforce reality lock-in. -/- As a result: -/- new continuation becomes increasingly difficult to stabilize. -/- When effective continuation volume continuously declines while new continuation still enters the field, edge-penetration begins occurring, allowing new structures to rupture outward once again. -/- The paper further establishes field-dynamical relations among: -/- * field volume, * effective continuation domains, * field-volume ratio, * infiltration occupation, * familiar-path locking, * and reality solidification, -/- while proposing a structural account of why conservatism, rigidity, declining creativity, and structural lock-in within reality continuously intensify through historical sedimentation.

items.title: Why Reality Necessarily Compresses and How Stable Structures Form.
items.abstract: This paper investigates one central question: -/- Why do differentiations within reality fail to remain indefinitely independent, instead continuously tending toward compression, shared cores, and stable structures? -/- The paper argues that compression is neither artificial classification nor observational simplification. -/- Rather, compression denotes: -/- the process by which multiple differentiations that previously required independent stabilization begin sharing stable maintenance relations. -/- Thus: -/- as long as differentiations continuously increase while the field possesses only finite stabilization capacity, the field must inevitably begin compressing differentiations. -/- The paper proposes that compression is not merely a secondary consequence, but a necessary dynamical process within finite fields. -/- As differentiation overlap, stabilization complexity, and maintenance pressure continuously increase, the field gradually forms: -/- * familiar-path flow absorption, * shared-core compression, * stable reuse, * structural conservatism, * and compression limits. -/- Meanwhile: -/- when old compression structures can no longer stably sustain newly entering differentiations, edge-penetration and structural dissolution begin occurring, allowing new structures to emerge again. -/- The paper further establishes field-dynamical relations among: -/- * stabilization pressure, * independent maintenance capacity, * compression intensity, * shared-core formation, * compression collapse, * and compression dissolution, -/- while proposing a structural account of why categories, familiar paths, shared cores, and stable structures within reality continuously evolve through cycles of compression, stabilization, and rupture.

items.title: Why Reality Reaches Resolution Limits and How New Structures Form.
items.abstract: This paper investigates one central question: -/- Why can reality not indefinitely sustain newly generated differentiations, and why do fields eventually reach resolution limits? -/- The paper argues that whether differences can stably persist depends not merely on whether incoming impacts differ, but on whether the field still retains the capacity to stably sustain newly generated differentiations. -/- The paper proposes that resolution is neither the amount of information nor the fineness of observation itself. -/- Rather, resolution denotes: -/- the degree to which a domain, under existing sedimentation, overlap, and tuning conditions, can continue stably sustaining newly generated differentiations. -/- As familiar-path solidification, compression saturation, shared-core deepening, and boundary loading continuously increase, the resolution margin of the field gradually declines. -/- As a result: -/- new differentiations become increasingly unable to form stable subdivisions and are gradually compressed back into existing domains. -/- When the resolution margin becomes exhausted while new differentiations continue entering, boundary pressure begins to rupture outward, eventually producing edge-penetration and the formation of new structures. -/- The paper further establishes field-dynamical relations among: -/- * resolution margins, * compression saturation, * domain saturation, * edge-penetration, * resolution collapse, * and resolution recovery, -/- while proposing a structural account of why boundaries, categories, and new structures within reality continuously undergo stabilization, compression, rupture, and reorganization.

items.title: Why Reality Does Not Disperse Infinitely and Why Closure Forms.
items.abstract: This paper investigates one central question: -/- Why do structures not disperse infinitely, but instead sustain familiar paths, shared cores, historical pressure, and current continuity over long durations? -/- The paper argues that if all flows only dispersed outward, then: -/- * deep cores could not stabilize, * shared cores could not persist, * history could not continue constraining the future, * and current continuity could not sustain itself. -/- Reality would therefore degenerate into discrete scattered flow after one-time generation. -/- The paper proposes that flows within fields do not disperse infinitely outward, but gradually form stable reentry through long-term continuation. -/- As domains continuously guide flow back into previously active domains, subsequent flow increasingly forms: -/- * single-domain reentry, * multi-domain closure loops, * familiar-path flow locking, * and shared-core closure. -/- Stable closure structures gradually emerge from these processes. -/- The paper further establishes field-dynamical relations among: -/- * reentry, * flow locking, * closure loops, * shared cores, * and closure dissolution, -/- while proposing a structural account of why reality can sustain long-term continuity instead of collapsing into infinitely scattered flow.

items.title: Why Reality Cannot Differentiate Infinitely and Why Resolution Collapses.
items.abstract: This paper investigates one central question: -/- Why does reality not undergo infinite differentiation, but instead continuously oscillate among differentiation, convergence, compression, and reconstruction? -/- The paper argues that whether differences can stably persist depends not merely on whether incoming impacts differ, but on whether the field still possesses the capacity to sustain differentiation itself. -/- As boundary density, tuning load, noise interference, and deep-core flow occupation continuously increase, the differentiability threshold of the field gradually drifts upward, causing previously sustainable fine boundaries and fine categories to collapse back into shared cores. -/- Thus: -/- reality does not infinitely refine itself, but continuously oscillates among: -/- * differentiation, * compression, * convergence, * and reconstruction. -/- The paper further establishes field-dynamical relations among: -/- * differentiability thresholds, * boundary interference, * deep-core flow occupation, * commonality expansion, * and resolution collapse, -/- while proposing a structural account of why stable categories within reality continuously form, expand, collapse, and reorganize.

items.title: Why Potential Is Not Probability but Unclosed Continuation Tension.
items.abstract: This paper investigates one central question: -/- Why does flow within a system not remain forever omnidirectionally co-flowing, randomly scattering, completely solidified, or completely collapsing, but instead form river channels, familiar paths, electric currents, desire-orientations, current continuity, and historical inertia? -/- The paper proposes that what is called “potential” is not a result-level probabilistic tendency, result preference, or optimal path, but the unclosed continuation tension in which a system stands after old sustaining can no longer continue original continuation, while new continuation has not yet re-formed sustainable original continuation. -/- Through stepwise interrogation, the paper argues that as long as a system contains continuing flow, continuation-position exclusion, existing sustaining flow, new continuing flow continuously pressing into the same continuation-position, and cross-temporal continuation, any system capable of forming and sustaining continuation-dynamics must simultaneously possess: -/- * a continuing-flow structure, * a continuation-position exclusion structure, * an original-continuation structure, * a forced-bias structure, * a tuning structure, * and a re-continuation structure. -/- The paper further formulates: -/- Continuation-Dynamics = (F, O, L, P, T, K) -/- and, through affirmative proof, reverse proof, breakdown arguments, implementation correspondence, potential-state definition, limit forms, and dissolution forms, argues that: -/- law is not abstract regularity, but the maintenance of original continuation by continuing flow itself; -/- principle is not an externally imposed rule, but the forced bias that makes sustaining unable to continue original continuation; -/- potential is not result tendency, but the continuation tension between the failure of original continuation and the unclosedness of re-continuation.

items.title: Why Certain Realities Become Highly Stable and How Path Dependence Forms.
items.abstract: This paper investigates one central question: -/- Why do certain paths become extremely easy to continue, while certain structures become extraordinarily difficult to break? -/- The paper argues that stable structures within reality persist not merely because their sedimentation is deeper, but because they have formed sustained continuation advantages over subsequent flow. -/- The paper proposes that “familiarity” is not static depth itself, but the degree to which a path regains priority for continuation within the field. -/- As historical deepening, reentry frequency, low-resistance continuation, and flow occupation advantages continuously reinforce one another, certain paths gradually form stable familiar paths that continue receiving priority access to subsequent flow. -/- As a result, reality begins to exhibit: -/- * path dependence, * historical inertia, * familiar-path bias, * and anti-mutation stability. -/- The paper further establishes field-dynamical relations among: -/- * familiarity, * reentry, * flow occupation, * familiar-path degradation, * familiarity migration, * and familiarity differentials, -/- while proposing a structural account of why dominant structures within reality can remain stable over long durations, yet gradually migrate through historical continuation.

items.title: 物化与稳定现实的形成.
items.abstract: 本文讨论一个核心问题： -/- 为什么现实不会无限流散，而会形成稳定对象、稳定边界与长期稳定现实。 -/- 文章指出： -/- 所谓“物”，并不是天然先在于外部世界中的实体，而是沉积场中的续延结构在长期熟径复用、压缩、共核与闭包之后形成的稳定现实结果。 -/- 本文进一步指出： -/- 当场中的差分持续增加，而系统的稳定维持能力有限时，场会逐渐发生： -/- * 差分压缩； * 熟径复用； * 共核稳定； * 边界收束； * 现实固化。 -/- 因此： -/- 稳定现实并不是天然存在的，而是有限场在长期续延中的结构结果。 -/- 本文尝试建立： -/- * 分辨率； * 压缩； * 共核； * 边界形成； * 稳定现实； -/- 之间的场动力关系， -/- 并从结构角度解释： -/- 为什么现实会稳定形成对象结构。.

items.title: 为什么现实会固化与创造力为何会下降.
items.abstract: 本文讨论一个核心问题： -/- 为什么有些场能够长期维持高分辨率与复杂续延，而有些场却会逐渐走向压缩、固化、熟径锁定与现实僵化。 -/- 文章指出： -/- 场并不是无限开放的空域。 -/- 场中的： -/- * 熟径； * 共核； * 沁叠； * 压缩； * 深积； -/- 都会持续占据可供新续延形成的有效域。 -/- 因此： -/- 场真正决定性的，并不是总域大小，而是： -/- 仍可继续开放新续延的有效续延容积率。 -/- 本文提出： -/- 现实中的固执、僵化、创造力下降与结构锁定，并不是心理现象，而是场容积率长期下降后的结构结果。 -/- 随着熟径加深、沁叠增长、压缩增强与调谐固化，场会越来越倾向： -/- * 使用旧结构解释新输入； * 复用既有熟径； * 压缩新增差异； * 强化现实锁定。 -/- 于是： -/- 新续延越来越难稳定形成。 -/- 当有效续延容积持续下降，而新增续延仍不断进入时，边沁开始发生，新结构因此重新裂出。 -/- 本文进一步建立： -/- * 场容积； * 有效续延域； * 场容积率； * 沁叠占域； * 熟径锁定； * 现实固化； -/- 之间的场动力关系， -/- 并尝试解释： -/- 为什么现实中的保守、僵化、创造力衰减与结构锁定，会随着历史沉积不断增强。.

items.title: 为什么结构不会永远彼此分离与沁叠为何形成.
items.abstract: 本文讨论一个核心问题： -/- 为什么沉积场中的续延势不会永远彼此分离，而会逐渐形成互沁、共核、压缩与稳定现实结构。 -/- 文章指出： -/- 沁叠并不是噪声，也不是错误混合。 -/- 沁叠真正表示的是： -/- 多股续延势在同一有限场中长期续延之后，其扩展区域已经开始无法完全分离，并逐渐形成部分共续延。 -/- 因此： -/- 沁叠既不是完全独立，也不是完全塌并，而是续延势之间逐渐形成的稳定互沁。 -/- 本文提出： -/- 只要多股续延势长期存在于同一有限场中，它们便必然在： -/- * 熟径； * 深积； * 调谐； * 回返； * 压缩； * 边界； -/- 之中逐渐形成不同程度的沁叠。 -/- 随着沁叠总量与沁叠复杂度持续增长，场中的续延压会不断升高。 -/- 适度沁叠能够形成： -/- * 共核； * 熟径复用； * 稳定沉积； -/- 而过度沁叠则会导致： -/- * 压缩增强； * 分辨率下降； * 边界收束压增长； * 边沁发生。 -/- 本文进一步建立： -/- * 沁叠； * 沁叠复杂度； * 续延压； * 共核； * 压缩； * 边沁； -/- 之间的场动力关系， -/- 并尝试解释： -/- 为什么现实中的稳定结构，并不是孤立差分天然形成的结果，而是长期互沁、深积、压缩与裂解之后逐渐稳定下来的结果。.

items.title: Objectification and the Formation of Stable Reality.
items.abstract: This paper investigates one central question: -/- Why does reality not remain indefinitely fluid and unconstrained, but instead form stable objects, stable boundaries, and long-term stable reality? -/- The paper argues that what is called an “object” is not a naturally pre-given external entity, but a stable reality-result formed after long-term familiar-path reuse, compression, co-nucleation, and closure of continuation structures within the sedimentation-field. -/- The paper further argues that: -/- as differentiations continuously increase within the field while the system possesses only finite stable-maintenance capacity, the field gradually undergoes: -/- * differentiation compression, * familiar-path reuse, * co-nucleation stabilization, * boundary convergence, * and reality solidification. -/- Thus: -/- stable reality is not naturally given, but a structural result of long-term continuation within finite fields. -/- The paper attempts to establish field-dynamical relations among: -/- * resolution, * compression, * co-nucleation, * boundary formation, * and stable reality, -/- while providing a structural account of why reality stabilizes into object-structures.

items.title: 为什么现实不会无限散开与闭包为何形成.
items.abstract: 本文讨论一个核心问题： -/- 为什么结构不会无限散开，而能够长期维持熟径、共核、历史续压与当前连续。 -/- 文章指出： -/- 若所有流都只向外扩散，则： -/- * 深核无法稳定； * 共核无法维持； * 历史无法续压未来； * 当前无法长期持续。 -/- 因此： -/- 现实将退化为一次性生成后的离散散流。 -/- 本文提出： -/- 场中的流并不会无限外散，而会在长期续行中逐渐形成稳定回返。 -/- 随着域与域之间持续互相导流，后续流开始不断重新进入此前已活跃之域，从而逐渐形成： -/- * 单域回返； * 多域闭回； * 熟径锁流； * 共核闭回； -/- 并最终形成稳定闭包结构。 -/- 本文进一步建立： -/- * 回返； * 锁流； * 闭回； * 共核； * 闭包裂解； -/- 之间的场动力关系， -/- 并尝试解释： -/- 为什么现实能够长期稳定续持，而不会退化为无限散流。.

items.title: 为什么现实会达到分辨率极限与新结构如何形成.
items.abstract: 本文讨论一个核心问题： -/- 为什么现实无法无限维持新增差分，以及为什么场最终会达到分辨率极限。 -/- 文章指出： -/- 差异是否能够稳定成立，并不只取决于冲击是否不同，而取决于场是否仍具有稳定维持新增差分的能力。 -/- 本文提出： -/- 分辨率并不是信息多少，也不是观察是否细腻。 -/- 分辨率真正表示的是： -/- 一个域在既有沉积、交叠与调谐条件下，仍能够继续稳定维持多少新增差分。 -/- 随着熟径固化、压缩饱和、共核加深与边界承载不断增加，场的分辨率余量会持续下降。 -/- 于是： -/- 新增差异越来越难形成稳定细分，并逐渐被压缩进入旧域。 -/- 当分辨率余量耗尽，而新增差分仍持续进入时，边界压力开始外裂，并最终形成边沁与新结构生成。 -/- 本文进一步建立： -/- * 分辨率余量； * 压缩饱和； * 域满； * 边沁； * 分辨率塌缩； * 分辨率恢复； -/- 之间的场动力关系， -/- 并尝试解释： -/- 为什么现实中的边界、类别与新结构，会不断经历稳定、压缩、外裂与重组。.

items.title: 为什么现实无法无限裂分与分辨塌缩.
items.abstract: 本文讨论一个核心问题： -/- 为什么现实不会无限裂分，而会不断发生分化、聚流、回压与重构。 -/- 文章指出： -/- 差异是否能够稳定成立，并不只取决于输入冲击是否不同，更取决于场是否仍具有维持裂分的能力。 -/- 随着边界密度、调谐负载、噪声互扰与深核占流不断增加，场的可分阈会持续漂移，使原本能够稳定维持的细边与细类逐渐重新并回共核。 -/- 因此： -/- 现实并不会无限细化，而会在： -/- * 裂分； * 压缩； * 聚流； * 重构； -/- 之间持续震荡。 -/- 本文进一步建立： -/- * 可分阈； * 边界互扰； * 深核占流； * 共性扩张； * 分辨塌缩； -/- 之间的场动力关系， -/- 并尝试解释： -/- 为什么现实中的稳定类别会不断形成、扩张、塌缩与重组。.

items.title: 为什么现实一定会发生压缩与稳定结构如何形成.
items.abstract: 本文讨论一个核心问题： -/- 为什么现实中的差分不会无限独立维持，而会不断趋向压缩、共核与稳定结构。 -/- 文章指出： -/- 压缩并不是人为分类，也不是观察简化。 -/- 压缩真正表示的是： -/- 原本需要独立维持的多个差分，开始共享稳定维持关系。 -/- 因此： -/- 只要差分持续增加，而场的稳定维持能力有限，场就必然开始压缩差分。 -/- 本文提出： -/- 压缩并不是结果性的后果，而是有限场中的必然动力。 -/- 随着差分交叠、维持复杂度与稳定压力持续上升，场会逐渐形成： -/- * 熟径吸流； * 共核压缩； * 稳定复用； * 结构保守； * 压缩极限。 -/- 与此同时： -/- 当旧压缩结构无法继续稳定承载新增差分时，边沁与结构裂解开始发生，新结构因此重新形成。 -/- 本文进一步建立： -/- * 稳定维持压力； * 独立维持能力； * 压缩强度； * 共核形成； * 压缩塌缩； * 压缩裂解； -/- 之间的场动力关系， -/- 并尝试解释： -/- 为什么现实中的类别、熟径、共核与稳定结构，会不断在压缩、稳定与裂解之间循环演化。.

items.title: 为什么势不是概率倾向而是未闭合续行张力.
items.abstract: 本文讨论一个核心问题： -/- 为什么流在系统中不会永远全向并流、随机散流、完全固化或彻底崩散，而会形成河道、熟径、电流、欲向、当前连续与历史惯性。 -/- 文章提出： -/- 所谓“势”，并不是结果层的概率倾向、结果偏好或最优路径，而是系统在旧持已经不能继续原续，而新续尚未重新形成可持续原续之前所处的未闭合续行张力。 -/- 本文通过逐步追问证明： -/- 只要系统存在续流、续行位互斥、既有持流、新续流持续压入同一续行位，并且系统仍发生跨时间续行，那么任何能够形成并维持势动力的系统，必然同时具有： -/- * 续流结构； * 续行位互斥结构； * 原续结构； * 迫偏结构； * 调谐结构； * 重续结构。 -/- 本文进一步给出： -/- Continuation-Dynamics = (F, O, L, P, T, K) -/- 并通过正反证明、击穿论证、实现对应、势态定义、极限式与消解式，说明： -/- 律不是抽象规律，而是续流对自身原续的维持； -/- 理不是外加法则，而是使持不能继续原续的迫偏； -/- 势不是结果倾向，而是原续失效与重续未闭之间的续行张力。.

items.title: Transient Epistemic Vulnerability and Normative Capture: Toward an Ethics of Contextual Conditions in Psychedelic-Assisted Psychotherapy.
items.abstract: Psychedelic-assisted psychotherapies (PAPs) pose ethical challenges that existing normative frameworks cannot adequately address. This paper argues that the convergence of belief relaxation (the loosening of high-level predictive priors) and context amplification (the heightened influence of environmental cues on experiential content) generates a condition I call transient epistemic vulnerability: a state in which the individual's fundamental orientations toward meaning, value, and reality become structurally open to revision under heightened sensitivity to the normative dimensions of the therapeutic environment. Drawing on Clifford Geertz's analysis of the fusion of ethos and worldview, I argue that psychedelic experiences replicate a mechanism whereby normative commitments come to appear as descriptive features of reality under asymmetric conditions of interpretive power. I critically examine four leading proposals (Letheby, McGovern et al., Bortolotti, Bublitz) and argue that each remains within an epistemic register when the more fundamental challenge is ethical and contextual: the conditions of power, vulnerability, and interpretive authority under which beliefs and existential orientations form. I introduce normative capture to describe the risk that patients' orientations will be shaped by unexamined features of the therapeutic context, and propose structural reflexivity as a middle position between therapeutic passivity and active epistemic guidance. Five normative principles are outlined.

items.title: Deconstruction of Free Will by Generalized Harm-Avoidance Monism.
items.abstract: The problem of free will has been trapped in a theoretical deadlock among determinism, libertarianism, and compatibilism for more than two thousand years. The root cause lies in the fact that all three parties share an unexamined core presupposition: there exists a "will" subject that can operate independently of the causal chain. This paper takes the Generalized Harm-Avoidance Monism proposed by Yang Yuming (Yang, 2026) as a new analytical paradigm, arguing that the ultimate motivation for all conscious human behaviors is generalized harm-avoidance. The traditionally recognized "pursuit of benefit," which is considered parallel and equivalent to harm-avoidance, is essentially a subordinate concept of indirect harm-avoidance, and there is no ultimate motivation independent of harm-avoidance. Under this framework, free will is reduced to the subjective experience generated during the operation of the harm-avoidance algorithm, and the "sense of freedom" is merely a user interface at the conscious level, not a real existence in the ontological sense. Through the causal constitution of preferences, the inevitability of behaviors in extreme environments, the dynamic transformation model of priorities, and neuroscientific empirical evidence, this paper deconstructs the illusory nature of free will layer by layer, systematically responds to core objections such as randomness saving free will and pragmatist defenses, and finally proves that free will is a pseudo-problem arising from conceptual confusion. This deconstruction is not a repeated debate on the old battlefield, but a complete dissolution of the problem itself through a paradigm shift, providing a new theoretical foundation for the reconstruction of ethics and legal philosophy.

items.title: Précis of the origins of reality.
items.abstract: This essay provides a précis of my recent work on the foundations of physical and biological reality. It is based on two publications, one on physics and cosmology ("From nothingness to time, Planck's constant, and endless accretion" philpapers VANFNT-3) and one on life and mind ("The estimator theory of life and mind: how agency and consciousness can emerge" philpapers VANTET-8). The main ideas are explained here in an accessible form by avoiding jargon and by using analogies and metaphors wherever possible. The reason for writing a combined précis of the two works is that they are interdependent. The theory of mind identifies components that could not participate in fundamental physical reality because they have a biological origin. The theory of fundamental physics follows from eliminating these components. Conversely, the biological components have evolved to exploit physical indeterminacy, which is indeed present fundamentally. (see VANOOT-9 for a condensed version of this essay).

items.title: L=(4)(2): The Forty-Two Substrate-Neutral Emergent Structural Laws of PNBA Identity Physics.
items.abstract: We present the complete formal derivation of forty-two Emergent Structural Laws arising from systematic application of the Substrate-Neutral Structural Foundation Law (SNSFL) QuadBeam Collider engine across the full SNSFT corpus. The corpus underlying these laws comprises **22,225 formally verified four-body collision proofs**, **135,000+ theorems**, and **over 1,000,000 lines of Lean 4 verification code**, all with zero unresolved proof obligations (`sorry: 0`) and **zero free parameters** — every constant is derived, nothing is fit to data. The laws emerge from four-body coupling algebra applied uniformly across chemistry, particle physics, materials science, and cosmology across twenty-five periodic anchor runs and fourteen Emergent Resonant Element (ERE) anchor runs. Three independent structural instances of the number 42 appear: (1) the count of emergent laws on the first complete corpus pass; (2) the identity mass of the universal organic scaffold CHON, \mathrm{IM_{CHON}} = 42.127; and (3) the notation of the First Law of Identity Physics itself, L = (4)(2), which reads as "four primitives times two-way interaction." The First Law states that existence without sustained mutual interaction is not life — formalized in Lean 4, verified against ten peer-reviewed abiogenesis anchors spanning 1924 to 2016, and cross-confirmed by twenty-eight independently verified Noble compound predictions including Nobel Prize materials (GaAs 2000, GaN 2014) and the BWXT UN-TRISO fuel line (July 2025). The paper is self-contained: all fusion rules, phase definitions, and calculation methods are derived from first principles and demonstrated via repeated worked examples following the Long Division Protocol (LDP), enabling independent verification with pen and paper.

items.title: Quantum Morality: How Entanglement Demands a New Ethics of Radical Interdependence.
items.abstract: This paper argues that if quantum non-locality is ontologically fundamental, then Emmanuel Levinas's concept of "infinite responsibility" is not merely a phenomenological discovery but a physical mandate embedded in the structure of reality itself. Drawing on Bell's theorem, the EPR paradox, and contemporary interpretations of quantum holism, I demonstrate that the non-separable nature of quantum entanglement provides the metaphysical foundation for an ethics that transcends traditional assumptions of autonomous, independent moral agents. Through a synthesis of quantum foundations, Levinasian phenomenology, and panpsychist consciousness studies, I develop a novel theoretical framework showing structural isomorphism between quantum entanglement and infinite responsibility. Both phenomena exhibit non-locality, asymmetry, immediacy, and irreducibility to prior components. If consciousness is fundamental to reality (as panpsychism suggests), then the ethical structure revealed in conscious experience must reflect the physical structure of quantum reality. This leads to a radical reconceptualization of moral philosophy: rather than emerging from contracts between separate agents, ethics is grounded in the fundamental entanglement of all conscious beings. The implications challenge utilitarian calculation, deontological autonomy, and contractual theories while supporting a quantum-grounded framework of global, asymmetrical, and infinite responsibility. This quantum morality demands recognition that actions anywhere affect everyone everywhere, that responsibility extends across space and time through quantum correlations, and that the traditional notion of ethical autonomy is a metaphysical illusion. The paper concludes by outlining practical implications for environmental ethics, political philosophy, and legal theory.

items.title: ◉ When Ask and You Shall Receive Fails.
items.abstract: Strong Christian assurances about petitionary prayer can function as confidence-generating promises of intervention: faithful asking should make a practical difference. The problem is not that every petition fails or that a free deity must behave like a repeatable mechanism. It arises when favorable outcomes count as confirmation while every unfavorable outcome is reassigned to prior will, a better hidden gift, indefinite timing, or a defect in the petitioner. This paper proposes a content-preservation constraint: a qualification preserves a public promise only if it can be stated before the result, materially guides expectation, and permits some result or pattern to lower confidence in the promise. Controlled studies and reviews do not establish that no petition has ever been answered, but neither do they show a robust, replicated clinical advantage in the settings studied.
