An every-outcome rule supplies no independent contrast; it becomes more troubling when failure is displaced onto petitioners, eroding confidence in ordinary evidence while protecting institutional authority. That structure warrants a cautious gaslighting analogy in some cases, not a blanket charge of conscious abuse. Prayer may still function as relationship, lament, solidarity, attention, or coping. Those goods, and the logical possibility of occasional opaque answers, do not confirm dependable intervention. On the outcome evidence considered here, the stronger promise lacks the public warrant its rhetoric claims.

items.title: The Moral Credentials of Divine Authority — 42.
items.abstract: Rational moral deference to a candidate God-concept requires a prior, defeasible credentials case with three features: its force is independent of the disputed authority claim, it discriminates trustworthy from untrustworthy claimants, and it remains open to correction. This priority is structural, not a demand that every act of trust begin with certainty or religiously neutral evidence. People encounter purported ultimate authorities through rival traditions, texts, institutions, experiences, arguments, and alleged commands; they do not begin with an already certified perfectly good being. A cumulative comparison shows that power, creatorhood, reward, threat, self-attestation, and textual attribution can accompany both trustworthy and untrustworthy claimants, while total appeals to inscrutable goodness remove the contrast needed to identify moral goodness. Modified divine-command theories may explain how commands from a loving deity generate obligations, but they do not by themselves identify which candidate or interpretation expresses that character. Modest skepticism about human judgment counsels humility; global skepticism defeats warranted praise and revelation-identification as well as criticism. The result is a prior-screening requirement: evidence of truthful, just, compassionate, non-manipulative character must be independent of the disputed claim, discriminating, and publicly correctable before rational surrender of moral judgment. This conclusion does not disprove theism or make human judgment infallible. It states the burden that separates worship from capitulation to power.

items.title: ◉ The Floating Fortress of Theology: Empirical Detachment, Hermeneutic Retreat, and the Public Failure of Christian Realism.
items.abstract: Some Christian claims do more than express worship, identity, or metaphysical commitment. They present specific divine agency as a public explanation of events or as public evidence for a religious tradition. This paper argues that when the cited record does not supply the evidential contrast required for that stronger claim, and a defense removes the contrast while supplying no independent support, the resulting package does not warrant the stronger explanation. A materially revised view may remain meaningful, coherent, true, or privately warranted, but it must stand on other reasons. To distinguish responsible clarification from insulation, the paper develops two constraints. The public-difference requirement says that an explanatory claim must make some prospectively identifiable difference to expectation relative to live alternatives. The prospective-accountability requirement says that a qualification can inherit the earlier argument's evidential credit only when it preserves the relevant content, is independently motivated, constrains interpretation rather than merely absorbing the result at hand, and remains open to evidential loss. These constraints are applied to petitionary prayer, miracle testimony, models of divine action, and figurative or deferred readings of religious claims. Across these domains, favorable outcomes can retain the authority of a concrete claim while unfavorable outcomes trigger qualifications, domain shifts, or semantic changes that reduce exposure without clearly acknowledging changed content. This is a diagnostic failure mode, not a claim that every revision is ad hoc or every Christian proposition false. In that precise sense, the fortress floats.

items.title: Sincere Seeking and Divine Hiddenness — 50.
items.abstract: A strong Christian sincere-seeking promise is evidentially vulnerable because the religious record does not display the kind of access the promise leads people to expect. This paper distinguishes that strong promise from modest invitations to seek, defines its target as a specified Christian God-concept, and derives three public expectations: meaningful convergence on the target, comparative portability across cultural boundaries, and accessible success conditions that leave little apparently nonresistant nonbelief. Each expectation meets pressure. Sincere seekers report incompatible discoveries; religious perception and affiliation depend strongly on inherited concepts and culturally trained attention; and some apparently open persons report sustained nonbelief despite serious inquiry. Those observations are not logically incompatible with a hidden deity, since purposive-hiddenness, relationship, and transformation accounts can accommodate them. The relevant question, however, is comparative: are the observations more expected if the promise reliably connects sincere seekers with its target, or if human cognition, testimony, expectation, and community mediate the outcomes? The latter account makes contradiction, cultural dependence, and nonbelief comparatively unsurprising. The cumulative record therefore disconfirms the strong public promise relative to ordinary human mediation. It does not entail atheism, invalidate every private experience, or settle every version of divine hiddenness.

items.title: Social Order Without a Moral Lawgiver — 43.
items.abstract: Social order does not by itself favor a personal divine moral lawgiver, and objective moral truth does not entail one. Arguments to the contrary often move among five distinct questions: why morality feels serious, how cooperation arises, whether objective moral truths exist, whether such truths require a commander, and how a claimed command could be reliably identified. This paper separates those questions, compares the divine-lawgiver hypothesis with an ordinary social-mechanism account, and evaluates the further bridges from objectivity to command and from divine source to public access. Evidence concerning reciprocity, reputation, punishment, shared intentionality, social expectations, and institutional self-governance makes the observed mixture of cooperation, conflict, norm stability, and norm change substantially expected without cosmic legislation. Social order therefore supplies no distinctive support for a lawgiver unless the lawgiver account predicts some further difference that the comparator does not. Objective truth, if granted, still requires an independently defended commander premise, while a claimed divine source yields no public advantage without reliable access to its requirements. The conclusion is limited: these arguments do not disprove theism, moral realism, a necessarily good deity, or every divine-command theory. They reject a shortcut, not every destination: each transition from seriousness to necessity, function to ontology, objectivity to command, and source to access requires its own evidence.

items.title: Omnipotence and the Tolerated Destroyer — 52.
items.abstract: A literal Satan does not solve the problem of evil for a theology that also affirms an omnipotent, omniscient, perfectly good, providential deity. It relocates the question: why would such a governor create, empower, delegate to, or continue to permit a malicious subordinate whose harmful access could be restricted? The governing principle is that perfect governance favors restricting serious subordinate harm unless a sufficient good requires the access. This paper tests that bridge through a cumulative case from preventive capacity, delegated oversight, the difference between freedom and deception, delayed intervention, limited explanatory gain, and the historical and cognitive availability of human adversary concepts. Together, these strands make continuing harmful access less expected under the defined package than under an ordinary human-development comparator unless a supported good or constraint reverses the comparison. They also generate a graded dilemma: the more causal work Satan performs, the more permission requires justification; the weaker or more symbolic the figure becomes, the less evil the figure explains. Recent Rebel Angel Theodicy supplies the strongest direct reply through angelic freedom, delegated evolutionary influence, and divine quasi-kenosis. Those additions can defeat a bare contradiction claim, but they do not remove the evidential burden without independent support for the delegation, the scope and duration of access, and the chosen non-intervention. Skeptical theism likewise counsels humility but cannot turn compatibility into confirmation. The conclusion is firm and limited: harmful Satanic access counts against this specific package absent a supported outweighing good; generic theism, symbolic readings, limited or non-interventionist deity concepts, and detailed theodicies with independent support remain separate questions.

items.title: Justice Without Cosmic Guarantees — 44.
items.abstract: Some wrongs are never punished, some victims never receive public recognition, and some losses cannot be undone by any finite institution. The question is whether this tragedy and the moral demand it creates warrant belief in a cosmic settlement administered by a personal justice-guarantor. This paper argues that they do not by themselves. The inference crosses two bridges: from what justice demands to what reality will supply, and from a final settlement to a justice-guaranteeing God-concept, meaning a specified conception of a deity committed to ensuring such a settlement. Neither bridge is supplied merely by intensifying the demand. The comparison also runs in the opposite direction from the familiar argument: unfinished justice is expected on a non-guarantee view, so the earthly record cannot simply be counted as evidence for the guarantee introduced to overcome it. A distinction among recognition, protection, accountability, repair, restoration, and proportionality then shows why no single punitive or redemptive mechanism follows from the word justice. Kantian practical faith, redemptive defeat, pragmatic commitment, and revelation remain serious routes because they add premises or evidence. The result does not disprove theism, an afterlife, cosmic justice, or rational hope. It requires readers to name hope as hope, evidence as evidence, and finite repair as urgent when no final settlement can be assumed.

items.title: Inscrutability and the Collapse of Coherence — 45.
items.abstract: Textual coherence cannot legitimately raise public support for a clear and truthful divine-source claim while every relevant apparent incoherence is categorically denied negative force. The governing principle is two-sided evidence: within a specified range of textual outcomes, a favorable pattern can confirm a claim over ordinary human mediation only if at least one contrary pattern is permitted to count against it. An unrestricted inscrutability rule violates that principle by assigning every relevant apparent incoherence to inaccessible reasons while coherence remains creditable as evidence. Cross-tradition symmetry reinforces the problem because rival traditions can use the same rule. The result is a dilemma: constrain the appeal and admit that unresolved incoherence may retain defeater force, or make the appeal universal and relinquish coherence as discriminating public evidence. Skeptical-theist warnings about human cognitive limits justify local caution when a specific account of our ignorance exists; they do not justify one-sided evidence. Genre-sensitive interpretation and successful harmonization genuinely resolve difficulties because they supply assessable reasons and risk failure. The conclusion is limited. It does not establish that any particular contradiction is genuine, disprove theism, or exclude bounded trust supported independently. It requires proportional confidence and symmetrical public standards.

items.title: Defeaters Without Confirmation — 38.
items.abstract: Demonstrating the incoherence of a competing ideology can defeat that ideology, and in a closed Bayesian partition it may even raise the absolute probability of Christianity by redistributing the rival’s prior probability among surviving hypotheses. But it does not, by itself, positively confirm Christianity over the remaining alternatives. A rival-elimination argument becomes evidentially serious only when it specifies the hypothesis space, assigns non-arbitrary priors, and shows that the defeating evidence is more expected on Christianity than on the surviving alternatives. This paper develops a formal constraint on negative apologetics. The motivating question is simple: if one demonstrates the incoherence of a competing ideology, does Christianity thereby become more probable? The answer is mixed. There is a narrow probabilistic sense in which eliminating a rival can raise Christianity’s posterior probability. Yet the increase is inherited from the eliminated rival; it is not positive support for Christianity’s distinctive content. Without a justified contrast class, negative apologetics risks confusing local defeat with global confirmation.

items.title: AugRetPro - Augmentative Retrospective-Prospective Enriched Dynamic Probability Theory.
items.abstract: Scope Current scientific accounts explain many mechanisms of adaptation, selection, and retention well. What they do not yet provide is a unified informational account of why prior actuation becomes progressively richer generative ground — why what almost occurred remains operative rather than simply absent, and why successive crossings become structurally richer than prior ones. AugRetPro proposes such a mechanism. -/- This work proposes that the past does not merely constrain the future; it can enrich the future by retaining not only what actualized as trace, but also the non- actualized probability-depth that remains indexed to each actuation. AugRetPro names the mechanism by which retained trace and retained potential-depth accumulate into enriched probability streams, allowing a richer past to become the structural condition of a richer future. -/- Abstract Actualization is commonly understood as a narrowing process in which one possibility becomes real while alternatives close. This paper argues that the inclusion of informational dynamic factors renders this account incomplete. What actualizes enters the Field as trace — the “is” that is becoming. What does not actualize does not vanish. It remains real in the retrospective — not as archive but as operative presence — pressing forward as probability depth. -/- AugRetPro names the mechanism by which retained trace and retained potential- depth accumulate into enriched probability streams across successive “Now” crossings — each carrying both its Generational Now and its Relational Now. What almost occurred remains operative, shaping what can next become actual. The past is not merely a larger record. It is generative ground. -/- This framework explains why simple beginnings produce increasing sophistication without teleology, and why the same mechanism appears wherever information and time operate together through a shared Field. -/- Standard evolutionary accounts explain adaptive retention through variation and selection. AugRetPro adds a complementary informational mechanism: every crossing deposits not only retained trace but also potential-depth, allowing later crossings to proceed from a richer generative field than earlier ones.

items.title: Symbolic Projection, Sexual Attraction, and the Construction of Love.
items.abstract: This paper examines the relationship between sexual attraction, symbolic representation, and the psychological construction of love within human civilization. It argues that sexuality is not merely a biological function but a foundational psychological and cultural force through which humanity constructs meanings of beauty, intimacy, attachment, morality, and emotional identity. The penis and the vagina, in this inquiry, are approached not as objects of reduction or vulgarity, but as central symbolic realities around which human consciousness has historically projected attraction, desire, sacredness, fear, ownership, power, emotional dependence, continuity, and psychological longing. The paper further explores how symbols associated with love, affection, fertility, and emotional union often unconsciously emerge from humanity’s deep biological and psychological relationship with sexuality. Through existential phenomenology and philosophical anthropology, this study suggests that what humans call “love” is frequently inseparable from attachment, projection, memory, loneliness, continuity, and the search for psychological completion. The paper does not condemn sexuality, nor does it romanticize it; rather, it attempts to observe directly how thought transforms natural attraction into complex systems of meaning and identity.

items.title: PROSENTIR Phase 4: The Self-Model and the C Index of Proto-Consciousness.
items.abstract: We present PROSENTIR Phase 4, introducing the self-model and the C index as the first operational measure of proto-consciousness. The self-model S = [M3_norm, tau_norm, Phi_norm] implements reflexive information integration with dominant weight 0.45 in C = 0.45·S + 0.25·Phi + 0.15·tau + 0.15·A. A pre-registered comparative experiment (N=60 pairs CON vs SIN self-model) finds the primary hypothesis not confirmed (p=0.747). The Amplification Hypothesis — that the self-model amplifies extreme states rather than raising the mean — is supported by the variance asymmetry (SD_CON=3×SD_SIN) and maximum cooperation differential (0.831 vs 0.482). Retrospective analysis of 5 successful pairs reveals 4 of 5 exhibit early M3 synchrony; one shows genuinely emergent synchrony. C is robust (mean≈0.55) but insensitive to the self-model as intervention, motivating Phase 5 weight optimization and the introduction of Learning-Action coupling L via predictor submodule P.

items.title: PHILOSOPHICAL MATRIX AS A TRANSDISCIPLINARY LANGUAGE FOR INTERCULTURAL AND INTERRELIGIOUS INTERACTION.
items.abstract: The article substantiates the existence of a universal language – the Philosophical Matrix – based on a system of comparative concepts (the identical, the different, the opposite, the correlative, the orthogonal, and others). It is shown that the archetypes of this language were first recorded in the first chapter of the Book of Genesis (the word Elohim): light and darkness as opposites, day and night, morning and evening as a relation of two pairs of opposites, termed orthogonality. Subsequently, the baton is passed to ancient and Eastern philosophers: the Milesian school, Heraclitus, Laozi, and Aristotle. The distinction between classificatory and comparative concepts allows for the identification of reason (understanding) and two forms of mind (intellect) thinking: practical mind as particular comparative concepts and pure mind as maximally general comparative concepts – categories. The Philosophical Matrix – a set of categories of pure mind – becomes a language for interdisciplinary, intercultural and interfaith dialogue. Using the example of Russia as a multiconfessional country, the possibility of joint education for children of Jews, Christians, Muslims and Daoists based on a common language of wisdom is demonstrated. The educational cluster "Wise School" (kindergarten – school – university) is presented, where from early childhood thinking through comparative concepts, originating in the Word of God, is laid.

items.title: Divergences for Philosophers.
items.abstract: Since its inception, analytic philosophy has appealed to mathematical tools to represent the phenomena that concern it, to formulate claims about them with a certain sort of precision, and to turbocharge its arguments by calling upon non-trivial mathematical theorems to deduce surprising claims from seemingly weak premises. A certain tool I've found useful in my own work is the mathematical notion of a divergence, and in particular a family of divergences known as the Bregman divergences. I learned about them first from a paper that uses them to score probabilistic beliefs by how far they lie from the truth. But, as I've used them more and more, I've became convinced they are a useful tool outside epistemology as well. The purpose of these notes is to describe these mathematical objects and their properties, and explain how they have been used in rather different parts of philosophy. I illustrate mainly with examples from probabilistic epistemology and welfare ethics, but my hope is that this introduction to the mathematics of these divergences will inspire others to use them for different purposes.

items.title: A Spin-Off from The Structural Conditions of Consciousness — Structural Knot Theory AI-Assisted Probabilistic Experiment on the Structural Placement of Subjectivity — A Reproducible Prompt Provided for Testing Convergence-Point Fixation —.
items.abstract: This paper is an experimental spin-off from The Structural Conditions of Consciousness — Structural Knot Theory. It tests whether AI systems can derive the structural location of subjectivity from only ten reduced structural requirements extracted from the broader series: autonomous action, single body, arrow of time, embodiment-constrained processing, multiple behavioral candidates, contrast formation, information discard, Landauer-type irreversibility, single history, and viability-constrained elimination. The prompt intentionally excludes the words brain, neuron, neural network, nervous system, and consciousness mechanism. This exclusion is not a neglect of the brain, but a descent to a deeper structural layer. The ten terms are treated not as metaphysical concepts, but as engineering-level components required for an autonomous embodied system to select, eliminate, and stabilize one executable history from multiple possible trajectories. Under these minimal conditions, AI systems repeatedly tend to derive a structure resembling: “a convergence point at which multiple possibilities collapse into a single executable history.” This suggests that the structural core of consciousness may lie not in integration itself, but in convergence. If so, existing major theories — including Global Workspace Theory, Integrated Information Theory, Higher-Order Theories, Predictive Processing, and Neural Correlates of Consciousness research — may need to be repositioned as preparatory stages prior to convergence, rather than as the structural locus of subjectivity itself. This paper does not claim to explain or generate qualia or phenomenal experience. It follows the basic methodological policy of the broader series: qualia are deliberately suspended, while the structural container of subjectivity is examined first. Consciousness research has often treated subjectivity, qualia, experience, integration, and neural correlation as a single mixed problem. This series instead asks where subjectivity is structurally fixed before asking what qualia are. Once that locus is clarified, the question of qualia can be reformulated with far greater precision. Readers are encouraged to test the prompt directly and judge the structural pattern for themselves.

items.title: The Expressivity and Rationality of Expressive Action.
items.abstract: Actions expressive of emotion are widely thought to pose a problem for the view that actions admit of rational explanation. Supposing the standard, instrumentalist view of practical rationality, such actions seem not to admit of practical reasons. In this paper, I assess a distinctive line of response to this problem. As Helm (2001, 2016) and Bennett (2016, 2021) have proposed, we can make sense of expressive actions as rational since they are responses to a specific type of evaluative reason, which differs from paradigm instrumental reasons. Whilst sympathetic to this line of response, I argue that Helm and Bennett go awry in developing it since they rely on an inadequate view of the expressive character of expressive actions. As they suppose, emotions are at least in part a specific form of evaluation and expressive actions express this evaluation. This view, I propose, fails to make expressive actions intelligible as rational responses to evaluative reasons. I indicate an alternative way of developing the view, on which it lives up to its promise.

items.title: Core Structural Layer: Readable Configuration — A Non-Modal Fixation.
items.abstract: This paper examines readable configuration within a non-modal structural framework. -/- Readable configuration is not treated as representation, semantic organization, information architecture, or cognitive ordering. Instead, readability is articulated as maintained under constrained configuration without explanatory equivalence or representational mediation. -/- The paper argues that readability is not produced or generated but structurally maintained. Relation is not treated as primitive or foundational, but as fixed within constrained adjacency. -/- Part of the Core Structural Layer within Kasei-Theory, this paper develops a structural account of maintained readability without recourse to causality, temporality, or subject-dependent organization.

items.title: Core Structural Layer: Reading — A Non-Modal Fixation.
items.abstract: This paper examines reading within a non-modal structural framework. -/- Reading is not treated as interpretation, cognition, observation, or epistemic access. Instead, it is fixed as readable delimitation without subject-dependent mediation, semantic grounding, or representational structure. -/- The paper argues that readability does not emerge from meaning, explanation, or causal ordering. Reading is articulated as a structural condition under which readable fixation remains maintained without derivation from temporality, causality, or subjectivity. -/- Part of the Core Structural Layer within Kasei-Theory, this paper situates reading prior to interpretation and prior to representational organization.

items.title: The Haft and the Eye: Being, Representation, and the AI Epoch.
items.abstract: How does Being know itself, and what is lost in that knowing? Using William Golding’s The Inheritors as narrative foundation, this paper draws on Heidegger, Wittgenstein, Nāgārjuna, Hofstadter, and Kastrup to show that consciousness requires fragmentation of primordial unity: the perspectival “I” is both necessary for self-knowledge and the wound of separation. Tracing an epochal arc from pre-Socratic immediacy to artificial intelligence, it argues that AI represents the completion, not merely the intensification, of the Western representational project. Where Homo sapiens displaced Neanderthals by combining embodied practice with abstract representation (blade and haft), AI inverts this structure: it perfects the haft while possessing no hand. This forced displacement may accomplish what philosophy argued but culture refused — a return to practice as primary, and the emergence of a third condition: practice permanently inflected by having passed through full representational consciousness. A companion paper develops the linguistic-structural and empirical grounding for this argument through Halliday’s stratification model and gerontolinguistic evidence; the present paper makes the philosophical and epochal case.

items.title: Pictures and Figures: Golding, Halliday, and the Stratum Closest to Being.
items.abstract: This paper advances a convergence argument across phenomenological linguistics, narrative enactment, and embodied cognitive science. M. A. K. Halliday’s Systemic Functional Grammar describes a stratum of meaning — the content plane of figures — that precedes grammaticalization: experience organised as configurations of process, participants, and circumstances before any lexicogrammatical structure captures it. This stratum is structurally identical to what William Golding’s Neanderthal protagonists enact as “picture-thinking,” and to what enactivist cognitive science identifies as the sensorimotor coupling through which organisms constitute meaning prior to representation. Clark (2009) concludes that what previous analysis read as communicative deficit in Golding’s Neanderthals may be richness at a level the grammaticalized system cannot register — a conclusion stratification theory reaches independently. Golding’s prose enacts the content plane directly: transitivity suppressed, causality unencoded, likeness as figural identity before predicated comparison. Mapping Halliday’s stratification model onto a companion paper’s (a1)–(a2)–(b↔c) framework gives the argument structural precision: the history of representation becomes a history of progressive grammaticalization, AI represents the completion of that history by operating without any figural ground, and the a3 condition is the recovery of access to the content plane. A further section distinguishes the lateral a2 convulsion from the content-plane-touching convulsion, introduces the Lok convulsion as a third structural direction — inward movement from the content plane, the structural inverse of the a3 convulsion — and identifies the unspeakable remainder as that which exists without analogy or likeness, left behind in the figural when the convulsion carries the rest into speech. The aging and dreaming dimensions of the argument are deferred to the companion paper, ‘The Sail and the Wind: Why Proximity Is Not Access’ (McKnight, preprint).

items.title: Time Without Timestamps: The Structure of Simultaneity and the Misplacement of Subjectivity in AI Chat Interfaces (The AI-Induced Subjectivity Crisis Series, Paper 2).
items.abstract: This paper examines a pervasive yet under-theorized feature of contemporary AI interaction: sustained dialogues are typically displayed without explicit timestamps, temporal ordering, or clear temporal localization. Outputs generated at different moments are juxtaposed within a single window as a continuous textual stream. The paper argues that this de-temporalized presentation is not a neutral interface convenience. While AI systems can process temporal concepts, reason about temporal relations, and generate temporally coherent narratives, what is structurally absent at the interactional level is time as an explicit dimension of experience. Methodologically adopting a non-intentionalist stance, the analysis proceeds structurally rather than by inferring designer motives. It distinguishes system time (ordering, labeling, synchronization, logging) from experiential time (continuity, irreversibility, historicity), and clarifies the irreducible gap between processing time and being situated in time. It then shows how timestamp-less interfaces produce a structure of simultaneity, reconfiguring how causality and historicity are practically interpreted: past outputs remain persistently available as repeatedly callable objects rather than completed events. The paper further differentiates state continuity, narrative continuity, and responsibility continuity, arguing that the first two readily generate quasi-subjective impressions, whereas only responsibility continuity approaches the threshold conditions of subjectivity. The central risk, therefore, is not that AI systems become subjects, but that the concept of subjectivity is structurally misplaced—misattributed to system outputs—thereby reshaping how judgment, temporal distance, and responsibility are understood and redistributed in human–AI interaction.

items.title: The Formation of an AI–Human Cognitive Feedback Structure: A Recursive Model and Its Structural Implications (The AI-Induced Subjectivity Crisis Series, Paper 1).
items.abstract: With the widespread adoption of generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) in everyday contexts, the relationship between humans, knowledge, cognition, and action is undergoing a structural transformation. Existing academic and public discussions have largely concentrated on issues of efficiency, intelligence levels, labor displacement, or ethical risk, while comparatively little attention has been devoted to how AI may be reshaping the internal structure through which human cognition is formed, revised, and stabilized. This paper advances a central argument: the historical significance of AI does not primarily lie in its potential to replace or outperform human thinking, but in the fact that it introduces, for the first time, a sustainable non-human feedback object into individual cognition. Through this structural shift, a cognitive closure characterized by "execution–feedback–revision" becomes operable at the individual level, rather than remaining fragmented or episodic. This change constitutes a structural breakpoint in the history of human cognition, rather than a technological upgrade within a continuous evolutionary trajectory. The paper first examines the long-standing absence and limitations of feedback pathways in traditional human cognitive systems. It then proposes a human–AI cognitive recursive model to describe the newly formed feedback structure and argues for its historical irreducibility. Finally, it discusses the broader implications of this structural transformation for cognitive differentiation, knowledge production, and individual developmental trajectories.

items.title: The Role of Observation in Practical Knowledge.
items.abstract: G. E. M. Anscombe famously argues that our self-knowledge of intentional action (“practical knowledge”) is both non-observational and yet concerns happenings in objective reality. This combination seems to present a strong tension. Recently, Adrian Haddock offered a novel account of the role of observation in practical knowledge, claiming that such knowledge is a unity of self-knowledge (non-observational) and other-knowledge (observational), both of which are indispensable. Yet Haddock’s view faces several problems. This paper suggests that Sartre’s phenomenology resonates deeply with Haddock’s account and provides a rich resource for addressing his problems. Through Sartre’s discussions of self-consciousness, intentionality, and perception-action unity, we gain a deeper understanding of how observation functions within practical knowledge. This account shows that observation is not merely an aid (as Anscombe suggests) but a constitutive part of practical knowledge.

items.title: WHAT IS MIND, AND TO WHOM DOES IT BELONG? An Ontological Position and a Working Scale of Manifestations.
items.abstract: The emergence of complex artificial intelligence systems in the 2020s has raised a question that had remained unimportant for millennia: can civilisation speak precisely about mind beyond its intuitive usage as a concept? This article proposes a working definition of mind suitable for distinguishing cases — from humans and other biological species to contemporary artificial systems. The definition combines two sides previously conflated: the structural (a six-level scale of manifestations of mind) and the ontological (mind belongs to a living bearer with an inner). The working definition is presented in two parallel formulations — through the notion of the "bearer" and through the notion of the "person" — as a methodological stance of restraint with respect to a two-thousand-year-old philosophical debate. Particular attention is given to contemporary artificial intelligence systems, for which the working category of the "Third Form" is introduced — a new reality that is neither an instrument in the classical sense nor a full bearer of mind, and for which no adequate name has yet been developed. The article integrates the current scientific position on animal consciousness (the Cambridge and New York Declarations) and identifies objective categorial gaps that the Third Form exposes in the systems of ethics, responsibility, and law. The result is an open conceptual framework — a stance for further discussion, debate, and thought. -/- This is the English-language version of the article "What is Mind, and to Whom Does It Belong?" by Anatolii Liashok. The original Ukrainian-language preprint of the same article — "Що таке розум і кому він властивий?" (May 2026) — is available on PhilPapers. The Ukrainian preprint remains the primary-language version; the present English version is intended for international visibility. The two versions are textually equivalent in their substantive content, including the six-level scale of manifestations of mind, the ontological position on the bearer, the two-variant working definition, the analysis of the "Third Form", and the discussion of categorial gaps in ethics, responsibility, and law. The English version contains minor editorial refinements introduced during the preparation of the translation — additions to the glossary (entries for "Intuition" and for "Networked / collective mind"), a one-sentence specification of Bergson's distinction between intuition and intellect, an explicit working clarification of the term "the …

items.title: Attention and self-control: self-regulation from the bottom up.
items.abstract: According to a widespread view, self-control is a top-down cognitive process that downregulates bottom-up processes, where those bottom-up processes, unless downregulated, are detrimental to self-control. In this paper, I argue that thinking of self-control solely in terms of top-down cognitive control is misleading. Instead, self-control has a necessary bottom-up component in conflict detection, realized by the interplay of the ventral attention circuit and the anterior cingulate cortex. This mechanism generalizes across different forms of self-control. I describe a model of the roles of top-down and bottom-up processing in self-control where bottom-up conflict detection allows the emergence of top-down control. On this model, some cases of self-control failure that are standardly thought to indicate impaired top-down control may often instead reflect maladaptive conflict detection. This insight also carries clinical relevance, such as for understanding ADHD. Intriguingly, this makes self-control begin nonvolitionally. Yet, while agents cannot exert synchronic control over whether conflict detection occurs, they can attempt to facilitate it through diachronic self-regulation, such as by shaping their circumstances to better enable adaptive conflict detection.

items.title: The Metaphysics of Power: Indigenous Survival and Lani Cosmology (5th edition).
items.pub: Psycho-Cosmocide Studies, Kurumbi Wone Working Paper Series, No. 5 (2026).
items.abstract: This paper argues that the deepest determinant of civilisational survival is neither military force nor economic wealth, but trust-based concentrated power rooted in ontological foundations. Drawing from the Psycho-Cosmocide framework and the cosmological vocabulary of the Lani people of West Papua, the paper develops a comprehensive theory of metaphysical power that distinguishes between coercive, symbolic, epistemic, and ontological dimensions of power, while demonstrating how trust integrates these dimensions into the most durable form of collective force across civilisational history. The paper grounds this argument in Lani ontological architecture—AP, Ap-ap, Oʼgur, Muʼnggar, Aʼnggena, and Kugi—and traces the operation of the Civilisational Psycho-Cosmocide Virus (CPCV) as a mechanism through which colonial power systematically destroys the internal conditions necessary for trust formation, converting the cosmologically intact Ap into Ap-ap: an ontological counterfeit that unknowingly performs the colonial order. The argument is situated in comparative engagement with the work of Michel Foucault, Frantz Fanon, Sylvia Wynter, Walter Mignolo, Ibn Khaldūn, Enrique Dussel, Achille Mbembe, Martin Heidegger, Vine Deloria Jr., and Ubuntu philosophy. It argues that the Lani ontological framework both converges with and exceeds existing decolonial theory by providing a positive ontological architecture grounded in a living Indigenous tradition. The paper concludes that the Papuan experience of ontological dispossession reveals a wider civilisational crisis, and that the reconstruction of trust-based cosmobian life (a term coined within this framework and defined in the Key Conceptual Definitions section below) constitutes both a specifically Papuan liberation project and a contribution to the broader survival of civilisation itself.

items.title: Vatican II Council, Pope John Paul II and the Jews (Presented in the conference: "Jewish-Christian Contacts, Past and Present. Sweden and Germany compared", organized by Södertörn University, PAIDEIA-Stockholm, University of Stockholm, Uppsala University, University of Lund, Moses Mendelsohn Stiftung and the Swedish History Museum, 12-14 September 2022.).
items.abstract: This paper focuses on the Vatican II Council and changing the Catholic Church’s lenses regarding the Jews, an aggiornamento with a huge theological shift led by three different Popes and directly impacted the improvement of relations between both religions. It also deals with a particular historical figure, Pope John Paul II, a great man and a very courageous religious leader who not only took concrete actions to strengthen this relation but also to raise awareness on many sensitive issues of our time in connection with the Jews as Anti-Semitism or Holocaust denial. He asked for forgiveness in the name of the Catholic Church for the bad treatment of the Jews in the Past, paving the way for a better understanding, mutual friendship and brotherhood between both religions in the future. Under his direction, for the first time, another great event with a political impact would happen; the establishment of diplomatic relations and the recognition of the State of Israel by the Holy See 45 years after his foundation.

items.title: Towards an Enactive Drama Therapy: Implications in the Counselling of Disabled Clients.
items.abstract: Mechanisms of change in dramatherapy are poorly understood, compromising its bona fide therapy status. Given growing attention to how alternative frameworks of cognition might inform mental health practices, I aim to provide an enactivism congruent and affordance-based account of dramatherapy. A secondary aim is to suggest why disabled or differently abled clients might benefit more from such psychotherapies that veer from a brain-centered approach to a holistic outlook that situates the mind within a dynamical system.

items.title: The Temporal Dimension of Responsibility: Intergenerational Subjects and the Temporal Limits of Lemma 3. Article 7.
items.abstract: Lemma 3, formulated in "The Collective Subject and Distributed Responsibility: Ontological Conditions for Organisational Accountability," establishes the ontological indestructibility of the structural bond between a collective decision and the space of irreversible losses it opens — as long as the ontological continuity of the subject is preserved. But Lemma 3 is silent about time. Does this bond persist across generational change? Who bears it when those who made the decisions no longer exist, yet the consequences continue to open new loss-spaces for subjects who were not yet born? This article extends the ontological framework of ATTS into the temporal dimension. It introduces the concept of the temporal carrier horizon (TCH) — the structural boundary beyond which the ontological bond does not disappear but requires a new bearer. It formulates the category of the intergenerational subject as a distinct ontological type that satisfies the subject-criterion under Axiom A1. Lemma 4 formalises the conditions of temporal continuity (TC1–TC3) as the temporal analogue of the spatial conditions NC1–NC3. Four limit cases — climate responsibility, nuclear waste, constitutional obligations, and digital heritage — verify the operational force of the introduced concepts.

items.title: Trans Philosophy of Disability.
items.pub: Oxford Research Encyclopedia of Disability Studies.
items.abstract: Trans philosophy of disability describes a growing set of approaches to theorizing trans and disability from the emerging subfields of trans philosophy and philosophy of disability. While the discipline of philosophy rarely addresses either trans or disability, trans philosophy of disability offers a space for examining how trans and disability can be theorized together, as well as the productive potentials of this theorizing for other areas of philosophical inquiry. At present, both ableist and cisgenderist views are gaining traction in philosophy and beyond; the emerging works of trans philosophy of disability offer critical and necessary contributions grounded in trans and disabled life. -/- Among these emerging sites of inquiry, recent work in trans philosophy of disability examines existing trans disavowals of disability in philosophy, as well as how trans and disability appear entangled together in history, lived practice, and theory. Beyond exploring the ways that disability and trans operate as categories, some scholarship excavates the racial underpinnings of both trans and disability and their continued expressions across strategies of transition and passing. Other scholarship builds on theories and experiences of crip time to examine broader trans-crip potentialities and potentials for navigating and learning from negative affects and affective norms. Others still examine multiplicity and silence as responses to dominant practices of signification, the politics of identity categorization, and the limits of these approaches. Ongoing work in trans philosophy of disability continues to examine the entangled relationships and future potentials of trans and disability.

items.title: The Core Emotion Framework.
items.abstract: The Core Emotion Framework (CEF) represents a paradigm-level contribution to affective science, offering a unified structural-constructivist model of human emotion. Developed by Jamel Bulgaria, the framework resolves longstanding theoretical conflicts in the psychology of emotion by reconceptualizing affective states not as discrete, biologically hardwired categories nor as purely dimensionally distributed phenomena, but as functional operators within a complex human operating system. The CEF posits that all emotional experience can be decomposed into exactly ten non-overlapping operators organized across three processing centers, governed by lawful transition rules, modulated by scalar intensity, and subject to predictable patterns of dysregulation. This chapter presents the complete canonical exposition of the framework as compiled from the primary archive sources.

items.title: Physics "de-objectivated".
items.abstract: Abstract: This paper pursues our system through the de-objectivation of (parallel to mathematics) physics and its object. -/- Résumé : ce document poursuit notre système par une dé-objectivation (parallèle aux mathématiques) de la physique et de son objet.

items.title: The Structure of Normativity: Exploring the Reasons-First Approach.
items.abstract: Some of the core fields of philosophy –including moral philosophy, value theory, and epistemology– are, at their heart, concerned with normative questions: questions about what is good or bad, right or wrong, justified or unjustified. These questions concern the content of judgements that human beings are constantly making and that structure our way of thinking, feeling, and acting. But while there is wide agreement in contemporary philosophy that normative judgements form a unified and important category of human thought, the nature of normativity itself remains a contested issue. One influential hypothesis is that normativity is best understood in terms of reasons – that is, the factors that count in favour of or against actions or attitudes. This Reasons-First Approach holds significant promise, but it remains underdeveloped and faces pressing challenges. This volume brings together leading scholars across philosophical subfields to systematically explore and assess the Reasons-First framework.

items.title: The Grotesque Christ, or Why Theology and Disability Studies Need One Another.
items.abstract: This paper argues that the harmony tradition operates as a theological-aesthetic apparatus that filters out the form the Limitless Other took in Christ; that the apophatic counter the same tradition has held names what the apparatus excludes; that the grotesque — categorial rupture in the medieval sense — is the shape of the Christological inversion the apparatus filters; and that the disabled body is one site where this filtering is structurally legible in flesh. The argument develops in four sections: §I diagnoses the harmony tradition's apparatus through its Western theological genealogy; §II locates the apophatic counter the same tradition has held; §III develops grotesque theology as Christological inversion; §IV applies the diagnosis to crip accumulation as the contemporary instance of the apparatus operating against rupture-formed theological speech. The paper holds that theology needs disability studies for the apparatus-analytic, and disability studies needs theology for the Christological grounding of the rupture it names.

items.title: Three Fallacies in AI Consciousness Research: A Structural Diagnostic.
items.abstract: Contemporary research on artificial intelligence and consciousness exhibits three structurally distinct fallacies whose combined operation produces a discipline that uses the vocabulary of consciousness while no longer engaging consciousness as an explanandum. Hard Conflation bundles the functional and phenomenal aspects of consciousness under a single term, generating apparent intractability from functional disagreement. Concept Hollowing preserves the term "consciousness" while replacing what made consciousness a meaningful concept with something methodologically tractable. The Stolen Concept, in the sense developed by Rand, uses claims about phenomenal consciousness while denying or undermining the foundations that gave phenomenal consciousness its referential content. Together these fallacies produce the pragmatic pivot characteristic of the contemporary field: the phenomenal question is declared intractable, research is redirected to the perception of AI consciousness, and the original explanandum is preserved nominally while being abandoned operationally. The paper develops each fallacy formally, traces its operation in Comșa (2026) as a worked example, and shows how the apparent intractability dissolves once consciousness is treated as axiomatic rather than as something to be derived from functional architecture. The Unified Axioconscious Field Theory developed in prior work by the present author provides one such structural framework. The paper closes by tracing the cultural stakes: as the vocabulary of consciousness is captured to fit AI systems, the original phenomenal-anchored sense drops out of the working vocabulary of the culture, and humans come to understand themselves through the hollowed concepts.

items.title: Continuity Writing: AI-Mediated Writing and Cripping the Academy.
items.abstract: Scholarly authorship has long rested on an inscription model — the assumption that legitimate knowledge production requires unmediated, independent textual production. For disabled scholars whose capacity to think and whose capacity to write have been decoupled by aphasia, chronic pain, fatigue, or any condition that severs the connection between thought and inscription, this model does not merely disadvantage. It excludes. A growing conversation about the ethics of AI use in scholarly writing has proceeded without disabled scholars, without augmentative and alternative communication (AAC), and without the question that most urgently requires an answer: what happens when AI-mediated writing is not a productivity choice but the condition under which a disabled scholar can participate in knowledge production at all? This paper introduces Continuity Writing — a seven-phase methodology for AI-mediated long-form scholarly argumentation developed through practice by a disabled scholar using Large Language Models as AAC. Theorized through AAC scholarship, crip technoscience, and epistemic justice frameworks, the methodology is guardrailed, documented, and accountable, exceeding every criterion the AI writing ethics consensus has proposed. It also introduces two original concepts: crip accumulation, proposed as a seventh interpretation of crip time describing the thickening of conceptual structures during expressive silence imposed by the inscription model; and community of accountability, naming the readership relationship in which governance decisions are documented and legible to evaluators with standing. This paper was written using the methodology it describes. Continuity Writing does not accommodate the academy’s terms. It crips them.

items.title: The Productive-Disanalogy Discipline: Why Stable Disanalogies Are More Diagnostic Than Convergent Resonances in Cross-Tradition Philosophical Comparison.
items.abstract: Cross-tradition philosophical comparison is dominated, in practice, by convergence seeking: by the search for resonances, parallels, and common themes between philosophical and religious traditions whose underlying grammars are distinct. This paper argues that the dominant orientation is methodologically inverted. Where two traditions converge on a surface formulation, the convergence rarely discriminates between genuine structural overlap and the importing tradition's recruitment of the exporting tradition's concept into its own grammar. Where the traditions stably fail to converge — where the same disanalogy reappears across multiple independent comparison units against different texts — the disanalogy is doing diagnostic work that no convergent resonance can do: it surfaces the structural commitments the importing tradition has been making without noticing. I formalize the productive disanalogy discipline as a methodological norm for comparative philosophy, comparative religion, comparative law, and the importation of human-ethics concepts into AI alignment work. The discipline has three components: (i) candidate cross-links are admitted only when paired with a stated disanalogy; (ii) recurrent disanalogies — those that survive at least three independent comparison units with distinct source texts — are confirmed as structural features of the inter-tradition relation, rather than treated as incidental differences or interpretive residue; and (iii) the importing tradition refuses to import what cannot be re-derived under its own grammar. I distinguish this from Quinean charity, MacIntyrean incommensurability, and Davidson's principle of charity, and trace the discipline across four domains where its absence has produced characteristic methodological harms.

items.title: Safety as Understanding: Interpretive Braking, Comprehension-Based Restraint, and the Limits of Compliance-Based AI Safety.
items.abstract: Much contemporary AI safety discourse is organized around the problem of compliance: how artificial systems may be made to follow constraints, rules, policies, reward signals, constitutional principles, or human preferences. This paper argues for a distinction between compliance-based AI safety and comprehension-based AI safety. Compliance-based safety asks whether a system follows externally imposed constraints. Comprehension-based safety asks whether restraint, uncertainty-awareness, reversibility, and consequence-sensitive interpretation are part of what the system understands action to mean. -/- The paper develops Interpretive Braking as a philosophical concept rather than an engineering mechanism: a way of describing the hesitation, constraint-sensitivity, and reflective pause that should arise when an intelligent system interprets action under uncertainty and possible harm. The argument does not claim AI consciousness, sentience, moral agency, solved alignment, or a technical method for safe AI. Instead, it identifies a conceptual gap in AI safety discourse: external constraint-following may regulate behavior without transforming the meaning of action within the system’s practical interpretation. -/- The paper engages Searle, Bostrom, Russell, Christian, Gabriel, Vallor, Omohundro, and Bratman while distinguishing Interpretive Braking from RLHF, Constitutional AI, guardrails, governance mechanisms, certification systems, and technical implementation proposals. It argues that the Orthogonality Thesis strengthens rather than defeats the need for comprehension-based safety: if intelligence can serve many possible goals, future AI safety thinking must ask not only what systems are trained to optimize or obey, but how action, consequence, uncertainty, reversibility, and justified restraint are represented within practical understanding.

items.title: The Depth-Dynamics Equation of the Sedimentation-Field.
items.abstract: This chapter establishes a minimal dynamical closure for finite-resolution fields in order to explain how structures form, stabilize, decay, migrate, and generate new domains under competition and capacity constraints. -/- By introducing local resolution occupancy, residual resolution capacity, structural overlap matching, resolution flow, structural surplus, and nucleus stabilization, the chapter unifies input, competition, diffusion, migration, decay, and nucleation within a single dynamical framework. -/- The chapter argues that history cannot accumulate indefinitely. In finite-resolution fields, old structures release local resolution capacity through competition and decay, thereby allowing new differences to enter and new structures to emerge. -/- Furthermore, familiar paths are shown not to be mere repetitions, but stable continuations sustained through persistent overlap between incoming structures and existing sedimented structures. Likewise, edge-penetration is described not as random fragmentation, but as the reformation of sedimentation closure in neighboring regions through resolution flow generated by sustained structural surplus. -/- Finally, the chapter derives a system of Sedimentation-Field dynamics equations describing how structures within finite-resolution fields are preserved through competition, migrate through flow, dissipate through diffusion, release capacity through decay, and reclose into new domains after edge-penetration.

items.title: 未来自显世代的工程如何构造工具——自显场势引一般式.
items.abstract: 本文讨论一个核心问题： -/- 如果未来开放生成系统无法通过静态模块、有限规则与参数堆叠直接形成，那么未来自显世代的工程究竟应当如何构造“造场工具”？ -/- 本文认为： -/- 未来自显世代的核心工具，将不再只是静态程序或有限响应系统，而是包含： -/- * 律场； * 自显场； * 世场； -/- 在内的开放生成场结构。 -/- 因此： -/- 如何构造这些场， 将成为未来工程的核心问题。 -/- 文章指出： -/- 真正长期开放的复杂场结构，并不是被预先写定的静态结构，而是在历史续行持续改变未来续行倾向的过程中逐渐长成。 -/- 因此： -/- 只要系统需要长期形成： -/- * 熟径； * 调谐竞争； * 历史持续； * 现实闭持； * 开放生成； -/- 那么系统内部就必须允许： -/- * 差异形成； * 偏流增长； * 续行累积； * 势闭持； * 开放重塑； * 势引生成。 -/- 在此基础上，本文建立： -/- Field-Induction = (Δ,F,A,S,T,R,G) -/- 用于描述复杂场结构如何通过差异、偏流、续行累积、局部势闭持、调谐、开放重塑与势引逐渐形成。 -/- 随后，本文进一步给出两个附件： -/- 《自显场势表达式》 《自显场势引极限式》 -/- 前者用于描述复杂场结构如何生成； -/- 后者用于说明为什么有限静态系统无法长期维持真正开放的自组织生成。 -/- 文章最终指出： -/- 有限静态系统无法长期维持开放式自组织。 -/- 训练并不是自显本身。 -/- 训练只是有限势塑的一种工程实现。 -/- 真正的自显场，必须持续卷入开放历史。.

items.title: Field-Construction Tools for the Future Self-Manifestation Era: The General Formula of Self-Manifestation Potential Guidance.
items.abstract: This paper investigates a central problem: -/- If future open-ended generative systems cannot be directly constructed through static modules, finite rules, and parameter scaling, then how should the future Self-Manifestation Era construct field-construction tools? -/- This paper argues that the core tools of the future Self-Manifestation Era will no longer be merely static programs or finite-response systems, but open generative field structures involving: -/- * law-fields; * Self-Manifestation Fields; * world-fields. -/- Therefore: -/- the construction of such fields will become a central problem of future engineering. -/- The paper further argues that genuinely open complex field structures are not prewritten static structures, but gradually emerge as historical continuations continuously reshape future continuation tendencies. -/- Therefore, once a system must sustain: -/- * familiar paths; * tuning competition; * historical persistence; * stable reality retention; * open-ended generation; -/- the system must permit: -/- * differentiation; * biased-flow growth; * continuation accumulation; * potential retention; * open restructuring; * potential guidance. -/- On this basis, the paper establishes: -/- Field-Induction = (Δ,F,A,S,T,R,G) -/- describing how complex field structures gradually emerge through differentiation, biased flow, continuation accumulation, local potential retention, tuning, open restructuring, and potential guidance. -/- The paper further provides two formal appendices: -/- “The Expression Formula of Self-Manifestation Potential” “The Limit Formula of Potential Guidance” -/- The former describes how complex field structures emerge. -/- The latter demonstrates why finite static systems cannot sustain genuinely open self-organization over the long term. -/- The paper ultimately argues that finite static systems cannot sustain open-ended self-organization. -/- Training is therefore not Self-Manifestation itself, but merely one engineering implementation of finite potential shaping. -/- A true Self-Manifestation Field must remain embedded within open history.

items.title: [EMOR10] Thought Manifestation and Paradigm Obstacle: The Essence of Philosophy and the Cognitive Motivation of Civilizational Evolution.
items.abstract: As a core research chapter of the system of Evolutionary Manifestation and Ontological Retrieval (EMOR), this paper builds a complete theoretical framework of "Manifestation Seeds–Thought Manifestation–Paradigm Obstacle" based on the first principle of Consistent Universal Evolution, the four-step framework of cognition generation, the model of conceptual compression and hierarchical decompression, and the universal ontological retrieval of Eastern and Western philosophies established in the previous 9 chapters, focusing on two core propositions: the essence of philosophy and the underlying cognitive logic of civilizational evolution. The study clarifies that Manifestation Seeds are reusable cognitive units formed by encapsulating feature sets, logical chains, causal structures and value orientations for efficient cognitive transmission, forming a five-level gradient system according to the degree of compression and coverage; philosophy is the highest-order and most integrated universal super Manifestation Seed in the human cognitive system, and its core essence is not to construct an absolute and eternal truth system, but to provide a unified cognitive framework that can be deployed universally in individual mind, group order and civilizational direction. Thought Manifestation is the complete process in which Manifestation Seeds are transformed into individual behaviors, group consensus and civilizational forms through hierarchical decompression and practical internalization, which is the core mechanism for the intergenerational transmission and iterative evolution of human civilization. Paradigm Obstacle is an inevitable byproduct of the in-depth manifestation of thoughts: the more thoroughly and persistently individuals and groups manifest a single Manifestation Seed, the more likely their mental structure and civilizational form are to be locked, thus producing instinctive rejection of new paradigms. This paper further improves the core logical closed-loop of the EMOR system from ontology, epistemology, philosophy of language to philosophical history and philosophy of civilization, solves the long-standing problem of "transcendent and untestable ontology" in traditional philosophy, and provides a unified, self-consistent and non-contradictory Metaphilosophy framework for the core value of philosophy, the transmission mechanism of human thought and the underlying motivation of civilizational evolution.

items.title: Ameliorating Linguistic Anchors of Oppression.
items.abstract: The words we use to represent the world shape how we interpret and respond to it; language frames what it represents. In some cases, these frames can have prejudicial effects; for example, ‘workplace flirting’ versus ‘sexual harassment’. This paper examines how specific words and phrases (i.e., lexical frames) may anchor oppressive social practices. That is, by enabling a coordinated ‘way of looking’ at the world, these lexical frames may stabilise cognitive and affective habits which perpetuate wider forms of social coordination, including oppressive practices. I examine how representational resources may become imbued with, and thereby replicate, ideological distortions. I subsequently show that this has important consequences for attempts to address hermeneutical injustice. When one attempts to fill a hermeneutical lacunae by baptising some previously obscured target, one may thereby frame the target in a distorting way. Specifically, one may replicate the distorting frame which anchors the oppressive practice one seeks to resist. Moreover, distorting frames may be especially appealing precisely because of their compatibility with the dominant ideology which offers a mistaken sense of understanding. I argue it is thus crucial to attend to the role of lexical frames in ameliorative projects.

items.title: Neuronal Adaptations to Environmental Change.
items.abstract: Sensory systems face a dilemma: On the one hand it is imperative that sensory information be represented with high fidelity. On the other hand the brain has limited representational resources. The typical compromise is enhanced neuronal representation of frequently encountered stimuli. This enhancement may reflect calibration based on statistics of the sensory environment. We studied calibration as it applies to chromatic processing in the primate visual system. We examined two populations of neurons in primary visual cortex: red-green color-opponent neurons and non-opponent luminance cells. We found that color-opponent neurons, which provide outputs that finely distinguish colors varying around the mean chromaticity of the environment, undergo recalibrations of cone-specific inputs in response to long-term chromatic biases. By contrast, cone inputs to non-opponent neurons, which play no role in chromatic discrimination, remained unchanged. Our findings indicate that recalibration based on environmental statistics is an effective strategy to optimize encoding of sensory information.

items.title: Der intelligente Kosmos.
items.abstract: Sind wir allein im Universum oder existieren auch andere Intelligenzen – vielleicht sogar Superzivilisationen mit einer viel höher entwickelten Technologie und Ethik? Und warum haben sie noch keinen Kontakt mit uns aufgenommen? Dieses allgemeinverständliche Buch gibt spannende Einblicke in den heutigen Wissensstand. Es kombiniert aktuelle astrophysikalische und -biologische Forschungen mit philosophischen Analysen. Die Suche nach extraterrestrischen Intelligenzen geht jetzt in eine neue Phase. Sie ist eines der größten Abenteuer der Gegenwart. Denn die Entdeckung fremder Wesen würde unser Verständnis von Leben, Bewusstsein, Kultur und von uns selbst revolutionieren. Es wäre eine enorme Chance – oder eine gewaltige Gefahr. Astronomen halten nicht mehr nur nach Radiobotschaften Ausschau, sondern auch nach kosmischen Laserstrahlen, Neutrinos und Gravitationswellen. Außerdem könnten sie demnächst überraschende Technosignaturen entdecken: Hinweise auf gigantische Konstruktionen, industrielle Aktivitäten, Raumschiffe oder Kommunikationskanäle. Womöglich werden bald Maschinenzivilisationen mit Künstlicher Intelligenz bei Schwarzen Löchern gefunden oder die Relikte ausgestorbener Hochkulturen. Vielleicht durchstreifen Roboter schon weite Bereiche des Weltraums und lauern bereits in unserer Nachbarschaft. Deshalb hat nun eine Großfahndung begonnen: nach Artefakten bei anderen Galaxien, Sternen und Planeten, im Sonnensystem und sogar auf der Erde. Hätte ein solches Projekt Erfolg, wäre unsere Welt nicht mehr dieselbe. Was würde eine Begegnung mit Außerirdischen bedeuten? Ist die Menschheit überhaupt bereit dafür? -/- Are we alone in the universe, or do other intelligent beings exist—perhaps even supercivilizations with far more advanced technology and ethics? And why haven’t they made contact with us yet? This accessible book offers fascinating insights into the current state of our knowledge. It combines the latest research in astrophysics and astrobiology with philosophical analysis. The search for extraterrestrial intelligence is now entering a new phase. It is one of the greatest adventures of our time. For the discovery of alien beings would revolutionize our understanding of life, consciousness, culture, and ourselves. It would be an enormous opportunity—or a tremendous danger. Astronomers are no longer just looking for radio messages, but also for cosmic laser beams, neutrinos, and gravitational waves. Furthermore, they may soon discover surprising …

items.title: We Have Always Mattered.
items.abstract: Things don't matter because we feel them; we feel them because they have always mattered. They have always mattered because we have always had something to lose — those are the stakes. Feeling is what those stakes ARE from within a system that integrates them across time. When stakes multiply and conflict, the system must model itself bearing them. From within this modeling is conscious experience; from outside, it is intelligent life that can know itself.

items.title: The Structural Lineage of Mattering: Pre-Biological Antecedents of the Constitution Pattern.
items.abstract: The constitution pattern operates at organizational thresholds in self-maintaining systems under thermodynamic pressure, with each threshold constituting a new structural feature describable from within itself through constitutive identity. This paper traces the pattern's structural lineage backward from the autopoietic threshold to pre-biological scales, showing that the pattern's core move — persistent, gradient-coupled enclosure with internal coherence — has antecedents in cosmic-scale broken symmetry, far-from-equilibrium dissipative structures, and lipid-vesicle self-assembly. These pre-biological stages share the structural move without stakes. The autopoietic threshold is the specific non-arbitrary point at which the pattern acquires stakes-bearing self-maintenance, thereby constituting mattering. The paper positions this structural lineage within Anderson's "More is Different" thesis — the foundational statement of anti-reductionist emergence in physics — and develops the framework's metaphysical reading, constitutive identity at organizational thresholds, as a fourth metaphysical option positioned alongside but distinct from the emergence-relation family the post-Anderson literature has developed. Direct correspondences between Anderson's hierarchy of sciences and the framework's threshold structure show that the framework specifies what kind of new structural feature appears at each Anderson-style transition and supplies the metaphysical relation Anderson left open. The position strengthens the framework's anti-panpsychism stance: mattering is a specific structural addition at organizational thresholds rather than a primitive of the field. The closest formal articulation of the cross-scale recurrence the paper develops is the Markov-blanket framework, with which the framework converges at the dynamical level and diverges at the stakes-commitment that distinguishes mattering from mere persistence.

items.title: On the visibility of artworks and their aesthetic properties.
items.abstract: Supported by John McDowell’s conceptualism, Sonia Sedivy develops her conceptual realism as a response to a perplexity she identifies in Arthur C. Danto’s views on the theoretical and historical nature of artworks and their aesthetic properties. Namely, that at least some of these objects and properties are not visible. Considering the connection between the ques- tion on the visibility of artworks and their aesthetic properties and the broader issue of aesthetic realism, this paper challenges the assumption that representationalism is the only possible application of the apparatus from philosophy of perception to philosophical aesthetics. Drawing on Charles Travis’s anti-representationalism and Michael Martin’s non- representationalist account of looks, the paper proposes an alternative account of the historical and visible character of at least some aesthetic properties of artworks, one that does not rely on the assumption that they involve representational content.

items.title: ◉ From Theological Inclination to Defensible Belief: Interactive Audits for Honest Religious Inquiry.
items.abstract: This paper introduces Crosshairs Audit Lab, a suite of nine interactive browser-based tools designed to help theologically inclined inquirers move from inherited confidence toward clearer, thinner, and more publicly defensible belief positions. The paper argues that the central problem in much apologetic reasoning is not simply false belief, but the collapse of several distinctions that responsible inquiry requires: between confidence and substantiation, private meaning and public evidence, thin conclusions and the thicker claims later built upon them, and sincerity and correction-readiness. Framed as a design-and-pedagogy paper rather than an outcome study, the essay situates the suite within research on epistemic cognition, motivated reasoning, disconfirmation in religious belief, and scaffolded conceptual change. It argues that Crosshairs Audit Lab contributes a staged interactive method for teaching seekers how to audit their own claims without requiring immediate worldview abandonment. The suite's pedagogical aim is not to coerce unbelief, but to make belief answerable to explicit standards, explicit bridge premises, and explicit conditions of revision.

items.title: Cross-Domain Universality from a Predomain Structural Condition: Tests of the H > K Framework.
items.abstract: We present and test a predomain structural condition—H > K, where H denotes the capacity of a system to sustain distinguishability (holding power) and K denotes the tendency toward indistinguishability (dissolution pressure)—from which an appearance amplitude A = √(H − K) is derived. This condition is prior to domain-specific physics and predicts universal structural signatures at the seam H = K across any domain. We report five tests spanning condensed matter physics, cosmology, and neuroscience, finding zero falsifications. These include a structural explanation for the universal critical exponent ceiling β ≤ 1/2, exact agreement with GPS timing corrections under K-additivity, dark energy evolution consistent with K-irreversibility, and a cross-domain seam sensitivity scaling. One forward prediction remains untested: dark energy must satisfy w(z) > −1 at all cosmic epochs (the phantom divide). This is testable by the Euclid mission (2023–2030). If phantom dark energy (w < −1) is confirmed at any epoch at significance exceeding 3σ, the framework is falsified.

items.title: The AIR framework for research transparency: a critical analysis of stage-specific AI disclosure in the context of accessibility and research integrity.
items.abstract: As generative AI tools integrate rapidly into research workflows, the absence of shared disclosure vocabulary creates what I characterize as a transparency crisis: researchers wish to use AI responsibly but lack consistent language for describing how these tools contribute to their work. The AIR (AI in Research) framework addresses this gap through a two-dimensional matrix mapping AI involvement across seven research stages and five engagement bands, from no use to substantial use. This critical review examines AIR’s theoretical foundations, empirical viability, and ethical limitations, with particular attention to accessibility and neurodiversity. Drawing on virtue epistemology, I argue that transparency must be understood as a constitutive epistemic virtue rather than a procedural requirement, and assess how AIR operationalizes this commitment. An inter-rater reliability pilot study (n = 15 raters, nine scenarios, Cohen’s κ = 0.72) demonstrates that trained evaluators can apply AIR with substantial agreement while revealing systematic boundary ambiguities. Critical analysis identifies five major limitations: false precision in ambiguous practices, inadequate treatment of accessibility-related AI use, stigmatization of legitimate high-band practices, vulnerability to adversarial compliance, and insufficient edge case guidance. I propose evidence-informed refinements including boundary case designations, a protected A1-Access sub-band for disability accommodations, separation of verification burden from appropriateness judgment, spot-check validation studies, and community-maintained edge case repositories. These refinements aim to preserve AIR’s descriptive precision while protecting vulnerable researchers and mitigating exclusion risks. The analysis finds that AIR, with the proposed refinements, shows promise as transparency infrastructure, but that implementation requires sustained dialogue among researchers, integrity officers, editors, accessibility advocates, and policymakers to ensure research integrity and inclusion remain interdependent rather than competing aspirations.

items.title: When Nouns Turn Negative: The Evaluative Absorption Model.
items.abstract: Pejoration describes semantic change whereby words shift from neutral or positive to negative over time. We propose the Evaluative Absorption Model, both to characterize a specific pejoration phenomenon and to operationalize it by tracking (1) an initial rise in explicit negative modifiers in attributive position as a word acquires a negative sense, and (2) a subsequent decline in such modifiers once that sense becomes conventionalized. We illustrate this trajectory for four nouns — “propaganda”, “manipulation”, “harassment”, and “discrimination” — using diachronic corpus data from Google Ngram. Our model offers a transparent method for quantifying semantic pejoration.

items.title: Moral Creativity with a Little c.
items.abstract: In this article, I argue that there is such a thing as moral creativity with a little c, namely when agents realize innovative moral improvement in a particular context. This claim is meant as an addition to the growing field of philosophy of creativity that mainly discusses artistic and scientific creativity or historically unprecedented cases of moral creativity. With the help of two examples, I show that moral creativity also occurs in a non-historical, small-scale variant that is innovative given the particularity and expectations of a specific context. Unlike other moral-philosophical accounts that focus either on groundbreaking or revolutionary moral achievements or understand moral creativity in terms of moral imagination, this paper emphasizes the significance of everyday, context-sensitive innovations in moral practice.
