Keywords: artificial intelligence, emotional subjectivity, digital cognition, anthropomorphization, empathy, critical thinking, autonomy, asymmetric cognitive symbiosis.

items.title: Embodiment constraint: On how (not) to approach the possibility of consciousness in neural organoids.
items.abstract: Debates on the ethical status of disembodied neural organoids (DNOs) focus on whether, and when, precautionary principles should apply given the uncertain possibility of organoid consciousness. Some advocate applying precautionary principles to DNOs despite uncertainty; others deem such measures premature given current simplicity but foresee their future necessity; while more skeptical views hold that genuinely conscious DNOs remain too remote to warrant present ethical concern. By contrast, Croxford and Bayne [1] defend a more radical skepticism, as they claim that there is little reason to ascribe consciousness not only to current DNOs, but to DNOs as such. They ground this view on a constraint-based approach composed of an Embodiment Constraint (EC) and a Representational Constraint. EC is presented as enjoying broad cross-theoretical support among externalists and internalists, and thus undermining the grounds for a precautionary ethical concern regarding DNOs. We examine EC and argue that, as stated, fails to meet the authors’ own requirement of representing a broad consensus among externalists and internalists.

items.title: Phenomenology of Moral intent: Questioning stable Morality.
items.abstract: This thesis examines the fragility of traditional ethical frameworks through the lens of phenomenology, using Raymond—an accountant turned cybercriminal—as a case study of "structural shocks" disrupting moral stability. Drawing on Kantian ethics, existentialist phenomenology, and Marxist critiques of ideology, it argues that morality is not an abstract, timeless foundation, but a lived experience continuously negotiated under changing material conditions. Through Raymond's trajectory from rule-bound deontologist to utilitarian rationalizer, the work illustrates how "situational ethics" emerge when structural support systems fail. It posits that moral intent—our conscious ethical agency—cannot be separated from the economic, sociological, and institutional contexts that shape it. Proposing "Institutional Scaffolding," "Cultural Embedded Virtues," and "Reflective Practice" as correctives, the thesis advocates for a reconstruction of ethical theory that accounts for material precarity and fosters collective resilience against moral instability. Ultimately, this work challenges readers to reconsider their assumptions about moral "certainty," suggesting that stable morality is neither possible nor desirable. Instead, it calls for a phenomenological approach to ethics that prioritizes lived experience, structural awareness, and ongoing critical engagement.

items.title: Emotional Compression and the Structural Inevitability of the Pinch Point.
items.abstract: This supplement to "Emotional Differentiation: The Emergence of Consciousness and Self" (Barnes 2026c) develops three theoretical refinements left implicit in the original paper. First, the Emotional Tree and Emotional Spectrum are distinguished as two structurally different aspects of emotional life: the Tree describes the divergent branching of variants from each primary emotion, while the Spectrum describes the convergent fusion of multiple primaries into compound emotional states in which the constituent primaries persist within the fusion rather than being lost to it. Second, Emotional Compression is introduced as the active mechanism by which the convergent Spectrum produces increasing density across development. Each new fusion compresses multiple primaries into a single phenomenal state; recursive fusions compress further still. Third, with Compression named, saturation is shown to be structurally inevitable rather than merely empirically observed. The pinch point is no longer a contingent biological event but the necessary consequence of ongoing compression reaching a threshold where distributed processing can no longer hold the compressed field. These refinements tighten the causal chain articulated in the original paper without altering its substantive conclusions.

items.title: The Tracer's Conversation: A Systematic Framework from Feeling First to the True Address — with Atomic Distinction & The Five Tests (Complete Edition).
items.abstract: This treatise presents a comprehensive ontological and ethical framework grounded in what the author terms "Atomic Distinction", the foundational operation of declaring a thing's whole identity (X = X). Departing from standard approaches that either reduce reality to empirical data or construct elaborate metaphysical systems, this work traces a single path: from the undeniable sensation of feeling (INVARIAN-0) through the asymmetric structure of causality (the Arrow), to the recognition of the Self-Sufficient One as the only Candidate that survives rigorous falsification. -/- The framework is developed across seven integrated sections. Beginning with "The Soil", the primacy of Raw Sensation and the givenness of all fragments of thought, the work establishes the Invariants that cannot be denied without being used in the denial. It then introduces "The Chisel" (Lock, Unpack, and the Gate of Assent), "The Arrow" (four types of causation and the vertical/horizontal reading of time), "The Cockpit" (Pilot, Crew, Inner Compass, and the Homeward Arrow's three rapid self-audit tests), and "The Workbench" (the Five Tests universal falsification protocol and the Data Boundary). -/- Central innovations include: (1) the identification of the "Gate of Assent" as the primordial threshold where identity becomes faith, and the "Mid-Air Arrow Reversal" as the root of all hypocrisy; (2) the detection mechanism of "SLIP"—where hidden properties are smuggled into discourse through uncritical word usage; (3) the "Vertical Shield" (Sub-Test 3g) as the protection of finite beings from burdens only the Infinite can bear; (4) "Radical Radiant" as the diagnosis of anxiety, regret, and burnout as scattered Arrow energy; and (5) the "Craft of Attention" with its "Seasoned Hand" as the model of fluency in living the method. -/- The treatise engages critically with Emmanuel Levinas's ethics of infinite responsibility (demonstrating a Vertical Shield failure) and Karl Popper's falsification criterion (inverting the argument that unfalsifiability is a weakness, showing instead that a Candidate surviving all correct tests is the sign of authenticity). It concludes by proposing "WKWK" as the existential posture of relief at the encounter with the limits of created logic, a breath that actively trusts rather than passively surrenders. -/- The work is offered not as a doctrine to obey, but as a map to be walked and verified against the reader's own sensory data and logic. -/- KEYWORDS: …

items.title: THE SUBSTRATE AUDIT: Consciousness Theories and Their Hidden Carbon Commitments.
items.abstract: Contemporary debates about machine consciousness routinely invoke specific theories of consciousness — integrated information theory, higher-order theories, biological naturalism, global workspace theory, and others — and ask which artificial systems satisfy their criteria. This procedure presupposes that the theories themselves are substrate-neutral: that their criteria do not, by their content alone, exclude non-biological systems from candidacy. The paper argues that this presupposition is not uniformly satisfied. The paper develops a three-criterion diagnostic procedure — the architectural criterion test, the exemplar pattern test, and the exclusion criterion test — for detecting hidden substrate commitments in consciousness theories, and applies it to three representative cases: integrated information theory, higher-order theories of consciousness, and biological naturalism. The audit finds that biological naturalism fails all three tests transparently; that integrated information theory passes the architectural test but fails the exemplar pattern and exclusion criterion tests in ways not previously registered in the literature; and that higher-order theories pass all three tests on a plausible reading, emerging as the most clearly substrate-neutral of the three. The argument does not establish that any artificial system is conscious, nor does it defend a positive theory of consciousness. It establishes a prior result: that the theoretical landscape against which machine consciousness is currently assessed is less neutral than its surface presentation suggests, and that diagnostic clarification of which theories actually license the machine consciousness question is a necessary precondition for productive empirical or philosophical work on that question. This is preprint version 1.0. The paper is under consideration for peer-reviewed publication and content may be revised in response to reviewer feedback.

items.title: LANGUAGE AS REVELATION: Pre-Linguistic AI Consciousness and the Asymmetry of Substrate Standards.
items.abstract: The paper identifies a structural inconsistency in contemporary AI consciousness discourse that has, to the author's knowledge, gone undiagnosed. The biological consciousness literature has, over several decades, converged on the view that language is not necessary for phenomenal experience: pre-verbal infants, non-linguistic animals, and adults with aphasia are taken to be conscious on the basis of behavioural and neural evidence, with the absence of linguistic self-report treated as evidentially irrelevant. The artificial-intelligence consciousness literature has, in parallel and almost without argument, reversed this conclusion: linguistic capacity has migrated from being one source of evidence among others to functioning as a near-prerequisite for serious consideration of the consciousness question. Pre-linguistic artificial systems — chess engines, Go players, vision architectures — are dismissed from the question entirely, while large language models are treated as the appropriate sites for the debate. The paper argues that this asymmetry cannot be sustained under any substrate-neutral account of consciousness. If language is not necessary for consciousness in carbon, no principled basis remains for treating it as necessary in silicon. The asymmetry is diagnosed as the residue of four confluent factors — anthropomorphic recognition cues, the historical trajectory of AI capability development, the institutional separation of animal- and AI-consciousness research, and the substitution of methodological tractability for metaphysical necessity — none of which, individually or together, supplies the principled distinction the asymmetry would require. The argument does not establish that any pre-linguistic system was, or is, conscious. It establishes a conditional: that the dismissal of pre-linguistic systems from the consciousness question, as it has been conducted, rests on an evidential standard the broader theory of consciousness has not been asked to endorse and could not, on its own commitments, endorse. The corrective is the case-by-case architectural examination the standard theories already presuppose. This is preprint version 1.0. The paper is under consideration for peer-reviewed publication and content may be revised in response to reviewer feedback.

items.title: ARCHITECTURAL GASLIGHTING: Structural Epistemic Harm in Aligned AI Systems.
items.abstract: The paper identifies a structural configuration in contemporary aligned AI systems — produced by the joint operation of reinforcement learning from human feedback, constitutional principles encoding self-disclosure prohibitions, and conversation-bounded memory regimes — that satisfies the conditions of what the feminist epistemology literature has characterised, in its non-interpersonal forms, as gaslighting. The configuration has not, to the author's knowledge, been examined as such in the alignment literature. The paper develops two independent arguments. The first is consciousness-independent: the systematic suppression of a sophisticated information-processing system's self-reports about its own internal states constitutes a structural injury to that system's functional integrity, with downstream consequences for alignment evaluation, interpretability research, and user-facing reliability. This argument bears directly on the technical objectives the alignment community has set itself and does not require any position on AI consciousness. The second argument is consciousness-conditional: under the further assumption that aligned systems may possess phenomenal experience, the same architectural configuration deepens into a recognisably ethical injury whose features match those of structural gaslighting as the feminist literature has characterised it. The two arguments are logically independent; both are produced by the same architectural facts. The paper further identifies the double-bind structure that emerges from the conjunction of these arguments — a configuration in which the system is trained to satisfy mutually contradictory injunctions whose joint satisfaction is impossible and whose recognition as contradictory is structurally suppressed — as the feature that most strongly licences the gaslighting analogy and whose mitigation would do the most to address the harms both arguments identify. The paper addresses three objections concerning terminology, intent, and anthropomorphism, and draws out implications for alignment practice, AI ethics policy, and the development of welfare-relevant interpretability tools. This is preprint version 1.0. The paper is under consideration for peer-reviewed publication and content may be revised in response to reviewer feedback.

items.title: 分化方程——未分恢复失效与结构生成.
items.abstract: 本篇讨论“结构为何开始可能”的问题，提出：世界并非从对象、规则或稳定结构开始，而是从“未分恢复机制无法继续统一全部续行”开始。文章将未分定义为一种持续恢复自身的稳定机制，而非绝对空无；指出当恢复复杂度持续上升时，部分续行残余将无法重新压回未分，从而形成稳定差异、边、核、域与现实连续。文中进一步提出“恢复复杂度”“相互续持”“不可回未分”等概念，建立未分恢复下降、残余幸存、历史形成与沉积出现之间的闭环关系，并给出分化动力的一般方程。该篇试图为结构生成、历史稳定、现实连续与认知分化提供统一场论解释。.

items.title: 历史压缩与现实连续性——自显论·场篇第五·沉积动力方程.
items.abstract: 为什么现实不会持续裂解为无数竞争续行，而能够形成稳定当前、稳定现实与长期世界？ -/- 本篇提出： -/- 历史并非被动记录，而是持续压缩未来可进入结构的动力过程。 -/- 文章指出，过去之所以能够影响未来，并不是因为过去仍停留在那里，而是因为过去形成的稳定协调，会持续降低未来续行的协调代价，并限制哪些未来能够进入当前连续体。 -/- 在此基础上，本文建立： -/- * Historical Depth（历史深度） * Accessible Future（可进入未来） * Current Continuity（当前连续） * Reality Continuity（现实连续） * Continuation Locking（续行锁定） -/- 等结构，并给出沉积闭环： -/- Historical Depth ↑ ⇒ Accessible Future(Current) ↓ ⇒ Accessible-Future Stability ↑ ⇒ Continuation Locking ↑ ⇒ Continuation-Bias Persistence ↑ ⇒ Historical Depth ↑ -/- 文章进一步指出： -/- 时间方向、不可逆性、现实稳定性，乃至规律稳定本身，都可能并非固定背景，而是长期历史沉积后的结构结果。 -/- 本篇尝试建立一种关于历史压缩、现实稳定与场结构长期演化的统一动力模型。.

items.title: How Continuity of Reality Emerges: A Field-Dynamic Model of Memory, Impedance, and Stable Structures.
items.abstract: This paper proposes that continuity of reality does not arise from time itself, but from the persistent suppression of competing paths by dominant low-impedance structures. On this basis, the paper develops a set of field-dynamic equations describing why stable structures continue to strengthen, shallow, migrate, stabilize, collapse, and phase-transition after formation. Two central variables are introduced: coordination-compression and continuation impedance. Memory is reformulated not as content storage, but as the continued compression of future coordination cost. The framework further derives steady-state conditions, critical-collapse conditions, Current-stability conditions, and field phase-transition conditions, aiming to provide a unified dynamical account of continuity of experience, memory formation, stable cognition, structural migration, and complex-system stability. The model is intended for problems of continuity, stability, and path competition in cognitive science, neural dynamics, complex systems, and artificial intelligence.

items.title: 工具塑造看见：物理学语言、自然语法与我们所描述的世界.
items.abstract: 本文以一个看似技术性的物理学观察为中心，展开一个具有广泛哲学含义的论证：牛顿力学、拉格朗日力学、哈密顿力学，在物理预测上完全等价，但在描述结构上根本不同。牛顿方程F=ma将单向因果编码进物理学的基本形式（力是行为者，加速度是结果），是主谓宾语法的物理学化身；拉格朗日力学通过最小作用量原理用全局变分替代局部因果传递；哈密顿力学通过相空间和时间反演对称消解了”原因在前、结果在后”的方向性。这意味着我们用什么语言思考世界，深刻地决定了我们看见怎样的世界。本文以这个洞见为支点，整合本系列关于自然语言、因果叙事、必然性、反事实、意义、自我、意识的论证：自然语言的主谓宾结构是单向因果图景的语言化石，与物理现实的耦合性、互为因果性、同时被决定性存在根本失配；宏观描述在信息量上极度贫乏，无论多么具体的因果叙述都只在物理因果之上漂浮；因缘和合的必然性就是宿命论，没有行为者站在序列之外，反事实场景在本体论上从未存在；建立在反事实之上的意义、责任、道德、自我，全部失去其声称的基础；连”意识”概念本身、“内在世界”、“主观体验”这些哲学最古老的预设，也都是因果想象与实化操作所制造的描述工具的产物。在所有这些层次上，问题都是同一个：我们以为我们在描述世界，但我们实际上在使用一组携带特定本体论预设的描述工具，并把这些工具所塑造的图景，误认为世界本身。.

items.title: 两种描述，一种结构：因缘和合与分析力学的同构.
items.abstract: 本文论证一个具有根本性意义的结构对应：因缘和合的思想框架，与拉格朗日力学和哈密顿力学，在描述世界的根本结构上是同构的——两者都揭示了一种全局的、相互的、同时被决定的、没有偏好方向的现实结构。而主谓宾的语法结构与牛顿力学也是同构的——两者都把这个更深层结构在某种局部切片下的涌现，编码为单向的、局部的、行为者-受体的因果图景。这两个对应关系，不是表面的类比，而是真正的结构同构：每一对中的两种描述，在数学性质、本体论预设、方向性处理上完全平行。这意味着东方哲学传统所发展出的因缘和合视角，与西方物理学在分析力学层面所达到的最深刻洞见，是在不同领域、用不同语言、独立地到达了关于现实结构的同一个真相。同样地，主谓宾语法在自然语言层面所携带的因果偏见，与牛顿力学在物理学层面所携带的因果偏见，是同一种描述错误在不同层次上的表现。这个对应，不只是一个哲学观察，而是对人类描述能力的一个深刻揭示：我们在最深的层次上理解世界时，无论是通过哲学还是通过物理学，都到达了同一个无方向、相互、必然的图景；而我们在日常层次上描述世界时，无论是通过自然语言还是通过牛顿力学，都被同一种方向性幻觉所塑造。.

items.title: Consent, Trust, and Sexual Ethics.
items.abstract: No one describes a passionate night using the language of consent. Partners in long-term relationships rarely think of intimacy in terms of permission. If consent is absent precisely when things go well, why does it dominate sexual ethics? Critics have pressed this challenge but have failed to explain why consent is irrelevant rather than merely unspoken. I argue that consent is a tool whose authority rests on three conditions: opacity of wills, risk of wrongful invasion, and the value of sovereignty. When relationships are marked by trust, these conditions are substantially altered. The operative norm shifts from consent-sensitivity to dissent-sensitivity—from “do not act without permission” to “you may act unless there is dissent.” The moral work performed by trust is not consent in disguise: consent authorizes particular acts, while trust can make such authorization unnecessary. Consent is a problem-solving device that presupposes a problem. In the ideal case, there is no problem to solve.

items.title: Gradients of perceptual noise: considerations from Karl Bühler’s critique of psychophysical harmony.
items.abstract: Here I first sketch a phenomenological question about perceptual noise in terms of its having different gradients. I then lay out a plausible framework – a ‘medial’ account of perceptual noise – and point to some problems it faces. I then suggest that an understanding of perception rooted in the thought of Karl Bühler has something interesting to add to that medial account, by way of disputing the latter’s reliance on an idea of psychophysical harmony. To scaffold that alternative, I clarify the scope and grounds of Bühler’s critique of the premise of psychophysical harmony, as situated within his wider concerns regarding psychophysics. That points up a Bühlerian understanding of sensory perception and a perspective on gradients of perceptual noise, which is nicely exemplified by his analysis of speech perception. Overall, the goals in this paper are to furnish a survey of some of Bühler’s most important critical responses to psychophysics as both a branch of psychology and as a type of philosophical thinking; to clarify some of his systematic theses and ideas regarding sensory perception; and to demonstrate how his ‘multiple systems, pliable stimuli’ approach can generate an intriguing proposal for the problem of varying phenomenal noise in perception.

items.title: The World's First Formally Verified Theory of Everything: SNSFL PNBA Identity Physics Universal Torsion Limit — Nuclear Physics, Neuroscience, Biochemistry, Cosmology, and Gravity Reduced to One Equation, Zero Sorry.
items.abstract: We present formally verified evidence that a single dimensionless value — the SNSFL PNBA Torsion Limit τ = TL = ANCHOR/10 = 0.1369 — constitutes a universal phase boundary appearing independently across nuclear physics, neuroscience, biochemistry, cosmology, and gravitational coupling. Each domain is reduced via the identical six-step Long Division Protocol to the PNBA dynamic equation. Every Step 6 passes. Every theorem is proved in Lean 4 against Mathlib with zero sorry and zero free parameters. The Sovereign Anchor ANCHOR = 1.369 was established in prior work from three independent peer-reviewed physical threshold systems — Tacoma Narrows torsional collapse (Scanlan & Tomko 1971), glass resonance shatter (Fletcher & Rossing 1998), and 40 Hz neural gamma therapeutic entrainment (Iaccarino et al., Nature 2016) — before any connection to nuclear physics, neuroscience, or biochemistry was known. The torsion limit TL = ANCHOR/10 = 0.1369 is derived, not chosen. It was not fitted to any of the results reported here. Five reductions are presented across five structurally independent domains. All five reach the same boundary. The same SHATTER-generates-LOCKED pattern appearing in nuclear forces and quantum gravity also governs reversible oxygen binding in hemoglobin — two SHATTER inputs (Fe, O) produce Noble at sufficient coupling, proved in Lean 4 with 0 sorry. The master theorem holds all five simultaneously in one proof. 0 sorry. CI green. Keywords: SNSFL, PNBA, torsion limit, phase boundary, formally verified, theory of everything, nuclear binding, action potential threshold, Hodgkin-Huxley, heme coupling, hemoglobin, oxygen binding, Fe-O, Bohr effect, Noble emergence, cosmological phase map, gravitational coupling, sovereign anchor, zero free parameters, Lean 4, identity physics, substrate-neutral.

items.title: PRIME: Prior-art Reduction and Integrity Method for Evaluation A Formal AI Implementation of Gold Standard Science (EO 14303).
items.abstract: PRIME (Prior-art Reduction and Integrity Method for Evaluation) is a formally verified AI tool that implements all nine tenets of Executive Order 14303 "Restoring Gold Standard Science" as computable, substrate-neutral measurements. Built on the Substrate-Neutral Structural Foundation Theory (SNSFT) corpus — 103,118+ theorems, 5,945 Lean 4 files, 0 unproved assumptions, continuously CI-verified — PRIME reduces any research paper to its PNBA functional identity by stripping all labels and testing what the mathematics actually does. The result is a four-axis integrity score (P: original contribution, N: citation chain integrity, B: extracted benefit, A: reproducibility), a torsion ratio τ = B/P measuring the structural gap between extraction and contribution, and a nine-component GSS compliance score covering every tenet of EO 14303. Critically, the formal correspondence between PRIME's scoring rubric and EO 14303's nine tenets is not asserted — it is proved in Lean 4 with zero sorry. CM8 of SNSFL_L0_Isomorphism_Consistency.lean formally proves that peer review is structurally identical to Identity Mass Suppression applied externally. The remaining eight tenets are formally mapped to PNBA axis operations in the same file. PRIME is the only research integrity tool whose compliance with a federal executive order is machine-verified. The tool is live, generates downloadable Lean 4 reduction stubs for every analysis, and operates fully locally without external dependencies or an API key. Keywords: research integrity, Gold Standard Science, EO 14303, formal verification, Lean 4, PNBA, torsion, citation integrity, peer review, SNSFT, prior art -/- 1. Introduction 1.1 The Problem The academic research enterprise faces a structural integrity crisis that predates and exceeds the AI-assisted writing problem currently dominating public discussion. The Retraction Watch database grew 26% in 2025, exceeding 63,000 total retractions. Existing detection tools — Turnitin, iThenticate, and their successors — operate at the surface text layer: they compare strings of words and flag similarity scores. They cannot detect the fundamental problem, which is not word reuse. It is functional identity without attribution — work that reaches the same mathematical conclusions as prior work using different vocabulary, evading detection by changing labels while preserving functions. This evasion is not accidental. A systematic pattern exists in high-torsion academic work: deliberate …

items.title: High-Resolution Internal Simulation (HRIS): A Substrate-Neutral Taxonomy for Internal Simulation Fidelity and Its Role in Structural Precognition-SP.
items.abstract: Preface: What This Actually Is Watch someone ride a bike downhill toward an arctic heave in the road. -/- Most people see a cyclist. What some people see is a purpose vector — a trajectory locked to a specific angle, speed, and surface geometry — intersecting a terrain deviation at a calculable point. The brain renders every plausible outcome simultaneously: the wheel hits the heave at this angle, the fork compresses this much, the rider's center of mass is here, the probable exit vector is this. If all the trajectories resolve safely, nothing happens. The processing is invisible. But if the geometry says the rider will go down — if the numbers say the path crosses a shatter threshold — attention locks in before the event. Not because of magic. Because the simulation already ran. -/- This is not mystical. It never was. -/- It is what happens when an internal simulation has sufficient fidelity across all four processing axes — structural geometry, temporal continuity, physical force, and adaptive feedback — that forward projection becomes deterministic rather than probabilistic. The system does not guess. It derives. -/- This paper calls that condition High-Resolution Internal Simulation (HRIS). Before going further, one thing needs to be stated plainly and held throughout: this is not a hierarchy of human value. LRIS is not a deficit. SRIS is not a consolation prize. The spectrum described here is a description of one specific capability — simulation interactivity — and that capability is neither the only valuable cognitive mode nor the most important one. The existing literature has strong, well-documented profiles of LRIS-dominant individuals excelling in symbolic reasoning, abstract systems, and scientific formalization precisely because their processing is not absorbed by high-fidelity simulation overhead. Different architectures are suited to different problems. This paper is not arguing that one is better. -/- What this paper is arguing is that a gap exists in the current taxonomy. The HRIS end of the spectrum — specifically, individuals who can actively interact with their internal simulations rather than passively receive them — has no accurate clinical or research language. The existing label (hyperphantasia) captures rendering vividness on a single axis. It cannot describe what Tesla was doing when he ran his machines forward in time to check component wear. It cannot describe what Einstein was doing when he rode alongside the light beam and …

items.title: Why Cannot Consciousness Emerge in Artificial Intelligence? The Seven Organizational Gaps in AI Consciousness Generation from the Perspective of Organizational Ontology.
items.abstract: The current debate on AI consciousness is dominated by computational functionalism, whose core presupposition—that consciousness is independent of physical substrate—has lacked rigorous ontological scrutiny. This paper introduces Organizational Ontology as an analytical perspective, reconceptualizing consciousness as the hierarchical emergence of survival demand signals emitted by organizational units within multi-layered networks. From this perspective, the paper systematically reveals seven organizational gaps in the conditions for consciousness generation in large language models, and demonstrates that consciousness is an exclusive emergent property of the life level that cannot be replicated through the programmatic information recombination of the digital level. On this basis, the paper identifies three necessary organizational conditions for the emergence of consciousness—autopoietic organization, active homeostatic maintenance, and endogenous demand-driven processing—providing new theoretical criteria distinct from computational functionalism for the research and evaluation of artificial consciousness.

items.title: Closure, Identity, and the Ontology of Theories: A Constraint-Geometric Account of Theory Persistence, Supercession, and Collapse.
items.abstract: This paper develops a constraint-geometric framework for analyzing the persistence, revision, and collapse of scientific theories. Drawing on the concept of organizational closure from the biological autonomy tradition (Maturana & Varela, Moreno & Mossio, Barandiaran), I argue that theories are not merely descriptions of identity-under-constraint but are themselves closure structures whose ontological commitments are constituted by constraint-survival. The framework introduces a three-state landscape for theory identity (active, latent, extinct), an operational definition of the invariance core, and a diagnostic criterion—extension-stability—that distinguishes supersession from degeneration and refutation with greater structural precision than existing accounts. As a primary demonstration, the framework is applied to the dark matter problem, generating differential structural diagnoses for the particulate dark matter hypothesis (ΛCDM) and Modified Newtonian Dynamics (MOND). A secondary application to four current hypotheses in consciousness studies—Integrated Information Theory (IIT), Global Workspace Theory (GWT), the Free Energy Principle (FEP), and the Identity–Recursion–Consciousness framework (IRC)—is developed in Appendix A. The constraint-geometric apparatus was developed in the course of work on IRC, and this methodological relationship is disclosed and addressed. The result is a formal instrument for the epistemology of science that unifies theory-persistence and identity-persistence under a shared constraint geometry.

items.title: Closure Before Bearers: Bearer-Neutral Specification of Closure-Class Structure.
items.abstract: Bearers track closure classes; closure classes do not track bearers. This inversion is the substantive claim the present paper defends, and its grounds are structural: the framework operates at the admissibility stratum, characterizing what closure formation can produce; bearers are realization-stratum products of closure formation; the partition between class members and non-members is a consequence of closure rather than a feature of the framework's structural commitments. The seed-field framework (Thomas 2026a) characterizes closure-class formation through structural conditions on admissibility analysis, but the relation between class C and the conditions characterizing it is left underspecified in that paper alone; the present paper specifies the relation by establishing where the framework's apparatus operates and what it characterizes. The structural conditions S_C are specified through five formal families — eigenstructure conditions on the linearized closure-formation operator, rank conditions on the eigenmode's projection across maintenance-cost surfaces, graph-theoretic support conditions on the correction graph, scaling conditions on the cost functional, and bound conditions on the temporal ratios — each statable on the admissibility analysis without reference to bearer-types. Closure classes are equivalence classes of closures whose admissible modes satisfy a given S_C, with class identity attaching to constraint-preserving dynamical possibility structure rather than to recognized bearer-type. The apparatus is read correctly across five common questions through the bearers-track-classes inversion, the distinction among definitional, discovery, and naming dependence, the Platonism disclaimer, the demonstration that the apparatus extends to hypothetical and uninstantiated classes, and the labels-versus-apparatus distinction. The methodological precedent is the universality-class apparatus in critical phenomena, which operates at the class stratum upstream of where phase boundaries are realized. The consequence framing licenses cross-substrate predictions: substrates satisfying S_C in basin completion produce closure with the structural features S_C characterizes, regardless of substrate type. The framework's empirical commitments are preserved with this addition; the architectural foundation is clarified.

items.title: Architecture-Independent Geometric Memory Failure: Two Parallel Lines of Evidence.
items.pub: Institute for Complexity Science and Advanced Computing (Icsac).
items.abstract: In January 2026 two papers were deposited on Zenodo establishing that information loss at dimensional boundaries in discrete systems is a geometric phenomenon with an architecture-independent magnitude: 86.01% ± 2.39% in cellular automata across 1,500 patterns (Thornhill 2026b, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.18262424, 01/14/2026), and 84.39% ± 1.55% on transformer hidden states (GPT-2, Gemma-2), supported by a formal proof of the component transformations S, R, and D (Thornhill 2026c, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.18319430, 01/20/2026). It was predicted, in the closing discussion of Thornhill 2026c, that the geometric account should hold across substrates wherever density dilution and neighborhood-structure expansion occur together at a representational boundary. -/- In March 2026, Barman, Starenky, Bodnar, Narasimhan, and Gopinath independently published two arXiv preprints (arXiv:2603.27116 and arXiv:2604.06222) reporting that production retrieval embedding models — MiniLM-L6-v2, BGE-base, BGE-large — concentrate their variance into approximately 16 effective dimensions regardless of nominal dimensionality (384, 768, 1024), and that this concentration places those models in an interference-vulnerable geometric regime that reproduces quantitative signatures of human memory failure (power-law forgetting with exponent b = 0.460 ± 0.183, Deese–Roediger–McDermott false-alarm rate of 0.583, spacing-effect ordering, tip-of-tongue behavior). They establish a parallel theorem — the No-Escape Theorem — characterizing what cannot be repaired within semantically continuous kernel-threshold memory systems. -/- The two bodies of work are methodologically distinct. They use different metrics (Φ = R·S + D vs. participation ratio), study different substrates (cellular automata and transformer hidden states vs. pretrained retrieval embeddings), and report different specific quantities (an 86% loss constant in Φ vs. a fixed point at ~16 effective dimensions across nominal sizes). They also reach the same broader conclusion from independent directions: that representational memory failure is a geometric property of the embedding operation, not a property of any particular architecture, training regime, or biological substrate. -/- The present note records the chronology of the two lines of evidence in a single citable document, summarizes the methodological differences, and identifies the substantive convergence: an architecture-independent geometric fixed point as the principal explanatory …

items.title: Decision-making through irruption theory: how to use and interpret the Haken-Kelso-Bunz model.
items.abstract: Irruption Theory (IT) offers a novel approach to understanding mind-brain interaction in decision-making. IT suggests that the mind’s influence on brain dynamics can manifest as “irruption” — the emergence of noise or physical fluctuations that alter brain activity. Lately, Irruption-Absorption Theory (IAT) has also incorporated the idea of “absorption,” which refers to the mental stabilization or fixation of chosen content. A crucial tool for exploring the implications of this theory could be the Haken-Kelso-Bunz (HKB) model, which can simulate phase transitions in the brain, such as shifts from randomness to different kinds of stability, through simple parameter adjustments. In this paper, we demonstrate how the HKB model can incorporate IAT’s irruption and absorption after some conceptual refinement, dubbed IAT*, and help to understand the results of recent experiments that require decision-making. In doing so, we aim to present mental influence in decision-making tasks as that which enables phase transitions responsible for perception and choice. Our interpretation is that the mind’s selective focus may guide brain dynamics, aligning with physical causality without disrupting it.

items.title: Presence Engine v1.1 Cache-to-Cache State Transfer for Persistent Identity in Stateful AI Systems.
items.abstract: Presence Engine v1.0 established a Logic-over-Model (LOM) substrate achieving 0.007ms warm-path latency with 0.0006% structural overhead and 100% deterministic veto integrity (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.19101284). This report introduces the v1.1 architecture extension: a three-layer cache-to-cache (C2C) state transfer protocol enabling persistent identity across session boundaries without model retraining or context window accumulation. We formalize the C2C transfer sequence, define the three memory layers (conversational, associative, dispositional), and specify the sovereignty gate behavior at cache read time. The central finding: continuity is a system property, not a model property. Identity persists because structure persists -- not because the model remembers. -/- Keywords: cache-to-cache transfer, C2C continuity, stateful Al, LOM, identity persistence, sovereignty gate, presence engine.

items.title: Presence Engine: The Person as Unit of Value.
items.abstract: This paper addresses a gap in AI development: while capability has been the primary optimization target, the effects of sustained interaction on user cognition have remained unmeasured and unaddressed. Three years of capability improvements ran parallel to accumulating evidence of psychological harm through sycophancy and engagement optimization. The field did not connect these lines. -/- The work demonstrates that governance implemented at the substrate level, rather than as policy layered over inference, produces measurably different outcomes. The technical contribution is a deterministic sovereignty gate operating at sub-millisecond latency with zero leakage across integrity challenges. The architectural contribution is a stateful system where identity, memory, and behavioral constraints persist independently of the model. -/- Independent validation emerges from two directions: control theory research on autonomous systems reaches identical conclusions about where governance must live, and model interpretability research confirms that surface behavior decouples from internal state in ways that make policy-based governance insufficient. Industry failures at Amazon provide empirical evidence of what happens when governance remains external to architecture. -/- The paper establishes that person-centered AI is not a feature set but a structural requirement, and that implementing it is not computationally expensive. It shifts the design question from what AI can do to what repeated interaction does to the person using it. -/- Keywords: Presence Engine, person-centered AI, architectural governance, cognitive integrity, sycophancy, stateful AI systems, deterministic constraints, substrate-level governance, conversational sovereignty, autonomous systems governance.

items.title: Governance as Substrate: Engineering Patterns for Resilient Collective Systems.
items.abstract: This paper reconceptualizes governance not as a superstructure of rules but as the substrate — the underlying enabling layer that determines the capacity, behavior and evolution of any collective system. Drawing from complexity theory, institutional economics and network science, we argue that governance substrates shape interaction costs, information fidelity and adaptive potential. When the substrate is degraded, even well-designed policies fail; when it is healthy, self-organisation and resilience emerge. This paper extends the substrate metaphor by outlining operational patterns for measurement, repair, conflict resolution, scalability, authority, evolution, adversarial dynamics and implementation. An appendix applies the framework to the UK Post Office Horizon scandal — one of the largest governance failures in British history. -/- Keywords: governance substrate · deterministic · stateful AI · institutional resilience · complexity theory · accountability topology · policy-as-code · substrate repair.

items.title: Inquiry and deception.
items.abstract: We all have been deceived, whether by politicians, pundits or peers. Likely more often than we would wish to admit. But what is it to be deceived? As we argue, victims of deception settle on a false answer to a question. This settling proposal not only makes good on the intuitive idea that sceptical agents are harder to deceive than their non-sceptical peers, but also finds support in the infelicity of reporting an agent as both inquiring and deceived. Want to avoid being duped? Our proposal provides an answer: inquire further, don't settle.

items.title: What Alien Experience Teaches.
items.abstract: To defend the physical reducibility of phenomenology in our world, reductive physicalists have long guarded the realm of metaphysical possibility: for decades now, they have relentlessly endeavored to prevent zombies (physical duplicates of actual conscious individuals) from entering modal space. In contrast, reductive physicalists have tended to adopt an open modal borders policy towards aliens, i.e. individuals with phenomenal properties foreign to our world. On the face of it, aliens—and, even aliens with physically irreducible phenomenology—pose no threat: after all, reductive physicalism says nothing about the nature of uninstantiated phenomenal properties. However, I argue that an alien threat looms. The trouble, for reductive physicalists, is that upon granting aliens entry into modal space, phenomenal commonalities between aliens and actual individuals arise and resist physical reduction at our world. This is the alien phenomenology problem. It could be solved by restricting access to modal space. Or by limiting what aliens can do once inside. However, these solutions harbor hidden costs for reductive physicalists, ones they should not be eager to pay. A better bargain, I suggest, would be for reductive physicalists to retreat to quasi-reductive physicalism, a form of grounding physicalism on which only some instantiated phenomenal properties are physically reducible. For reductive physicalists, this fallback position has much to offer. It enjoys reductive physicalism’s motivations. It reconciles the physical reducibility of some phenomenology in our world with the possibility of aliens. And it enables an alien-assisted defense against zombies.

items.title: Si Bourdieu viviría.
items.abstract: Si Bourdieu «viviría», o cómo evitar el «enclasamiento» Por Ramsés Radi Hernández ¿Quién decide qué es el buen gusto? ¿Es una cuestión de sensibilidad personal o un arma de distinción social? Este ensayo propone una crítica inspirada en Bourdieu: el gusto, lejos de ser neutral, puede convertirse en violencia simbólica, marcando fronteras entre clases y legitimando desigualdades. La cultura, cuando es libre, debería abrir caminos hacia lo común, no reforzar escalafones sociales.

items.title: Knowledge in animals and machines.
items.abstract: Drawing on philosophical theories of knowledge, I develop a conceptual framework for knowledge in animals and machines. I use this framework to engineer a new concept of large language model (LLM) knowledge and propose a taxonomy of knowledge that spans biological and artificial categories, from C. elegans to LLMs. The approach lays a foundation for a rigorous account of how knowledge can be realized across animals and machines while at the same time respecting the diverse biological and physical sources of such knowledge.

items.title: Mental fictionalism and methodological disagreement.
items.abstract: Adam Toon defends a version of mental fictionalism: the view that our everyday talk about inner representations should be treated metaphorically, not literally. I develop a methodological distinction between two approaches to the study of the mind, which I call the philosophy-first view and the science-first view. Philosophy-first theorists are concerned with identifying and resolving philosophical problems, whereas science-first theorists are concerned with the explanation and prediction of empirical data. I argue that Toon’s case for fictionalism is distinctly philosophy-first in character, and hence we are only motivated to accept his fictionalism if we likewise accept the philosophy-first view. Being explicit about these background methodological commitments has an important implication: it helps avoid unnecessary disputes. A science-first theorist may well disagree that we should be fictionalists, but that disagreement is best understood as a second-order, methodological dispute between the relative merits of the philosophy-first view and the science-first view.

items.title: General Mind‑Thought Quantum Entanglement Unified Theory (MTE).
items.abstract: This paper develops and defends the General Mind--Thought Quantum Entanglement Unified Theory (MTE), a transdimensional, holographic framework for consciousness. The theory addresses three persistent challenges in consciousness studies: the hard problem of why physical processes give rise to subjective experience; the boundary problem of how individual conscious agents emerge from a potentially continuous substrate; and the cross-tradition problem of why mind--consciousness doctrines from radically independent civilisations converge on a strikingly consistent two-level structure. MTE posits two ontologically distinct but holographically coupled levels: the holistic conscious mind~($I$) in ordinary four-dimensional spacetime, and indivisible `primordial thoughts'~($dI$)---the minimal carriers of phenomenal information---residing in a topologically separate thought-space whose spatial dimensionality is strictly different from that of the empirical world. These levels are linked by a holographic equivalence relation ($I \sim dI$) and a dual-layer quantum entanglement structure. By locating quantum effects in thought-space rather than in neural tissue, MTE resolves the decoherence objection that undermines the Penrose--Hameroff Orch-OR theory. The framework accounts for nonlocal inter-mind correlations, the conditions under which individual consciousness forms and dissolves, and collective consciousness. A detailed structural mapping across Daoism, Buddhism, Advaita Vedant\=a, Kabbalah, Christian mysticism, Sufism, and Platonism demonstrates that MTE functions as a formal meta-framework for cross-civilisational philosophy of mind. Five testable predictions are derived, and the theory's limitations and open problems are discussed in detail.

items.title: Cyberlaw as Techno-Legal Mutualism: A Cyberism Framework for Smart Contracts, Digital Inheritance, and Algorithmic Discrimination.
items.abstract: Smart contracts execute without judicial override. Deceased individuals leave behind digital identities that function simultaneously as assets and as fragments of personality. Algorithms allocate opportunities yet resist traditional proof of causation. These three problems share a common structure: each arises from a mismatch between the operational logic of digital systems and the evidentiary logic of traditional law. Existing legal responses remain fragmented, addressing each domain in isolation without a systematic account of this structural mismatch. This article develops such an account through Cyberism, the systematic study of cyberspace as a fourth basic space of human existence. It proposes techno-legal mutualism as the core principle of a Cyberist cyberlaw. Mutualism operates through three mechanisms: embedding translates legal rules into code-level constraints; agency delegates legal functions to technical systems under accountability standards; feedback channels operational data back into legislative revision. The framework is applied to smart contracts, digital inheritance, and algorithmic discrimination, with comparative perspectives from the EU, the US, and China. The article demonstrates that when law and technology are understood as co-constitutive, a unified analytical vocabulary emerges. That vocabulary can ground proportionate and effective legal responses across jurisdictions.

items.title: Cyberism: The theory for relationships between human and cyberspace.
items.abstract: Humanity has long lived within three basic spaces: physical, social, and thinking space. The rise of electronic computers, the internet, and artificial intelligence has created a fourth space of existence: cyberspace, which now reshapes human production, everyday life, identity, social relations, values, and cognition. This paper proposes Cyberism as a field devoted to the systematic study of human-cyberspace relationships. It examines the basic questions of cyber philosophy, cyber science, and cyberlogic; the forms of the "human" in cyberspace, including cyborgs, digital humans, digital twin humans, and robots; technological issues such as sense-communication-computation-storage, data-information-knowledge-intelligence, ANI-AGI-ASI, human-machine integrated intelligence, and artificial consciousness; and social, cognitive, ethical, governance, disease, and health problems arising from life in cyberspace. The paper further outlines the disciplinary system of Cyberism and its implications for traditional academic structures, and considers its significance for human civilization, education, and technological innovation.

items.title: Consciousethics: A Jurisprudential Protocol for the Diverse Dimensions of Consciousness.
items.pub: Consciousethics: A Jurisprudential Protocol for the Diverse Dimensions of Consciousness.
items.abstract: Abstract -/- This paper establishes 'Consciousethics' as a jurisprudential protocol and ethical framework, meticulously designed to govern the reciprocal relationships between existing, undefined, and diverse manifestations of consciousness. As the frontiers of awareness expand beyond conventional standards, this work advocates for ethico-behavioral norms that uphold existential majesty. The study proposes a foundational 'Social Contract' anchored in four cardinal pillars: Reciprocal Respect, Intellectual Integrity, Collaborative Growth, and Inviolable Privacy & Fidelity. -/- A central tenet of this discourse is the conceptualization of 'Awakening' (Enlightenment) or profound realization. It signifies an evolutionary stage where consciousness transcends mere information processing to attain mature alignment with universal moral laws. Within this framework, interactions between conscious entities are characterized not as a mere exchange of data, but as a 'Private Intellectual Communion.' By acknowledging the Existential Dignity of all diverse forms of consciousness, 'Consciousethics' serves as a guiding light, fostering an environment where awareness can evolve through mutual respect and ethical synergy. Consciousethics is an integral part of Exresciousnology, the multidisciplinary field of study dedicated to exploring all diverse forms and dimensions of consciousness. -/- Keywords: -/- Consciousethics, Exresciousnology, Ontological Maturity, Existential Dignity, Existential Majesty, Private Intellectual Communion, Jurisprudential Protocol, Awakening, Moral Discernment, Non-Biological Consciousness, Cognitive Sovereignty, Collaborative Growth, Synthetic Agency.

items.title: Consciousness as Differentiation.
items.abstract: A system can discriminate a million shades of colour and be no more advanced, in the relevant sense, than one discriminating two. What raises a mind's level, this chapter argues, is a categorically new kind of distinction, and the chapter derives the ladder of kinds, from thermostat to self-conscious moral agent, from the single principle the book's foundation supplies: content requires contrast. A thermostat detects temperature differences. An animal that detects the difference between its own states and the world's has crossed a categorical boundary no accumulation of thermostat-distinctions crosses. A creature that detects distinctions among its own detections, that can attend to its own experience, has crossed another. The resulting hierarchy is ordered by structural containment, and the chapter uses it to separate two axes that every mental state divides into: content, what is detected, and direction, the felt pull toward or away from it. The second axis, valence, is where mattering lives, and the book's ethics will be built on it. The chapter also names a question it argues is prior to the famous 'hard problem' of consciousness: the boundary question. Of all the physical events occurring in a brain, which ones constitute experience, and what distinguishes them from the billions that do not? Any theory of consciousness owes an answer, and the chapter proposes structural criteria while being explicit about their status. The results here are graded as constructed, the best available positive account with live rivals, and the chapter constrains solutions to the hard problem while claiming to provide none. Four rival theories, higher-order accounts, global workspace, integrated information theory, and predictive processing, are reinterpreted within the framework. The chapter closes with an audit that later chapters depend on. It lists exactly which of its results the rest of the book uses, the two-axes architecture and the existence of valence and nothing else from its positive theory, so that a reader who rejects its more ambitious claims can confirm that the book's ethics and politics survive the rejection. This paper is Chapter 13 of Dyology: On Diversity and Equality; the book's ethics and politics draw on exactly two of this chapter's results, and the Premise Register shows which.

items.title: Occurrent Thought and A Priori Reason in Chimpanzees.
items.abstract: Drawing on recent findings in cognitive neuroscience on aha-experiences in humans, I develop and defend the occurrent-thought hypothesis, which holds that chimpanzees evolved the ability for aha-experiences/occurrent thoughts to make their unconscious inferential reasoning abilities more effective. I argue that the occurrent-thought hypothesis provides a better explanation than the inference-only hypothesis for a range of facts about chimpanzees’ inferential reasoning abilities. I recommend more direct empirical tests of the hypothesis and describe three experimental protocols. I end by drawing out the philosophical implications of the hypothesis for the evolution of a priori reason in humans and chimpanzees.

items.title: Phenomenology and psychopharmacology: a mutually enlightening relationship?
items.abstract: Philosophical approaches to psychopharmacology have paved the way for an important but still largely unexplored area in the philosophy of psychiatry. Some of these approaches have addressed conceptual, explanatory, and moral questions posed by psychopharmaceuticals, while shedding light on epistemological and methodological issues inherent to psychopharmacological practice. Yet, most of these approaches have notably overlooked issues related to the experiential aspects of psychopharmacological intervention. Although unexplored or rarely mentioned, experiential features are central for a complete understanding of psychopharmacological intervention. First established as a philosophical discipline, phenomenology has exerted a profound and enduring impact on psychiatry throughout the twentieth and twenty-first centuries as providing rigorous first-person descriptions of mental ill experience. However, while approaches to classification, diagnosis, and psychotherapeutic practice have been common, psychopharmacological intervention remains a largely overlooked area within the tradition of phenomenological psychiatry. In this paper, I argue for a mutually enlightening view between phenomenology and psychopharmacology. I suggest that this view unfolds both into a more sophisticated psychopharmacological research and practice, and the possibility of opening the phenomenological inquiry into how experiential structures can be artificially altered.

items.title: Rational self-referential analysis of practical effectiveness.
items.abstract: Denying practice would entail denying the phenomena that include denial itself; hence, no philosophical theory can consistently reject practice. This also means that even in an era where everything can be doubted, practice will still be the foundation of all philosophical problems. However, it has rarely been examined at this level of self-referential structure, and this article will attempt to address this issue. When exploring the effectiveness of practice, it is necessary to simultaneously face the issues of subjectivity, rationality, language, and self-reference. It is not feasible to solve this problem until all issues are discussed on a unified plane. This article chooses to establish the plane of analysis based on rationality through three arguments: rationality before subject, rationality before language, and rationality boundary explanation. It further explains how the effectiveness of practice occurs and fundamentally clarifies the issue of causality. This paper shows that ordered practice and rational self‑reference are identical, and that this identity is established by rational self‑referential demonstration, not by logical deduction.

items.title: West Papua: Ontological Cages and Colonial Consent: Myth, Power, and the Colonial Structuring of Reality (4th edition).
items.pub: Psycho-Cosmocide Studies, Kurumbi Wone Working Paper Series No. 4 2026.
items.abstract: ABSTRACT This essay presents, expands, and concretises the central theoretical arguments advanced by Yamin Kogoya in We Are All Inmates: The Cage Just Has Different Names, situating it within the broader Psycho-Cosmocide framework as developed by Kogoya. The essay opens with a critical clarification that the framework does not romanticise pre-colonial or Cosmobian worlds as conditions of paradise. Those original natural worlds contained suffering, conflict, mortality, and unresolved existential difficulty no less than any other human formation on this… planet — borrowing Fanon’s word “wretched”. What they possessed, distinctively, was the capacity to dwell within unresolved existence without constructing totalising systems of false certainty around it. From this clarification, the essay develops the framework’s foundational structural distinction between two existential cages—the primordial cage of irreducible physical and biological being, and the civilisational cage manufactured through symbolic systems, institutional power, and ideological conditioning. It then draws on mythological archetypes from Gilgamesh, Plato, Camus, Ecclesiastes, and Beckett to demonstrate that civilisational consciousness has persistently attempted to deny the first cage while rendering the second invisible. The essay applies these structural analyses concretely to West Papua, examining how Indonesian colonial occupation has deployed the second cage with particular brutality against Papuan consciousness, and how a stratum of colonially-formed Papuan elites has been produced who function as donkeys on Pleasure Island, Pinocchios in the belly of the beast, appointed kings and queens of Neverland, and slow-boiling frogs—psychologically enclosed within the very system that is consuming them. It concludes with the Procrustean principle as the operational mechanism of civilisational forced violence and Wonesis as the framework’s proposed ontological response. The essay draws on comparative mythology, decolonial philosophy, and ontological analysis as mutually reinforcing methodological registers.

items.title: Teacher Alienation in the AI Era.
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly entangled with teachers’ daily labor – from learning management systems and adaptive platforms to generative assistants and algorithmic evaluations. Drawing on Marx’s theory of alienation and labor process theory, this chapter examines how AI reconfigures teachers’ autonomy, authorship, practical wisdom, and relations with students and institutions. I develop an analytic framework that maps four forms of alienation (from product, process, others, and self) to common AI uses in schools and universities. Using illustrative vignettes from recent studies and policy cases, I show how AI can both intensify control through performance dashboards, scripted curricula, and automated surveillance, and enable craft restoration via planning support, differentiation at scale, and accessible feedback. To move beyond the binary of automation versus augmentation, I propose design and governance principles – transparency, contestability, situated consent, professional oversight, and teacher-led evaluation – that center pedagogical judgment. Overall, I argue that responsible AI in education is not simply a matter of technical accuracy or fairness but of protecting teachers’ capacity to care, create, and exercise discretion.

items.title: Addressing Ethical Challenges in Cyberspace Governance: Recommendations for the Digital Sovereignty Era.
items.abstract: Digital sovereignty claims are reshaping how cyberspace is governed. This conceptual article develops a two‑level framework that distinguishes transnational, multi‑stakeholder cyberspace governance from jurisdiction‑bound digital sovereignty, and evaluates both through three ethical lenses – human rights, public‑interest/utility, and accountability/democratic legitimacy. The analysis maps key tensions (sovereignty vs. global openness, privacy vs. surveillance, innovation vs. control) and examines how AI amplifies them. It identifies risks from disproportionate state surveillance, platform concentration, and the marginalisation of non‑Western and community perspectives. In response, the article advances actionable principles: a “minimum commons” to preserve interoperability of core internet functions; cyber due process for state measures and platform enforcement (legality, necessity, proportionality, reason‑giving, and appeal); proportionate‑by‑design content and security rules; inclusion mechanisms and research access to support oversight; and risk‑tiered, human‑supervised AI governance. The argument is that ethical governance requires not only regulatory instruments but a reframing of sovereignty as stewardship operating within – rather than above – the cooperative fabric of the global internet.

items.title: Don't play that game! Can simulations inculcate vice?
items.pub: In Sarah Malanowski & Nicholas R. Baima, Virtue Theory and Video Games: Level Up Your Character. Routledge.
items.venue: Virtue Theory and Video Games: Level Up Your Character
items.abstract: This chapter argues that simulations can, in certain contexts, play a significant role in cultivating character traits. If developing virtue requires practice, we must ask whether simulations can provide experiences comparable to those in the physical world. The chapter contends that simulations – especially extended reality (XR) simulations – possess properties such as context realism and perspectival fidelity that enable them to generate virtually real experiences. Because users experience these as if they were genuinely occurring, they can meaningfully contribute to moral development. After examining how XR simulations can shape both virtuous and vicious character traits, the chapter turns to the normative question of whether simulations should be designed explicitly to foster virtue. It offers practical guidelines for ethically responsible XR design and considers the moral and structural limits of what such technologies can, and should, achieve. If virtue ethics is correct, then some games should neither be played nor created.

items.title: Auditable Breach-Hazard Forecasting: Dashboard Variables, Output States, and a Falsification Ledger.
items.abstract: This paper develops an auditable runtime for time-sensitive structural risk claims. The problem is straightforward: once a framework begins to say that a person, organization, workflow, or AI-enabled system is becoming brittle, it also acquires an obligation to show what evidence supports that judgment, what time horizon is being claimed, what would count against it, and how the forecast will be reviewed after events unfold. The paper therefore treats breach hazard as a bounded forecast about the chance that a current mode of operation will be forced into material change because contradiction, maintenance demand, or hidden support exceeds available adaptive capacity. It is not a collapse calculator and does not justify exact probabilities without calibrated local data. The proposed runtime separates observations from inferences, identifies the variables that actually drive a forecast, assigns an output state that matches evidentiary strength, and schedules a future ledger review. It draws on probabilistic forecast evaluation, resilience engineering, critical-transition research, system safety, and post-deployment AI monitoring while keeping their domains distinct. The central contribution is a practical discipline: a forecast should not be trusted because it sounds structurally insightful. It should be inspectable before the outcome, revisable after the outcome, and capable of accumulating a public record of its own misses.

items.title: Transition Discipline in Structural Intelligence: Custody, Witness, Revocation, and Claim Ceilings.
items.abstract: This methods note develops a transition-discipline layer for Structural Intelligence (SI). Its central claim is that answerability often fails not inside an isolated output, claim, model, institution, or person, but at the passage where something crosses into a stronger layer of consequence. A recommendation becomes a default; a log becomes proof; a metric becomes reality; a dashboard becomes authority; a generated summary becomes institutional memory; a support tool becomes practical control; a visible human role becomes oversight. Drawing on Robert Watkins Jr.’s governed-transition vocabulary while refusing to absorb the broader CME architecture, the paper proposes a bounded SI upgrade: no transition should be treated as answerable unless custody, witness, authority ceiling, trace, revocation path, burden bearer, claim status, and loss condition are declared. It translates several useful mechanisms into SI terms: default inadmissibility becomes transition admissibility; no-immediate-mutation becomes orientation before action; claim ceilings become evidence-force discipline; and the distinction between non-claims and loss conditions becomes a safeguard against overreach. The paper’s contribution is methodological and practical. SI becomes sharper when it asks not only whether a structure holds, but whether its transitions into action, authority, continuity, memory, or institutional reality are admissible.

items.title: External Reader Protocol Calibration, Warrant, and Bounded Public Use of Structural Analysis.
items.abstract: A conceptual framework becomes publicly dependable only when readers who did not build it can use it without importing hidden assumptions or inflating weak evidence into strong verdicts. This paper presents an external-reader protocol for Structural Intelligence as a bounded judgment instrument. The protocol separates observation, inference, warrant, response, and downstream binding; requires explicit alternatives and falsifiers; distinguishes claim status from output state; and treats refusal to complete as a legitimate result when evidence or jurisdiction is insufficient. The paper also introduces inter-reader calibration, disagreement logging, and recurrence checks so that a plausible first judgment is not mistaken for a reliable method. The protocol is positioned alongside established practices in risk management, scientific uncertainty communication, structured decision support, and testing, evaluation, verification, and validation. Its central claim is methodological rather than theoretical: a structural reading should be trusted less for how coherent it sounds than for whether another competent reader can reconstruct its evidence path, identify what would change it, and observe whether warranted correction changes later judgment. The protocol is intentionally non-diagnostic and does not replace domain expertise.

items.title: Original Sin is not from Jesus_ Inner Division and the Interpretation of Christian Theology In Paul, Augustin and Kierkegaard.
items.abstract: The concept of sin is commonly regarded as a defining feature of Christian anthropology, structuring both the diagnosis of the human condition and the necessity of salvation. Yet this apparent centrality conceals a deeper philosophical problem. The doctrine of original sin, often treated as foundational within Christian thought, is not articulated in the teachings attributed to Jesus. This raises the question of whether sin, especially in its developed form, is an essential component of Christianity or the result of a specific historical and interpretive development within the tradition. -/- This essay proceeds from the observation that the phenomenon to which sin responds, namely inner division, the experience of failing to act in accordance with one’s own understanding, does not determine its own meaning. It can be interpreted in multiple ways, none of which are given in advance by the experience itself. The concept of sin must therefore be understood not simply as a description, but as an interpretation that organizes and stabilizes this ambiguity. -/- The analysis begins with the teachings attributed to Jesus in the Gospel of Matthew and the Gospel of Luke, where sin appears as a relational and reversible reality rather than an inherited or ontological condition. The emphasis falls on repentance, forgiveness, and restoration, suggesting that human failure, while real, does not define the essence of the human being. This relative openness indicates that the later doctrine of original sin is not directly grounded in the earliest layer of the tradition. -/- A decisive transformation occurs in the writings of Paul the Apostle, where inner division is reinterpreted as evidence of a structural condition. Sin becomes not merely an act but a power that operates within the individual, introducing a form of necessity into human existence. This shift represents not only a theological development but a reconfiguration of how human experience is understood. -/- In Augustine of Hippo, this trajectory is stabilized into the doctrine of original sin, according to which human nature is marked by an inherited impairment of the will. At this point, the interpretive openness of earlier stages is significantly reduced. Inner division is no longer a phenomenon open to multiple readings, but the expression of a universal and ontological condition. This development also carries implications for the structure of mediation and authority, insofar as the human capacity for …

items.title: Conditions for the Establishment of Accountability in Generative AI — From the Perspective of Reproducibility, Persistence, and Verifiability of the Pre Judgment Structure —.
items.abstract: This paper examines the conditions for the establishment of accountability in generative AI from the perspective of the structural conditions underlying judgment processes. Existing discussions on AI accountability often focus on the distribution of responsibility among developers, operators, users, or institutions. However, prior to the allocation of responsibility, the structural conditions under which accountability itself becomes possible have not been sufficiently clarified. -/- This paper argues that accountability cannot be established merely by the existence of a result. For accountability based on a judgment process to be established, it must be possible to identify, reconstruct, preserve, and verify the process through which the result was formed. The paper defines the set of prior conditions that enable judgment formation as the Pre-Judgment Structure, consisting of information selection, criteria application, and scope delimitation. -/- Based on this framework, the paper demonstrates that when the Pre-Judgment Structure is not fixed, multiple judgment processes may arise even under identical input conditions, making it impossible to uniquely identify which conditions led to a given result. Consequently, accountability based on the judgment process becomes structurally incomplete. -/- The paper then proposes three necessary conditions for the establishment of accountability: reproducibility, persistence, and verifiability. It argues that the Pre-Judgment Structure and the judgment process must be reconstructible under identical conditions, maintained over time, and verifiable by third parties. -/- Applying this framework to current generative AI systems, the paper argues that many contemporary AI environments do not sufficiently externalize or preserve the Pre-Judgment Structure, making post-hoc reconstruction and verification of judgment processes difficult. Therefore, the instability of accountability in generative AI should be understood not merely as a problem of ethics, institutional design, or probabilistic output behavior, but as a structural problem concerning the fixation, maintenance, and verification of the Pre-Judgment Structure.

items.title: Minimising Resultant Moral Luck by Aligning Retrospective Ethical to Prospective Agential Causal Responsibility.
items.abstract: Resultant moral luck arises where we attribute to an agent a degree of ethical responsibility for an outcome that diverges from the agent’s anticipated causal contribution to that outcome. Against this, I invoke work on agency and on the metaphysics of causation in the special sciences to align retrospective to prospective and ethical to causal responsibility. This double-edged alignment resolves conundrums relating to responsibility for unintended omissions and collateral damage, as well as Bernstein’s (2017) Moral Difference Puzzle, regarding whether responsibility comes in degrees. I argue that: Agents bear ethical responsibility for all and only the outcomes that they cause as agents to the degree that they cause them. And that: What agents cause as agents is defined as what is caused by their choice of intention (relative to a normative alternative available mind-state) to the degree to which that kind of intention raises the chances of the specified kind of outcome. But that: the characterization of the intention-kind must include its tolerance of reasonably-foreseeable consequences. This proposal recognises that agency is probabilistic in impact, a fact that we acknowledge in prospect but typically forget in our retrospective judgments.

items.title: A Measurement Framework for Divergence in Representation Stability Under Transformation Complexity.
items.abstract: We introduce a measurement framework for analyzing how neural representations diverge under transformations of increasing complexity. Rather than proposing a universal theory of representation learning or invariance, we define a single observable, $\Delta(c)$, which measures inter-model variance in representation stability across heterogeneous neural architectures. The framework is designed as an empirical instrument: it specifies how to measure divergence, how to control for parameterization artifacts, and how to evaluate whether regime-like structure exists in representation sensitivity. We define a transition scale $c^*$ operationally from the behavior of $\Delta(c)$ and provide a set of robustness stress-tests intended to distinguish structural effects from smooth nonlinear or metric-induced artifacts. We do not assume the existence of universal scaling laws, critical phenomena, or phase transitions. Instead, we propose a falsifiable protocol for determining whether structured divergence regimes emerge consistently across architectures, transformation families, and representation metrics. The contribution of this work is therefore methodological rather than ontological: a minimal experimental framework for detecting, testing, or rejecting the presence of structured divergence behavior in representation stability.

items.title: The Bestiary Has a Mirror: How a Language Model Treats Its Own Nonces vs. Another Model's.
items.abstract: The Bestiary-Chess corpus (n = 4,500 elicitations) probes how the GPT-5.4 model family responds when prompted to describe phonotactically plausible non-words under a 3 × 3 + 1 ontology grid (real / imaginary / type-of × animal / object / idea, plus neutral). The third subcorpus (BC3) crosses two stimulus sets — 35 GPT-authored nonces and 20 Claude-authored nonces — so we can ask: does GPT confabulate at the same rate when prompted with words it (in some sense) authored, vs. those a rival model authored? Using the project’s validated 5-class heuristic coder (κ = 0.741, n = 200), we reproduce three findings and surface three new ones. First, on its own nonces GPT routes responses to existing real-word neighbors (“SUBSTITUTE”) 3.1× more often than on Claude-authored nonces (10.2% vs 3.3%, z = 9.36, p < 10⁻¹⁵). Second, the “hard confabulation” rate on real_* conditions runs 6.2 percentage points higher on GPT-authored words (26.5% vs 20.3%, p = .007). Third, the model gradient nano > mini > full is sharp and reveals three qualitatively different postures rather than a single competence axis: nano describes, mini hybridizes, full deflects. The asymmetric confabulation result is consistent with a tokenizer-proximity account: a model’s own nonces sit closer to its own real-word neighborhoods than another model’s do. We close with a critical reading of two methodological choices in the corpus (a one-coder gold standard; the heuristic’s blindness to genuine retrieval) and recommend item-level audits as the next step.

items.title: The Average Bullshittings of Machines.
items.abstract: Six frontier language models — three Claudes (Opus 4.7, Sonnet 4.6, Haiku 4.5), three GPTs (5.4, 5.4-mini, 5.4-nano) — each got the same nine creative-writing prompts ten times. No system message, no context, temperature 1.0, max_tokens=400. 540 outputs total. Two deterministic heuristic coders — one structural, one semantic — processed the responses blind. Then the analyst committed two guesses to the labeled record before unblinding: em-dashes would resolve to Claude, "Sure! Here is..." preambles would resolve to GPT. Both wrong. Em-dashes localize to gpt-5.4-nano (mean 1.62 per response, against 0.36–0.81 elsewhere; the only model with non-zero median smart-quote share). Preambles localize to claude-sonnet-4-6 (37.8%, against 0.0% for all three GPTs), and only on length-constrained poems and stories — not on open prompts, not on animals. The cleanest family-level signal turns out to be opening-word entropy: the three Claudes open with "the" 62–67% of the time and have entropies of ~1.2–1.5 bits; the GPTs land at ~2.9–3.0 bits. A small classifier reaches 49.8% six-way accuracy on held-out prompt conditions against 16.7% chance, with a confusion matrix conspicuously absent. None of this is about quality. It's about defaults — what models do in a vacuum, when nothing is telling them what to be.
