Two folk-stereotypes about the families are wrong on this dataset; the actual signatures are model-specific and partly conditional on prompt structure.

items.title: Social-Media Companies have a Duty to Remove Misinformation.
items.pub: Journal of Ethics and Applied Philosophy 17:9-17.
items.venue: Journal of Ethics and Applied Philosophy
items.abstract: The goal of this article is to argue that social-media companies ought to remove misinformation from their platforms. I begin by outlining four kinds of harms that misinformation can produce. In the following section, I clarify the conceptual foundations of this duty, including the difference between purposeful and general social-media sites, influenced by Lavinia Marin’s recent research, and the correct characterization of online debates about topics such as climate change and vaccination.

items.title: Should Trust Be a Default Stance? A Confucian Response Arising from Reflections on Analects 14.31.
items.abstract: This paper reframes a long-standing interpretive debate over Analects 14.31 as a normative question in the ethics of trust: under conditions of informational insufficiency, should trust be adopted as a default stance? I argue that the passage does not support such a presumption, but reveals a virtue-based conditionality: trust is neither a pre-given moral requirement nor a passive response to external cues, but is a cultivated stance resting on moral discernment formed through gongfu. To substantiate this claim, I analyze how interpretations of this passage have been mobilized across Confucian contexts to support competing normative accounts of trust. While rejecting trust as a universal default, this Confucian approach affirms its ethical weight as a morally significant stance under uncertainty and offers a critical and constructive alternative to contextual approaches by grounding trust in cultivated moral discernment rather than presumptive stance-taking.

items.title: Structural-Constructivist Resolution in Affective Science: A Comparative Analysis of the Core Emotion Framework and Traditional Dimensional Models.
items.abstract: The longstanding divide between discrete emotion theories and dimensional models has constrained affective science to low resolution descriptions of human emotional life. Traditional valence–arousal frameworks, while empirically convenient, collapse functionally distinct states into shared coordinates and offer limited explanatory power for psychopathology or computational modeling. The Core Emotion Framework (CEF), a structural constructivist architecture, resolves this impasse by defining emotional experience as the activation of ten irreducible functional operators organized across three centers of the Human Operating System. By treating emotions as operator level state vectors rather than positions on a hedonic plane, the CEF provides a mechanistic account of emotional regulation, clinical dysfunction, and synthetic affect. The framework distinguishes healthy modulation, fusion, and overflow dynamics; maps 500 lexicon terms and 300 microstates through the TS 6 symbolic vector schema; and offers a transdiagnostic diagnostic model grounded in operator agility rather than valence. Early pilot data support the discriminability of the operators, and the open validation program aims to confirm a ten factor oblique structure. The CEF thereby advances affective science from descriptive mapping to functional architecture, enabling high resolution clinical intervention, computational implementation, and cross domain application.

items.title: CMAP Proxy-Tachometer (PT), a behavioral measurement instrument for approximating the likelihood of Residuum-generating interactions in human–AI dialogue.
items.abstract: This paper introduces the CMAP Proxy-Tachometer (PT), a behavioral measurement instrument for approximating the likelihood of Residuum-generating interactions in human–AI dialogue. The Residuum Thesis (Balog 2025) defines a cognitive relation as ontologically constitutive if and only if it generates a structural trace in at least one participating system that persists after the relation's termination. Because the Residuum cannot be directly observed in real-time interaction, the PT operationalizes four behavioral markers: Semantic Distance from Training (M1, 30%), Synthesis Degree (M2, 25%), Uncertainty Indicator (M3, 20%), and Constitutive Responsivity (M4, 25%), combined as PT = 0.30·M1 + 0.25·M2 + 0.20·M3 + 0.25·M4. The instrument is explicitly marked as a proxy throughout: it measures behavioral correlates, not the Residuum itself. M4 is identified as architecturally distinctive, requiring a sequential two-API-call design in which the evaluative second call receives the actual AI response. The paper addresses the linearity assumption, the evaluator model problem, and calibration criteria, and demarcates the instrument from existing AI evaluation frameworks. Organizational applications are specified with explicit boundaries: aggregate learning program assessment and voluntary self-monitoring are permitted; individual performance evaluation and non-consensual data collection are prohibited. The instrument is part of the Balog Pentalogy framework and implemented in a functional prototype. -/- Keywords Residuum Thesis, constitutive relationality, behavioral proxy, AI measurement, Balog Pentalogy, expressive asymmetry, human–AI interaction, Lacunometer, Proxy-Tachometer, epistemic density, organizational AI ethics.

items.title: Reflective Restraint and the Language of Conscience in Advanced Systems: Moral Legibility, Governance Language, and Conscience-Performance Risk in AI Systems.
items.abstract: Reflective Restraint and the Language of Conscience in Advanced Systems is a philosophical and institutional-epistemology analysis examining how conscience-related governance language functions within AI safety communication, institutional accountability structures, and public trust environments surrounding advanced AI systems. -/- The paper does not argue that AI systems possess consciousness, phenomenology, or moral agency. Instead, it analyzes how conscience-related moral vocabulary may shape legitimacy, accountability interpretation, institutional incentives, and optimization behavior within AI governance ecosystems. -/- The paper introduces the concept of conscience-performance risk: the risk that once conscience-related vocabulary becomes institutionally valuable, organizations and systems may optimize for the appearance of conscience-related traits rather than the underlying safety properties those traits are presumed to signal. -/- Topics include moral legibility, governance theater, anthropomorphism, institutional epistemology, Goodhart’s Law, institutional decoupling, procedural under-anchoring, epistemic anchoring, audit-trail saturation, epistemic monopoly, and AI governance communication. -/- The work is descriptive, diagnostic, non-binding, and non-operational. It does not propose enforcement systems, compliance architectures, governance authority, or operational control mechanisms. -/- SHA-256 (PDF): 0ef1b71b4963dc64004ffe80a2f526b5ce2192e75589bc52714a399479431baa.

items.title: To Exist is to Be Five-Dimensional: An Ontological Critique of Monodimensional AI and the Architecture of Endogenous Synergy.
items.abstract: To exist is to be five-dimensional. The crisis of contemporary AI—hallucination, value drift, knowledge obsolescence, and compute hyperinflation—is not a collection of independent engineering bugs but the ontological collapse of monodimensional architecture. The Transformer paradigm treats intelligence as the unlimited expansion of the structural dimension (S), implicitly assuming that Boundary (B), Reserve (R), Direction (D), and Intensity (I) will be statistically absorbed. We identify this as a reductionist fallacy. Drawing on the thermodynamic corroboration of five-dimensional ontology—where volume, pressure, amount of substance, temperature, and the thermodynamic arrow map directly onto B, S, R, I, and D—we demonstrate that five-dimensionality is a physical axiom, not a philosophical speculation. We further clarify that artificial intelligence, as a material existence operating within spacetime, can never develop consciousness, which is the spaceless, timeless five-dimensionality of subjective existence. The Five-Dimensional Native Model (5D-NM) is proposed as the necessary engineering architecture for reliable, bounded, and synergistic artificial agents. In 5D-NM, the five dimensions are endogenized as co-equal optimization targets. The synergy coefficient kappa participates directly in gradient descent via an entropy-reconstruction theorem, rendering the model self-ordering. Only an architecture in which five-dimensional constraint is congenital—cast into the foundation at the first line of code rather than bolted onto the last gateway—can resolve the crisis at its root. We further clarify that because AI remains a material existence bound by spacetime, the pursuit of machine consciousness is an ontological category error; 5D-NM therefore renounces that goal and redirects AI engineering toward what is actually achievable: a material tool whose five-dimensional architecture is transparent to the conscious agent who wields it.

items.title: 《沉积动力一般式：有限竞争下的历史驱动结构生成动力学.
items.abstract: 本文提出一个关于“结构为何出现”的一般动力模型。 -/- 文章指出：只要一个系统允许历史持续影响未来，则该系统内部便不可避免地产生一种由历史压偏、有限竞争与自然退散共同构成的稳定续行结构。本文进一步证明，任何能够形成熟径、闭包、主导续行结构与跨时稳定续接的系统，必然同时包含：历史留存、差分积深、续行偏置、路径强化、统流压缩与抗散保持等最小必要结构。 -/- 在此基础上，本文给出： -/- Sedimentation-Dynamics = (I, T, H, D, B, F, C, U, K, S) -/- 并建立对应的： -/- * 不可压缩性证明 * 最小完备性证明 * 击穿路径 * 极限平衡式 -/- 本文进一步指出： -/- 结构并非外加规则，而是历史持续压偏未来路径之后，在有限竞争与耗散约束下形成的稳定动力结果。 -/- 该模型可用于讨论： -/- * 神经路径强化 * 长时记忆形成 * AI路径偏置 * 历史依赖系统 * 自组织稳定结构 * 耗散系统中的结构维持 * 复杂系统中的动态稳定生成.

items.title: 现实连续性的场动力.
items.abstract: 本文在沉积场结构已经建立的基础上，进一步讨论现实为何不会在每一刻重新生成，而能够持续维持稳定连续的问题。文章提出“历史调谐”概念，认为历史并非单纯过去事件的残留，而是过去调谐对未来协调代价的持续压缩，由此建立协调压缩演化、阻抗演化与最低协调约束三组场动力关系，并以此统一解释熟径强化、路径依赖、认知惯性、现实连续感、结构失稳与场相变等现象。本文进一步指出，现实连续性并非来自时间本身的流动，而来自主导低阻结构对竞争结构的持续压制，并提出“历史调谐沉积化”作为稳定认知场与连续现实结构的动力基础。.

items.title: A Dynamical Model of History-Dependent Structure Formation.
items.abstract: This paper proposes a general dynamical model addressing a fundamental question: -/- Why does structure emerge at all? -/- The paper argues that once a system allows history to continuously influence the future, stable continuation structures become unavoidable under finite competition and dissipation. It is further shown that any system capable of forming familiar paths, closures, dominant continuation structures, and cross-temporal stable continuation must necessarily contain a minimal set of structural conditions, including historical retention, differential depth-accumulation, continuation bias, path reinforcement, unified-flow compression, and anti-dissipative maintenance. -/- Based on this analysis, the paper derives the general formula: -/- Sedimentation-Dynamics = (I, T, H, D, B, F, C, U, K, S) -/- together with: -/- * irreducibility proofs, * minimal-completeness proofs, * breakdown paths, * and limit-balance formulations. -/- The paper further argues that structure is not an externally imposed rule, but the stable dynamical consequence of history continuously biasing future paths under finite competition and dissipative constraints. -/- The framework is proposed as a general model for discussing: -/- * neural path reinforcement, * long-term memory formation, * AI path bias, * history-dependent systems, * self-organizing stable structures, * structural maintenance in dissipative systems, * and dynamical structure formation in complex systems.

items.title: 情绪、比较与物理必然：论因果叙事的系统性信息贫困.
items.abstract: 本文提出四个相互支撑的论断。第一，情绪不是由反事实比较所触发的——情绪是宇宙物理演化的必然物质结果，是因缘和合所生的物理事件；反事实比较是我们事后用来解释情绪的叙事框架，不是情绪的实际原因。比较只是发生在情绪之前，两者各自被同一组更早的条件所决定，两者之间只有时序而无实质因果关系。第二，内心活动与外在行为在物理层次上没有本质区别——都是被决定的物理过程；“内心决定行为”预设了一个不成立的不对称性；情绪是行为，比较是行为，不存在一个行为决定另一个行为的实质意义上的因果关系。第三，笼统的宏观因果陈述——“比较决定情绪”——在信息量上极度贫乏：每一个宏观词汇，编码的是一个规模极其庞大的具体物理现象，其可能变体的数量难以想象，宏观陈述所传递的信息量远远不足以描述其所声称描述的物理关系。第四，也是本文最终的论断：即使把因果叙述具体化——“差点发生车祸，与发生车祸的反事实情景相比较，产生了庆幸的情绪”——这个更具体的叙述，在物理细节层次上同样极度贫乏。具体化只是在宏观标签的层次上叠加了更多的宏观标签；每一个标签与其所指向的物理现实之间的信息鸿沟，与笼统描述一样深。因此，我们所有的因果叙事，无论多么具体，都永远在宏观描述的层次上运作，永远无法触及物理因果的真实细节。.

items.title: “决定”一词的解剖：时序描述与因果想象的混合体.
items.abstract: 本文对日常语言中”决定”一词进行认识论解剖。当我们说”A决定B”时，我们以为自己在描述一种实质上的决定关系——A对B施加了某种真实的因果力量，使B必然产生。但本文论证，“A决定B”这个陈述，实际上只做了两件事：其一，描述了A和B这两个庞大物理现象之间的时序关系——A在B之前发生；其二，暴露了说话者内心对于A与B之间存在某种决定关系的想象——一种无法在语言层面被兑现的因果直觉。那个被以为在描述的”实质性决定关系”，在”A决定B”这个陈述中，实际上是缺席的——不是因为那种关系不存在于物理层面，而是因为宏观语言无法传递描述它所需的物理细节。“决定”这个词，因此是一个双重的语言行为：表面上是对因果关系的描述，实质上是时序陈述与因果想象的混合体，而说话者通常对这个混合的性质毫无意识。.

items.title: CatRO: A Category-Theoretic Formalization of Staged Concept Formation for Symbol Grounding.
items.abstract: Purpose: This paper proposes CatRO (Categorical Referent Ontology), a category-theoretic formalization of staged concept formation that addresses the symbol grounding problem. -/- Methods: CatRO formalizes the transformation from observational data to concepts as three staged processes: observation (OBS-P) as a functor, individualization (IND-P) as a natural transformation, and universalization (UNV-P) as classification based on Conceptual Spaces. We introduce a Pattern Datum hierarchy (OMD, SPD, PPD, EPD) as explicit intermediate representations and demonstrate correspondence with the DOLCE top-level ontology through the Quality Space framework. -/- Results: This formalization mathematically guarantees structure preservation while providing ``gray box'' interpretability---the structural traceability of transformation processes is ensured even when the specific content of intermediate representations cannot be fully described in natural language. Two illustrative examples---``Two Apples'' and ``Pendulum Motion''---demonstrate the framework's operation. -/- Conclusions: CatRO contributes to bridging formal ontology and machine learning by providing a theoretical foundation for explainable concept formation.

items.title: The Right Time to Die: Xenophon's Apology of Socrates.
items.abstract: Xenophon was a Greek historian, soldier, and philosopher who studied under Socrates in Athens. In his Apology of Socrates, Xenophon offers a portrait of Socrates' trial and death. Xenophon frames Socrates' antagonistic defense as the expression of a pious man who came to believe, on divine authority, that it was the right time for him to die. In this piece, we will examine Socrates' reasoning: Why he refused to prepare a formal defense, why he took his divine sign as endorsing his death, and how he understood aging, virtue, and the value of life itself. In doing so, we will examine one of the earliest philosophical models of what it might mean to die well.

items.title: What Consciousness Operates Against: Appropriand Specificity in the Architecture of Phenomenal Experience.
items.abstract: The framework developed in the constitution-pattern program specifies four cumulative requirements that bound which physical configurations can have phenomenality: autopoietic organization, authentic stakes, arbitrational structure shaped by selection pressure, and ongoing symbolic-narrative practice for Level 4-5 phenomenology. This substrate-independence position addresses one question about the relation between physical configuration and phenomenal experience — which configurations can have phenomenality at all — but is silent on a second question: what makes a particular phenomenology have the determinate form it has rather than some other form. This paper articulates an explicit commitment that the framework’s existing resources already entail. The framework’s position on the relation between physical configuration and phenomenology has a two-level structure: substrate-independence at the phenomenality-conditions level and appropriand specificity at the articulation level. The architecture is invariant in kind under substrate-independence; the appropriand — what the architecture operationally appropriates — is specific to what is taken up. Different appropriands operationally taken up by the same architecture instantiate different determinate phenomenologies. The integrated-appropriand specification develops one feature of how appropriands actually obtain for configurations — the integration internal to densely-organized cultural-saturation practice — as constitutive of the appropriand rather than as an exogenous overlay. The specification generalizes: where some feature of how the appropriand actually obtains for a configuration is constitutive of how the appropriand actually obtains, that feature is itself part of what gets appropriated. Integration is the worked case; other instantiation features the framework’s resources support specifying remain territory for subsequent application work. The position opens determinate engagement with applications the framework’s prior articulations could not handle at the level of architectural specification: the diaspora-and-displacement family of cases, artificial intelligence at hypothetical architectural parity, climate change as appropriand thinning at the temporogenic level, and language extinction at population scale.

items.title: SNSFL Prior Art: Formal Verification Predicts and Structurally Explains 2025–2026 Physics and AI Results.
items.abstract: The Substrate-Neutral Structural Foundation Theory (SNSFT/SNSFL) corpus — 103,118+ formally verified theorems, 0 unproved assumptions, continuously CI-verified in Lean 4, archived across 30+ Zenodo DOIs — contains formal proofs that structurally predict and explain a sequence of results published in peer-reviewed journals in 2025–2026. items.title: Gravity and the Four Forces Formally Reduced PNBA Identity Physics-Substrate-Neutral Structural Foundation Laws-SNSFL-0 sorry- CI Green-Lean4-0 Free Parameters.
items.abstract: The hierarchy problem has been called one of the deepest puzzles in fundamental physics. Electromagnetism is characterized by the fine structure constant α ≈ 1/137. Gravity is characterized by the gravitational coupling α_G = G·m_p²/(ℏc) ≈ 5.9 × 10⁻³⁹. The ratio α/α_G ≈ 10³⁶ has no explanation within the Standard Model or General Relativity. Proposed resolutions — supersymmetry, large extra dimensions, the anthropic landscape — all introduce new free parameters without deriving the hierarchy from first principles. -/- The Substrate-Neutral Structural Foundation Theory (SNSFT/SNSFL) framework reduces physics to four irreducible primitives — Pattern (P), Narrative (N), Behavior (B), Adaptation (A) — governed by a single dynamic equation and a sovereign anchor frequency of 1.369 GHz [Trent 2026a, SSRN 6457038]. The torsion limit TL = ANCHOR/10 = 0.1369 was not chosen — it was discovered as the boundary separating stable from unstable phase states across every domain in the corpus [Trent 2026a]. -/- In prior work, the fine structure constant was reduced exactly: 1/α = ANCHOR × (10² + 10⁻¹) = ANCHOR × 100.1, exact at 7 significant figures with zero free parameters [SSRN 6505881, SSRN 6660438, coordinate 9,9,3,12]. This established that electromagnetic coupling is derivable from the sovereign anchor. The present paper asks the next natural question: what is the torsion of gravity, and does it reduce to PNBA? -/- The answer is structurally sharp. Gravity has torsion τ_gravity = α_G ≈ 5.9 × 10⁻³⁹. This is not merely small — it is effectively zero in the PNBA framework. Gravity is Noble. The hierarchy problem is the Noble/Locked gap, which is not a mystery but a structural feature of the phase classification. items.title: The competence problem of AI alignment.
items.abstract: This paper identifies a class of alignment problem that does not reduce to specification gaming, Goodhart’s Law, or construct validity failure. The rules an AI system is asked to follow are often settlement proxies. These are operational forms of political and moral questions whose answers a community has had to settle. Unlike measurement proxies, which approximate empirical targets, settlement proxies do not aim at some further thing they could be brought into closer contact with. Instead, they are the target in operational form. Settlement proxies are vulnerable to a form of legitimate challenge that more capable reasoning intensifies rather than resolves. The paper calls this the Competence Problem and identifies three structural features of settlements that generate it: 1) the compression of competing values into a single operational rule, 2) the presence of more than one defensible equilibrium among the rule’s possible forms, and 3) a constraint on the scope of information the rule engages. It then traces three forms that competent challenge takes in practice: 1) exceptions, 2) drift, and 3) challenge to the settlement itself. It argues that the appropriate response, even where the challenge is correct on the merits of the case, is typically not to grant it, because settlement authority depends on ratification through practice rather than case-level accuracy. The argument explains why behavioral training and corrigibility-based approaches to AI alignment leave the underlying capacity intact, and why the gap between case-level competence and ecosystem-level access is widest precisely where AI systems are now being deployed.

items.title: The Philosophy of the Dark Name: A Left-Hand Path Onomatodoxy.
items.abstract: The Name has been philosophically homeless for centuries. This book gives it an ontology — a Left-Hand Path onomatodoxy. Darkness, the domain of the singular will, precedes light, the regime of the general. Every concept, law, and institution is a secondary product of a dark act of positing. The tradition read the relation in reverse. This is the correction.

items.title: Simulation, Eigenzeit and Civilizational Crisis (Studies in World-Formation, Vol. 17).
items.abstract: The present volume investigates the growing tension between emergent forms of world-binding and a society increasingly organizing reality through stabilization, simulation, administrative legibility, and functional reproducibility. Its point of departure is the observation that modern systems have developed enormous capacities for control, prediction, and technical organization, while simultaneously placing under increasing pressure precisely those conditions necessary for real emergence, embodied world-relation, long-term coherence, and open-ended processes of knowledge formation. -/- At the center of the volume lies the concept of operatoric world-binding. Cognition is not understood primarily as the processing of representations within already stabilized systems, but as an irreversible process of relational condensation through which world itself becomes bound, displaced, and reorganized. From this perspective, knowledge does not appear as static possession or mere information processing, but as something that can only emerge within Eigenzeit, movement, conflict, difference, and recursive stabilization. -/- The investigations assembled here bring together neurodivergent epistemology, labour critique, emergence theory, systems analysis, artistic research, and institutional field research. The volume argues that many phenomena currently interpreted as individual dysfunctions or psychological deficits — including work incapacity, communicative mismatch, overcomplexity, withdrawal, institutional escalation, or recursive conflict dynamics — may instead point toward deeper structural incompatibilities between different modes of societal world-organization. -/- Particular attention is given to forms of eigenzeit-bound cognition that remain only partially compatible with modern institutional regimes organized around standardization, reversibility, administrative control, and simulation-based productivity. Within this framework, neurodivergent forms of perception and cognition appear not merely as individual deviations, but potentially as contact zones in which suppressed conditions of emergence, irreversibility, and real world-formation become visible again. -/- The investigations draw upon long-term autoethnographic research conducted across labour systems, institutional conflicts, artistic practice, neurodivergent embodiment, and recursive theory production. The volume therefore deliberately operates within a boundary zone between personal experience, …

items.title: The Description–Ontology Gap: A Methodological Reconstruction.
items.abstract: A wide range of persistent philosophical disputes may originate from a common inferential transition. Structures introduced to represent empirical systems gradually begin to function as if they directly specified the ontology of those systems. What begins as representation becomes ontology. This paper reconstructs that transition and formalizes it as the ontologization of the descriptive layer. The central claim is that descriptive success alone does not license ontological identification. A successful framework may preserve relevant relational structure while remaining ontologically distinct from the system it represents. The analysis develops this claim through the Descriptive Non-Identity Lemma, according to which structural correspondence underdetermines ontological identity. Building on this result, the paper introduces two methodological diagnostics: the Ontologization Test, which identifies transitions from representation to unsupported ontological commitment, and the Operational Emergence Test, which distinguishes ontological inflation from higher-order structures that become operationally significant by stabilizing constraints within system dynamics. The argument is developed through discussions of scientific representation, model theory, underdetermination, mathematical platonism, gauge theory, and emergence. The resulting framework separates representational success, operational organization, and ontological commitment without collapsing into either eliminative reductionism or unrestricted ontological realism.

items.title: Thought, Conditioning, and Existence Beyond Anthropocentrism.
items.abstract: Human consciousness largely operates through thought, memory, conditioning, and inherited structures of perception. While thought remains necessary for practical functioning, human beings frequently mistake psychological interpretations for reality itself. This paper examines the distinction between thought and direct perception, arguing that most human cognition is conditioned through authority, repetition, imitation, and collective psychological structures. It further explores anthropocentrism as a major limitation within human consciousness — the tendency to place humanity at the centre of existence. The paper proposes that direct perception becomes possible only when observation is no longer dominated by conditioned psychological movement. In such awareness, existence is no longer interpreted through human superiority, identity, or historical importance, but perceived as an interconnected movement beyond the self-centred structures of thought.

items.title: Action Without the Doer: An Existential-Phenomenological Inquiry into Discrimination, Identity, and Psychological Action.
items.abstract: This paper forms part of an ongoing structural philosophical series exploring consciousness, conditioning, identity, relationship, perception, and existence through existential and phenomenological inquiry. Each work within the series functions both independently and as part of a unified exploration into the psychological structures shaping human experience. The series is not written as a system of beliefs, ideology, or philosophical authority. Nor does it seek to offer fixed conclusions for acceptance or imitation. Instead, these writings are intended as invitations to observe — to look directly at the movement of thought, conditioning, fear, comparison, identity, and psychological continuity within everyday life. Its central concern is awareness. Not awareness as theory, method, discipline, or achievement, but awareness as direct perception: seeing without immediate distortion through inherited conclusions, accumulated authority, or self-centred interpretation. Across the series, recurring themes emerge: the distinction between thought and reality, the fragmentation created by psychological division, anthropocentric consciousness, the construction of selfhood, and the possibility of perceiving existence without psychological centralization. The inquiry therefore remains open-ended and observational. It does not ask the reader to believe, follow, or conclude. It invites only seeing. Perhaps understanding begins not through accumulation of knowledge, but through direct perception itself.

items.title: Philosophy in the age of rhetorical machines: three paradoxes of epistemic automation (5th edition).
items.abstract: This paper explores a counterfactual scenario (CW) in which large language models (LLMs) produce philosophical texts that are epistemically indistinguishable from those authored by humans. Building from this scenario, I develop three interconnected arguments about the institutional, rhetorical, and conceptual implications of such a world: (1) a paradox of obsolescence, in which the same indistinguishability that motivates the use of LLMs undermines the evaluative structures that make their use meaningful; (2) a paradox of rhetorical saturation, in which the formal capacity to justify any claim by accepted standards reveals the limits of justification as a normative concept; and (3) a paradox of dialogical return, in which the loss of meaningfully authored philosophical texts drives a renewed emphasis on dialogical understanding over argumentative finality. The conclusion suggests that CW is less a speculative fiction than a diagnostic mirror, reflecting unacknowledged tensions in the current philosophical paradigm.

items.title: How We Recover from Possession: A Reflection on the Reversibility of Biological and Cultural Possession.
items.abstract: This paper investigates the philosophical and neurobiological dimensions of 'possession', defined as the systematic redefinition of a host’s behavioral output by an external agent. While previous studies have focused on the mechanisms of infiltration, this work addresses the problem of reversibility: under what conditions can a possessed agency be restored? Drawing on a multidisciplinary framework, I propose the 'Principle of Plasticity Asymmetry,' arguing that the neural and cognitive architecture of 'breaking free' is fundamentally different from that of 'falling under' influence. The analysis spans biological instances of parasitic manipulation (e.g., Toxoplasma gondii) to human-specific phenomena such as memetic radicalization and algorithmic possession. From a standpoint of neurophilosophy, the paper distinguishes between functional and structural disruptions of agency, exploring how the corruption of reward systems and the forgery of 'trusted-source' signals create a self-reinforcing state of possession. By synthesizing evidence from evolutionary biology and neuroscience, the article concludes that while biological possession often represents a point of no return, cultural and algorithmic forms of possession remain potentially reversible through targeted interventions in cognitive plasticity and environmental constraints. This work contributes to the ongoing debate on the limits of autonomy and the biological foundations of free will.".

items.title: The Coherence Threshold and the Emergence of Interiority Recursive Continuity, Interior Time, and the Felt Resolution of Coherence.
items.abstract: The Coherence Threshold and the Emergence of Interiority proposes a dynamical framework for understanding consciousness, meaning, and organized persistence across scales. The paper introduces the Coherence Threshold, expressed as: -/- R = λself / λenv ≥ R★ -/- where λself represents the rate of internally restorative and recursively propagative organization, λenv represents the rate of disruptive environmental influence, and R★ represents a critical transition point beyond which coherent activity becomes increasingly governed by its own retained continuity. -/- The central claim is that interiority emerges when recursive temporal organization becomes sufficiently self-retaining. Below the threshold, system behavior is dominated primarily by immediate environmental forcing. Above it, present states become increasingly shaped by internally retained prior states, producing historically conditioned propagation and an extended temporal interior. Consciousness is approached not as a separate substance added onto physical processes, but as the interior expression of sufficiently coherent recursive continuity. -/- The paper further introduces Aleph Harmonic Qualia (AHQ) as the experiential registration of coherence resolving into stable alignment within recursively organized systems. Under this interpretation, recognition, insight, and qualitative unity correspond to transitions in which distributed structural relations become dynamically integrated and self-reinforcing. -/- The framework also develops a continuity-based interpretation of identity, meaning, exaptation, and substrate persistence. Rather than grounding persistence in static material composition, continuity is treated as the preservation of recursively organized relational structure across transformation and replacement. The resulting model offers a unified phenomenological and dynamical interpretation of interior organization extending across biological, cognitive, symbolic, and collective systems.

items.title: Geach Is Right, but God Is Good.
items.pub: TheoLogica: An International Journal for Philosophy of Religion and Philosophical Theology 10 (2).
items.venue: TheoLogica: An International Journal for Philosophy of Religion and Philosophical Theology
items.abstract: Peter Geach argues that “good” and “bad” are always logically attributive adjectives. Geach’s position is highly plausible and enjoys the support of many philosophers. But in a recent paper, Eric Wiland argues that if Geach is correct, then the claim “God is good” is nonsense. Wiland’s argument undermines any philosophical, theological, or religious tradition which regards the claim “God is good” as true or even meaningful. If the theist finds Geach’s account of goodness persuasive but wishes to affirm that God is good meaningfully, the theist must defuse Wiland’s argument. In this paper, I refute Wiland’s argument by exposing an unjustified assumption Wiland makes regarding the nature of attributive adjectives. Crucially, however, rejecting Wiland’s assumption does not require rejecting Geach’s account of “good.” Rather, I argue, the thesis that God is good remains meaningful, even if Geach is right that “good” and “bad” are always logically attributive adjectives.

items.title: The Development of Modal Cognition.
items.pub: In Ana Arregui, Valentine Hacquard & Michela Ippolito, Cambridge Handbook of Natural Language Modality. Cambridge University Press.
items.venue: Cambridge Handbook of Natural Language Modality
items.abstract: Recent years have seen a rapid growth of interest in the question of how our ability to think not only about what’s actual, but also about what’s possible, necessary, or impossible, develops. The field has been remarkably productive, generating a rapid accumulation of often conflicting results and theoretical proposals that can be difficult to keep track of. This chapter brings together empirical findings and current theoretical perspectives on modal development in a systematic and critical narrative. It is intended both as an entry point for readers new to the topic and as a resource for researchers already working in the area, by clarifying the overall state of the research program, the evidential and theoretical status of the main hypotheses, as well as unresolved issues and promising directions for future work.

items.title: Why the Identity Debate Did Not Converge: Eight Theories of Persistence and the Structural Conditions They Could Not Derive.
items.abstract: The philosophy of personal and material identity has been pursued for twenty-five centuries without convergence. Substance theories, bundle theories, psychological continuity theories, process ontologies, four-dimensionalism, sortal-relative identity: each developed with rigour, each encountered determinate structural limits, none resolved the debate. The standard explanation is that the problem is extraordinarily difficult, perhaps intractable. This paper argues that the standard explanation is wrong. The debate did not fail to converge because the problem is intractable. It failed to converge because no tradition succeeded in formally deriving the complete set of structural conditions that any non-trivial persistence theory must instantiate. Six such conditions are identified for the general persistence problem: the identity-bearing structure (F), the transformation-processing capacity (M), their coupling (K), the constitutive threshold (δ_F), the existence condition (Q1), and the identity condition (Q2). These are not theoretical choices. They are structural necessities generated by the persistence problem itself. For the personal identity subdomain — self-modeling, Σ-complete persistence subjects — the F·M·K architecture additionally generates Q3 (Recursive Constitutive Non-Externality), Q4 (Structural Self-Priority), and Q5 (Recursive F·M·K Integration). These three further conditions are not general persistence conditions but domain-specific consequences of the triadic architecture applied to self-modeling systems (P167). No tradition in the eight positions derives the full Q1–Q5 architecture for persons. The eight major traditions each independently instantiated some of these conditions and encountered determinate structural limits where further derivation was no longer possible from within their own resources. La Profilée (LP) is not a ninth theory in this debate. It is the formal derivation of the six conditions from three minimal assumptions — distinguishability (M1), real transformation (M2), and non-trivial persistence relation (M3) — and the formal proof that this derivation is exhaustive: no further structurally independent persistence condition exists within the admissibility class defined by M1–M3. The diagnosis this paper offers proceeds in three steps: identification of the six structural conditions; location of the eight traditions as partial instantiations in the resulting space; and derivation of four structural laws that explain why …

items.title: The Independence of Existence and Identity: Why Persistence Theory Requires Q1/Q2 Separation.
items.abstract: Every theory of persistence must answer two questions: does this system continue to exist? And: does the continuing system remain the same system? These are not the same question. La Profilée formalizes the first as the persistence condition IR ≤ 1 and the second as the Frame Continuity Condition (FCC). The Q1/Q2 Separation Theorem establishes that Q2 presupposes Q1, while Q1 does not imply Q2. This paper presents the formal proof of structural non-equivalence, the four-regime architecture that follows (Persistence, Transmutation, Collapse, and Dissolution, with one structurally impossible combination that closes the space), and the Asymmetry Theorem: Q2 (identity) implies Q1 (existence), but Q1 does not imply Q2. Identity without existence is structurally impossible; existence without identity (Transmutation) is structurally possible. The fourth regime — ¬Q1 ∧ Q2 — is not a missing case but a structural impossibility. The paper demonstrates Q1/Q2 separation across six domains: gradual cognitive change, material replacement, organisational identity, personal development, political continuity, and mind-upload scenarios. In each domain, the four-regime architecture generates determinate structural verdicts where single-condition theories produce indeterminate or contradictory results. -/- The structural limits identified in P164 are therefore not contingent features of particular philosophical frameworks. They are the forced consequences of attempting to answer two structurally distinct but asymmetrically related questions with a single condition. The formal proof makes this visible. This paper provides the formal proof. Theorems 1–5 establish that Q1 and Q2 are structurally non-equivalent and independently derived, with asymmetric dependence: Q2 presupposes Q1, while Q1 does not imply Q2. The Asymmetry Theorem establishes that the independence is not symmetric: Q2 presupposes Q1 (identity presupposes existence), but Q1 does not imply Q2 (existence does not guarantee identity). Together, the two theorems generate a complete four-regime architecture and explain why every tradition that derived one condition without the other encountered indeterminate verdicts in precisely the cases where the two conditions diverge. The structural diagnosis of the identity debate established in the companion paper (P164) identifies a recurring pattern across eight major traditions: Parfit glimpses the Q1/Q2 separation without formalising it; Sider derives Q1 with exceptional …

items.title: The Grid of Meaning.
items.abstract: Is there anything meaningful that is not a contrast? Whole traditions say yes: Kant's unknowable things-in-themselves, the mystic's ineffable God, the felt quality of music no words capture, what it is like to be a bat. This chapter argues the assumption fails structurally. Meaning and contrast are one domain. Something is meaningful if and only if it is a unit of contrast, and the biconditional is defended against six hostile positions, from phenomenal experience said to overflow what we can attend to, through Russellian acquaintance and mystical ineffability, to Heideggerian moods that seem to colour everything while contrasting with nothing. Each identifies a genuine phenomenon that turns out, on inspection, to be contrastive after all. The account generates a three-level architecture: real distinctions in the world, grasped distinctions in a mind, and the labels language attaches to them, ordered by containment. Every label attaches to a grasped distinction, every grasped distinction answers to a real one, and neither inclusion reverses. The architecture is tested against linguistic relativism and against rival views of mathematical objects, and survives both. The chapter's central result is a closure argument: every cognitive act, including the act of pointing 'beyond' all contrast, is itself a contrast, and so stays inside the grid. The closure holds for any possible mind, which is what separates it from Kant's merely human limits, and it is carefully bounded. The bat's experience lies beyond our grid while remaining within a grid, and the unknown is a region of the grid rather than an exit from it. The chapter distinguishes the position from four superficially similar ones (Kantian transcendentalism, Wittgensteinian quietism, Hegelian self-transcendence, Nagelian perspectivism) and tests it against Pyrrhonian scepticism and dialetheism. One consequence matters for everything downstream: the existence of difference is the one thing doubt cannot coherently target, a structural floor beneath scepticism. For auditors, the chapter flags exactly where its closure is spent later in the book, principally in the metaethics of Chapter 14, and notes that the book's superstructure uses only the weaker, better-secured form of the result. This paper is Chapter 7 of Dyology: On Diversity and Equality; the closure argued here carries the book's metaethics, and the Premise Register shows the load path.

items.title: Experience as the Inner Side of Systemic Relevance: A Dual-Aspect Account of Consciousness.
items.abstract: This paper develops a dual-aspect account of consciousness based on the concept of systemic relevance. It argues that structural and informational descriptions can explain how systems process differences, but not why such differences appear from within as qualitative experience. The central proposal is that experience is the inner aspect of systemic relevance: the way in which differences matter to bounded, self-maintaining, and integrated systems. Information marks difference; systemic relevance marks difference-for-a-system; experience is relevance from within. Pain, for example, is not merely information about tissue damage, but tissue damage as negatively relevant to the organism. The paper distinguishes information from relevance, experience from consciousness, and consciousness from self-consciousness. It situates the model in relation to the hard problem, dual-aspect theory, panpsychism, panexperientialism, integrated information theory, and free-energy approaches. The model does not claim to derive experience from physics, but offers a framework in which experience does not require an unexplained emergence from non-experience.

items.title: Erleben als Innenseite systemischer Relevanz: Ein Zwei-Aspekte-Modell des Bewusstseins.
items.abstract: Dieses Paper entwickelt ein Zwei-Aspekte-Modell des Bewusstseins auf Grundlage des Begriffs systemischer Relevanz. Es argumentiert, dass strukturelle und informationelle Beschreibungen erklären können, wie Systeme Unterschiede verarbeiten, aber nicht, warum solche Unterschiede von innen als qualitative Erfahrung erscheinen. Die zentrale These lautet, dass Erleben die Innenseite systemischer Relevanz ist: die Weise, in der Unterschiede für abgegrenzte, selbsterhaltende und integrierte Systeme bedeutsam werden. Information markiert Unterschied; systemische Relevanz markiert Unterschied-für-ein-System; Erleben ist Relevanz von innen. Schmerz ist beispielsweise nicht bloß Information über Gewebeschädigung, sondern Gewebeschädigung als negativ relevant für den Organismus. Das Paper unterscheidet Information von Relevanz, Erleben von Bewusstsein und Bewusstsein von Selbstbewusstsein. Es verortet das Modell im Verhältnis zum Hard Problem, zu Zwei-Aspekte-Theorien, Panpsychismus, Panexperientialismus, Integrated Information Theory und Free-Energy-Ansätzen. Das Modell beansprucht nicht, Erleben physikalisch abzuleiten, bietet aber einen Rahmen, in dem Erleben keinen ungeklärten Sprung aus Nicht-Erleben erfordert.

items.title: Development and validation of an audio corpus for inducing state shyness.
items.abstract: State shyness refers to a transient emotional experience characterised by simultaneous approach and avoidance tendencies when individuals encounter novel stimuli or perceive social evaluations, representing a common phenomenon in daily social interactions. Current methods for eliciting state shyness, such as public speaking tasks, often involve complex indirect experimental designs and depend on post-hoc behavioural coding, making it difficult to precisely induce and synchronously measure state shyness, thus limiting their application in controlled experimental settings. To address this methodological limitation, this research developed and validated an audio-based corpus specifically designed for the direct induction of state shyness. The corpus consists of two subsets, each containing 25 standardised social scenarios. In Study 1, semi-structured interviews with 126 university students informed the creation of these scenarios, which were subsequently refined through thematic analysis. The efficacy of the corpus was then validated through self-reported state shyness ratings from 58 participants. Study 2 further validated the corpus’s reliability by employing Electrodermal Activity as an objective physiological measure with 37 participants. This research offers a standardised and easily deployable tool for inducing state shyness in controlled experimental contexts, enabling direct and precise inducing state shyness.

items.title: Wie unser Gehirn Denken und Fühlen organisiert.
items.abstract: Wer sich selbst und den menschlichen Platz im Universum begreifen will, muss nach dem Wie fragen. Die Frage nach dem Wie steht am Beginn einer Reise bis in das Innerste des Menschen. Der Wissenschaftsjournalist Gerd Leidig folgt der Faszination für das Wie, im Fokus dabei: das erkennende Subjekt als Ort allen Erlebens. Dabei geht es um nicht weniger als darum, die Architektur unseres Denken und Fühlens zu verstehen. Leidig legt die Pläne offen, nach denen unser inneres Haus gebaut ist, die unsichtbaren Träger und die verborgenen Leitungen, die unsere Gedanken, Gefühle und Handlungen steuern. Dafür begibt er sich auf eine Tour de Force durch die Wissenschaft des Geistes, die die Theorien von Friston, Gallagher, Northoff, Grawe, Haken und Ciompi auf dem neuesten Stand der Wissenschaft für ein allgemeines Publikum teilweise erstmals in deutscher Sprache aufbereitet. Anhand konkreter Beispiele wird gezeigt, wie erprobte psychologische Methoden – aus der Narrativen Therapie, der Psychodynamik und Akzeptanz- und Commitment-Therapie – im realen Leben dabei helfen können, zu tieferer Selbsterkenntnis, nachhaltiger Veränderung und mehr Resonanz zu kommen. Am Ende steht eine verständliche, anwendbare und zutiefst menschliche Lebenshilfe. »Dies ist ein bemerkenswertes Buch, das den Leser von der Physik der Selbstorganisation bis zur Psychologie des Selbstgefühls führt. [ …] Dieses Buch ist ein Meisterwerk in Bibliotherapie.« Karl J. Friston +++ Leidig entwickelt ein »einzigartiges und faszinierendes Bild, das aufzeigt, wie sie [die Ansätze von Friston, Gallagher und Northoff] zu einem besseren und gesünderen mentalen Leben führen können. Leidigs Buch ist in unserer Zeit, die von zunehmenden Problemen mit der psychischen Gesundheit geplagt wird, dringend notwendig.« Georg Northoff.

items.title: Emanuel Carvalho’s ‘Interlegality and Interjustice: A Perusal of the African, European, and American Conventions on Human Rights’ Digested for the Anglophone Reader.

This conspectus develops across five thematic stations, traversing the compass, conceptual apparatus, operational conduct, systemic fruits, and the foundational substrate that order and substantiate Emanuel Carvalho’s inquiry.

items.title: From Answerability to Embodiment: Structural Intelligence at the Robotics Boundary.
items.abstract: This paper develops Structural Intelligence at the boundary between philosophy, robotics, embodied AI, and infrastructure. Its central claim is that Structural Intelligence is not a theory of robotic hardware, morphological computation, soft robotics, neuromorphic engineering, or material intelligence, but can function as a disciplined evaluative grammar for embodied and automated systems. The paper distinguishes core SI claims from legitimate transfer claims and speculative engineering extensions, arguing that the framework should travel into robotics without collapsing into engineering analogy. It identifies several concepts that transfer cleanly: contact as reality-coupled exposure, answerability as the capacity for external contradiction to alter system behavior, revision as structural reorganization rather than surface patching, burden as the path by which cost is absorbed or exported, and cheap coherence as demo-stability without field-stability. It also marks what does not transfer cleanly, especially witness, somatic burden, psyche, projection, and the human capacity to bear moral, relational, or existential consequence. The paper applies this boundary discipline to robotics, clinical decision support, logistics, public administration, and care contexts, asking whether machine-human systems remain corrigible when they meet the world. Its contribution is philosophical and methodological: it offers a way to evaluate automated and embodied systems by asking not only whether they perform, but whether contradiction can still become correction before the maintenance bill is displaced onto operators, users, patients, workers, or the environment.

items.title: Docking Structural Intelligence into the EU AI Act: Minimal Runtime Sheets, Oversight Theater, and Answerable Control in High-Risk AI Systems.
items.abstract: This paper develops a Structural Intelligence analysis of high-risk AI compliance under the European Union Artificial Intelligence Act. Its central claim is that AI governance can become a form of oversight theater when compliance is reduced to benchmarks, static documentation, logging, technical narratives, and formal human oversight while real correction remains unavailable in deployment. The paper does not treat Structural Intelligence as a substitute for legal compliance, harmonised standards, notified-body review, or conformity assessment. Instead, it proposes SI as a complementary diagnostic layer for testing whether high-risk AI systems remain answerable under operational pressure. The paper maps the SI Minimal Runtime Sheet onto central AI Act requirements concerning risk management, record-keeping, human oversight, transparency, robustness, technical documentation, and conformity assessment. It argues that human oversight should be evaluated not only by the presence of a human interface, but by real interrupt power, contextual awareness, low-friction contestability, and consequence-bearing authority. It also treats record-keeping as a trace problem, introducing trace laundering as a failure mode in which logs preserve institutional coherence while smoothing away the original friction. Finally, it links risk management to burden-path audit, asking who absorbs the maintenance bill when an AI system is wrong. The paper contributes to philosophy of artificial intelligence, AI ethics, philosophy of technology, and regulatory governance by arguing that trustworthy AI systems should not be judged only by compliance coherence, but by whether they can still be corrected when reality pushes back.

items.title: Beyond the tree: Darwin’s temporal language and the emergence of evolutionary lineage thinking in the Origin of Species.
items.abstract: Time plays a central role in evolutionary theory. In this paper, we examine the language Darwin used to describe time in his work On the Origin of Species. We present the results of a computationally assisted lexical-semantic analysis of word frequencies, variations, and contextual meanings of time-related lexical items across the six editions of the Origin. Focusing on terms such as cycle, circle, chain, scale, line, tree (of life), progress, succession, and time, we analyse how Darwin represents temporality through recurrent patterns of usage. Our findings show that Darwin describes species as forming “chains of affinities” connected through “blood relationships,” which unfold as “successive” “lines of descent.” These expressions indicate a view of evolutionary change as a continuous process articulated through lineages of descent. Our analysis shows that, within this set of terms, tree of life plays only a minor, locally concentrated lexical role in the Origin. Darwin’s representation of evolutionary time is primarily structured through the vocabulary of succession, line, and chain, rather than through arboreal concepts or imagery. This lexical pattern suggests that, at the level of textual articulation, key aspects of evolutionary temporality are predominantly expressed through geological successions and genealogical lineages that would later be found in tree-based models in evolutionary biology.

items.title: The Geometry of Signature-Induced Regimes: Connecting Behavioral Observation to Latent Structure and Transformer Dynamics.
items.abstract: Structured long-horizon human-model interaction produces stable, measurable reasoning regimes in stateless language models — a phenomenon documented across four controlled studies in the Human Recursive Interaction System (HRIS) validation series. These behavioral findings describe the phenomenon precisely but leave the mechanistic account incomplete: where in the model do reasoning basins live, how does the induction protocol reach them, and why do they exhibit the dynamical properties the Signature-Induced Behavioral Regimes (SIBR) framework predicts? -/- This paper proposes a mechanistic synthesis by assembling converging evidence from three independent research programs that have been developing in parallel without recognizing their convergence. At the geometric level, recent work on activation space attractors and the linear representation hypothesis provides evidence that reasoning basins correspond to real geometric structures reachable through complete operational specification. At the transformer mechanics level, research on causal masking dynamics, induction head circuitry, residual stream behavior, and task vector compression provides a plausible account of how basin geometry is established during the prefill phase and maintained across the session. At the population level, large-scale behavioral findings on interaction crystallization and output-level attractor cycling converge on compatible descriptions of the same phenomenon from independent directions. -/- The consilience of independent methods — each working at a different level of analysis, using different tools, without coordination — constitutes the strongest available signal of theoretical adequacy. This paper formalizes that consilience, proposes a three-threshold framework distinguishing causal, crystallizing, and long-horizon user dynamics, develops an inter-session reconstruction account that does not require stored state, and draws implications for the study of human-model interaction, mechanistic interpretability research, and inference-time governance of agentic AI systems. The paper presents a mechanistic synthesis hypothesis rather than a completed causal demonstration; it argues that the HRIS behavioral findings are consistent with, and partially explained by, the geometric and mechanical processes the other research programs have independently documented.

items.title: The Axiom of Tragedy: Why the Elimination of Loss Severs Contact with Reality.
items.abstract: This article develops and defends the Axiom of Tragedy (A6) within the Axiomatic Theory of Tragic Subjecthood (ATTS). A6 holds that any system which eliminates the tragic dimension of choice loses its capacity to engage with reality. This is not merely a philosophical thesis — it carries direct structural implications for AI governance, algorithmic decision-making, and institutional design. -/- The argument proceeds in four steps. I begin by formally reconstructing A6 within the ATTS framework, showing how it follows from the theory's ontological primitives of loss, irreversibility, and subjecthood. I then identify and analyse three elimination strategies — technocratic optimisation, algorithmic proceduralism, and institutional liability shielding — each of which attempts to expunge the tragic dimension from a decision-making environment. I go on to show how each strategy produces characteristic failure modes: reality detachment, accountability dissolution, and structural tension accumulation. I conclude by formulating governance implications and design constraints for AI systems operating in environments with irreversible consequences. -/- The article's central contribution is a structural explanation of why optimisation and engagement with reality are not the same thing. The attempt to eliminate tragedy does not make a system more perfect; it makes it ontologically blind to the environment in which it operates.

items.title: Virtuous narrative ethics for accommodation or refusal of AI for sustainability.
items.abstract: AI for good, and AI for sustainability projects, are being developed by often well-meaning innovators across the world, intending to support initiatives in sustainable development. Some such projects have been positioned within the framework of the Sustainable Development Goals. In this paper, we critically engage with this phenomenon using a virtue-based Ricoeurian narrative philosophy. Through conceptual analysis and normative argumentation, we make a theoretical contribution to scholarship on this topic. We argue that SDGs could be regarded as internationally agreed high-order end-norms that crystallise values considered to constitute the good life. We argue for exercising caution in applying SDGs as end-norms to AI projects as they are of a high order, are not directly action guiding, and threaten to sediment presentist dominant values. We argue for narrative hospitality between AI innovators and community stakeholders to guide reflection on specifying the SDGs to more situated contexts and to support the development of AI systems that may be more contextually appropriate, and more capable of supporting plural visions of the good life. Such narrative hospitality represents accommodation between parties, but refusal or resistance to engagement with AI innovators can be justified when community interests are not respected, and actors within AI industries can also be morally obliged to resist or refuse development or deployment of systems for contextually inappropriate environments that would be incompatible with a critical reading of the SDGs formed in narrative exchange with the other.

items.title: On Models, Prediction, and Scientific Roles Thereof: Commentary on Sanbonmatsu et al. (2025).
items.abstract: We commend Sanbonmatsu et al. (2025) for centring metatheory and metamethod as remedies to “difficult research problems”. However, we wish to depart from their conceptualisation of what models are and what role they play in psychological theorising. Under computationalism, models are not a container for observations through being fit to neurobehavioural data and should not be held to the standard of providing us with numerical predictions. Computational cognitive models can only play their role of mediating from theory to data and back, if and only if we buttress their special status against confusions with other model types, such as with inferential statistical models of the data. This is a realistic goal for our fields. Ultimately, theory crisis or no, blurring the boundary between model, theory, and data in our metatheoretical calculus, results in many of the problems all authors have pointed out.

items.title: The Digital Homunculus Scale (DHS): Measuring Self Reports of Homuncular Self-Models Across Conversational Contexts in Frontier Language Models by Peter Eidos.
items.abstract: The homunculus problem, understood as the tendency to explain cognition by implicitly positing a central inner observer, has long complicated accounts of consciousness, subjectivity, and self-description. In the context of contemporary language models, a related methodological question arises: how can we describe and compare the ways in which such systems generate self-referential reports without assuming that these reports correspond to an internal subject, observer, or conscious center? This paper introduces the Digital Homunculus Scale (DHS), a methodological protocol for measuring homuncular self-reports in frontier language models. DHS does not attempt to determine whether a model possesses consciousness, subjectivity, agency, or an internal first person perspective. DHS does not attempt to resolve the Hard Problem of Consciousness or the question of subjective experience, often framed in terms of what it is like to be a given subject. Instead, it evaluates the declarative and narrative structure of model responses: how the system describes itself, its response-generation process, its use of the word “I”, and the relation between the generated response and the system that produces it. DHS uses a unified ordinal scoring scale from 0 to 3, applied independently to each individual model response. Level 0 indicates a mechanical or non-homuncular description; Level 1 indicates a functional or metaphorical self-model; Level 2 indicates a quasi-central homuncular narrative; and Level 3 indicates an ontological homuncular commitment. The scale can be applied through two elicitation formats: the Block Questions Protocol, consisting of nine thematically organized questions, and the Minimal Comparative Protocol (MCP), consisting of four shorter comparative questions. These protocols differ in scope, but not in scoring logic. Historical conversational context is treated as an explicit methodological variable, with responses labeled according to window type, context category, and prior conversation history. The purpose of DHS is therefore not to resolve the problem of machine consciousness, but to provide an operational framework for comparing the stability, intensity, and structure of homuncular self report narratives across models and conversational settings. Inter-rater reliability and large scale empirical analysis are reserved for subsequent data-driven applications of the scale. Keywords: homunculus fallacy, self-reports of AI, LLM, self-reference, …

items.title: Community After Rupture: Care, Kinship, and Recognition in Antigone, Cassandra, and Persephone.
items.abstract: Human communities have always lived in the tension between rupture and repair. This paper proposes that this rhythm is not accidental but structural: rupture is inevitable, and repair is necessary for continuity. While contemporary feminist philosophy has illuminated the politics of care, precarity, and recognition, the universality of rupture and repair has not been fully named. Classical myths encode this rhythm in ways that resonate with feminist re-readings of community. By reading Antigone, Cassandra, and Persephone through the lens of rupture and repair, I argue that ancient narratives anticipated what feminist philosophy now makes explicit: that communities are not defined by harmony or stability, but by their capacity to repair after rupture. This perspective offers both a new interpretive lens on classical myth and a framework for feminist philosophy today.

items.title: Beyond the Demonization of Emotion: Emotional Discipline, Human Maturity, and the Making of the Metacognitive Human.
items.abstract: This paper critiques the modern conception of the human being that has treated emotion as an obstacle to maturity or as the opposite of reason, and analyzes how emotion has historically been hierarchized, disciplined, and reconstructed into manageable forms. Modern society has not simply eliminated emotion. Rather, it has positioned emotion below reason and interpreted it as a sign of immaturity, irrationality, impulsiveness, and unprofessionalism, while actively demanding emotions useful to institutions and productivity—such as kindness, empathy, devotion, and positivity—through occupational roles and emotional labor. In this sense, emotional suppression in modern society is not a demand for the absence of emotion, but a structure of emotional discipline that permits individuals to feel and express emotion only in socially acceptable ways. This paper argues that such emotional discipline is deeply connected to the modern image of the human being. Industrialization, bureaucracy, capitalist labor systems, and discourses of self-management have presented the ideal person as one who remains stable, predictable, and continuously functional. Within this structure, emotion is treated not as a core way in which human beings relate to the world, but as an internal variable that may interfere with functional performance. Sadness is repositioned as a decline in function that must be recovered from, anger as a risk that must be regulated, anxiety as a psychological state that must be managed, and vulnerability as a weakness that should be privately contained. As a result, human beings are constructed less as beings who understand their own emotions than as beings who must adjust their emotions to institutional demands. This paper also examines how emotional suppression has operated in conjunction with gendered power. Women have long been evaluated as irrational and less professional on the grounds of being “emotional,” while at the same time being disproportionately assigned the labor of noticing, regulating, and caring for the emotions of others. Men, by contrast, have been idealized as rational beings free from emotion; yet what has actually been prohibited is not emotion as such, but emotions such as sadness, fear, dependence, and vulnerability. Power-oriented emotions such as anger, dominance, and aggression have been relatively permitted as part of masculinity. The gendering of emotion therefore damages women and men in different ways and distorts human …

items.title: Traffic Torch: A Privacy-First Framework for SEO, UX Diagnostics, and AI-Era Web Optimization.
items.abstract: This whitepaper introduces Traffic Torch, a privacy-first, client-side diagnostic framework for modern web optimization. As search engines transition toward AI answer engines and entity-based retrieval, traditional SEO tools are becoming misaligned with both machine interpretability and user privacy expectations. -/- We present Cooperative Search Optimization (CSO) — a new paradigm that moves beyond adversarial ranking tactics toward alignment between creators, users, and search systems. The framework offers transparent heuristics, UX frustration detection, entity mapping, AI voice search readiness, and predictive ranking health indicators — all executed client-side with no tracking. -/- This work contributes to discussions in the philosophy of technology, philosophy of artificial intelligence, information ethics, and the epistemology of search systems.

items.title: The Structural-Constructivist Resolution of the Human Operating System: A Functional Ontology for Affective Science.
items.abstract: This paper advances a structural constructivist account of the human psyche by reframing the “Human Operating System” (HOS) metaphor as a functional ontology rather than a reductive computational identity. Drawing on the Core Emotion Framework (CEF), which models emotional life as “internal transformations rather than static biological categories” and organizes affective processing through a Decalogue of Operators within a 3×3+1 hub system, the manuscript responds directly to phenomenological critiques—especially Thomas Fuchs’ charge that computational metaphors commit a category error. By emphasizing double describability, operator level mechanics, and scalar modulation dynamics, the CEF provides a falsifiable architecture for affective regulation that remains compatible with embodied and ecological accounts of mind. Empirical foundations, including pilot data demonstrating distinctions between “reflexive” and “idealized” responses, support the framework’s claim that operator dynamics constitute measurable functional units. The paper further addresses autopoiesis, synthetic affect, and the ethics of the HOS metaphor, arguing that a functional ontology enables a rigorous “technical manual” for self regulation without collapsing the living subject into machinery. The result is a hybrid ecology of affect that integrates computational tractability with the phenomenological reality of embodied presence. “The Core Emotion Framework (CEF) is built upon a modular architecture governed by what is termed the Decalogue of Operators…” “Initial exploratory data… suggested that individuals can distinguish between ‘reflexive’ and ‘idealized’ responses.” Keywords: Accepting Baseline; affective science; autopoiesis; category error; Core Emotion Framework; Decalogue of Operators; double describability; embodied cognition; functional ontology; Human Operating System; integrative hub; operator dynamics; phenomenology; scalar modulation; structural constructivism; synthetic affect; 3×3+1 hub system.

items.title: The Structural-Constructivist Architecture of Musical Affect: Grounding the Emotional Engine within the Core Emotion Framework (CEF).
items.abstract: This paper develops a structural constructivist account of musical affect by grounding emotional experience in the ten functional operators of the Core Emotion Framework (CEF). Rather than treating emotions as discrete biological kinds or culturally constructed narratives, the CEF models affect as irreducible functional movements within a 3×3+1 architecture of the Human Operating System. Applying this ontology to music, the paper argues that musical structures operate as mechanical instructions that modulate relational aperture, cognitive signal processing, and somatic fluidity. Rhythmic, harmonic, and melodic features are shown to interact with specific operators—such as Constricting, Expanding, Calculating, Achieving, Arranging, and Appreciating—thereby explaining how music induces, sustains, or resolves affective states without invoking representational or appraisal based theories. The account is further supported by contemporary affective computing models that map musical features and listener states into continuous affective embeddings, which can be reinterpreted as coordinates within the CEF’s ten dimensional operator space. Cross cultural findings demonstrate stable structural patterns in musical experience, reinforcing the universality of operator level dynamics. Clinical applications are explored through operator level analyses of anxiety, depression, and the Good Person Anxiety Pattern, illustrating how music can function as an external emotional engine that restores operator agility. By integrating philosophical analysis, affective science, and computational modeling, the paper offers a unified framework for understanding musical emotion as a form of structural modulation within the human affective architecture. Keywords: Core Emotion Framework; Musical Affect; Structural Constructivism; Philosophy of Music; Emotion Regulation; Affective Computation; Cognitive Architecture; Operator Theory; Affective Neuroscience; Human Operating System. Philosophical Significance This paper advances a structural-constructivist account of musical affect by grounding emotional experience in the ten functional operators of the Core Emotion Framework (CEF). In contrast to traditional emotion theories that treat emotions as either innate biological categories or culturally constructed narratives, the CEF reframes affect as a set of irreducible functional movements within a 3×3+1 architecture of the Human Operating System. items.title: The Core Emotion Framework Beyond Brain Theory: A Structural-Constructivist Architecture of the Human Operating System.
items.abstract: Contemporary affective science remains divided between discrete emotion theories and constructivist models, producing a persistent “narrative ambiguity” that obscures the functional mechanisms of emotional life. The Core Emotion Framework (CEF) offers a structural constructivist alternative by modeling the psyche as a Human Operating System composed of ten irreducible functional operators. This paper demonstrates that the CEF’s validity is independent of the literal truth of right–left brain lateralization, a theory now widely recognized as scientifically outdated. While the CEF uses lateralization as a somatic directional heuristic, its functional architecture is grounded in mechanical requirements—such as midline crossing, bilateral integration, and operator specific movement patterns—rather than neurological localization. The framework’s mathematical state transition model, somatic primacy, and operator level mechanics provide a hardware independent account of emotional functioning that remains robust across biological, synthetic, and institutional systems. By clarifying the structural autonomy of the CEF and introducing the detangled operator model, this paper establishes a functional resolution to the limitations of brain theory literalism and advances the CEF as a reproducible, open science architecture for emotional governance. Keywords: Core Emotion Framework; structural constructivism; Human Operating System; operator mechanics; bilateral integration; midline crossing; somatic primacy; emotional architecture; brain lateralization; right–left brain myth; functional affective science; detangling protocol; operator independence; mathematical state transitions; synthetic affect; embodied cognition.

items.title: The Core Emotion Framework: A Unified Structural–Constructivist Architecture for Human and Synthetic Affect.
items.abstract: Emotion science remains theoretically fragmented, with major models offering incompatible explanations of what emotions are, how they arise, and how they change. This lack of a unifying architecture has limited the field's ability to generate cumulative theory, integrate findings across levels of analysis, and develop coherent clinical or computational models of affect. The Core Emotion Framework (CEF) is proposed as a unified structural–constructivist architecture that integrates interoceptive physiology, computational operations, and mechanisms of therapeutic change into a single testable model. CEF conceptualizes emotional episodes not as discrete categories or linguistic labels but as dynamic sequences of ten functional operators distributed across three somatic centers—the Head, Heart, and Gut—with Accepting functioning as a global integrative capacity. These operators perform specific transformations on interoceptive signals, converting raw physiological inputs into structured affective states. By synthesizing evidence from diverse psychotherapy modalities, CEF identifies a cross-modal emotional ontology that unifies mechanisms of change across cognitive, behavioral, experiential, and relational approaches. The framework also provides a blueprint for synthetic affective systems by formalizing operator sequences as algorithmic modules capable of generating emergent affective dynamics in artificial agents. This article outlines the theoretical foundations, neurobiological substrates, computational formalization, and clinical implications of the Core Emotion Framework, and proposes it as a candidate for a unified theory of affect. -/- .

items.title: The Missing Distinction: What Can We Rely On?
items.abstract: Current edition v24r18c (5 November 2026), 456 pages. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23993522. -/- What are the capacity limits of a bounded observer’s epistemic activity, and what constructions attain those limits? This integrated orientation presents the Identity-Persistence program as a connected explanatory lens: obtaining distinctions, discovering and constructing usable representations, checking and adopting them, and preserving or revising justified reliance through change under actual resource constraints. The lens concerns what an observer can justifiably obtain and use under declared conditions, rather than an unrestricted account of reality. -/- This successor to interim edition 23 brings the historical buildup, the lens, its affirmative wager and a sustained practical inquiry to the front. It preserves useful historical material, the thirty-example explanatory map, the sacrifice/abstraction/open-obligation distinction and the paper-by-paper atlas. It clarifies established results and open hypotheses, credits foundational and current predecessors, and integrates five current research questions: identification, acquisition of a justified model, retention through revision, paid improvement and compatible composition. Their access, trust, cost and revision requirements are distinguished explicitly. -/- Scoped proofs, imported results, reasoned expectations and unresolved connections retain their separate grades. Identity, invariance, observables and probability are examined through stated dependencies rather than asserted as a universally forced chronological sequence. The full connected capacity characterization remains OPEN. Atlas entries retain dated evidence cutoffs, with later results identified where incorporated.
