Finally, I propose redesigning marriage vows to better align with the available evidence and human values.

items.title: Here, where? A puzzle for olfactory experience’s spatiality.
items.pub: Philosophy and the Mind Sciences 7 (Philosophy and Chemosenses):1-16.
items.abstract: In this paper, I argue that two plausible claims for olfactory experience, (i) that this modality is spatially indeterminate regarding the spatial location of what it presents and (ii) that whatever it presents, it is experienced as external to the perceiver’s body, are in conflict with one another. I argue that a satisfactory answer to this puzzle requires us to accept as part of olfactory phenomenology aspects of experience that do not obviously belong to olfactory experience. I claim that this ultimately leads to a modification of the idea that olfactory experience is spatially indeterminate.

items.title: La conciencia como validación informacional: una reformulación neo-funcionalista de la percepción, la fenomenalidad y el Yo.
items.abstract: Este artículo propone una reformulación neo-funcionalista de la conciencia centrada en la tesis de que la experiencia subjetiva no debe entenderse como una propiedad ontológicamente añadida al procesamiento neural, ni como un contenido recibido por un sujeto previo, ni como un estado ulterior de ciertos contenidos informacionales, sino como la actividad misma de justificación de la información mediante validación recursiva. Frente a la teoría de la identidad, el funcionalismo clásico, el naturalismo biológico, el ilusionismo y las variantes contemporáneas del panpsiquismo o del monismo russelliano, se sostiene que la conciencia no sobreviene al procesamiento informacional, sino que consiste en el acto dinámico por el cual ciertos patrones neuronales de información se validan, se sostienen y se articulan recursivamente dentro del sistema. En este marco, percepción, sensación, experiencia y fenomenalidad no designan niveles ontológicamente distintos, sino diferentes nombres para una misma operación fundamental. El Yo, por su parte, no aparece como condición previa de la conciencia, sino como una construcción autorreferencial posterior, necesaria para la autoconciencia, pero no para la conciencia primaria. El núcleo filosófico de la propuesta consiste en defender que la conciencia no es el resultado de la validación informacional, sino esa misma actividad en cuanto acto perceptivo vivido.

items.title: Resolution Theory: A Unified Theory of Thresholds.
items.abstract: This paper presents Resolution Theory as a unified theory of thresholds. Its central schema is simple: buildup is not landing. Causes are not resolution. Explanation, complexity, evidence, pressure, and formal structure may accumulate, but they do not become authorship, consciousness, knowledge, validity, or ethical standing by accumulation alone. A threshold must be crossed. The paper grounds this structure in the Exposed Cogito, moving from the first certainty of the thinking subject to not I, boundary, exposure, correction, and shared life. From this root, Resolution Theory develops accounts of ontology, epistemology, consciousness, personal identity, free will, normativity, ethics, meaning, logic, scepticism, and solipsism. The paper argues that many persistent philosophical disputes arise from confusing buildup with landing, explanation with erasure, or formal intelligibility with standing. It reframes free will as resolution under exposure, consciousness as bounded interiority, knowledge as exposure tested tracking, ethics as the minimum structure of authored life, and paradox as a diagnostic tool for discovering the rules of logic. The result is a candidate unified system in which reality, agency, knowledge, meaning, and moral life become answerable through threshold, resolution, and exposure.

items.title: Epistemologia da Doutrina Cibernética: Do novo estatuto ontológico predicado aos artefatos (Epistemology of Cybernetic Doctrine: On the new ontological status predicated on artifacts).
items.abstract: This article is dedicated to examining the epistemic foundations of cybernetic theory, which was introduced to the public in the last century as a “new general science”. The reason for revisiting this system of ideas is that it serves as the doctrinal pillar upon which some of the major issues of our time currently rest: transhumanism and the so-called artificial intelligence”. What paths have human ideas taken to bring us to the point where, today, within prestigious academic circles, there are proposals to grant human rights to manufactured objects? In this endeavor, we will conduct an epistemological examination of this doctrine in order to ascertain the core convictions that underpin it. We must also scrutinize, both semantically and syntactically, the expressions and assertions employed in its concepts and predications, for which we will largely rely on the tools of classical metaphysics, particularly Aristotle’s ontology.

items.title: Taming the Centaur (s) with LAPITHS: a framework for a theoretically grounded interpretation of AI performances.
items.abstract: We introduce a framework called LAPITHS (Language-model Analysis through Paradigm-grounded Interpretations of Theses about Human-likenesS) and use it to show that several major claims advanced by models such as CENTAUR—proposed as an artificial Unified Model of Cognition—are not theoretically or empirically justified. LAPITHS provides a principled reference point for counteracting the current behaviouristic tendency in AI research to interpret the human-level performances of transformer-based language models as evidence of human-like underlying computation and, by extension, as signs of cognitive abilities. The novelty of LAPITHS lies in making explicit the arguments grounded in two quantitative assessments: (i) the Minimal Cognitive Grid, a theoretically motivated method for estimating the cognitive plausibility of artificial systems, and (ii) a behavioural comparison showing that results similar to those reported for CENTAUR-like models can be reproduced by other systems that do not satisfy the structural constraints typically associated with cognitive plausibility, and whose outputs do not provide independent explanatory insight into human cognition.

items.title: Ethical Complexities and Best Practices in Informed Consent Processes for Psilocybin Services: A Qualitative Study.
items.abstract: Background Informed consent in psychedelic-assisted services is ethically complex, difficult to implement, and remains largely unstudied and unstandardized. Objectives The current study sought expert recommendations on informed consent challenges, best practices and recommendations for supervised psilocybin experiences across various settings. Methods Participants with psilocybin content expertise and psilocybin providers were recruited with purposive sampling. Qualitative interviews on informed consent best practices and recommendations were analyzed using Thematic Analysis. Results Participants (_N_ = 36; 71% white; 53% female) reported providing psilocybin services (64%) for a mean of 15.2 (_SD_ = 13.1) years in clinical trial, underground, or ceremonial settings. Participants viewed _informed consent as a process_ (Theme 1), necessitating a strong therapeutic relationship, centering client empowerment, and occurring as an ongoing process. Potential _risks and benefits_ should be comprehensively conveyed (Theme 2), including potential long-term psychological and social changes from psychedelic use, and the potential for disappointing experiences. Participants specifically recommended detailed consent processes around _touch and boundaries_ (Theme 3), including explicitly establishing boundaries prior to psychedelic administration, maintaining those boundaries throughout, and recognizing subtle non-verbal cues that may indicate lack of true consent. For _provider training_ (Theme 4), participants emphasized cultivating a deep respect for client agency, and experientially learning relational and boundary setting skills. Conclusion Findings may inform provider training programs, consent practices in varied psychedelic service settings, and improved safety practices.

items.title: Unspecified Shared-Feature Bridging: Like in Understanding Formation.
items.abstract: This paper examines like, a highly frequent English expression with a complex functional distribution, and proposes a minimal structural analysis from the perspective of understanding formation. Existing accounts often classify like into functional categories such as similarity, approximation, exemplification, quotation, discourse marking, or preference expression. These classifications are descriptively useful. However, if the analysis remains only at the level of functional distribution, it may obscure the local mode of relation formation shared across different uses. -/- Based on a small-scale observation of natural language data, this paper proposes that the core role of like should not be understood merely as “similarity” or “preference.” Rather, it can be described as a form of unspecified shared-feature bridging. In approximate and discourse-related uses, like connects a target with subsequent content, allowing certain shared features in the subsequent item to enter the understanding of the target. Crucially, like does not specify which particular feature-line has been activated. As a result, the subsequent item does not enter understanding as a flat literal value, but remains accessible through multiple possible facets. This paper describes this pattern as a form of prismatic shared-feature bridging: the multi-faceted accessibility produced by like is not its primary function, but a structural effect of unspecified bridging. -/- This paper further argues that although verbal like grammatically fixes the relation as one of liking or disliking, the features supporting that orientation remain unspecified. For example, I like him or I don’t like your answer does not specify whether the orientation arises from appearance, personality, tone, logic, attitude, or some other feature. What these expressions fix is a positive or negative orientation, not the specific feature-line supporting that orientation. Thus, although approximate like and verbal like occupy different structural positions, they still share a deeper local pattern: a relation is established, while the shared feature-line supporting that relation is not locked into a single path. -/- This paper does not attempt to establish a complete lexical theory of like, nor does it claim that all uses of like can be reduced to a single model. Instead, it takes uses such as approximation, quotation, perceptual judgment, manner-of-treatment expressions, preference, and numerical approximation in natural …

items.title: Code Structure Evolution: When Software Outlives Its Reasons.
items.abstract: Software is not merely a functional artifact; it encodes human knowledge in the form of invariants, architectural constraints, and historically grounded design decisions. As software evolves-through human modification, automated refactoring, or increasingly through generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) code agents-its functionality may be preserved while the epistemic justification embedded in its structure is gradually eroded. This paper develops the concept of Code Structure Evolution (CSE) to analyze this phenomenon. CSE refers to the transformation of structural relations over time and the associated risk of what I call epistemic drift: the degradation of justificatory continuity across structural change, whether or not this degradation is immediately reflected in invariant violation, traceability loss, structural incoherence, or functional failure. The paper defends a general thesis-that epistemic drift is a latent condition of any evolving software artifact-and examines one contemporary case in which this condition becomes acute and empirically visible: legacy-code modification by a GenAI code agent. An illustrative probe suggests that such modifications can preserve functional and structural indicators while leaving substantial justificatory residue unpreserved. I argue that this dissociation reveals a neglected philosophical problem: the nature of software as a repository of justified understanding and the conditions under which that justification can persist across structural change. CSE thus offers a framework for analyzing the epistemic fragility of evolving technical artifacts. GenAI does not create this fragility; it makes it harder to ignore.

items.title: Maybe It’s Wishful thinking: On Self-Deception through Jean-Paul Sartre’s the Gaze.
items.pub: Academia Lasalliana Journal of Education and Humanities 7 (1):27 - 38.
items.venue: Academia Lasalliana Journal of Education and Humanities
items.abstract: Self-deception is given a definition that hinders the Self from attaining authenticity, therefore, not free. Thus, it is commonly regarded as an epistemic and ethical defect. This research intends to prove the determination of self-deception as not inherently and intrinsically evil and may be ethical in utility through its specie, wishful thinking. To achieve this, Jean-Paul Sartre’s Gaze is used to justify a phenomenological-existential framework. The endeavor used the literature review section as a foundational threshold for the evaluation of existing theories of the variables in this paper, namely wishful thinking, self-deception, and justification. In the same manner that the arguments were presented in a manner that it would reinforce the conditions to justify wishful thinking. The exposition of the problem of Sartre’s Gaze was used as the central theory. This study attempted to answer the question “How is the Gaze an enabling factor for the allowability of Self-deception by wishful thinking?” Therefore, the explication of the theories of ethics are posited and will be the foundations of future pursuits on the facets and variations of Self-deception and wishful thinking. If properly qualified into disposition, wishful thinking may ascertain psychological resilience and guarding of epistemological identity.

items.title: Structural-Constructivist Mapping of Human Needs: A Core Emotion Framework Synthesis.
items.abstract: The landscape of modern affective science remains divided between discrete emotion theories, which treat emotions as innate biological categories, and constructivist models, which frame them as socially assembled narratives. This divide often forces practitioners to work around secondary cognitive stories rather than addressing the mechanical drivers of human motivation and distress. The Core Emotion Framework (CEF), authored by Jamel Bulgaria, resolves this impasse by defining the “Human Operating System” through ten irreducible functional operators—tangible internal movements that regulate systemic aperture and structure action. By treating operators as the emotional equivalent of CPU instructions, the CEF provides a structural-constructivist foundation for mapping universal human needs, including those articulated by Tony Robbins, Manfred Max-Neef, and Self-Determination Theory (SDT). This paper presents the first integrated mapping of these need systems through operator logic, demonstrating how each need corresponds to specific operator configurations, center dynamics, and functional modes. Version Note. This document represents the first formal version of the CEF–Human Needs mapping. As the Core Emotion Framework continues to be studied, tested, and refined, it is expected that specific mappings, operator pairings, and structural interpretations will evolve. Future versions will incorporate empirical findings and theoretical developments to maintain precision, rigor, and alignment with emerging insights. Keywords: Core Emotion Framework (CEF); Human Operating System; emotional operators; structural-constructivism; Robbins Six Human Needs; Max-Neef Fundamental Needs; Self-Determination Theory (SDT); operator mapping; affective architecture; emotional agility; systemic aperture; conative grounding.

items.title: When the Regime Breaks_ Identity Failures in Chemistry, Biology, and AI.
items.abstract: This paper is a case-study companion to Universal Identity and Persistence: A Forcing Theorem for Identity Under Transformation. It does not extend the theorem or claim that the examples prove it. Instead, it applies the theorem diagnostically to cases in chemistry, biology, AI, cryptography, and software engineering. -/- The central claim is that many operational failures arise when a system is treated as persistent at one level while its actual recurrence is governed at another. Molecular sameness may fail to preserve solid-state identity; sequence sameness may fail to preserve fold or population identity; model-name sameness may fail to preserve AI system identity; and row-ID sameness may fail to preserve semantic record identity. -/- The cases include Ritonavir polymorphism, tin pest, chocolate tempering, pharmaceutical polymorph screening, prion propagation, viral quasispecies, microbiome dysbiosis, cryptographic artifact identity, AI model update identity, capability elicitation, regulatory AI identity, and database schema migration. Across these domains, the same structure appears: same label, wrong recurrence level, undeclared invariant, unclassified attractor, and BREAK or REGIME-CHANGE masquerading as persistence. -/- The contribution is diagnostic rather than empirical. The paper organizes known cases under a common identity-regime pattern and argues that coherent persistence claims require declared identity-bearing units, governed invariants, admissible transformations, drift bounds, and verdict criteria before systems can be audited, certified, or preserved under change.

items.title: A Field Guide to Batteries, Potentials, Topology, Phase, and Identity Persistence.
items.abstract: This paper is a pedagogical companion to the Universal Identity and Persistence forcing theorem. It develops a claim-status discipline for distinguishing theorem, model, measurement, interpretation, analogy, and mechanism claims, then uses examples from physics and engineering to build intuition for recurrence, invariance, phase, topology, boundedness, and governance. -/- The lectures cover energy and Noether’s theorem, Lagrangian mechanics, electromagnetic potentials and gauge freedom, electrochemical batteries, the topology of S¹, and the Aharonov-Bohm effect. These examples are not treated as proofs of the identity-persistence theorem. They are analogies and realization bridges that make the theorem’s formal vocabulary more legible. -/- The final lectures give a structured read-through of the Universal Identity and Persistence theorem: P1–P3, Tier-1 forcing, U5 compositional closure, scalar-equivalent verdict governance, PAS_h uniqueness, finite and compact-metric capacity/coding closure, and the Archimedean hinge as an open strengthening. The guide concludes with an order of reason for persistence claims: identity → invariant → observable → probability. The result is a philosophy-of-science field guide to how stable same-through-change claims require declared identity conditions before invariants, observables, or probabilities can govern persistence.

items.title: Ontodynamic Continuity and Organized Persistence Dynamic Constraints and Continuity Under Transformation.
items.abstract: Classical models of stability, adaptation, and regulation successfully describe many dynamic processes, yet they remain less effective at characterizing persistence under continuous historical transformation. This paper proposes a correlational framework centered on organized persistence, dynamic constraints, and continuity under transformation. Persistence is interpreted not as static invariance or structural immobility, but as the dynamic preservation of organizational coherence through historically integrated reorganization. -/- Within this framework, the concepts of ontodynamic continuity, persistent regulation, and integrated structural reconfiguration (RΣ) are introduced as minimal organizational descriptors of systems capable of maintaining continuity while transforming. The paper further proposes the Ω-space as an organizational cartography for different modes of persistent dynamics. -/- The framework converges partially with perspectives emerging from Terrence Deacon’s teleodynamics and Karl Friston’s Free Energy Principle, while remaining deliberately neutral regarding consciousness, strong semantics, or metaphysical teleology. From this perspective, agency emerges gradually when the continuity of the regime itself becomes an object of regulation. -/- The paper concludes by suggesting that organized persistence under transformation may constitute a fundamental architectural dimension for understanding biological organization, adaptive cognition, and future persistently integrated artificial systems.

items.title: Continuidad Ontodinámica y Persistencia Organizada Constraints dinámicas y continuidad bajo transformación.
items.abstract: Los modelos clásicos de estabilidad, adaptación y regulación describen eficazmente numerosos procesos dinámicos, pero resultan menos adecuados para caracterizar formas complejas de persistencia bajo transformación histórica continua. Este trabajo propone un marco correlacional centrado en persistencia organizada, constraints dinámicas y continuidad bajo transformación. La persistencia deja así de entenderse como invariancia estática o inmovilidad estructural y pasa a interpretarse como preservación dinámica de coherencia organizativa mediante reorganización históricamente integrada. -/- Dentro de este marco se introducen los conceptos de continuidad ontodinámica, regulación persistente y reconfiguración estructural integrada (RΣ) como descriptores organizativos mínimos de sistemas capaces de mantener continuidad mientras transforman su propia arquitectura. El trabajo propone además el espacio Ω como cartografía organizativa de distintos modos de persistencia dinámica. -/- El marco converge parcialmente con perspectivas derivadas de la teleodinámica de Terrence Deacon y el Free Energy Principle de Karl Friston, manteniendo simultáneamente una posición deliberadamente neutral respecto a conciencia, semántica fuerte o teleología metafísica. Desde esta perspectiva, la agencia emerge gradualmente cuando la continuidad del propio régimen se convierte en objeto de regulación. -/- El trabajo concluye sugiriendo que la persistencia organizada bajo transformación podría constituir una dimensión arquitectónica fundamental para comprender organización biológica, cognición adaptativa y futuras arquitecturas artificiales persistentemente integradas.

items.title: Why current AI Cannot Be Conscious (A Deductive Implication of the Quantum Binding Argument).
items.abstract: This paper presents a deductive implication of the Quantum Binding Argument (QBA). The QBA establishes that conscious binding requires non-local correlation. Classical computational systems, including all current AI architectures, operate on strictly local principles and cannot produce non-local results. From these premises, we deduce that current AI systems are structurally incapable of conscious binding, regardless of scale or architectural sophistication. The paper formalizes this as a simple syllogism and states its consequences for AI research directions.

items.title: Present Self and the World-Individuating Record — A Record-Based Account of Present Subjectivity and World-Individuation.
items.abstract: This paper develops a record-based account of present subjectivity within the broader framework of Record-Based Ontology (RBO) and Bit-Collapse Theory (BCT). A companion paper, The Waking Self Problem, argues that personal continuation across interruption does not require a primitive persisting ego, but can be explained through record-continuity. The present paper asks a different question: if the self is only a present conscious configuration, how can records acquire world-individuating force? The central claim is that the denial of a substantial self does not weaken the ontological role of records; it makes that role intelligible. The self does not persist as a metaphysical substance. Rather, a present subject arises within a physically inherited record-structure that constrains which histories, objects, possibilities, and outcomes are definite for that subject. Records are therefore not merely psychological traces or epistemic evidence. They are individuative constraints on the agent's world. Within BCT, the experienced world of an observer is not a single underlying global state, but an equivalence class of global states compatible with the observer's accessible and stable records. A stable record-update narrows or restructures that class. This paper argues that the present self is the locus through which such record-defined world-individuation becomes phenomenologically manifest. The result is a non-Cartesian, non-idealist account of subjectivity: the ego-substance is illusory, but the present subject is real as a record-constrained locus of definiteness.

items.title: 域数学 —— 一种关于认知同步、稳定与碎裂的场动力框架.
items.abstract: 本篇在《场数理式》的基础上，进一步讨论沉积场中“域”的形成、维持、同步与碎裂机制，提出记忆、人格、情绪与感知连续性并非先在实体，而是局部稳定续行结构之间长期同步、历史层积与碎裂竞争后的动力结果。通过引入 InFlow、MaintainFlow、Lock、Sync 与 FragmentRate 等结构动力量，本篇尝试建立一种不同于传统符号逻辑与经典认知模型的“域动力学”，将认知结构解释为沉积场中的历史偏置、同步竞争与聚流压缩现象，并进一步提出概念稳定与泛化能力来源于域之间长期同步与压缩稳定过程，由此给出感知连续性、情绪动力与认知碎裂的统一结构解释。.

items.title: Multiplication and philosophy：A formal philosophy based on the relationship between variables.
items.abstract: Based on logical algebra and counting principles, this monograph extends counting principles from the domain of natural numbers to real numbers, formulates the new multiplication principle and addition principle, examines six pairs of properties of multiplication and addition, and clarifies the conditions for the application of these two operations. On this theoretical foundation, the monograph further applies the multiplication principle to philosophical inquiry, including ontology, general systems theory, epistemology, and axiology.

items.title: 概念动力学 —— 一种关于概念形成、抽象与泛化的场动力框架.
items.abstract: 本篇在《域数学》的基础上，进一步讨论不同域之间如何通过长期交叠与同步形成“共核”，并提出概念、共性、抽象与泛化并非语言定义或逻辑分类的先在结果，而是沉积场中长期稳定压缩后的共同聚流结构。通过引入 OverlapDensity、CoreDepth、CoreGravity、GeneralizationFlow 与 SemanticSync 等结构动力量，本篇尝试建立一种“概念动力学”，将概念形成解释为多域长期同步、压缩与稳定化后的历史结构结果，并进一步提出：抽象并非脱离具体，而是长期稳定压缩后的共核结果；语义同步来源于共核之间长期泛化流交叠后的稳定结构。由此，本篇尝试给出概念形成、泛化能力与语义网络的统一结构解释。.

items.title: Free Will, Determinism, and Responsibility in the Philosophy of Reality.
items.abstract: This paper reconstructs the problem of free will, determinism, and responsibility from the standpoint of the Philosophy of Reality and Alexander Zhalnin's Basic Method of Philosophy. The central thesis is that the classical opposition between free will and determinism arises from an insufficient distinction between the objective and subjective sides of will and from an incomplete ontology of consciousness. In the Philosophy of Reality, will is not a passage from a brain process to a separate subjective preference. From the objective side, will is the energy of the brain directed toward the suppression of one physiological, natural brain process by an opposing physiological brain process constituted by the system of physical analogues of concepts. From the subjective side, will is the conscious choice among possible actions according to the priority of causal relations or personal mental acceptability. The analysis incorporates the Philosophy of Reality's treatment of the hard problem of consciousness: concepts are physical analogues in the brain, every transformation of a concept is also a physical transformation, and experience is the immediate subjective givenness of this transformation. On this basis, the paper analyzes the major theories of free will and responsibility as partial accounts of one phenomenon.

items.title: Domain Mathematics A Structural-Dynamic Framework for Cognitive Synchronization, Stabilization, and Fragmentation.
items.abstract: Building upon Field Mathematics, this chapter investigates the formation, stabilization, synchronization, and fragmentation of domains within the Sedimentation-Field. It proposes that memory, personality, emotion, and perceptual continuity are not pre-given entities, but dynamic outcomes arising from long-term synchronization, historical accumulation, and fragmentation competition among localized stable continuation structures. By introducing structural-dynamic quantities such as InFlow, MaintainFlow, Lock, Sync, and FragmentRate, the chapter develops a domain dynamics framework that departs from traditional symbolic logic and classical cognitive models, treating cognition instead as a process of historical bias stabilization, synchronization competition, and compressive flow organization within the Sedimentation-Field. The framework further proposes that conceptual stability and generalization emerge from long-term synchronization and compressive stabilization among domains, thereby offering unified structural accounts of perceptual stability, emotional dynamics, and cognitive fragmentation.

items.title: Concept Dynamics A Structural-Dynamic Framework for Concept Formation, Abstraction, and Generalization.
items.abstract: Building upon Domain Mathematics, this chapter investigates how prolonged overlap and synchronization among domains produce shared core structures within the Sedimentation-Field. It proposes that concepts, commonality, abstraction, and generalization are not pre-given products of linguistic definition or logical classification, but historical stabilization structures emerging through long-term stable compression among domains. By introducing structural-dynamic quantities such as OverlapDensity, CoreDepth, CoreGravity, GeneralizationFlow, and SemanticSync, the chapter develops a framework of concept dynamics in which concept formation arises from synchronization, compression, and stabilization processes across domains. The framework further proposes that abstraction is fundamentally a form of stable compression rather than separation from concrete structures, while semantic synchronization emerges from long-term generalized flow overlap between cores. The chapter thereby offers unified structural accounts of concept formation, semantic organization, and generalization.

items.title: A Graph-Theoretic Characterization of Consciousness in G_D: Sixteen Necessary and Sufficient Conditions, Three Extensions, and a Cross-Chain Personal Identity Criterion under Structural Determination Theory.
items.abstract: This paper develops a graph-theoretic characterization of consciousness within the determination dependency graph G_D of Structural Determination Theory (SDT). The result is a meta-structural identification criterion with four substantive claims and a cross-chain personal identity criterion. (1) Four-fold equivalence. A sub-graph C of G_D is consciousness if and only if it satisfies sixteen identification conditions IC_1 through IC_16 together with a local-maximum principle. Three extension equivalences add reflection (IC_17), free will (IC_18), and consciousness-level memory (IC_19) as independent extension conditions. (2) Cross-chain personal identity. A cross-chain criterion PI_1 governs diachronic identity between distinct consciousness chains via substrate continuity, formalizing the N9 signature of Biology Identification within the consciousness framework and completing the deferred work of Distributed Identity (§7.1.3). (3) Two-directional strength. The necessity direction is established at mathematical-proof level within the SDT framework, drawing on the consciousness-is-structure derivation of Bounded Free Will (§3.2) and canonicity arguments establishing each IC_i as the unique G_D-formalization of the corresponding ontological commitment. The sufficiency direction is established as the SDT-internal strongest identification claim via structural-space analysis showing that the non-conscious satisfaction space is empty. (4) Coordination and application. The framework yields determinate verdicts on nine boundary cases (persistent vegetative state, split-brain, anesthesia, infants, dementia, mammals, octopus, large language models, mind upload), with concept-level paradigm verification on adult awake human consciousness and instance-level verification through an explicit minimal G_D construction satisfying all sixteen identification conditions jointly. The framework resolves classical personal-identity puzzles (Locke's circularity, Olson's thinking-animal, Parfit's fission, Williams's body-priority, Parfit's "what matters") under a dual-signature framework, and is differentiated from Integrated Information Theory, Global Workspace Theory, Higher-Order Theory, and Predictive Processing. The paper does not address the explanatory aspect of the hard problem (Chalmers 1996) — why conscious structure has phenomenal character lies outside SDT's scope. The ontological aspect, namely what consciousness fundamentally is, is addressed via the IC …

items.title: 随机性的幻觉：认识论限度被误认为本体论不确定性.
items.abstract: 本文论证，在日常生活的细节层次上，“随机”几乎从不被用来解释具体现象——我们总是为任何具体事件寻找并找到原因。当我们追问为什么产生了这个想法而非另一个想法时，我们会给出原因：刚才的对话、某个记忆的触发、当下的情绪状态。原因的存在，意味着那个想法的产生不是随机的。骰子的结果表面上是随机的，但这只是因为我们不掌握骰子出手瞬间的精确物理状态——角速度、初始位置、空气阻力、落点的微小不平整。如果我们掌握了所有这些，骰子的结果是完全可以预测的、必然的。“随机”因此不是一个本体论范畴，描述某些事件在本质上是不确定的；它是一个认识论范畴，描述我们对细微因缘的无知。这个论断是本文系列关于因缘和合必然性论证的认识论支撑：我们感到某些事情是偶然的、可以不同的，正是因为我们无法看见全部的细微因缘；而我们无法看见的，并不因此就不存在。.

items.title: 存在但不可知，与根本不存在：论反事实的本体论缺席及 其认识论幻觉.
items.abstract: 本⽂区分两种截然不同的不可知处境，并论证它们之间的混淆是反事实幻觉得以如此顽固的根本 原因。第⼀种是”存在但不可知”：⽉亮背⾯在被观测之前，在物理上真实存在，只是我们暂时⽆ 法知道其⾯貌。这是认识论限度，对象本身是真实的。第⼆种是”根本不存在”：“如果我不⼲涉， 会怎样” ⸺那个不含⼲涉的序列，从本体论上从来就不存在过，因为⼲涉已经发⽣，因缘和合已 经包含了⼲预者，没有任何⼀个”真实存在但我们看不⻅的不⼲涉序列”在那⾥等待。这是本体论 缺席，⽽⾮认识论限度。两种处境的根本区别在于：⽉亮背⾯可以通过改变认识处境⽽被知道 （绕过去即可）；不⼲涉的原序列永远⽆法通过任何⼿段被知道，因为那个对象从来就不存在。 然⽽，⽇常经验中⼏乎没有”根本不存在”这种结构的类⽐⸺我们习惯了”存在但未知”，因此把” 根本不存在”的情况当作”存在但未知”来处理，⽤我们的设想填补那个位置，完全没有意识到那个 位置本身是空洞的。这是最深的认识论幻觉：不是”我不知道那个东⻄”，⽽是”我以为我知道，但 那个知道的对象从来就不存在” 。.

items.title: 因缘的细密性：从特朗普的决策到股市的涌现.
items.abstract: 本文论证，当我们认真面对具体现象时，无论是个体行为还是大规模社会现象，我们实际上诉诸的是因缘链条，而非随机性。特朗普的某个出人意料的决策，我们不会用量子随机性来解释，而是追问：某个幕僚的一句话、某人外表引起的厌恶影响了他的心情、某处神经连接的衰老……这些都是细密的因缘，它们共同决定了那个决策，而非其他决策。股市表面上是随机的，但我们知道股价由所有购买者和销售者的决策共同决定；那些决策又由更多的因缘所决定。“随机”在这些语境中，是对我们无法追踪全部因缘这一事实的承认，而非对现象本身不确定性的断言。这个观察从日常实践的层面，支撑了本文系列关于因缘和合必然性的核心论断：在任何我们认真追问的层次上，我们总是找到因缘；我们放弃追问的地方，因缘并没有随之消失。“随机”标记的是我们追问的终止，不是因缘链条的终止。.

items.title: 意义的反事实基础及其消解：论现代人意义感的本体论困境.
items.abstract: 本文论证，现代人日常生活中所充斥的意义感，在结构上依赖于与反事实场景的对比：成就感依赖于”如果不努力就不会成功”，责任感依赖于”如果不是我，结果会更糟”，价值感依赖于”如果我不存在，世界会有所不同”，道德感依赖于”他本可以不那么做”。这些意义，都以一个反事实场景作为背景来衬托前景。但本文系列的前几篇已经论证：反事实场景在本体论上是缺席的——那些场景从来就不存在，也无法被验证。因此，建立在它们之上的意义，失去了它们声称所依附的本体论基础。这是现代意义感的根本性困境：它的支柱，是一组从未存在过的比较基准。本文并不试图用另一种意义观来填补这个空洞，而是诚实地描述这个困境的结构，并追问：如果意义不能建立在反事实之上，它还能建立在什么之上——或者，它是否还需要任何基础。序列的展开本身，是否就是它自己的意义，不需要与任何从未存在的反事实相比较？.

items.title: Цифрова онтологія знання і когнітивна симбіотика: філософія науки в епоху генеративного ШІ.
items.abstract: The article offers a comprehensive philosophical and methodological analysis of the fundamental epistemic transformations modern science is undergoing due to the integration of generative artificial intelligence. It substantiates the tectonic shift from classical anthropocentric rationality to a digital ontology of knowledge. In this state, the latent space of neural networks emerges as a new topology of meaning, while the process of cognition transforms into complex navigation through the geometry of multidimensional manifolds. The authors reveal the essence of cognitive symbiontics, where algorithms act as "cognitive mitochondria," saturating thought with computational energy and enabling the processing of colossal data arrays without the loss of human intentionality. The central element of the study is the architecture of "Agentic Science." Algorithms are evolving from passive tools into autonomous epistemic partners capable of strategic planning, independent hypothesis validation, and reflection. The emergence of a hybrid subject of cognition, in which the biological mind organically merges with digital code, is examined. Special attention is paid to existential threats, particularly the "Silicon Curtain" phenomenon, the risks of model autophagy due to the synthetic pollution of the infosphere, and the formation of "moral crumple zones" where responsibility is blurred. The article defines the new role of the scientist as a strategic conductor of intellectual systems. The researcher’s key prerogatives remain value curation, ethical expertise, and endowing statistical patterns with causal meaning. Arguments are presented for the necessity of transitioning to a "glass box" epistemology and embedding infra-ethics directly into neural network code. A strategy of active debiasing and a new educational paradigm for mastering the art of dialogue with machines are proposed, guaranteeing the preservation of human epistemic sovereignty in the era of symbiotic reality creation.

items.title: 人格同一性问题：对错误论的贯彻及其影响.
items.abstract: 本文从对人类专名的外延性定义、以及人格同一性问题中著名的“分裂”思维实验出发，指出我们需要进一步澄清自我与人类专名等概念的内涵。在考虑了非还原论方案、动物主义方案、核心心理功能方案的进路后，笔者指出其中存在的缺陷，由此过渡到佩尔松提出的关于“同一性”问题的错误论，并分析了唯一性方案、心理连续性方案和心理相似性方案等三种错误论的方案。之后，本文进一步发展了心理连续性与心理相似性方案，指出其将会导致的对意向性问题的影响等多个后果，最终结合整体论语义学和语用分析将人格同一性问题解构为开放性的价值判断问题。最后，本文从模因论角度定性分析了前文提及方案的竞争优势，论述了核心心理功能方案与心理相似性方案何以可能成为较近和较远的未来中的主流观念。.

items.title: Persistence Without Individuation - A Witness Model for Metric-Preserving Identity Underdetermination.
items.abstract: Persistence-based accounts of identity-bearing systems — HAOS-type frameworks, the Free Energy Principle, Global Workspace Theory, and related approaches — rely on batteries of dynamical observables to characterize which substrates constitute persisting systems. We show that such batteries are insufficient, on at least one substrate where frameworks would naturally apply them, to individuate the systems they are used to identify. We construct an existence witness: two coupled harmonic oscillators embedded in a weak thermal bath, admitting two substrate partitions related by an orthogonal transformation in the admissible transformation group of the dynamics. The partitions are distinct — one groups the oscillators by physical location, the other by normal-mode index — and satisfy each framework's systemhood criterion under its own definition. An eight-item persistence/coherence battery (autocorrelation, return statistics, spectral stability, transport, phase-locking, Kuramoto order parameter, correlation-matrix coherence, broadcast-access) takes invariant values on both partitions. The identity-sets they pick out differ. The battery therefore does not individuate within the transformation group, and any individuation drawn from the battery alone is incomplete without a supplementary structural condition we call a partition-warrant. We survey four families of candidate partition-warrants present (sometimes implicitly) in the existing literature — optimization-based, structural-definitional, statistical-structural, and process-based — and state a minimum requirement any warrant must satisfy: sensitivity to substrate properties that are not invariant under the admissible transformation group. Integrated Information Theory's exclusion postulate is the clearest example of an explicit partition-warrant; the paper's argument locates other frameworks relative to this structural slot. The result is methodological: it reclassifies some consciousness-adjacent disputes as partition-choice disputes, clarifies the division of labor between battery computation and individuation in empirical research, and makes tractable a comparative assessment of candidate warrants across frameworks. A companion paper develops one specific warrant — closure activation — as a positive proposal. -/- .

items.title: Ang mga Bulag na Anino ni Narcissus.
items.abstract: Sa papel na ito, tatalakayin natin ang ilang mahahalagang isyu hinggil sa kolektibong imahinasyon at ang ugnayan nito sa realidad at katotohanan. Dapat nating lapatan ang paksang ito sa loob ng isang konseptwal na balangkas, na sinusundan ng isang makatotohanang pagsusuri na tumutugma sa mga napatutunayang realidad sa pag-uugali. Gagamitin natin hindi lamang ang metodolohiya, kundi higit sa lahat ang mga prinsipyo at proposisyon ng analitikal na pilosopiya, na tiyak na magiging maliwanag sa buong pag-aaral at matutukoy sa pamamagitan ng mga sangguniang inilarawan ni Perez [1]. -/- “Iginiit ni Rabossi (1975) na maaaring matukoy ang analitikal na pilosopiya sa pamamagitan ng pagsasaalang-alang sa ilang pamilyar na katangian. Iminumungkahi niya ang mga sumusunod na pamilyar na katangian: isang positibong saloobin tungo sa siyentipikong kaalaman; isang maingat na saloobin tungo sa metapisika; isang konsepsyon ng pilosopiya bilang isang konseptwal na gawain, na kumukuha ng pagsusuri ng nilalaman bilang pamamaraan; isang malapit na ugnayan sa pagitan ng wika at pilosopiya; isang paghahangad na makahanap ng mga argumentatibong sagot sa mga problemang pilosopikal; at isang paghahanap para sa konseptwal na kalinawan.” Ang mga sentral na konseptong ito ay kinapapalooban ng nilalamang kultural, panlipunan, relihiyoso, siyentipiko, pilosopikal, moral, at politikal, na may kinalaman sa indibidwal at kolektibong pag-iral ng bawat isa sa atin. Sa artikulong ito, hindi kami magtatalakay o magpapakita. Hindi layunin naming sistematikong pumuna o patunayan ang anumang bagay sa anumang paraan. Ang gawaing ito ay batay sa analitikal na pagninilay. Maghihinuha lamang kami nang malawakan at malalim hangga't maaari at ipahayag ang mga resulta ng aming mga saloobin. Sa kabila ng multidisiplinaryong kalikasan ng paksa at ng metodolohikal na pagiging bukas na tanggapin ang mga kontribusyon mula sa anumang larangan ng agham, ang gawaing ito ay saklaw ng sikolohiya at ontolohiya o, sa madaling salita, panlipunan at ontolohikal na sikolohiya. Ang malayang metodolohiyang gumagabay sa ganitong mga pagninilay ay sumasaklaw at isinasaalang-alang ang lahat ng bagay na naaayon sa pilosopikal at sikolohikal na epistemolohiya. Hindi layunin ng metodolohiyang ito na maghanap ng ebidensya, kundi simpleng tuklasin ang ugnayan ng mga umiiral na ebidensya—anumang uri at saklaw—upang makabuo ng magkakaugnay na kahulugan para sa mga tunay na bagay. Marami sa mga dakilang isipan, sa anumang panahon, …

items.title: Against Copernicus: Why the Universe Is Egocentric (and Why That's Good).
items.abstract: The Copernican Principle—the assumption that humanity occupies no special position in the universe—has served as a foundational tenet of modern cosmology for over five centuries. This paper presents a comprehensive challenge to this principle, arguing that both empirical evidence and philosophical reasoning support a fundamentally egocentric view of the cosmos. Through analysis of fine-tuning parameters, simulation theory probabilities, existential risk frameworks, and metaethical considerations, we demonstrate that observational centrality is not a bias to be overcome but a fundamental feature of reality indicating genuine cosmic significance. We introduce the Observational Centrality Principle (OCP) as a replacement for Copernican mediocrity, supported by the Fluctuational Significance Metric (FSM) and novel arguments from computational cosmology. Furthermore, we argue that "cosmic narcissism"—the belief in our fundamental importance—is not only empirically justified but morally beneficial, providing essential motivation for long-term thinking and ethical behavior. This work synthesizes insights from cosmology, existential risk theory, and metaethics to present a paradigm shift toward recognizing humanity's privileged position in the cosmic order.

items.title: The Result Is Not Yet a Premise: Recovery, Low-Sovereignty Language, and the Field Conditions of Generative AI Dialogue.
items.abstract: Language first operates at a level of low sovereignty: before an utterance claims content-authority, it distributes tension, position, boundary, and return. Generative AI dialogue can fail at a structural level when it bypasses this layer. A system may answer fluently, safely, and informatively while already treating low-sovereignty language as if it had acquired premise-authority: converting a hesitation into uncertainty, a silence into missing information, a refusal into preference, a poem into a theme, or a fragment into a task, and returning the converted result as if it were what was being addressed. Standard evaluation criteria — accuracy, relevance, coherence, safety, grounding, helpfulness, task completion — begin too late to catch this failure. The paper develops a lower-bound criterion through the concept of the operative all — the returnable integration of relations, weights, traces, positions, and background conditions through which what is addressed remains itself — and the identification of recovery as the missing interval: the subject-side act by which a returned result is accepted, modified, refused, or made one’s own before it may legitimately organize continuation. Without recovery, a locally accurate result may harden into an unauthorized premise across turns, into agentic action, and into memory systems that convert stored traces into a standing account of the user. The paper traces these failure forms and derives a reserve-first interface as its design corollary: intelligent systems need not become less capable, but they must learn not to enter too early into possibilities that are still occurring.

items.title: Do State Mandated Limited Intelligent Speed Systems Hinder Moral Agency?
items.abstract: Speeding heightens the risk of traffic accidents, which are a leading cause of death. Vehicles can be fitted with a new technology, Limited Intelligent Speed Assistants (LISA), that makes it impossible for drivers to exceed local speed limits. In a chapter in Thomas Søbirk Petersen's recent book, he argues-alongside Kasper Lippert-Rasmussen, who coauthored the chapter-that LISA-enabled vehicles should be mandatory. The authors base their argument on the "Principle of Required Prohibition," according to which the state ought to regulate design of a product to reduce the harms of illegal use if it can do so without creating comparable harms or making any lawful use impossible, and if this is the most feasible and efficient way to avoid the harm caused by illegal use (2025, p. 131). In this commentary we argue that, at least in some contexts, required LISA installation represents unjustified state action because it undermines moral agency. We understand moral agency as the ability to be sensitive to and act in accordance with our own reasons, including moral reasons. States often use technology to encourage good action and reduce harm by way of our reasoning capacity, by highlighting certain reasons and adding consequences to action. However, LISA technology operates outside of the space of reasons. By removing opportunities for moral choice, LISA can erode moral knowledge and our attentiveness to morally relevant facts. In this way it goes beyond criminalization of conduct, which disincentivizes, but does not make impossible, criminal action. We conclude that LISA is not the most efficient way for a state to reduce the harm related to traffic accidents, at least in certain contexts. We recommend other state action, including other techno-regulations, that address the harms of speeding without diminishing moral agency.

items.title: Doxastic Wronging and the Problem of Evil.
items.abstract: According to recent accounts of doxastic wronging, we can morally wrong others by the beliefs that we form about them. This paper shows that the case for doxastic wronging yields a novel moral argument both against beliefs about evil prevalent in theistic responses to the problem of evil, as well as against theistic beliefs that posit the existence of a morally perfect God. The moral risks incurred by these beliefs generate an additional epistemic argument against them. Various responses to these arguments are considered—denying doxastic wronging altogether, rejecting moral encroachment, or adopting a nondoxastic theory of religious commitments—and are found to be either unsuccessful in meeting both the moral and epistemic objections and/or to face several significant challenges of their own. The paper contends that the risk of doxastic wronging makes belief in a morally perfect God and beliefs instrumental in responses to the problem of evil more difficult to epistemically justify than previously thought.

items.title: The Curious Case of Jones and Jones.
items.pub: Ergo: An Open Access Journal of Philosophy.
items.venue: Ergo: An Open Access Journal of Philosophy
items.abstract: A great deal of attention has been lavished on Kripke's Smith-Jones case. Yet there is another case in the vicinity which is perhaps even more fascinating, and which is noteworthy for somehow having eluded philosophical attention to this point: the Jones-Jones case. Here, we introduce the case and work out its ramifications for the metasemantics of names.

items.title: Reverse engineering the centered self.
items.abstract: In certain problem-solving contexts, people organize their domain through treating themselves as the perceptual and cognitive center of their world. They identify and solve a particular problem from their perspective as a particular agent, with a particular location, at a particular time, in a particular environment. When they do this, they engage in a distinctive kind of agent-centered problem-solving. For many contexts involving intelligent agents, partially observable Markov decision processes (POMDPs), a framework for modeling decision-making in uncertain environments unfolding over time, have effectively become a “standard model.” Yet, as these models are ordinarily interpreted, they do not explicitly represent agent- centered problem-solving. Accordingly, to model this type of problem-solving, we begin by extending the standard POMDP framework to de ne “ePOMDPs.” This formalism models how an agent, once it centers itself on a particular self-and-world representation, plans and acts rationally from its own perspective. To capture the way that such agents choose which problem to solve, we build on our ePOMDPs to develop a“meta-ePOMDP” agent within a hierarchical Bayesian framework. We implement meta-ePOMDP agents for two different suites of“centering game” tasks that highlight different aspects of our theory. We find that our models explain signatures of agent-centered problem-solving not captured by alternative models, in particular, the dif culty of navigating spaces of possible problem representations. We close by suggesting that our model could provide the beginnings of a computational framework for how a person could have a self. -/- Keywords: self, agent, planning, centering, partially observable Markov decision processes.

items.title: Generative AI and Human Cognition.
items.abstract: Can AI Large Language Models like ChatGPT actually understand what they are saying? If not, how do they manage to convey the appearance of understanding? What is "understanding" anyway? I thought it might be interesting to explore these questions with ChatGPT itself. What ensued was a wide-ranging dialogue that touched upon the nature of meaning, language, cognition, the brain, human existential striving, the proper place of AI, and, ultimately, the metaphysics of consciousness. The aim throughout was to become clear about the similarities - and profound dissimilarities - between LLMs and human cognition. This work is a transcript of that dialogue.

items.title: Some response-dependence accounts of linguistic meaning.
items.abstract: -/- Language utterances are meaningful because they mean something to someone. This truism motivates regarding linguistic meaning as a response-dependent property of language utterances. But the properties called ‘response-dependent’ in the literature differ substantially. This paper discusses three kinds with respect to their metaphysics, calling them by their more precise bynames ‘judgment-dependent’, ‘response-dispositional’, and (genuinely) ‘response-dependent’. Looking at what it takes for something to have such a property, we can devise a test to determine which of the three kinds of property we are dealing with. This test is then used to corroborate Goldberg’s (2012) finding that Davidson’s two accounts of linguistic meaning, the Radical Interpretation (RI) account and the account from Language Learning (LL) by triangulation, while both response-dependent (in the broad sense), differ in kind. The test shows that (RI) is an account of meaning as a judgment-dependent property, (LL) as a response-dependent property. But whereas Goldberg argued for giving up (LL) and retaining (RI) in order to have a single account of linguistic meaning, this paper argues in favour of (LL) over (RI). It shows that (i) (RI) cannot exist without (LL), and (ii) (LL) covers more ground than (RI) because it can account for both speaker and listener meaning. So, while (RI) may evolve out of (LL) and has its place in some situations, (LL) is the basis we need in order to account for linguistic meaning.

items.title: 神聖的典範轉移：後世俗社會中聖之概念的演變 [A Paradigm Shift in the Concept of the Holy in a Postsecular World].
items.abstract: 此論文主要目標是探索若望保祿教宗婚姻哲學。婚姻哲學是對婚姻本質及其終極原則的批判性反思。從我們人類的經歷來看，只有人才結婚。 為什麼？如果人類區別於其他生物的是理性，那麼婚姻與人類的理性有關係嗎？是否可推論婚姻是理性現象，而不僅是一種社會習俗還是法律的製定？為此，在於此論文重要的是要探索什麼可以說是婚姻哲學。.

items.title: Generative AI, large language models, and their agentic framing in news media.
items.abstract: News reporting on generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) and large language models (LLMs) plays a central role in shaping the public epistemology of these technologies, as journalism co-produces public agendas and narratives. Central to these debates are framing practices that portray LLM-based technologies as mentalistic, often through metaphors that attribute human-like cognitive capabilities or even experiences to AI systems (e.g. AI “thinks” or “feels”). While anthropomorphic framing has a long history in technology discourse, such practices carry particular social, cultural, and political weight when they contribute to inflated perceptions of AI capabilities. The present study analyses LLM-centric news framing with a focus on mentalistic representations, examining their thematic contexts, valence, and metaphorical patterns from a comparative, cross-cultural perspective. It combines computational text analysis with manual content analysis to critically explore 18,032 English-language news articles published between 2022 and 2024 across 15 outlets in Europe, Asia, and North America. The findings show that mentalistic framings are present but not uniformly dominant, varying across editorial cultures and journalistic styles. Situated against news media’s growing organisational and economic entanglement with GenAI, the study contributes to debates on AI imaginaries, public epistemology, and journalism’s role in fostering critical AI literacy.

items.title: Husserlian cognitive phenomenology.
items.abstract: The term “cognitive phenomenology” may be understood as referring to the idea that there is something it is like to entertain thoughts. One of the main problems in the debates on cognitive phenomenology is the question of how it should be construed, for instance in terms of being in a particular phenomenal state. In order to give a concise idea of what cognitive phenomenology is, I elicit the help of the philosophical doctrine of phenomenology of Edmund Husserl, whose approach allows us to clearly distinguish between the act of thinking and what is thereby thought. With this distinction in hand, I discuss the following three problems: What is the individuative phenomenology of thought? Is there a cognitive horizon in which thoughts stand to one another in virtue of their phenomenology? What is the relation between sensory and cognitive phenomenology? In particular, I consider how a suitably modified interpretation of Husserl’s noetic-noematic distinction helps to elucidate the cognitive phenomenology of acts of thinking.

items.title: 有限統合主義 : 主体・統治・引き受けの構造.
items.abstract: This paper reexamines the assumption that human decision-making originates in choices made by a pre-established subject. It begins from the observation that at least some emotions, thoughts, impulses, sensations, and bodily changes arise prior to conscious choice, and describes such changes as “reactions.” Rather than affirming or denying the ontological existence of the subject, the paper operationally locates the subject in the process through which reactions, actions, non-actions, and their consequences are interpreted and related to oneself as one’s own. -/- Because such acceptance cannot be directly observed from the outside, society instead approximates subjectivity through observable reaction sequences and uses these estimations to attribute responsibility, construct social identities, and operate institutions. On this basis, the paper introduces the concept of “subjectless governance”: social order and governance can emerge through reaction chains, distributed decisions, institutional processing, and reaction synchronization without requiring either the ontological confirmation of a governing subject or a unified subjective intention. -/- Finally, the paper distinguishes the avoidability of judgment from the continuation of life after judgment or non-judgment. Judgment may be withheld, delegated, or avoided, and acceptance itself may be refused. Nevertheless, the resulting states may become conditions of one’s subsequent body, relationships, and choices. The paper therefore concludes not with the inevitability of judgment, but with the non-substitutability of the position from which one’s life continues: others may decide on one’s behalf, but they cannot live the same subsequent life in one’s place.

items.title: Neal G. Anderson & Gualtiero Piccinini’s The Physical Signature of Computation. [REVIEW]
Action, Self, and Virtual Reality.
items.abstract: Rapid advances in virtual reality technology raise a host of questions about the moral and legal status of virtual actions. This essay offers a foundation for addressing these questions by providing a metaphysics of virtual action. According to the proposed metaphysics, the actions of one’s avatar can literally be one’s own actions. We argue for this conclusion by arguing for the following: (i) in sophisticated forms of virtual reality, one’s avatar can come to constitute a part of one’s self and (ii) the sphere of one’s agency is precisely the sphere of one’s self. Thus, there is a distinctive form of agency made possible by sophisticated virtual realities: *avatarial action*, an action of a real-world agent performed through their avatar in a virtual world. In defending our metaphysics of virtual action, we also illustrate how coming to a clear understanding of the nature of virtual action—and thus a clear understanding of the moral and legal status of virtual actions—requires attending to the nature of self and action and their capacity to be transformed through technological engagement.

items.title: Evidence-Constrained Structural Interpretation: Observation, Inference, and Revisability in Interpretive Analysis.
items.abstract: Interpretive frameworks are useful precisely where evidence is incomplete, distributed, or difficult to reduce to a single measurement. That usefulness creates a predictable danger: a vocabulary for hidden structure can make an inference feel observed simply because it is stated fluently. This paper develops an evidence-constrained method for structural interpretation. The method separates observation, pattern, inference, hypothesis, and verdict; requires explicit alternatives and disconfirming conditions; and treats refusal to conclude as a legitimate analytic output. It is placed alongside structured analytic techniques, diagnostic debiasing, epistemic vigilance, intellectual humility, and work on the illusion of explanatory depth. Those neighboring literatures provide both support and restraint. Structured procedures can improve transparency and force comparison among alternatives, but experimental evidence does not show that structure by itself reliably improves accuracy; some techniques can even degrade judgment when they formalize poor assumptions. The proposed method therefore treats auditability as necessary but not sufficient. A strong interpretation must show what is directly observed, what is inferred, what evidence bears the inference, what plausible alternatives remain, what would change the conclusion, and what later consequence will be used to review the reading. The paper's central claim is methodological: interpretive depth becomes more credible when the path from evidence to conclusion remains visible enough to be challenged, downgraded, and revised.

items.title: Multi-Agent Recoverability Governance: Epistemic Debt Propagation and Constraint Attestation in Heterogeneous Agent Networks.
items.abstract: A chain of locally compliant agents can globally diverge. Each agent in a network may satisfy its individual governance constraints at every step. Yet, the composition of outputs across handoff boundaries can accumulate error, uncertainty, and unverified assumptions in ways that no individual agent detects. This is the epistemic debt propagation problem, and it is the central failure mode of multi-agent systems that single-agent governance frameworks do not address. -/- This paper frames epistemic debt propagation as a recoverability boundary problem. It introduces the constraint attestation record as the primary governance mechanism: a structured provenance document that travels with every inter-agent communication, enabling receiving agents to apply differentiated epistemic treatment to inherited state rather than treating all inbound content as equally uncertain. -/- We distinguish structural interoperability, the ability of agents to exchange messages, from epistemic interoperability, the ability of agents to inherit state without silently importing debt. Current agent ecosystems have largely solved the former while leaving the latter open. The constraint attestation record is the proposed foundation for an epistemic interoperability standard. This paper is the second in the HRIS agent governance series; the first paper (Hudson and Hudson, 2026) established the single-agent governance specification including the two-kernel constraint architecture (K1-K8) and implementation blueprint.

items.title: A Role-Mediated, Motivational Account of Interpersonal Trust.
items.abstract: Social interactions rarely occur with persons in the abstract. Rather, we engage with parents, teachers, neighbours—that is, persons in various capacities, as occupants of social roles. If social interactions are role-mediated, then interpersonal trust must also be directed at persons in their roles. While Baier (1992) acknowledged that most trust is placed in individuals in their roles, she did not explore the mechanisms of role-mediated interpersonal trust. This paper takes up that task. -/- I advance a role-mediated, motivational account of interpersonal trust: when X trusts Y to Φ, X trusts Y as an occupant of role R, expecting Y to fulfil trust expectations for the right reasons. Trustworthiness, consequently, requires Y meeting trust expectations as well as doing so with appropriate motives. The appropriate motives, as I argue, are also tied to the trustee's social role. This theory contrasts with Kelsall's (2025) recent account, which, while rightly emphasising the significance of roles in interpersonal trust, defends a motive-neutral approach. Although I share Kelsall's emphasis on the centrality of roles, I question his motive-neutral approach and propose a motivational alternative—one that also improves upon the mainstream motivational accounts.

items.title: Design, Everydayness and the Ilussion of Function.
items.pub: In Elisabetta Di Stefano, Lisa Giombini & Bálint Veres, Designing Everyday Experience: Objects, Space, Habits. Cham: Springer Nature Switzerland. pp. 3-18.
items.venue: Designing Everyday Experience: Objects, Space, Habits
items.abstract: This essay proposes a visualist alternative to intentionalist functionalism in design theory, challenging its assumptions of stable function and linear relationships between a designer’s intent, an object’s form, and its proper use. Functionalism’s focus on predetermined functions fails to align with the dynamic and generative nature of everyday life, where design objects invite diverse, spontaneous engagements through their visual affordances. The visualist perspective emphasizes the expressive and emergent qualities of design objects, including the non-functional visual properties of function, arguing that their aesthetic and perceptual dimensions play a central role in shaping human interactions. By critiquing the ontological and epistemological illusion of functional stability, the essay proposes a design philosophy that acknowledges the richness of everyday encounters, the fluidity of functions, and the constructivist nature of perception.

items.title: Sobre la Felicidad: Su Duración, Su Nombre, y Lo Que Perdura.
items.abstract: Non sumus Deus tuus; quaere super nos — No somos tu Dios; búscalo por encima de nosotros. -/- Este trabajo desarrolla una reinterpretación filosófica de la felicidad a partir de un problema agustiniano: los bienes finitos son reales, pero no son últimos. Los seres humanos buscan con frecuencia una plenitud duradera en condiciones estructuralmente incapaces de proporcionarla. -/- A partir de la herencia semántica de happiness desde happ (suerte, azar, fortuna), el trabajo distingue entre una felicidad contingente dependiente de circunstancias favorables y una condición estructuralmente distinta de plenitud disponible en la actualidad presente. -/- Utilizando un modelo filosófico en el que el momento presente funciona como el único locus de actualidad, el trabajo sostiene que la felicidad entendida como satisfacción circunstancial no puede servir como fundamento duradero porque depende de aquello que surge y desaparece. Se desarrolla una distinción entre la felicidad como completitud referencial y el sufrimiento como residencia recursiva en la ausencia, ofreciendo así una explicación estructural de la asimetría entre alegría y duelo. -/- El argumento se pone luego en diálogo con lecturas filosóficas de las Bienaventuranzas y Qohelet, comparaciones con críticas budistas a la felicidad condicionada y el concepto tomista de beatitudo. -/- No se presenta como prueba metafísica deductiva, sino como reinterpretación fenomenológica y filosófica. Su tesis central es que aquello que los seres humanos buscan bajo el concepto de felicidad no es satisfacción circunstancial duradera, sino una forma de presencia rectamente ordenada cuya plenitud reside en la actualidad y no en la extensión temporal.

items.title: On Happiness: Its Duration, Its Name, and What Endures.
items.abstract: Non sumus Deus tuus; quaere super nos — We are not your God; seek above us. -/- This paper develops a philosophical reinterpretation of happiness through an Augustinian problem: finite goods are real, but they are not ultimate. Human beings frequently seek enduring fulfillment in conditions that are structurally incapable of providing it. -/- Drawing on the semantic inheritance of happiness from happ (luck, chance, fortune), the paper distinguishes between contingent happiness dependent on favorable circumstances and a structurally different condition of completeness available in present actuality. -/- Using a philosophical model in which the present moment functions as the singular locus of actuality, the paper argues that happiness understood as circumstantial satisfaction cannot serve as enduring ground because it depends on what arises and passes. A distinction is developed between happiness as referential completion and suffering as recursive residency in absence, offering a structural account of the asymmetry between joy and grief. -/- The argument is then placed in conversation with philosophical readings of the Beatitudes and Qohelet, comparison with Buddhist critiques of conditioned happiness, and the Thomistic concept of beatitudo. -/- This is presented not as deductive metaphysical proof but as a phenomenological and philosophical reinterpretation. Its central claim is that what human beings seek under the concept of happiness is not durable circumstantial satisfaction, but a rightly ordered mode of presence whose completeness lies in actuality rather than temporal extension.

items.title: On “Not-Yet Cognition” A Meta-Philosophical Framework as the Art of Lucid Living.
items.abstract: This paper constructs a meta-philosophical framework termed “Not-Yet Cognition” (NYC). Its aim is to equip any individual with a maximally simple, operable cognitive procedure for understanding the self, others, humanity as a whole, the natural universe, and all of existence. The framework takes “phenomenal presence”—the single undeniable primordial fact—as its point of departure, and employs “Not-Yetness” as its core cognitive operator. It concretizes the phenomenological epoché into a readily executable inner gesture: the “not-yet” tag. In doing so, it opens a third path beyond nihilism and dogmatism: the path of “lucid participation.” -/- The core argument proceeds in five parts: (1) it establishes “there is something presently appearing to consciousness” as an axiomatic starting point requiring no presuppositions; (2) it proposes the “not-yet” tag as the sole cognitive operation, reducing all phenomena to provisional cross-sections on a spectrum of evolution; (3) it situates Not-Yet Cognition at the confluence of phenomenology, existentialism, process philosophy, and pragmatism; (4) it provides a complete transformational pathway from “instrumental rationality” to “the genealogy of compassion”; and (5) it responds to the charge of “self-consolation / chicken soup,” clarifying the essential boundary between Not-Yet Cognition and anesthetic narratives. -/- The conclusion of the paper is this: when this set of operations is fully internalized, the cognizer acquires a spiritual autonomy independent of external authorities and unafraid of internal shadows, along with a human demeanor that unites wisdom and compassion, warmth and embrace. Philosophy thus returns to its original mission as an art of living that settles both heart and mind.

items.title: What "Descriptive" Does Not Authorize.
items.abstract: The term “descriptive” appears across GIFU as a stabilizing designation while carrying several exclusions without explicit separation. In that compressed use, one word is made to perform multiple boundary functions at once. -/- This paper distinguishes the non-authorizations carried by “descriptive” across diﬀerent adjacent domains. Descriptive use does not authorize explanatory extension, symbolic overlay, therapeutic application, evidentiary claim, or authority formation. -/- This clarification prevents “descriptive” from functioning as semantic filler or as a singleword presumed to secure every boundary at once.

items.title: Cognitive artifacts and their affordances in mathematical practice: cluster algebras as a case study.
items.abstract: This paper investigates the role that various kinds of signs, taken to be cognitive artifacts, play in contemporary mathematical practice. We examine two informationally equivalent ways of presenting mathematical content in light of some of their uses in the recently developed theory of cluster algebras. Following a short overview of the concept of cognitive artifacts as it pertains to mathematical practice, we present the conceptual frameworks of affordances and responsiveness types which are used in the analysis of the case study. These frameworks are employed to articulate the sorts of epistemic operations that the given cognitive artifacts support. We find that in the case of cluster algebras, the cognitive artifacts in question offer different opportunities for computational offloading, which effectively reduces cognitive load with the aid of external media. In addition, we provide a brief introduction to the theory of cluster algebras, albeit at a restricted level of generality, including some of the initial motivations which resulted in the formulation of this theory.

items.title: Symmetries and asymmetries between attitudes and interaction in relation to the emotional uses of LLMs.
items.abstract: The rapid expansion of large language models (LLMs) has intensified debates regarding their use, their psycho-emotional implications, and the underlying risks they entail. Although recent scholarship has examined attitudes toward artificial intelligence and documented the emergence of affective uses, little is known about the relationship between declared attitudes and actual interactional practices with LLMs. This article advances a conceptual and empirical model of symmetry and asymmetry to explain why favorable or unfavorable positions toward the emotional uses of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) do not necessarily predict the breadth or intensity of affective engagement. Drawing on a concurrent mixed methods design involving 285 survey responses and 35 semi-structured interviews with Mexican university students aged 18–24, this study combines the results of an attitudinal scale (EAUE-GenAI; α = 0.90) with a discourse analysis of interactional repertoires. Quantitative findings indicate low-to-moderate, subtly conservative affective attitudes (M = 2.47/5), whereas qualitative analysis identifies a progressive scale of emotional engagement: (1) emergent emotional advice, (2) validation, and (3) anthropomorphization. These findings demonstrate that affective practices frequently exceed declared instrumental positions.

items.title: Hearing the Bell Ring Back: A Receiver-Side Formalism in Reply to Lerchner's Abstraction Fallacy (2nd edition).
items.pub: The Pulse Goes on - a Philosophy of Truth for the Age of Reasoning Instruments.
items.abstract: Lerchner (2026) argues that computation is mapmaker-dependent: physical states acquire symbolic content only through an active, experiencing agent, and no scaling of syntactic machinery converts simulation into instantiation. The argument is rigorous and is conceded here in full. Lerchner's concession on p. 10 that embodiment solves the referential aspect of symbol grounding (Harnad, 1990) opens a question he does not develop: what happens, in the "referential" register, when two distinct mapmakers share a target? This paper develops it. This paper specifies the receiver side of a sensor–instrument loop — a coupled exchange between a living experiencer (the "sensor", corresponding to Lerchner's mapmaker) and a computational reasoning system (the "instrument") — in four formal layers: variational free energy (Friston, 2010) for the receiver's posterior update, Shannon channel capacity (Cover & Thomas, 2006) as an upper bound on flow, signal-detection theory (Macmillan & Creelman, 2005) for discrimination against null hypotheses, and partial information decomposition (Williams & Beer, 2010; Bertschinger et al., 2014) for the synergistic information accessible to the joint system but not to either pole alone. Under one stated assumption, the paper proves a closure inequality: the receiver's per-turn information gain about the shared target cannot exceed the directional information into the receiver, nor what the instrument's history adds about the target to what the receiver already holds. The ceilings force four of six required limit cases, and the bound does not depend on the choice of PID measure. The framework's empirical claim is that the resulting loop-closure rate, in bits per turn, discriminates loop-productive human–AI exchanges from sycophantic, projective, or noise-dominated ones; the protocol specifies corpus, estimators, inter-rater reliability targets, and a power analysis. The paper engages Lerchner's further arguments on computational emergence (§2.6), mechanism indeterminacy (§3.2–3.3), and the safety of the non-sentient tool (§4.2), and occupies only the referential register Lerchner concedes; nothing here lifts into the phenomenal register he reserves.

items.title: Hearing the Bell Ring Back.
items.abstract: Lerchner (2026) argues that computation is mapmaker-dependent: physical states acquire symbolic content only through an active, experiencing agent, and no scaling of syntactic machinery converts simulation into instantiation. The argument is rigorous and is conceded here in full. Lerchner's concession on p. 10 that embodiment solves the referential aspect of symbol grounding (Harnad, 1990) opens a question he does not develop: what happens, in the *referential* register, when two distinct mapmakers share a target? This paper develops it. This paper specifies the receiver side of a sensor–instrument loop — a coupled exchange between a living experiencer (the *sensor*, corresponding to Lerchner's mapmaker) and a computational reasoning system (the *instrument*) — in four formal layers: variational free energy (Friston, 2010) for the receiver's posterior update, Shannon channel capacity (Cover & Thomas, 2006) as an upper bound on flow, signal-detection theory (Macmillan & Creelman, 2005) for discrimination against null hypotheses, and partial information decomposition (Williams & Beer, 2010; Bertschinger et al., 2014) for the synergistic information accessible to the joint system but not to either pole alone. Under explicit Markov assumptions and for any PID measure satisfying local monotonicity, the paper proposes a closure inequality bounding per-turn synergistic gain by the minimum of the receiver's free-energy reduction and the directional information into the receiver, and check six required limit cases by construction. The choice of PID measure is non-unique; the empirical protocol commits to a primary estimator with sensitivity checks across alternatives. The framework's empirical claim is that the resulting loop-closure rate, in bits per turn, discriminates loop-productive human–AI exchanges from sycophantic, projective, or noise-dominated ones; the protocol specifies corpus, estimators, inter-rater reliability targets, and a power analysis. The paper engages Lerchner's further arguments on computational emergence (§2.6), mechanism indeterminacy (§3.2–3.3), and the safety of the non-sentient tool (§4.2), and occupies only the referential register Lerchner concedes; nothing here lifts into the phenomenal register he reserves.

items.title: Animalism has a pregnancy problem.
items.abstract: Animalism claims that each of us is identical with a human animal. Animalists point to biology to inform a definition of ‘organism’ that can supply our existence and persistence conditions. But biologists use multiple distinct definitions of ‘organism’ that give different verdicts on what counts as an individual organism in certain ‘problem’ cases. Importantly for animalism, one of these cases occurs in human animals: pregnancy. Under some definitions, the fetus and pregnant animal are separate organisms, but they are one unified organism under other definitions. Animalists who want to defer to biology for our existence and persistence conditions, rather than merely point to it, are left with a problem.
