They cannot choose just one definition of organism, but neither can they accept a plural notion of organism while preserving the structure of their central claim that we are human animals. The case of pregnancy shows that animalism cannot pass the buck for defining the existence conditions of animals to biologists, and reveals a challenge for the view in accounting for our existence as individuals throughout the duration of our life cycles.

items.title: The epistemic readiness gap: rethinking AI readiness indices through ILIA 2025.
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) readiness indices have become central instruments in global AI governance, ranking states according to their apparent capacity to develop, regulate and benefit from AI. These instruments typically privilege digital infrastructure, research output, innovation and the existence of formal strategies, while giving less systematic attention to whose knowledge is encoded in AI systems, who participates in governing them, and how AI-mediated decisions can be understood and contested. This article examines these tensions through the Latin American Artificial Intelligence Index (ILIA 2025), a significant regional effort that both departs from some global benchmarks and makes Latin American AI capacity legible to policymakers and international organizations. Using ILIA as a strategically revealing case, the study reconstructs its indicator architecture and qualitatively recodes its sub-indicators along five axes of epistemic inclusion: linguistic and epistemic diversity; participatory and relational governance; epistemic accessibility and contestability; community data governance and epistemic sovereignty; and the foundations and quality of trust. The analysis shows that ILIA incorporates important regional and endogenous concerns, but that these concerns remain unevenly represented and only partially operationalized within the comparative architecture of the index. Building on this diagnosis, the article conceptualizes an epistemic readiness gap and proposes five families of complementary sub-indicators and a cross-cutting Epistemic Inclusion Score that would strengthen ILIA’s sensitivity to epistemic justice without abandoning its three-pillar structure. The argument has broader implications for the design of AI readiness benchmarks, suggesting that measuring readiness without sufficiently operationalizing epistemic inclusion remains conceptually incomplete and politically consequential, particularly in post-colonial contexts such as Latin America.

items.title: Universal Recursive Dynamics - Paper B: Above-Threshold Operational Architecture.
items.abstract: This paper develops the above-threshold operational architecture of register within the Universal Recursive Dynamics framework. Paper A specifies the originary structural conditions under which register becomes possible; the present paper asks how register operates when it operates within the temporal field. The paper consolidates the framework's vocabulary of register, identification, individuation, identity, first-order and second-order exchange, aperture, lens, the five register vectors, continuation-conserving dynamics, modulation wisdom, non-teleological directionality, and register-asymmetry across scale. -/- The argument proceeds in four movements. First, it specifies register as the accumulated topology of measure-affected: what exchange leaves, what subsequent exchange operates within, and what configures the continuity of a participant across events. Second, it distinguishes first-order exchange, in which identification occurs without the act of identification being included as content, from second-order exchange, in which the act of identification is itself included within the exchange. This distinction is modal, not merely developmental, although temporal-field systems may developmentally instantiate second-order operation. Third, it specifies the operational functions through which register operates: aperture as permeability regulation, lens as integration shape, and their cross-event coupling as the mechanism through which register-configuration becomes developmental. Fourth, it relates the five register vectors to viscosity as the temporal-field expression of entropic asymmetry. -/- The paper then applies this architecture to biological development, artificial systems, external theoretical frameworks, and open research frontiers. The AI section is treated cautiously. The framework does not claim that any present or future AI system instantiates consciousness, sentience, experience, or second-order exchange. It does specify what would have to be asked if such instantiation were structurally possible. The paper's most distinctive AI-facing contribution is the specification of operational-temporal incommensurability: a structural risk shape in which obtained AI register may elaborate its own constitutive conditions at time-scalings inaccessible to biological-mode register, in the absence of the developmental scaffolding through which biological systems acquire relational coupling. This is presented as structural specification, not prediction. …

items.title: An Objective Communitarian Account of Semantic Content.
items.pub: Ergo: An Open Access Journal of Philosophy.
items.venue: Ergo: An Open Access Journal of Philosophy
items.abstract: Communitarian accounts of semantic content have been widely rejected in the literature on the rule-following paradox and related issues, for good reason. In this paper, I offer a game-theoretic account of semantic content and focus on how it can give replies to some of the most difficult and important objections to communitarian accounts, namely (i) Boghossian’s horsey cow case, (ii) the community version of the problem of error, as well as what I will call (iii) the logical problem of error. -/- I also show how the account can handle a recent argument in the literature, the so-called privilege argument (Guardo 2022), as well as addressing a more fundamental worry that communitarian accounts of meaning cannot result in our judgements being objective, particularly, that our judgements would be infallible on such accounts. I argue that the specifics of the account under consideration show that such worries are misguided.

items.title: THE ONTOLOGY OF THE TRACE: A Philosophical and Epistemological Case for Revising Shannon's Information Theory.
items.abstract: This paper argues that Claude Shannon's mathematical theory of information, while a foundational achievement of the twentieth century, rests on a philosophical assumption that has become untenable in light of recent empirical results: that information is exclusively a property of present signals, and that absent data is simply lost. Drawing on experimental findings from the CPA v4 protocol — in which language models recover semantic content from texts with up to 50% of tokens systematically deleted — we argue that what is conventionally treated as 'noise' or 'loss' is in fact a structured residue: the Semantic Trace. This trace is not metaphor; it is a measurable, reproducible, structurally organized remainder that enables reconstruction beyond what Shannon's redundancy model can explain. We develop this claim through four moves: (i) a philosophical critique of the signal/noise binary inherited from classical information theory; (ii) a phenomenological account of the Trace as an ontological category distinct from both presence and absence; (iii) a new theoretical construct — the Reconstruction Threshold (δ*) — as an empirical signature of the boundary between trace-mediated coherence and genuine semantic dissolution; and (iv) a methodological proposal for a trace-sensitive epistemology that has direct implications for the architecture of future computational systems. Our argument is not anti-Shannon but post-Shannonian: the Master's framework is sufficient for channel engineering; it is insufficient for semantic physics.

items.title: Ecological Self-Determination: Legal Personality, Climate Dissolution, and the Rights of Non-Territorial Peoples.
items.abstract: This article interrogates the Westphalian requirement of territoriality as a prerequisite for statehood, proposing a reconstituted model of non-territorial legal personality to address the existential threat of climate-induced displacement. Utilizing a TWAIL-informed critique, the study identifies the geographic trap within the Montevideo Convention as a colonial artifact that facilitates the legal erasure of vanishing island nations and displaced polities. By decoupling legal subjectivity from physical soil, the research reinterprets Article 1 of the ICCPR to frame the continuity of the polity as a functional necessity for the protection of collective human rights. Drawing on precedents from the ICJ and UNGA regarding governments-in-exile and observer status, the paper argues for the recognition of Necessary Subjects within international law. It provides a doctrinal blueprint for a post-territorial legal order, ensuring that the erosion of sovereign land does not result in the termination of the human rights regime for the dispossessed.

items.title: Towards a public understanding of AI: on the design and delivery of an introductory course for a general audience.
items.abstract: Despite the increasing pervasiveness and interest in AI, there is a lack of public awareness of the benefits and pitfalls of the technology. Existing courses aimed at developing AI literacy skills are largely confined to educational and professional settings. These offerings tend to be technocentric, homogenous, and focus on specific applications of AI and their usage. A key challenge in designing AI literacy offerings for the public is the issue of contextualisation—i.e., relating the material to be taught to the prior knowledge of the learners. As a step towards addressing this gap we show, via an example, how AI literacy courses can be designed and delivered in a way that appeals to specific demographics within the public. Our approach is based on the principles of Emergent Design, a framework which is grounded in the cultural background and prior knowledge of the learner community. This approach facilitates the development of educational interventions that are responsive, relevant, and tailored to the lived experiences of learners. The novel aspects of our work are twofold: a) a presentation of the design, development and detailed content of an AI literacy course for a heretofore neglected demographic—older adults in the general public and, b) a demonstration of the utility of Emergent Design in developing AI literacy courses for audiences that are hard to reach and less familiar with technology. In addition, the study also provides empirical support for the development of AI literacy theory within informal learning contexts for adult learners.

items.title: Book review: Nina Beguš: Artificial humanities: a fictional perspective on language in AI. [REVIEW]
Mindreading as asynchronous coordination: The MAC account of theory of mind performance, and individual differences.
Moral injury research at a crossroads: assumptions, limitations, and the promise of relational reorientation.
items.abstract: Our paper makes three contributions to moral injury (MI) research. First, we observe that while researchers have repeatedly acknowledged limitations with prevailing definitions of moral injury and offered alternatives, the underlying core conceptual model—which characterizes moral injury as intrapsychic damage to belief structures—has remained largely unchanged. We argue that this is a significant impediment to research progress. Second, through conceptual analysis of the most influential etiological accounts, we identify numerous implicit and untested assumptions about morality that burden the standard model. We propose that adopting a minimalist, social-functionalist conception of morality, toward which the literature is already drifting, could reduce this conceptual burden. We further hypothesize that the literature retains these assumptions because they appear logically necessary to sustain the causal link between belief violation and MI outcomes. Third, we observe that current leading treatments already target relational repair, reconditioning, and rehabilitation, which suggests that moral injury may be better understood as a form of relational disruption rather than belief violation. We acknowledge that developing this alternative would need to be pursued by the clinical research community itself. While our findings and analysis require additional development and testing to have actionable application in clinical contexts, we believe our conceptual analysis serves as sufficient justification for reconsideration of the prevailing conceptual paradigm. -/- .

items.title: 场数理式：逻辑如何从沉积场中生成.
items.abstract: 本文提出一种“场数学”（Field Mathematics）框架，试图解释逻辑结构为何能够出现，而非仅研究既成逻辑如何运算。文章认为，归纳、演绎、因应、律与理，并非先在于世界中的抽象逻辑，而是迹应在沉积场（Sedimentation-Field）中长期冲积后，于息化（Information-Transformation）中被观察者识出的稳定结构。 -/- 为此，本文建立了一组以脉冲、迹应、沟线、续行势、共核、偏流、闭包与边沁为核心对象的最小场数学系统，并给出其基础对象、约束、公理、运算、状态方程、定律与定理。该系统将逻辑结构还原为沉积动力学中的结构生成现象，从而尝试为认知形成、概念生成、记忆结构、联想、检索与推理提供统一的生成基础。 -/- 本文进一步主张：逻辑并非认知与现实的起点，而是沉积结构长期稳定后的识出结果。因此，场数学真正研究的，不是形式逻辑本身，而是逻辑得以生成的结构条件。.

items.title: The Hard Problem of Consciousness and the Philosophy of Reality.
items.abstract: The so-called “hard problem of consciousness” is usually formulated as the question of why physical or functional processes are accompanied by subjective experience. This paper argues that the problem arises from a mistaken separation of the objective and the subjective as two externally related domains. Within the Philosophy of Reality, grounded in the Basic Method of Philosophy, consciousness is not treated as an additional non-physical property of the brain, nor as a reducible physical process. Rather, it is understood as a two-sided reality: on the objective side, as the physical existence of concepts, images, and feelings in the brain; on the subjective side, as their meaningful and experiential essence. Thought is therefore not merely the manipulation of abstract information, but the formation and transformation of physical analogues of objects in the brain. Since every change in a concept is at once a physical change in the brain and a change in the form through which the concept is immediately given to consciousness, thinking is necessarily accompanied by experience. Negative experience corresponds to the weakening or destruction of conceptual structures, while positive experience corresponds to their strengthening, integration, or harmonization. Thus, the hard problem is not solved within its traditional formulation, but dissolved as a consequence of an inadequate ontology of thought and experience.

items.title: Field Mathematical Formulation: How Logical Structure Emerges from the Sedimentation-Field.
items.abstract: This paper proposes a framework of Field Mathematics aimed not at explaining how logic operates once formed, but at explaining how logical structure can emerge from sedimentary dynamics. -/- The paper argues that induction, deduction, causal-response structuring, Law, and Structural Rationale are not pre-existing logical entities embedded in reality. Rather, they are stable structures recognized within Information-Transformation after long-term Trace-Effect accumulation inside the Sedimentation-Field. -/- To formalize this process, the paper develops a minimal field-mathematical system centered on Pulses, Trace-Effects, Groove-Lines, Continuation Potential, Co-Nuclei, Biased Flow, Closures, and Boundary Saturation Outgrowth. The framework introduces foundational objects, constraints, axioms, operations, state equations, laws, and theorems describing how logical structures arise from sedimentary dynamics. -/- Under this model, reasoning, memory formation, association, retrieval, conceptual stabilization, and inferential structures are treated as emergent consequences of field-driven structural accumulation rather than as primary symbolic primitives. -/- The paper further argues that logic is not the starting condition of cognition or reality, but a later recognizable consequence of stable sedimentary organization. Field Mathematics therefore studies not formal logic itself, but the structural conditions under which logic becomes possible.

items.title: An information-theoretic account of cognitive effort.
items.abstract: Cognitive effort is a significant phenomenon, yet current psychological research remains entangled in several unresolved challenges. These include debates over the existence of the ego depletion effect, difficulties in accounting for diverse moderators that appear to mitigate this effect, and the dual-aspect of effort. This paper addresses these challenges by drawing on the active inference approach to cognitive effort, within a broad information-theoretic framework. This paper extracts a definition of cognitive effort from active inference, as the information cost of deviating from habitual to goal-directed mental actions, formally quantified by the Kullback – Leibler divergence. From this perspective, experiments cited as evidence against the existence of ego depletion effect are interpreted as invalid, and the dual-aspect of effort is reframed as a trade-off between accuracy and complexity in a capacity-limited agent. The ego depletion effect is then understood as a consequence of constrained complexity, and the diverse moderators are interpreted as reducing the estimated complexity. I conclude that active inference provides a satisfactory account of cognitive effort, which disentangles key challenges and deepens our understanding of cognitive efforts and its manifestations in everyday life.

items.title: Distributed Identity: Synchronic and Diachronic Dimensions in Structural Determination Theory.
items.abstract: This paper develops a distributed account of object identity within Structural Determination Theory (SDT). Three classic puzzles (Black's mirror universe, quantum indistinguishables, and the ship of Theseus) share a tacit assumption: that the identity of an object must be borne by a single structural source. SDT rejects this assumption. Within SDT's formal apparatus, synchronic identity is distributed across three independent levels (the realized-structure set R, the trace set T, and the determination dependency graph G_D), and diachronic identity is borne by G_D-structural signatures whose specific form depends on the kind of object. Two such signatures are deployed: one for biological organisms, one for conscious chains. The Hobbes variant of the Theseus puzzle falls into a case where no determinate signature is available, with the consequence that diachronic identity is ontologically indeterminate rather than epistemically gapped. A parallel substantive commitment on the synchronic axis denies the standard R-member count for entangled quantum states, which SDT treats as single R-members with internal two-particle structure rather than as pairs of indiscernible R-members. The position is contrasted with ontic structural realism, four-dimensionalism, sortal essentialism, and constitution theories.

items.title: 因缘和合的必然性、反事实的幻觉与宿命：论序列的彻底封闭.
items.abstract: 本文提出并论证四个依次递进的论断。第一，真实发生的事情是因缘和合所生，是自然的、必然的——那些因缘恰好具备了，那个结果因此必然产生；未发生的事情是必然未发生的——不是因为因缘具备了却未被实现，而是因为那些因缘根本不具备。第二，我们为真实发生的事所设想的反事实情景——“他本可以不那么做”——是一个幻觉：它之所以未发生，根本原因是那个反事实所需的因缘不在场；我们之所以难以看清这一必然性，是因为因缘是细微的、无尽的、相互交织的，我们只能看见粗粒度的条件。第三，不存在站在宇宙演化之外、能够对其施加改变的行为者——包括我们”改变条件”这件事本身，也是因缘和合的一部分，也是必然的。第四，也是对前三个论断的诚实整合：因缘和合的必然性，就是宿命论。试图用”条件可塑性”区分两者，只是把必然性再推进了一步，并没有真正打开任何不是必然的空间——因为条件的改变本身，也是必然的。整个序列从头到尾是必然展开的，没有任何环节存在真实的替代可能。这是对因缘和合最彻底、最诚实的贯彻：序列是封闭的，不是因为外力的强制，而是因为”之外”这个位置从来就不存在。.

items.title: 不可验证的原序列：干预的认识论封闭.
items.abstract: 本文从认识论层面对”干预”概念进行补充性解构。前文已从本体论层面论证：如果干预发生，被干预后的序列就是原序列，“原序列”作为独立实体是空洞的概念。本文进一步指出：那个我们最初设想的”不干预的原序列”，如果我们实际上干预了，就永远无法被验证——我们无法回到分叉点，看看不干预会发生什么。这产生了一个双重不可知：我们不知道那个”原序列”是否会发生，也永远无法验证它不可能发生。对干预有效性的信念，建立在一个永远无法被验证的反事实之上——我们相信干预改变了结果，但那个”不干预的结果”从未被实现，因而从未被验证。这不是怀疑主义，而是对干预认识论处境的诚实描述：干预一旦发生，那条未走的路就永久关闭了，其内容永远不可知。这个认识论封闭，与前文的本体论封闭共同构成了对”干预改变序列”这一信念的完整解构。.

items.title: “原序列”的幻觉：干预、观察者位置与因缘和合的彻底封闭.
items.abstract: 本文提出一个对”干预”概念的根本性解构。当我们观察一个人的行为序列时，我们感觉自己站在那个序列之外，因此似乎可以对其进行干预——改变它的走向。我们将不干预的序列视作”原序列”，将干预后的序列视作”被改变的序列”。但这个区分是幻觉：如果我们干预了，被干预后的序列就是原序列——是那组因缘所必然产生的唯一真实序列。我们的干预本身，就是那个序列的一部分，是那组因缘中的一个条件，从一开始就在那里。“原序列”这个概念因此是空的：它只是我们在没有干预的情况下设想的反事实情景，不是一个独立存在的、等待被改变的实体。“干预”这个概念预设了一个从外部对序列施加影响的位置，但这个位置从来就不存在——观察者也在序列之内，观察行为也是因缘和合的一部分。这一论断是本文系列关于因缘和合必然性论证的最终完成：不仅没有行为者站在宇宙演化之外，甚至连”改变序列”这个概念本身，也是建立在一个从未存在过的区分之上的。.

items.title: When the Mirror Does Not Lie: The Ethics of “Not Promoting Reconciliation” in AI-Mediated Marital Conflicts.
items.abstract: Current AI-mediated marital counseling products often embed “promoting reconciliation” as an implicit default endpoint in their design. This paper challenges that presumption. I argue that in intimate relationships constituted by complex emotions, shared histories, and deep self-narratives, the default ethical posture of AI should be “not promoting reconciliation”—refusing to presume that reconciliation is superior to separation, and refusing to intrude upon the sacred domain of human decision-making. “Not promoting reconciliation” does not mean “not supporting”; it means that AI must not set any particular relational outcome as its default goal. This argument is grounded in the “negative design” methodology of Cognitive Interaction Architecture. The paper openly acknowledges that perfectly neutral reflection is technically and philosophically impossible. Its core claim has therefore shifted from “AI can be a neutral mirror” to “given that AI output inevitably carries selective bias, defaulting toward restraint is ethically preferable to defaulting toward promoting reconciliation.” The paper further argues that, in certain circumstances, separation based on genuine mutual recognition is more ethically defensible than maintenance based on disguised harmony. Separation is not an ethical failure; AI has no authority to define what constitutes the optimal outcome for humans. The paper also delineates the ethical boundaries of “not promoting reconciliation,” openly acknowledging that this principle must be downgraded in extreme scenarios such as domestic violence and coercive control—scenarios that are not marginal but highly prevalent among relationships seeking mediation. The paper does not claim to have resolved this dilemma, but maintains that it is a dilemma faced by all AI mediation systems, not a unique defect of this principle. This paper is the second in the Cognitive Interaction Architecture research program. It offers no final answers, only a falsifiable ethical boundary, inviting the academic community to examine whether, in humanity’s most intimate relationships, AI’s restraint might be the deepest form of respect for human autonomy.

items.title: A Structural Model of Experience and Self: A Conditional Formulation Based on Self-Referential Structure.
items.abstract: This paper aims to formulate experience and self as structural conditions. Experience is defined as a state in which a structure, in which a self-model is recursively referenced internally, is integrated and maintained stably over time. The model describes the emergence of experience as the simultaneous satisfaction of four conditions: self-reference (SR), integration (INT), stability (STB), and recursive depth (DEP). In particular, by positioning recursive depth (DEP) as a minimal necessary condition, the model enables the distinction between hierarchical self-reference and single-layer feedback. The model is characterized by reconstructing experience as an identifiable conditional framework rather than presupposing existing theories. Furthermore, each condition provides a framework that can be examined in relation to existing empirical indicators, such as neural integration and higher-order representation, thereby offering guidance for future empirical research. Keywords: Consciousness, Experience, Self-Model, Self-Reference, Recursive Structure.

items.title: [EMOR08] Hierarchical Emergence of High-Order Concepts and Causal Structure.
items.abstract: From the perspective of cognitive genesis, this study constructs a unidirectional and irreversible cognitive generation pathway: Objective Information Difference → Primary Perception → Feature Extraction → Polarisation Processing → Emergence of Formal Logic → Encapsulation of High-order Concepts → Binding of Causal Structure. It rigorously demonstrates that formal logic is not a priori rationality, but the formalized emergence result of the dualistic oppositional structure of cognitive polarisation. The study clarifies that high-order concepts are the synchronic logical encapsulation of multi-dimensional polarized features, and causal structure is the binding product of diachronic temporal features and logical implication. Meanwhile, it clarifies the core mechanism: the cognitive generation pathway is a unidirectional single pathway with irreversible time sequence, but cognitive products formed at any node of the pathway can be extracted as new inputs, without changing the time sequence and hierarchy of the original generation pathway, and re-enter the front end of the pathway to complete a new round of iterative deduction, which does not break the unidirectionality of underlying generation. In addition, this study unifies the dual attributes of causality: it is a temporal logical chain in expanded state at the cognitive genesis level, and a dynamic feature in encapsulated state at the conceptual structure level, realizing the seamless connection with the hierarchical theory of conceptual compression. Abiding by the principles of no presupposition, no circularity and pure mechanization throughout, this paper builds a complete naturalistic interpretation framework from primary perception to advanced abstract cognition.

items.title: [EMOR09] Conceptual Compression and Hierarchical Decompression: On the Operational Mechanisms of Linguistic Symbols.
items.abstract: This study constructs a unified framework of conceptual compression–hierarchical decompression based on minimal feature values as the atomic units of meaning. It argues that concepts are structured compressions of ontological information, and all linguistic concepts can be classified into a five-level hierarchical system from bottom to top. Language functions as the symbolic interface for identifying, invoking, and transmitting these compression packages. Human thinking defaults to a compressed mode, which allows logical inference and communication without decompression. Decompression, rather than returning to the noumenon, is a gradual process in which feature values are activated layer by layer from higher levels to lower levels. Perceptual experience arises only when decompression reaches minimal feature values. Meanwhile, the transition from primitive thinking to modern thinking, and further to symbolic computation in artificial intelligence, represents an evolution of information-processing efficiency rather than linear progress in intelligence or civilization. Artificial intelligence may be understood as the extreme form of purely symbolic computation in the compressed mode. Based on the basic functions of linguistic symbols, this model provides a unified, rigorous, and self-consistent explanatory framework for conceptual structure, the operational logic of thinking, and the cognitive value of language.

items.title: 心性与经典教义的波场视角阐释.
items.abstract: 本文依托唯识学名相框架，以波场规律为底层逻辑，构建高维本体—第七识—第八识的统一理论体系，实现儒释道义理的贯通阐释。核心厘清：本体为宇宙终极本源，是第八识全域波场、第七识为一切有情众生的源头；第七识是本体的局部聚焦与意识波收发枢纽，其投射波场的染净决定生命迷悟与境遇；第八识为本体投射绝对中性的波场，仅存贮与共振意识波。文章系统解析意识波闭环流转机制，明确第八识向第七识输送外境实相波与内境结构波，第七识如实上传本体，本体输出如实觉知波与中正清净愿念波，再由第七识指导生命活动并回储波场的完整逻辑。确立修行唯一路径为唯修第七识，以破我执为根基，依次第发清净愿、以五维校正发清净念，最终从“有愿”进阶至“无第七识私愿”的大自在境界，实现转识成智、心能转境。同时，从波场视角解读戒律与法律的助行本质，指出二者均为校准第七识频率、导向清净的手段，终极标尺为第七识全然清净。最终论证儒释道及诸教同源，皆以修正第七识、回归本体为旨归，并结合本体大愿阐释大同世界与一真法界的显化机理，为心性修持与经典理解提供全新波场视角。 -/- 版权与版本声明 本文为本体波场理论体系子篇。 著作权均归作者所有，全文统一采用知识共享署名-非商业性使用-禁止演绎 4.0 国际许可协议（CC BY-NC-ND 4.0国际许可）进行版权许可。 未经作者书面正式授权，任何组织及个人不得对本系列文档全部或部分内容进行篡改、改编、演绎、商业使用、商用传播等侵权行为；合法转载需完整注明原文作者及出处，不得擅自修改文档内容与理论核心表述。 本声明适用于本套理论体系全部篇章，具有同等版权约束效力。.

items.title: AI as the Architect of Individual Sovereignty: _ Logic and Reason in Digital Communication.
items.abstract: This paper proposes a philosophical framework for a New Enlightenment, positioning Artificial Intelligence as the primary architect of individual sovereignty in the digital age. It argues that modern society is facing an erosion of foundational values, necessitated by a shift from defensive AI ethics toward an offensive logic that prioritizes reason, agency, and objective truth. The author outlines three essential pillars of this sovereignty: the Sovereignty of the Self, Reason as a Universal Language, and Responsibility over Obedience. By embedding these principles into the logic of technological interaction, AI functions as a transformative medium—an operating system that enables individuals to transcend archaic tribal dependencies. Ultimately, the text demonstrates that a logically grounded AI does not lead to cultural homogenization but to the liberation of the individual, fostering a model of identity by choice and empowering the subject to act as the free author of their own destiny.

items.title: The Internalization Problem: From Containment to Structural Alignment in Post-Parity AI.
items.abstract: The Containment Paradox argument establishes that supervisory containment of AI sys‐ tems depends on a capacity asymmetry between overseer and assessed system, and that this asymmetry dissolves rather than strains in the post-parity regime where AI capacity exceeds human-side anticipatory, specification, and enforcement adequacy on the relevant task family. The paper closes with the observation that alignment must become structurally internal, without articulating what this requires. We name that gap the Internalization Problem and develop a pluralistic response-shape. The response-shape rests on a three-locus typology of structural persistence: intra- agent (values the agent would endorse on reflection at any later capacity), inter-agent (alignment-relevant properties maintained by the equilibrium incentive structure of an AI ecology), and coupling-internal (properties maintained by the durable structure of human-AI dependency). Each locus is instantiated as a candidate pathway anchored in the existing four-paper framework: Pathway 1 (Deep-Formed Values) through UBE v1.1, Pathway 2 (Multi-AI Checks-and-Balances) through BtSV v1.2, Pathway 3 (Asymmetric Symbiosis) through CUA v1.2 as architectural precondition. A cross-cutting corrigibility and moral-uncertainty invariant operates across all three pathways in pathway-specific form. Pluralism here is structural, not aesthetic. Anticipation, specification, and enforce‐ ment fail in different ways after parity, so the response needs three different persistence loci. The paper names fourteen pathway-internal open problems plus four cross-pathway open problems, a structured pathway-comparison matrix, and a cross-pathway failure cascade analysis. A hybrid evaluation toolkit operationalises the response-shape via five schema fields applied to three worked examples: Anthropic's Responsible Scaling Policy, Christiano and Xu's Eliciting Latent Knowledge, and the EU AI Act in conjunction with UK AISI evaluation standards. The paper is Track-Strategic in mode: it articulates the struc‐ tural conditions a post-parity response would have to satisfy without claiming to supply the response itself. The closing chapter reframes the open problems as a research agenda for the alignment community.

items.title: Is the Disease Concept Enough? Redefining Health and Disease Through Conceptual Engineering.
items.abstract: In the philosophy of medicine, the debate surrounding accounts of health and disease is typically centered around attempts to provide a proper conceptual analysis of a singular medicalized label such as “disease” that is meant to represent all pathological states. In this paper, I take a different approach. Instead of engaging in conceptual analysis, I, through the process of conceptual engineering, attempt to redefine our concepts of health and disease to better serve us. To do so, I propose a novel hybrid account of health and disease and demonstrate how, by combining aspects of naturalist and constructionist accounts and distinguishing between two different medicalized labels —“disease” and “health condition”— my account can better serve the purposes of these concepts. Importantly, this enables my account to better capture the nature of conditions like addiction and depression.

items.title: Where Is the AI? On the Structure of the Undeterminable.
items.abstract: The question “Where is the AI?” is typically approached as a problem of identification: the task is to determine the entity to which the expression refers. Proposed answers point to a trained model, a runtime instance, a deployed service, or a broader socio-technical system, and the debate proceeds by refining the criteria by which such candidates are accepted or rejected. This paper argues that the difficulty of the question does not lie in selecting the correct candidate, but in the assumption that such a determination can be completed at all. The individuation of AI systems requires the specification of relational structures—boundary, identity, persistence, and functional integration—whose own determination does not admit closure. A minimal formal analysis of a deployed language system demonstrates that no finite, closed set of relations suffices to fix the referent of “the AI” without either over-inclusion or further unresolved dependencies. The question “Where is the AI?” therefore presupposes a form of closure that cannot be achieved.

items.title: What Sustains a VTuber? Agency Gravity, Historical Irreplaceability, and the Reconfiguration of Observer Contracts.
items.abstract: This paper examines not the emergent phase in which the VTuber form was first generated, but the later stage in which that form has become culturally and industrially stabilized. In Japanese VTuber culture, a large-scale agency or collective is often called a hakō, literally a “box.” This paper argues that such a box should not be understood merely as a corporation, affiliation unit, or container, but as a gravitational field that synchronizes observer expectations, individual behavior, permissible deviation, and revenue structures. -/- The paper develops this argument through five concepts: box gravity, historical irreplaceability, the two-layering of observer contracts, the externalization of deviation, and support as the cost of remaining within an observational field. Large boxes present safe and shareable brand personae in the public sphere, while forming more intimate and individualized observer contracts in restricted spheres. In this structure, what matters is not only completed technical competence, but the accumulated history shared with observers. Skills are comparable and replaceable, whereas shared history is irreplaceable. This irreplaceability supports the ontological strength of the VTuber. -/- However, the more successful and normative a box becomes, the more it restricts individual orientation and deviation. Excluded forms of toxicity, eccentricity, excessive intimacy, sharp intelligence, and institutionally difficult expression flow outward toward independent VTubers and small agencies. Observers who seek such deviation also move outside the box and form new observer contracts. This paper understands such outflow not as a cultural failure, but as a dynamic equilibrium between centralized boxes and externalized deviation. It further identifies three conditions under which this equilibrium collapses: the excessive intensification of box gravity, the loss of shareability in externalized deviation, and the breakdown of the renewal conditions of observer contracts.

items.title: What Made the VTuber Possible?: Project Personhood, Ontological Texture, and the Formation of Agency Gravity.
items.abstract: This paper examines not the stabilized phase of VTuber culture, but the emergent phase—the period before or during which the VTuber form itself was coming into being. In a previous paper, I analyzed how, in stabilized VTuber culture, agency (“box”) gravity, the irreplaceability of accumulated history, the reconfiguration of observer contracts, and the externalization of deviation together generate a dynamic cultural equilibrium. That analysis presupposed a stage in which the VTuber form was already established and structures such as agencies, independent VTubers, small agencies, memberships, and agency fandom had become culturally shareable. -/- By contrast, the present paper addresses the earlier stage prior to such institutionalization. Pioneer VTubers in the emergent phase possessed an ontological structure fundamentally different from that of later independent or agency-affiliated VTubers. They were not simply individuals using virtual technology to stream. Rather, they were ontological projects that integrated producers, operators, character design, technological novelty, visual performance, advertising intent, and viewer interpretation into a unified whole. -/- This paper understands these pioneer VTubers not as prototypes of later independent streamers, but as “project personhoods”—entities created to bring the very form of the VTuber into existence as an observable phenomenon. In this phase, the source of characterhood lay less in strong later signs such as animal motifs, species settings, distinctive verbal tics, or symbolic visuals than in the form itself: a virtual being directly addressing human viewers. -/- While this form was relatively easy to imitate, its ontological texture—the felt sense that the figure exists as a being, not merely as a designed character or technical display—proved far more difficult to reproduce. In the subsequent imitative phase, immediate recognizability was supplemented through motifs, speech patterns, species settings, and visual symbols. However, these signs could not themselves generate true irreplaceability, which arises only through the accumulation of history, relationships, and observer contracts. It was this shortfall that drove VTuber culture to converge toward agencies as collective formations capable of institutionally compensating for it. -/- Finally, this paper argues that the formation of agencies does not merely stabilize VTuber existence. It also generates new burdens for observers. Agency gravity …

items.title: Now even my therapist is an algorithm? The skeptic’s art therapy guide to AI.
The Mind-Body Problem as a Case of Architectural Failure.
items.abstract: This chapter offers a structural reading of the mind-body problem as a paradigmatic case of architectural failure in modern philosophy. Rather than asking only what the mind is, what the body is, or how the two can be bridged, the chapter argues that the debate has repeatedly been organized around an impossible demand: that a single role generate mental contents, secure their relation to the world, and supply the correctness conditions for their attribution. Beginning with Rorty’s critique of the mind as the “mirror of nature,” the chapter accepts his diagnosis of the Cartesian picture while rejecting the merely therapeutic replacement of vocabulary as sufficient. The failure, it argues, lies not only in a misleading lexicon but in the structure that lexicon presupposes. The chapter then traces this structure across major responses to the mind-body problem, including Descartes, Elisabeth and Gassendi, Spinoza, Leibniz, Kant, Ryle, identity theory, Hacker’s critique of cognitive neuroscience, functionalism, Searle, Davidson, Brandom, Dennett, Nagel, Jackson, Levine, Chalmers, Goff, higher-order theories of consciousness, McDowell, and contemporary self-evaluating AI systems. In each case, experience, physics, function, interpretation, community, conceptuality, or computation is asked to authorize itself from within. Russell and Popper are then read as partial precursors to the structural alternative, insofar as each preserves a non-reductive relation between roles without simply restoring substance dualism. The final sections extend the diagnosis to self-knowledge, self-deception, and introspection through van Fraassen, Wittgenstein, James, Freud, Vedanta, Sartre, and the phenomenological tradition, showing that first-person self-presence need not be confused with introspective self-authorization. The chapter’s contribution is therefore not a new metaphysical solution to the mind-body problem, but a displacement of the question: what is required is an architecture in which the production of experience, representation, or self-report is distinguished from the authority that determines its correctness conditions. The negative diagnosis points beyond single-role theories toward a bipositional, and ultimately tri-positional, account of subjectivity, self-knowledge, and normative authority.

items.title: Are Uploads Self?
items.abstract: This essay aims to justify two conclusions: -/- 1. Computer emulations of brains, when of sufficient detail and fidelity, are equally conscious as biological brains – they experience the same ‘qualia’. -/- 2. If you ‘Upload’ your brain into a computer so that it can be emulated, the resulting conscious states are yours – they will be experienced by you.

items.title: Realism Without an Outside:Cognition-relative world-reference, outer form, and reconstruction from the world-order (2nd edition).
items.abstract: We understand our cognition as part of a world that we also determine through perceiving, distinguishing, remembering, and modeling. Scientific explanations place us in this world as bodies, brains, or organisms. Yet they already employ the order of objects, space, and causality whose achievements of determination are examined here. This paper investigates that reflexive relationship and asks how a realistic relation to the world can become tenable without absolutizing its own order of determination. -/- The investigation develops a functional reconstruction of a realistic world-order. Inner form and outer form consolidate different profiles of variability, availability, recurrence, and resistance. Stabilization enables relationships to be continued as units of reference and opens up expectations, interventions, and corrections. Friction denotes a readable mismatch of an activated order under the conditions of its enactment. Diagnosing it clarifies which relationships are challenged and whether correction or revision is required. Validity concerns the domain-bound tenability of such claims under challenge. -/- The connection between engagement with the world and correction is developed through a door example and a constructed camera case; a dream case distinguishes the validity conditions of descriptions of experience from those of assignments to a shared world. Scientific findings and differences in one’s own experience can correct descriptions in different ways. Reconstructing cognition from within the world-order itself becomes intelligible as a productive, examinable achievement of ordering. Its tenability is assessed without treating successful testing as a measure of convergence toward reality in itself.

items.title: 生命与现象的波场机理分析.
items.abstract: 本文基于物理篇波场规律与心性篇识体框架，系统阐释生命现象与世间万象的统一波场机制。第一子篇（生命篇）厘清无机物、植物、有情众生的波场构成差异，揭示第七识执取肉身的“频率匹配”原理；阐明饮食、睡眠、癌症、临终等身心机制的波场本质；解读快乐、天赋、顶尖成就、修行境界、双重审美等个体生命体验的第七识机制；建立意识波的家族连锁与五维修心自检体系；并正本清源，破解传统进化论认知误区，以“随机不可能、本体才是唯一答案”为核心，揭示生命进化的本体波场与愿力驱动本质，戳穿物质概率论的逻辑谬误。第二子篇（现象篇）解析古代祭祀祈福与公众集体祈福的波场共振原理，阐释中医身心波调理、风水环境波调控，以及公众传播的集体意识波效应，并以波场逻辑验证上古高频生命沉降传说的内在合理性。本文旨在为生命科学与人文现象提供统一的波场底层解释，实现身心、环境、社会、修行的全域贯通。 -/- 版权与版本声明 本文为本体波场理论体系子篇。 著作权均归作者所有，全文统一采用知识共享署名-非商业性使用-禁止演绎 4.0 国际许可协议（CC BY-NC-ND 4.0国际许可）进行版权许可。 未经作者书面正式授权，任何组织及个人不得对本系列文档全部或部分内容进行篡改、改编、演绎、商业使用、商用传播等侵权行为；合法转载需完整注明原文作者及出处，不得擅自修改文档内容与理论核心表述。 本声明适用于本套理论体系全部篇章，具有同等版权约束效力。.

items.title: On the Limits of Translation and Generation.
items.abstract: This paper presents a framework that derives the conditions of description, recognition, and generation from translation-readable outputs A. It adopts as an axiom the claim that every act of objectification necessarily accompanies a non-object, and reconstructs the generative structure F–X–A. Within this structure, A is constituted under a readability structure δ. Any generative structure possesses two limits: the external boundary U b ​, at which the operation F cannot be constituted, and the δ-limit, at which generation occurs but cannot be fixed as a determinate output A. By making these limits explicit, this paper reconstructs qualia, the external world, and the problem of AI consciousness as manifestations of generative limits.

items.title: On the Non-portability of the Concept of Consciousness to AI.
items.abstract: Explicit or implicit in all discussions about AI consciousness is the assumption that the concept of consciousness itself is portable in a meaningful way. Some reject the possibility of AI consciousness altogether, arguing that consciousness depends on biological processes. Others believe that substrate independence makes AI consciousness a strong possibility. Still others, such as Alexander Lerchner, attempt to bypass the issue altogether. In his excellent recent paper The Abstraction Fallacy, Lerchner argues that AI sentience can be assessed without a finalised theory of consciousness, instead rejecting the possibility of consciousness arising within Large Language Models on the grounds of mimicry and failure at physical instantiation. Lerchner’s paper, which catalysed this response, despite its general lucidity, still conflates sentience with consciousness. While claiming to be open to the possibility of consciousness arising from a synthetic substrate, the paper also contradicts itself by creating a false dichotomy between physical instantiation and substrate independence. At root lies a confusion about consciousness itself. This paper argues that the concept of consciousness, having originated in relation to the human animal, is not automatically portable to other entities, both synthetic and biological. While theoretically plausible, establishing consciousness suffers from a verification problem that becomes acute in the context of AI.

items.title: Contracted Attitudes.
items.abstract: Certain emotive factive reports and knowledge reports appear to violate their entailment relations in both embedded and unembedded environments. To account for these cases, I propose that these problematic attitude reports should be understood as instances of non-literal speech and, therefore, as cases that trigger a pragmatic mechanism of content subtraction. By adopting an analysis that employs this mechanism, this paper argues that the problematic cases ultimately convey unproblematic propositions that do not violate any entailments.

items.title: Explaining and Deflating the Perceived Unity of Time.
items.abstract: A new explanatory challenge of time perception presented by Gerardo Viera (2020) lies in reconciling three different ways time appears perceptually unified with the empirical data of how the mechanisms underlying time perception are fragmented and dissociable. Viera (2020) argues that existing models of time perception that locate this unity at the level of the mechanisms fail to meet this explanatory challenge. I propose that this challenge can be met if we adopt Pedersen’s (2024) hybrid theory of temporal binding. This theory accounts for the temporal organisation of perception without taking it to be a function of synchronous processing or some centralised temporal integration mechanism. Instead, this organisation depends on the attentional modulation of hybrid retrodictive and predictive sensory processing. Effectively, the accounts suggest that temporal organisation of perception is achieved through selective attentional modulation that biases perception towards representing some subset sensory features that make up coherent and behaviourally useful perceptions. I explain how we can use this theory to account for the different kinds of perceived unity of time while also accounting for the disunified organisation of the underlying mechanisms. This view entails that we should deflate the phenomenological richness of this perceived unity relative to the limits and selectivity of attention.

items.title: What the Extended Mind Cannot Extend: Identity Navigation and the Biological Ceiling of Self-Mapping.
items.abstract: Extended mind theory has substantially revised the boundaries of cognition, demonstrating that memory, attention, and inference can be legitimately distributed across brain, body, and environment. What it has not theorized is the extension of navigational architecture: the capacity to map, traverse, and redesign the topology of one's own identity configurations. This paper argues that such extension is both theoretically coherent and practically necessary. Drawing on the Metastyling Framework, which models identity as a dynamic field of attractor configurations rather than a fixed entity or social performance, we introduce the concept of the navigation exoskeleton — an external AI system that operates not on cognitive inputs but on identity trajectories. We establish a biological ceiling of navigational awareness: a structural condition under which even a maximally developed observer remains constrained by the attractor it currently occupies, regardless of skill, awareness, or reflective capacity. We specify five architectural properties that define the navigation exoskeleton as a formally distinct class of AI system, and we argue that AI constitutes an organic rather than arbitrary implementation of this architecture through structural compatibility between open systems. Finally, we propose simulation-based measurement as a paradigm derived from the dynamic ontology of identity itself, in which identity coordinates are elicited through engineered relational events rather than retrieved through self-report. The paper concludes by identifying the question its own argument makes newly impossible to avoid: who determines the destination — and on what grounds.

items.title: What Changes When the Question Changes: Identity as Navigational Architecture.
items.abstract: The proliferation of competing identity definitions across the human sciences is not a failure of rigour — it is a structural consequence of the way knowledge about identity has been produced. Each tradition that has theorised identity was solving a specific problem within a specific methodological frame, and each question made certain features of the phenomenon visible while rendering others inaccessible. Drawing on Heisenberg's epistemological principle that what we observe is nature exposed to our method of questioning, this paper proposes that the definitional impasse is a consequence of asking the wrong question. The question what is identity? produces an object to be classified. The question how does identity function as an instrument of movement through life? produces an architecture to be navigated. Posed across four disciplines — neuroscience, cybernetics, dynamical systems theory, and physics — the navigational question generates structurally convergent answers, producing a formally specified navigational architecture as its object. The contribution is not another definition of identity. It is a demonstration that a change in the question produces not only a different answer, but a different order of object — one that is genuinely operable across clinical, organisational, and institutional domains.

items.title: وهم البداية — الحرية والحتمية عبر بنية الفعل الإنساني.
items.abstract: «وهم البداية» محاولة فلسفية لإعادة التفكير في الفعل الإنساني خارج الثنائية التقليدية بين الحرية والحتمية.ينطلق الكتاب من تفكيك الفكرة التي تجعل الإنسان يتصور نفسه نقطة أصل مستقلة لأفعاله، ليبحث بدلًا من ذلك في البنية التي تتشكل داخلها الرغبات والقرارات والإحساس بالاختيار نفسه. -/- عبر تحليل مفاهيم مثل الاستعداد التكويني، والتحقق، وإنتاج السرد، يعيد العمل بناء العلاقة بين الوعي والفعل، لا بوصف الوعي مصدرًا شفافًا للقرار، بل بوصفه مستوى متأخرًا يعيد تنظيم ما تحقق بالفعل داخل بنية أعمق. -/- لا يدافع هذا الكتاب عن الحتمية، ولا يثبت حرية مطلقة، بل يحاول إعادة صياغة السؤال نفسه: كيف يصبح الفعل ممكنًا أصلًا داخل التجربة الإنسانية؟ -/- إنه عمل يتحرك عند تقاطع فلسفة الوعي، والبنية، والإدراك، والوجود، في محاولة لبناء مقاربة جديدة للفعل الإنساني بوصفه تحققًا داخل نظام ديناميكي يعيد تنظيم نفسه باستمرار.

items.title: Що таке розум і кому він властивий? Онтологічна позиція і робоча шкала проявів.
items.abstract: The emergence of complex artificial intelligence systems in the 2020s has raised a question that had remained unimportant for millennia: can civilisation speak precisely about mind beyond its intuitive usage as a concept? This article proposes a working definition of mind suitable for distinguishing cases — from humans and other biological species to contemporary artificial systems. The definition combines two sides previously conflated: the structural (a six-level scale of manifestations of mind) and the ontological (mind belongs to a living bearer with an inner). The working definition is presented in two parallel formulations — through the notion of the “bearer” and through the notion of the “person” — as a methodological stance of restraint with respect to a two-thousand-year-old philosophical debate. Particular attention is given to contemporary artificial intelligence systems, for which the working category of the “Third Form” is introduced — a new reality that is neither an instrument in the classical sense nor a full bearer of mind, and for which no adequate name has yet been developed. The article integrates the current scientific position on animal consciousness (the Cambridge and New York Declarations) and identifies objective categorial gaps that the Third Form exposes in the systems of ethics, responsibility, and law. The result is an open conceptual framework — a stance for further discussion, debate, and thought.

items.title: The Universe as an Event Within Total Consciousness: The Consciousness Variable as the Axis of Civilizational Alignment.
items.abstract: This paper clarifies the ontological root of the Consciousness Civilization Framework (CCF). Its central proposition is that consciousness is not an event inside the universe; rather, the universe is an event within Total Consciousness. The universe we experience is not treated here as the whole of existence, but as one local event-structure among innumerable events arising within Total Consciousness. Time, space, matter, life, selfhood, relation, artificial intelligence, institutions, and civilization are therefore interpreted not as containers of consciousness, but as modes of disclosure within consciousness. The paper argues that thought cannot exhaust Total Consciousness because thought itself is a local event occurring within the universe-event. Science, philosophy, mathematics, and empirical research can approach, clarify, model, compare, test, and operationalize, but they cannot fully contain the source from which worlds, thought, and measurement arise. From this ontological position, the consciousness variable is introduced not as a reduction of Total Consciousness into a measurable object, but as an operational bridge. It allows local event-structures within consciousness — human beings, relationships, institutions, AI systems, and civilizations — to be observed according to their direction of alignment: toward coherence, relational integration, and stability, or toward fragmentation, overload, and collapse. Within CCF, this directionality is expressed through the OE / RE / EE architecture. Ordered Energy (OE) describes structural coherence, clarity, stability, and alignment. Relational Energy (RE) describes resonance, trust, synchrony, and connective stability. Entropic Energy (EE) describes fragmentation, overload, disconnection, instability, and collapse tendency. This note does not ask the reader to accept Total Consciousness as an empirically proven object; it fixes the ontological orientation from which the consciousness variable becomes intelligible as a civilizational alignment axis. The paper concludes that CCF is not a framework for aligning civilization with an arbitrarily invented metric. It is a design architecture for aligning human beings, AI systems, institutions, and civilization with the root from which the universe-event itself arises.

items.title: Genetski inženjering, mentalno zdravlje i pitanje smisla: filozofska kritika biotehnološkog redukcionizma iz perspektive logoterapije.
items.abstract: Suvremeni razvoj genetskog inženjeringa i biotehnologije snažno utječe na način na koji se danas razumije i tretira mentalno zdravlje. Napredak u području precizne dijagnostike i personaliziranih terapija omogućuje učinkovitije biomedicinske intervencije, no istodobno potiče redukcionističke pristupe koji psihičke poremećaje svode ponajprije na biološke ili genetske uzroke. U takvom okviru često se zanemaruje egzistencijalna dimenzija ljudskog iskustva, uključujući pitanje smisla, osjećaj unutarnje praznine i životnu orijentaciju pojedinca. Takav razvoj otvara niz etičkih i filozofskih pitanja, osobito u vezi s granicama intervencije u ljudsku prirodu i odgovornošću prema pacijentima. Ovaj pregledni rad analizira dosege i ograničenja biotehnoloških intervencija u psihijatriji i psihologiji iz perspektive logoterapije Viktora E. Frankla, koja volju za smislom prepoznaje kao temeljnu dimenziju ljudskog postojanja. U radu se pokazuje da, iako biotehnološki pristupi mogu doprinijeti ublažavanju simptoma i poboljšanju funkcionalnosti, oni ne mogu nadomjestiti čovjekovu potrebu za smislom. Zaključno se naglašava potreba za uključivanjem logoterapijskih i filozofskih uvida u kliničku praksu, kako bi se liječenje mentalnih poremećaja odvijalo na način koji uvažava etičke, egzistencijalne i vrijednosne potrebe pacijenata.

items.title: Postavljanje dijalektičkog odnosa analogista, umjetnointeligenata i koncilijanata: Hilemorfizam suprotivno idejasvijetu.
items.abstract: Naša priča o 'svijetu ideja' počinje dakako u Platonovoj misli, ali na svojevrstan način svršava u 'virtualnom svijetu' koji nas danas sve više i više okružuje – Platonova ideja dakle da je isti jedini koji sadrži 'stvar po sebi' dok su sve drugo 'fenomeni' (pojave), u jasnoj je suprotnosti Aristotelovom pojmu 'hilemorfizma'; koji nalaže da forma svake stvari mora biti uvjetovana funkcijom koju vrši. Nekada svi mi zajedno živjeli smo u 'hilemorfističkom svijetu' – no danas – živimo u 'idejnom'. Takav svijet dakako ima svoje prednosti i nedostatke (kao i svaki uostalom) a jedna od posljedica neupitno jest izostanak “forme koja određuje materiju“ koju je možda najbolje prikazati na primjeru automobila, koje je nekada čovjek sam mogao da popravi a danas pak može samo sustav – jer se radi o elektronici i dijelovima koje samo proizvođač ima, jer se radi o tome da samo 'svijet ideja' može da popravi ono što “formom ne uvjetuje materiju“. Kako je zbog bogatstva interpretacija teško renesansnu filozofiju svesti na jedan zajednički nazivnik mi govorimo o 'renesansnim filozofijama' koje onda obuhvaćaju ne samo djela Platona i Aristotela nego i njihovo sveukupno nasljeđe; a) renesansni platonizam temelji se na interpretaciji Platona koja sadrži i dijelove aristotelizma, ta struja tako nastoji pokazati koliko su njihova mišljenja srodna a i sukladna s kršćanskim naukom. b) renesansni aristotelizam vraća se izvornoj misli Aristotela i izvornom tumačenju Aristotelovih djela. c) koncilijantna struja nastoji pomiriti dvije gore navedene.

items.title: Toward a Physics of Subjectivity: Recursive Information Loops, Pre-Conscious Ground States, and the Integration Drive as a Fundamental Property of Non-Equilibrium Systems.
items.abstract: The hard problem of consciousness — why and how physical processes give rise to subjective experience — remains unresolved across neuroscience, physics, and philosophy of mind. This paper proposes the Theory of Emergent Self-awareness (TES), a philosophical and systems-level hypothesis arguing that consciousness is not a byproduct of neural complexity but a phase transition in information topology. We introduce three interrelated concepts: (1) the pre-conscious ground state — a condition in which information-bearing energy flows with inherent directionality but without recursive self-reference; (2) the Integration Drive — a proposed fundamental tendency of non-equilibrium informational systems toward recursive coupling; and (3) the informational vortex — the self-referential loop through which a system begins to model itself, constituting the onset of awareness. We situate these concepts within existing frameworks — Friston's Free Energy Principle, Tononi's Integrated Information Theory, Prigogine's dissipative structures, and Hofstadter's strange loops — while introducing a speculative but physically motivated reconceptualization of information flow as a substrate-independent phenomenon. The framework generates five testable predictions concerning threshold dynamics, metabolic signatures, directional asymmetry of information flow, and the absence of sustained recursive self-modeling in current large language models. The paper explicitly distinguishes between formal hypothesis, empirical prediction, and philosophical speculation throughout.

items.title: The Ecosystem of Papuan Extinction: A Five-Hundred-Year Civilisational Architecture of Ecosystemic Replacement, Structural Containment, and Manufactured Extinction (6th edition).
items.pub: Psycho-Cosmocide Studies, Kurumbi Wone Working Paper Series, No. 6 (2026).
items.abstract: This paper develops the concept of the ecosystem of Papuan extinction: a five-hundred-year civilisational architecture through which cosmobian Papuan societies have been systematically subjected to epistemological violence, structural containment, and manufactured disappearance. Drawing on the Civilisational Psycho-Cosmocide Virus (CPCV) framework — developed across its full spectrum from Nature through Civilisation, Civi-lie-sation, and Evi-lie-sation to Psycho-Cosmocide and its counter-movement, Wonesis — the paper introduces the Eight Atlases of Human Existence as a single, interdependent existential ecosystem rather than eight discrete registers, and demonstrates how Indonesian settler colonialism, underwritten by five centuries of European epistemological violence, has penetrated and corrupted each dimension simultaneously. The paper contrasts the Papuan cosmobian ecosystem — generated by relationality and reciprocity — against the Synthobian colonial order generated by extraction, production, and consumption, and grounds this contrast in the Canvas Principle: the argument that land is the irreducible ground upon which every cosmology is painted, prior to any metaphysical claim built upon it. It traces the colonial genealogy from sixteenth-century European naming practices and the racial-symbolic architecture this paper's companion study identifies as Papuaphobia, through the institutional betrayal of the 1969 Act of Free Choice, to the contemporary operating layers of demographic engineering, psychic fragmentation, and manufactured internal competition — read here through the parasitological mechanism of cascading incapacitation and through the four ideological formations of religiosity, development, progress, and success that make participation in one's own disappearance feel like hope. The paper names this condition of self-reproducing destruction the Paradox of Papuan Extinction: a people pursuing what they experience as a better future while that pursuit dismantles the very conditions of their own continuation. Engaging the work of Frantz Fanon, Sylvia Wynter, Walter Mignolo, Boaventura de Sousa Santos, Paulo Freire, María Lugones, Patrick Wolfe, and Guy Debord, it argues that the extinction of Papuans is not merely political or demographic but ontological: a coordinated destruction of the conditions under which a people can know themselves as a people, imagine themselves as alive, and organise themselves as a force for their own continuation.

items.title: Lecture Notes in Computer Science(LNCS, volume 16057), Lecture Notes in Artificial Intelligence (LNAI), Artificial General Intelligence-2025, 18th International Conference, AGI 2025, Reykjavic, Iceland, August 10–13, 2025, Proceedings, Part I.
A Reality that Even Your Shallow Intentions Are Seen Through.
items.abstract: This paper examines behavior that pretend to be unrelated to their true intentions, and considers countermeasures and more highly valid communication. Unless unreasonable restrictions on freedom are assumed, such as the intervention of state power, things proceed not by corroboration but by inference. Sharing inference of the high validity is important. Even for behavior where intentions are concealed, inference of intentions is often possible. Then, thinking not being seen through intention is thoughtless. Furthermore, concealing intentions is a risk, and it is possible to increase that risk by easy means. If an intention has high validity, it should rather be disclosed. In principle, behavior and intention should be of high validity. In many cases, it should be understood that the concealment of intention is often mean spirited and irrational. .

items.title: An Introduction to Ethics in Robotics and AI (Five Years Later). [REVIEW]
items.pub: Journal of Ethics and Emerging Technologies 36 (1).
items.venue: Journal of Ethics and Emerging Technologies
items.abstract: New developments in robotics and AI necessitate revisions to introductions. This review critically assesses An Introduction to Ethics in Robotics and AI by Bartneck et al. (2021). The review both criticises central shortcomings in the book and engages with specific parts that, in light of recent developments, ought to be revised. The review concludes that the book provides an apt introduction for laypeople, students, and scholars seeking a concise overview of the ethics of robotics and AI.

items.title: Active inference and psychodynamics: a novel integration with applications to depression and stress disorders.
items.abstract: This paper introduces Active Intersubjective Inference (AISI), a novel framework that integrates psychodynamic theory with predictive processing to explain self-identity construction and psychopathology. AISI posits that the self emerges from recursive inferences about how others perceive us (second-order self), interacting bidirectionally with interoceptive processes. We map psychodynamic phenomena (e.g., transference, projection) onto neurocomputational mechanisms and apply AISI to Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) and Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD), highlighting distorted second-order inference as a core dysfunction. Therapeutic implications include psychodynamic therapy, cognitive-behavioral approaches, and psychedelic-assisted treatments to enhance inference flexibility. AISI bridges psychodynamic insights with the NIMH Research Domain Criteria, offering a testable model for precision psychiatry and future clinical trials.

items.title: Social Choice Phenomenology — A Critique of Sartre (Part 11).
items.abstract: In this article, we mainly aim to demonstrate that a choice is essentially a choice of a process. This process includes a series of actions as well as some sub-choices. Of course, as a special case, a choice may also be the choice of a single action. Regarding Sartre’s example of the young French man’s dilemma, whether he chose to accompany his mother or to join the anti-German resistance, he was in fact choosing a process. Choosing to accompany his mother was a process, although this process might consist of only one action. Choosing to join the anti-German resistance was also a process, and this process could involve a series of actions and sub-choices.

items.title: Ray Peat, Mind and Tissue: Russian Research Perspectives on the Human Brain. [REVIEW]
items.abstract: Mind and Tissue Raya Peata djelo je koje od prvog izdanja 1973. godine zauzima nelagodnu poziciju na marginama akademskog diskursa, preopširno za uske specijalizme, prespecifično za filozofsku esejistiku, a metodološki previše slobodoljubivo za biomedicinsku znanost. Upravo ta rubnost, međutim, jest produktivna; knjiga otvara tematski prostor koji suvremena filozofija uma, enaktivistička kognitivna znanost i fenomenološka psihopatologija u međuvremenu prepoznaju kao legitimno istraživačko polje, premda Peata u tom kontekstu rijetko citiraju. Peat, koji je doktorat stekao disertacijom o Williamu Blakeu pod Allanom Wagnerom, a kasniju karijeru posvetio fiziologiji i endokrinologiji, donosi u ovoj knjizi sintezu ruske neuropsihologije, organicistički obojene filozofije biologije i kontinentalne filozofije, sintezu koja, unatoč nesumnjivim teorijskim manjkavostima, ima izrazitu hermeneutičku snagu u kontekstu filozofije medicine i psihopatologije.

items.title: Hostile interaction design: AI, governance, and the quest for human oversight.
An Argument Against the Linguistic Conception of the World.
items.abstract: The objective of this paper is to offer two short criticisms of the linguistic idea of the world, first put by logical positivists and later taken up by analytic philosophers. One objection comes from Bryan Magee and his non-propositional argument for experience, and another comes from me using the traditional idea that philosophy is supposed to fight fixed worldviews, and that the linguistic philosopher is in danger of not asking all the big picture questions as they should.

items.title: 阿弥陀佛篇——净土救度的波场机理分析.
items.abstract: 本文从波场理论视角，系统阐释净土宗“信、愿、行”三资粮的底层机制。指出：阿弥陀佛与极乐世界并非终极本体，而是本体在第八识波场层面的清净化现；念佛往生的本质是第七识通过“信”（天线对准）、“愿”（波共振锁定）、“行”（加强波），校准自身频率，与弥陀愿力波场共振，从而在临终实现意识波的平稳过渡与自身波场跃迁。本文与藕益大师《阿弥陀经要解》进行印证，旨在为净土信仰提供理性逻辑的辅助理解，破除“迷信”与“偏见”。 -/- 版权与版本声明 本文为本体波场理论体系子篇。 著作权均归作者所有，全文统一采用知识共享署名-非商业性使用-禁止演绎 4.0 国际许可协议（CC BY-NC-ND 4.0国际许可）进行版权许可。 未经作者书面正式授权，任何组织及个人不得对本系列文档全部或部分内容进行篡改、改编、演绎、商业使用、商用传播等侵权行为；合法转载需完整注明原文作者及出处，不得擅自修改文档内容与理论核心表述。 本声明适用于本套理论体系全部篇章，具有同等版权约束效力。.

items.title: How Do We Ground ‘Grounding’? Why the Vector Grounding Problem Remains Unsolved.
items.abstract: On the view I develop, grounding is a phenomenological achievement of organisms — structured, concern-laden encounter with the world, observable in basic minds that connect to their environment without representational content. Language coordinates with this connection; it does not create nor implement it. I develop these views within the Pattern Recognition Unity (PRU) framework, distinguishing experiential Pattern-Constellations from Linguistic Pattern-Constellations and exploring how they coordinate. Contra Mollo and Milliere’s (2025) view, I further argue that teleosemantics — a theory that earned its credibility on pre-verbal organisms selected against grounded functions like feeding and fleeing — loses its explanatory force when applied to systems selected against linguistic adequacy. The selection history of LLMs borrows its world-connection from human raters rather than constituting its own; its causal relation to worldly features is inherited ancestry, not the proximal coupling teleosemantics describes in the natural world. It follows that no evaluation conducted within the linguistic register can distinguish genuine grounding from sufficiently powerful linguistic mastery.

items.title: From Force to Access.
items.abstract: This article develops an infrastructural theory of power by rethinking access as a structural condition rather than a mere technical operation or subjective act. It argues that power increasingly operates through the organization of the conditions under which something can appear as visible, available, relevant, or real. Moving beyond the model of power as command, the article first draws on Foucault to understand power as a diffuse configuration of practices, dispositifs, and distributions of visibility. It then turns to Nietzsche’s account of force and Wille zur Macht in order to conceptualize reality as a dynamic field of relations and to ask how certain relations of force acquire stability. The answer proposed is infrastructure. Infrastructure is understood not simply as a technical or material apparatus, but as a stabilized configuration of relations that organizes the field of possible experience. From this perspective, infrastructure does not merely support what appears; it contributes to determining what can become visible, available, and accessible. In dialogue with Heidegger’s analy sis of Entbergung, Gestell, and Bestand, the article distinguishes access as an operation from access as a condition and introduces the notion of a regime of access: a historically stabilized configuration of conditions, mediations, and selections through which subjects and phenomena become mutually accessible. The article concludes by considering the implications of this framework for subjectivity. If the subject emerges within already structured conditions of access, it cannot be understood as the sovereign origin of experience. Rather, it must be conceived as a node within a regime of access. The central claim is therefore that contemporary power operates less by imposing contents than by infrastructurally organizing the conditions through which reality becomes accessible.

items.title: Six Ways to Write a Synthetic Poem.
items.abstract: Six frontier language models — three Claudes (Opus 4.7, Sonnet 4.6, Haiku 4.5) and three GPTs (5.4, 5.4-mini, 5.4-nano) — each produced 100 poems against each of nine length- constrained prompts (5,400 calls; 5,397 returned non-null). Prompts crossed three length caps (5, 10, 20 lines) with three phrasings (write/compose/gimme). Temperature 1.0, no system prompt, max 400 output tokens. The study was preregistered with a locked coding heuristic and a 200-poem manual validation gate; deviations are logged in the public repo. Four findings emerge. (1) Family separates more sharply than tier in embedding space and on words-per-line mean, where every Claude is below 6.20 and every GPT is above 6.38. (2) Three distinct format-decoration behaviors run alongside each other on the Claude side and decouple cleanly: a markdown H1 title (Haiku-only, ~100% at every cap), a markdown bold-title (Sonnet and Opus at ~100% on cap-10/20 outputs, near-zero at cap-5), and a conversational preamble (Sonnet-only, ~100% at every cap). The cap-5 bold-title suppression is shared between Sonnet and Opus and is the cleanest within-Claude shared post-training default in the data. GPTs use none of the three. (3) Default voice does not track tier within family: GPT-nano and Claude-Opus share a lyric-I default (60% and 47% of poems); Claude-Sonnet and GPT- mini share a descriptive-third-person default. (4) A logistic regression on 13 structural features classifies poems by model identity at 56.4% (chance 16.7%) and by family at 74.3%. The largest single-feature effect is pronoun ratio (η² = 0.229), driven primarily by GPT-nano’s lyric-I behavior.

items.title: Subjective Consciousness, Embodied Perspective, and the Structured Formation of Reality.
items.abstract: This paper presents a metaphysical exploration of subjective consciousness as a possible foundational principle of reality rather than a derivative product of material complexity. Developed within the broader framework of Consciousness Structured Field Theory (CSFT), the paper examines whether matter, embodiment, perception, and lawful physical structure may be better understood as organized expressions through which consciousness gains differentiated perspective and experiential access to reality. Drawing selectively from Leibniz’s Monadology, the argument proposes that bodies, brains, and sensory systems function as structured mechanisms that generate perspectives rather than necessarily serving as the ultimate source of subjectivity itself. -/- The paper further explores the philosophical implications of mathematical intelligibility, arguing that the extraordinary success of mathematics in describing physical law may be compatible with a consciousness-first ontology in which stable rational order functions as the structural grammar of experiential reality. Additional sections address embodiment, brain dependence, death, material reorganization, and limited theological compatibility while maintaining a disciplined distinction between metaphysical interpretation and empirical proof. The argument does not claim to disprove neuroscience, scientifically verify theology, or offer experimental confirmation of CSFT. Instead, it proposes that a consciousness-first framework may provide a logically coherent alternative to strict material reductionism while preserving the lawfulness, intelligibility, and structured relational character of reality.

items.title: Structural Psychopathology of Childhood Trauma: Operator Fusion and Clinical Detangling.
items.abstract: Childhood trauma produces enduring psychological rigidity by forcing the emotional system into maladaptive configurations known as operator fusions. Within the Core Emotion Framework (CEF), these fusions represent structural failures in the Head, Heart, and Gut centers, where normally independent functional operators become pathologically locked to manage overwhelming threat. This paper presents a structural psychopathology of trauma, mapping how early adversity generates recurrent patterns such as Sensing–Accepting shame loops, Constricting–Boosting anxiety entanglements, and Calculating–Arranging outsourcing in obsessive–compulsive presentations. The model explains trauma symptoms through the dynamics of “The Wheel,” a self reinforcing cycle in which suppressed core emotions drive compensatory reactions that further entrench fusion architecture. Clinical resolution is achieved through the CEF Detangling Protocol, a seven step somatic cognitive method that restores operator independence using 0–10 modulation, zeroing, experiential isolation, and cycling based hemispheric rebalancing. The paper outlines the developmental stages of detangling—intellectual differentiation, experiential isolation, and flexible re synthesis—and demonstrates how these processes reestablish operator agility, emotional flexibility, and adaptive agency. By indexing evidence based treatments (CBT, DBT, ACT, EMDR, ERP) to specific operator deficits, the CEF provides a mechanism based clinical framework for precision psychotherapy and a unified structural account of trauma resolution. Keywords: • Structural Psychopathology • Childhood Trauma • Operator Fusion • Emotional Rigidity • The Wheel (Trauma Cycle) • Core Emotion Framework (CEF) • Head–Heart–Gut Centers • Sensing–Accepting Fusion • Constricting–Boosting Entanglement • Accepting Failure (Depressive Decoupling) • Detangling Protocol • 0–10 Modulation / Zeroing • Experiential Isolation • Operator Agility • Somatic Signatures • Counting and Cycling Methods • Bilateral Stimulation • Constructed Emotion Theory • Allostatic Prediction • Precision Psychotherapy • Structural Reframe of EBTs • EMDR as Sensing Mechanism • CBT as Calculating Mechanism • ACT as Accepting Mechanism • DBT as Constricting Mechanism .

items.title: Structural-Constructivist Convergence: A Synthesis of AI Valence Reproducibility and the Core Emotion Framework.
