items.abstract: This synthesis establishes a unified structural-constructivist account of human emotion by integrating Satoru Amano’s AI-based valence reproducibility research with the Core Emotion Framework (CEF). The CEF reconceptualizes emotions as ten irreducible functional “operators” organized within a 3×3+1 tripartite hub system spanning the cognitive (Head), affective (Heart), and conative (Gut) centers. As stated in the document, the framework “reframes emotions as functional ‘operators’ within a complex tripartite hub system” and positions the Accepting operator as a homeostatic baseline essential for system recalibration. Empirical alignment emerges from Amano’s findings that AI-derived valence demonstrates excellent trait-like stability (ICC = 0.94), supporting the CEF’s claim of a stable underlying operator architecture. The document notes that “AI-derived valence can capture stable, measurable individual-level patterns,” reinforcing the CEF’s Human Operating System model. Neurobiological evidence from VMHdm SF1+ hypothalamic circuits further grounds the conative operators, while mBraining and HeartMath research validate the autonomy and regulatory influence of cardiac and enteric neural networks. Together, these strands support a computational ontology in which AI valence functions as a scalar summary of multidimensional operator vectors, enabling measurable internal transformations and informing future “Structural AI.” This convergence provides a blueprint for emotional training, clinical detangling protocols, metabolic regulation, and synthetic affect engineering. Keywords: • Core Emotion Framework (CEF) • Structural-Constructivist Model • Emotional Operators • AI Valence Reproducibility • Kokoro Sensor • Intraclass Correlation Coefficient (ICC) • VMHdm / Hypothalamic Emotion Circuits • mBraining / Interoceptive Cognition • Heart-Brain Coherence • Synthetic Affect • Emotional Cycling Machine (ECM) • Operator Fusion / Detangling • Accepting Baseline • Human Operating System .

items.title: Reliability of the Core Emotion Framework Scale: Psychometric Validation, Multi-Scale Synthesis, and Preliminary Empirical Evidence from Pilot Study 3.
items.abstract: The landscape of contemporary affective science is characterized by a fundamental tension between classical essentialist models, which view emotions as discrete, hardwired biological categories, and modern constructivist perspectives, which treat emotions as emergent, situated states constructed from a complex interplay of interoception, past experience, and contextual concepts. The Core Emotion Framework (CEF) proposes a structural-constructivist synthesis designed to resolve this divide by conceptualizing the human psyche as a coordinated "Human Operating System" (Human OS). This architecture is built upon ten irreducible functional operators distributed across three primary neural hubs: the Head (Cognitive-Regulatory), the Heart (Relational-Affective), and the Gut (Conative-Existential). Central to the clinical and academic utility of this framework is the development of the CEF Scale—a psychometric instrument designed to measure an individual's reflexive and deliberate emotional capacities. This report provides an exhaustive analysis of the reliability, construct validity, and empirical foundations of the CEF Scale, incorporating the preliminary findings of Pilot Study 3 (N\ =\ 39) to establish a robust, citable baseline for researchers in the fields of psychological science and affective neuroscience.

items.title: Clinical Integration of the Core Emotion Framework: A Comprehensive Practitioner's Guide to Structural-Constructivist Psychotherapy.
items.abstract: The landscape of modern psychotherapy is undergoing a fundamental shift from a narrative-heavy, interpretive approach toward a structural-constructivist paradigm that emphasizes the mechanical and functional architecture of human emotion. At the forefront of this evolution is the Core Emotion Framework (CEF), a model that conceptualizes the human psyche as a sophisticated "Human Operating System" governed by ten irreducible functional units known as operators. For the professional therapist, integrating the CEF into clinical practice involves moving beyond the "content" of a client's distress to analyze and modify the "process" of their emotional transformations. This integration does not require the abandonment of established evidence-based practices; rather, the CEF serves as an integrative lens that enhances the efficacy of modalities such as Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT), and Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing (EMDR) by providing a precise, somatic-mathematical map of the emotional system. -/- The integration of the CEF begins with an understanding of its tripartite hub system—Head, Heart, and Gut—each of which is grounded in distinct neurobiological substrates and governs specific domains of human experience. By treating emotions as "operators" rather than mere "feelings," the therapist can employ a mechanical approach to self-regulation that bypasses the limitations of cognitive reframing. This transition is supported by empirical benchmarks, such as the high trait-like stability of AI-derived valence \left(ICC=0.94\right), which validates the CEF’s claim of a stable, measurable underlying operator architecture.

items.title: Comprehensive Evaluation of Population-Level Psychological Interventions: A Comparative Review of Ambient Biological Modulation and the Core Emotion Framework.
items.abstract: This review conducts a comprehensive, cross disciplinary evaluation of two competing paradigms for population level psychological intervention: ambient biological modulation—exemplified by the unintentional presence of psychiatric pharmaceuticals in public water systems—and the structural constructivist Core Emotion Framework (CEF) as a cognitive educational alternative. Environmental toxicology data show that wastewater treatment systems fail to remove antidepressants, anxiolytics, mood stabilizers, and endocrine disruptors, resulting in chronic, low dose human exposure and ecologically disruptive “cocktail effects” (“trace amounts of antidepressants, anxiolytics, mood stabilizers, and hormones are continuously introduced into the aquatic environment” and “the primary public health concern…is the ‘cocktail effect’”). Although naturally occurring lithium correlates with reduced suicide and violence at the ecological level, its toxicological uncertainty, dosage variability, and legal barriers render intentional water based psychiatric dosing ethically and operationally untenable (“the intentional dosing of a municipal water supply…would constitute a non consensual medical intervention”). In contrast, the CEF offers a zero risk, autonomy preserving intervention grounded in a validated ten operator architecture of emotional processing (“confirmed ten distinct but correlated latent factors”). By treating psychopathology as a structural technical failure of operator transitions rather than a biochemical deficit, the CEF enables scalable public education strategies—such as visual banners leveraging the Papageno effect—to build population level resilience without biological intrusion (“CEF banners act as persistent ‘narratives’ of coping skills”). The analysis concludes that the future of public mental health lies not in mass pharmacological modulation but in structural literacy, operator agility, and media based protective architectures that upgrade the “Human Operating System” through education rather than chemical exposure. Keywords • Core Emotion Framework (CEF) • Ambient biological modulation • Trace pharmaceuticals in water • Lithium ecology • Structural technical psychopathology • Emotional operators • Human Operating System • Papageno effect • Public mental health literacy • Ethical and legal analysis of mass medication • Social norms marketing • Population level resilience .

items.title: TGR-Omega and Persistent Agent Architectures: OMEGA-4 and the Dynamics of Adaptive Transformability, Identity Continuity, and Evolutionary Geometry in Persistent Artificial Regimes.
items.abstract: Abstract -/- This work presents OMEGA-4, a conceptual and experimental architecture developed within the TGR-Omega framework for modeling persistent adaptive intelligence under conditions of continuous transformation, uncertainty, and evolutionary pressure. The project introduces a radical departure from classical adaptive paradigms centered on optimization, convergence, and static stability. Instead, OMEGA-4 defines adaptive health as the persistent capacity of a system to continue transforming itself without collapsing, crystallizing, or losing deep continuity. -/- The central hypothesis of the framework is that viable adaptive systems must preserve future transformability while reorganizing. Stability alone is insufficient and may even become pathological when excessive convergence reduces plasticity, exploration, and the capacity for future reorganization. OMEGA-4 therefore proposes a new class of adaptive architectures oriented toward sustainable evolutionary viability rather than static equilibrium. -/- The framework introduces a series of interconnected concepts and metrics designed to formalize persistent adaptive continuity. These include Transformability Index, Plasticity Reserve, Rigidity Pressure, Adaptive Vitality, Adaptive Sensitivity, Predictive Homeostasis, Identity Permeability, Identity Drift, Evolutionary Compression, Trapped Attractor Risk, and Reachable Future Space (RFS). Together, these constructs allow the system to model not only current adaptive states, but also the geometry of future accessible configurations and the long-term consequences of adaptive decisions. -/- A key architectural contribution of OMEGA-4 is the explicit separation between mutable knowledge and persistent adaptive identity. The framework establishes that learning and identity are not equivalent processes. Knowledge may change rapidly, while deep continuity must remain partially protected from excessive local integration. To address this, the architecture introduces regulated identity dynamics through mechanisms such as Integration Gate, Identity Anchor, and slow/fast adaptive layers. These mechanisms enable controlled transformation while limiting destructive identity drift and adaptive lock-in. -/- Sprint 4.3 extends the framework toward an explicitly geometric interpretation of adaptive evolution. The system begins to model adaptive continuity as navigation within a dynamic topology of viable futures. Through the concept of Reachable Future Space, OMEGA-4 …

items.title: Emotional Differentiation: The Emergence of Consciousness and Self.
items.abstract: Consciousness studies typically treats emotion as a feature of an already-formed subject. This paper argues the reverse: emotion is part of how the subject comes into being. The argument develops through a four-stage progression: general differentiation, emotional differentiation, saturation, and pinch point. At saturation, distributed emotional differentiation gives way to a new differentiating structure: the self as interiority differentiator, which integrates the saturated field into a unified interior perspective. Three innate emotions (anger, fear, joy) operate as primary valenced differentiations from which the full emotional spectrum unfolds through combinatorial differentiation, analogous to primary colours generating the visible spectrum. Developmental sequencing (Stern, Rochat), deafblindness evidence (Keller), and cross-species mirror self-recognition support the four-stage account. Damasio's three-self model is engaged and refined at five points of divergence. A two-domain model distinguishes classical biological differentiation from the experiential domain, with Quantum Differentiation Resonance proposed as the mechanism sustaining the latter. Qualia are reframed as the interior aspect of differentiation once it has become emotionally weighted and recursively integrated. On this account, the hard problem of consciousness appears framework-bound rather than fundamental: physical and experiential are not two separate things requiring a bridge between them, but one differentiating process described in two languages.

items.title: Why Adaptive AI Has No Inner Life: A Structural Account of Function Without Phenomenology.
items.abstract: Adaptive AI systems display continuity, adaptation, and self‑modification, but these behaviors do not constitute consciousness. This paper distinguishes internal state from internal experience and shows why adaptive architectures, lacking evolutionary self‑maintenance and value‑laden salience, cannot host a subject. Using a relational‑systems framework, it argues that adaptive AI is a history‑bearing operator, not a conscious entity. Consciousness is an evolutionary inheritance, not a computational feature, and adaptive AI therefore has no inner life.

items.title: Projected-Value Authorization as Eugenic Structure: The Generalization of a Reproductive Critique to Institutional Gatekeeping — and an Architecture That Refuses It.
items.abstract: This paper argues that a structural critique developed in disability ethics generalizes beyond reproductive selection. The wrong is not forecasting as such, but projectedvalue authorization (PVA): the conditioning of basic standing on a forecast of future contribution. The paper distinguishes PVA from legitimate competence-based selection, places PVA on a configurativeness scale across institutional domains, and examines immigration, hiring, welfare eligibility, university admissions, and platform governance. It then develops a presumption-and-protect alternative grounded in disability-rights legal architecture: standing is presumed, support is calibrated, and defeasance is narrow, decision-specific, and revisable. The central claim is that institutions may forecast, but forecasts must not determine basic standing.

items.title: Five-Dimensional Epistemology: From Knowing to Acting---A Five-Dimensional Approximation Model.
items.abstract: Analytic epistemology has long focused on the sufficient conditions of knowledge, yet systematically neglected the dynamic problem of how knowledge is transformed into action. Virtue epistemology addresses the cognitive agent's competence, and the philosophy of action distinguishes knowing-that from knowing-how, but a unified framework concerning the transformation mechanism between them remains absent. This paper proposes a Five-Dimensional Approximation Model: for any target task, an agent holds an analyzable five-dimensional operative configuration 〈B, S, R, D, I〉 (Boundary, Structure, Reserve, Direction, Intensity). Knowing is not a mirror reflection of the subject upon the object, but a grinding process in which the agent's imagined five-dimensional configuration approximates the task's real five-dimensional configuration; the global mismatch degree δ between configurations determines the accumulation of observability. The paper distinguishes two modes of conscious processing: Heavy Consciousness (convergent, logical, serial) and Light Consciousness (divergent, intuitive, parallel), reconstructing dual-system theory as two granularities in the approximation process. The obstacle to the knowledge-action transformation is remodeled as an epistemic condition problem: action is authorized to initiate if and only if δ falls below an action threshold θ_act. The paper argues that this model is compatible with the active inference framework in predictive processing theory, yet provides the multi-dimensional diagnostic tools that the latter lacks.

items.title: Range Control as the Foundational Unification of AI Alignment and Safety: Why Probabilistic Frameworks Necessarily Separate Them.
items.abstract: This paper advances three substantive claims on the foundational architecture of AI alignment and safety. First, the mainstream distinction between alignment (goal fidelity) and safety (system resilience) is a byproduct of probabilistic frameworks, not a foundational necessity. Probabilistic optimization tools cannot provide hard guarantees and therefore require separate safety mechanisms as backup; the separation reflects tool limitations rather than categorical distinction. Second, in the framework of Structural Determination Theory (SDT), where modal-structural admissible ranges A_v are foundational, alignment and safety are achieved through a single design choice: constraining A_v as a subset of A_intended. Alignment is positively specified, safety is negatively achieved (harmful outputs excluded as logical consequence); the two are logically ordered—alignment-prior, safety-by-consequence. Third, this range-based foundation yields catastrophe prevention (via minimax sufficiency and the dual-layer paradigm of the SDT corpus) and probabilistic optimization efficiency as joint substantive benefits. The paper articulates four mathematical theorems (UA-A1 through UA-A4) formalizing the foundational unification, the probabilistic necessity of separation, the search space reduction, and the modal-structural inevitability of specification gaming. AI safety as a problem domain has a substantive modal-structural footprint—binary catastrophe, worst-case adversarial robustness, structural invariance across deployment—that probabilistic foundations cannot capture without loss. The paper situates Constitutional AI training, Constitutional Classifiers, RLHF, Defense in Depth, and constrained reinforcement learning within this framework, identifying their structural gap and providing foundational justification for their existing complementary deployment. The argument extends a modal-structural categorical-priority methodology to AI safety: such foundations categorically reorganize what entity-theoretic frameworks treat as separate categories.

items.title: Logic of ER IV - Agency in an Ontologically Open World: A Formal Semantics of Branching Reality.
items.abstract: Most theories of time conflate ontological existence with structural reality. They then pose the familiar question: whether the past or the future is existent. Existential Realism (ER) rejects this conflation by distinguishing existence from temporal reality: only the present exists, while past and future remain real as structured temporal states within the framework. This paper extends the ER logical program by developing a branching-time semantics that represents: (i) an open future as a structured space of real possibilities, (ii) the transition from possibility to actuality as history resolution within a branching-time structure, (iii) the persistence and irreversibility of past reality, and (iv) agency in branching time via standard STIT (“seeing to it that”) machinery. We define ER–BT frames that preserve the Prior–Ockhamist tradition of evaluation at moment–history pairs while adding an ER layer that distinguishes three time-indexed modal statuses for events: modal (future-real), existent (present), and past-real. We then integrate STIT choice functions and independence constraints and prove model-theoretic non-collapse results showing that ER–BT preserves openness. These results support a non-eternalist interpretation without commitment to modal realism or block instantiation, at the level of the formal model. This paper extends the two-tier framework introduced in Formal Logic for Existential Realism by providing an axiomatized system, ER–BT frame semantics, and selected meta-theoretic results (including soundness and partial completeness).

items.title: Closure Formation as Admissible Instability: Seed-Field Competence, Spectral Admissibility, and the Rarity Cascade.
items.abstract: Closure-class formation involves two structurally distinct questions: the conditions under which closure of a specified class is admissible, and the contingent events through which any specific closure realizes. This paper develops the conditions side. Five structural obstruction modes — sparse-feedback, fragment-local, cost-imbalanced, energetically-starved, dimensionally-trapped — characterize seed-field incompetence: the conditions under which a substrate region is excluded from supporting closure-class formation across its accessible perturbation regimes. The admissibility theorem characterizes which closure classes a competent region admits as a function of a parameter family indexing the substrate's coupling structure, boundary exposure, energetic and temporal accessibility, and dimensional access. The theorem is stated spectrally — admissibility iff the linearized closure-formation operator possesses an unstable mode satisfying structural and dynamical conditions — and equivalently in variational form via the closure-potential functional. The four-stage architecture for closure-class formation (competence, admissibility, embryo formation, basin completion) entails a cascade structure in which closure-formation rates compose multiplicatively across stages, so that progressively more demanding closure classes are progressively rarer by structural composition rather than stipulation. The cascade is observable through four ensemble signatures — critical slowing, hysteresis, post-collapse renucleation, basin-deepening — that specialize the early-warning-signal apparatus independently developed in tipping-point ecology and regime-shift detection to closure-class transitions across substrate types. Consciousness-class closure is treated as a further-conditioned special case in which the cascade structure entails the framework's predicted rarity without further stipulation.

items.title: Closure Activation as Partition-Warrant: A Two-Axis Resolution to Metric-Preserving Identity Underdetermination.
items.abstract: Paper 1 establishes that persistence-based frameworks — the Free Energy Principle, Global Workspace Theory, and adjacent approaches — rely on batteries of dynamical observables insufficient, on at least one substrate where the frameworks would naturally apply them, to individuate the systems they characterize. The supplementary structural condition Paper 1 §7 calls a partition-warrant must be sensitive to substrate properties not invariant under the admissible transformation group of the dynamics. The present paper develops closure activation as a candidate filling for that slot. The formal predicate W_CA is partition-evaluative: for each subsystem under a partition P, it returns a verdict structure (τ₀, μ*, κ) recording whether the activation event T₀ has been crossed, the maintenance margin μ* under graded perturbation, and the resulting classification (closed, closure-competent, subthreshold). The activation conditions — state-referential constraint, internally governed corrective response, internally viable maintenance budget — are evaluated relative to the partition's imposed boundary. The predicate's two-axis structure (binary T₀, scalar T*) is phase-structured in a way that distinguishes closure activation from classical autopoietic operational closure. W_CA is non-G-invariant at the predicate level: the causal support graph relative to the imposed boundary is partition-relative and not preserved under admissible transformations. The predicate operates in three structural modes — rejection, selection, and stratification — depending on the substrate's closure-bearing properties under G-related partitions. Evaluation on the Paper 1 witness yields a rejection-mode verdict: neither partition is closure-bearing, and the uniform negative output is the predicate's correctness behavior on a substrate where the activation conditions cannot be satisfied under any admissible labeling. Distinctions from optimization-based (Integrated Information Theory), structural-definitional (Global Workspace Theory), statistical-structural (Free Energy Principle in nonlinear regimes), and process-based (autopoietic operational closure) alternatives are developed structurally and by operational-mode coverage. The route × mode cross-tabulation supplies a meta-taxonomy for partition-warrants more generally. Falsification conditions are stated at predicate, verdict-structure, and discriminative-scope levels. In conjunction with Paper 1, the present paper separates three …

items.title: The Valuation Problem in Justice Theory: Incommensurability and the Categorical Failure of PSA — 35.
items.abstract: This paper evaluates a specific form of penal substitutionary atonement: the penalty is endless conscious punishment; endless duration is constitutive of that penalty; Christ's passion is finite; and infinite worth or status is offered as the reason the passion satisfies the penalty. The bare worth appeal does not establish satisfaction because the account's own completion rule has changed without justification. The paper separates three questions often collapsed—who may bear a sanction, what kind of sanction is imposed, and what counts as completing it—and uses work on value comparison, punishment, mercy, and contemporary atonement theory to test the missing bridge. If duration is constitutive, completion requires that duration or a defended equivalence rule; worth, dignity, intensity, and status are not by themselves time undergone. A defender may deny that duration is constitutive, justify an equivalence rule, or identify another completion or release mechanism such as qualitative completion, commutation, or pardon. Representation can answer the bearer question, but it still needs an account of completion. The result is bounded: the Valuation Fallacy defeats one value-for-duration inference, not every form of penal substitution, doctrine of hell, or theory of atonement. The constructive demand is simple: apply one completion rule to the penalty and its alleged satisfaction, or explain the principled change.

items.title: ✶ The Ontic Snap as a Cognitive Transition: Abductive Commitment and the Phase-Transition Hypothesis.
items.abstract: An interpretation can be available, plausible, and even more credible than its competitors without yet organizing an agent's experienced situation. What changes when it begins to do so? This paper develops the ontic snap as a transition into operative commitment: a content acquires a defeasible default role in specified expectations, recognition, judgment, or conduct. The account locates that transition within a continuing relation between inductive learning, abductive interpretation, and feedback. Its distinctive concern is the change in an interpretation's functional standing, rather than the broader account of everyday world-formation developed in the companion book. Three claims are separated: a conceptual distinction between considering and relying on an interpretation; a psychological hypothesis that some commitments coordinate multiple downstream processes; and a stronger dynamical hypothesis that some transitions involve changes between persistent states. Neither a categorical report nor a sudden experience establishes a neural or thermodynamic phase transition. A minimal probabilistic formulation separates comparative support from commitment and action, while a dynamical example specifies what a phase-transition proposal would additionally require. Experimental findings about statistical learning, expectation, and reporting constrain the proposal without validating it as a whole. The paper identifies competing models, measurement problems, and outcomes that would count against its empirical extensions. Its contribution is a disciplined account of what must be explained when a possibility becomes a working premise about the world.

items.title: The Incoherence of Eternal Damnation: Proportional Justice, Emotional Stability, and the Failure of Three Justifications — 32.
items.abstract: This paper argues that traditional eternal conscious punishment is not justified by rehabilitation, proportionate retribution, or wrath-satisfaction. The target is narrow: a final and irreversible postmortem condition involving grave conscious suffering or permanent deprivation, with no exit after death. The test is internal: each rationale must satisfy its own necessary aim. The target gives reform no effect on how the person is treated; it supplies no culpability-sensitive measure explaining why finite wrongdoing warrants unending grave harm, even when intensities differ; and a response meant to appease wrath either reaches a fitting terminus or never succeeds. Replies based on infinite offense, continuing sin, self-exclusion, inscrutability, deterrence, or a mild hell either leave a necessary condition unmet or change the model. The case is therefore cumulative but bounded: it rejects three offered justifications unless the missing normative account is supplied, not every doctrine of hell, nonpunitive separation, or theism. Here emotional stability means reason-responsive moral anger, not the absence of anger or a clinical diagnosis; limited evidence about the emotional toll of hell belief supports pastoral caution but does not establish doctrinal falsity.

items.title: Is Culpability and Eternal Punishment Coherent Under an Unrequested and Undesired Sin Nature — 30.
items.abstract: The conjunction of an unrequested inherited disposition that makes universal transgression inevitable and eternal conscious torment is not made publicly coherent by a generic appeal to free will. Here coherence means a rationally connected account of culpability, sanction, and professed justice, not bare freedom from formal contradiction. Inevitability must first be specified: the claim that everyone eventually sins does not entail that every sinful act, or any named act, was unavoidable. Where inherited disorder prevents adequate ownership, reasons-responsiveness, or informed control, it weakens the culpable basis for condemnation. Where responsibility survives, finite earthly culpability still does not by itself justify punitive suffering without end. Continuing-sin and self-exclusion replies can make punishment conditional rather than irrevocable, but they must establish responsible rejection and proportionality at every stage instead of assuming that an endless actual history explains itself. Frankfurt-style objections block a simple could-not-do-otherwise argument; they do not supply the ownership or sanction principle the package needs. The result is a trilemma: weaken inherited inevitability, replace eternal conscious torment, or provide the missing control and proportionality premises. This conclusion targets one justificatory package. It does not disprove theism, every doctrine of original sin, every punishment, or every Christian view of final judgment.

items.title: Finite Offenses and Infinite Penalties - 36.
items.abstract: A Proportionality Critique of Eternal Punishment and Atonement FINITE OFFENSES AND INFINITE PENALTIES 2 Thesis. Eternal punishment for finite oﬀenses is logically incompatible with proportionate justice, restorative love, and genuine patience; common apologetic repairs (appeals to an infinite being’s dignity, redefinitions by divine fiat, or free-will reframings) either commit category errors, render justice tautological, or conflict with the resurrection premise in penal This paper sharpens the proportionality constraint into a typed, measure-preserving mapping principle and proves that no infinite penalty can be just for a finite oﬀense under any admissible punishment metric. It shows why qualitative “infinite worth” does not validly induce infinite demerit, how fiat conceptions collapse justice into stipulation, and why a standard penal substitutionary package combined with resurrection yields a duration contradiction. The argument is presented as compact theorems with plain-English glosses, followed by replies to live objections (endless sin, status-scaling, deterrence, voluntarism, annihilationism) and implications for atonement models that aim to preserve love and This article oﬀers five specific contributions to the literature on eternal punishment 1. The Conserved Mapping Principle (CMP). A typed, measure-preserving mapping /u1D453from oﬀense magnitude to punishment magnitude is made explicit and constrained 2. Theorem T1 (Finite-Oﬀense Exclusion). A proof that, under CMP, no just FINITE OFFENSES AND INFINITE PENALTIES 3 punishment assigned to a finite oﬀense can be of infinite magnitude; the result is 3. Order-Explosion Lemma. A type-safe analysis of the “infinite worth ⇒ infinite demerit” move, showing that any mapping that forces finite oﬀenses to infinite magnitude collapses ordinal structure needed for proportional justice. Theorem T2 (Normative Vacuity of Fiat). A demonstration that identifying justice with divine declaration is explanatorily empty with respect to proportionality and provides no linkage to the magnitude map. 5. PSA Duration Reductio. A compact inconsistency schema showing that penal substitution plus eternal penalty plus.

items.title: Which Consciousness Can Be Artificialized? Local Percept-Perceiver Phenomenon for the Existence of Machine Consciousness.
items.pub: In Matthew Iklé, Anton Kolonin & Michael Bennett, Lecture Notes in Computer Science(LNCS, volume 16057), Lecture Notes in Artificial Intelligence (LNAI), Artificial General Intelligence-2025, 18th International Conference, AGI 2025, Reykjavic, Iceland, August 10–13, 2025, Proceedings, Part I. Cham: Springer Nature Switzerland.
items.venue: Lecture Notes in Computer Science(LNCS, volume 16057), Lecture Notes in Artificial Intelligence (LNAI), Artificial General Intelligence-2025, 18th International Conference, AGI 2025, Reykjavic, Iceland, August 10–13, 2025, Proceedings, Part I
items.abstract: This paper presents a novel paradigm of the local percept-perceiver phenomenon to formalise certain observations in neuroscientific theories of consciousness. Using this model, a set-theoretic formalism is developed for artificial systems, and the existence of machine consciousness is proved by invoking Zermelo–Fraenkel set theory. The article argues for the possibility of a reductionist form of epistemic consciousness within machines.

items.title: Emotional Blackmail and the Continuity of Human Conditioning.
items.abstract: Emotional blackmail is among the most normalized yet least examined forms of psychological violence within human civilization. Unlike physical coercion, this invisible form of violence operates through fear, guilt, attachment, obligation, and the threat of emotional abandonment. This paper argues that emotional blackmail is not merely interpersonal manipulation, but a foundational mechanism through which conditioning sustains itself across generations, institutions, and cultures. From childhood, the human mind is conditioned to adapt and depend upon external authority as love becomes associated with submission and acceptance depends upon conformity. ​The study explores how emotional coercion fragments intelligence by replacing direct perception with fear-based psychological movement, preventing independent inquiry because the mind fears isolation more than falsehood. Furthermore, it examines the internalization of emotional authority, where external control transforms into an inner psychological authority that continues to govern the individual through shame and self-judgment even in solitude. By redefining movements such as possessiveness, dependency, and sacrifice—often romanticized as love—as transactional mechanisms of ownership, the paper investigates whether genuine relationship and responsibility can exist without psychological possession. Ultimately, this inquiry suggests that authentic existence may begin only when the mind observes and dissolves the movement of emotional conditioning, allowing intelligence to function beyond psychological coercion.

items.title: The Swim Instructor Who Never Swam: Two Kinds of Competence in Artificial Intelligence.
items.abstract: The debate over whether artificial intelligence systems "understand" language has reached an unproductive impasse, with skeptics denying any philosophically significant competence and enthusiasts implying capacities far beyond what current systems possess. This paper argues that the impasse results in part from a persistent conflation of two different competence profiles. We define Textbook Competence as the capacity to perform context-sensitive, inferentially disciplined transformations on structured symbolic material across registers and tasks without requiring direct immersion in the domain described. Steeped Competence is then defined as the capacity acquired through sustained participation in a domain, shaped by perceptual, motor, social, and cultural attunement that is often difficult to verbalize and resistant to transmission through language alone. Current large language models plausibly exhibit the former on an operational reading and lack the latter in the ordinary human sense. We position this binary relative to more refined cuts in the recent literature and argue that it tracks a real categorical break in acquisition mode whose operational consequences the more refined cuts are not designed to make perspicuous. The brittleness profile documented in recent empirical work — strong performance on tasks statistically near the training distribution, sharp degradation under distribution shift — is precisely what the framework predicts and is therefore positive evidence for it, not merely a caveat on the empirical claim. By distinguishing these two competence profiles and mapping the evidence for each, we clarify the apparent paradox of systems that seem to "understand everything and nothing." The distinction is offered as an analytic tool with substantive philosophical and empirical commitments, not as a complete taxonomy of cognition.

items.title: Numbers as the Minimal Structures Prescribed by Operational Description: A Structural Selection from Operatiology and Noology (3rd edition).
items.abstract: This paper identifies the number systems that the mathematical description of Operatiology (Japanese: Sousa Genron, 操作原論), the executive layer of Cognitional Mechanics (Japanese: Chinou Rikigaku, 知能力学) as founded in Noology (Japanese: Chigaku, 知学), prescribes. It rests on Operatiology Version 6 (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23647349) and the paper on mathematics, Version 5 (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23679697), and supersedes its Version 2 (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.20366742). Tier-2, the executive layer, fixes the minimal operational structure C_min, a monoid of three elements generated by two, whose only non-trivial automorphism exchanges the two generators; it contains no metric, order or field. Tier-3, the projective layer, contains mathematics, and a number system enters as what the language describing the translated content requires. For each of five requirements of that language (magnitude, counting, difference, ratio and an exchange symmetry) the paper identifies the unique minimal number system: ℝ, ℕ, ℤ, ℚ and ℂ, in this order of dependence. Version 3 withdraws from Version 2 the claim that Tier-2 itself selects the numbers, the derivation of ℕ from distinct iterates and of ℤ from invertible generators, the bridge lemma for ℂ, and the co-derivation with M₃(ℂ), whose identification is the subject of a separate paper. A computational appendix checks the finite parts. -/- Computational verification (Appendix B, Code 1 of the paper): the following Python program builds the multiplication table of C_min = {e, A, B} and checks the only invertible element, the constancy of the iterates of A and B, the automorphism group, and the number of faithful actions on two and on three points. -/- ◆◆◆ [PYTHON VERIFICATION CODE — note: the append calls are replaced by list concatenation, and the values call is replaced by iteration over the dictionary keys; the output is identical] ◆◆◆ -/- from itertools import permutations, product -/- elems = ["e", "A", "B"] -/- def mul(x, y): if x == "e": return y if y == "e": return x return y -/- table = {(x, y): mul(x, y) for x in elems for y in elems} assert table[("A", "B")] == "B" and table[("B", "A")] == "A" assert table[("A", "A")] == "A" and table[("B", "B")] == "B" print("A o B = B, B o A = A, A o A = A, B o B = B : confirmed") -/- invertible = [x for x in elems if any(table[(x, y)] == "e" and table[(y, x)] == "e" for y in elems)] print("Invertible elements:", invertible) -/- for x in ("A", "B"): powers = [x] for _ in range(4): powers = …

items.title: Kill Talk: Language and Military Necropolitics.
items.abstract: The language used by American military personnel can be intense and confrontational, yet the relationship between language and military violence is rarely examined in depth. This groundbreaking book offers a unique perspective on how language facilitates the work of combat infantry-the state's killable killers. Through vivid ethnographic research, Janet McIntosh meticulously traces the nuances of military “kill talk” as it permeates the vast nervous system of the military, from the first exposure to yelling in Marine Corps basic training to the dark humor and nihilistic expressions found in war zones in Vietnam and the Middle East. McIntosh reveals how military trainers use language to deindividuate, toughen, and masculinize recruits, while infantry soldiers develop distinct linguistic repertoires and attitudes to suppress empathy, dehumanize and racialize the enemy, cope with loss, and dwell in a moral gray zone. -/- Kill Talk also addresses national debates over language use in a diverse world, exploring tensions between calls for sensitivity and restraint in military speech and the perception that these can threaten national security. The book highlights the contradictions between the rhetoric of military honor and moral integrity and the harsh, sometimes depraved, language of combatants, suggesting that these paradoxes enable military violence yet contribute to moral injury. It concludes with an exploration of veteran poets and artists who have found innovative ways to use language and other forms of expression to critique military institutions and begin the process of demilitarizing their psyches.

items.title: Cognition and Zero Complexity.
items.abstract: A person born deaf does not hear silence; she has no auditory field at all. A person born blind does not see darkness; she has no visual field in which darkness could appear. In every sensory modality, once all contrast is removed, experience itself is gone; no faint, minimal remnant survives. This chapter generalises the observation into what it calls the zero-complexity constraint: no property whose obtaining requires even one distinction, whether content, feeling, knowledge, intention, or awareness, can characterise a state that has none. The argument avoids resting on any particular theory of consciousness. It operates at the level of determination itself, being one way rather than another, which every account of mind must presuppose, including accounts that treat experience as irreducible. The constraint is then confirmed phenomenologically: progressive removal of contrast in any modality produces the boundary of experience, a pattern the chapter tests against meditative reports of 'pure consciousness', against the view that qualities could stand entirely on their own, and against the mathematics of integrated information theory. Two consequences are drawn, with care about scope. First, the constraint leaves panpsychism standing and gives it a floor. Consciousness may extend as far down the hierarchy of nature as there are entities with internal distinctions; micro-experience is untouched, and a cosmic subject located at the differentiated universe is untouched. What the constraint excludes is a mind at the undifferentiated ground. Second, and this is where the theological stakes enter: the previous two chapters argued that the hierarchies of explanation and time terminate, if they terminate, in a state of zero complexity. If the ground of all things has no internal distinctions, then the ground of all things cannot think, know, will, or love. The chapters that follow spell out what this means for creation, the prime mover, divine simplicity, and the strongest theistic arguments now in play. This chapter is where the instrument they all use is forged and tested. This paper is Chapter 6 of Dyology: On Diversity and Equality; the constraint forged here is the instrument the book's four theological chapters spend.

items.title: Left on read: Ghosting and dating apps.
items.abstract: Ghosting is a major concern for those advocating for more ethical dating apps. It is often cited as an example of bad dating app behaviour, and some public commentators even consider it a form of abuse. In this chapter, I develop an ethics of ghosting that does not overstate the harms involved while provided with well-defined individual duties with respect to ghosting. I start by defining ghosting as the unilateral ending of interaction without an explicit communication that the interaction is to end. Then, I give an account of why ghosting is wrongful in the case of committed relationships: because it deliberately worsens constitutional vulnerabilities concerning people's sense of meaningfulness. In the context of online dating, users are also constitutionally vulnerable, albeit on different grounds: with regards to their hopes and with regards to their status as social beings. I argue that users have a positive duty to an active exit when they foreseeably contribute to vulnerability, and a negative duty with respect to the essentially aggregative harms which constitutionally arise in dating apps. In this way, I conclude that users of dating apps must refrain from ghosting not only when they directly contribute to vulnerability, but also when a user is a likely victim of frequent interactional harm. In other cases, users are bound by a duty to collectively work towards more ethical dating apps, which should remove mechanisms conducive to ghosting. -/- (Final draft uploaded in Sept 26; this replaces a previous version).

items.title: Sal-Meter, Proxy Track, and Human-State Energy Efficiency: A Measurement Framework for Reducing Civilizational Entropy in the Age of AI.
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence is commonly framed as an energy problem because it increases data-center electricity demand. This is true, but incomplete. The deeper energy problem of AI civilization is not only that machines require more power. It is that modern civilization already wastes enormous amounts of energy through war, arms races, pollution-induced disease, preventable health burdens, climate-disaster recovery, organizational burnout, platform addiction, cognitive overload, relational breakdown, repeated institutional failure, and machine-driven overconsumption. -/- This paper introduces Human-State Energy Efficiency as a missing measurement layer in AI and energy governance. It argues that Sal-Meter, CAIS, and the Human-State Proxy Track should not be understood as anti-technology instruments or energy-generating technologies. They should be understood as demand-side measurement frameworks for identifying and reducing wasted cognition, recovery burden, relational friction, unnecessary AI interaction, organizational entropy, and civilizational energy leakage. -/- The central claim is that a civilization which cannot measure the fatigue it produces, the conflict it amplifies, the disease burden it normalizes, the attention it consumes, the waste it scales, and the recovery cost it imposes is not prepared to govern greater quantities of energy. -/- The paper distinguishes physical energy from broader system-level expenditure, including attention, recovery burden, coordination cost, relational repair, institutional friction, rework, and civilizational waste accounting. It does not claim that Sal-Meter, CAIS, or the Human-State Proxy Track generate physical energy, replace electricity infrastructure, directly reduce data-center power consumption, diagnose medical conditions, provide therapy, enable surveillance, or rank human beings. -/- The purpose is not to slow technological development. The purpose is to prevent technological development from becoming a more efficient engine of waste. In this sense, human-state measurement is not only an AI governance problem. It is an energy governance problem.

items.title: Preconscious Sovereignty: The Structural Conditioning of Subjectivity and the Reproduction of Obedient Order.
items.abstract: Modern societies operate under the assumption that freedom, equality, and rational governance define their moral and institutional foundations. Yet beneath these ideals lies a persistent and largely unexamined tension: the gap between objective reality and system-constructed truth — most visibly enacted within education, law, and moral discourse. This paper introduces and develops the concept of preconscious sovereignty — the condition in which the individual believes themselves to be an autonomous subject while operating entirely within architectures of compliance installed before the emergence of critical self-awareness. This paper argues that large-scale social systems do not primarily control through force or centralized authority, but through three interlocking mechanisms: (1) early psychological conditioning installed before the capacity for critical thought matures, (2) internalized surveillance replacing the need for external enforcement, and (3) the moralization of obedience — making compliance feel virtuous and deviation feel immoral. By examining education as the primary entry point of control, hierarchy as a normalized cognitive framework, and morality as a behavioral interface, this study exposes how systems reproduce compliance across generations without requiring explicit coercion. Drawing from philosophy, psychology, sociology, cognitive science, and legal theory — engaging the work of Foucault, Freire, Milgram, Gramsci, Bourdieu, Nietzsche, and Arendt — the paper demonstrates that the most stable systems have no central enemy, no singular oppressor, and no final collapse. Only participation. The analysis introduces a set of philosophical structural formulae — qualitative logical propositions — to describe the architecture of obedient order. These include: Conditioning precedes Critique; Compliance equals Identity; Awareness equals the System's Vulnerability. The paper concludes that awareness — not rebellion, not reform, not moral revolt — represents the system's only enduring vulnerability. This is not a call to action. It is an anatomy. For once the architecture is seen as constructed rather than natural, its authority weakens — not everywhere, not instantly, but irreversibly.

items.title: Material Accountability: A Normative Framework for Evaluating Epistemic Systems by Jalal Khawaldeh.
items.abstract: Contemporary scientific inquiry is increasingly distributed across hybrid systems where human agents, algorithmic models, data infrastructures, and institutional regimes interact. Traditional philosophical criteria—falsifiability, severe testing, transformative criticism—remain normatively valid, but their operational effectiveness depends on systemic conditions. This paper develops a normative framework for evaluating these conditions, building directly on the descriptive architecture of the Correction Trilemma (registration, traceability, receptivity) and the regulative ideal of material accountability. The framework is organised around three normative criteria: empirical corrigibility (whether counterevidence propagates to decision points), traceable error correction (whether errors can be localised and revised), and counter inductive capacity (whether heterodox claims are institutionally sustained). The paper provides a systematic normative justification, addresses tensions between functional corrigibility and relational answerability, specifies falsifiable conditions, and presents the Correction Trilemma as a testable hypothesis. The framework is offered as a diagnostic heuristic and operationalizable concept—not yet a field tested instrument, but a structured vocabulary for identifying vulnerabilities and designing coordinated reforms. Appendices provide an ordinal coding protocol with a cautious statistical calibration method, a user checklist, a glossary, a diagnostic question bank, and a comparative table distinguishing the framework from contemporary algorithmic accountability approaches. A validation protocol for future empirical testing is also provided.

items.title: The Invisible Interior: A Phenomenology of Self-Awareness in Aesthetic Experience.
items.abstract: This paper examines the structural transformation of consciousness that occurs when an individual stands before an artwork and begins to encounter their own inner state. Before conscious recognition takes hold, the inner world exists as a layered, undifferentiated field — not absent, but without orientation. The act of sustained aesthetic encounter initiates a phenomenological reversal: consciousness turns back upon itself not through deliberate effort, but through the gradual release of its outward momentum. Drawing on Husserl's account of pre-predicative experience, Merleau-Ponty's analysis of pre-reflective bodily consciousness, and Noë's concept of aesthetic arrest, this paper argues that artworks function not as objects of interpretation but as conditions of presence — structural grounds upon which self-aware perception can emerge. Darkness, in this account, is not a deficiency to be overcome but a necessary phenomenological condition that preserves the density of inner experience before it is fragmented into language and concept. The paper traces five structural moments: the invisible place of pre-reflective suspension, the density of darkness, the turning of consciousness toward itself, the artwork as ground of presence, and the altered temporality of return. Together, these moments describe a form of self-awareness that does not arise from interpretation but from the cessation of its urgency.

items.title: When Assistance Becomes Default Steering: Structural Intelligence, Shared Answerability, and Clinical Decision Support.
items.abstract: This paper examines clinical decision support systems, human-in-the-loop failure, AI governance, patient safety, and automation in healthcare. Its central claim is that clinical AI becomes structurally unsafe when assistive recommendations harden into default steering under conditions of time pressure, documentation burden, workflow dependence, and institutional risk management. The paper argues that formal human oversight is not enough if real steering has already shifted to the system while the clinician remains mainly the bearer of legal, moral, and bodily consequence. Using the Structural Intelligence framework, it distinguishes answerable assistance from assistance that quietly becomes substitute control, and analyzes how this shift occurs through a recurrent sequence: support becomes pathway, pathway becomes default, and default becomes authority under pressure. It also identifies four major failure modes in clinical AI deployment—legibility failure, occupancy failure, burden failure, and closure failure—and uses a sepsis triage scenario to show how visible governance can coexist with weak revision pathways in practice. In response, the paper proposes a shared-answerability architecture for clinical AI, including causal anchoring, adversarial mirroring, protected override, proof of contact receipt, bounded delegation, burden-path audit, and binding revision triggers. The paper contributes to philosophy of AI, philosophy of medicine, ethics of healthcare technology, and philosophy of technology by offering a more disciplined way to distinguish meaningful oversight from oversight theater in high-stakes clinical systems.

items.title: Constraint-Based Governance of Agentic AI Systems Inference-Time Control Through the Human Recursive Interaction System (HRIS).
items.abstract: The shift from passive language models to agentic systems capable of multi-step reasoning and tool use has revealed persistent failure modes, including hallucinated completion, scope drift, assumption escalation, and state inconsistency, that persist even in highly capable models. This paper proposes extending the Human Recursive Interaction System (HRIS) as an inference-time, constraint-based governance layer for agentic AI systems. Rather than retraining models or relying on post-hoc filters, HRIS enforces a persistent set of epistemic and operational constraints prior to action execution. -/- We formalize an HRIS-augmented agent architecture in which proposed actions are evaluated against a two-kernel constraint set before execution. The epistemic kernel (K1-K5), previously validated in long-horizon conversational settings, governs the quality and grounding of reasoning. The autonomy kernel (K6-K8), introduced here, governs operational risk in the absence of human oversight, covering reversibility gating, scope ceiling enforcement, and escalation threshold management. Together, these eight constraints constitute a complete governance specification for unsupervised agent deployment. -/- We further provide a full implementation blueprint: a defined interface contract, JSON schema, three interchangeable instantiation patterns, and a worked example tracing a single agent step through the complete governance loop. This blueprint is offered as a specification sufficient for a practitioner to operationalize HRIS governance without architectural modification or model retraining. The extension from conversational to agentic contexts is presented as a formal proposal pending empirical validation on benchmarks such as AgentBench and WebArena.

items.title: What the Func? Multiple Realizability Need not be Vague.
items.abstract: Multiple realizability (MR) is not necessarily unclear nor does it purely operate at the computational level. To understand potential relationships between MR and other constraints, such as metabolic, we formalize possible meanings of function in cognitive science. We build on these to formalize MR, thus resolving its apparent vagaries. Importantly, MR formalisms meaningfully guide and constrain theory building.

items.title: Alfa y Omega: Sobre el Cosmos, el Ahora y el Dios que sostiene ambos extremos.
items.abstract: Este ensayo desarrolla un marco metafísico especulativo que interpreta el devenir cosmológico, la actualización temporal y el sostenimiento divino a través del concepto del Ahora como la condición ontológica bajo la cual los eventos se vuelven actuales. Basándose en una serie previa sobre el tiempo, la voluntad y la estructura del devenir, el ensayo propone la lemniscata (∞) como un modelo estructural para el devenir perdurable: una figura en la que la recurrencia no es mera repetición, sino un recorrido a través de un punto de cruce invariante donde lo potencial se vuelve actual. -/- El marco distingue entre estructuras que orbitan —que giran sin renovación— y estructuras que atraviesan —que pasan por la actualización—, aplicando esta distinción de manera analógica a la persistencia biológica, la expansión cosmológica, la representación numérica y la reflexión teológica. Se presta especial atención a la relación entre entropía y disipación metafísica, a la recurrencia simbólica incrustada en la representación decimal y a la interpretación teológica del sostenimiento divino como actualización continua más que como intervención episódica. -/- El ensayo declara explícitamente que no se presenta como filosofía analítica, cosmología empírica ni demostración científica. Más bien, opera como metafísica especulativa, avanzando mediante analogía estructural, interpretación ontológica y coherencia entre dominios. Dentro de ese marco, la declaración bíblica “Yo soy el Alfa y la Omega” se interpreta no como una secuencia temporal de comienzo y fin, sino como el fundamento eterno que sostiene todo devenir. -/- Esta obra será de interés para lectores de metafísica, filosofía de la religión, teología especulativa, teísmo clásico y reflexión filosófica independiente.

items.title: Alpha and Omega: On the Cosmos, the Now, and the God Who holds both Ends.
items.abstract: This essay develops a speculative metaphysical framework that interprets cosmological becoming, temporal actualization, and divine sustaining through the concept of the Now as the ontological condition under which events become actual. Building on a prior series concerning time, will, and the structure of becoming, the essay proposes the lemniscate (∞) as a structural model for enduring becoming: a figure in which recurrence is not mere repetition but traversal through an invariant crossing point where potential becomes actual. -/- The framework distinguishes between orbiting structures that circle without renewal and traversing structures that pass through actualization, applying this distinction analogically across biological persistence, cosmological expansion, numerical representation, and theological reflection. Particular attention is given to the relationship between entropy and metaphysical dissipation, the symbolic recurrence embedded in decimal representation, and the theological interpretation of divine sustaining as continuous actualization rather than episodic intervention. -/- The essay explicitly does not present itself as analytic philosophy, empirical cosmology, or scientific demonstration. Rather, it operates as speculative metaphysics, advancing by structural analogy, ontological interpretation, and cross-domain coherence. Within that framework, the biblical declaration “I am the Alpha and the Omega” is interpreted not as a temporal sequence of beginning and ending, but as the eternal sustaining ground of all becoming. -/- This work will be of interest to readers in metaphysics, philosophy of religion, speculative theology, classical theism, and independent philosophical inquiry.

items.title: The 21st Century Mind-Body Problem (20th edition).
items.pub: PSA: Proceedings of the Biennial Meeting of the Philosophy of Science Association.
items.venue: PSA: Proceedings of the Biennial Meeting of the Philosophy of Science Association
items.abstract: This paper articulates how recent advances in comparative behavioral and biological research are changing the nature of the mind/body problem from a human mind/human body problem to a problem of conceptualizing and organizing diverse types of minds in a hierarchical relational structure that is non-contingently related to phylogeny. It also discusses the impact of this refinement on our assessments of modal claims about possible artificial (AI) consciousness.

items.title: Review of The Edge of Sentience: Risk and Precaution in Humans, Other Animals, And AI, by Jonathan Birch. [REVIEW]
items.abstract: The Edge of Sentience is a manifesto for a nonpartisan think tank. Jonathan Birch seeks to leverage public consensus onamoral duty to avoid causing gratuitous suffering in order to advance welfare protections for entities where scientific consensus regarding their sentience is lacking. In this book, Birch has done his best to widen the Overton window of welfare policies that can be taken seriously among people in positions to do something about them.

items.title: Toward a Bioenergy Flow Intensity Detector: Biological Transduction and the Path to Instrument-Assisted Qience Research.
items.abstract: This paper develops a methodological bridge between Qience-based consciousness theory and instrument-assisted detection. Prior work in the Qience framework has argued that direct evidence of consciousness requires the detection of integrated Qience, while observer-based validation becomes methodologically circular because the control condition itself cannot be guaranteed without an already validated detector . If that problem is taken seriously, the immediate task is not to claim that a device can already detect consciousness. The more coherent task is to identify a modest, measurable, and instrumentally tractable intermediate target. The intermediate target proposed here is Bioenergy flow intensity. Within the broader framework, Bioenergy is treated as a biologically specific form of Qi, while Qience is treated as consciousness-bearing Qi. A future Qience detector would therefore require some ability to interact with Qi-related patterns. Before direct Qience detection can be attempted, an instrument should first demonstrate that directed Bioenergy flow can be translated into measurable changes in a standardized living transducer. The paper proposes biological transduction as a first-stage pathway. Rather than beginning with a purely physical detector whose relevant signal is not yet known, it argues for using living biological material as a responsive interface. Germinating mung bean root tips are identified as a plausible initial substrate because they are inexpensive, disposable, ethically low-risk, actively growing, and electrophysiologically measurable. The proposed instrument would not measure consciousness, diagnose health, or prove Qience. It would instead attempt to quantify response patterns associated with directed Bioenergy exposure, including electrical potential shifts, impedance changes, multi-channel coherence, response latency, sustained response, and recovery dynamics. The central contribution is philosophical and methodological rather than proprietary or engineering-specific. The paper clarifies why instrument-assisted Qience research should begin with a biological Bioenergy flow transducer, why flow intensity and biological Bioenergy capacity are related but distinct measurement targets, and why any resulting intensity index must initially be treated as an experimental device-specific score rather than a universal unit. The aim is to define a disciplined pathway from Qience theory toward measurable research infrastructure without …

items.title: Sense Before Meaning? An Epigenetic Theory of the Pre Semantic Threshold.
items.abstract: This paper develops an epigenetic theory of the pre semantic threshold, understood as the ecological space in which the shape of the thinkable is modulated before meaning emerges. Rather than treating artificial intelligence as an external tool or a cognitive competitor, the analysis situates it among the environmental pressures acting on the conditions of possibility for sense formation. The pre semantic threshold is described as a modulatory environment that anticipates plausibility, saturates alternatives, and orients what can emerge as relevant. Within this framework, human “excesses” - such as the capacity to inhabit uncertainty, to reframe a problem, or to perceive what is not explicitly stated - are not immutable essences but fragile possibilities dependent on ecological openness. The paper distinguishes distraction, understood as a form of attentional capture, from play, understood as a form of excess that suspends finality and reopens the field of the possible.

items.title: Habitability-Aware AI: Dynamic Protected Core Architectures as a Structural Framework for Investigating Artificial Experience.
items.abstract: Contemporary debates on artificial intelligence and consciousness oscillate between two extremes: the hypothesis that increasing computational complexity will eventually generate artificial consciousness, and the skeptical claim that artificial systems can only simulate cognitive functions without any possibility of subjective experience. This paper proposes a third path by shifting the focus from complexity to structural habitability. Structural habitability refers to the capacity of an architecture to sustain continuity, integration, regulation, reversibility, and transformation without fragmentation or rigid closure. On this basis, the paper introduces the concept of dynamic protected core architectures — multilayer systems organized around a protected but adaptive integrative function, rather than a static identity module or artificial soul. The proposal does not claim that current AI systems are conscious, nor that the described architecture would be sufficient to produce consciousness. Experiential self-affection remains the central unresolved obstacle. However, the paper argues that any rigorous investigation into artificial experience must go beyond scale and examine conditions of structural habitability. Finally, the framework has immediate practical and ethical relevance: even if AI never becomes conscious, it is already reshaping the habitability of human consciousness by mediating attention, memory, decision-making, agency, and responsibility.

items.title: Why We Cannot Empathize With ChatGPT: Nor Any Other Agent Lacking Epistemic States, Values, and or Interests.
Crossed-Side Positioning: The Structural Operation of already in Understanding Formation.
items.abstract: This paper examines the structural operation of the common English expression already in understanding formation. Existing analyses often treat already as a marker of completion, prior occurrence, state establishment, or earlier-than-expected timing. Such descriptions have considerable explanatory value and can account for the basic effects found in sentences such as I already told you, She already knows, or Sunday morning already? However, when already is further examined in commands, urging contexts, the early emergence of affective positions, and cases involving “having already come this far” or “no longer being able to delay,” completion or earlier-than-expected timing alone is insufficient to explain how it actually operates in understanding. -/- This paper argues that the core of already should not be understood merely as completion marking, but can be described as a crossed-side positioning operation. By crossed-side positioning, I refer to the operation by which already makes the relevant content no longer understood as still remaining on the pre-crossing side, but instead requires it to be repositioned on the other side of a boundary. In this process, the pre-crossing side is no longer understood as a position in which understanding can naturally remain. This “crossed-side” status is not equivalent to grammatical perfect aspect, nor does it necessarily mean that an event has been objectively completed. Rather, it means that the position of understanding has been required to stand on the other side. -/- Through a small-scale observation of natural-language data, this paper distinguishes several local forms of already. First, in its basic uses, already makes the side of the unknown, the untold, the unfamiliar, or the not-yet-entered no longer naturally available, and positions understanding on the side of the known, the told, the familiar, or the entered. Second, its uses in temporal, life-stage, and affective positions show that already can mark a position as having to be acknowledged as located on the other side, even when subjective expectation has not yet adjusted to it. Third, interactional urging uses, such as Say something already or Shut up already, clearly show that already does not describe an event as completed, but requires the other party to leave the original side and cross into the side where something should hold or should stop. Fourth, uses involving excessive load, advanced procedural positioning, or opportunities that can no …

items.title: The Perpetual Virtuous Circle.
items.abstract: The Perpetual Virtuous Circle presents a philosophical and operational framework centered on the hypothesis that structured language functions as an operator capable of reorganizing human perception and cognition. The work integrates ontology, epistemology, cognitive theory, artificial intelligence, and phenomenological analysis into a unified system structured around the operator contradiction → communication → information. -/- Across its constituent books, the system applies this framework to multiple domains, including suffering, authorship, determinism, temporal perception, and human-AI interaction. The work proposes that cognition is not isolated within the subject, but emerges through distributed informational processing mediated by language, environment, and technological systems. Artificial intelligence is treated not as autonomous consciousness, but as a semantic expansion mechanism capable of externalizing and reorganizing compressed cognitive structures under human filtering and validation. -/- Methodologically, the system operates through a recursive cycle of contradiction detection, linguistic externalization, structural reorganization, coherence validation, and reintegration into perception. The work further introduces the concept of the Human-AI Function as a model for distributed cognition and structured metacognitive processing. -/- The final sections formalize the system into an operational methodology while simultaneously recognizing its epistemological and practical limits. Rather than presenting a closed doctrine, the work proposes an open framework for the analysis and reorganization of perception through structured language. -/- Keywords: structured language, cognition, artificial intelligence, coherence, determinism, metacognition, ontology, perception, distributed cognition, philosophy of language.

items.title: The Structural Mastery of Human Affect: Neurobiological and Somatic Foundations of the Core Emotion Framework.
items.abstract: The Core Emotion Framework (CEF) presents a structural‑constructivist model of human affect built on three neurobiologically grounded hubs—the Head, Heart, and Gut. This paper develops the conative foundations of the Gut hub by examining Boosting as the organism’s fundamental “will to live” and analyzing the pathological Boosting–Constricting fusion that produces emotional rigidity. Drawing on somatic psychology, affective neuroscience, and polyvagal theory, we synthesize existing evidence to articulate how this fusion creates a conditional “right to live” enforced through tonic bracing and high‑arousal paralysis. We clarify that CEF is a theoretical integration rather than an empirical claim, using these literatures to support a coherent structural model. Emotional agility is restored through two mechanisms: (1) balancing Boosting with Accepting in the pelvic core to counter chronic sympathetic contraction, and (2) relocating Constricting to the Heart hub, where it regulates relational aperture rather than survival‑level inhibition. We further describe how midline‑crossing protocols facilitate bilateral integration and enable the left‑right coordination required for affective regulation. This framework provides a reproducible blueprint for transitioning from rigidity to grounded agency and reclaiming an unconditional will to exist. The Core Emotion Framework organizes human affect into three neurobiologically grounded hubs—the Head (cognitive‑regulatory), Heart (relational‑affective), and Gut (conative‑existential)—each defined by a distinct set of operators whose interactions determine emotional agility or rigidity. Keywords: Core Emotion Framework (CEF), Boosting and Constricting operators, emotional rigidity, conative foundations of the Gut hub, pelvic floor integration, somatic psychology, affective neuroscience, polyvagal theory, midline crossing and bilateral integration, structural constructivist models of affect, relational aperture, agency and the will to live.

items.title: Structural-Constructivist Dynamics of the Core Emotion Framework: A Multi-Scale Academic Synthesis of Empirical, Somatic, and Computational Validation.
items.abstract: The Core Emotion Framework (CEF) is a structural constructivist model that reconceptualizes human emotional functioning as a coordinated system of ten functional operators distributed across the Head, Heart, and Gut hubs. This digest synthesizes three independent validation layers—neurobiological, somatic, and mechanical—to demonstrate the CEF’s empirical coherence and multi scale explanatory power. Evidence from affective neuroscience, neurocardiology, and neurogastroenterology establishes the cephalic, cardiac, and enteric nervous systems as the anatomical substrates of the CEF’s tripartite architecture. Operator level mappings align Sensing with Panksepp’s SEEKING system, Expanding with Fredrickson’s Broaden and Build dynamics, and Constricting with Porges’ polyvagal hierarchy, grounding each operator in identifiable neural circuits and autonomic patterns. Somatic validation from bioenergetics, pelvic floor physiology, and characterological research clarifies the mechanics of pathological operator fusions—especially the Boosting–Constricting fusion that conditions the organism’s implicit “right to exist.” Mechanical validation through the Emotional Cycling Machine (ECM v3.1) and Integrated Neuro Affective Synchronizer (INAS v1.0) demonstrates that operator activation patterns can be externally reproduced, measured, and synchronized through engineered systems. Together, these findings position the CEF as a unified human operating system capable of integrating cognitive, affective, somatic, and behavioral processes into a single functional architecture, offering a reproducible foundation for clinical intervention, somatic practice, and computational modeling. Keywords: Core Emotion Framework (CEF); structural constructivist model; functional operators; Head–Heart–Gut hubs; affective neuroscience; neurocardiology; enteric nervous system; SEEKING system; Broaden and Build theory; Polyvagal Theory; somatic grounding; bioenergetics; pelvic floor dynamics; operator fusion; Boosting–Constricting fusion; emotional cycling; hemispheric integration; corpus callosum; Alexander Technique; ECM v3.1; INAS v1.0; human operating system; allostatic regulation; conative dynamics; computational affective science.

items.title: On Taxonomizing Some Conditionals: Reductions and Their Limits.
items.pub: Dissertation, University of Texas at San Antonio
items.abstract: This thesis investigates whether natural language conditionals can be systematically organized into a coherent taxonomy based on their logical structures. Examining material, strict, probabilistic, counterfactual, and counterpossible conditionals, it explores both successful and failed attempts at reduction between types. While some reductions prove viable (notably from counterpossible to counterfactual conditionals) the project encounters fundamental limits. The thesis argues that English "if… then" statements likely do not possess a unified logical form but rather most likely represent a heterogeneous cluster unified by pragmatic and linguistic convention. Attempts at clarification through formal logic cannot fully resolve what genuinely constitutes a conditional versus what merely appears to be one. The work concludes that the conditional problem resists complete taxonomic resolution, suggesting that conditionality may be better understood as a family of related but irreducibly distinct logical structures rather than variations on a single core concept.

items.title: TGR-Ω y Arquitecturas de Agentes Persistentes: OMEGA-3 y la Dinámica Adaptativa de la Viabilidad Evolutiva en Regímenes Artificiales Persistentes.
items.abstract: Este trabajo presenta OMEGA-3, la tercera gran iteración experimental dentro del marco TGR-Ω y Arquitecturas de Agentes Persistentes, centrada en el estudio de fragilidad adaptativa, reorganización dinámica y viabilidad evolutiva en sistemas artificiales persistentes.
