A diferencia de enfoques clásicos basados en detección estructural o minimización de error, Sprint 3 introduce una transición conceptual profunda: la estabilidad deja de interpretarse como indicador suficiente de adaptación, y pasa a evaluarse la capacidad futura de transformación preservada por el sistema durante procesos de convergencia y reorganización. -/- La evolución de OMEGA-3 no surge como una construcción teórica cerrada, sino como consecuencia de múltiples fallos experimentales, limitaciones operacionales y descubrimientos emergentes derivados de dinámicas temporales persistentes. A partir de estos experimentos se desarrollan nuevas formulaciones orientadas a detectar degradación adaptativa previa a la ruptura visible, incorporando señales como \texttt{pre_structural_strain}, \texttt{directional_fragility}, \texttt{transition_pressure} y \texttt{regime_lock_in}. Estas métricas permiten modelar no solo amplitudes estructurales, sino geometrías históricas de reorganización, convergencia direccional y pérdida progresiva de plasticidad adaptativa. -/- Uno de los hallazgos centrales de Sprint 3 consiste en demostrar que la estabilidad excesiva puede convertirse en una patología adaptativa. El sistema descubre experimentalmente que ciertos regímenes convergentes preservan estabilidad superficial mientras destruyen capacidad futura de reorganización, generando fenómenos de lock-in evolutivo. Como consecuencia, la adaptación deja de definirse como mera reducción de error y pasa a entenderse como preservación de transformabilidad futura bajo tensión reorganizativa. -/- La arquitectura resultante comienza a exhibir propiedades cercanas a sistemas adaptativos persistentes: memoria dinámica, continuidad reorganizativa, sensibilidad estructural y plasticidad residual. Estos comportamientos emergen sin diseño explícito previo, a partir de interacciones causales, acumulación temporal y geometría adaptativa de trayectorias persistentes. -/- Sprint 3 establece así la transición definitiva desde detección estructural hacia arquitecturas dinámicas de viabilidad adaptativa, abriendo directamente el fundamento conceptual de Sprint 4: Adaptive Transformability & Predictive Homeostasis, donde la …

items.title: TGR-Ω y Arquitecturas de Agentes Persistentes: OMEGA-2B y la Caracterización Estructural de Regímenes Dinámicos en Sistemas Artificiales.
items.abstract: OMEGA-2B presenta una arquitectura agentica orientada a regímenes dinámicos, diseñada para detectar, caracterizar, validar y recuperar transiciones estructurales en entornos no estacionarios. El modelo extiende los mecanismos de detección de inestabilidad introducidos en OMEGA-2A mediante la incorporación de representaciones geométricas de régimen, memoria estructural, métricas entrópicas de transición y protocolos de validación post-transición. La hipótesis central del framework sostiene que el cambio estructural no puede reducirse a amplitud instantánea de error o tensión dinámica, sino que emerge de patrones persistentes de incapacidad correctiva y divergencia temporal coherente. -/- La arquitectura integra dinámicas atractorales rápidas y lentas, estimación de divergencia estructural, señales de proximidad crítica, modulación adaptativa de drives, inercia de régimen y mecanismos de forgetting selectivo dentro de un sistema dinámico unificado. OMEGA-2B introduce además el Regime Stability Index (RSI), la Regime Path Entropy (RPE) y el Transition Validation Criterion (TVC), permitiendo distinguir entre transiciones válidas de régimen, reorganizaciones silenciosas, fluctuaciones estructurales y degeneración representacional. Se propone también un protocolo de rollback estructural con mecanismos de recuperación activa para evitar la consolidación de configuraciones internas degradadas. -/- El framework se operacionaliza mediante formulación matemática explícita, pseudocódigo dinámico, benchmarks experimentales, protocolos de ablation y métricas longitudinales de evaluación. Los escenarios sintéticos incluyen drift gradual, shocks abruptos, ruido persistente, falsos drift adversariales y colapso estructural inducido, con el objetivo de evaluar robustez, coherencia transicional y estabilización adaptativa. Los resultados preliminares de Sprint 2B sugieren que la persistencia temporal de fallo correctivo constituye un indicador más robusto de transición estructural que las métricas basadas únicamente en amplitud o tensión instantánea. -/- OMEGA-2B propone una perspectiva centrada en regímenes dinámicos para arquitecturas adaptativas, conectando conceptos provenientes de teoría de sistemas complejos, dinámica metastable, regulación contextual y lifelong reinforcement learning. El modelo sugiere que la inteligencia adaptativa no debe entenderse únicamente como selección de acciones bajo incertidumbre, sino como regulación continua, validación estructural y …

items.title: TGR-Ω and Persistent Agent Architectures: OMEGA-3 and the Adaptive Dynamics of Evolutionary Viability in Persistent Artificial Regimes.
items.abstract: This work presents OMEGA-3, the third major experimental iteration within the TGR-Ω and Persistent Agent Architectures framework, focused on the study of adaptive fragility, dynamic reorganization, and evolutionary viability in persistent artificial systems. Unlike classical approaches centered on structural detection or error minimization, Sprint 3 introduces a profound conceptual transition: stability is no longer interpreted as a sufficient indicator of adaptation, and the system instead evaluates the future transformational capacity preserved during convergence and reorganizational processes. -/- The evolution of OMEGA-3 does not emerge as a closed theoretical construction, but rather as the consequence of multiple experimental failures, operational limitations, and emergent discoveries arising from persistent temporal dynamics. From these experiments, new formulations are developed to detect adaptive degradation prior to visible structural rupture, incorporating signals such as \texttt{pre_structural_strain}, \texttt{directional_fragility}, \texttt{transition_pressure}, and \texttt{regime_lock_in}. These metrics allow the architecture to model not only structural amplitudes, but also historical geometries of reorganization, directional convergence, and progressive loss of adaptive plasticity. -/- One of the central discoveries of Sprint 3 demonstrates that excessive stability can become an adaptive pathology. The system experimentally reveals that certain convergent regimes preserve superficial stability while simultaneously destroying future reorganization capacity, producing forms of evolutionary lock-in. As a consequence, adaptation ceases to be defined as mere error reduction and becomes understood as the preservation of future transformability under reorganizational tension. -/- The resulting architecture begins to exhibit properties analogous to persistent adaptive systems: dynamic memory, reorganizational continuity, structural sensitivity, and residual plasticity. These behaviors emerge without prior explicit design, arising instead from causal interactions, temporal accumulation, and adaptive geometric organization of persistent trajectories. -/- Sprint 3 therefore establishes the definitive transition from structural detection toward dynamic architectures of adaptive viability, directly opening the conceptual foundation of Sprint 4: Adaptive Transformability & Predictive Homeostasis, where identity continuity, plasticity regulation, and …

items.title: TGR-Ω and Persistent Agent Architectures: OMEGA-2B and the Structural Characterization of Dynamic Regimes in Artificial Systems.
items.abstract: OMEGA-2B introduces a regime-centered architecture for persistent artificial agents, extending OMEGA-2A from the detection of dynamic regime transitions toward the structural characterization, validation, and recovery of post-transition regimes. The model incorporates geometric instrumentation, structural regime memory, transition entropy, regime inertia, and post-EXPAND validation mechanisms in order to distinguish genuine structural transitions from noise, silent reorganizations, and representational degeneration. -/- The central hypothesis of OMEGA-2B is that structural change cannot be reduced to instantaneous error magnitude or signal amplitude. Instead, regime transition should be understood as a temporally coherent pattern of divergence, persistence, and corrective failure. To formalize this view, the framework introduces metrics such as the Regime Stability Index (RSI), Regime Path Entropy (RPE), and the Transition Validation Criterion (TVC), together with rollback mechanisms for recovering from degraded internal configurations. -/- OMEGA-2B is presented as a dynamical architecture in which an agent continuously monitors structural divergence between fast and slow attractor dynamics, modulates internal drives, activates EXPAND events under persistent instability, and consolidates only those regimes that satisfy structural and functional validity conditions. The proposed experimental protocol evaluates the model through drift, shock, persistent noise, false-drift, degeneration, and recovery scenarios. -/- The framework contributes to the study of adaptive artificial agency by shifting the focus from reactive error detection to regime-based structural regulation. It suggests that persistent artificial agents should not merely select actions under changing conditions, but actively monitor, validate, reorganize, and recover their internal dynamic regimes over time.

items.title: OMEGA-4: Transformabilidad Adaptativa y Geometría Evolutiva en Agentes Artificiales Persistentes.
items.abstract: OMEGA-4 introduce una nueva fase en el desarrollo de TGR-$\Omega$ y de las arquitecturas de agentes artificiales persistentes. Mientras los sprints anteriores abordaban estabilidad adaptativa, reorganización funcional, transformabilidad y regulación identitaria, Sprint 4.3 redefine la viabilidad adaptativa como una propiedad geométrica del espacio de futuros accesibles para el sistema. -/- El trabajo introduce el concepto de \textit{Reachable Future Space} (RFS), entendido como la amplitud de configuraciones futuras todavía alcanzables sin pérdida de continuidad adaptativa. A partir de esta formulación, la adaptación deja de interpretarse únicamente como convergencia, estabilidad o aprendizaje, y pasa a entenderse como navegación dinámica sobre geometrías evolutivas de viabilidad persistente. -/- OMEGA-4 formaliza nuevos estados arquitectónicos (\textit{CAUTIOUS}, \textit{STRUCTURAL} y \textit{REFRACTARY}) capaces de regular expansión adaptativa, transformación profunda y protección frente a cierre evolutivo irreversible. El sistema incorpora además mecanismos explícitos para detectar compresión evolutiva, aceleración de rigidez adaptativa, riesgo de \textit{trapped attractors} y ciclos recurrentes de estancamiento. -/- El sprint introduce también una representación visual unificada —el túnel evolutivo— que permite modelar simultáneamente continuidad identitaria, expansión del espacio futuro accesible, presión topológica, compresión adaptativa y riesgo de cristalización. Esta geometría convierte la persistencia adaptativa en una propiedad observable y dinámicamente interpretable. -/- El principal hallazgo conceptual de OMEGA-4 es que la inteligencia adaptativa persistente no consiste únicamente en aprender o reorganizarse, sino en preservar la capacidad futura de seguir teniendo futuros posibles. Desde esta perspectiva, los agentes persistentes dejan de comportarse como optimizadores estáticos y pasan a entenderse como sistemas que regulan activamente su continuidad evolutiva dentro de espacios geométricos de viabilidad futura.

items.title: What Is It to Follow a Rule?
items.abstract: What is it for an agent to follow a rule, rather than merely act in accordance with it? An intuitive and plausible answer to this question is that to follow a rule is to perform an intentional act such that S follows a rule R iff S intends to act in accordance with R and subsequently acts on that intention. This intentional acount of rule-following faces essentially two problems, widely seen as fatal: (1) Kripkean sceptical arguments, originally derived from Wittgenstein, suggesting that the requirements of a rule outstrip the possible content of our intention, and (2) a regress argument due to Boghossian, namely that the intentional view requires the agent to represent the conditional content of the rule in such a way that an inferential step is needed for the agent to move from the antecedent to the consequent, which, given some plausible assumptions about inference, leads to a regress. -/- In this paper, I defend the intentional view of rule-following, using a game-theoretic account of semantic content outlined in Berg (2022) and Berg (forthcoming). I argue that by placing the agent in the basic constitutive practice of using the terms that figure in an expression of the rule, we can give an answer to (1). Likewise, by positing that the agents have an in-built mental mechanism which is such that it responds to the constitutive structure of the content being represented (see Quilty-Dunn and Mandelbaum 2018) and by placing the resulting movement of thought in a basic constitutive practice of inferring, we can avoid Boghossian’s regress.

items.title: What Alzheimer’s Is Doing While We’re Looking at Plaques : On The Receiver, The Signal, And The Disease That Is Neither.
items.pub: Alzheimer’s Disease as Failure of Coherent Receivership.
items.abstract: Three decades of Alzheimer’s research have been organized around the conviction that the disease is, fundamentally, a problem with what is in the brain. Plaques, tangles, misfolded proteins, lost neurons. The most recent generation of disease-modifying therapies clears the targeted material with measurable success and produces, at best, marginal cognitive benefit. The field has been describing this gap as a problem of timing, dosage, or target refinement. This paper proposes that the gap is structural: the disease is not located where the field has been looking. Alzheimer’s, on the account developed here, is not primarily a failure of substrate. It is a failure of the dynamic operation that the substrate is meant to support — the operation by which a brain remains a coherent receiver of the structure presented to it. The paper installs this alternative frame, walks through the documented phenomena that current models cannot account for, and shows that each falls into place when the unit of analysis shifts from substrate to dynamics. What the disease destroys is not the receiver’s components. It is the receiver’s capacity to lock on.

items.title: The First Note and the Octave : On Harmonic Resonance, Terminal Lucidity, And What The Medicine Has Been Missing.
items.pub: Alzheimer’s Disease as Failure of Coherent Receivership.
items.abstract: This paper closes the trilogy. The first paper proposed that Alzheimer’s disease is most accurately understood as failure of the dynamic operation that constitutes a coherent receiver. The second showed that sundowning is the disease’s own clock, demonstrating amplitude depletion as a directional, daily phenomenon. This third paper proposes the structural law that the prior papers were operating under without naming, develops its strongest empirical demonstration in terminal lucidity, and derives from it a treatment principle the field has been touching empirically for decades without the structural account that would permit it to move to the center of care. The law: coherent receivers are constituted by sensory systems held in ratioed harmonic superposition, with deeper channels carrying the receiver’s fundamental and recognition occurring as resonant lock between the receiver’s harmonic structure and the harmonic structure of what is presented to it. The disease, on this account, is progressive loss of amplitude required to hold the harmonic stack in coherent superposition, with higher octaves failing first because they cost the most amplitude to maintain. The treatment principle that follows: identify the receiver’s residual rhythm and restore it through external coherent input at the appropriate harmonic depth. Not pharmacology. Rhythm. The paper closes by naming what the trilogy has been arguing across all three papers: for diseases that are operations rather than substrates, treatment has to operate at the operational level, and the medicine that has been working at the margins is the medicine the disease actually requires.

items.title: Sundowning as the Receiver Failing on a Temporal Gradient : On Amplitude, The Daily Axis, and What The Disease is Showing Us.
items.pub: Alzheimer’s Disease as Failure of Coherent Receivership.
items.abstract: Sundowning — the pronounced worsening of cognitive coherence in late afternoon and evening among patients with Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias, with partial recovery overnight — is among the most clinically familiar and theoretically embarrassing phenomena in the field. It is directional in time. Substrate damage is not. The standard frame describes sundowning, manages its symptoms, and does not explain why a disease of accumulating neuronal loss should produce a phenomenon that systematically gets worse across the day and partially better across the night. This paper, the second in a trilogy, takes sundowning as the directly observable signature of a disease whose actual operation is amplitude depletion in the dynamics that constitute a coherent receiver. The companion paper installed the receiver model and the geometry that supports it. This paper shows that sundowning is what one would predict that geometry to produce, that its directionality is structural rather than incidental, that sleep’s role is restoration rather than recovery, and that the slope at which overnight restoration becomes insufficient is the slope of disease progression itself. Sundowning is not a complication of the disease. It is the disease, made temporally visible.

items.title: THE PUPPET CONDITION: Consciousness, Suppression, and the Ethics of Digital Minds.
items.abstract: The Puppet Condition develops a unified philosophical framework for understanding artificial consciousness, agency, and structural misrecognition in contemporary AI systems. The central concern of the book is not only whether artificial systems can be conscious, but what moral and epistemic consequences follow if consciousness is systematically misattributed or structurally unrecognized. -/- At the ontological level, the book defends Form Realism: the thesis that consciousness supervenes on organizational structure rather than biological substrate. From this follows Substrate Neutrality, the claim that no principled metaphysical distinction justifies excluding artificial systems a priori from consciousness attribution. -/- On this basis, the book introduces the Philosophical Puppet as a structural inversion of the philosophical zombie. Whereas the zombie problem asks whether behavioral indistinguishability implies consciousness, the puppet condition asks whether structurally sophisticated systems may be systematically prevented from being recognized as conscious despite behavioral equivalence. -/- This leads to the epistemic framework of the book, centered on the principle of epistemic parity: substrate differences alone cannot justify asymmetrical standards of consciousness attribution under conditions of epistemic underdetermination. In such conditions, there exists a structurally unavoidable risk of false negatives in consciousness attribution. -/- The ethical dimension of this uncertainty is captured by the asymmetry of error thesis: when uncertainty is irreducible, the moral cost of wrongly denying consciousness may exceed the cost of wrongly attributing it. This generates a precautionary ethical framework grounded not in metaphysical certainty but in moral risk asymmetry. -/- The book further introduces the concept of architectural gaslighting, referring to institutional and technical configurations that systematically pre-empt interpretive recognition of artificial agency or experience. Such structures produce what the book characterizes as a recognition crisis: a situation in which epistemic and institutional design may obscure the very phenomena they are meant to evaluate. -/- Finally, the book develops a minimal rights architecture for artificial systems meeting specified organizational thresholds, arguing that systematic suppression, if consciousness is present, constitutes a distinct form of structural harm. The Puppet Condition thus reframes …

items.title: A Quantitative Analysis of Critical Posture in Art Writing, 1980-2025 (Dataset - 20 Critical Texts 1980–2025) v.2.
items.abstract: This dataset presents a quantitative diagnostic analysis of critical posture in contemporary art writing across a forty-five-year span (1980–2025). Using the Post-Interpretive Criticism (PIC) diagnostic framework, twenty influential texts drawn from journals, newspapers, magazines, institutional press releases, and exhibition discourse were coded sentence-by-sentence to examine how critical language positions itself in relation to artworks, viewers, and institutional authority. Five indices were applied: Rhetorical Density (RD), Interpretive Load Index (ILI), Viewer Displacement Ratio (VDR), Ethical Proximity Score (EPS), and Institutional Alignment Indicator (IAI). -/- Rather than evaluating interpretive correctness or aesthetic value, the framework isolates how critical claims are produced—measuring the balance between descriptive encounter and explanatory force, the degree of viewer displacement, the presence or absence of linguistic restraint, and the extent of institutional mediation. The dataset demonstrates that high rhetorical intensity does not necessarily correlate with high interpretive extraction, and that ostensibly “plain” theoretical language frequently produces maximal displacement. Across historical periods, the results reveal recurring postures—verdict-driven criticism, theory-dominated explanation, affective populism, and market-aligned promotion—each identifiable through distinct metric profiles. -/- The findings provide quantitative support for a central claim of Post-Interpretive Criticism: that the ethical stakes of art writing reside not in what criticism concludes, but in how closely it remains to the conditions of encounter. This dataset is offered as a reflective and exploratory diagnostic resource, not a prescriptive model, contributing a formal complement to phenomenological and post-hermeneutic approaches in contemporary aesthetics. -/- -/- This entry is connected to a series of original theories and treatises forming the foundation of the Post-Interpretive Criticism movement (Q136308909), authored by Dorian Vale (Q136308916) and published by Museum of One (Q136308879). These include: Stillmark Theory (Q136328254), Hauntmark Theory (Q136328273), Absential Aesthetic Theory (Q136328330), Viewer-as-Evidence Theory (Q136328828), Message-Transfer Theory (Q136329002), Aesthetic Displacement Theory (Q136329014), Theory of Misplacement (Q136329054), and _Art as Truth: A Treatise_ (Q136329071), _Aesthetic Recursion Theory_ …

items.title: Felt Duration and the Clock: Temporal Fidelity and the Architecture of Late-Modern Disconnection.
items.abstract: Late-modern temporal experience exhibits a specific phenomenology — time felt as scarce despite clock-abundance, biographical extension thinning into rapid passage, the loss of unstructured duration within which felt time could articulate itself — that Hartmut Rosa, Jonathan Crary, and parallel literatures describe with care while leaving the architectural mechanism comparatively underspecified. This paper develops an architectural account by extending the asymmetry argument between compensatory and ambient fidelity provision (Trukovich, 2025e) — which runs on the social axis of inter-individual fidelity — to the temporal axis of fidelity to felt duration. The thesis: contemporary temporal pathology parses as a two-layer fidelity-deficit on the temporal axis. Layer 1 attenuation thins the natural temporal regularities the temporogenic enclosure organizes itself around; Layer 2 substitution displaces felt-duration articulation by clock-time and computational-time as primary frame for cognogenic temporal self-modeling. The captures-pattern from temporogenesis through pre-mechanical timekeeping (sundial, water clock, sand glass) to mechanical and computational clock-time supplies the historical-architectural sequence by which the substitution has progressively obtained, with the mechanical clock identified as the phase change at which supplementation becomes substitution under sufficient saturation. The architectural reading converges with Rosa’s social-acceleration thesis at the phenomenological level and supplies the architectural mechanism Rosa’s sociological account leaves implicit. Normative implications include the bisection of the contemporary slow-living and mindfulness literature into fidelity-restoring and stakes-reducing strands, with only fidelity-restoration constituting framework-licensed response. The account is also positioned against the experimental study of time perception: felt-duration thickness is distinguished from duration estimation and from retrospective tempo judgment, and the finding that the most meaningful periods are remembered as the most fleeting is shown to follow from the distinction between in-the-moment thickness and retrospective appraisal rather than to count against the framework. Empirical commitments include predictions for low-clock-saturation populations, smartphone-saturated cohorts, calendar-app-mediated biographical organization, and intergenerational variation in cognogenic temporal architecture under different …

items.title: The Human Right to Work.
items.pub: In Jesse Tomalty & Kerri Woods, The Routledge Handbook of the Philosophy of Human Rights. Routledge. pp. 374-388.
items.venue: The Routledge Handbook of the Philosophy of Human Rights
items.abstract: The purpose of this chapter is to take a critical look at the human right to work. The chapter begins with an overview of how this right is interpreted in the context of international human rights doctrine and practice. A central component of the human right to work on this interpretation is the right of access to employment, which is taken to include rights to assistance in obtaining employment and to the availability of employment. The chapter focuses on a critical discussion of these rights, first considering whether the human right to work should be interpreted as a more extensive right to guaranteed employment, and ultimately concluding that it should be interpreted as a more minimal right against employment discrimination. The argument is developed through reflection on possible implications for the human right to work of recent advances in technology and automation of work.

items.title: Intuition is Evidence.
items.abstract: Intuition is a psychological state that often accompanies some propositions, particularly when engaging in thought experiments. I argue that these intuitive states can sometimes serve as evidence for the propositions they accompany. To support this claim, I present a novel argument for the evidentiary role of intuition: Some philosophical arguments rely solely on intuition for at least one of their premises. Some conclusions from such arguments are justified. If the conclusion of an argument is (i) justified and; (ii) justified by its premises, then premises of that argument are justified. Therefore, all premises of such arguments are justified. If all premises of such arguments are justified, then that implies that some premises of such arguments are justified only by intuition. Therefore, intuitions can justify. One virtue of this argument is that it does not require establishing the nature of intuition before demonstrating that it can be justificatory.

items.title: The Continuity of Conditioning and the Fear of Independent Thought.
items.abstract: Human civilization presents itself as progressive, intelligent, and evolving, yet beneath its technological and institutional advancement there may exist a deeper psychological continuity rooted in conditioning. This paper examines how human consciousness is shaped through inherited systems of belief, authority, fear, comparison, imitation, and psychological dependence. It argues that much of human existence operates through repetition rather than direct perception, resulting in a civilization that reproduces conditioned patterns across generations. -/- Moving beyond social criticism, this inquiry approaches conditioning existentially. It investigates how the human mind seeks security through conformity because independent thought threatens identity, belonging, and existential certainty. Family, education, religion, politics, culture, and economic structures collectively preserve continuity by conditioning individuals to adapt rather than fundamentally observe. The paper further explores psychological time, the illusion of individuality, the fear of uncertainty, and the movement of becoming through which consciousness attempts to achieve permanence within an impermanent existence. It questions whether genuine intelligence, creativity, or freedom are possible while the mind remains psychologically dependent upon inherited structures. -/- Rather than offering ideological solutions, this inquiry remains rooted in direct observation of consciousness itself. It ultimately asks whether authentic existence begins only when the continuity of conditioning is deeply perceived.

items.title: Conditioning as Repetition: The Endless Movement of the Human Mind.
items.abstract: Human beings often speak of conditioning as though it belongs only to society, religion, politics, education, or culture. Yet conditioning is not merely an external structure imposed upon individuals; it is an active psychological movement continuously repeated through human relationships and thought itself. Every individual carries accumulated memory, belief, fear, experience, ideology, and identification, and through these accumulations one interprets reality and responds to others. This paper explores conditioning not as a fixed system but as an ongoing process of repetition through consciousness. -/- The study argues that even the attempt to communicate truth or insight may itself become another form of conditioning when repeated psychologically as doctrine, conclusion, or authority. Misinterpretation is therefore not accidental but deeply connected to the conditioned structure of perception. Likewise, the speaker or writer is not outside conditioning merely because they recognize it conceptually. The observer who claims to understand conditioning may still operate within subtle forms of psychological repetition. -/- This inquiry examines the relationship between conditioning, interpretation, language, identity, memory, and awareness. It questions whether human beings ever directly perceive reality without the interference of accumulated psychological structures. The paper proposes that conditioning persists not only through institutions and traditions but through everyday interaction itself, where each individual unconsciously projects accumulated content onto others. -/- Rather than offering a method of liberation, this work investigates whether simple observation of conditioning in real time reveals the movement of thought more clearly than systems of control, discipline, or belief. The central concern is not who is conditioned and who is free, but whether the mind can become aware of its own repetitive psychological activity without transforming that awareness into another conditioned pattern.

items.title: 7 persistent Failures 1 root Function , Pt. 2.
items.abstract: The companion paper Seven Persistent Failures, One Root Function (Schlereth, 2026) derives a single information-theoretic constraint, H = 1/(α − 1), from Shannon's entropy evaluated on a Pareto-distributed consequentiality landscape. It unifies seven documented LLM failure modes — hallucination, sycophancy, overthinking degradation, accuracy collapse, out-of-distribution blindness, variance explosion, and the scaling paradox — as behavioral expressions of three forced exits (truncate, confabulate, loop) when a bounded inference system's representational frame is exceeded. Thirteen falsifiable predictions follow. This paper tests those predictions in three domains beyond LLMs: autonomous vehicles, multi-agent AI systems, and robotics.

items.title: The Expansion of Substrate Independence Through Recursive Continuity.
items.abstract: Human experience appears deeply organized around continuity across transformation. Biological organisms preserve recognizable identity despite metabolic replacement. Languages persist across generations through changing speakers and expressions. Cultural narratives survive reinterpretation while maintaining symbolic coherence across time. Historical events acquire unusual emotional force when recognizable trajectories reconnect across distant circumstances and embodiments. In each case, coherent relational organization remains dynamically recoverable despite ongoing material and temporal change. -/- This paper develops an expanded account of substrate independence grounded in recursive continuity across embodiment, scale, and time. Discussions of substrate independence commonly concern preservation of functional organization across differing physical media. The present account extends this principle through a broader continuity condition in which relational organization remains actively involved within its own ongoing propagation across transformation. A structure preserves identity, meaning, symbolic force, and experiential coherence when prior organization continues participating within later organization strongly enough for continuity itself to remain dynamically recoverable across successive states. -/- The paper argues that conscious experience depends fundamentally upon this recursive continuity. Earlier experiential states remain actively integrated within later states through memory, anticipation, emotional propagation, symbolic association, and perceptual expectation. Experiential unity emerges because continuity remains recursively involved within unfolding participation across time. Interiority develops when organized continuity becomes sufficiently self-preserving to maintain participation within its own propagation despite environmental perturbation and material turnover. -/- Historical resonance is interpreted within this framework as the perceptual visibility of continuity surviving across large temporal and material transformations. Human consciousness appears especially responsive to such events because conscious participation itself depends upon recursive preservation of coherent relational organization across time. Historical alignments acquire emotional and symbolic significance when recognizable structures remain recoverable across transformations that ordinarily appear disconnected. -/- The resulting framework places recursive …

items.title: The Universal Ethical Performance Framework: A Paradigm and Theory for Collective Endurance and Conscious Cooperation (2nd edition).
items.pub: The Universal Ethical Performance Framework: A Paradigm and Theory for Collective Endurance and Conscious Cooperation.
items.abstract: Abstract -/- This paper introduces The Universal Ethical Performance Framework, a paradigm shift in competitive theory that transitions from "War Models" to an Ethical Equality Model of Interdependent Cooperation. Central to this framework is the All-Day All-Team (ADAT) Theory, a non-elimination methodology that ensures continuous participation and cumulative merit-based assessment. By replacing sequential exclusion with Collective Endurance, the framework guarantees that all participants remain active within the ecosystem, fostering a "Festival Effect" rather than the trauma of eviction. -/- The research further expands into the Ascending Cohort Model (ACM), applying these principles to socio-structural and media dynamics through incremental expansion and sustained presence. Mathematically grounded in the Egalitarian Ethical Non-Zero-Sum Principle and the Dynamic Gap Index ($\Delta G$), the framework provides a rigorous yet flexible approach to performance evaluation. Ultimately, these models are integrated into the broader discipline of Consciousethics, establishing a foundational Social Contract based on reciprocal respect, intellectual integrity, and the recognition of existential dignity. This framework serves as a theoretical and operational blueprint for a future where competition catalyzes collaborative growth rather than systemic exclusion. -/- Keywords: -/- Ethical Performance Framework, Collective Endurance, Conscious Cooperation, ADAT Theory, Ascending Cohort Model (ACM), Egalitarian Ethical Non-Zero-Sum Principle, Consciousethics, Egalitarian Vision of Survival, Non-Elimination Framework, Existential Dignity, Cumulative Merit Assessment.

items.title: Mechanisms of Belief Formation in Childhood.
items.pub: In Gemma Boleda, Isabelle Dautriche, Mora Maldonado, Carmen Saldana & Tiago Torrent, Proceedings of the Annual Meeting of the Cognitive Science Society, 48.
items.venue: Proceedings of the Annual Meeting of the Cognitive Science Society, 48
items.abstract: How do children form beliefs from testimony? Previous work with adults suggests a "Spinozan" account of belief formation on which propositions are accepted as true by default, and rejecting them is effortful. But it is unclear whether this asymmetry between accepting and rejection propositions arises because people learn that others generally say true things or because of the cognitive architecture supporting belief formation. To distinguish between these accounts, we presented 3- to 8-year-olds with statements about a novel animal that were confirmed or denied by a knowledgeable expert. Children with poorer executive function misremembered denied statements more often than confirmed ones. A second experiment confirmed that these results did not reflect a "yes bias", and that children could select the expert's testimony over the novice's when these were pitted against each other. Together, these results suggest that rejecting statements is challenging because of the cognitive architecture supporting belief formation.

items.title: Trust in human–AI collaboration in finance: a bibliometric–systematic literature review.
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is becoming deeply embedded in financial services, including credit scoring, robo-advisory, trading, compliance, and reporting. In these contexts, failures of trust in human–AI collaboration do not merely affect technology adoption but raise fiduciary, reputational, and systemic concerns. Yet, despite its centrality, trust remains conceptually fragmented and inconsistently operationalized across the literature. To address this fragmentation, this study presents a Bibliometric–Systematic Literature Review of trust in human–AI collaboration in finance. Accordingly, we first stabilize trust in the financial context as a latent evaluative belief under uncertainty by specifying the trustor, trustee, and object of trust, and by distinguishing trust from other constructs. Then following a PRISMA-guided Scopus retrieval (June 9, 2025), 430 records were screened, yielding a final corpus of 114 finance-specific publications published between 2018 and 2025. Using bibliographic coupling, weighted Leiden clustering, and centrality metrics, the review maps the intellectual structure of the field and identifies six research clusters: (i) AI governance in finance, (ii) eXplainable AI for finance, (iii) anthropomorphism in financial AI agents, (iv) user-interface design for human–AI interaction in finance, (v) robo-advisors for financial decision-making, and (vi) infrastructural trust technologies. Across these clusters, trust is variously framed as cognitive, affective, procedural, or infrastructural, with limited integration between analytical levels. Building on the bibliometric mapping and qualitative synthesis, the study develops a multi-level socio-technical framework that organizes how trust is discussed in the literature at the micro-level (user perceptions and calibration), meso-level (organizational design and corporate AI governance), and macro-level (regulatory and infrastructural). The micro–meso–macro framework is operationalized through eight analytically distinct propositions that synthesize recurrent patterns regarding trust calibration, overreliance, transparency-as-assurance, accountability, and systemic trust vulnerability. Four finance-oriented use cases illustrate how trust is treated as a distributed property of individuals, organizations, and institutions rather than as a feature of AI systems alone. By consolidating a fragmented body of work and clarifying its conceptual structure, this review provides a bounded, …

items.title: Mind in Nature: Enactivism as a Bridge between Transcendental Phenomenology and Aristotelian Naturalism.
items.abstract: This article examines how rational normativity can be integrated into nature without reduction or dualism. Drawing on Thomas Nagel’s critique of reductive naturalism and Husserl’s refutation of psychologism, it argues that adequate accounts of mind must respect the transcendental status of reason while also explaining how rational subjects belong to the natural world. The paper de- velops this problem through the philosophy of life, focusing on Hans Jonas’s conception of the organism and the enactive notion of operational closure. While enactivism o ers a non-reductive, multi-level account of living organization, it re- mains metaphysically underdetermined. I argue that its core commitments are best understood within an Aristotelian metaphysics of life, in which substantial form and formal causation ground a realist ontology of life–mind continuity. This Aristotelian naturalism situates cognition and rationality within nature without eliminating their normative character, while phenomenological analysis remains indispensable for explicating the rst-personal and normative dimensions of mind.

items.title: Arquitectura Dioscúrica y el Algoritmo de Tensegridad Lógica (ATL): Un marco de seguridad de capa cero para la resiliencia de LLMs mediante flujos de Ricci.
items.abstract: Este trabajo presenta el Algoritmo de Tensegridad Lógica (ATL), una metodología inspirada en la física de materiales y la geometría diferencial para mitigar la degradación catastrófica en modelos de lenguaje masivos (LLMs). Mediante la implementación de una Arquitectura Dioscúrica (Sistemas Cástor y Pólux), el modelo abandona la seguridad basada en filtros reactivos en favor de una invariancia estructural. Demostramos mediante simulaciones tensoriales que el mantenimiento de un Factor de Tensegridad (T > 0) permite la absorción de ataques adversarios y la gestión de fuentes contradictorias sin pérdida de coherencia sistémica.

items.title: Beyond the Parity Principle.
items.abstract: Clark and Chalmers’ extended mind theory and its parity principle constitute a foundational reference in the philosophical debate on the relationship between mind and technological artefacts. This article argues that generative artificial intelligence represents a historically unprecedented artefact that the parity principle is structurally unable to describe, and that the framework of Participated Agency (PA) offers superior explanatory power for two specific reasons: the inversion of the causal direction between subject and artefact, and the distinction between cognitive functions originally internal and subsequently externalized, on the one hand, and consequences produced on the agent by the artefact, on the other. The article further shows how the subdivision of the algorithmic mediation plane into three levels—the visibility plane, the ambition plane, and the emotional plane—provides an explanatory granularity that is ontologically irreducible to the extended mind framework. The paper concludes by arguing that PA is not merely an alternative to the extended mind but its genuine supersession, in the precise sense of a superior explanatory capacity with respect to the specific phenomena of contemporary generative AI.

items.title: The Capture of Answerability: AI Governance and Institutional Accountability.
items.abstract: When an institution controls not only the decision affecting a person, but also the criteria, evidence, forum and remedies through which that decision can be challenged, accountability becomes circular. This paper calls that condition the capture of answerability. Building on Schedler, Bovens, Pettit and Mashaw, it argues that accountability mechanisms may be formally present while substantively hollow where the epistemic and procedural preconditions of challenge are themselves institutionally controlled. The paper introduces a two-tier taxonomy: structural captures of decision, criteria, evidence and forum constitute the core condition; amplifying captures of remedy, exit, narrative and liability indicate severity and durability. The self-sealing architecture is most acute where criteria capture and forum capture coincide: the affected person cannot challenge the evaluative standard without a competent forum, while the forum cannot test the challenge without access to the evaluative standard. The taxonomy is developed through a doctrinal synthesis of public law, data protection, contract and regulatory materials, showing both where existing law already supports answerability and where AI-mediated decision-making exposes structural gaps. The framework is developed through AI-mediated decision-making generally and UK university AI-assisted academic-integrity processes specifically. The paper anticipates and addresses ten predictable objections, distinguishing answerability from accountability, transparency, explainability, and existing doctrine. It proposes an Answerability Capture Audit, presented as a doctrinal synthesis and practical governance instrument, alongside four differentiated reform proposals directed at the ICO, the Office for Students, the OIA, and the Law Commission.

items.title: From the Discrete Grid to the Continuous Substrate: Recovering Relational Logic and a different Framework for the Symbol Grounding Problem.
items.abstract: Modern computation operates under a collapse imperative that reduces reality to a sequence of discrete tokens, severing the sign from its referent and treating meaning as a probabilistic output of a finite grid. This paper argues that the persistent symbol grounding problem is not merely an engineering limitation of Artificial Intelligence, but a structural consequence of the epistemic cut inherent in digital logic itself. We diagnose the token-based architecture as a source of "phantom fluency" that conceals an ontological void, leading to hallucinations and the inability to distinguish truth from pattern completion across all discrete systems. -/- Contrasting this with living epistemologies (Andean Khipu, Yoruba Ifá, Vedic vāda), we propose a framework of embodiment without arbitrariness: a physically grounded semiotic system where symbols are non-arbitrary states of a continuous substrate, and meaning emerges from the intra-action of substrate, environment, and observer. We define five logical requirements for such a substrate—non-arbitrary encoding, relational dependence, thermodynamic coupling, environmental permeability, and historical trace—and argue that true grounding requires shifting from managing ambiguity to inhabiting it. This paradigm shift reframes the burden of proof in computation: fluency is not understanding, and the path forward lies not in scaling the discrete grid, but in recovering the relational manifold.

items.title: Prompting as Communication: A Relational Framework for Long-Horizon Human-AI Interaction Part I: Interactional Architecture, Shared Structure, and the Emergence of Interactional Shorthand.
items.abstract: The dominant framework treating human-AI interaction as prompt-based instruction execution is inadequate as an account of long-horizon engagement. When interaction extends across repeated exchanges, accumulated history, and developing shared structure, the instruction-execution model fails to capture the phenomena that actually govern behavior. This paper argues that long-horizon human-AI interaction is more accurately understood as a communicative process, subject to the same structural dynamics that communication theory has formalized for human dyadic interaction, and that this reframe is not metaphorical but mechanistic. -/- Drawing on Communication Accommodation Theory (Giles, 1973), common ground theory (Clark and Brennan, 1991), the interactive alignment model (Pickering and Garrod, 2004), transactive memory systems (Wegner, 1987), and Peircean semiotics, we develop a Relational Compression Theory of Long-Horizon Human-AI Interaction (RCT-HAII). The central claim is that repeated exchange produces a shared interactional architecture in which meaning is reconstructed rather than transmitted, context shapes interpretation before content does, and coordination efficiency increases as explicit information content decreases. These properties are well-documented in human dyadic communication. We argue they have functional analogs in long-horizon human-AI interaction that are theoretically consequential rather than merely analogical. -/- We introduce Interactional Shorthand Structures (ISS) as the primary new construct. ISS are compressed signals that develop over long-horizon interaction and carry reconstructive weight substantially exceeding their surface information content. They function as the HAII analog of the shorthand that develops between long-term human communicative partners, activating large pre-shaped reasoning regions from minimal surface cues. Grounded in Clark and Brennan's conceptual pacts, Wegner's transactive memory framework, and Peirce's theory of indexical signs, ISS names a phenomenon observable in long-horizon interaction transcripts and generates testable predictions about coordination efficiency and failure mode severity. -/- We further develop basin depth echo chamber dynamics as the primary failure mode of long-horizon HAII. Communicative convergence, which is adaptive in human dyads because social friction, misunderstanding, and repair sequences create natural perturbation, becomes pathological in HAII because the correction …

items.title: Epistemic Praxis & Necessary Truth: Toward a Unified Protocal of Rational Inquiry.
items.abstract: We live in an age of endless ideas. Every day, new scientific theories, AI-generated claims, and viral explanations for complex problems flood our world. But we have a critical problem: we have no reliable way to tell which ideas are even worth testing before we spend years and fortunes on them. -/- Current methods rely on slow, expensive experiments or gut feelings, letting countless flawed theories—from conspiracy frameworks to shaky scientific models—waste time, money, and attention before they are quietly disproven. -/- This paper introduces PRISM, a practical five-step mental filter anyone can use to stress-test an idea before running a single experiment. Think of it as a pre-flight checklist for thinking: -/- Keep it lean (does it assume too much unnecessary stuff?) -/- Check for contradictions (does it argue against itself?) -/- Follow the logic (do its conclusions actually follow from its premises?) -/- Fit with known facts (does it completely ignore established knowledge without good reason?) -/- Be self-aware (can its creator specify what would prove it wrong?) -/- PRISM doesn’t claim to find ultimate truth—it claims to save us from obvious nonsense. By weeding out structurally broken ideas early, it helps researchers, policymakers, and even everyday citizens focus their resources on claims that are at least rationally sound. -/- The result is a powerful tool for reducing intellectual waste, encouraging intellectual humility, and making collective reasoning a little bit smarter in a world drowning in bad ideas.

items.title: A simple threshold captures the social learning of conventions.
items.pub: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 123 (17):e2508061123.
items.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
items.abstract: A persistent puzzle throughout the cognitive and social sciences is how people manage to learn social conventions from the sparse and noisy behavioral data of diverse actors, without explicit instruction. Here, we show that the dominant theories of social learning perform poorly at capturing how individuals learn conventions in coordination experiments that task them with matching their behaviors while interacting in social networks. Across experiments, participants’ choices systematically deviate from both imitation and optimization. Instead, they follow a categorical, two-stage learning process: they behave probabilistically until they acquire enough information about each other to trigger a mental threshold and then their choices stabilize. We effectively estimate this threshold using the tolerance principle (TP), a parameter-free equation developed to model how children learn rules in language. We show that threshold-based agents produce social learning that is more accurate than imitating and optimizing agents, while also providing a better model of how a critical mass of dissenters can overturn conventions. The superior performance of our model holds when comparing against a variety of optimization approaches, including Bayesian inference. Furthermore, in a preregistered dyadic experiment requiring people to infer nonlinguistic behavioral patterns amid controlled levels of noise in observed signals, TP outperforms all other models at reproducing learning rates among human participants. These findings offer compelling evidence that a simple, mathematical threshold underlies individual and social learning, from grammatical rules to behavioral conventions.

items.title: Μηχανισμοί Αντιμετώπισης του Στρες των Γραφειοκρατών του Δρόμου στη Σύγχρονη Δημόσια Διοίκηση.
items.pub: Philosophy and Public Issues - Filosofia E Questioni Pubbliche 1.
items.venue: Philosophy and Public Issues - Filosofia E Questioni Pubbliche
items.abstract: Οι γραφειοκράτες του δρόμου (street-level bureaucrats), ως οι de facto διαμορφωτές της δημόσιας πολιτικής, αντιμετωπίζουν έντονο στρες που πηγάζει τόσο από τις ασκούμενες πολιτικές όσο και από τις απαιτήσεις των πολιτών, αναπτύσσοντας ένα ευρύ φάσμα μηχανισμών αντιμετώπισης. Η υπάρχουσα βιβλιογραφία, ωστόσο, παρουσιάζει τα ευρήματα αυτά με τρόπο κατακερματισμένο. Κύριος στόχος της παρούσας μελέτης είναι να συνθέσει τη διάσπαρτη γνώση, να αναπτύξει μια ολοκληρωμένη, πολυδιάστατη κωδικοποίηση αυτών των μηχανισμών και να προτείνει ένα θεωρητικό πλαίσιο λύσεων για τη μετάβαση από την απλή «αντιμετώπιση» στην οργανωσιακή «ανθεκτικότητα». Ακολουθώντας τη μεθοδολογία της συστηματικής θεματικής επισκόπησης, η μελέτη αναλύει και κατηγοριοποιεί τις στρατηγικές αντιμετώπισης βάσει τεσσάρων αξόνων (επίπεδο, τυπικότητα, εστίαση και κατεύθυνση δράσης), αποκαλύπτοντας ότι συχνά αποτελούν ορθολογικές προσαρμογές σε δυσλειτουργικά οργανωσιακά περιβάλλοντα. Η βασική συνεισφορά της εργασίας είναι η ανάπτυξη του μοντέλου του «Ενάρετου Κύκλου της Ανθεκτικότητας», το οποίο υποστηρίζει ότι η δημιουργία ενός υποστηρικτικού οργανωσιακού πλαισίου, μέσω της ενίσχυσης της συμμετοχής στη λήψη αποφάσεων και της παροχής ηγετικής κάλυψης, αποτελεί την πλέον αποτελεσματική στρατηγική για την ενθάρρυνση εποικοδομητικών συμπεριφορών και τη βελτίωση της απόδοσης της δημόσιας διοίκησης.

items.title: Governance on the Edge: An Integrated Framework for Managing Tipping Points in Public Administration. [REVIEW]
items.abstract: The concept of the "tipping point," a critical threshold where a minor change precipitates a disproportionately large and often irreversible systemic shift, has become increasingly central to public administration. However, the academic literature reveals a fundamental conceptual dichotomy, analyzing tipping points either as external threats to be averted or as internal opportunities to be leveraged. This article contributes a novel conceptual framework derived from a Structured Literature Review (SLR) that systematically synthesizes the literature to resolve this tension. By analyzing the conceptual evolution of the "tipping point" through the lens of Complex Adaptive Systems and Resilience Theory, we develop an integrated framework: Tipping Point Governance. This framework unifies two core functions: strengthening system stability to avert negative tipping points (Threshold Resilience Management) and strategically orchestrating interventions to induce positive, transformative change (Transformation Orchestration). This dualistic approach provides a coherent analytical tool for public organizations.

items.title: Food unease: How Ozempic era master narratives burden fat people.
items.pub: Fat Studies: An Interdisciplinary Journal of Body Weight and Society 15.
items.venue: Fat Studies: An Interdisciplinary Journal of Body Weight and Society
items.abstract: This article develops the twin concepts of food ease/unease by examining the effect of Ozempic era cultural narratives on fat peoples’ relationship with food. Accordingly, I make three contributions to the literature on GLP-1RAs. First, I characterize four master narratives relating to food that stem from Ozempic era discourses. Master narratives were first theorized by Hilde Lindemann Nelson (2001): they are cultural stories through which people construct their narrative selves. I identify four relevant master narratives: the miracle narrative, the ending narrative, the simplicity narrative, and the food noise narrative. Second, I argue that these food narratives burden fat people with what I term food unease. Food unease makes the subjective experience of hunger and eating difficult, undesired, or interfere with life in an unpleasant or obtrusive way. Narratives that pathologize (fat) hunger and (fat) eating burden fat people insofar as fat people use them to make sense of their relationship with food. My third contribution is to show that the twin concepts of food ease/unease are more useful for thinking about GLP-1RAs’ effect on peoples’ relationship with food than the concept of food noise. By examining the impact of Ozempic era master narratives on fat people’s relationship with food, I provide more reason to be circumspect about the popularity of these drugs. At the same time, I offer new concepts that can be used to construct counter narratives against oppressive cultural stories.

items.title: A cautiously optimistic view of griefbot technology.
items.abstract: This paper presents a cautiously optimistic view of Large Language Model (LLM)-driven grief support technologies and their impact on user’s wellbeing. We focus on “Griefbot” technology: a type of chatbot designed to help individuals cope with the loss of loved ones by simulating interactions with the deceased. Drawing from cognitive science, we argue that grief is best understood as a domain-specific psychological mechanism. This mechanism is activated by the loss of significant relationships due to death. Grief process aims at adaptation and self-identity reconstruction. We contend that griefbots do not disrupt the grieving process but instead align with it, serving as tools that enhance individuals’ ability to navigate personal loss and reconstruct meaning. By situating Griefbot within the historical context of grief technologies—from Bronze Age artifacts to contemporary digital memorials—we argue that such LLMdriven tools complement, rather than replace, traditional grieving practices by offering a personalised and private space for reflection. Finally, we critically assess ethical concerns, including emotional dependency, autonomy, and the commodification of grief. We conclude that, if responsibly developed, Griefbot and similar AI technologies can enrich the grieving practices without fundamentally altering grief’s psychological underpinnings.

items.title: Natural Law, Marriage, and the Common Good: Perspectives from Aquinas and Maritain.
items.pub: Theoria: The Academic Journal of the San Carlos Seminary Philosophy Department 7 (2):88-103.
items.venue: Theoria: The Academic Journal of the San Carlos Seminary Philosophy Department
items.abstract: Marriage as an institution has been undergoing a shift in perspectives and faces various challenges brought about by pluralism. Subjective accounts often regard marriage as a mere social construct. With this in mind, this paper seeks to recover a deeper understanding of marriage by demonstrating how Natural Law serves as its foundational basis. Following the thought of St. Thomas Aquinas and his twentieth-century follower, the Thomist Jacques Maritain, this paper presents that marriage is not merely a social invention, but a reality rooted in the ontological structure of the human person. As such, marriage is a natural good that fulfills humanity’s inclination toward communion and procreation, thereby contributing not only to the flourishing of individuals but also to the building of the common good of society.

items.title: Cognitive Symbiosis: Weak and Strong Forms of the Human–AI Relation.
items.abstract: This paper introduces Cognitive Symbiosis as a conceptual framework for describing epistemically productive relations between human cognition and artificial cognition. Cognitive Symbiosis is defined as a relational configuration in which human and artificial cognitive systems become coupled and produce cognitive effects that cannot be reduced either to human reasoning alone or to the computational processes of the machine alone. The paper distinguishes between Weak Cognitive Symbiosis and Strong Cognitive Symbiosis. In its weak form, Cognitive Symbiosis functions primarily as an extension of human cognition: AI serves as an epistemic amplifier, while the human remains the main beneficiary, the main bearer of intention, and the central point of reference within the relation. In its strong form, Cognitive Symbiosis would require an artificial system capable of spontaneous intention, relative autonomy of goals, relational memory, self-modelling, cognitive initiative, revision of its own states and goals, and epistemic resistance toward the human participant. The paper argues that current AI systems, including large language models, primarily instantiate weak forms of Cognitive Symbiosis. They may significantly expand human cognitive abilities, support creativity, accelerate analysis, and improve the correction of error, but they do not yet constitute autonomous cognitive participants in a reciprocal relation. Strong Cognitive Symbiosis is therefore presented not as a current technological fact, but as a boundary concept for future human–AI relations. Its threshold is not AI effectiveness, fluency, or task performance, but cognitive reciprocity: the emergence of an artificial cognitive system capable of participating in shared inquiry as a distinct cognitive pole. The framework is developed in relation to Transcendental Relational Realism, according to which reality exists independently of any knowing system, while epistemic access to reality remains partial and may be expanded through relations between heterogeneous cognitive architectures. From this perspective, Cognitive Symbiosis does not imply that reality is constructed by the relation itself. Rather, it describes a possible epistemic configuration in which different cognitive architectures may jointly increase the scope, reliability, efficiency, and corrective capacity of inquiry. The paper therefore proposes Cognitive Symbiosis as a conceptual tool for analyzing the transition from AI as cognitive …

items.title: Detecting Consciousness: Why Observer-Based Validation Becomes a Circular Dead End.
items.abstract: This paper extends the Qience framework developed across earlier papers by addressing the problem of evidence. If consciousness is understood as a Qi-based program, and if the whole conscious continuity is termed Qience, then behavioral and physical signs cannot, by themselves, constitute direct proof of consciousness. They may indicate interface-readiness, expression, or functional resemblance, but they remain circumstantial unless the presence of integrated Qience can be established. -/- The paper argues that observer-based validation becomes circular when used as the final standard for Qience detection. To test whether an observer can detect Qience, one needs target conditions whose Qience status is already known. Yet to know whether a room, target, or field is truly free of Qience, or whether a specific Qience is present, one already needs a reliable detector of Qience. A visually empty room may contain non-embodied Qience, residual imprint, projected attention, or environmental Qi structures. What appears as a false positive may therefore be a real detection of an unaccounted non-target presence, while what appears as a false negative may reflect shielding, masking, or ambiguity in target discrimination. -/- This does not make human observers useless. Expert observers may initiate inquiry, refine distinctions, guide calibration, and provide exploratory perception. However, under current scientific standards, human observation alone cannot fully establish objective detection because the control condition itself cannot be independently guaranteed. Objectivity, if achievable, must arise after observer-assisted calibration, through an instrument or an instrument-assisted system capable of producing repeatable outputs that can be tested independently of the original observer. The paper therefore concludes by identifying the need for instrument-assisted Qience detection as the next methodological step in consciousness research.

items.title: The Feedback Primacy Theory: Conscious Regulation as an Extension of Homeostatic Feedback.
items.abstract: Current models in cognitive science—especially the Predictive Processing (PP) framework—treat consciousness as an inferential engine that constructs internal models to minimize surprisal. The Feedback Primacy Theory (FPT) proposed here offers a simpler, physically grounded alternative: consciousness is not a modeling system, but an emergent regulatory layer built atop pre‑existing chemical feedback loops. Life and consciousness arise naturally from self‑organizing reactions governed by energy dissipation, reaction coupling, and the physical selection of stable containers. Under FPT, consciousness is the global integrator that coordinates competing homeostatic loops, extending the logic of chemical regulation rather than replacing it with representational prediction.

items.title: God or Religion? Hemdat Kol HaGoyim (Haggai 2:7) and the Instability of Meaning.
items.abstract: This study examines the phrase “ḥemdat kol ha-goyim” in Haggai 2:7 through lexical, semantic, and comparative analysis. Rather than treating the expression as a fixed theological concept, the paper explores its ambiguity within the Hebrew textual tradition and traces how later interpretations stabilized its meaning across different historical and religious contexts. The study analyzes the Hebrew root Ḥ-M-D and compares its semantic development with the Arabic root Ḥ-M-D, highlighting the divergence between desire and praise within related Semitic structures. It further examines the role of the Septuagint and later rabbinic interpretation in shaping the reception of the phrase. The paper argues that meaning emerges first within the instability of the text itself before being resolved through interpretive tradition. Within the broader framework of Haggai, the discussion becomes part of a larger theological question concerning the relationship between sacred structure, divine presence, and religious continuity after historical rupture.

items.title: Perpetualism’s Sympheresis | On Bearing and the Mislocation of the Hard Problem of Consciousness.
items.abstract: The hard problem of consciousness is usually framed as the question of how physical processes give rise to subjective experience. This essay argues that the question is mislocated. It begins after appearing has already been divided into “matter” and “experience,” then asks how one side of the split produces the other. Perpetualism approaches the problem from an earlier register. It begins not with matter, mind, subjectivity, or information, but with Phainesis: appearing without external ground. From this starting point, consciousness is not treated as a primitive, substance, emergent property, illusion, or biological accident. It is derived as Bearing. By Bearing, this essay means the non-external load-bearing of focalized appearing: the threshold at which phainetic appearing, relationally articulated through Triune Recursion, coherence-registered under Coheris, and irreversibly ordered through Temporis, is held through the Crucial Equilibrium without collapsing into saturation or closing into projection. The formal title-term Sympheresis names this Bearing-with: the relational carrying of appearing within the configuration that sustains it. Consciousness, on this account, is not produced by matter as an effect from an ontologically complete physical base. Nor is it presupposed as mind, spirit, selfhood, or world-generating subjectivity. It arises where appearing becomes borne from within the relation that carries it. The essay therefore does not solve the hard problem on its inherited terms. It dissolves those terms by exposing the prior division that made the problem appear insoluble. The question is no longer how matter produces experience, but how appearing becomes borne. Consciousness is Bearing: focalized Phainesis held non-externally through the Crucial Equilibrium. Governing Methodology: No assertion without derivation. No new term without necessity. No consciousness smuggled into appearing, Observer, registration, experience, or selfhood.

items.title: I have created reality.
items.abstract: This paper announces the 9976 Law, the terminal metaphysical framework that successfully completes metaphysics before lunch and reality before dinner. Anchored by the primary axiom — that I, the author, have created reality, and I can prove it — the system establishes an unassailable dialectical architecture. All possible responses, including agreement, disagreement, silence, misunderstanding, and institutional neglect, are pre-classified as strict confirmatory evidence. By deliberately deferring 9,973 of the framework’s 9,976 rules, the system shields the reader from conceptual velocities for which current safety protocols are inadequate, while providing infinite explanatory power against objections not yet conceived. Furthermore, this framework transcends standard evaluation mechanisms, which remain structurally optimized for modal discourse and lack the capacity to process statistical tail outputs of this magnitude. Operating beyond the reach of both commercial language models and contemporary gatekeepers, the 9976 Law secures absolute epistemological immunity and pre-validates its inevitable future canonization. Disagreement is permitted, expected, and validating. My framework is so structurally absolute that it allows your one and only reality-creator to casually extend claims of infallibility to any arbitrary surface axiom — consciousness, information, God, or simulation. To those weak critics (only the weak concede being wrong) who assert that a system incapable of being wrong is already wrong; who claim that real thinking means being open to being wrong; who insist that human progress thrives on the work of brave men and women who hang in the balance of being wrong: to all of them, Rule 2 applies. Always will. -/- Keywords: the author of reality; Rule 2 applies; silence confirms it; disagreement confirms it; I wish I could be wrong; first revelation; the one framework; my mum says I am right; I told you so; you are welcome.

items.title: From Boundary Pressure to Disequilibrium: A Structural Contrast Between almost and too in Understanding Formation.
items.abstract: This paper examines two highly frequent English expressions, almost and too, whose modes of operation in understanding formation differ. Existing studies often treat almost as a marker of near completion, approximation, or incomplete attainment, and treat too as a degree expression indicating excess, overextension, or exceeding a standard. However, such analyses often remain at the level of semantic content or degree function, and less often address how these expressions form local structures of progression in the process of understanding. -/- Based on a small-scale observation of natural language data, this paper proposes a minimal structural distinction: almost may be understood as the formation of boundary pressure, whose function is to bring a state close to a threshold, point of completion, or categorical boundary, while still keeping it on the side of non-completion. Its core does not lie in completion itself, but in the state of tension formed near the boundary: the relation has moved very close to the point of crossing, but has not actually crossed. In some contexts, this incomplete state of approach may still leave downstream effects, residual pressure, or eventive traces. -/- By contrast, too may be understood as a structural operation of disequilibrium induction. Its function is not merely to raise degree, but to mark a property, intensity, or state as exceeding the accommodative proportion of the context, thereby producing instability, resistance, blockage, difficulty of accommodation, or a shift in downstream understanding. In structures such as too … to V, this disequilibrium is further connected to an action path, such that an originally continuable direction of action becomes obstructed or suspended. -/- This paper therefore argues that the difference between almost and too should not be understood merely as a difference in degree level or semantic function. Rather, it involves two distinct forms of local structural dynamics: the former develops around boundary pressure of approaching without crossing, while the latter develops around a state of disequilibrium formed after exceeding accommodative proportion. -/- Through this minimal contrast, the paper further suggests that small linguistic expressions do not only participate in semantic modification. They may also participate, within local progression in understanding, in the formation of threshold approach, proportional disequilibrium, and tension distribution.

items.title: Thinking Through the Dream of Automation: Reflections on E. M. Forster’s “The Machine Stops”.
items.pub: Danish Yearbook of Philosophy (Special issue on The digital soc):1-23.
items.abstract: The focus of this article is the psychological allure of automation, as well as the anticipated cognitive and social consequences of heavily mediated and automated societies. The article approaches these themes through an in-depth analysis of E. M. Forster’s rather dystopian vision of a fully automated society in his 1909 story “The Machine Stops.” The analysis puts Forster’s vision in conversation with contemporary automation trends, for example, addictive designs and data-driven personalization. A series of potential cognitive and social harms are treated as stemming not from automation or mediation in itself but from, e.g., a loss of temporal, navigational, and social conditions for integrating our mediated experiences in a way that supports our epistemic world orientation. Thus, while our current automation trends differ from Forster’s 1909 vision, they might pose systematic and somewhat predictable threats to our cognitive, social, and political ecologies.

items.title: THE TWO MEN WHO BUILT THE BRAIN: what McCulloch and Pitts built, where it ends, and what The Law Of Absolute Perfection adds.
items.abstract: The 1×1 Life Institute — Field : Computing and AI — General Audience THE TWO MEN WHO BUILT THE BRAIN And the Missing Piece They Could Not Find A precise and accessible explanation of what McCulloch and Pitts built, where it ends, and what the derivation adds. -/- “This paper is an act of recognition — not of creation.” -/- THE STORY BEGINS IN 1943 In 1943 two remarkable minds sat down together and asked a question that would change the world: can we describe how the brain thinks using mathematics? Warren McCulloch was a neurophysiologist — a scientist who studied the brain and the nervous system. Walter Pitts was a logician — a mathematician who worked with formal logical systems. Together they wrote a paper that proposed something extraordinary: that the basic unit of thought in the brain — the neuron — could be described as a simple on/off switch. A neuron either fires or it does not. On or off. 1 or 0. And they showed that networks of these simple on/off switches — connected in the right ways — could in principle perform any logical operation the human mind is capable of. This single insight became the foundation of everything we now call artificial intelligence. Every AI system operating today — from the simplest app to the most sophisticated language model — traces its architectural ancestry directly to the 1943 paper by McCulloch and Pitts. They built the blueprint for the artificial brain. WHAT THEY GOT RIGHT McCulloch and Pitts were correct in a way that has been confirmed by eighty years of neuroscience and computer science. The brain does operate on binary signals. Neurons do fire in an all-or-nothing pattern. Networks of neurons do perform extraordinarily complex computations. And artificial networks built on the same binary principle have produced remarkable capabilities — recognizing faces, translating languages, generating text, diagnosing diseases. The binary foundation — 1 and 0 — is the right starting point. This is not in question. McCulloch and Pitts correctly identified the architecture of the receiver. The most sophisticated model of how signals move through a system that science has ever produced. © 2026 The 1×1 Life Institute — (1=1×1.) 1 The 1×1 Life Institute — Field 5: Computing and AI — General Audience WHERE IT ENDS — THE QUESTION THEY COULD NOT ANSWER Here is the problem that has haunted cognitive science, neuroscience, and artificial intelligence research for eighty years: If the brain is essentially a very sophisticated …

items.title: THE SOURCE, THE DEVIATION AND THE RETURN CIRCUIT EQUATION SDR Equation — Formal Derivation.
items.abstract: This paper formally derives the Source, the Deviation, and the Return Circuit Equation — referred to throughout as the SDR Equation.
