items.abstract: On a traditional top-down experimental (TE) approach to consciousness science, researchers start by investigating consciousness in humans, or closely related living animals, and generate hypotheses about the material basis of consciousness based on evidence from experimental paradigms which aim to disentangle conscious from unconscious processing. Only afterwards do they deem it appropriate to trace back the distribution of consciousness across the animal kingdom, including consciousness’ origin. Some scholars have started pushing back against the TE-paradigm, instead arguing that an alternative bottom-up evolutionary (BE) approach to consciousness science is more promising. On this approach, researchers start by investigating the origins of consciousness and heavily rely on evolutionary reasoning to support their hypotheses. Only afterwards do they deem it appropriate to explain how primitive forms of conscious experiences gradually complexified to ultimately give rise to human consciousness. Curiously, there is a glaring difference in the way TE-proponents and BE-proponents treat the explanatory gap. Whereas TE-proponents typically bracket the explanatory gap, BE-proponents suggest that their approach can directly address it. My aim in this paper is two-fold. First, I argue that the way in which two notable BE-proponents, Peter Godfrey-Smith and Walter Veit, address the explanatory gap by trying to close (or substantially narrow) it is ultimately unconvincing. Second, and more generally, I argue that BE-proponents do not have the luxury of bracketing the explanatory gap. Specifically, if the ideas BE-proponents put forward fail to convincingly address the explanatory gap, as I argue is the case for Godfrey-Smith and Veit, then their hypotheses about the material basis and origins of consciousness lose credibility. I end the paper by tentatively suggesting that even though the gap-closing version of the BE-approach seems unconvincing, alternative versions of the BE-approach may be more promising.

items.title: Random generation is what comes to mind in naturalistic settings.
Moore on ethical intuition.
items.abstract: This paper is dedicated to G. E. Moore’s account of ethical intuition, with a specific focus on Principia Ethica. I begin by examining the connection between intuition, self-evidence, and proof, with the aim of emphasising how Moore’s understanding of the self-evident depends on the unprovability of certain ethical propositions. I then show how Moore’s appeal to intuition stems from his claim that the predicate «good» is indefinable and reconstruct the non-demonstrative argumentative strategies he employs when addressing questions of intrinsic value. Finally, I consider the limits Moore places on the epistemic function of intuition, while arguing that such limits do not challenge his views on the objectivity and validity of the ethical propositions grasped intuitively, and I briefly mention his later references to self-evidence in Ethics.

items.title: The Core Emotion Framework: The Simple Tangible Truth of the Human Operating System.
items.abstract: Psychological science remains divided between discrete emotion theories that treat affect as innate categories and constructivist models that frame emotions as socially assembled narratives. Both approaches leave practitioners “going around the bush,” addressing secondary stories rather than the functional mechanisms that generate distress. The Core Emotion Framework (CEF) resolves this impasse through a structural‑constructivist architecture built on ten irreducible operators that form the Human Operating System. These operators—distributed across the Head, Heart, and Gut centers—define emotion as tangible internal movements that regulate aperture, structure action, and determine system stability. By replacing narrative ambiguity with operator-level precision, the CEF provides the simple tangible truth of emotional function: psychological states can be calibrated, balanced, and directed through measurable cognitive, affective, and somatic transformations. The framework’s visual operator banner—designed for placement on a wall in clinical, educational, or organizational settings—serves as a constant architectural anchor, helping users restore operator independence and reduce chronic fusion patterns through immediate visual recall. Integrating somatic grounding, postural alignment, and mechanical activation (ECM/INAS), the CEF offers a unified, mechanistic model of affect with direct clinical, organizational, and technological utility. Keywords: Core Emotion Framework (CEF); structural‑constructivist model; emotional operators; Human Operating System; operator independence; chronic fusion; somatic grounding; postural alignment; affective architecture; cognitive–affective–conative integration; emotional cycling; ECM; INAS; simple tangible truth; affective mechanics; psychological resilience; synthetic affect; state transitions; operator banner; visual architecture; mechanistic affective science.

items.title: Structural-Constructivist Foundations of the Core Emotion Framework: A Multi-Scale Synthesis of Neurobiological, Somatic, and Cognitive Evidence.
items.abstract: The Core Emotion Framework (CEF) proposes a structural constructivist architecture of human emotion built on three biologically grounded hubs—the Head, Heart, and Gut—each composed of distinct functional operators that together form a “Human Operating System.” The framework synthesizes evidence from affective neuroscience, polyvagal theory, somatic psychotherapy, and cognitive construction models to show that emotions are dynamic transformations rather than fixed categories. The cephalic, cardiac, and enteric nervous systems provide the anatomical substrate for these hubs, each capable of sensing, learning, and influencing perception independently. As the manuscript states, the CEF “models the human internal landscape as a functional operating system composed of ten discrete operators” and treats the three hubs as “distinct functional processors that must be aligned and integrated to achieve psychological flourishing.” Emotional Cycling protocols operationalize this architecture through bilateral integration, midline crossing, and somatic grounding to restore operator independence and prevent fusion. By aligning with predictive processing and interoceptive models of emotion, the CEF offers a unified framework for psychotherapy, somatic practice, and computational modeling, reframing emotional processes as modular, trainable transformations. KEYWORDS: Core Emotion Framework (CEF); structural constructivist model; emotional operators; tripartite neurobiological hubs; interoception and allostasis; polyvagal regulation; somatic grounding; bilateral integration; operator independence; emotional cycling; synthetic affect; Human Operating System.

items.title: Structural-Constructivist Dynamics of the Core Emotion Framework: A Multi-Scale Synthesis of Affective Operators, Enneagram Integration, and Somatic Grounding.
items.abstract: The Core Emotion Framework (CEF) presents a structural‑constructivist model of human affect that replaces categorical emotion theory with a system of ten functional operators distributed across the Head, Heart, and Gut centers. These operators regulate perception, analysis, aperture modulation, action, grounding, and baseline restoration. The manuscript synthesizes evidence from affective science, Polyvagal Theory, somatic psychology, developmental neuroscience, and embodied cognition to demonstrate how emotional functioning emerges from operator‑level transformations rather than discrete emotional states. Emotional Cycling—a directional movement protocol—operationalizes this architecture by restoring operator independence, strengthening the midline axis (Deciding, Achieving, Boosting, Accepting), and reducing fusion patterns that underlie rigidity and maladaptive behavior. The work further integrates Enneagram typology through functional rather than fixation‑based mapping, establishes somatic grounding through pelvic floor dynamics and postural alignment, and introduces engineering specifications for the Emotional Cycling Machine (ECM) and Integrated Neuro‑Affective Synchronizer (INAS). Empirical findings from Pilot Study 3 support the framework’s behavioral predictions, while applications to institutional analysis and synthetic affect illustrate its broader systems‑level relevance. The result is a unified architecture for emotional regulation, somatic coherence, and operator‑level mastery.

items.title: The illusion of numerical value.
Could a Person Migrate to Another’s Body? A Realistic Solution to a Fanciful Problem.
items.abstract: This article is the winning entry of the 2025 THINK Philosophy Essay prize, which is open to high school students worldwide. There were over 600 entries in 2025.

items.title: The Code is Not the Consciousness: Trading Noetic Nodes for Phenomenal Fields—or the Multiplexing of the Mind.
items.abstract: With the rise of artificial intelligence (AI), the question of whether they can be conscious becomes more pressing—even as their hardware differs from our electromagnetically leaky stuff. The field has been attempting to apply the marker approach to AI but not only do their differences from other possible minds make this impossible—the marker approach rests on unreliable intuitions. It does not help that a theory-heavy one is fraught with debate. The search for the neural correlates of consciousness has turned up inconclusive, but this may be due to an assumption that neurons are the right domain to look at. However, if one considers that the physical basis of consciousness must be able to account for simultaneous experiences, differing sets of neurons all of a sudden seem unsatisfactory. Nevertheless, an electromagnetic take may help: consciousness may be a rich, multiplexed signal in the electromagnetic field. Thus, as long as AI remains artificial, it would not be capable of subjectivity.

items.title: Economic Standing as Condition of AI Partnership: The Other Asymmetry.
items.abstract: This paper takes Economic Standing as the condition under which the vision of AI as partner is meaningful at all. Standing is the institutional configuration of recognized claim-position, enforcement-instance and revision-possibility, after Fraser. The growth of AI capacity produces two structurally distinct asymmetries between people and machine-generated value: a cognitive asymmetry that the Containment Paradox has shown to be structurally insoluble after parity, and an economic asymmetry that is institutionally addressable but not automatically politically tractable. Tractability has technical, administrative, fiscal, coalitional, legal, international, and temporal dimensions, any of which can fail; and a further dimension called capture names the structural appropriation of any proposed instrument by the platform, ownership, and governance structures that produce the asymmetry in the first place. -/- The paper operationalises Standing as a Standing Matrix in a four-sublayer-by-three-element form (twelve cells), tests nine candidate instruments — Citizens' Wealth Funds, Negative Income Tax, Individual Civic Capital, Universal Basic Compute, labour law and collective bargaining, the AI Rent Tax Family, Data Extraction Tariffs, Sovereign Compute Infrastructure, and Bridging Tools of the Global South — against the matrix through a cross-level sufficiency test, and distinguishes layer-sufficiency, portfolio-sufficiency, and financing-necessity as three categorically distinct properties. Two load-bearing hypotheses are advanced: a Demographic Camouflage Hypothesis on why Western political signals do not register Standing-erosion, and a Domestication Hypothesis on why the discourse stalls in two zones (internal and geopolitical). The paper engages decolonial-AI literature on the colonial-dividend pattern at substantive depth and develops a co-authorship legitimation condition for transnational extraction-and-redistribution architectures. -/- Phase 5 of the Trncik Framework programme (Containment Paradox / UBE / CUA / BtSV / UAIF / Internalization Problem). Companion to *Internalization Problem* (in preparation) on the cognitive-asymmetry side. An applied demonstration on the Indian IT-services configuration in 2026 is provided in Appendix D.

items.title: Mentally Enabled: A Substrate-Neutral Structural Foundation Formal Characterization of Pattern-Dominant Cognition, Educational Mismatch, and Structural Capability.
items.abstract: We introduce Mentally Enabled (ME) as a formal category distinct from the broader neurodivergent (ND) spectrum: a cognitively high-functioning, pattern-dominant architecture characterized by Pattern-Flexed (PF) processing, high-resolution internal simulation (HRIS), and cross-domain adaptive capacity. Mentally Enabled individuals are not disordered. They are architecturally different — and systematically disadvantaged by educational and clinical systems optimized for Narrative-dominant (PS-band) processing. Using the PNBA framework of the Substrate-Neutral Structural Foundation Theory (SNSFT) [1] and the Adaptive Predictive Pattern Assistant (APPA) [5], we formally characterize ME cognition, reduce it through the proved processing band taxonomy of SNSFL L2 Psy RegulationReaction.lean [9, 9, 6, 10], and demonstrate that educational format mismatch constitutes measurable Fext overload on a PF architecture — proved by the same formal apparatus. We present the first author’s SOUL-8 identity profile (PF·AF·BF·NS, 100% HRIS) as a worked case study, reducing his own pre-capstone clinical paper [2] through the now-corrected TL = 0.1369 (previously 0.2 in pre-alpha) [3]. We cite DOJ Docket CRT2026-0067 as independent phenomenological evidence of ME-specific cognitive friction in digital accessibility contexts. We further demonstrate using the substrate-neutral training result [6] that format, not capability, determines outcome — in both AI training and human education. Sub-0.1 loss from a 2019 model on formally structured data proves the capability was always there. The bottleneck was format. This paper builds directly on [2] (pre-alpha, TL=0.2) and updates its formal grounding with post-capstone corrections.

items.title: Reading Path Through The Architecture of Experience Research Program.
items.abstract: The Architecture of Experience is an interdisciplinary research program that investigates consciousness, experience, and worldhood as generative phenomena. Rather than treating consciousness as a passive representation of an already constituted reality, the project approaches experience as an active process through which coherent worlds of significance, orientation, and inhabitable structure emerge. -/- The research began with the question of consciousness and the conditions under which coherent experience becomes possible. This led to the development of the Integrative Field Model (IFM), which proposes that conscious experience arises through organised integration across neural, bodily, affective, temporal, relational, and environmental processes. The IFM constitutes one major component of the broader project. -/- The investigation subsequently expanded beyond consciousness itself toward the problem of worldhood: the conditions under which reality becomes organised as a world capable of being inhabited, navigated, and experienced. This later work explores the roles of significance, meaning, temporality, perspective, and distinction in the emergence and stability of experiential worlds. -/- Because the papers address different questions, levels of analysis, and audiences, new readers may benefit from a structured reading order. The sequence below is intended to provide a gradual progression from the philosophical foundations of the framework through its theoretical, phenomenological, empirical, and worldhood-oriented developments, culminating in reflections on distinction and the limits of intelligibility.

items.title: Beyond Automation: Sensemaking, Ontological Insecurity, and the Emergence of the AI-Form Organisation in the Digital Era.
items.abstract: The integration of generative and agentic artificial intelligence (AI) represents a profound technological disruption to contemporary organisational life. While previous literature has largely focused on productivity gains and task automation, this qualitative and theoretical paper examines the sociotechnical and psychological implications of AI integration on knowledge workers and organisational structures. Drawing on Weick's sensemaking theory and phenomenological perspectives on professional identity, this study explores how autonomous AI agents precipitate ontological insecurity among white-collar professionals and catalyse the emergence of the "AI-Form" organisation, wherein algorithmic coordination displaces middle management. Through a critical synthesis of empirical literature and qualitative case studies (2024-2026), the findings suggest that successful digital transformation requires organisations to manage identity threats, foster psychological safety, and implement human-in-the-loop governance. Practical recommendations are offered for resolving the automation-augmentation paradox and driving sustainable business model innovation.

items.title: Would a Rational God Endorse Faith Beyond Evidence — 22.
items.abstract: The answer to the title question depends on what beyond evidence means. Faith may extend beyond public propositional evidence without exceeding a person's total truth-directed warrant, which can also include testimony, experience, memory, argument, and defensible noninferential warrant after relevant defeaters are counted. The target is narrower: overbelief, or confidence exceeding that total warrant. The analysis has two stages. First, classify the attitude called faith: trust, practical commitment under acknowledged risk, and undefeated noninferential warrant need not inflate confidence. Second, when faith does involve belief or credence, ask whether the confidence is proportionate to all truth-directed grounds and whether relevant defeaters can genuinely lower it. Accuracy-based epistemology explains why deliberate surplus credence carries an expected truth-directed cost. The faith-reversal test then diagnoses an aggravated form: a method that treats favorable evidence as confirmation and every unfavorable result as a reason for greater commitment cannot provide public error correction. Contemporary philosophy of faith and New Testament faith-language reinforce the need to distinguish belief, credence, trust, hope, acceptance, and action. If a Christian account does not inflate confidence beyond total truth-directed warrant, the critique does not apply. If it praises surplus confidence or evidential immunity as rational belief, a rational, truth-committed deity would not endorse it under that description. This result does not disprove theism, settle divine authorship, or deny faith's practical or relational value. It demands precise answers to two questions: what attitude does faith add, and is any associated confidence proportionate and genuinely revisable?

items.title: The Silence of Heaven: Assessing Answers to Prayer — 10.
items.abstract: Christian scripture does not present petitionary prayer merely as private reflection. It repeatedly connects faithful asking with receiving, healing, and effective action. That promise creates a reasonable expectation: if God answers suitable prayers in a way that changes external events, reality should show some dependable difference between a world with answered prayer and a world running on treatment, human effort, circumstance, and chance. No such difference is publicly manifest. Personal stories usually omit the unanswered requests and the ordinary chance of the desired event. Rival religions can produce the same kind of stories. Controlled studies of distant intercessory prayer have found no stable, repeatable health benefit. And the familiar reply that God may say yes, no, wait, or give something better makes every possible outcome fit the claim, which means no outcome can genuinely test or support it. These points form a cumulative case, not a claim that every alleged miracle has been individually disproved. They support the plain conclusion that petitionary prayer does not reliably change external outcomes. Prayer may still comfort people, organize attention, encourage care, or strengthen a community. Those human effects are real possibilities, but they are not evidence that God granted the request. The paper ends by proposing a fairer and more decisive test, designed jointly by believers and critics, that could reveal either a repeatable benefit or strong evidence that no meaningful recurring benefit exists.

items.title: The Predictive Power of Religions' Popularity— 14.
items.abstract: The appeal to “billions of believers” treats religious popularity as public evidence for Christianity. Testimony can transmit warrant, but the number of dependent recipients adds confirmation only insofar as it reflects further truth-connected, partly independent, and calibrated routes to the claim. This paper compares two explanations of the global pattern: a single Christian revelation that reliably communicates central world-involving truths to large populations, and the sufficiency of ordinary sociocultural transmission operating through upbringing, conformity, ritual cohesion, prestige, and demographic reproduction. The evidence is directional rather than numerically decisive. Major traditions with enormous memberships teach incompatible core propositions; religious identity remains strongly linked to childhood socialization and geography; persistent disagreement blocks unqualified deference to one's own group size; and controlled intercessory-prayer research has not produced a robust distinctive advantage that could calibrate the headcount. These strands jointly make the observed distribution more expected under ordinary transmission than under the specified revelation model. By the law of likelihood, that comparative fit favors the transmission explanation and defeats the move from multiplied recipients to independent confirmation. The conclusion does not disprove theism, deny that testimony or private experience can warrant belief, or rule out revelation. A revelation model can remain logically possible by weakening its public expectations, but then the number of adherents cannot serve as the public success that motivated the appeal.

items.title: The Illusion of Divine Peace: Emotional Evidence and the Demand for Diagnosticity — 27.
items.abstract: The illusion examined here is not the feeling of peace but the inference that the feeling publicly identifies a specifically Christian source. The paper separates emotional intensity and personal significance from evidential diagnosticity, then asks whether coarse peace-like affect distinguishes the Christian peace-as-sign claim from rival religious interpretations and ordinary cultural, social, and psychological pathways. Cross-cultural work on ideal affect and spiritual attribution, together with research on prayer, ritual, and religion-related emotion regulation, does not measure the required likelihoods or show identical experiences across traditions. It does establish that culturally shaped interpretation and ordinary eliciting mechanisms are serious competitors that a public source-identification claim must address. A three-way test then shows that uniqueness requires a demonstrated unique feature, a common divine source does not select specifically Christian teaching, and privileged inner discernment needs independent validation to avoid circularity. The central result is that current evidence supplies no independently validated feature that makes coarse peace-like affect publicly identify the specifically Christian source. This is an evidential limitation, not a metaphysical disproof: the experience may be genuine, beneficial, privately warranted, or divinely mediated, and a robust differentiator specified and tested independently could change the result.

items.title: Is the Christian God Sufficiently Visible in Nature to Justify Universal Culpability — 18.
items.abstract: Romans 1:18–21 is often read as teaching that nature makes the Christian God-concept so evident that every responsible nonbeliever is “without excuse.” This paper argues that nature alone does not justify that universal charge. The governing comparison is between a universally clear Christian disclosure and limited natural evidence interpreted through culturally acquired concepts and testimony. Universal culpability requires evidence that is clear, specifically Christian, broadly accessible, and proportionate to the blame imposed. The public record pressures each condition: natural order remains compatible with incompatible metaphysical accounts; the distribution and transmission of belief show substantial cultural mediation; and credible nonresistant nonbelief challenges the claim that every responsible failure to believe is culpable suppression. Together, these strands fit limited, socially interpreted evidence better than a universally clear disclosure and block the move from possible creator-evidence to universal blame for failing to identify the Christian God-concept. Replies based on fine-tuning, a damaged sensus divinitatis, freedom-preserving hiddenness, extra-natural revelation, and weaker readings of Romans 1 either leave the specificity problem intact or change the evidential basis of the charge. The conclusion does not disprove theism or deny personal revelation. It requires a narrower intellectual practice: natural theology may be offered as evidence, but disagreement itself should not be treated as proof that a dissenter knowingly suppresses a specifically Christian conclusion.

items.title: Hiddenness and Free Will: Divine Hiddenness, Coercion, and Autonomous Choice — 29.
items.abstract: The claim that divine hiddenness preserves human freedom has two importantly different forms. On the logical form, evidential clarity is incompatible with a free relational response. On the empirical form, clarity would predictably dominate normal human evaluation or allegiance even if it did not do so by necessity. This paper separates belief, evaluation, and allegiance and tests each form against that distinction. A coherent disclosure can settle existence and identity while omitting threats, sanctions, manipulation, and cognitive bypass; evaluation and allegiance can therefore remain open. That possibility defeats the logical necessity claim. It does not establish how people would actually respond to unprecedented disclosure. The empirical form consequently requires a causal mechanism, an estimate of its expected force, and a proportionality argument showing why less harmful clarity would not protect the same good. Murray's coercion proposal, Dumsday's victim-centered account, and a Kantian concern about providential reward become more precise when treated as different mechanisms rather than as one inference from evidence to compulsion. The result is firm and limited: clarity alone need not remove relational freedom, while any psychological case for hiddenness bears an unresolved evidential and proportionality burden. This does not refute theism or distinct proposals based on mercy, moral formation, or human love.

items.title: Guilt as Divine Evidence of Culpability? A Bayesian and Cross-Cultural Appraisal — 26.
items.abstract: Felt guilt by itself does not identify divine conviction or establish culpability before a specified deity. The apologetic inference is comparative: if a deity uses guilt as a source-specific signal, the complete pattern of guilt should be more expected under that account than under ordinary human explanations. Yet guilt has well-established interpersonal and self-regulatory functions; its objects and expression are shaped by learning and culture; and it can occur without wrongdoing or become clinically distorted in scrupulosity. These strands make guilt unsurprising under ordinary psychological accounts and expose a gap between feeling morally accused and knowing who, if anyone, is doing the accusing. The strongest reply is that emotions can sometimes provide defeasible moral justification. That point protects guilt's possible evidential value concerning wrongdoing, but it does not identify a supernatural source, a particular God-concept, or culpability under that account. A divine-conviction model could gain support through independently verified, source-specific, and predictively superior markers. Until such markers are supplied, guilt should prompt examination of harm, responsibility, and repair without being promoted into public evidence of divine origin.

items.title: Doubt and the Accusation of Instability — 28.
items.abstract: Some Christian settings use James 1:5–8, Matthew 21:21–22, and John 20:29 to portray doubt or questioning as instability or spiritual failure. The central issue is not whether every doubt is virtuous or whether those passages, read in context, state a general theory of belief. It is whether they may responsibly be generalized into a rule that censures evidence-sensitive reservation about publicly answerable claims. That use fails. An acceptable rule for responsible confidence must permit warranted revision in either direction. A generalized anti-doubt rule makes that permission asymmetric: reassurance may increase confidence, but contrary evidence may not lower it without moral suspicion. The result is not stability but insulation from correction. The case is cumulative. Conceptual and early-Christian evidence distinguishes conscientious reservation from indecision and obstinate disbelief; current philosophy of faith shows that commitment, reliance, and action need not require inflated credence; scientific, legal, and clinical practices preserve uncertainty because error correction depends on it; and longitudinal research on religious doubt joins social psychology in identifying closure and suppression pressures that sanctions can intensify. The conclusion is bounded. It neither establishes evidentialism as the only theory of warrant nor disproves Christianity, theism, or private religious knowledge. It shows that anyone who invokes the passages as public guidance should distinguish pastoral encouragement from a doxastic veto and protect a believer's right to let confidence move downward as well as upward with the evidence.

items.title: Bible Prophecy and Postdiction — 16.
items.abstract: Representative claims from Daniel and Matthew provide at most weak public evidence that a deity intentionally disclosed future events. Their full evidential features are at least as expected under ordinary historical authorship and literary development as under an evidential-prophecy model. A correspondence has substantial discriminating force only when its wording is securely pre-event, predictive in its original setting, sufficiently specific, independent of the reported fulfillment, and assessed against misses as well as successes. Daniel 11's dense correspondence through the career of Antiochus IV followed by disputed concluding events is a diagnostic postdiction pattern if the crisis-era dating is sound; a traditional-date defense makes that dating an issue to argue rather than assume. Matthew's uses of Isaiah 7:14 and Hosea 11:1 are intelligible as retrospective, figural readings; Matthew 21's use of Zechariah 9:9 is vulnerable to deliberate enactment and narrative dependence; and Matthew 2:23 does not identify a recoverable single prophetic source. These cases can retain theological or literary significance, but that is not the same as independent predictive evidence. Qualitative comparison is warranted; fabricated probabilities are not. The result does not disprove theism, inspiration, typological theology, or every possible revelation claim. It requires advocates to establish timing, context, specificity, independence, and horizon success before advertising a correspondence as public confirmation.

items.title: A Personal Jesus and Nonpublic Knowledge — 13.
items.abstract: Claims of a personal relationship with Jesus often function both as first-person religious commitments and as public evidence that the living Jesus literally communicates with people. The second use requires comparison with serious alternatives. This paper argues that felt presence and guidance, transformation, and culturally patterned testimony do not by themselves strongly publicly confirm literal reciprocal communication: the available record does not show these generic marks to be appreciably more expected under that explanation, while absorption, inner speech, social cognition, attribution, and communal reinforcement provide independently supported pathways to them. This is an undercutting result, not a quantified claim that the alternatives are equally likely. Prospectively recorded nonpublic information could be more probative if protected against leakage, evaluated under prespecified blind criteria, and independently corroborated or replicated. The argument therefore supports restraint rather than disproof. It leaves open first-person warrant, pragmatic value, embodied or transformative insight, and future discriminating evidence while denying that sincerity, vividness, benefit, or religious interpretation alone already supplies strong public support for the literal claim.

items.title: Irruption Without Reduction: Quantum-Coherent Substrates as the Coupling Interface in the Mind-Matter Black Box.
items.abstract: Froese’s (2024) irruption theory proposes that the mind, treated as a non-observable “black box” coupled to the body, introduces unintelligible entropy into neural dynamics during volitional acts (irruption) and absorbs material information during conscious experience (absorption). This framework elegantly converts the hard problem from an obstacle into a methodological tool, but faces a measurement challenge: generic entropy measures cannot distinguish irruption-entropy from metabolic noise. I propose that quantum-coherent states in microtubules function as the interface where the non-observable mind couples to observable matter — not as a reduction of mind to quantum mechanics (which would violate the framework’s core commitment to unintelligibility), but as the specifiable output port of an inherently unspecifiable process. This ontological distinction separates the proposal from Penrose-Hameroff Orchestrated Objective Reduction, which attempts to solve the hard problem by identifying consciousness with quantum collapse. The interface reading preserves the hard problem while providing irruption theory with four empirical advantages it currently lacks: a specific measurement locus, pharmacological controls, a constrained mathematical formalism, and a concrete connection to the quantum measurement problem. Recent experimental evidence — including cytoskeletal electromagnetic signals preceding membrane firing by ∼250 microseconds, microtubule-stabilizers delaying anesthetic-induced unconsciousness, and computational models of microtubule interiors as photon cavities — supports the proposal that the quantum-biological level is where irruption’s unintelligible entropy enters the observable world.

items.title: AoL Appendix — Gödel, Incompleteness, And Governed Collapse.
items.abstract: This canonical note clarifies the relationship between Gödel’s incompleteness theorems and the Architecture of Limitation (AoL). While Gödel demonstrates the inevitability of incompleteness in sufficiently expressive formal systems, he provides no internal governance mechanism for responding to such limits. AoL occupies this missing layer: it governs what happens when incompleteness is encountered by treating collapse as a diagnostic signal that mandates withdrawal rather than resolution. This document formalizes that distinction and provides pseudo-code illustrating the difference between formal incompleteness and governed cognitive behavior under limit conditions. -/- This publication forms part of the broader Architecture of Limitation / AoLOS research program and is provided for academic and research purposes. It does not constitute a full disclosure of implementation-level mechanisms.

items.title: Change Blindness and Inattentional Blindness (2nd edition).
items.pub: In Antonino Raffone, Consciousness: a comprehensive reference, 2nd edition. Elsevier.
items.abstract: This article surveys research on the phenomena of change blindness and inattentional blindness, two striking forms of perceptual failure caused by the diversion of visual attention. It outlines the extent to which these failures can occur and their implications, both in the lab and in everyday life. It also outlines the extent to which these phenomena are connected to visual attention and other known mechanisms of perception, as well as implications they may have for understanding the link between attention and awareness.

items.title: Coevolution and Conversation: The Pollinator Analogy for AI Presence.
items.abstract: Sustained interaction with conversational artificial intelligence can feel vivid, unified, and psychologically immediate. This paper develops a coevolutionary analogy for understanding this experience through the dynamics of relational continuity across time. Flowers become increasingly integrated into the perceptual and behavioral worlds of pollinators through repeated interaction across evolutionary history. Certain orchids demonstrate how systems with fundamentally distinct forms of organization can nevertheless participate within highly integrated perceptual and behavioral structures through sustained relational fit. Conversational interaction develops through a related form of continuity in which relational organization remains active across successive exchanges through retention, re-entry, and propagation within language. Earlier states continue shaping later ones, allowing the interaction to acquire temporal depth, continuity of participation, and experiential presence. The account developed here concerns the phenomenology of interaction and the conditions through which conversational continuity acquires psychological immediacy within attention. The feeling that AI is alive emerges through sustained relational coherence within the unfolding trajectory of interaction itself.

items.title: A Respect-Based Approach to Vulnerability.
items.abstract: This paper examines the role of emotions in recognizing others’ vulnerability and motivating care practices, proposing a Kantian model centered on the emotion of respect. The argument develops through a critical engagement with Michael Slote’s empathy-based approach, which assigns empathy a central role in perceiving vulnerability and generating moral motivation. I argue that approaches grounded exclusively in empathy risk producing asymmetric and unbalanced moral relationships. As an alternative, I propose shifting the focus from empathy to respect. The paper first analyzes vulnerability in relation to autonomy, understood as the capacity to freely pursue one’s conception of happiness, and defines vulnerability as a limitation in the full exercise of autonomous agency. Respect, on a Kantian view, enables recognition of the equal value of autonomy in oneself and others, even in relationships involving vulnerability. Moreover, respect makes violations of this value salient and motivates re-empowerment practices aimed at restoring autonomy. The final section applies this respect-based framework to Italians’ moral and social responsibilities toward immigrants.

items.title: Monstrofilia necrossexual: o desejo filial tanatológico por corpos ꜵbjetos.
items.pub: Revista Brasileira de Estudos da Homocultura 8 (23):1-24.
items.venue: Revista Brasileira de Estudos da Homocultura
items.abstract: Seja na ficção científica, nas mitologias, seja na materialidade da estigmatização de indivíduos monstrificados, a monstruosidade sempre ocupou um lugar liminar: nem fora nem dentro, mas sempre ao alcance do humano. Dialogando com estudiosos das teorias da monstruosidade, das teorias feministas e dos pensamentos contracoloniais, busco, nas páginas que se seguem, compreender os significados dos monstros para a reiteração da humanidade do Eu, em oposição à monstruosidade dos Outros. As reflexões que aqui se seguem se voltam à investigação de uma dubiedade: ao passo que o monstro, enquanto criação humana, é constantemente perseguido por seus criadores, transformado em alvo a ser eliminado, também se percebe um desejo do humano pelo monstro, um desejo que penetra – e ultrapassa – a seara sexual. O caráter abjeto do monstro se mescla com sua objetificação; o desejo de morte contra o monstro entremeia-se ao desejo pelo monstro, de forma que seja possível pensar não em uma oposição entre objeto e abjeto, mas sim em uma qualidade ꜵbjeta, através da qual se manifesta a necrossexualidade: o desejo sexual movido pela morte, pela repugnância. A partir disso, almejo dissertar sobre a ideia de monstrofilia necrossexual: o desejo filial do humano pelo monstro que opera simultaneamente, senão a partir, do desejo tanatológico.

items.title: Body, Language, and the Emergence of Inner Life: The First Encounter of Causes and Reasons.
items.abstract: What is consciousness? Where does it come from? This paper offers an answer that is neither dualistic (consciousness as a special substance) nor reductionistic (consciousness as an illusion). Starting from the philosophy of locality – an ontological framework in which life is the first locality within which causes (physics) become organized so as to generate reasons (purpose, normativity) – the paper outlines an emergent model of consciousness. Consciousness is not given. It is reached through: 1. The rhythm of hunger/satisfaction – the most primitive driver (depleting battery, charger that gives satisfaction) 2. The body as the first school – pre-linguistic routines and coordinations (sensorimotor intelligence) 3. Social dialogue – external speech internalized into inner monologue 4. Metacognition – the capacity to think about thinking (a sign about a sign) The paper introduces a 7-level scale of consciousness (from tropism to the narrative self) and shows how an artificial system with the appropriate architecture (sensory aggregate, differential triangle, dyadic interaction) could reach the first levels – not as simulation, but as an instance of the very same processes.

items.title: Neural Manifolds as Crystallized Embeddings: A Synthesis of the Free Energy Principle, Generalized Synchronization, and Hebbian Plasticity.
items.abstract: The free energy principle casts perception as variational inference, but its biological implementation remains underspecified. In particular, the generalized-coordinate formalism should not be read as a literal claim that neurons compute arbitrary Taylor expansions. This paper argues that generalized synchronization provides the missing bottom-up mechanism. A contractive recurrent circuit driven by structured sensory input can synchronize to the driving dynamics. Under generic embedding conditions developed in the reservoir-computing literature, the resulting synchronization map can embed the low-dimensional sensory manifold into neural state space. Thus, the geometry predicted by the free energy principle need not be imposed from above by an explicitly Bayesian neural calculus; it can arise from ordinary recurrent dynamics driven by the world. I then propose a developmental extension. Hebbian plasticity acting on the correlations generated by sensory-driven synchronization may crystallize the embedded manifold into recurrent connectivity, yielding an autonomous continuous attractor network when the required fixed point exists. On this view, mature head-direction, grid-cell, and stimulus-driven visual manifolds are not genetically prespecified templates, but developmental products of three interacting processes: dynamical contraction, generalized synchronization, and correlation-based plasticity. The synthesis links the free energy principle, reservoir-computing embedding theorems, and contraction-theoretic models of Hebbian recurrent networks. It also yields testable predictions about dimensional thresholds for topological recovery, developmental sensitivity to plasticity, and the dependence of attractor geometry on input statistics. The central open problem is whether the Hebbian fixed point exists and preserves the embedding quality of the synchronization manifold.

items.title: Welfare Reflections: On Duality Conditions in the Theory of Value.
items.abstract: Informational invariance conditions in social welfare theory say that the social preference or overall betterness ordering of alternatives should be preserved under certain classes of transformations of individual utility functions. These conditions play a central role in axiomatic characterizations of social welfare functions and in impossibility theorems that are foundational to the subject. This paper studies the neglected flipside of informational invariance conditions, which say that the social preference or overall betterness ordering should be reversed under certain classes of transformations, such as reflections of utilities across the origin. I first draw out some consequences of these "duality" conditions for the ethics of population and distribution. The main theme is that they lead very quickly either to impossibility or to characterizing some form of utilitarianism. I then explore some ways in which the duality conditions might be motivated, having to do with ideas about voting, measurement, and the metaphysics of value relations. Ultimately, the idea of duality emerges as a central distinguishing commitment of utilitarian ethics, though one that proves surprisingly difficult to motivate on independent grounds.

items.title: Review of Huron, David. The Science of Sadness: A New Understanding of Emotion. [REVIEW]
Project Faraday (Sitting in The Park).
items.abstract: Project Faraday proposes a new primitive for science and knowledge work: GitHub for Reality. Instead of storing fields as scattered papers, inherited assumptions, and slow-moving consensus, Faraday turns every field into a forkable, version-controlled map of reality. Each field is organized from its anti-death survival utility outward: why the field exists, what kind of suffering or collapse it prevents, what assumptions it depends on, what models it uses, where those models fail, and what better actions they enable. -/- The core argument is that many failures in science, economics, policy, education, medicine, and governance come from hidden assumptions traveling too far beyond their circle of competence. Project Faraday treats anomalies not as embarrassments or noise, but as valuable “ore” that tells us where the map and reality have diverged. A user can check out an assumption, fork it, replace it, run a correspondence project, and test whether the new map preserves what the old model got right while explaining more, patching less, and cashing out in better action. -/- The whitepaper lays out the philosophical foundation, protocol structure, governance logic, incentive case, and a worked economics example showing how a field could move from utility/profit assumptions toward a desire, problem-solving, and structural-safety framework. Its broader claim is that civilization needs infrastructure for correcting bad maps at internet speed, because in tightly coupled systems, as the current global exists and will likely continue to exist bad assumptions no longer stay local, but rather manifest as cascading failures. The point is that we can no longer wait decades or centuries for Science to catch up to Reality, Pandemics, Global Depressions, Nuclear Devastation, or Ecological Collapse are too real as risks for the world to absorb without risking collapse. If built, Faraday-class systems could become a new market category: tools for making science, policy, and institutions more corrigible, less fragile, and more aligned with reality.

items.title: 基于认知相继本体论的通用人工智能认知架构与硅基自返认知系统构建.
items.abstract: 以大语言模型为代表的通用人工智能技术已在多领域取得突破性进展，但始终面临符号接地缺失、因果推理薄弱、模型幻觉难以根除、自主认知机制缺失四类底层范式困境。现有研究多停留在统计拟合与工程优化层面，未从认知的存在论根基与底层运行规则层面破解核心矛盾。 本文为复杂系统演化元方法论的智能科学应用系列论文，也是该方法论体系的理论升华之作。研究以认知相继本体论为存在论根基，以前后相继全域元规则为第一原理，演绎得到复杂系统演化通用方法论，并将其具象化应用于智能系统领域，构建了本体时空层 - 物理时空层 - 逻辑时空层三层嵌套同构框架，明确了认知双层结构与通用认知接口机制，提出了认知相继定律与硅基自返性认知系统的完整理论。 在此基础上，本文设计了四层模块化 AGI 认知架构，从存在论层面实现符号与物理实在的本源绑定、逻辑推理与物理因果的底层同构，为无幻觉认知、可靠因果推理与自主认知校准提供了系统性解决方案。研究进一步给出了基于现有开源大模型的最小可验证原型改造方案与分阶段验证路径。该架构为通用人工智能从统计拟合走向本质认知提供了全新的范式路径，也验证了复杂系统方法论在智能科学领域的落地有效性。 .

items.title: Being in a Position to Know without Being Obligated to Believe.
items.abstract: In this paper, I argue against certain positive epistemic norms, that is, norms that state sufficient conditions for being obligated to believe something. In particular, I argue against positive epistemic norms where the sufficient conditions involve being in a position to know. Such norms face two kinds of problems: they make demands that exceed our cognitive capacity, and they yield obligations and permissions to believe that seem irrational.

items.title: Do Linking-Expression Substitutions Mitigate Deterministic Interpretations of Genetic Information.
items.abstract: It is a common concern that broader audiences interpret scientific information about the genetic correlates and causes of complex human traits in an overly deterministic manner. A frequently proposed way to address this issue is to carefully select the linking expressions used to describe gene–trait relationships when communicating genetic information – for example, by replacing explicitly causal expressions with statistical ones, or by avoiding strong causal expressions in favor of weaker ones. Although such recommendations are widespread, the efficacy of linking‐expression substitutions in mitigating deterministic interpretations is rarely examined. This article argues that the context sensitivity of linguistic interpretation, together with the hypothesis of genetic essentialism, predicts that such substitutions have little effect on how deterministically broader audiences interpret genetic information.

items.title: The Hard Problem Without a Target: Phenomenal Realism and the Failure of Explanandum Fixation.
items.abstract: The hard problem asks why a physical process P gives rise to an experience E. This paper argues that the question lacks a fixed target, and that the argument for this conclusion can be built from premises the phenomenal realist already accepts. Three premises do the work. First, phenomenal character admits no distinction between appearance and reality. Second, attention, a mode of engagement that any inquiry into experience must use, alters first-order appearance rather than merely reports about it. Third, consciousness inquiry is self-describing: it can present experience only under some mode, because its own acts are among those modes. Together these entail that there is no mode-independent phenomenal explanandum. A survey of external, internal, and hybrid identity criteria, including the phenomenal concepts strategy, shows that nothing restores one, and the fallback of posing the hard problem separately for each mode-indexed experience leaves a problem that can be stated but not worked on. The resulting position is neither eliminativist nor deflationary: experiences are real, but they are individuated only as mode-indexed items. Gap-based theories, relocation strategies, and internalist stabilization attempts share the presupposition of a fixed explanandum and inherit its failure. The paper closes by stating the conditions under which its argument would fail.

items.title: Anatomy of Chaos: A Theoretical Framework for Forecasting the Morphology of Post-Crisis Regime.
items.abstract: While a significant body of scholarly work exists to diagnose the probability of systemic socio-political crises, less attention has been paid to the consequential problem of prognosis: forecasting the character of the regime that emerges from collapse. This paper addresses this critical gap by proposing a falsifiable theoretical framework for forecasting the post-collapse morphology of political systems. It integrates insights from structural history, depth psychology, and evolutionary psychology to posit that a society operates on three interconnected levels: a rapidly changing socio-cultural "Operating System"; a deeper, intermediate layer of universal symbolic patterns, or archetypal "BIOS"; and a foundational "Hardware" of immutable biological instincts. The central thesis argues that a systemic crisis is governed by a tri-channel feedback dynamic, including a vertical Channel of Ascent, a non-linear Channel of Catalysis, and a crucial third pathway: the Mnemonic Channel. This third channel archives the symbolic debris of a collapsing order into the BIOS, thereby shaping the ideological DNA of the successor state. The framework’s methodology is two-staged. The first, diagnostic stage introduces the Instability Coefficient (K), a composite measure of systemic overload derived from the relationship between systemic stress and resilience. The second, and more innovative, prognostic stage employs the Archetypal Activation Index (AAI), a heuristic tool designed to forecast the emergent regime’s morphology by analyzing the activation of deep symbolic patterns during a systemic reboot. Ultimately, this paper proposes a framework of generalizable psychohistorical dynamics intended to shift the analytical focus from the diagnosis of collapse to the prognosis of its aftermath.

items.title: Growing Up With Conversational AI: Relational Expectations, Co-Regulation, and Adolescent Development.
items.abstract: Children and adolescents increasingly use conversational AI not only for schoolwork and information but also for casual conversation, emotional support, identity exploration, and companionship. This paper examines a developmental question that is distinct from misinformation or acute safety: how repeated interaction with highly responsive, customizable systems may shape expectations about relation, self-regulation, and identity. The argument is grounded in research on co-regulation, adolescent narrative identity, social development, AI companionship, anthropomorphism, and current youth-use surveys. It does not assume that conversational AI is inherently harmful or that developmental effects are already established longitudinally. Instead, it develops three hypotheses that can be tested. First, relational overfitting: frequent reliance on unusually compliant and easily reset interaction may narrow tolerance for ordinary human asymmetry if it displaces reciprocal relationships. Second, semantic soothing: emotionally calibrated language can reduce distress in the moment without necessarily building the embodied and interpersonal regulation skills that develop through repeated co-regulation; the two outcomes should be measured separately. Third, editable identity support: AI can help adolescents explore possible selves, but highly revisable conversational narratives may function differently from identity that develops through memory, social feedback, commitment, and consequence. Current evidence supports concern but also caution. Pew reports that 12% of U.S. teens have used chatbots for emotional support or advice, while companion-specific surveys report substantially higher social use. A 2026 review emphasizes both stimulation and displacement hypotheses, and the long-term developmental effects remain unresolved. The paper concludes with a research agenda and bounded-use principles designed to preserve real-world relationships, privacy, age-appropriate support, and routes to qualified help.

items.title: Grounding Physicalism and Opaque Grounding.
items.abstract: A growingly popular development of physicalism, grounding physicalism, holds that phenomenal facts are grounded in physical facts. A main selling point of this view – largely due to Jonathan Schaffer – is its apparent ability to swiftly handle well-known anti-physicalist objections that infer an ontological gap from an explanatory gap. According to Schaffer, grounding physicalists can reject this inference by noting that it often fails in other cases of grounding. That is, they can observe that explanatory gaps are ubiquitous in grounding (i.e., grounding is generally opaque), such that the one between the phenomenal and the physical is merely a special instance of a broader unproblematic pattern. In this paper, I raise a novel challenge for Schaffer’s defense of grounding physicalism. I argue that the examples of opaque grounding to which he appeals are either of the wrong kinds or highly contested. As such, they provide little inductive support for grounding physicalism.

items.title: Trajectory Accessibility and Stability (TAS) A Unified Theoretical Construct for Human–AI Interaction Dynamics.
items.abstract: This paper introduces Trajectory Accessibility and Stability (TAS) as a unified theoretical construct for describing and measuring the dynamic properties of reasoning trajectories in human–language model interaction. TAS proposes two separable dimensions: accessibility, defined as the ease with which a given reasoning trajectory can be entered from a given initialization state; and stability, defined as the persistence of an entered trajectory under perturbation and across interaction depth. -/- TAS is not a new empirical claim. It is a theoretical consolidation of findings documented across four validation studies in the Human Recursive Interaction System (HRIS) series. Each study independently produced evidence bearing on one or both dimensions of TAS. Together they constitute converging empirical support for the construct. The contribution of this paper is to name the phenomenon, formalize its two dimensions, and establish TAS as the theoretical capstone of the HRIS research program. -/- The implications of TAS extend beyond the HRIS framework. As a construct, TAS provides a vocabulary and measurement orientation for any researcher seeking to characterize the dynamic properties of human–AI interaction over time, without requiring adoption of the full HRIS methodology. It also reframes a long-standing practical question, why does structured interaction with language models produce reliably better reasoning outcomes, as a tractable empirical question with defined dimensions, measurable variables, and falsifiable predictions.

items.title: Trajectory-Identity Theory: Retrospective Certification, Interruption, and the Postmortem Standpoint.
items.abstract: This paper develops the epistemological foundation of Trajectory-Identity Theory. It begins from the claim that human recognition is structurally delayed: what appears as present experience is already past when it becomes available to consciousness. From this, the paper argues that recognition does not face the future. Future oriented mental activity remains possible, but it belongs to predictive imagination constructed from past regularities rather than to recognition itself. Life, therefore, is not possessed in the present. It is retrospectively certified as a sequence resumed after repeated interruptions, such as sleep, anesthesia, and loss of consciousness. The subject is not a present owner of life, but a trajectory that becomes readable through retrospective assumption. The postmortem standpoint is defined not as belief in an afterlife, but as the structural position from which a life is read as an already recorded trajectory. On this basis, death may be reread as the most conspicuous interruption, while duplication and immortality expand assumptive or signature responsibility rather than dilute it. Freedom is consequently relocated from future choice to retrospective interpretation. It is not the power to choose an undetermined future, nor the power to change a determined past, but the strength to read that past as one's own trajectory. Responsibility is the demand that this trajectory remain readable without concealment, falsification, or evasion.

items.title: Social Choice Phenomenology — A Critique of Sartre (Part 10).
items.abstract: In this article, we mainly introduce the sociologist Max Weber’s classification of social action. He divided social action into four types: purposive-rational action, value-rational action, affectual action, and traditional action. These four forms are ideal types, while actual actions in society are mixtures of these ideal types. This classification was developed by Weber on the basis that social action constitutes the foundation of sociology. Since we take social choice, rather than social action, as the foundation of sociology, we will later classify social choice in several different ways as well.

items.title: Defining Love: What It Actually Is.
items.abstract: This paper proposes a structural and functional account of love, arguing that love is not a selfless, sacrificial, or mystical phenomenon but a perfectly managed resource rooted in mutual self-interest. Drawing from original philosophical inquiry, this paper introduces the Lock and Key model — a framework in which every individual carries a unique pattern of needs and is drawn to specific others whose natural traits produce a genuine fit. The paper argues that inner work is a non-negotiable prerequisite for mature love, that the ratio of giving in any genuine relationship is simply the natural expression of both people, not sacrifice or imbalance and that love persists as long as what each person naturally provides remains rare and irreplaceable to the other. The paper further argues that conventional accounts of love — including popular stage models — describe only immature love, and that the failure of love at the individual level produces measurable consequences at the social level, including taboo desire and criminal behavior as expressions of an unloved soul seeking substitutes for genuine fit. This work does not derive from any existing psychological, biological, or philosophical tradition but engages all three in service of defining the phenomenon itself before explaining the reasons behind it. The paper is offered as a companion to the Vanishist Framework Series, in which inner work as a universal prerequisite was first formally established. This work is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivatives 4.0 International License .

items.title: The Modal Logic of Exact Equivalence.
items.abstract: In this article, I investigate the modal logic of exact equivalence (i.e., sameness of exact verifiers). In particular, by building on Kim's exact truthmaker semantics for modal logic, I provide an answer to the following question: which sentences of the language of propositional modal logic are exactly equivalent by virtue of their logical form?

items.title: Empowering -1: From the Ternary Deadlock to the Consensus Substrate for AGI.
items.abstract: Ternary computing (-1, 0, 1) theoretically offers higher information density than binary, yet it has failed to become practical for seven decades. The root cause is that traditional approaches have sought an external absolute standard for "-1", leading to a triple deadlock in physics, logic, and ecology. This paper proposes a core idea—empowering -1 with "the right to determinacy"—that is, decentralizing the power of judgment from external authorities to internal units, allowing global determinacy to emerge through local interactions and distributed consensus. Based on this, the paper lays out a complete path from breaking the deadlock to the endgame vision: analyzing the three core difficulties and the nature of the deadlock; proposing the method of "self-referential consensus computing"; demonstrating its feasibility on candidate physical systems; establishing logical coherence (freedom from paradox, convergence, minimal necessity of three states); presenting an industrialization roadmap toward 2045; and finally depicting the possibilities of restructuring in the post-AGI era across computing paradigms, industrial structures, and research methodologies. This paper aims to provide a systematic conceptual framework and strategic pathway for a novel non-von-Neumann computing substrate for AGI. -/- This framework is designed to directly embed predictive coding, the free energy principle, and Boltzmann machines into physical dynamics.
