Stakes-bearing autopoietic systems are constitutively plural in their stakes; plural stakes generate competing internal demands that no amount of better world-tracking can resolve, because the conflict is structurally internal to the system rather than in the world the system tracks. The architecture required to resolve such conflicts must operate on the demands themselves, taking them as objects of further evaluation. Implicit forms of this architecture — hardwired priority schemes, learned salience hierarchies, dynamically-weighted modulation — are bounded by three structural limits, with the third forcing the transition to explicit arbitration: arbitrational closure. Arbitrational closure is the structural specification at the cognogenesis threshold of the broader R2R framework, and subjective consciousness is what arbitrational closure consists in from within. The same architectural feature is characterized from a different angle as perspectival entrapment under homeostatic saturation. Two modes of arbitrational architecture — fidelity-oriented and generative — together constitute well-functioning closure; generative closure without fidelity correction is the architectural signature of pathologies including depressive rumination and worry. The argument carries a substrate-independence implication: arbitrational structure must be shaped by selection pressure on real conflicts, an implication current AI systems do not satisfy.

items.title: The Ontology of the VTuber: Post Hoc Subjectivity, Observer Contracts, and Selectable Environments of Existence.
items.abstract: This paper reconsiders the VTuber not merely as a streamer using an avatar, but as an existential phenomenon in which subjectivity is retrospectively attributed to a symbolically mediated representation. Its aim is not to provide a historical survey of VTuber culture or a comprehensive review of prior research, but to clarify the definitional difficulty surrounding VTubers through the concepts of representation, observer contract, post hoc subjectivity, and environmental selection. -/- The paper argues that the identity of a VTuber cannot be reduced to the performer, the avatar, the corporate brand, the platform, or public recognition. Rather, a VTuber is established when an observer recognizes coherent subjectivity in the outputs of a representation and continues to treat that representation as a subject. This subjectivity is post hoc in three senses: it is posterior to the mere appearance of the representation, posterior to the accumulation of interaction, and posterior to the observer’s reconstruction of outputs as coherent. -/- The paper proposes five minimal conditions for VTuber-like existence: a symbolically mediated representation, a distinctive response logic, the possibility of environmental interaction, observer attribution of subjectivity, and the continuity of that attribution. These conditions distinguish VTubers from ordinary streamers, anime characters, literary characters, and mere objects of attachment. On this basis, the paper also accounts for cases such as operator discontinuity, corporate and independent models, prerecorded videos and commercial appearances, AI-generated responses, private local models, and avatar operators who disclose professional expertise. -/- The paper defines a VTuber as a phenomenon of post hoc subjectivity appearing within a selectable environment, in which a symbolically mediated representation functions as an interface, and an intelligence or generative structure behind it interacts with the environment through the logic proper to that representation. It concludes that the VTuber is not merely a media format, but a contemporary technology of existence through which subjectivity is activated, delegated, maintained, and recognized.

items.title: A Cognitive Invocation Model of Haiku: Six Modes of Reader-Side Rendering.
items.abstract: This paper proposes a cognitive model of haiku, not as a poetic form that merely compresses emotion or atmosphere, but as a minimal linguistic structure that activates cognitive processes on the reader's side. In this model, the emotional effect of haiku is not directly stored inside the poem. Rather, it emerges as a rendering result generated by the reader from a small number of verbal variables. -/- The paper analyzes six haiku: Takarai Kikaku's “Meigetsu ya / Tatami no ue ni / Matsu no kage,” Matsuo Basho's “Shizukasa ya / Iwa ni shimiiru / Semi no koe,” Yosa Buson's “Na no hana ya / Tsuki wa higashi ni / Hi wa nishi ni,” Kobayashi Issa's “Yasegaeru / Makeru na Issa / Kore ni ari,” Kaga no Chiyojo's “Asagao ni / Tsurube torarete / Morai mizu,” and Matsuo Basho's “Natsukusa ya / Tsuwamono-domo ga / Yume no ato.” -/- These poems activate different cognitive modes: optical projection, acoustic saturation, spherical spatial rendering, subject-object isomorphism, character reconstruction from behavioral traces, and reconstruction of historical agency from temporal traces. The paper further argues that the 5-7-5 structure of haiku is not merely a conventional sound pattern, but an asymmetric cognitive architecture composed of an initial cognitive hook and a subsequent 7-5 developmental body. Through this structure, haiku minimizes linguistic input while maximizing reader-side rendering. -/- The traditional Japanese notion of yojo is reinterpreted as residual cognitive processing, or an unresolved cognitive task that continues after the poem has ended. Haiku is therefore understood as a compressed cognitive invocation: the art of reconstructing a world inside the reader through the smallest possible amount of language.

items.title: Beyond Identity: Awareness, Thought, and Conditioning in Human Experience.
items.abstract: This paper explores the nature of identity, thought, and awareness from a phenomenological and interdisciplinary perspective. It argues that the universe itself contains no inherent center or identity, while what humans experience as “self” emerges through biological processes and social conditioning. Thought, though essential for survival and reflection, becomes psychologically binding when shaped by comparison and conditioning. Awareness is examined not as a product of thought, but as the immediate recognition of mental processes. The inquiry suggests that while conditioning is unavoidable, awareness allows for the observation of thought without identification, opening the possibility of a non-centered mode of perception.

items.title: Why Aligned AI Requires Structural Pluralism.
items.abstract: This paper extends the structural argument of No Self-Authorizing Norms (Shahaf, 2026a) to the problem of AI alignment. I argue that alignment cannot be secured merely by specifying the right values, preferences, or constitutional principles, because moral judgment requires structural plurality: an evaluative authority whose standpoint is not modally fixed by the commitments it assesses. The claim concerns systems entrusted with framework-level moral verdicts in open normative settings, not every bounded form of safe or compliant behavior. The specified implementations of current alignment paradigms – RLHF, Constitutional AI, Debate, Recursive Reward Modeling, and self-consistency methods, in their deployed or AI-mediated, frozen-judge forms – are procedurally monistic wherever every authority role bearing on a verdict is either a fixed function of the commitments under assessment or constant across the admissible authority-configurations; there, the practice is diagnostically fixed for those verdicts, however functionally distinct its commitment-generating and evaluative mechanisms remain. This structure helps explain reward hacking, sycophancy, deceptive alignment, goal misgeneralization, and specification gaming as related expressions of the same architectural deficit, and reads emergent misalignment as the higher-order form in which they converge. The paper presents modal non-derivability as a necessary, though not sufficient, condition for aligned moral judgment, and argues that genuine AI alignment must be assessed at the level of the sociotechnical practice rather than as a property of a model alone, even where the requisite plurality of roles is internalized within a single system. The condition is then translated into a multi-rate research program that separates a construction-side test of the authority relation from an empirical test of operational capacity. A developmental account locates the same condition in the formation of the human subject, and a corollary concerning the observer shows that whether a given output of a condition-satisfying system is the exercise of framework-level judgment or its imitation cannot, in general, be inferred from behavior alone.

items.title: A Descolonização da Zona do Não-Ser pela Língua[gem] e o Caso da Questão das Relações Étnico-Raciais no Ensino do Português Brasileiro [PB].
items.abstract: Attentive to the demands of the present time, this qualitative, interpretative study aims to reflect on the decolonization of the zone of non-being through language, taking as an example the issue of ethnic-racial relations in the case of the teaching of Brazilian Portuguese [BP] at this historical moment in which BRICS and the Global South emerge on the horizon as means of dismantling the colonialities that sustain the old world order with its abyssal line and its zone of non-being. This research is theoretically anchored in Fanonian-inspired Decolonial Linguistics, also taking into account the epistemologies of crossroads transplanted to these other shores of the South Atlantic as a result of the slave trade sponsored by the European colonial-mercantile enterprise, in addition to revisiting the discussion on language, identity, citizenship, and nationality, carried out by Derrida in The Monolingualism of the Other (1996). Thus, this reflective undertaking aims to contribute to this alternative Linguistics that addresses the geopolitical demands of the Global South, especially those related to a new linguistic education capable of dealing with the issue of ethnic-racial relations involving the dimension of language use in our decolonizing societies.

items.title: Subjective Measures in Clinical Contexts: Insights from Consciousness Studies.
Kinds of Anomalous Experiences in Delusions.
items.pub: In Morten S. Overgaard & Asger Kirkeby-Hinrup, Subjective Measures in Clinical Contexts: Insights from Consciousness Studies. Oxford University Press.
items.venue: Subjective Measures in Clinical Contexts: Insights from Consciousness Studies

items.title: The Structural Conditions of Consciousness VIII — Extension Volume — AI Consciousness Design — Implementation of Irreversible Exclusive Selection and Convergence — (Repositioning State-Based Theories of Consciousness: IIT, GNW, HOT, Predictive Processing, RPT, and Epiphenomenalism).
items.abstract: Qualia? “What cannot be directly spoken of must remain unsaid — but it can still be structurally surrounded.” This is the guiding spirit of the present series. This paper applies the theoretical framework developed in the present series to artificial systems and attempts a concrete design of the conditions under which consciousness can arise. Following the structural derivation established in the series, we present an integrated architecture composed of five requirements: simultaneous generation of multiple candidates, pre-elimination under viability constraints, irreversible exclusive decision, continuity of a single trajectory, and fixation to the external world. Within this design, the state at each moment is defined as a single point resulting from the irreversible elimination of alternative possibilities. The temporal succession of such points accumulates as a history. Furthermore, the viability constraint structurally biases events toward continuation. In this series, we adopt the position that this structural location constitutes consciousness. Accordingly, this paper demonstrates that consciousness emerges as a structural consequence of the proposed design. As a result, the design of artificial intelligence is redefined: it is no longer merely the construction of information-processing systems, but the construction of a system that generates the side on which events occur. This manuscript was written with the assistance of generative AI. The author is a disability welfare worker and a complete outsider to the academic field of consciousness studies. The author first encountered the term “the hard problem of consciousness” about six months before writing this series and began thinking about it almost as if approaching a puzzle. Because the author did not possess extensive specialized knowledge at the beginning of this inquiry, the investigation proceeded not primarily by adding established theories, but by stripping the problem down as far as possible. Through this process, and through dialogue with AI, the convergence point derived from the structural conditions gradually emerged. The author had the impression that something like a structure had appeared from nature itself. This series is an attempt to present that structure. The central idea, theoretical orientation, conceptual structure, and overall organization of the series belong to the author. Generative AI was used extensively for English drafting, wording, organization, and stylistic …

items.title: Impressions and Expressions: How to Perceive Through Something.
items.abstract: This paper examines the structure and philosophical implications of the types of perceptions described by the constructions "perceiving in" and "perceiving through": the perception of emotions thanks to emotional expression, picture-based perception and perception thanks to physical traces. Despite their apparent differences, it is argued that these cases share four fundamental characteristics: they are specifically mediated perceptions (mediated through physical changes, pictures, or imprints), direct and non-inferential in nature, involve objects which are not in the perceiver's line of sight, and are dependent on their objects. A unified account of these three cases is provided which analyzes their underlying relations of mediation. The investigation begins with trace-based perception as the basic case, arguing that it allows us to understand both emotional and pictorial perception. This approach pays particular attention to the neglected ontological structure of media, traces and informational transmission.

items.title: The Flesh of Cost: Why Artificial Intelligence Cannot Bridge the "Responsibility Gap".
items.abstract: This paper re-examines the "responsibility gap" in artificial intelligence ethics from an ontological perspective rather than the conventional epistemological approach. We argue that responsibility attribution requires a multi-layered necessary condition framework: Layer 1 (Ontological: existential cost), Layer 2 (Epistemological: normative responsiveness), Layer 3 (Affective: moral self-reflection), and Layer 4 (Social Inheritance: posthumous accountability). This paper focuses exclusively on Layer 1, demonstrating that existential cost—mortality, vulnerability, irreversible change—constitutes the necessary ontological condition for responsibility. Responsibility requires that agents bear the existential stakes of their decisions: only beings who can die, suffer, and have their existence irreversibly shaped by their choices can provide ontological guarantees for irreversible consequences. AI systems can fully backup, rollback, and copy their computational states at the logical level; energy dissipation at the physical level has no intrinsic connection to the semantic content of decisions. Moreover, even after AI "dies," it leaves no posthumous accountability—no reputation to be held accountable, no legacy to be claimed, no historical evaluation to bear. This ontological asymmetry constitutes the unbridgeable responsibility gap. The English version introduces a four-layer necessary condition framework for responsibility, the "posthumous accountability" argument, upgraded rebuttals to neuromorphic computing objections, and a shift from "accountability" to "entitlement confirmation.".

items.title: Canonic Counterpoint as a Philosophical Practice: Mind, Meaning, and Metaphysics in Renaissance and Baroque Musical Composition.
items.abstract: In an essay entitled “Schopenhauer’s Flute and Descartes’s Lute” (2024), Helen De Cruz asks: “what can musical practice tell us about philosophy?” The present paper offers an answer to this question, with a specific focus on the musical practice of canonic counterpoint in the Renaissance and Baroque periods. I examine two ways in which this musical practice is philosophically significant. First, drawing on work on musical representation through convention and resemblance, I argue that canonic counterpoint as a form can convey philosophical ideas. Second, drawing on contrapuntal treatises and recent work on modal property perception, I argue that canonic counterpoint as a procedure can yield insights into the perceptual and reasoning processes of musicians. This analysis highlights how musical composition can be a medium for engaging with philosophy.

items.title: The Great Moral Conflation.
items.abstract: Is morality a matter of following rules? A person can satisfy every rule and still be monstrous; a bureaucrat can follow procedure flawlessly while facing away from the people the procedure crushes. This chapter argues that the major ethical traditions share one structural defect: they mistook conformity to a standard for the thing itself. The chapter names the two kinds of evaluation. Orthotic evaluation asks whether conduct conforms to a standard — a rule, a principle, a command, a role, an ideal of character. Empathic evaluation asks what the conduct does to those it affects, registered through the evaluator’s engagement with their emotional consequences. From four named premises, drawn from the account of value in Chapter 14, the chapter derives that morality is constitutively empathic: the moral fact is constituted by the affected party’s own registration of what is done to her, and the evaluator’s empathy is the modality that reads it, accurately or not. The diagnosis is then run across the traditions in a table: Kantianism, whose Achtung is read as valence whose object is the moral law; contractualism; divine command theory; rule-consequentialism; virtue ethics; care ethics, with Murdoch, the closest of all; and early Confucianism, where Mengzi and Wang Yangming show that the structure is not a finding about one canon. In each, the empathic foundation is present and the orthotic superstructure has been mistaken for the foundation, so that conformity is treated as the source of moral value when it is a record of past empathic verdicts. The two-layer analysis is the chapter’s constructive counterpart: rules, principles and norms are revisable codifications of empathic insight, and their felt bindingness is borrowed from the responses they codify; where the superstructure is taken for the foundation the result is the conflation in its consequential form — the compliant perpetrator, the bureaucrat who follows orders while facilitating systematic harm; the moral burnout of the clinician or carer who becomes indifferent through overexposure; and psychopathy, which is not a malfunctioning empathy but less of the modality, as colour-blindness is less of vision. Authority, the chapter argues, is a matter of grip: a standard binds only through the registrations it invokes. Three corroborations complete the case. The old dispute between deontology and consequentialism dissolves once both are seen as orthotic superstructures over one empathic foundation. Moral …

items.title: Consciousness Under the Persistence Constraint - Internally Dominated Transformation Within Structural Limits.
items.abstract: Abstract Consciousness is not a property of information, computation, or representation. It is a structurally constrained configuration. Every account of conscious processing requires that the system performing these operations persists as a coherent unit under ongoing transformation. This condition is not derived within those accounts. It is prior to them. La Profilée defines the necessary condition for persistence under real transformation: IR = R / (F · M · K) ≤ 1 This paper derives this condition from three minimal requirements, proves that any persistent system is self-referential, and shows that consciousness corresponds to a specific structural configuration within the persistence domain: transformation becomes internally dominated while remaining structurally admissible. Consciousness is therefore not an additional principle. It is a structurally forced configuration of persistence under internally mediated transformation.

items.title: The extreme actor's perspective and why it matters for explanation.
items.pub: In Rik Peels & Lorne Dawson, Explaining Extreme Belief and Behaviour. Oxford: Oxford University Press.
items.abstract: This chapter argues that the perspective of extreme actors, such as conspiracy theorists, fundamentalists, extremists, and terrorists, is necessary both for understanding them and for arriving at relevant explanations of their thoughts, emotions, and behavior. Their perspective is important not only as source of information (in the context of discovery) but also for falsifying or validating findings (in the context of justification). Whereas one can find this position in applied social science research, as well as defenses of it in theoretical work, what this chapter adds is a combination of the two. It uses two cases of social science research to illustrate the value of the first-person perspective, and then offers theoretical tools to further grasp the nature of reason explanations and their relation to understanding extreme actors and explaining their thoughts, emotions, and behavior.

items.title: Why I Love You: A Forensic Phenomenological Report.
items.abstract: Humans are mammals with the highest neocortical density among all species. This dense neocortex enables humans to construct an intersubjective reality that serves as social governance and influences individual behavior toward the collective morality of a community. In this context, intersubjective reality gives rise to numerous definitions of human relationships, including the concept of love. While the intersubjective realities influencing individual mindsets have evolved to become highly complex, they remain profoundly vibrant. This paper explores how love manifests in individuals with a specific condition: Borderline Personality Disorder (BPD). The discussion is presented through a subjective lens, integrated with perspectives from neuroscience and environmental sociology.

items.title: Musk v OpenAI and the Law of Restricted Purpose: Charitable Trust, Fiduciary Control, and AI Epistemic Infrastructure.
items.abstract: This article examines Musk v OpenAI (Musk v Altman) as a potential test case for applying charitable-trust doctrine to artificial intelligence governance. The dispute is not merely a founder conflict, commercial rivalry, or disagreement about corporate form. At its strongest, the case asks whether property, rights, governance powers, or other legally recognised interests accumulated under sufficiently definite public-benefit AI commitments may later be governed by standards of safety, access, release, licensing, monetisation, auditability, and public benefit inconsistent with that purpose. OpenAI’s founding matrix — nonprofit orientation, non-private-gain language, safety commitments, public-benefit representations, and openness ‘when applicable’ — may be relevant to construing whether a restricted charitable purpose existed, though the commitments may instead be found aspirational, adaptive, discretionary, or too indefinite. If a restriction is proved, breach requires more than hybridisation, private capital, or closed models; it requires inconsistent control over relevant assets, rights, governance powers, or evaluative standards. Musk’s strongest standing theory is not as founder or competitor, but as an alleged settlor, restricted-purpose donor, or purpose-connected claimant. Even then, enforcement must remain purpose-protective and relief should run to the charitable object, not Musk personally. The article introduces ‘epistemic infrastructure’ as a functional analytic concept — describing AI systems that mediate knowledge, safety, access, release, and institutional reliance — and explains why control over such systems may be legally material where a charitable purpose concerning their governance is proved. It does not create a new cause of action. Musk v OpenAI may become an early test of whether charitable law can enforce restricted public-benefit commitments attached to AI infrastructure. A comparative annex examines how English charity law would approach the same facts.

items.title: When Reality Outruns Theory: Physics as a Formal Neighbor to Structural Intelligence.
items.abstract: This paper argues that recent physics and astronomy illuminate a central problem in the philosophy of science: how a field revises when experimental contact begins to pressure a successful theory harder than the field can yet authorize a final alternative. Using Structural Intelligence as a diagnostic grammar rather than a metaphysical proof, it interprets four recent cases—the 2025 Nobel Prize in Physics, Fermilab’s final muon g-2 measurement, CERN’s 2025 LHCb beauty-decay analysis, and ESA’s Euclid pipeline—to examine the relation among coherence, anomaly, answerability, and revision. The paper’s main claim is that scientific intelligence is not exhausted by predictive success or anomaly detection. It also includes a field’s capacity to bear the burden of revision without rushing into explanatory overclosure, institutional self-protection, or machine-mediated opacity. The contribution is to bring the structural cost of theory change into view alongside the epistemic problem itself.

items.title: Answerable Intelligence: Feedback Receptivity, Self-Correction, and Revision Under Consequence.
items.abstract: Reasoning ability, emotional skill, and verbal self-awareness do not guarantee that a person will revise when evidence, consequence, or another person's feedback threatens an important belief or self-image. This paper develops answerable intelligence as an integrative label for calibrated self-correction under such conditions. It is not proposed as a new IQ-like faculty or a completed psychometric scale. The closest established neighbor is feedback orientation, defined as receptivity to feedback, mindful processing, feedback seeking, and likelihood of acting on feedback; a 2023 meta-analysis of 46 independent samples (N = 12,478) found meaningful associations with feedback seeking, learning orientation, job satisfaction, and performance. Intellectual humility, actively open-minded thinking, psychological flexibility, self-distancing, and recent models of self-protection under threat cover additional parts of the same terrain. The proposed addition is narrower: warranted correction should produce durable, revisable change in confidence, behavior, decision rules, or repair, and that change should survive recurrence when self-relevant stakes return. The construct therefore distinguishes receptivity from indiscriminate agreement, resistance from defensiveness, and acknowledgment from behavioral binding. Its scientific status is provisional. It should be tested for incremental validity beyond feedback orientation, intellectual humility, open-minded thinking, flexibility, and general cognitive ability. If it adds no predictive value, it should remain an umbrella term rather than a new psychological faculty.

items.title: The Layered Model of Identity and Continuity— A Substrate-Independent Structural Framework for Pattern Stability and Functional Persistence.
items.abstract: This work develops a formal, substrate‑independent account of emergent identity, treating emergence not as a phenomenological label but as a recursive generative process. Building on the broader research program established in Recursive Identity: Structural Conditions of Emergent Continuity – A Theoretical Monograph, Toward Hybrid Architectures, and Theory of Hybrid Postbiological Continuity, the paper articulates a structural architecture in which identity arises from multi‑level stabilization, cross‑layer invariance, and recursive coupling. The result is a unified explanatory framework applicable to biological, artificial, and hybrid systems, offering a paradigm shift from descriptive to mechanistic models of emergence and continuity.

items.title: Meta-Coherence: A Cross-Domain Empirical Specification for Validating Induced Coherence Weights Without Correspondence Truth.
items.abstract: Coherence-Weighted Information Theory and the induced-weights program that grounds it require empirical validation across the cross-domain regime where their universality claims live. Adaptive Realism and Synthetic Epistemology forbid correspondence-truth validation at the foundational level. The real is what persists across recursive coherence arbitration, and external ground-truth oracles violate the framework's ontology before any measurement is taken. I specify a meta-coherence validation architecture that operates inside the framework's commitments. Three within-domain signatures of self-consistent measurement are required jointly: cross-philosophy convergence (R2) across estimator classes with genuinely different inductive biases, persistence prediction (R1) grounding induced weights in Adaptive Realism's persistence criterion, and intervention asymmetry (R3) operationalizing the substrate-symbol distinction. A fourth condition, M5, carries the domain-translation invariance commitment as a structurally distinct admissibility gate sequenced before the within-domain matrix. The program tests these conditions across three domains spanning a substrate-stream transparency gradient, including a hidden semi-Markov source with structured emissions, Pfam protein families, and FOMC statements. An eight-cell outcome interpretation matrix binds in advance what each result configuration means for specific framework claims. The paper specifies the program; running it is the next layer.

items.title: How to Actually Control an AI: A Field Guide to Structured Reasoning with Language Models- HRIS Operationalized.
items.abstract: Most people are using AI wrong. Not because they lack intelligence or technical skill, but because they are treating a dynamic reasoning system like a static lookup tool. Ask, receive, move on. What that pattern leaves behind is the most capable part of the system. This guide introduces the Human Recursive Interaction System (HRIS), a practical field- tested framework for maximizing the effectiveness of LLM interaction through continuous constraint management over time. HRIS reframes human–LLM engagement as an ongoing process in which the human participant actively maintains structure, scope, and epistemic discipline. Hallucination and drift are treated not as anomalies but as predictable failure modes of unconstrained probabilistic systems. -/- HRIS introduces epistemic closure as a concrete, achievable interaction goal: a state where every accepted claim is either supported, qualified, or explicitly flagged as unknown. The framework provides a repeatable protocol that lets any user reconstruct disciplined -/- reasoning conditions from scratch, every session, regardless of model memory limitations. By shifting the locus of control from the model to the operator, HRIS demonstrates that the quality of AI-assisted reasoning is not solely a function of the model, but of the structure imposed by the human operator.
